title: Import Word 97-2003 .doc files (#28)
author: edurbs
body:
Fixes #28 — opening a `.doc` (or `.dot`) file no longer produces an empty document.

## What this adds

A new L2 crate, `wordcraft-docbin` (`crates/docbin`): a clean-room reader for the Word
97-2003 binary format, written from the public [MS-DOC] / [MS-CFB] specifications (via the
MIT-licensed `cfb` crate for the container; no GPL/AGPL sources were read or copied).
Import only — saving stays `.docx` and friends.

`engine` dispatches `doc | dot` to it (`OPEN_EXTS` already listed them), so `Open`, the CLI
(`wordcraft-cli convert x.doc out.pdf`) and MCP all get it.

What's read:

- **Text**: the piece table with both encodings (UTF-16 and cp1252), fast-saved files included.
- **Formatting**: stylesheet (styles with inheritance), font table, CHPX/PAPX FKPs, and a
  core sprm set → `CharProps`/`ParaProps`.
- **Structure**: sections (page size/margins/orientation, columns, page-number restart),
  headers/footers (even/odd/first) as document parts, tables (grids, horizontal/vertical
  merges, borders, shading, cell widths/valign, row height/header/cant-split) and lists
  (`PlfLst`/`PlfLfo` resolved into the numbering model).
- **Extras**: footnotes and endnotes as parts with `NoteRef` anchors, fields (0x13/0x14/0x15
  state machine; HYPERLINK results become linked runs, others become `Field` objects),
  bookmarks, and inline pictures from the Data stream (PICF sizing; PNG/JPEG/GIF/BMP).

Explicit rejections with clear errors: encrypted files, and Word 6/95 (dead format).
Metafile-wrapped images and OLE objects are dropped with a `log::warn`, matching the docx
reader's policy.

## How it's tested

- 40 unit tests with synthetic fixtures built in code from the spec (the repo never commits
  Word-produced files), including a combined document that round-trips table + list +
  sections + header through Document JSON.
- Hostile input: proptest truncation and bit-flips over structured fixtures; no panics, and
  the crate carries the never-crash deny lints.
- Real-corpus validati…

title: Tables: draw style borders when w:tblBorders is empty (#143)
author: edurbs
body:
Fixes #143.

## Problem

Tables whose only border definition lives in the table style rendered with no grid at all when the document carried an *empty* `<w:tblBorders></w:tblBorders>` (and per-cell `<w:tcBorders></w:tcBorders>`), as in the issue's attachment: every side resolved to "no border".

## Root cause

The reader correctly parses an empty border element to "no side set" (all sides `None`, wrapped in `Some`). The defect was in resolution: `crates/layout/src/table.rs` picked the table's own borders *or else* the style's as a unit, so a `Some`-with-nothing-inside hid the style's borders entirely. Verified causality by rebuilding the attachment without the empty elements — the grid rendered fine, proving style application worked and the empty elements alone killed it.

## The fix

Border resolution between the table and its style is now per side (ECMA-376 order): the style's borders form the base and the table's own borders overlay side by side, via a new `Borders::overlay` (`crates/doc/src/props.rs`). This also fixes the previously-broken partial case — a table specifying only some sides now inherits the rest from its style — and preserves explicit `w:val="nil"` kills (they stay `Some` and override the style side).

Because unset sides now inherit from the style, the `table.borders` presets that intentionally clear sides ("Outside Borders", "Inside Borders") would have rendered like "All Borders" on styled tables; they now mask their cleared sides with explicit `nil`, matching Word's presets (`crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs`).

## Tests

- `wordcraft-doc`: `Borders::overlay` unit test (per-side merge, nil override, empty patch is a no-op).
- `wordcraft-layout`: four tests — the issue case (empty `tblBorders` + styled table renders the grid), partial override (own side + style sides), explicit-nil kill, and no-style-stays-borderless.
- `wordcraft-docx`: hand-written ECMA-376 fixture pinning the parse contract (empty elements parse to all-`None` sides; style bord…

title: #147: wire Picture Format UI for inserted pictures
author: gittonyp
body:
Fixes #147 — inserted pictures had no editing UI; the engine commands existed but nothing called them.

- Ribbon: contextual Picture Format tab appears when a picture is selected (Adjust: Corrections/Color/Transparency presets, Change via picker, Reset; Picture Styles + Border; Arrange; Size with W/H spinners, per-side Crop fields, Alt text)
- Canvas right-click menu: Change Picture / Reset Picture / Size and Crop
- Change Picture reuses the existing file picker and runs picture.change instead of insert.picture; the pending change is tracked by media key, cleared on picker cancel, on selection change, and on any unrelated action
- Alt text draft is kept in egui temp memory keyed by picture and commits only to the still-selected picture
- Drags join one undo entry; keyboard-entered values keep normal undo entries
- Stored contextual tabs (Picture Format and also Table Design/Layout, same wart) fall back to Home when the selection moves away

No model changes, no new dependencies.

Verified: cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui (30 passed) + cargo test -p wordcraft-engine (38 passed, incl. new alt+crop round-trip); clippy -D warnings clean; fmt clean; cargo build -p wordcraft OK.

Known limitation: undoing an alt-text change while the alt field still has focus can re-apply the draft on blur.

title: Desktop and web: ask to save changes before New, Open or Close; AutoSave only files you saved
author: goldsbd
body:
Two ways WordCraft could lose a user's work without asking: closing or replacing a document with unsaved changes, and AutoSave rewriting a file the user had only opened. Each commit has a regression test that fails before its fix.

**1. Ask to save before New, Open, Close or quit** (`ui-egui`, `web`). New, Open, file drop, Mod+W and the window's close button replaced or closed a dirty document without asking, and its undo history went with it (`Session::set_document` drops both). `WordApp::run`, the path every user action takes, now shows "Do you want to save changes to <name>?" with Save / Don't Save / Cancel and runs the command once it is answered. The window close is held with `ViewportCommand::CancelClose` until then. On the web, a `beforeunload` guard asks before leaving the tab, and Export (PDF/PNG) no longer marks the document saved.
- The answer is also a command, `ui.saveChanges`, so agents can answer it.
- Scripts and agents keep the old behaviour: the control channel and the MCP bridge call the new `WordApp::execute`, which never asks, since programmatic calls never open dialogs.

**2. AutoSave writes only to a file the user saved to** (`ui-egui`). AutoSave was on for every document with a path, and `file.open` sets the path. Opening a .docx and typing one character therefore rewrote the original about 2.5 s later, dropping everything the readers don't model (content controls, charts, SmartArt, macros). Save errors were discarded with `let _ =` and retried every 2.5 s.
- AutoSave now covers only a file explicitly saved (Save / Save As) in this session.
- A failure shows in the status bar and is logged, and AutoSave pauses for that file until the next explicit save.
- The title-bar toggle and the Options label say which documents it covers.

**Follow-up fixes after an adversarial review** (each with its own test):
- Enter clicks the focused button. Before, Enter with Cancel focused saved the file.
- A pending prompt is dropped when its document is replace…

title: Layout and PDF: repeating table headers, one URL per link, no tracked deletions in the final text
author: goldsbd
body:
Three layout bugs that show up in exported PDFs: a repeating table header that produced thousands of pages, hyperlinks that all pointed at the first URL, and tracked deletions printed as ordinary text. Each commit has a regression test that fails before its fix.

**1. Repeating table headers** (`layout/lib.rs`, `place_table`). A repeating header plus a row that couldn't fit below it on an empty page made the loop spin. After each page break the header was placed again, so the row never started at the top of a page, `split_row` had nothing to split, and the loop ran its 1,000 iterations per row. A 20-row table with a 640 pt header gave **19,002 pages**. A 300 pt header with 400 pt rows gave 2,002.
- `place_table` now notes when a page holds only the repeated header. A row that can't split is placed there, under the header, instead of breaking the page again, so every pass places something.
- Rows of text taller than the room still split across pages.
- This matches Word: on Word for Mac I measured four cases (normal, tall header, 640 pt header, splitting rows), and each one now matches Word's own PDF **page by page**, including Word's choice to let such a row run into the bottom margin.

**2. Each hyperlink keeps its own URL** (`layout/para.rs`). `Builder::style` memoised `StyleRun`s by a key that folded strike, double strike and "has a link" into booleans and left out the underline colour and baseline. In a paragraph of like-formatted links, every link pointed at the first URL in the PDF, and an external link after an internal one became a bookmark jump. Double strike also drew single after a struck run. The key is now the whole resolved format.

**3. PDF and No Markup leave tracked deletions out** (`layout`, `pdf`). PDF export defaults to no markup but laid out every deleted run and only switched off the strike, so `Keep ~~DELETED~~ INSERTED` printed "Keep DELETED INSERTED": neither the original nor the final text, and a leak of removed wording. The No Markup view …

title: Find/Replace skips text deleted under Track Changes (#89); a failed command keeps undo history
author: goldsbd
body:
Fixes #89.

Two engine bugs: Find/Replace matched text deleted under Track Changes, and a failed command threw away redo history. Each commit has a regression test that fails before its fix.

**1. Find/Replace reads the document as it now reads** (`cmd/edit.rs`). With Track Changes on, Replace marks the match deleted and leaves it in the paragraph, so the next Replace found the same deleted word again. Four Replaces on "one cat two cat" gave `one dogdogdogdog two cat`, and `remaining` never dropped.
- `search` (Find, Find Next/Previous, Replace, its `remaining` count, Replace All) now builds each paragraph without deleted runs and searches each stretch of live text separately with `regex_automata::Input::range`.
- As a result, "aaa" with the first "a" deleted matches "aa", and a deletion neither creates nor hides a `\b` / `^` / `$` boundary.
- `regex::Regex` can't bound a search's end without slicing (the slice end would become a word boundary). regex-automata is the engine `regex` already uses (0.4.18, already in the lockfile), so this adds a direct dependency but no new code to build.
- This complements #92: once Replace All is tracked, it uses the same `search`, so without this change a second Replace All would match its own deletions.

**2. A failed command keeps the undo and redo history** (`session.rs`). `run` checkpoints a mutating command first, and the checkpoint clears redo (and at the limit drops the oldest step). When the command then failed, the redo stack stayed cleared. For example: insert, Undo, then `text.insert {}` meant the undone work was gone for good. Nested commands (`file.inspect` runs `review.*`) could also evict steps the rollback never saw.
- Undo steps are now `Arc<Undo>`, and `run` snapshots both stacks before a mutating command and restores them exactly on failure. That costs one pointer per step, beside the two document clones each mutating command already makes.
- A top-level Undo still moves its document out without cloning.

**Verif…

title: Import: HTML without </head> keeps its body; RTF pictures inside \shppict are kept
author: goldsbd
body:
Two import bugs that lost content without an error. Each commit has a regression test that fails before its fix.

**1. HTML without `</head>` imports its body** (`formats/html.rs`). `</head>` is optional in HTML5, but a file that omits it imported as an empty document: the body was read as part of the head. A body-content start tag now closes an open head implicitly. Head metadata and the title are still captured.

**2. RTF pictures inside `\shppict` are kept** (`formats/rtf.rs`). Word writes pictures as `{\*\shppict{\pict…}}{\nonshppict…}`. `shppict` was an unknown `\*` destination, so the `\pict` inside it inherited Skip and the picture was dropped. A bare `\pict`, as LibreOffice writes it, already worked. `shppict` is now transparent, and `nonshppict` (the legacy duplicate) is still skipped.

**Verification**
- `cargo xtask ci` on this branch alone: all 6 steps pass (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm), 299 tests.
- `wordcraft-cli convert` of a `</head>`-less HTML file gives "Hello world" / "Second" (main: empty).
- A Word-style RTF picture converted to .docx carries 1 media part (main: 0). Opened in Word for Mac, Word's own PDF of the result shows the picture.

These two fixes were written by Codex (GPT) and reviewed and tested by me before committing.

title: Vendor winit 0.30.13 with the Windows 11 DPI fix
author: cyfung1031
body:
Target: WordCraft

Source: [PdfCraft #544](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/544), carrying the upstream winit [#4341](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4341) DPI fix.

Problem: WordCraft's clean `main` resolved winit 0.30.13 from crates.io and had no vendored patch, leaving Windows 11 fractional scaling vulnerable to incorrect physical window sizing.

Change: Vendor winit 0.30.13, apply the DPI backport, wire Cargo to the local copy, and add a target-specific provenance and structural regression check.

Validation: `cargo metadata --no-deps`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and the standalone DPI structural test passed. Full workspace builds, clippy, `cargo xtask ci`, and live platform testing were not run because of the local disk/platform constraint.

This branch is the prerequisite for the later winit PRs in this series.

title: Fix winit Wayland text input capability changes
author: cyfung1031

title: Fix winit Windows IME caret placement
author: cyfung1031
body:
Target: WordCraft

title: Envelopes, Labels, Finish & Merge: ask to save changes first (depends on #151)
author: goldsbd
body:
**Depends on #151** (the Save Changes prompt). This branch is #151 plus one commit, so please review only the last commit: "Envelopes, Labels, Finish & Merge: ask to save changes first".

Envelopes, Labels and Finish & Merge replaced the open document and wiped undo, with no prompt. On a document with unsaved work, that work was gone for good. `cmd/mailings.rs` builds a fresh `Document` and calls `set_document`, which resets history.

**Behaviour now, as in Word, where these commands produce a new document:**
- **In the app** (`WordApp::run`), the three commands on a document with unsaved changes ask "Do you want to save changes to <name>?" first. They use #151's prompt and pending-command mechanism unchanged.
- **A clean document** is replaced without asking.
- **Finish & Merge with a file `path`** writes the file and replaces nothing, so it never asks.
- **Scripts and agents** (`WordApp::execute`, control channel, MCP, CLI) never prompt.
- **The result is untitled,** with a new `document_id` and no path. Save goes through Save As, so it can't write over the original, and AutoSave doesn't cover it until it's saved.
- **Undo history is reset, as with New.** I first kept Undo across the replacement. An adversarial review showed that lets Redo attach the envelope to a file saved after Undo (Envelopes → Undo → Save As → Redo → Save wrote the envelope over that file). It also let a pending prompt about one document discard the other. Tracking which file each undo step belongs to is a lot of machinery for something Word doesn't offer either, so this is the simple version.

**Tests** (failing first, then passing):
- `engine tests::mailings_results_are_new_untitled_documents`
- `ui-egui tests::mailings_ask_before_replacing_unsaved_work`
- `programmatic_mailings_never_prompt`
- `mailings_results_never_save_over_the_original`
- `mailings_on_a_clean_document_or_into_a_file_do_not_ask` (a guard)

title: DOCX: keep a .docm's macros and signatures on save; right content types for .docm/.dotx/.dotm
author: goldsbd
body:
Saving a `.docm` deleted its macros, and `.docm`, `.dotx` and `.dotm` were all written with the plain-`.docx` content type, which Word rejects under those names. Each commit has a regression test that fails before its fix.

**1. The right package for each extension** (`docx/write`, `engine/io_ext.rs`). `io_ext.rs` sent `docx | docm | dotx` to `wordcraft_docx::write`, which always writes a `.docx` package, and `.dotm` couldn't be saved at all.
- A `Flavor` enum and `write_as(doc, flavor)` set the main content type: `.docx`, `.docm` (`macroEnabled.main`), `.dotx` (`template.main`) and `.dotm` (`macroEnabledTemplate.main`).
- `.dotm` is added to the open and save lists and to the desktop and web open dialogs.

**2. Macros survive a round trip** (`docx/read`, `docx/write`). The reader's existing `Document::passthrough` now keeps `word/vbaProject.bin` and every part `vbaProject.bin.rels` points to: `vbaData.xml`, the VBA signatures (legacy, Agile, V3) and anything else.
- Parts are kept as opaque bytes, with their relationship type and source content type. They are never parsed or run.
- Only the `.rels` part is read.
- `.docm`/`.dotm` write them back byte-for-byte. `.docx`/`.dotx` drop the whole set cleanly, with no dangling relationships.
- Bounded at 64 related parts. Targets outside `word/`, `.rels` parts and parts the writer produces itself are skipped, so a hostile relationship can't shadow them.
- `word/` is matched case-insensitively, as OPC requires. A part name whose first segment contains `:` is written as `./name`, so it can't parse as a URI scheme.

**3. UTF-16 XML parts** (`docx/xml.rs`). `xml::parse` rejected any part with a UTF-16 BOM, and `Package::rels` treated that error as "no relationships". So a UTF-16 `vbaProject.bin.rels` silently lost `vbaData.xml`.
- UTF-16 LE/BE is now transcoded to UTF-8 in the one shared place, so every part benefits. The conversion is bounded and lossy (U+FFFD), and never panics.
- An unreadable relationships part is logged …

title: Hidden text: no line breaks, hyphens, wrap areas or bookmark text from text that isn't shown (builds on #152)
author: goldsbd
body:
**Builds on #152** (tracked deletions left out of the final text). This branch is #152 plus the commits below, so please review only those.

Hidden text (`w:vanish`, directly or through a style) had the same gaps #152 closed for deletions. When hidden text isn't shown (the default, and always in PDF export), it was left off the page, but it still affected layout and the PDF structure. I measured each case in Word for Mac first and matched it.

**1. Line breaks and hyphenation.** A hidden soft hyphen or space still let the line break there. Word's results: hidden SHY → "xx" / "abcdef"; hidden space → "xx" / "abcdef".
- Break opportunities (UAX #14) and hyphenation points are now computed on the laid-out text and mapped back to paragraph offsets.
- A hidden space between "inter" and "national" now hyphenates as "inter-national", exactly as Word does (5 cases compared line for line with Word's PDF).

**2. Floating objects.** A float anchored in hidden text wasn't drawn, but its wrap area still pushed text aside (153 pt in the test). Word gives full-width text, and so does WordCraft now. The anchor's formatting is resolved through styles.

**3. Footnotes with a hidden reference mark.** Word still numbers them and still prints the note. WordCraft numbered them correctly but dropped the footnote text; it's now printed. (For deleted references, #152's behaviour is unchanged: no number and no note.)

**4. PDF bookmarks and heading tags.** These are built from what the layout actually left out (`ParaLayout::left_out`), including hidden text that comes from a table style's conditional formatting. They can't disagree with the page. Outline before: 'Intro SECRET Part', 'GONE', 'Last'. After: 'Intro Part', 'Last'. Word's AppleScript PDF export writes no outline, so this follows the pages, as #152 does for deletions.

One rule, `para::left_out(rc, show_hidden, hide_deleted)`, drives all four.

title: Zoom the page with Ctrl+scroll and pinch (#139)
author: Geljic
body:
Fixes #139.

The document canvas never read egui's zoom delta, so Ctrl/Cmd + mouse wheel (and trackpad pinch) did nothing over the page. egui already turns Ctrl+wheel into a smoothed zoom factor and suppresses scrolling for it, so the canvas only has to apply it.

**Change** (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, 7 lines): when the pointer is over the canvas and `zoom_delta() != 1`, run `view.zoom` with the current shown scale × delta, clamped to 10–500%. Starting from the shown scale (not `view.zoom`) means fit modes like Page Width zoom from where they are, the same way the status-bar slider works. Ribbon and panes are unaffected.

GridCraft and DeckCraft already zoom this way; this brings WordCraft in line.

**Test:** `tests::ctrl_wheel_over_canvas_zooms` in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` sends Ctrl+wheel up then down over the canvas and checks the scale rises then falls. It fails on `main` (scale stays at 1.333) and passes with the fix.

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` ✓
- `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` ✓
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui` ✓ (25 passed)

I didn't run the full `cargo xtask ci` (wasm etc.); the change only uses plain egui input APIs.

title: Desktop: send the window title only when it changes, so an idle app stops redrawing (#117)
author: g1obalworlds
body:
Fixes #117.

`WordApp::ui` sent `ViewportCommand::Title` at the end of every frame. egui's `send_viewport_cmd_to` calls `request_repaint_of` for every command, so each frame scheduled the next one and the app never went idle (about 180 commits per second and 14% CPU on an empty document, per the issue).

It now remembers the last title it sent and sends a new one only when the text changes. The title still follows renames, saves and the dirty marker.

**Test:** `window_title_is_sent_only_when_it_changes` runs full frames and counts `Title` commands: one on the first full frame, none on the following frames, and one more after the dirty flag changes. It fails without the fix (the title is sent twice instead of once).

**Checked:** `cargo fmt`, `cargo test --workspace` (298 passed), `cargo xtask assets`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm` all pass. I could only get a 1.95 toolchain, not the pinned 1.90, so clippy on the whole workspace stops at four lints that 1.95 added in files this PR doesn't touch (`collapsible_match` in `xtask/src/layers.rs`, `odt.rs`, `rtf.rs`, `nonminimal_bool` in `layout/src/hit.rs`); with those allowed it is clean. Please let CI confirm `cargo xtask ci` on 1.90.

Other repaints that remain are intentional and not per frame: caret blink and the 1 s autosave tick.

title: Lists: Enter and Backspace leave a list with its indent, and Enter works afterwards (#95)
author: g1obalworlds
body:
Fixes #95.

**Cause.** Applying Bullets or Numbering gives the paragraph the List Paragraph style, which has a 0.5" left indent. Enter on an empty item and Backspace at the start of one only cleared the numbering, so the paragraph kept that style and its indent: the bullet went but the text stayed in the list's margin. On top of that, the paragraph left behind has `numbering = {num: 0}`, and `split_para` treated any `Some(numbering)` as a list item, so pressing Enter on it did nothing ("enter gets stuck").

**Change**
- New shared `leave_list` helper (numbering off, list indent cleared, List Paragraph style dropped). Enter on an empty item and the Bullets/Numbering toggle-off use it; the toggle behaves exactly as before.
- `split_para` only treats an empty paragraph as a list item when its list number is not 0, so Enter works again after leaving a list.
- Backspace at the start of an item is two steps, as in Word: the first removes the bullet or number and keeps the paragraph's indent, the next removes the list's indent.

**Test:** `leaving_a_list_removes_its_indent` covers Enter (indent 36 then 0, a third Enter adds a paragraph) and the two-step Backspace. It fails without the fix, and I checked that it also fails if either half is reverted on its own.

**Checked:** `cargo fmt`, `cargo test --workspace` (298 passed, including `hostile_params_never_panic`), `cargo xtask assets`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm` pass. I could only get a 1.95 toolchain, not the pinned 1.90, so clippy on the whole workspace stops at five lints that 1.95 added in code this PR doesn't touch; with those allowed it is clean. Please let CI confirm `cargo xtask ci` on 1.90.

**Not in this PR** (existing behaviour, each deserves its own change): lists numbered only through a style such as Word's "List Bullet" still can't be left with Enter or Backspace; Enter on an empty nested item leaves the whole list rather than moving up one level; and the List Paragraph style is recognised by it…

title: macOS: open documents from Finder (double-click / Open With)
author: gledguri
body:
Fixes #27.

## The problem
Double-clicking a document in Finder, or using Open With, didn't open it. macOS delivers these as an Apple Event ("open documents"), not as command-line arguments, and nothing was listening for that event.

## The fix
- New crate `crates/macos-open` installs a handler for the open-documents Apple Event and passes the paths to the app (it also covers dropping a file on the Dock icon; on other platforms every function is a no-op).
- If the window holds an untouched blank document, the file opens there; otherwise it opens in a new WordCraft window, so unsaved work is never replaced.

## ⚠️ One thing to decide: `unsafe`
Defining and registering the Objective-C handler needs `unsafe` (objc2's class definition and messages), which the workspace forbids. This PR allows it **only in `crates/macos-open`** (a crate-level lint override, with a comment explaining why); every other crate still has `unsafe_code = "forbid"`. Happy to change approach if you'd prefer something else, for example if a winit/eframe version exposes this event safely.

## Testing

title: Typing parity with Word: lists, AutoFormat and AutoCorrect as you type
author: echelon
body:
Typed the same keystrokes into Word and WordCraft side by side (results read back paragraph by paragraph) and fixed every difference found.

## The "stuck Enter" bug
Leaving a list marked the paragraph `num: 0` ("not in a list") but kept the List Paragraph style. Enter's empty-list check treated that marker as a list item, so every further Enter re-ran "leave the list" and did nothing, and the list indent stuck to every paragraph typed afterwards. Nested lists hit it too.

## Now matching Word
- **Lists:** two Enters end a list and the next paragraph is Normal; more Enters add blank lines; an empty nested item moves up a level before leaving the list; Enter right after `* ` cancels the list.
- **Backspace** at an item's start: first removes the number, second removes the indent (no longer joins the paragraph above).
- **AutoFormat:** `1. ` always restarts at 1; `a. ` / `I. ` start lettered/roman lists; `- ` is a dash bullet; Enter after `---` `===` `***` `___` `~~~` `###` draws a bottom border on the paragraph above.
- **Undo** right after an AutoFormat/AutoCorrect change undoes only that change.
- **AutoCorrect:** sentence capitals (not after abbreviations/initials, not `iPhone` or `a.`), also on Enter; `word -- word` en dash, `wait...` → `…`, ½ ¼ ¾, ordinal superscripts, web addresses become links.
- **Layout:** no line break right after a slash (`and/or`, URLs), unless the word can't fit.

## Verification
- 30 short scenarios and a 3.8k-character mixed document match Word paragraph for paragraph (text, style, list level); the same document ×5 (~19k chars, 10 pages) matches 5× Word's result. Incremental layout stayed under 0.5 ms per keystroke.
- New regression tests in `crates/engine/src/tests_typing.rs` (built from Word's results), plus a layout test confirmed to fail without its fix. Three existing tests updated for the Word behaviour.

title: web: print straight to the system print dialog, not just export
author: Dejan-Port
body:
## What

The web build's Print backstage page (opened via Ctrl+P / Mod+P → `file.print`) only lets you save a copy in another format — there's no way to actually send the document to a printer short of exporting a PDF and opening it yourself. This adds a dedicated **Print** button that exports to PDF in memory and opens it in a hidden iframe, then calls the iframe's own `print()` once it has loaded — the standard way to drive the browser's native print dialog on a PDF without a download or a popup window the browser might block.

## How

- `ui-egui`: new `Services::print` hook (`Option<Box<dyn Fn(&[u8])>>`) — web: hand PDF bytes to the browser's print flow directly, no download.
- `ui-egui` backstage: "Print" button on the Print page, shown only when the host implements the hook. Goes through `wordcraft_engine::io::save_bytes` directly (not the existing save/download command path) since this wants raw bytes in memory, not a file write — avoids reusing the download-interception machinery in `lib.rs` for something that explicitly shouldn't download.
- `wordcraft-web`: implements the hook — `Blob` → object URL → hidden `<iframe>` → `iframe.contentWindow.print()` on `onload`. Added `HtmlIFrameElement` to the `web-sys` feature list.

Desktop builds are unaffected — no `Services::print` is set there, so the button doesn't render; `file.print` still just opens the Print page as before.

- `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p wordcraft-web` — clean.

title: Export: PDF, PNG and TXT downloads keep the document marked as edited (#168)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #168.

On the web, `file.save`, `file.saveAs`, `file.exportPdf` and `file.exportPng` become browser downloads in `WordApp::run` (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`). That branch set `session.dirty = false` after every download, so exporting a PDF, PNG or plain-text copy cleared the Edited indicator even though the editable document was not saved.

The download branch now clears `dirty` only when the file name has an editable extension (`docx`, `docm`, `dotx`, `dotm`, `odt`, `rtf`, `json`). This is the same list the engine's `file.save` already uses on desktop (`crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs`), so the web and native builds now behave the same. The desktop path was already correct and is unchanged. The other lossy Export formats (HTML, Markdown, LaTeX) follow the same rule.

Test: `lossy_downloads_keep_the_document_dirty` runs the command ids the Backstage Export page uses (`file.saveAs` for TXT and PDF, `file.exportPng` for PNG) and `file.exportPdf` with a download service installed. It checks that each export succeeds and leaves the document dirty, and that a `.docx` save still clears it. Without the fix the TXT, PDF and PNG cases end with `dirty == false`.

title: Use the browser clock for comment and tracked-change dates on the web
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
In the browser build, new comments and tracked changes were stamped 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z whatever the real time. `now_iso()` in the engine had a wasm32 branch that returned that fixed string, because `SystemTime::now()` panics on wasm32-unknown-unknown.

The wasm branch now reads the browser clock with `js_sys::Date::now()`. `js-sys` becomes a wasm32-only dependency of the engine. It's the same crate and version the web app already uses, so Cargo.lock gets no new package. A clock hook registered by the web app was the other option, but the engine has no host-hook mechanism and the repo already handles wasm differences with target-specific dependencies. The output format is unchanged: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, whole seconds.

The formatting moved into a pure `iso_from_unix_secs`, shared by both targets, with unit tests for the epoch, a known timestamp, two leap days (2000 and 2024) and the last second of 2024.

Not verified: the wasm branch itself only gets compile-checked by the wasm step of `cargo xtask ci`. I did not run the web build in a browser, so I haven't seen a real date on a new comment or tracked insertion there. `cargo xtask ci` passes. One earlier run failed `layout::lines_with_tabs_never_shrink`; it passed on re-run and on main, so it looks flaky.

Fixes #188.

title: Linux: default to XWayland for file drag-and-drop on Wayland desktops
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Rationale & History

Under Wayland sessions, dragging and dropping text documents or media from desktop file managers onto WordCraft showed a "no" (prohibited) cursor and drops did not arrive.

This occurs because `eframe 0.36.2` depends on `winit 0.30.13`. In `winit 0.30`, Wayland drag-and-drop was not implemented ([winit#1881](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/issues/1881)). Native Wayland drag-and-drop was added for `winit 0.31` in [winit#4571](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4571) (merged July 2026, tagged in `0.31.0-beta.3`). However, updating to `winit 0.31` directly is blocked by breaking event loop API changes until upstream `eframe` adds support.

On X11 / XWayland, drag-and-drop is fully supported in `winit 0.30`. This pull request adopts the established pattern from `designcraft` and `deckcraft` by Brandon Thomas:
1. Adds `winit = { version = "0.30", default-features = false, features = ["x11"] }` under `cfg(all(unix, not(target_os = "macos")))`.
2. Adds an event loop builder hook before running the native event loop: when an X server is reachable (`DISPLAY` is set) and `WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND` is not set, configures `EventLoopBuilderExtX11::with_x11()` to route through XWayland so file drops work out of the box on standard Wayland desktop sessions.
3. Allows users desiring pure native Wayland to opt out and preserve the native Wayland backend by setting `WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND=1`.

### Verification
Verified local compilation and dependency resolution with `cargo check -p wordcraft` on Linux (0 errors, 0 warnings).

title: Shift+F3 runs Change Case again, not Find Previous (#186)
author: vangel76
body:
## What
Shift+F3 now cycles Change Case (lower → UPPER → Title), as in Word.

## Why it broke
`edit.findPrevious` (`Mod+Shift+G / Shift+F3`) and `format.changeCase` (`Shift+F3`) shared a key. `Registry::by_shortcut` returns the first match, and edit commands register before format commands, so Shift+F3 always ran Find Previous.

title: macOS: open documents from Finder, the Dock and `open -a` (#27)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #27.

## Problem
Double-clicking a document in Finder, Open With, dropping a file on the Dock icon and `open -a WordCraft letter.docx` don't open the document; Finder reports "WordCraft cannot open files in the Word Document format". File > Open and drag-and-drop onto the window work.

## Cause
LaunchServices doesn't pass these paths on the command line. It sends the app a `kAEOpenDocuments` ('odoc') Apple event, and winit 0.30 doesn't handle it.

## Fix
This uses the approach PdfCraft and PhotoCraft already ship: the audited [`fmv-macos-events`](https://crates.io/crates/fmv-macos-events) crate, pinned to `=0.1.0`.
- It registers an `NSAppleEventManager` handler before Finder's launch event and leaves winit's delegate alone.
- The Objective-C interop stays inside that crate, so the workspace keeps `unsafe_code = "forbid"` and needs no new crate or layering exception.
- `apps/wordcraft/src/apple_events.rs` drains the queue each frame. Each path goes through `WordApp::run("file.open")`, the same as File > Open, so unsaved changes are asked about first.
- A quit event closes the window, which asks the same through `close_requested`.
- The registration lives in `main()` until the event loop returns, so the event that launched the app is caught too.
- The plist already declares the document types, so only the handler was missing.

#33, #107 and #192 fix the same issue by adding a `crates/macos-open` crate with its own `unsafe` Objective-C code. This PR is the alternative that keeps the code safe and matches the sibling apps (and the matching PRs for GridCraft, DeckCraft, FilmCraft and EffectCraft). Merge whichever fits best.

## Testing
Tested on macOS (Apple silicon) with a full `packaging/macos/package.sh` build installed in /Applications:
- [x] `open -a WordCraft letter.docx` with the app not running: the document opens.
- [x] Opening another document from Finder while the current one has unsaved edits shows the "Save changes?" prompt and keeps the document.

title: Headless: name the author of tracked changes, and list review.trackChanges' value param

title: Web: use the browser clock everywhere on wasm (follow-up to #214)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Follow-up to #214, refs #188. #214 gave `now_iso` the browser's clock on wasm, but the other clock helpers were still stubs in the browser:

- **Insert › Date & Time**: the weekday was always Thursday (`crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs`).
- **PDF export**: the creation date was left out (`crates/pdf`).
- **Layout and UI millisecond clocks** returned 0 (`crates/layout`, `crates/ui-egui`), so browser AutoSave's timer never fired, the caret didn't blink and status messages never cleared.

## Change
- The engine's clock is one `now_unix()` in `cmd/mod.rs` (std on native, `js_sys::Date::now()` in the browser, exactly as #214 does) that `now_iso` and the weekday share; `iso_from_unix_secs` is now `pub`.
- The pdf, layout and ui-egui clocks read `js_sys::Date` the same way on wasm (`js-sys` as a wasm-only dependency, already in the lockfile via #214). No new clock crate.

## Verification

title: Font picker: build only the visible rows, cache font fallbacks (#121, #59)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #121 and #59. Probably also #118 (same symptom: the app locks up when changing the font).

## Font menu freeze (#121)
Opening the font menu built a row, and so rendered a preview, for every installed family. Each preview loads that family's font files, so the menu kept repainting until every font on the system was read into memory (1.1 GB for 305 families here; far more on large collections). The combo list (`widgets.rs` `combo_list`) now uses `ScrollArea::show_rows`, so only the rows in view are built.

## Thai text slowing down (#59)
Layout asks `FontDb` for a fallback face once per character the font lacks, and each lookup sorted every loaded face, so text in a script the font lacks got slower with every font loaded. Fallback lookups are now cached per (character, excluded face) until more faces load (faces are only ever appended), capped at 20k entries and cleared when the system-fallback setting changes. Bold/italic selection from #207 still runs per call, after the cached base lookup. 5000 Thai characters now lay out in 5 ms instead of 96 ms with all fonts loaded.

title: Font list offers every installed weight (Light, Medium, SemiBold, Black…), as Word does
author: vangel76
body:
## Cause
The font database listed and matched fonts only by their typographic family name (OpenType `name` ID 16, e.g. "Roboto"). Word addresses faces other than Regular, Bold and Italic by their own family name ("Roboto Light", "Segoe UI Semibold": `name` ID 1, with ID 2 holding only Regular/Bold/Italic). So those weights never appeared in WordCraft's font list, and a document using "Roboto Light" resolved to a substitute font.

## Change (`crates/fonts`)
- Each face carries a `legacy_family` name: name ID 1 for static fonts, or for a variable font's named instances the family plus the style words other than Regular/Bold/Italic ("Inter" + "Light Italic" → "Inter Light").
- `FontDb::families()` (the font list in the ribbon and mini toolbar) includes these names. `has_family`, `face` and `styles` resolve them: the typographic family is matched first, then the legacy name. Bold and italic still choose a face, or synthesise one, within the faces that name covers.
- Asking for a legacy name loads the whole installed typographic family, so a family never ends up loaded with only some of its styles.
- The system font scan reads `fvar` as well as `name` (both size-capped), so a variable font's named instances are listed before the font is loaded.
- Nothing changes in how docx stores fonts: the run's `w:rFonts` name is the face's family name, as Word writes it.

## Testing
- New tests: legacy-name derivation on synthetic names; resolution on the bundled fonts, which include real name-ID-1 faces ("Inter Medium", "Source Serif 4 Semibold"); a scanned and renamed Semibold font found by its legacy name, loading its whole family; `word::resolve("Inter Medium", bold, italic)`; and a scan-vs-load consistency check for an installed variable font, which is skipped when no such font is installed.
- Ran `cargo test -p wordcraft-fonts`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-fonts --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets` and `cargo xtask wasm`. I…

title: DOCX: absolutely positioned VML text boxes float instead of pushing the body down (#149)
author: vangel76
body:
## Cause
`read_vml` in `crates/docx/src/read/story.rs` only read `width`/`height` from a VML shape's `style` and always gave the shape `Float::default()`, i.e. inline. An absolutely positioned text box in a header (`position:absolute`, `w10:wrap type="none"`) therefore sat inline in the header's flow, so its full height went into the header height and the body started near the bottom of the page.

## Change
VML shapes (`v:shape`, `v:rect`, … text boxes and `v:imagedata` pictures) with `position:absolute` now get the same float model as DrawingML `wp:anchor` objects (per the VML part of ECMA-376, Part 4):
- offsets from `left` + `margin-left` and `top` + `margin-top`
- reference areas from `mso-position-horizontal-relative` / `mso-position-vertical-relative` (`page`, `margin`, `text`, `char`, `line`, the `*-margin-area` values); without them, column and paragraph
- alignment from `mso-position-horizontal` / `mso-position-vertical` (`absolute` keeps the offset)
- wrapping from `w10:wrap` (`square`, `tight`, `through`, `topAndBottom`); `none` or no `w10:wrap` puts it in front of the text, or behind the text when `z-index` is negative
- `mso-wrap-distance-*` become the wrap distances

Shapes without `position:absolute` stay inline, as before. Values are clamped, so hostile style strings stay finite. Layout already keeps floating header objects out of the header height, so nothing changed there. On save, the boxes are written as DrawingML anchors with the same placement, and their text is kept.

## Testing
- New docx test `absolute_vml_text_box_in_header_floats`: builds the issue's header VML box (plus a square-wrapped, margin-centred box, a box with no `w10:wrap`, and an inline one) and checks wrap, reference areas, offset (0, 80 pt), size (405 × 491.4 pt) and the box's text. It also checks that all of this survives a write and read-back.
- New docx test `hostile_vml_style_values_stay_finite`: checks that out-of-range or garbage style values stay finite.
- New layout te…

title: Reject All removes paragraph breaks inserted with Track Changes on
author: vangel76
body:
## Cause

With Track Changes on, Enter (`text.newParagraph`) already recorded the new paragraph mark as a tracked insertion (`Paragraph::mark.ins`). But accept/reject only cleared that flag, whichever way it went, so Reject All left the two paragraphs split (`Owned ALPHA ` / `Owned BETA`). Paragraph marks also didn't appear in `review.changes` or Next/Previous Change. The DOCX writer and reader dropped them too.

## Change

- **Accept/Reject**: rejecting an inserted paragraph mark, or accepting a deleted one, joins the paragraph with the next one again. The joined paragraph keeps the first paragraph's properties, so a split heading comes back as a heading. The other outcome just clears the revision. A story's or cell's last mark can't be removed, so it only stops being a revision. This works for Accept All / Reject All, Accept / Reject at the caret (caret just before a tracked mark) or over a selection that goes past the mark, Next/Previous Change and the Reviewing Pane (`review.changes` lists the mark as an insert/delete by its author).
- **Tracked deletion of a paragraph break** (the symmetric case uses the same mechanism):
  - Backspace at a paragraph start or Delete at a paragraph end with tracking on now marks the mark deleted (`mark.del`). Before, it only moved the caret.
  - A mark the same author inserted is removed outright, like their own inserted text.
  - Tracked deletions that span paragraphs mark the marks between them too.
  - Delete steps the caret over a deleted mark, so pressing it again moves on.
- **DOCX**: reads and writes `w:ins` / `w:del` in the paragraph mark's `w:rPr` (ECMA-376 §17.13.5.16 / §17.13.5.15), alongside any mark formatting.
- **Display**: with formatting marks shown, a tracked ¶ is drawn in its author's revision colour. `Draw::Mark` gains an optional `color`.
- `docs/typing-parity.md` gets a Track Changes section.

Not in this PR: with "No Markup", a deleted paragraph mark doesn't yet show the two paragraphs as one. They join onl…

title: Table Layout › Text Direction turns the cell's text (#226)
author: vangel76
body:
## Cause
`table.textDirection` flipped a `vertical_text` flag on the cell, but layout and rendering never read that flag, so the button had no visible effect. The command also didn't invalidate the cell's cached layout, it only changed the caret's cell (not the selected cells), and docx always wrote the flag as `btLr`. The screenshot in the issue shows left-to-right Cyrillic text with several cells selected, so this is about rotating text, not right-to-left text (#207).

## Change
- **Model:** `CellProps::text_direction` is now `Horizontal | Down (tbRl) | Up (btLr)`. It maps to and from every `ST_TextDirection` value, both transitional and strict names (ECMA-376 §17.4.72).
- **Command:** `table.textDirection` cycles horizontal → top-to-bottom → bottom-to-top, like Word's button. The new direction goes to every selected cell. It takes an optional `{"value": "horizontal|down|up"}` and is disabled outside a table.
- **Layout:** turned cell text is laid out with the row height as its line length:
  - An exact row height sets the line length, so text wraps at it.
  - Otherwise the row grows to fit the unwrapped text (capped at a page body's height).
  - When the row ends up taller, the text is laid out again from the same list and equation counters.

  Lines stack from the cell's starting edge: the right edge for top-to-bottom, the left edge for bottom-to-top. Vertical alignment moves the lines across the cell. A turned row moves to the next page whole instead of splitting.
- **Drawing:** `Placed::Lines` carries a `turn`, and a new `Draw::Turned` draws its items in a rotated frame. The raster renderer and the PDF exporter both handle it, and the PDF keeps the text extractable.
- **Editing:** clicks, the caret and selection highlights follow the rotation. In turned text `Caret` gains a `width` and lies across the page; the canvas draws it that way.
- **docx:** reads and writes `w:textDirection` with `tbRl` / `btLr`. Horizontal cells write nothing.

title: File dialogs (Open, Save As, Export) no longer freeze the window on Linux (#94)
author: vangel76
body:
## Cause
The desktop app showed Open, Save As, Export and Insert/Change Picture with rfd's blocking `FileDialog`, called on the UI thread from inside the egui frame, with no parent window. On Linux the xdg-desktop-portal backend blocks on D-Bus until the dialog closes, so the event loop stopped. Because the dialog had no parent, GNOME/Mutter could open it behind the (often maximized) WordCraft window, which then looked frozen.

## Change
- **Desktop (`apps/wordcraft/src/file_dialogs.rs`)**: dialogs are now `rfd::AsyncFileDialog`, parented to the window with `set_parent(frame)`. `eframe::Frame` implements the raw-window-handle traits, so no unsafe is needed. The app queues a request, the eframe frame builds the dialog after the pass, and a background thread waits for the answer (`pollster`, already in Cargo.lock through rfd). It sends the path back through a channel and wakes the UI with `request_repaint`. The event loop keeps running the whole time.
- **ui-egui (`crates/ui-egui/src/file_dialogs.rs`)**: a new backend-agnostic hook, `Services::file_dialog(FileDialogRequest) -> Receiver<Option<String>>`. The app remembers what each dialog was for and finishes the job when the answer arrives (`logic` polls every frame):
  - Open opens the picked file.
  - Save As saves.
  - Export writes the copy.
  - Insert/Change Picture inserts or replaces the picture.
  - The AutoSave switch turns AutoSave on once the save has finished.
  - Hosts that only set the blocking `pick_open`/`pick_save` (used by tests) get the same follow-up straight away. The web build's `open_async`/inbox path is unchanged.
- **"Save changes?" → Save on a new document**: the held-back New/Open/Close now runs only after the later Save As has actually saved. It still checks that the format keeps everything and that the document wasn't replaced in the meantime. A cancelled Save As cancels the command and keeps the document.
- **One dialog at a time**: while a file dialog is open, more Save As/Open/Export/Pi…

title: Select Recipients lets you type a list or pick a CSV, instead of a parameters error
author: vangel76
body:
## Cause
The Mailings › Select Recipients button ran `mailings.recipients` with no parameters. The command needs `csv`, `path` or `rows`, so a click only put "`csv`, `path` or `rows` required" in the status bar. No dialog or file picker opened. Edit Recipient List, Insert Merge Field and Find Recipient had the same gap: with no input they failed (Insert Merge Field, Find Recipient) or did nothing you could see (Edit Recipient List).

## Change
- **Select Recipients is now a menu** with two items:
  - **Type a New List…** opens a new *Recipient List* dialog. It is an editable table of field names and entries, with New Entry, Add Field and × buttons to remove rows or fields, plus OK/Cancel.
  - **Use an Existing List…** opens the file picker for a CSV, TSV or text file (new `ui.openRecipientList`). On desktop the file loads by path. On the web the picked file comes back through the inbox and loads as recipients rather than opening as a document. A `.csv` or `.tsv` dropped on the web page also loads as recipients.
- **A user-run command without the input it needs opens a dialog** (`WordApp::run` → `input_dialog`). This covers the ribbon, keytips and command search:

title: Chinese interface shows every character instead of boxes on Windows
author: vangel76
body:
## Cause

The release workflow checks out `storytold/craft-fonts` at a pinned commit, `abb8331`. That is the commit that added the Japanese fonts. `Noto Sans CJK SC` (and Noto Sans Arabic) came one commit later, in `8dcdacd` on 2026-10-06. At the pinned commit, `fonts/manifest.txt` has only the Japanese faces, so `build.rs` embedded those and nothing else. `CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED` did not catch this because it only fails when the checkout is missing or broken, not when a face is absent.

`ui_cjk_fonts(true)` therefore found no `Hans` face, and the Simplified Chinese interface fell back to BIZ UDPGothic. That face lacks about 157 simplified-only hanzi (页, 选, 删, 标 …), and egui drew them as boxes. Document text was unaffected because it goes through the system font fallback.

Embedding is not limited to TrueType: egui 0.36 rasterizes through skrifa, which handles the CFF (`OTTO`) outlines of the SC `.otf`. A new test checks this against an installed CFF collection (Noto Sans CJK, face index 2).

## Change

- **Pin:** bump craft-fonts to `8dcdacd5153e64560d109541a47d806f26f048c0` in `release.yml` (all jobs) and `freebsd.yml`. Release binaries grow by the SC face (16.4 MB) and Noto Sans Arabic. Web builds still embed only BIZ UDPGothic Regular.
- **Guard:** with `CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED`, a native build now fails if the manifest has no `Jpan` or no `Hans` font (`crates/fonts/build.rs`). An outdated pin can no longer ship without the Chinese face.
- **Fallback (desktop only, not wasm):** when no embedded face covers the interface language, `theme::font_definitions` adds an installed CJK font at the end of the UI families. "Covers" means a `Hans` face for a Chinese interface, or any CJK face for other languages, which still need one for the language names in Options. The new `wordcraft_fonts::system_cjk_ui_font`:
  - looks in the existing `system_font_dirs()` for a short list of files per platform:
    - Windows: `Deng.ttf`, `msyh.ttc`, `simhei.ttf`, `simsun.ttc`, `NotoSansSC-V…

title: Add a System interface theme that follows the OS light/dark appearance (#115)
author: vangel76
body:
## Change

- **Interface theme is now a three-way choice:** *Use system setting*, *Light* or *Dark*. It replaces the "Dark mode" checkbox in **File › Options › General** with an *Interface theme* combo box, and adds an **Interface Theme ▾** menu next to *Switch Modes* in **View › Dark Mode**.
- **System follows the OS appearance** that egui/eframe 0.36 reports (`Context::system_theme`): winit's theme on macOS, Windows and Linux, and `prefers-color-scheme` on the web. It applies at launch and switches live when the OS appearance changes, because eframe repaints on the change and the theme is resolved every frame. **When the OS reports no appearance, System falls back to Light.**
- **egui's own theme preference is now pinned to ours** (`ctx.set_theme` in `theme::apply`). Before this, egui was left on its default (follow the OS), so an OS appearance change while the app was running swapped in egui's other style, which had none of our styling.
- **Prefs migration:** an existing `ui.json` with `"dark": true` becomes Dark, and `false` becomes Light. The old key is read once and never written again. The new value is saved as `"theme": "system"|"light"|"dark"`. An unknown value reads as Light instead of discarding the whole file. An OS appearance change never rewrites the saved choice.
- **Default for new installs stays Light**, because the issue leaves the default to maintainers. Making System the default is a one-line change (`#[default]` on `Appearance`).
- **Commands:** the new `ui.theme` takes `{"value": "system"|"light"|"dark"}`, or no value to read it, and an unknown value is an error. `ui.dark` still works and sets Light or Dark. Documented in `docs/control-protocol.md`.

- **Translations:** the new strings are translated in all six catalogs, and the unused "Dark mode" entry is removed. The new ribbon icon is drawn in code.

title: i18n: add Serbian, both scripts (sr, sr-latn)
author: Dejan-Port
body:
## What

Adds Serbian as an interface language, in both scripts it's actually used in day to day — Cyrillic (`sr`, the default per BCP 47) and Latin (`sr-latn`) — the same way the catalog already splits Chinese by script rather than treating it as one language.

- `sr-latn.tsv`: the real translation, written clean-room from the plain meaning of each English label (never consulted or copied from Microsoft Word's or another product's Serbian localization). Covers the full existing catalog — same 874-entry key set as `zh-hans.tsv`.
- `sr.tsv`: mechanically transliterated from `sr-latn.tsv` (standard Serbian Latin→Cyrillic digraph-aware mapping). Brand/product/format names and `{placeholders}` are protected from transliteration, same as every other catalog already does for Latin brand names. The transliteration script itself isn't part of the PR (a one-off tool, not project infrastructure) — the intended workflow going forward is editing `sr-latn.tsv` and re-running it, not hand-editing `sr.tsv`.
- `mod.rs`: registers both. Turns out no special-casing is needed in `candidates()` for the script split (unlike Chinese's region-implies-script fallback): `sr-Latn-RS` already produces `sr-latn` as a candidate before falling back to plain `sr`, and a bare `sr`/`sr-RS` (the common case — most systems don't tag the script) resolves straight to `sr`, which is registered as the default-script code.
- `tests.rs`: locale-matching for both scripts, full-catalog key parity against the reference language, and bundled-font glyph coverage for Cyrillic and for Serbian Latin's extended letters (š č ć ž đ) — mirroring the existing Ukrainian and Brazilian Portuguese tests.

## Testing

`cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui` — 100 passed, including the 20 i18n tests (the existing ones plus 5 new Serbian-specific ones). Built and smoke-tested the web build with the language switched to both `sr` and `sr-latn` in Options.

body:
## Change

title: Touchpad scrolling follows your fingers and coasts after a flick; the mouse wheel scrolls further (#122)
author: vangel76
body:
## Cause
The document canvas used egui's built-in `ScrollArea` wheel handling:
- On Wayland, winit reports touchpad scrolling as pixel deltas with Start/End phases. egui ignores the delta carried by the Start event and clears the deltas of any frame that also holds the End event, so the first and last bits of each swipe were dropped.
- Wayland compositors don't send kinetic scrolling. GTK, Qt and browsers synthesise it after the fingers lift; we didn't, so a flick stopped dead.
- A mouse-wheel notch scrolled egui's default 40 px, less than most desktop apps (the Fedora comment).

## Change
- New `crates/ui-egui/src/scroll.rs`. The canvas `ScrollArea` no longer scrolls on the wheel (`ScrollSource { mouse_wheel: false }`); the canvas reads the wheel events itself and sets the offset before drawing, so a scroll shows up in the same frame.
- **Touchpad (point deltas):** move the page 1:1 with no smoothing.
- **Momentum:** a small pure `Momentum` helper (`feed(delta, dt)`, `release()`, `tick(dt)`, `cancel()`). It keeps a time-weighted velocity while the fingers move. When they lift (End phase, or a 50 ms pause on devices that never report a lift), it coasts with time-based exponential decay, so it behaves the same at any frame rate. Slow drags, or fingers that rest before lifting, don't fling. A click, key press, wheel notch or reaching the end of the document stops it. It asks for repaints only while coasting. It's turned on only on Linux/BSD: macOS sends its own momentum events, Windows reports touchpads as line deltas and adds its own inertia, and browsers handle it themselves.
- **Mouse wheel (line deltas):** a notch now scrolls 56 px at 100% (about three lines), scaled by √zoom and clamped to 0.75–2×, so zoomed-in views move more and zoomed-out ones don't crawl. Whole notches still ease in over about 0.1 s, on the same curve egui uses. Fractional line deltas (X11/Windows touchpads, free-spinning wheels) apply immediately. On the web, browser lines are a third of a n…

title: docs: fix subject-verb agreement in README.md
author: lunar-me
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a grammar issue in `README.md` (line 208).

## Problem

Subject-verb disagreement in the Downloads section. The compound sentence joins two independent clauses: the [latest release] ... has every build listed below, and [all releases] ... has earlier versions and their notes. The second subject, "all releases", is plural, so it requires the plural verb "have"; the singular "has" copied from the first clause is wrong.

The problematic text:

```markdown
[all releases](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/releases) has earlier versions
```

## Fix

Replaced with:

```markdown
[all releases](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/releases) have earlier versions
```

- [x] Documentation fix (grammar, spelling, logical error)

title: On macOS, the window buttons sit centred in the title bar and the File back button no longer crowds them
author: vangel76
body:
## Cause

On macOS the window has no system title bar (`with_fullsize_content_view`, `with_titlebar_shown(false)`), and AppKit draws the traffic lights itself, centred in its standard 28 pt title-bar band at the top of the window. WordCraft's own title bar was 38 pt tall, so the lights sat about 5 pt above its centre line (#225).

The Backstage (File) covers the whole window, title bar included. Its back button was a 40 pt row starting 12 pt from the top, so the chevron sat right under the red button, almost touching it (#222).

Neither winit 0.30.13 nor egui/eframe 0.36 offers a way to move the traffic lights, and doing it directly means AppKit calls (`unsafe`), which the workspace forbids. So the title bar now fits the lights, rather than the other way round.

macOS only (`integrated_titlebar`, which `main.rs` sets on macOS only). Linux and Windows layouts don't change.

- **Backstage:** the top 28 pt of the blue column is now a title bar. The back chevron sits beside the lights, centred with them, and starts at the same inset as the main title bar's AutoSave label. author: vangel76
body:
## Change

You can now make your own table styles (for thesis tables, say) and keep them in the document. Tools that look up table styles by name, such as pandoc, can then find them.

- **Table Design › Table Styles › Styles ▾ › New Table Style… / Modify Table Style…** opens one compact dialog with: name, style based on, and apply formatting to (whole table / header row / banded rows). For the region you pick, you can turn borders on or off, set a fill colour, make text bold and set a font colour. The colour pickers reuse the ribbon's colour grid. The dialog only sends what you changed, so everything else stays inherited from the base style. The new style is applied to the table at the caret and appears in the gallery. Gallery tiles now redraw when a style changes.
- **Engine:** `table.newStyle` and `table.modifyStyle` are documented `CommandSpec`s. Their params are `name`/`style`, `basedOn`, `wholeTable`/`headerRow`/`bandedRows` regions (`borders`, `borderColor`, `borderWidth`, `fill`, `bold`, `italic`, `color`, `size`, `font`), `bandSize`, `para` and `apply`. They never open dialogs. `table.style` now accepts only table styles. Both new ids are added to the parity catalog: 380/430, 88.4%.
- **Model and layout:** table styles gain header-row and row-band cell borders, row-band character formatting and rows per band (`tblStyleRowBandSize`). Table layout applies all of these through the existing style resolution path.
- **DOCX:** custom table styles are written as `w:style w:type="table"`. Each one carries `tblPr` (including `tblStyleRowBandSize`) and `tblStylePr` parts for `wholeTable`, `firstRow`, `band1Horz`, `firstCol` and `lastRow`, with `rPr` and `tcPr` (`tcBorders`, `shd`). The reader reads the new parts back, and tables refer to their style via `w:tblStyle`. The work follows ECMA-376 §17.7.6.

title: The desktop app tells you when a new WordCraft version is out (#201)
author: vangel76
body:
## Change

Issue #201: `.deb` users (and everyone else on the desktop) never hear about new releases. This adds a **notice only**. Nothing is downloaded or installed automatically.

- **Check:** at most once every 24 h and only after the first frame, a background thread sends one `GET https://api.github.com/repos/storytold/wordcraft/releases/latest` (User-Agent `WordCraft/<version> (update check; +repo URL)`, 15 s timeout, response capped at 256 KB).
- **Parsing treats the response as untrusted:** drafts and pre-releases are ignored. `tag_name` must look like `v1.2.3` / `1.2.3` / `1.2`, and anything else (junk, `-rc` tags, overflow) is skipped. The version is compared against `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` (the same source as `--version` and About). The Download link opens only if it is a `https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/releases/…` page; otherwise the releases list opens.
- **Notice:** a slim bar under the ribbon reads "WordCraft X.Y.Z is available." with three buttons. **Download** opens the release page in the browser (existing `open_url` path). **Skip this version** is remembered in `ui.json`. **Dismiss** hides it for this session.
- **Layering:** the HTTP client lives only in `apps/wordcraft` (`update_check.rs`), injected through a new `Services::check_update`. `ui-egui` (`update.rs`) holds the pure logic, the thread and the bar. The web build and tests get no fetcher, so they make no check and show no checkbox.
- UI strings are in all six interface catalogs.

## Privacy

No telemetry, no identifiers, no cookies. The only traffic is that one GET request (GitHub sees the IP address and User-Agent, as for any request). This is stated in the README's "Private" bullet.

## Opt-out

- **File › Options › Check for updates** (on by default, saved in preferences; shown only where a check is possible).

body:

title: Tests: layout and PDF tests no longer depend on the fonts installed on the machine; PDF text of field results keeps ligature letters
author: vangel76
body:
On a Linux machine with many system fonts (CachyOS: Carlito, Noto Naskh Arabic, Noto CJK…), four tests failed on unmodified `main`. One of them showed a real bug in PDF export. The other three only passed with particular fonts.

## `wordcraft-pdf`: `tests::field_results_are_extractable_text`: product bug, fixed
- **Symptom:** the PDF text layer read `"See Sectio  3.01 fir details3"`.
- **Cause:** a field result is laid out as one cluster of many glyphs. The display list then gave each glyph one character. Carlito, which stands in for Calibri when it is installed, joins "ti" into one ligature glyph. That glyph got only the "t", and every later glyph's text moved by one character. Any font with ligatures in a field result (REF, PAGE, cross-references…) produced wrong copy/paste and search text in the PDF. With bundled Source Sans 3 the test text has no ligature, so CI didn't see it.
- **Fix:** `Builder::shape_atomic` (crates/layout/src/para.rs) now records each glyph's byte range in the shown text while merging the shaped clusters. A ligature's glyph spans the letters of the clusters that have no glyph of their own, as for normal text. `ParaLayout::shown` carries these ranges, and `display.rs` uses them, falling back to the old one-character-per-glyph guess only if they are missing.
- **New regression test:** `field_result_ligatures_extract_all_their_letters` uses bundled Source Sans 3 ("fi", "ffi" ligatures), so it doesn't depend on system fonts. It fails without the fix (`"See the first ofiie here."`).

## `wordcraft-layout`: `tests::fragmented_hidden_text_lays_out_like_the_visible_text`
- **Cause:** the fragmented paragraph's visible characters alternate bold and regular, but the plain paragraph it was compared with was all regular. Line breaks only matched when the default font's bold and regular widths happened to break the same (Source Sans 3, Liberation Sans). With Carlito or DejaVu Sans they don't.
- **Fix:** the plain paragraph now has the same alternating bo…

title: Table styles: format every region with a live preview, delete your own styles, and see new ones first (#146)
author: vangel76
body:
**Builds on #256; merge that first.** Until then this diff also shows #256's commit.

It uses the style as OK would leave it: `table_style::preview` runs the same validation and edit code as the commands, on a copy of the style sheet. The current table's Style Options are used, and the region being edited is always turned on so it shows.

title: Clipboard pane: the last 24 things you copied or cut, ready to paste again
author: vangel76
body:
## What changed

**Home › Clipboard › Clipboard Pane** (`edit.clipboardPane`) is now implemented: a pane that collects what you copy or cut, like an office clipboard.

- **Engine:** Copy and Cut now also add the item to a session list (`Session::clip_history`). Each item keeps the rich fragment that copy already makes, plus its plain text. The list holds at most 24 items, newest first. Copies over ~4 MB (estimated) are left out, and the whole list stays under ~24 MB by dropping the oldest items. Copying the same thing twice in a row adds it only once. The system clipboard and `s.clipboard` behave exactly as before.
- **Commands (scripts / MCP / CLI):**
  - `edit.clipboardPane` `{"value"?: bool}` shows or hides the pane.
  - `edit.clipboardItems` lists `{index, preview, chars, objects}`, newest first (index 0).
  - `edit.pasteClipboardItem` `{"index": n}` pastes one item.
  - `edit.pasteAllClipboard` pastes every item in the order it was copied, as one undo step.
  - `edit.deleteClipboardItem` `{"index": n}` removes one item.
  - `edit.clearClipboard` removes them all.

  Pasting swaps the item in for the existing `paste` entry point and then puts the clipboard back, so it is undoable and follows Track Changes. The paste code itself is unchanged, so this doesn't conflict with #235 (Paste Special). The commands start with `edit.paste…`, so they leave equation editing the same way Paste does. Bad indexes return errors.
- **UI:** the Clipboard group's dialog launcher opens a left side pane (same pattern as the other panes in `panes.rs`). It has Paste All and Clear All, and a card for each item with a three-line preview. Clicking a card pastes it at the caret, and each card has a Delete button.
- **i18n:** the new command labels and pane strings are translated in all six catalogs.

title: Group and ungroup pictures, shapes and text boxes (Layout › Arrange › Group)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #265

## What changed
- **Multi-selection:** Shift+click (or Ctrl/⌘+click) on a picture, shape or text box adds it to the selected objects (click again to take it out); the extra ones get an outline. Scripts use the new `select.addObject` (`{"pos"}`, `{"index"}` from the Selection Pane, or `{"objects": [...]}`).
- **Group** (`arrange.group`): combines the selected floating objects into one group object, anchored where the first of them was, in the box around them all. It moves, wraps, nudges and resizes as one; members keep their relative positions and scale with the group. Grouping a group with more objects merges its members in.
- **Ungroup** (`arrange.ungroup`): splits a group back into its objects, where and how big the group showed them, anchored where the group was. They stay selected, so Group regroups them right away.
- Ribbon: Layout › Arrange › Group is now a menu with Group and Ungroup (also on Picture Format › Arrange). New strings are in every catalog.

Members are pictures/shapes/text boxes at offsets in the group's own coordinate space (like DrawingML `a:chExt`), so resizing the group only changes `w`/`h`. Text box stories inside groups are handled by copy/paste, pruning, word count and notes.
- **Layout/render:** members are drawn inside the group's frame (floating or inline), and text boxes in a group show their text. Hit testing selects the group.

Reads Word's groups, including inside `mc:AlternateContent` (`Requires="wpg"` is now understood), with non-zero child offsets and nested `wpg:grpSp` (flattened through their transforms). Before this, a Word group came in as just its first picture or shape.

title: File › Info keeps the Title, Author and other properties you type, and browser saves update the revision and modified stamps (#260, #262)
author: vangel76
body:
## Cause

**#260:** File › Info built its property fields from a copy of `doc.core` that was cloned again every frame. The copy was written back through `file.properties` only when a field lost focus. Each keystroke went into that throwaway copy and was gone on the next frame, so the field looked empty and there was nothing to commit when focus moved. Leaving File with Escape never fires focus-lost at all. This affected the desktop and browser builds alike.

**#262:** In the browser, Save turns into a download in `WordApp::execute`, which calls `io::save_bytes` directly instead of running `file.save`. Only `file.save` stamped the modified time, `lastModifiedBy` and the revision, so browser downloads kept whatever metadata the document was opened with.

## Change

- `backstage.rs` (`info_page`): each change to Title, Subject, Author, Keywords or Category is committed through `file.properties` as it is typed. That makes it undoable and marks the document dirty. All keystrokes from one visit to a field are joined into a single undo step with `join_next_undo`. The join is keyed by field and by document revision, so an Undo or any other change in between starts a new step. The fields are now `labelled_by` their labels, so screen readers and tests can find them by name.
- `Session::stamp_save` (engine) holds the existing save-stamp logic: modified time, created time if it is empty, last modified by, and revision + 1. `file.save` calls it, and so does the web download path for `file.save` / `file.saveAs`. Exports to PDF and PNG are not stamped.

## Testing

- New `backstage::tests::info_fields_keep_typed_properties_through_a_web_save`: types `ALPHA` into Title and `BETA` into Author one key at a time and checks after each frame that the fields show the values and `doc.core` holds them. It also checks that the document is dirty. It then saves twice through the browser download path and reads the bytes back: title, creator and `lastModifiedBy` (the current user name) are cor…

author: vangel76
body:

title: Paste pictures from the clipboard: screenshots, Copy Image and copied picture files (#45)
author: vangel76
body:
## Cause

egui's paste event (`Event::Paste`) only carries text. When the system clipboard holds only a picture (a screenshot, a browser's Copy Image), egui-winit swallows Ctrl+V and sends nothing. The ribbon and right-click **Paste** only knew WordCraft's own copy, so they said "the clipboard is empty". On the web, eframe's paste handler also reads only text.

## Change

- **`Services::clipboard_picture`** (new, `crates/ui-egui`): the host's way to read the picture on the system clipboard. It returns either RGBA pixels or a list of copied files. Desktop (`apps/wordcraft`) implements it with `arboard`: copied files (`text/uri-list` / CF_HDROP / Finder files) first, then image pixels.
- **`crates/ui-egui/src/paste_picture.rs`** (new): checks what the clipboard gave and inserts it through the existing `insert.picture` command, so it's one undo step. Clipboard sizes are treated as hostile:
  - each side is at most 16,000 px, and the whole picture at most 50 Mpx (checked multiplication);
  - the pixel buffer length must match width × height × 4;
  - files must have a picture extension and be at most 200 MB, at most 20 files per paste.
  - Pixels are encoded to PNG with the `image` crate. It was already a dev-dependency of ui-egui and is now a normal one.
- **When the picture is pasted:**
  - **Mod+V with no clipboard text:** egui sends no paste event, only the key release. When a release comes with no paste event before it, `edit.paste` runs, and the picture is pasted.
  - **Paste from the ribbon, context menu or keytips** (`edit.paste` with no `text`, through `WordApp::run`): a picture on the system clipboard wins over WordCraft's own copy. Copying in WordCraft replaces the clipboard with text, so a picture there is newer. Agents' `execute` calls are unchanged.
  - **Pasted text that is only paths or `file://` URLs of picture files** (what file managers put on the clipboard): the pictures are inserted when the clipboard really holds those files. Otherwise the text is p…

title: Show/Hide ¶ shows section breaks: Next Page, Continuous, Even Page and Odd Page (#42)
author: vangel76
body:
## Cause
Section breaks were imported from DOCX and kept in the model (section properties on the last paragraph of each section), but the formatting-marks pass in `crates/layout/src/display.rs` only knew about ¶, spaces, tabs and line/page/column breaks. A paragraph that ends a section was drawn with a plain ¶, so with Show/Hide ¶ on nothing told you a section break was there.

## Change
- **Layout (display list):** when marks are on, a body paragraph that ends a section (not the document's last section) draws a dotted double rule from the end of its text to the column edge, with the break's name centred in it: *Section Break (Next Page)*, *(Continuous)*, *(Even Page)*, *(Odd Page)* (and *(Next Column)*). This replaces the paragraph's ¶. The label comes from the start type of the **following** section, which is where OOXML (and `layout.break`) store it. Right-to-left paragraphs get the rule on their left. If there isn't room for the rule, only the name is drawn.
- **New `Draw::MarkText`** (a label in the UI's mark colour, same face as the ¶ mark). The raster renderer draws it. PDF export ignores it like `Draw::Mark`, and PDF/print/PNG export render with marks off anyway, so the break mark only ever shows on screen.
- Inserting section breaks already works (Layout › Breaks › Next Page / Continuous / Even Page / Odd Page, via `layout.break`, undoable). Those breaks now show up too.

## Testing
- New `section_breaks_show_with_formatting_marks` (wordcraft-layout): a two-section document shows the right label for each break type and drops the ¶ of the paragraph that ends the section. With marks off there's no label, and a one-section document has none either.

title: Show/Hide ¶: paragraph mark no longer overlaps text in mixed-direction paragraphs
author: vangel76
body:
With Show/Hide ¶ on, a paragraph whose last characters run against the paragraph's direction drew its ¶ on top of a letter: a left-to-right paragraph ending in Hebrew got the mark over the Hebrew word's leftmost letter, and a right-to-left paragraph ending in Latin "abc" got it inside "abc".

**Cause.** `crates/layout/src/display.rs` anchored the paragraph mark (and the section-break mark from #273) at `Line::end_x()`, the caret position after the paragraph's *logically* last character, then offset it by the paragraph's direction. On a bidirectional line that position is in the middle of the line whenever the last run has the opposite direction.

**Change.** New `Line::visual_end_x()` in `crates/layout/src/para.rs`: the right edge of the rightmost cluster in a left-to-right paragraph, the left edge of the leftmost in a right-to-left one (it never goes inside `end_x()`, so plain lines, hyphens and empty lines keep their current position). The ¶ and the section-break mark use it. Pure left-to-right and pure right-to-left paragraphs are unchanged.

**Testing.**
- New `paragraph_marks_sit_past_text_running_the_other_way` in `crates/layout/src/tests.rs`: an LTR paragraph ending in Hebrew and an RTL paragraph ending in Latin; checks that each ¶ is beyond every glyph on the correct side. It fails without the fix and passes with it. It doesn't depend on any system fonts (the reordering applies even when a glyph falls back to .notdef).
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout`: everything passes except three tests that depend on the environment's fonts (`fragmented_hidden_text_lays_out_like_the_visible_text`, `tests_bidi::glyph_runs_carry_their_text_for_pdf_export`, `tests_bidi::persian_letters_join_and_brackets_mirror`). They fail the same way without this change and are fixed separately by #261.
- `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-layout --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`: clean.

Builds on #273; merge that first.
