title: Layout: a page break followed by another page start makes one page
author: finwarman
body:
A paragraph of only a page break, followed by another page start, makes one page, not two.

- After #932 the break's mark stays on the old page, but its space after still went onto the new page. A following heading with page break before then wasn't at the top and broke again.
- A next-page section break carried by that paragraph also started a second page. The empty page the break started is now taken back first.

Found on a 60-page report: two blank pages Word doesn't have. Test: `a_page_break_then_a_new_page_makes_one_page` (both cases).

title: Layout: paragraph spacing adds up when HTML auto spacing is off
author: finwarman
body:
Paragraph spacing adds up when the document sets `w:doNotUseHTMLParagraphAutoSpacing`.

- #733 made the gap the larger of space after and space before, which is Word's default. Measured in Word with 12 pt before and after: 24 pt with the option, 12 pt without, the same in compatibility modes 14 and 15.
- The option is read into `Settings::sum_paragraph_spacing`, laid out in the body and in boxes, and written back in `w:compat`.

Found on a 60-page report whose cover came out about 60 pt short, so the next page's anchored pictures landed on the cover.

Tests: `space_between_paragraphs_is_their_sum_when_html_auto_spacing_is_off` (body and cell), `html_auto_spacing_off_is_read_and_kept`.

title: Fonts: a missing roman font is drawn in Cambria, as in Word
author: finwarman
body:
A font that isn't installed is drawn in Cambria when the font table classes it as roman, as Word does.

- Measured in Word with one missing font: `w:family` roman gives Cambria, swiss or auto gives Calibri. WordCraft picked by name only, so an unknown brand font always came out sans.
- Roman fonts are read from the font table into `Settings::roman_fonts`. Layout looks a missing one up as Cambria, which falls back to Caladea.
- Other classes keep the existing substitutes, which already start with Carlito.

Limit: only the paragraph text path uses it; equations and watermarks still resolve by name.

title: Layout: an empty section mark stays on a full page
author: finwarman
body:
An empty paragraph closing a section before a new page stays on a full page, instead of starting a blank page of its own.

- Measured in Word: 50 lines filling a page, then an empty paragraph carrying a next-page section break, then the next section gives 2 pages. WordCraft gave 3.
- Control, also measured: a plain empty paragraph in the same place moves to the next page in both.
- `PageBuilder::next_starts_page` is set per section; the line-fit check skips an empty mark that closes the section.

Found after a full landscape drawing page in a 60-page report.

Limit: only empty marks, and only before a new-page section. A continuous break, or a mark with text, behaves as before.

title: Layout: a bookmark after a page break takes no line
author: finwarman
body:
A bookmark after a paragraph's closing page break takes no line on the next page.

- Word writes the next heading's TOC bookmark start (`_Toc…`) into the paragraph that ends with a page break. The line after the break then held that marker, so it wasn't treated as the empty mark kept with the break (#932). It went onto the next page with the paragraph's spacing and pushed the heading 17 pt down.
- Lines holding only zero-width markers (`InlineObject::is_marker`: bookmarks, comment and permission ranges, field and control boundaries) now count as empty there.

Found on a 60-page report, where it cost a page in the calculations section. Test: `a_bookmark_after_a_page_break_takes_no_line`.

title: Layout: a numbered paragraph opening with a page break takes its number along
author: finwarman
body:
A numbered paragraph whose text opens with a page break draws its number on the next page, with the text.

- The label was always drawn on line 0. When line 0 holds only the opening page break (and zero-width markers), the number stood alone at the bottom of one page and the heading text started the next.
- `ParaLayout::label_line()` picks line 1 in that case; display draws the label there. The label's x is unchanged and lines up as in Word.

Found on three numbered headings in a 60-page report (5.2.3, 5.4, 5.4.3). Test: `a_numbered_heading_opening_with_a_page_break_takes_its_number_along`.

title: Tables: text running past an exact-height row is cut off
author: finwarman
body:
Text that doesn't fit an exact-height table row is cut off at the cell's edge, as Word does, instead of being drawn over the rows below.

- Table layout marks such a cell: `Placed::Cell` gets `clip`, set when the row is `hRule="exact"` and the cell's content is taller than the row.
- `page_display` draws lines inside a clipped cell within a `Draw::Clip` of the cell's area. The PDF writer draws item by item for tagging, so it passes the page's clipped cells along with each line.
- Hit testing and the caret are unchanged: the lines keep their layout positions.

Found on a welder qualification certificate whose identification block rendered as overlapping lines. Test: `text_overflowing_an_exact_row_is_clipped_to_it`.

Limit: only text lines are clipped; a picture overflowing an exact row still draws in full.

title: Tables: a row with less room than its minimum height moves on whole
author: finwarman
body:
A table row with an at-least height doesn't split where less than that height is left on the page; it starts the next page whole.

Measured in Word, with about 49 pt left on the page:

| Row | Word | WordCraft before |
|---|---|---|
| 8 lines, no height | splits after line 3 | same |
| 8 lines, at least 63.6 pt | moves whole | split |
| nested table of 6 rows, no height | splits after its row 3 | same |
| nested table of 6 rows, at least 63.6 pt | moves whole | split |
| 2 lines, at least 63.6 pt | moves whole | same |

`place_table` skips `split_row` for the first part of such a row. Found on a report whose title row (a logo beside a small nested table) started at the foot of its cover page, two pages off by the end. Test: `a_row_with_less_room_than_its_minimum_height_moves_on_whole`.

title: Fonts: a Bidi theme slot names the theme's complex-script font
author: finwarman
body:
`minorBidi`/`majorBidi` theme font slots name the theme's complex-script font (`a:cs`), not its Latin font.

Measured in Word, with a run set to `w:asciiTheme="minorBidi"`:

| Theme `a:cs` | Word | WordCraft before |
|---|---|---|
| Times New Roman | Times New Roman | Calibri (the Latin minor font) |
| empty, style sets Arial | Arial (inherited) | Calibri |

- `PropCtx` keeps the theme's major and minor `a:cs` faces. `theme_font` returns them for `…Bidi` slots, and nothing when they're empty, so the font beside it in `w:rFonts`, or the inherited one, applies. `w:cstheme` resolves the same way.

Found on a template whose title runs use `asciiTheme="minorBidi"` with an empty `a:cs`: Word draws them in the style's Arial, WordCraft drew Calibri. Test: `bidi_theme_slots_name_the_complex_script_font`.

Limit: with an empty `a:cs` and no explicit font anywhere in the style chain, Word draws Times New Roman; WordCraft keeps the theme-based default (the model doesn't record whether an inherited font came from the theme). East Asian slots are unchanged.

title: Layout: an inherited footer sizes its percentage tables by its own section
author: finwarman
body:
An inherited header or footer sizes its percentage-width tables by the section that defines it.

Measured in Word, with a 100%-wide footer table defined by a portrait section:

| Landscape section | Word | WordCraft before |
|---|---|---|
| inherits the footer | portrait width (451 pt), centred | landscape width |
| names the same footer itself | landscape width | landscape width |

Paragraph alignment in an inherited footer follows the landscape page in Word, as it already did here, so only table percentage widths change.

- `defining_width` finds the section that names an inherited part. `Ctx::pct_base` carries its text width while the part is measured (header and footer heights) and laid out. A top-level table takes its percentage share of that width.

Found on a 60-page report whose landscape calculation pages drew the footer table full width. Test: `an_inherited_footer_sizes_its_percentage_table_by_its_own_section`.

title: Equations: a multi-letter subscript stays whole after build-up
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1609.

The linear-format parser reads a script or limit as one letter or a number, as in Word (#347 grouped the gallery templates for the same reason). `to_linear` didn't follow that rule: a subscript holding `dd` was written bare as `V_dd`. Build-up re-reads the text before the caret on Space, a relation sign or a move, so a subscript typed in the subscript box came back as V_d followed by d. Scripts, n-ary limits and `┬`/`┴` limits now write a run of more than one character as a group, `V_(dd)`. Single characters and numbers stay bare (`x_i`, `x_10`, `x^2.5`), so other equations write the same linear text as before.

What this doesn't change, so I left the issue open for you to decide:
- Typing `V_dd` straight in still gives V_d then d. That's Word's rule; `V_(dd)` is the way to get a two-letter subscript.
- `{…}` stay visible braces, as in Word. `V_"dd"` (quoted normal text) isn't read as text yet. That's a separate parser feature, and I can do it in a follow-up if you'd like.

Validation:
- `math::tests::multi_letter_scripts_round_trip`: fails on main (`V_dd` reads back as V_d then d), passes here
- `math_edit::tests::build_up_keeps_a_multi_letter_subscript` (subscript box → `dd` → Right → build-up): fails on main (build-up rewrites the equation), passes here
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-doc --lib math`, `cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --lib equation`, `cargo test -p wordcraft-formats --lib mathml`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-doc --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: DOCX: a picture's a:alphaModFix transparency is drawn
author: Morzilla
body:
## What

A picture faded with *Picture Format › Transparency* is written as `<a:alphaModFix amt="10000"/>` inside its `a:blip`. The DOCX reader dropped the element, so a letterhead's dotted pattern that Word draws at 10 % opacity came out at full strength on screen and in the PDF export.

## How

In `read_pic`, when the blip carries an `a:alphaModFix`, the picture's alpha is multiplied into its pixels and the result is kept as a PNG under its own media key (`image5_a10000.png`). This is the same approach the `picture.transparency` command already takes, so layout, screen and PDF need no new path and a save keeps the fade. Details:

- two uses of the same picture at the same fade share one faded copy;
- a picture that can't be decoded (a metafile, an unknown format, a side over 30 000 px) is kept as it is and a warning is logged;
- the original bytes stay under their key;
- `image` moves from dev-dependency to dependency of `wordcraft-docx` (it is already in the tree through `wordcraft-pdf`, with the same features).

## Tests

`alpha_mod_fix_fades_the_picture` in `crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs`: a 2×2 opaque PNG with `amt="25000"` reads back with alpha 64, two pictures share the faded copy, `amt="100000"` is a no-op, and undecodable bytes stay opaque. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-docx --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p wordcraft-docx` pass.

Found while converting a customer's DOCX to PDF through the `docx` and `pdf` crates; the header now matches Word's and LibreOffice's output.

title: Tables without w:tblGrid take their grid from the cells, and widths wider than the page are squeezed like Word
author: Morzilla
body:
## What

Template libraries write tables with no `w:tblGrid` and cell widths (`w:tcW`) that don't fit the page: 6000 and 24000 twips on an A4 page is a common pattern. Word rebuilds the grid from the cells on opening and squeezes the table into the text area. WordCraft gave every column of a grid-less table a fixed inch, so such a table came out a third of the page wide, with its labels broken over two lines and its exact-height rows overlapping.

## How

Two changes, one per crate:

- **`wordcraft-docx`**, `grid_from_cells`: a table without `w:tblGrid` takes its grid from the cells' preferred widths, the way Word rebuilds it: the widest `w:tcW` among the cells that occupy a column alone, a spanning cell's width shared among the columns no cell sizes, an inch for a column nothing sizes.

- **`wordcraft-layout`**, `autofit`: an autofit table wider than its room is squeezed into it the way Word does it. Every column gets its longest word, and the room left is shared in proportion to how far each preferred width exceeds that. The squeeze applies only to a table whose width comes from its columns (no `w:tblW` of its own), from 2 % over the room; a table that sets its own width keeps it, past the margin and the page, as Word does (see the second commit).

The layout rule was derived from Word's own PDF export of the document that showed the problem. With a label column (preferred 300 pt) and a text column (preferred 1200 pt) on a 482 pt text area, the rule predicts 115.9 pt for the label column; Word draws 116.3 pt. A plain proportional split gives 96 pt and wraps the labels. On a second table in the same document the prediction is 141.9 pt against Word's 144.6 pt.

## Tests

- `a_table_without_a_grid_takes_its_columns_from_the_cells` (`crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs`): grid from cells, from a spanning cell, and the fallback.
- `preferred_widths_wider_than_the_page_are_squeezed_like_word` (`crates/layout/src/tests.rs`): the table stays inside the margins, the label column…

title: Tabs left of the margin stay on a default stop they already sit on (Word)
author: Morzilla
body:
## What

Left of the left margin, Word's next default tab stop is the first multiple of the interval **at or after** the current position, not strictly after it (its arithmetic truncates toward zero). So a tab that already sits on a stop, a second tab in a row or a leading tab on a line that starts at −72 pt, doesn't advance. A tab preceded by text or a space, or a line starting between stops, moves to the next multiple as usual, and right of the margin nothing changes.

Letterheads that line a footer up with spaces and tabs under a negative indent rely on this. One had a registration number on its last footer line drawn 72 pt too far right, over a vertical rule; it now lands within 0.2 pt of Word.

## How

`next_tab` in `crates/layout/src/para.rs`: for a negative position the default stop is `ceil(x / d) · d` instead of `(floor(x / d) + 1) · d`. Explicit stops and the hanging-indent stop are untouched.

## Measurements

Synthetic documents exported to PDF by Word (Calibri 9 pt, default tab 36 pt, left margin 37 pt, about 40 positions in total):

| text | left indent | X in Word | old rule | new rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `a\t\tX` | −60 | −36 | 0 | −36 |
| `\tX` | −72 | −72 | −36 | −72 |
| `\tX` | −60 | −36 | −36 | −36 |
| `\t \tX` | −60 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `a\t\t\t\tX` | −30 | 108 | 108 | 108 |
| `a\tb\tc\td` | −108 | b −72, c −36, d 0 | same | same |

Positions are relative to the margin.

## Tests

`tabs_left_of_the_margin_stay_on_a_default_stop` in `crates/layout/src/tests.rs` pins the five cases above that distinguish the rules. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-layout --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout` pass.

title: A floating object anchored after a page break stays on the page its paragraph starts on
author: Morzilla
body:
## What

Word's cover pages (Insert › Cover Page) are one paragraph holding a page break and then the page-anchored text box with the title and the approval table. Word draws a floating object on the page its anchor paragraph starts on. WordCraft drew it with the line holding the anchor, which after the break is the first line of page two: the cover came out blank and the title box sat over the body text of page two.

## How

`place_objects` in `crates/layout/src/lib.rs` places a paragraph's floating objects from the paragraph's first piece, whichever of its lines holds the anchor, and none from later pieces. Inline objects still go with their own line. The wrap areas were already registered from the paragraph's first page (`anchor_floats` runs there), so nothing changes for text flowing around the object.

## Tests

`a_float_anchored_after_a_page_break_stays_on_its_paragraph_s_first_page` in `crates/layout/src/tests.rs`: a paragraph of a page break followed by a page-anchored shape lays out on two pages with the shape on the first one only, at its page offset. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-layout --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout` pass.

Found converting a 21-page customer document to PDF; its cover now matches Word's export.

title: DOCX: keep a bare w:pgNumType when saving
author: lhymes
body:
`w:pgNumType` in a section was only written back when it set a start number or a non-decimal format. A section that carries `<w:pgNumType w:fmt="decimal"/>` (or an element with neither attribute we model) lost the element on save.

The reader now records that the element was present and sets nothing else (`SectionProps::page_num_set`); the writer emits it in that case. Sections without the element still write none, and elements with a start or format are unchanged.

Found while round-tripping real-world documents.

Test: `crates/docx/tests/section_page_number_type.rs` (bare element kept, start and format still round-trip, absent element stays absent).

title: DOCX: keep an explicit horizontal w:textDirection when saving
author: lhymes
body:
Only turned (vertical) text directions were written back. `<w:textDirection w:val="lrTb"/>` in a section or a table cell is the horizontal default, so it was read as "nothing set" and dropped on save.

`SectionProps` and `CellProps` now remember that the file stated `lrTb` (`text_direction_set`), and the writer emits the element in that case. Turned directions are unchanged; unknown values and sections or cells that never had the element still write nothing.

Found while round-tripping real-world documents.

Test: `explicit_horizontal_direction_is_kept_in_sections_and_cells` in `crates/docx/tests/section_text_direction.rs`.

title: DOCX: keep w:formProt when saving
author: lhymes
body:
A section's `w:formProt` (form protection) was ignored on read, so it vanished on save.

`SectionProps` gains `form_prot: Option<bool>`: the reader records the element (honouring `w:val`), the writer emits it in the schema position (after `w:cols`, before `w:vAlign`). Editing does not act on it; it is carried so the file keeps its setting. Sections without the element write none.

Found while round-tripping real-world documents.

Test: `crates/docx/tests/section_form_protection.rs` (on, explicitly off and absent; element order; second read matches).

title: DOCX: keep row-level w:tblPrEx when saving
author: lhymes
body:
`w:tblPrEx` (table property exceptions on a row) was ignored on read, so rows lost their overrides on save.

`RowProps` gains `exceptions: Option<Box<TableProps>>`. The reader parses the element with the existing table-property reader; the writer emits `w:tblPrEx` before `w:trPr` (CT_Row order), writing only the properties the row actually sets: width, alignment, indent, borders, shading, fixed layout and cell margins. It never writes a style, float or look into the exception, and an empty element is kept as an empty element. Rows without the element write none.

Found while round-tripping real-world documents.

Test: `crates/docx/tests/row_property_exceptions.rs` (exceptions survive in position and re-read onto the right row only; empty element kept). Also updates two struct literals for the new field.

title: M12: open and export OTT/FODT Writer documents, preserve ODF paragraph spacing
author: LabDennis
body:
# OpenDocument Writer: OTT and FODT import/export

WordCraft now opens and exports Writer templates (`.ott`) and flat XML documents (`.fodt`) through the existing ODT content model. The Open picker and Export page expose both formats. ODT/OTT/FODT also retain explicit paragraph spacing, line spacing and indents; inherited ODF spacing respects explicit zero overrides.

- OTT writes the template MIME type in both the first, uncompressed `mimetype` entry and the manifest.
- FODT shares the ODT reader/writer, embeds raster images, resolves namespace aliases, keeps metadata and page setup, and rejects wrong-type/truncated/deep XML. Image collection and XML input are bounded; external image files and DTDs are not loaded.
- Refactors shared style/metadata/body serialization instead of converting flat XML through a temporary ZIP.
- OTT/FODT conversions deliberately retain dirty state, including browser downloads: these formats do not yet preserve every WordCraft feature.

This is **format-family support with partial content fidelity**, not full LibreOffice feature parity. It does not replace the pending work on notes/comments (#1057, #1075 / #1054), tracked changes (#1517), sections (#1506 / #1379), headers/footers (#873 / #863), or ODT save-loss diagnostics (#1511 / #1316). No automatic issue-closing claims. DOC/DOT work is separate.

Validation:
- All 95 `wordcraft-formats` tests pass, including rich-content round trips, all line-spacing modes, template packaging, namespace aliases, malformed XML, style inheritance and image/nesting limits.
- Public engine open/edit/save/reopen regression passes; picker and browser-save safety tests pass.
- Headless Export UI inspected, including German labels.
- Local LibreOffice headless ODT→FODT, FODT→ODT and OTT→FODT round trips preserve original synthetic Unicode text, table cells, raster image, indent and title. No LibreOffice-produced fixtures or code are committed.

title: M12: preserve document properties when importing legacy DOC and DOT
author: LabDennis
body:
DOC/DOT imports discarded the optional SummaryInformation stream, so a document with a title/author opened with empty File > Info properties and lost them when converted. The reader now preserves title, subject, author, keywords, description, last editor and revision.

The implementation follows the public MS-OLEPS specification. It reads the metadata separately with a 2 MiB stream cap and 64 KiB string cap, bounds property offsets/lengths, respects Windows single-byte code pages, UTF-8 and UTF-16, and skips malformed optional metadata without preventing the document body from opening. It adds no dependencies. Creation/modification timestamps and custom properties are outside this focused fix; DOC/DOT remain read-only.

Validation:
- All 70 binary-reader tests pass, including public-import regressions for normal DOCs and DOT templates, multiple encodings, malformed/truncated metadata, invalid offsets and oversized strings/streams.
- Original synthetic document exported to DOC and DOT by installed LibreOffice: title was empty before the fix and is retained afterward; Unicode text, table cells, image and paragraph indent still pass. These generated files are not committed.
- Formatting and WASM check pass. Focused all-target Clippy passes with the existing `collapsible_match` class allowed only on the command line; no repository suppressions were added.
- `cargo xtask ci` was attempted and stops on unchanged upstream Clippy findings (proofing; the strict binary-reader check also reports the existing OfficeArt match arms).

This complements the other pending legacy-DOC work; it does not claim to fix the image report #880 or encrypted-file support #1079. Upstream and overlapping PRs were rechecked before publication. Roadmaps and local agent instructions are unchanged.

title: Web: opt-in embedding bridge for host pages (?host=parent)
author: GhostMitra
body:
## Description

Adds an opt-in embedding bridge for host pages (such as Nextcloud apps or other web containers) that frame WordCraft web in an `<iframe>`, matching the clean-room convention established across craft sibling apps (`gridcraft`, `photocraft`).

### Details
- **Opt-in activation**: When loaded with URL flag `?host=parent`, the web shell activates the bridge in `apps/wordcraft-web/src/host.rs`.
- **Same-origin security**: Only messages originating from the same origin as the app and sent from the immediate parent window (`window.parent`) are accepted and answered.
- **Protocol**:
  - `wordcraft:ready` (to parent): sent when the app is initialized and ready to receive documents, carrying `{ version }`.
  - `wordcraft:open` (from parent): accepts `{ name, bytes }` (where `bytes` is an `ArrayBuffer` or `Uint8Array`) and feeds the file through the inbox to open directly.
  - `wordcraft:save` (to parent): intercepts saves and exports, transferring an `ArrayBuffer` with `{ name, bytes }` to the parent window for persistence.
  - `wordcraft:dirty` (to parent): notifies the parent with `{ dirty }` whenever unsaved document state changes.
  - `wordcraft:failed` (to parent): notifies the parent with `{ error }` if app startup fails.
- **Author parameter**: `&author=` URL query parameter sets the user name for comments and revision tracking in host environments.
- **Workflow ergonomics**: In host mode, the initial start screen / sample document is bypassed so the document loaded by the parent opens cleanly without intermediate UI noise. Leaving-page guard is deferred to the parent host.
- Also includes a fix for canvas focus restoration after chrome clicks and checked file access in sniff.

### Quality gates
- Passed all 6 CI gates locally via `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

title: Linux: build an Arch package (.pkg.tar.zst)
author: ujo4eva
body:
Adds an Arch Linux package to the Linux release, next to the `.deb` and `.rpm`. Arch users (Manjaro, EndeavourOS, Omarchy, ...) can then `sudo pacman -U` it, and ArtCraft Launcher can install and update it through pacman (storytold/craft-launcher#389).

## What changes

- `packaging/linux/package.sh`:
  - adds an `arch` format, on by default;
  - builds `wordcraft-<ver>-linux-<arch>.pkg.tar.zst` with nfpm's `archlinux` packager from the same `nfpm.yaml`.

  nfpm can't rename a package per format and doesn't env-expand `archlinux.packager`, so the script writes a copy of the config with both set.
- `packaging/linux/nfpm.yaml`:
  - an `overrides.archlinux` block with Arch dependencies: `glibc gcc-libs hicolor-icon-theme libxkbcommon vulkan-icd-loader`;
  - `provides: wordcraft`;
  - `conflicts: wordcraft, wordcraft-bin, wordcraft-git`.
- **Named `ai.storyteller.wordcraft`, not `wordcraft`.** The AUR already has `wordcraft`, `wordcraft-bin` and `wordcraft-git`. An AUR helper treats an installed package with an AUR name as its own and would rebuild it on the next update. The bundle id is also how the launcher tells this package (which it updates) from an AUR build (which it leaves to the AUR helper).
- The README's Linux download table gains an Arch row.

**No workflow change is needed.** `craft-common-actions` uploads and checksums everything `package.sh` writes to `dist/release`, and the riscv64 job passes `--formats "deb rpm tar"`.

## Notes

- nfpm has no `optdepends` for Arch, so the Debian `recommends` have no Arch equivalent.
- Pre-releases sort correctly: `0.7.0-rc.1` becomes pkgver `0.7.0rc.1`, which pacman places before `0.7.0`. Arm64 maps to `aarch64`.

## Testing

- I ran `package.sh --skip-build --formats arch` with the binaries from the published v0.6.1 x86_64 tarball, checked against `SHA256SUMS.txt`. It produced `wordcraft-0.6.1-linux-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst`.
- `pacman -Qip` reads the package, and `.PKGINFO` has the expected name, version, x86_64 arch, packa…

title: ODT import: text after a drawing shape stays in its paragraph (#1654)
author: benandez
body:
Fixes #1654 (the ODT half; see the issue comment for the DOCX findings).

## Problem
When a `draw:` shape (`custom-shape`, `rect`, `ellipse`, ...) is anchored in a `text:p`, the ODT reader read the shape's own `text:p` as a body paragraph. That closed the paragraph the shape sits in. After the inner `</text:p>` no paragraph was open, so `text()` dropped everything up to the next paragraph. LibreOffice's `sw/qa/extras/odfexport/data/MadeByLO7.odt` lost 3 of its 7 body paragraphs, both on screen and in the PDF.

## Change (`crates/formats/src/odt.rs`)
- The ODF 1.3 §10.3 drawing shapes (`rect`, `line`, `polyline`, `polygon`, `regular-polygon`, `path`, `circle`, `ellipse`, `connector`, `caption`, `measure`, `custom-shape`) are skipped with their text, as `text-box` already is. ODT shapes aren't imported as objects yet; that is out of scope here.
- `draw:g` is not skipped. The reader still goes through it, so pictures (`draw:frame`) inside a group are still read.
- The module doc is updated to match.

## Tests
- `text_after_a_drawing_shape_stays_in_its_paragraph`: one styled paragraph holding a custom shape with text, an empty rect and a group with an ellipse, with text between them. It checks that the paragraph keeps all its text and its style, and that no shape text leaks into the body. Hand-written XML. Seen failing first (`["", "In the shape", "", "In the group", "Next"]`).
- `MadeByLO7.odt` (LibreOffice core 0b6c4e65): `wordcraft-cli text` shows all 7 paragraphs, and the PDF goes from 109 to 277 words.
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-formats` (91 passed), `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-formats --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`.

## Notes
Possible textual conflict with #1651, which edits the same skip-list match arm in `Body::start`.

title: Legacy VML freeforms (header rule lines) are drawn and kept on save
author: mmazzieri
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @mmazzieri._

Legacy VML freeforms, a `v:shape` with its own `path`, were dropped by the DOCX reader. Many older headers use them for their rule lines, so those lines vanished on screen, in the PDF and on save. Found on the synthetic file attached to #1290 (`S08-documento-composto.docx`): the light-blue rule under every header is `path="m,10800l21600,10800xe"`. This was split out of #1328 so that PR stays on the watermark.

- `read_vml` now reads these shapes as freeforms, following ECMA-376 Part 4:
  - path commands `m`/`t`, `l`/`r`, `c`/`v` (Béziers, flattened), `x` and `e`, in the shape's `coordsize`/`coordorigin` space;
  - `nf`/`ns`, and `v:stroke` opacity.
- They are drawn on screen and in the PDF, and saved as DrawingML custom geometry.
- WordArt (`v:textpath`) is not touched here.

**Limits:**
- Fill opacity is either none (at 0) or opaque, as for DrawingML fills.
- Arcs are drawn straight.
- Shapes whose path uses formulas (`@n`) aren't drawn.
- Paths inherited from a `v:shapetype` aren't read.

**Validation:**
- `vml_freeform_rule_in_header` checks size, stroke, no fill, margin anchor and points, and the same again after write → read.
- `hostile_vml_paths_stay_finite` runs 16 junk paths × 5 junk coordinate spaces: no panic, all values finite.
- S08: 6 VML rules in, 6 custom-geometry freeforms out. The PDF draws the rule at y ≈ 79 pt.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-docx --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test -p wordcraft-docx` pass on this branch (Windows x64, MSVC).
- The full `cargo xtask ci` on current main has two unrelated failures, in code this PR doesn't touch:
  - `wordcraft-engine` `file_access::tests::commands_do_not_touch_the_file_system_themselves` (the `std::fs::File::open` in `cmd/file.rs`);
  - `wordcraft-ui-egui` `clicks_on_ribbon_and_status_bar_chrome_keep_typing_in_the_document`.

title: French proofing: fr-FR and regional spelling, suggestions, typography and grammar, hyphenation
author: DailyXplorer
body:
Refs #895, #1325. Both issues ask for a French interface, which already exists (`fr.tsv`, #729). This PR adds French proofing, the other half of working in French. Related to #100 (multilingual spell check).

## Summary

Before this change, French text resolved to `ProofLang::Other` and got no marks at all. This PR adds French as a proofing language, built on the merged Italian module (#1090).

- **`ProofLang::Fr` and `ProofLang::FrCa`.** Every `fr` and `fr-XX` tag maps to `Fr` (`fr-FR`, `fr-BE`, `fr-CH`, `fr-LU`, `fr-MC`, `fra`, `fre`), except `fr-CA`, which maps to `FrCa`. `FrCa` shares the dictionary, suggestions and hyphenation, and its grammar follows Quebec typography (no space before `;` `!` `?`). Both are in `PROOFED`, French is no longer the `Other` example, and the "Faute d’orthographe possible" message, suggestions, grammar and hyphenation are wired through every consumer.
- **Spelling (`crates/proof/src/fr/`).** Words are checked against the French Hunspell dictionary installed on the system: `fr_FR`, else `fr`, `fr_BE`, `fr_CA`, `fr_CH`, `fr_LU` or `fr_MC`. It is never bundled, because the Dicollecte files are MPL 2.0.
  - The dictionary itself encodes elisions (`l'arbre`, `qu'elle`, `jusqu'à`), and `’` is read as `'`.
  - Compounds the dictionary doesn't list are checked part by part (`va-t-il`).
  - The user dictionary applies, after an elision too.
  - Without a dictionary, French text gets no marks, as in Word without the language's tools.
- **Shared affix engine (`affix.rs`).** The engine can now read the Dicollecte dictionary, which uses long flags and more affix features than the Polish, Portuguese and Italian files:
  - `FLAG long` and `FLAG num`, each flag interned as one private-use character, so the rest of the engine and the compact format are unchanged;
  - up to 512 distinct flags, where the old limit was 128 (fr_FR uses about 180);
  - `NEEDAFFIX`, `KEEPCASE`, `FULLSTRIP` and `ICONV`;

title: RTF import: Mac OS Roman and DOS code pages (`\mac`, `\pc`, `\pca`) (#1653)
author: D13GOOOO
body:
Part of #1653: the single-byte code pages. The Japanese half needs a decision first, see below.

## What was wrong

8-bit RTF text (`\'xx`) in a Macintosh or DOS document was decoded as Windows-1252:

Two commits, plus a merge of today's `main`:

1. **Mac OS Roman** (`crates/doc/src/encoding.rs`, `crates/formats/src/rtf.rs`): a code page 10000 table, with the euro sign at 0xDB as in Mac OS 8.5 and later; it matches Python's `mac_roman`. The reader uses it for `\mac` documents, `\fcharset77` fonts and `\cpg` / `\ansicpg` 10000.

   - `SINGLE_BYTE_CODE_PAGES` stays Windows-only, so the `ansi` pages accepted by `text.typeCode` (#1146) are unchanged.

title: DOCX: read every VML shape in a `w:pict`, and a `v:group`'s members
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #1643.

## The bug

`read_vml` took `pict.els().find(..)` — the first `v:*` child that is not a `v:shapetype` — and read only that one. A `w:pict` may hold any number of VML elements, so:

- a `w:pict` with several sibling shapes kept the first and dropped the rest;
- a `v:group` was read as **no object at all**, not as one shape: `shape.local()` is `"group"`, which falls through the `line`/`rect`/`roundrect`/`oval` match to `None`. A group only survived if it happened to contain a text box, which `vml_textbox` finds by recursing — and then it became that one box, at the group's own size, with every other member gone.

Either way the loss is permanent: saving writes the model back as DrawingML, so what was not read is not written.

## The fix

The model already has the group. `InlineObject::Group { w, h, ch_w, ch_h, children, .. }` holds a VML group's two boxes — its own, and its members' coordinate space — and `read_group`/`group_members` already map a DrawingML `wpg:wgp` onto it from `a:chExt`/`a:chOff`, flattening nested groups with a cumulative transform. `coordsize`/`coordorigin` are those same two numbers, so `v:group` reuses that algebra and the renderer and the writer are untouched.

- **`read_vml_all`** walks every `v:*` child of a `w:pict` and emits one object each. `read_vml` now returns the first of them, for the two places that show a single drawing: an OLE object's picture and a `mc:Fallback` preview.
- **`read_vml_group`** turns a `v:group` into an `InlineObject::Group`, its members mapped from the `coordsize`/`coordorigin` space onto the group's box. Nesting is bounded by `MAX_VML_GROUP_DEPTH` (8, as the DrawingML path bounds it) and members by the existing `MAX_GROUP_CHILDREN`.
- **`read_vml_shape`** is the old per-shape body, unchanged except that it takes the group's scale, so a member's `width`/`height` and a `v:line`'s `from`/`to` come through in the group's coordinates. A member never floats — the group does, and places it.

title: Text typed after a footnote or endnote number is no longer superscript (#1593)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes the first part of #1593.

A footnote or endnote number in the text is an inline object carrying the `FootnoteReference` / `EndnoteReference` character style, which raises it (both styles set `vert_align: Superscript`). `Session::typing_props` takes the formatting of the run left of the caret, so with the caret right after a note number (where `references.footnote` / `references.endnote` leave the reference when the note is added at the end of a line) everything typed next picked up that style and came out superscript.

`typing_props` now drops those two character styles, the same way it already drops a hyperlink at the end of a link: typed text after a note number is body text, as in Word, LibreOffice and Pages. Any other formatting of the run (bold, font, size...) is kept. Every typing path goes through `typing_props` (`type_text` / paste, inserted objects), so all of them get this, and the ribbon's superscript/font state at that caret now shows what typing will actually produce. The same applies to the number at the start of the note text itself.

Test `typing_after_a_note_number_is_not_superscript` in `crates/engine/src/tests.rs`, for both footnotes and endnotes: inserts a note, puts the caret right after its number in the body, checks `typing_props()` has no style and that typed text gets no style. Fails on main (the typed text gets `FootnoteReference` / `EndnoteReference`).

Not in this PR: the second part of the issue (note numbers as clickable links between the text and the note) is a separate feature request and a design decision for the maintainers.

title: Dropping several images inserts all of them (#1592)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1592.

**Cause:** `insert.picture` places the picture at the selection and then selects it. When several images arrive in one drop, each file is inserted in turn, so the second insert replaces the picture the first one just placed. Only the last image stays.

**Fix** (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`): within one drop, after a picture is placed in the text, the selection collapses to just after it, so the next image goes after the previous one. This covers both entry paths: desktop file drops (`dropped_files`) and the inbox (web drops and picks, `drain_inbox`).
- The caret moves only after a picture was actually placed in the text. After a failed insert, the user's selection stays as it was.
- With a Drawing Canvas selected, a picture goes into the canvas and the canvas stays selected. So every image of the drop joins the canvas, as Insert › Shapes does (#344).
- The first image still replaces a selection, and the last one is still selected after the drop. This is the same as Insert › Picture.

About point 4 of the report (a later import deletes the first photo): after a drop, the last picture stays selected, and a new insert replaces the selection, the same as for typed text and Insert › Picture. Click after the picture first, and the next image is added. This PR does not change that behaviour, because changing it is a design decision for the maintainers.

**Tests**
- `several_dropped_images_are_all_inserted`: two images in one drop give two pictures. Without the fix, the count is 1.
- `several_dropped_images_all_join_a_selected_canvas`: with a canvas selected, both images become canvas members.

title: Layout: field instructions do not add blank paragraphs
author: finwarman
body:
Complex-field instructions spanning body paragraphs no longer add blank lines and push later content onto another page.

- Hide paragraph marks inside instruction code and suppress its line breaks.

title: Outside and inside aligned floats follow mirrored pages (#1524)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1524.

With mirrored margins, a shape aligned to the outside (or anchored to the outside margin) was drawn on the right of every page. `float_rect` always measured the horizontal reference area as on an odd page, and `mirror_even_pages` then moved the whole even page by the difference of the margins, so nothing ever switched sides.

Now the body and header/footer frames know when they are on an even page with mirrored margins (`PageFrame::flip`), and `float_rect` on such a page:
- swaps `FloatAlign::Inside` and `FloatAlign::Outside`, so outside means left on even pages, like Word;
- takes the inside and outside margins from the opposite sides (`InsideMargin` / `OutsideMargin`), and the left and right margins from the page as it ends up after mirroring;
- gives every area before the later `mirror_even_pages` move, so page- and margin-relative positions land where Word puts them instead of being pushed by that move.

Headers and footers are moved by `mirror_even_pages` too, so their floats get the same treatment. Pages without mirrored margins and odd pages are unchanged.

Tests:
- `outside_anchored_floats_follow_mirrored_pages`: shapes on page 1 and page 2 (inside margin 108 pt, outside 36 pt), aligned Outside and Inside in the margin and anchored to the outside margin; each lands on the correct side of its page.
- `outside_anchored_header_floats_follow_mirrored_pages`: a header shape anchored to the outside margin is on the right of page 1 and on the left of page 2.

title: Copy puts the formatted text on the system clipboard as HTML, not only copies with equations (#1523)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1523.

**Cause.** `copy_result` (used by Copy, Cut and the column copy) only built `clipboard_html` when the copied fragment held an equation (#816). For any other selection it returned text alone, so the desktop host put only `text/plain` on the system clipboard and Gmail, ONLYOFFICE and other programs lost bold, italic, fonts and sizes. Pasting between WordCraft documents kept the formatting because that uses WordCraft's internal copy.

**Fix.** Copy and Cut now always export the copied fragment as HTML through the existing `wordcraft_formats::html::export_fragment`. Equations are still written as MathML. The host-side path that sets HTML with its plain-text alternative (`system_clipboard::put` → arboard `set().html()`) is the same one #816 added, so every copy entry point gets the change: Ctrl+C/Ctrl+X, the ribbon Copy button and the context menu Copy. On X11/XWayland and on Wayland with data-control the clipboard now offers `text/html` beside the text. On Wayland without data-control and on the web it still offers text only, as before.

Pasting back into WordCraft is unchanged. When the system clipboard text matches WordCraft's own copy, Paste still uses the internal fragment (`paste_fragment`), not the HTML.

**How each point of the issue is handled**
1. Plain text is kept: the HTML goes on the clipboard with the text as its alternative.
2. `text/html` with the selection's formatting is now exported.
3. RTF on the clipboard is not written here. arboard can't set custom formats (see the note in `apps/wordcraft/src/clipboard.rs` about OMML, #1297), and HTML is enough for the browsers, mail clients and word processors the issue names. It is left as a follow-up and noted in `docs/gaps.md`.
4. XWayland and native Wayland use the same arboard path. It needs the data-control protocol on Wayland, which KDE Plasma has.
5. Internal rich copy/paste is unchanged (see above).

**Tests**
- `engine::tests::copying_bold_text_puts_html_on_the_clipboard`: copying "plain *…

title: CLI PDF export: Arabic and Persian fall back to the craft-fonts Arabic face (#1652)
author: benandez
body:
Fixes #1652.

## Problem
In a headless CLI with no system fonts, Arabic and Persian text was drawn as `.notdef` boxes. `FontDb::with_font_dirs` loaded only the craft-fonts Japanese and Simplified Chinese faces. The Noto Sans Arabic face (in craft-fonts since `8dcdacd`, the release pin) was embedded in the binary but never added to the document font database, so nothing could fall back to it.

## Change (`crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs`)
- After the Japanese document faces, which stay first so they remain the Japanese fallback, the database now loads every other craft-fonts face, not only the Chinese ones. Arabic is the new one today. Any script added to craft-fonts later becomes a fallback automatically.
- The doc comment is updated to match.

title: Shift+Delete cuts the selection on macOS and Linux too (#1669)
author: D13GOOOO
body:
Fixes #1669.

## What Word does

I checked these by hand in Word for Windows (Microsoft 365), using a new document with "Prova di testo":

| Keys | Word |
|---|---|
| Shift+Backspace, no selection | erases the character before the caret, like Backspace |
| Shift+Delete, no selection | nothing |
| Shift+Delete, a word selected | the word is **cut**: gone, and Ctrl+V brings it back |

## What WordCraft did

- **Shift+Backspace** already erases everywhere (#707, in 0.6.1).
- **Windows:** egui-winit sends Shift+Delete as `Event::Cut` (`is_cut_command`), so WordCraft already matched Word: it cuts a selection and does nothing without one.
- **macOS and Linux:** Shift+Delete arrives as `Key::Delete` with Shift. No shortcut is bound to that combo, and `shift_variant_params` only covers caret moves and Backspace, so it did nothing, even with text selected. This is the part of #1669 that reproduces on current `main`.

## Change (`crates/ui-egui/src/keys.rs`)

`canvas_events` runs Cut for Shift+Delete (Shift alone, no other modifier) when there is a selection. It goes through the same `system_clipboard::put_result` path as the `Cut` event, so the system clipboard gets the text too. With no selection the key does nothing, as in Word. Ctrl, Alt or ⌘ with Shift+Delete still go to the shortcut lookup unchanged.

On macOS this follows Word for Windows, since I couldn't check Word for Mac. If Word for Mac turns out to forward-delete on Shift+Fn+Delete instead, the check is one `cfg` away.

## Tests

- `tests::shift_delete_cuts_the_selection_and_shift_backspace_erases` (ui-egui, through the real canvas key path): Shift+Backspace erases, Shift+Delete without a selection changes nothing, and Shift+Delete on "fire " removes it and puts it on the clipboard. It fails without the change (`"Kilns fire cla"` vs `"Kilns cla"`).

title: Fields: refresh unlocked DATE and TIME when a document is opened
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #1672.

## The bug

A `DATE` or `TIME` field showed the result cached when the file was last saved. Word refreshes both whenever it shows, prints or exports a document; WordCraft refreshed them only on an explicit *Update Field(s)*, on insert, or when printing with *Update fields before printing* on. So a letter written from a template carried the date the **template** was last saved, and `convert … out.pdf` gave no hint the date was old.

Against the reporter's fixture, on 2026-10-14:

| | `main` | this branch | Word 365 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DATE \@ "yyyy-MM-dd"` | `2020-01-01` | `2026-10-14` | `2026-10-14` |
| `TIME \@ "dddd, d MMMM yyyy"` | `Wednesday, 1 January 2020` | `Wednesday, 14 October 2026` | `Wednesday, 14 October 2026` |

## The fix

There are two output paths that show a field: layout and PDF go through `fields::field_text`, while `wordcraft-cli text` goes through `plain_text()`, which reads the stored result straight off the model. Patching both would have meant threading a clock into two places — and `format_date` lives in `engine` (L5) while both consumers are L2, which `cargo xtask layers` forbids, so it would also have meant moving the clock down into a low layer that would then need `js_sys` for wasm.

Refreshing where the document is **read** avoids all of that and fixes every output at once, because the stored result is the one source they share. The new `io::opened` sits beside `ensure_nonempty` as the two things a freshly-read document needs, so a future open path gets both:

```rust
fn opened(doc: &mut Document) {
    doc.ensure_nonempty();
    crate::cmd::references::refresh_date_fields(doc);
}
```

`refresh_date_fields` reuses the existing `date_picture` and `insert::format_date`, with Word's defaults (`M/d/yyyy`, `h:mm am/pm`) when the code carries no `\@` switch.

Deliberately narrow:

- **only `DATE` and `TIME`** — `CREATEDATE`, `SAVEDATE` and `PRINTDATE` record when something happened and are not "now"; `REF`, `PAGEREF`, `TOC` …

title: Proofing: download a missing dictionary from LibreOffice's collection (File › Options › Proofing)
author: fabiodalez-dev
body:
Refs #8 (proofing languages), #1063 / #1084 (dictionaries folder), #1167.

## Why

WordCraft proofs Polish, Portuguese, Italian, Croatian, Turkish and Russian, but only when a Hunspell dictionary is on the system. On a typical Mac or Windows machine there is none. #1084 made that visible: File › Options › Proofing › Dictionaries lists each language with "no dictionary found". This PR adds the next step, a way to get one from the app.

## What this does

- **A Download button beside Polish, Portuguese, Italian, Russian and Czech when they have no dictionary**, in #1084's list (File › Options › Proofing › Dictionaries), with "Downloading…" while it runs. There's no new section: the button goes on the line that already says the dictionary is missing, and a note under the list appears only when a download is possible.
- The `.aff`/`.dic` pair comes from LibreOffice's dictionary collection (https://github.com/LibreOffice/dictionaries), **pinned to one commit** (`67032ee`, 2026-10-12) rather than `master`. Each file must match the **SHA-256** recorded for it in `libreoffice.rs`; a changed upstream file, a different file served at that path, or a truncated or tampered download is refused and nothing is written. It is then checked to decode and parse as a non-empty dictionary, and only then saved. Each file is written next to its final name and renamed into place, so a failed download never leaves a broken pair.
- **Where it goes**: the dictionaries folder the user chose there (#1084), else `dictionaries` in the WordCraft settings folder. That folder is always searched, right after the chosen one and before the system's. The language's dictionary is reloaded and the list refreshes, so marks appear without a restart.
- The download runs on a background thread with the system's `curl` (shipped with macOS, Windows 10 and later, and most Linux distributions): HTTPS only, failing on HTTP errors, capped at the 64 MB the loader reads and at 5 minutes. No HTTP or TLS crate is added…

title: A click on the ribbon's chrome keeps typing in the document (#1093 follow-up)
author: matstrange
body:
Follow-up to #1138 (#1093), which left `clicks_on_ribbon_and_status_bar_chrome_keep_typing_in_the_document` failing on a clean tree.

Clicks on ribbon chrome that isn't a command button — Styles gallery tiles, tab names, empty ribbon space, View check boxes, status-bar items — did leave the page without keyboard focus, but the hand-back happened a frame too late to matter.

**Why.** `refocus_after_chrome_click` runs at the end of `WordApp::ui`, after the page has been drawn. It set `canvas.want_focus`, which the page only picks up on the *next* frame, and the page's own `focused` flag — which gates `keys::canvas_events` — isn't recomputed until then either. So the keystroke that arrived in the frame right after the click found `canvas.focused == false` and was dropped. One more frame later everything worked, which is why it went unnoticed: nobody types within 16 ms of a click.

Command buttons don't hit this: `widgets::run_from_ribbon` sets `want_focus` during the ribbon pass, so the page consumes it in the same frame.

**Fix.** Claim the keyboard in the same frame — set `canvas.focused` and `request_focus` on the page's widget id, taken from the frame just drawn (`CanvasState::widget_id`).

**Verify:** `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-ui-egui --all-targets`, `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui` → 393 passed, 0 failed (the whole `ui-egui` suite is green for the first time since #1138 landed).

Unrelated to #1700 (Home tab on startup), which is a separate PR off the same base.

title: Tables: repeated header rows move to the next page with the first row (#1704)
author: dfgodvan
body:
Fixes #1704.

## Problem
A table with a repeated header row (`w:tblHeader`) that starts near the bottom of a page left the header row there alone when the first body row didn't fit under it, then repeated the header on the next page above that row. LibreOffice starts the table on the next page.

## Fix
`crates/layout/src/lib.rs`, `place_table`: before the first row, if the table has header rows and the page already holds something, check whether the first row after the header rows can start under them on this page, whole or (when it may split) as the part `split_row` keeps there. If it can't, the table starts on the next page.

A table that starts at the top of a page is unchanged: its header row stays there even when no body row fits under it, as in Word (the existing `repeated_header_is_followed_by_the_next_row_even_when_it_overflows` cases still pass). Tables without header rows are unchanged.

## Result
Repro from #1704, 43 filler paragraphs, `pdftotext`:

| | page 1 ends with | page 2 starts with |
|---|---|---|
| main | `Header 1 2 3` | `Header 1 2 3`, `Row 1`, `Row 2` |
| this PR | `Filler paragraph 43` | `Header 1 2 3`, `Row 1`, `Row 2` |
| LibreOffice | `Filler paragraph 43` | `Header 1 2 3`, `Row 1`, `Row 2` |

38-42 and 44-46 paragraphs lay out as before.

## Testing
- New test `repeated_header_moves_with_the_first_row_that_does_not_fit` (`crates/layout/src/tests.rs`): a paragraph leaves 80 pt or 40 pt of the page, then a table with a 20 pt header row and 40 pt rows. With 80 pt the header and row 1 stay on page 1; with 40 pt the whole table moves to page 2. Fails on main: `left: [[0], [0, 1, 2]]`, `right: [[], [0, 1, 2]]`.
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-layout --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.

#1177 and #1486 also touch `place_table`; whichever lands later needs a small merge.

title: packaging: RPM requires library sonames, so openSUSE can install it
author: tydude001
body:
## What and why

WordCraft's RPM requires Fedora package names: `libxkbcommon`, `(vulkan-loader or libglvnd-egl)`.
openSUSE has no `libxkbcommon`, `vulkan-loader` or `libglvnd-egl` package, so zypper refuses it with
`nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` (exit 4, which the ArtCraft Launcher shows as "error 4";
storytold/craft-launcher#341).

This requires the libraries' sonames instead, as PhotoCraft and VectorCraft already do, so the same RPM
resolves on Fedora/RHEL and openSUSE. It also declares the binaries' glibc floor, matching the deb's
`libc6 (>= 2.35)`. The floor names libm, not libc: the
binaries' only GLIBC_2.35 symbols are `hypot` and `hypotf` from libm, and RHEL 9's current glibc
(`2.34-283.el9_8`) provides `libc.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)` through backports but not libm's.

## How it was tested

WordCraft 0.7.0's released x86_64 binaries, repackaged with nfpm 2.47.0 and this branch's `nfpm.yaml`, then
installed with the distro's own package manager in a fresh x86_64 container and run with `wordcraft-cli --version`.
The released RPM is the same test on the release's own package.

| | released 0.7.0 RPM | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Fedora 44 | installs, runs | installs, runs |
| openSUSE Tumbleweed | `nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` | installs, runs |
| openSUSE Leap 15.6 | `nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` | installs, runs |
| Rocky Linux 9 (glibc 2.34) | installs; `wordcraft-cli`: ``libm.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.35' not found`` | refused: `nothing provides libm.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)(64bit)` |

The aarch64 RPMs get the same requires. I checked that side on FilmCraft only: its 0.7.2 arm64 binaries need
GLIBC_2.35 for the same two libm symbols, and its branch RPM installs and runs on arm64 Fedora 44,
Tumbleweed and Leap 15.6 (qemu-user).

`cargo xtask ci` passes. This tests installation and the CLI, not the GUI. The same results for every
Crafting App: https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/issues/341#issuecomment-6171570045

title: Make File › Close close only the document, not the app
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1712

## Cause
The `file.close` command pushed a `close` UI request, and `handle_request` in `ui-egui` turned every such request into `quit_requested = true`. Clicking File › Close therefore closed the window and quit the app, as the window's X button does.

## Fix
`file.close` now closes only the document. The window stays open with no document, as in the start-up state without a document (#1129), and the Backstage goes back to Home if it was open. The request now carries a `quit` flag. Only `WordApp::close_requested` (the window's close button) sets it, so that path still asks about unsaved changes and then quits. The existing tests that treated Close as quitting now assert the document is closed and the app stays open.

## Verified
- Regression tests `tests::close_asks_before_closing_the_document`, `backstage::tests::backstage_close_asks_then_closes`, `backstage::tests::backstage_close_on_a_clean_document_closes_at_once`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui --lib close`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Did not add a separate File › Exit menu entry. `app.quit` on the control channel and the window's close button still quit the app. The window-close flow (`window_close_asks_first`) is unchanged.

title: Tables: a table with its own width is not squeezed to the margins (#1721)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1721.

`layout_table` scaled every non-fixed table wider than 1.5x the text width down to the margins, even when that width was the table's own preferred width (`w:tblW`). Word keeps such a table at its width and lets it run past the margin, which the letterhead layout in the issue relies on (13608 tw on A4 with 1" margins, 1.51x).

**Change** (`crates/layout/src/table.rs`): the 1.5x squeeze now runs only when the table has no width of its own (`target` is `None`). A percentage width is already capped at 100% of the text width, so it never reached the squeeze; fixed-layout tables are unchanged. This covers every "own width" row of the issue's table (1.51x, 2x, 3x, no cell widths, long text, header, nested), since all of them go through `layout_table`.

**Not changed:** squeezing an automatic-width table as soon as it is wider than the text (the issue's "automatic width, cells 1.2x" row) is left for the follow-up the issue proposes, because dragging a column border clears the table's own width (`set_widths`) and Word's behaviour there should be observed first.

**Test:** `layout::tests::table_with_its_own_width_is_not_squeezed_to_the_margins` lays out a 3-column table twice the text width: with its own 936 pt width the second column starts 312 pt in (fails on main, where it starts 156 pt in); with an automatic width the same columns are still squeezed.

**Docs:** `docs/layout-parity.md` (tables autofit row and revision history).

title: Engine: the Word 2003 XML save sniffs through a new io read_file_head, so the file_access guard passes (#1729)
author: albayazid
body:
0.7.0's `cargo xtask ci` fails on its first real run because `commands_do_not_touch_the_file_system_themselves` (the guard that keeps engine filesystem access inside the `io` gateway) finds a new offender: PR #1088's `is_word_2003_file` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs`) opened the file with `std::fs::File::open` directly. The check was right in spirit — it calls `file_access::check_read` first — but the hygiene rule is that all filesystem access goes through `io`, so the sandbox stays enforced in one place. Since tests don't run on PRs (#974), the guard never saw it until now.

The sniff moves behind a new gateway helper, `io::read_file_head(path, max)`: `check_read`, then at most `max` bytes from the start. `read_file_capped` would have been the obvious home for this, but it rejects files larger than the cap, and a format sniff must not — a 50 MB document still gets its first 64 KiB read. `is_word_2003_file` keeps its exact semantics: any error reads as "not Word 2003".

Validation:

- `cargo test -p wordcraft-engine commands_do_not_touch` green with the change, failing on plain 0.7.0 (`fc41918`, reproduced before fixing).
- New test `io::tests::read_file_head_reads_at_most_max_bytes_from_the_start`: a 4 KiB file read with `max = 1024` returns exactly the first 1024 bytes; a shorter-than-`max` file reads whole; a missing path errors.
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-engine` green (435 passed); `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` clean; `cargo xtask ci` green (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm).

Not in this PR: `tests::clicks_on_ribbon_and_status_bar_chrome_keep_typing_in_the_document` also fails at 0.7.0 on Windows — filed separately, it is unrelated to the gateway (reproduced on plain `fc41918`).

title: Scroll the selected command into view in Customize Keyboard
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1696

## Cause
The Commands and Categories lists in Customize Keyboard never scrolled to the selected row. Opening the dialog, changing category (which selects that category's first command) or having a stale scroll offset could leave the selected command off-screen, so Assign and Remove targeted a command the user couldn't see.

## Fix
`list()` now calls `scroll_to_rect` on the selected row whenever the selection or the row set changes. Scrolling by hand doesn't change the selection and isn't overridden, because the scroll runs only on a change. The target position is the row's index times the row step, measured from the top of the visible row range.

## Verified
- Regression tests `selected_command_is_scrolled_into_view`, `changing_category_shows_the_new_selection`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui --lib dialogs_keyboard::tests`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The '<location> · <id>' line under the lists already shows the command that Assign targets, so it is unchanged. The selection model and the `tools.customizeKeyboard` command are unchanged.

title: UI: Font dropdown list height doesn't update when filter results increase
author: mbaksa
body:
### Problem

When filtering the font dropdown, the list correctly shrinks as the number of matching fonts decreases. However, when characters are deleted and more fonts match the filter, the dropdown remains at its previous height instead of expanding.

For example, filtering for _Arial_ reduces the list to a few rows (three in my case), but changing the filter back to _Aria_ leaves the dropdown at the same height (three rows), even though more results are available. In some instances, the list could shrink to just two rows and a bit, for example when I filer for _Segoe Print_.

So, essentially, the list shrinks, but it doesn't grow back when filter is lessened.

### Fix

Explicitly set the minimum UI height using `ui.set_min_height(desired_h)`.

This allows the dropdown to expand when the number of matching results increases, while `ScrollArea::max_height()` continues to limit its maximum height.

### Tests
#### Automatic tests
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — OK
- [x] `cargo check --workspace` — OK
- [x] `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui` — OK - 411 tests (ok. 410 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 27.36s), 6 tests (6 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.01s)

#### Manual test:

1. Select font name in edit box for font selection so that you can type over it
2. Type _Calibri_ → 2 rows should be displayed in a dropdown font list (Calibri, and Calibri Light; the number depends on which fonts user has installed)
3. Start pressing Backspace → 2 rows until...
4. When it only say _Cal_ → 3 rows (Caladera, Calibri, and Calibri Light) - before fix it displayed 2.5 rows
5. Another Backspace, so it says only _Ca_ → 15 rows (full list) - before fix it displayed 2.5 rows

title: Keep ruby annotations (furigana) in HTML export
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1681

## Cause
Paragraph flattening in `formats/src/model.rs` had no case for ruby objects, so they fell into the catch-all that keeps only the base text. The `Inline` enum had no ruby variant, and the HTML writer had no ruby arm, so the reading was dropped.

## Fix
Added an `Inline::Ruby { base, ruby, fmt }` variant, which the flattening step now produces. The HTML writer emits `<ruby>base<rp>(</rp><rt>reading</rt><rp>)</rp></ruby>` with escaped text and the run's formatting. The `<rp>` parentheses make browsers without ruby support show `道(みち)` instead of `道みち`. An empty reading writes just the base text. TXT, Markdown, ODT and RTF go through `equations_as_text`, which turns ruby into its formatted base text, so their output is unchanged. LaTeX writes the base text directly. The regression test checks the HTML, TXT, Markdown, ODT and RTF output. A unit test in `html.rs` covers escaping and the empty-reading case.

## Verified
- Regression test `ruby_annotations_survive_html_export`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-formats ruby_annotations_survive_html_export`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Ruby is not written to ODT, RTF, Markdown or LaTeX. Those formats still write only the base text. HTML import is also unchanged and does not read `<ruby>` back.

title: Outline view: draw a long sheet in tiles so it isn't blurry (#1531)
author: maxm11
body:
Fixes #1531

## What was wrong

Draft, Outline and Web Layout lay the whole document on **one long sheet** — a single `Page` whose height is the whole document (`crates/layout/src/lib.rs`). The canvas rasterised each page into **one** texture, and clamped the raster scale so that the whole texture fitted the GPU's limit:

```rust
// crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs (before)
let scale_px = (geo.scale * ppp)
    .min(max_tex / page.w.max(1.0))
    .min(max_tex / page.h.clamp(1.0, 1e6))   // <- shrinks the whole sheet
    .max(0.05);
```

`max_texture_side` is the device limit (`egui-wgpu` asks for 8192). On a 2× display at 100% zoom the screen wants 2.67 device pixels per point, so the moment a sheet passes `8192 / 2.67 ≈ 3072 pt` — about four pages — the scale is clamped and the *whole* sheet is drawn from a texture far smaller than the screen. The 2,759-word report in the screenshot is a few thousand points tall, so its text was drawn at roughly a third of the screen's resolution: everything on the page, including the outline symbols, looked blurry. Any long document showed it, not only that file.

## What changed

- `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`: a page taller than one texture is rasterised in **vertical tiles**, each within the texture limit and drawn at the full screen scale. `page_tile_count` cuts the sheet (whole device pixels, contiguous); each tile is rendered with `render_area` over its slice of the page and placed at the device pixel it belongs to, so a tile is drawn 1:1 and tiles abut exactly.
- The canvas' scale is no longer clamped by the page height, only by the page width.
- An ordinary page (Print Layout at any normal zoom) is **one tile** and is placed exactly as before, so nothing else changes.
- Textures are keyed by `(page, tile)`. A tile is rendered only when it is on screen or already cached, and the tiles a page no longer has (the sheet got shorter, or was zoomed so it needs fewer) are dropped along with the pages scrolled out of view, so the cach…

title: Options: default paste behavior per situation (#1727)
author: tarpescu
body:
Fixes #1727.

## What

File > Options > Advanced gains a **Cut, copy, and paste** section with four dropdowns (as in Word):

- Pasting within the same document: Keep Source Formatting (default) / Merge Formatting / Keep Text Only
- Pasting between documents: Keep Source Formatting (default) / Merge Formatting / Keep Text Only
- Pasting between documents when style definitions conflict: Keep Source Formatting / **Use Destination Styles** (default) / Merge Formatting / Keep Text Only
- Pasting from other programs: **Merge Formatting** (default) / Keep Source Formatting / Keep Text Only

They are saved between runs (in the editing preferences / `ui.json`) and apply to **Ctrl+V** and **Home > Paste**; the specific Paste commands (`edit.pasteMerge`, `edit.pasteText`) stay explicit overrides.

## How the default is chosen

`edit.paste` asks where the clipboard content came from:
- **same document** - a copy whose source document id matches the open document
- **between documents** - our own copy from another WordCraft document (a copy now records the document id it came from)
- **style clash** - between documents, when the fragment names a style the destination also defines
- **other programs** - anything else on the system clipboard

`file.options` reads and sets the four settings (`pasteSameDocument`, `pasteBetweenDocuments`, `pasteStyleConflict`, `pasteFromOtherPrograms`), refusing unknown values without changing anything; the pane sets them through the same command agents use.

## Testing

- `default_paste_format_follows_the_clipboards_origin` (engine): between-document Keep Text Only; a shared style name uses the clash default.
- `paste_keeps_source_formatting_from_other_programs` updated: other programs now default to Merge Formatting (Word's default), and Keep Source keeps the font.
- `default_paste_settings_round_trip` (options): command round-trips, junk refused, saved/restored.
- `options_panes_open_and_change_settings` also checks the section renders.
- Labels …

title: Tables nest 24 deep at most, so pasting a table into its own cell can't build a document that crashes (#1596)
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #1596

Pasting a table into its own cell doubles the nesting each time; about a dozen pastes build a document that overflows the stack when it is saved as JSON, copied, closed or replaced by a new one (numbers in #1596, lower with the 1 MiB MSVC stack).

Tables now nest 24 deep at most, the depth the .docx reader (`MAX_TABLE_DEPTH`) and writer (`MAX_DEPTH`) already keep (`wordcraft_doc::table::MAX_TABLE_DEPTH`):

- `Document::insert_fragment` (paste, Insert › Text from File, Quick Parts, Zotero) fits what it inserts: a table that would go deeper arrives as its paragraphs, in document order, with their text and formatting, much as the .docx reader turns a deeper table into text.
- `Document::insert_block` refuses a table that would go deeper, so Insert › Table in a cell 24 tables deep fails with "tables can't nest more than 24 deep" in the status bar and leaves the document as it was (`Session::run` restores it).
- The depth is measured without recursion, since a pasted fragment can be deep.

Checked against Word (2019, Windows): Word nests without a limit (3,000 levels inserted one at a time, 4,096 by pasting, and it opens files 2,000 deep). WordCraft already reads and writes .docx tables to 24 levels, so editing now stops at the same depth.

Not covered: a text box keeps its own story, so tables in a text box count from the text box; the .docx writer counts both together. JSON documents still open to 20 levels only (serde_json's recursion limit), unchanged.

**Tests**
- `crates/doc`: `tables_nest_at_most_max_table_depth` (24 tables nest, a 25th is refused and changes nothing, a table holding a table doesn't fit one level up); `pasting_a_table_into_its_own_cell_stops_at_max_table_depth` (the #1596 steps: eight rounds of copying everything and pasting it into the deepest cell; the nesting stops at 24 and all 256 copies of the text are there). Both fail with the limit switched off.
- `crates/engine`: `tables_nest_at_most_24_deep` (Insert › Table 24 tables deep …

title: Tests: a table that starts mid-page never leaves a repeated header row alone (#1704)
author: albayazid
body:
Tests-only follow-up to #1705, which fixed #1704 by moving a table's repeated header rows to the next page together with the first body row. That merged fix handles the issue's repro; this PR adds a sweep test that pins the contract across page-boundary configurations and table geometries instead of one hand-picked case.

For six table geometries — height ratios (100/400, 300/100, 50/250), a `cantSplit` body row, an exact-height body row, and a two-row header — the test lays the table out after filler counts sweeping the page boundary (60 counts for the primary geometry, coarser steps for the rest) and asserts for every configuration, while the table continues onto a next page:

- no page ends with only header rows (the #1704 symptom), with #1705's top-of-page exemption noted;
- no row is dropped — every row of the table is placed somewhere.

Plus: a start that fits keeps the header and the first body row together on the page. No production code is touched; #1705's implementation already satisfies the sweep on current main, and the top-of-page exemption keeps the existing pinned behaviour (a 300 pt header at the top of a letter page) intact.

Validation:

- The sweep fails on the code before #1705 with the issue's orphan (`a page ends with the header row alone`), checked during development against the pre-#1705 base — so it pins the merged behaviour rather than passing vacuously.
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout` green (332 passed, including #1705's own tests); `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` clean; `cargo xtask ci` run to completion — the only failures are the two pre-existing `crates/render` colour-emoji tests filed as #1874 (environment-dependent; `crates/render` untouched by this PR).

title: Fonts: bold Arial Black is not emboldened again, as in Word
author: naxvog
body:
Bold text set in Arial Black was drawn heavier than in Word.

**Cause.** WordCraft adds synthetic bold when the face it finds for bold text is lighter than semibold (`word::resolve`, `weight < 600`). Older releases of Arial Black, such as the one in the widely installed core-fonts package, say weight 400 in their OS/2 table. Current releases say 900. So bold Arial Black was emboldened a second time. Word draws it unchanged: in the Word reference PDF of the docxide-pdf fixture `scraped/nabl_lab_preassessment_guidelines`, the bold Arial Black run uses plain Arial-Black with no fill-and-stroke text.

**Fix.** `make_face` reads a static face's weight through a new `static_weight`. If the file says less than 600, the last word of the family name decides: Black or Heavy is 900, ExtraBold or UltraBold is 800. A file that already declares a heavy weight keeps its own value, so for example an 800 "Heavy" doesn't become 900. Variable-font instances are unchanged. Raising the weight in the font database, instead of special-casing `resolve`, keeps face matching, fallback ordering and the fallback emboldening in `layout::para` consistent with each other.

Only Arial Black has been checked against Word. Other Black and Heavy families follow the same naming, but their old and new releases weren't compared.

**Test.** `fontdb::tests::a_family_named_for_a_heavy_weight_is_that_heavy` loads bundled faces under these names and checks the weight:

| Family name | Weight |
|---|---|
| Arial Black | 900 |
| Franklin Gothic Heavy (with a trailing space) | 900 |
| Segoe UI ExtraBold | 800 |
| Blackadder ITC | 400 |
| Arial | 400 |
| A 600-weight face named "… Heavy" | stays 600 |

A render of a document with a bold Arial Black heading, using the core-fonts Arial Black, went from two fill-and-stroke runs to none. The heading now matches Word's Windows PDF.

title: Layout: less memory on long tables
author: dfgodvan
body:
## Problem
Laying out one long table of short cells (synthetic: 5000 rows x 4 columns, one line of text per cell, 120 Letter pages) holds much more heap than the pages need, and the pass peaks well above what it keeps:
1. `place_table` lays the whole table out, then **copies** every row's items onto the pages. The laid-out table (`tl.rows`) lives until the last row is placed, so the table is held twice while it is placed.
2. A `ParaLayout` lives as long as the document doesn't change (in `LayoutCache` and, through `Arc`, on the pages), but its `glyphs`, `clusters`, `styles`, `issues`, `lines` and each line's `xs` keep the spare capacity they doubled to while the paragraph was shaped and broken into lines. Many short paragraphs make that a large share of the layout.
3. Every page's `items` keeps the spare capacity it doubled to while the page was filled (on the repro: capacity 243 776 for 122 857 items; `Placed` is 176 bytes).

## Fix
One commit each, `crates/layout` only:
- **Rows move onto the pages** (`lib.rs`, `place_table`). The rows are taken out of the table layout (`std::mem::take(&mut tl.rows)`) and placed by value; `place` moves the items onto the page, translated in place. Only the header rows, which repeat on each page, are copied (once up front, then cloned per repeat, as before).
