title: PDF tests read ActualText spans, so RTL extraction no longer depends on the installed Arabic font (#1773)
author: Sriram-PR
body:
Fixes #1773.

`right_to_left_text_extracts_in_logical_order` fails on Linux machines where Noto Naskh Arabic is the first Arabic font in `RTL_FALLBACKS`. The exported PDF is fine. The problem is in the test helper.

Noto Naskh draws a dotted letter as a dotless body plus a separate dot glyph, and other letters reuse the same body. ToUnicode can only map a glyph to one string, so when a cluster can't be spelled from its glyphs' entries, krilla wraps it in an ActualText span. `stream_glyphs` only looked at ToUnicode, so inside the span it took the body glyph's own entry as well as the cluster's text. On my machine that turned مَرْحَبًا into مَرْحَببًا. rabis7575 got السالم for السلام, which looks like the same thing with their Noto Naskh build. Vazirmatn draws these letters as single glyphs, so the span never came up where the test was written.

I checked the same PDF in other extractors. PDFium (pypdfium2), poppler (`pdftotext`) and mupdf all read the span and give ب once. pdf.js doesn't use ActualText, so it does show the doubled letter. It also outputs U+0003 for the dot glyph, which has no ToUnicode entry. That part is down to how krilla writes ToUnicode, so I've left it out of this PR.

Changes, all test-only in `crates/pdf/src/tests.rs`:
- `stream_glyphs` pre-scans each page's BMC/BDC operators for `/ActualText`. Inside a span, the first glyph gets the span's text and the rest get none, which is how PDFium and poppler read it.
- New `stream_glyphs_read_actual_text` test. It draws one bundled Source Sans 3 glyph twice with the texts "A" and "B", which makes krilla write an ActualText span, so it works whatever fonts are installed. It reads `["A", "A"]` without the change.

Testing: `cargo test -p wordcraft-pdf` passes (37 tests), including all four RTL tests, on Fedora 44 with Noto Naskh Arabic. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-pdf --all-targets -D warnings` are clean. I didn't run `cargo xtask wasm` because the change is test-only.

title: Escape block syntax after manual line breaks in Markdown export
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/formats/src/markdown.rs:1222` (no existing issue): Markdown export: lines after a manual line break aren't escaped, so a paragraph comes back as a list or heading.

## Cause
Markdown export writes a manual line break as a trailing backslash plus newline, but `escape_line_start` only escaped block syntax at the start of the whole paragraph. A line after a break that started with `- `, `1. `, `# `, `---`, `==` or `--` was read back as a list item, heading, thematic break or setext underline, so the paragraph was split or lost text.

## Fix
A new `escape_lines` helper runs `escape_line_start` on every line after a manual break. Plain paragraphs, quotes and list items now use it. List items are escaped before the continuation indent is added. A line made only of hyphens (like `--`) is now also escaped because it would otherwise be read as a setext underline.

## Verified
- Regression tests `lines_after_line_break_stay_in_paragraph`, `lines_after_line_break_stay_in_list_item_and_quote`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-formats --lib lines_after_line_break`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Title paragraphs still join their lines with spaces, and code spans in list items are unchanged.

title: Fonts: ✅ and other emoji-by-default characters fall back to a colour emoji font before a black-and-white symbol font (#1754)
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #1754
Closes #1874

With Segoe UI Emoji and Segoe UI Symbol both installed, ✅ fell back to Segoe UI Symbol and was drawn in black and white beside a colour 🧠: looking for 🧠 loads Segoe UI Symbol on the way to Segoe UI Emoji, and the fallback takes the first loaded face that covers a character. The two colour emoji tests from #1504 failed there (`both emoji use the colour emoji font`, 1 ≠ 2), as #1874 reports on Windows.

A character with Unicode's `Emoji_Presentation` (✅, ☕, 🧠; not ©, ☺ or ✓) now prefers a colour emoji family (Segoe UI Emoji, Apple Color Emoji, Noto Color Emoji):
- among the loaded faces, ahead of the other ranks;
- when a system font is loaded for it, before the usual fallback list;
- and when only a black-and-white face covers it so far, an installed colour emoji font is loaded.

Other characters choose their fallback as before. Firefox's font matching does the same (its reftest `layout/reftests/font-matching/emoji-fallback-3.html` lists symbol fonts first and expects colour emoji). title: Read ^0nnn character codes 128-159 as Windows-1252 characters
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/find_pattern.rs:97` (no existing issue): Find: ^0nnn character codes (e.g. ^0151 for an em dash) are searched as literal text instead of the character.

## Cause
`numeric_code` passed the decimal value of `^nnn`/`^0nnn` straight to `char::from_u32`. For 128–159 this gives C1 control characters (e.g. `^0151` became U+0097). The control filter rejected these, so the code was searched for, or inserted, as the literal text `^0151`.

## Fix
Added an `ansi` helper that maps codes 128–159 to their Windows-1252 characters (151 to U+2014 em dash, 128 to U+20AC € and so on). `numeric_code` uses it for `^nnn`/`^0nnn` codes, but not for `^unnnn` codes. This covers Find, wildcard Find and Replace with, since all three go through `numeric_code`.

## Verified
- Regression test `ansi_codes_128_to_159_are_windows_1252`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --lib ansi_codes_128_to_159_are_windows_1252`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`^unnnn` Unicode codes still use the Unicode value as is. The five undefined Windows-1252 slots (129, 141, 143, 144, 157) and every code outside 128–159 behave as before.

title: Tables: a header's or footer's tables resize with the mouse (#1930)
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #1930.

Tables in a header or footer couldn't be resized. The table mouse looked only at the cells the page draws in its body (`Page::items`), while the layout draws a header's and footer's tables in `Page::header` / `Page::footer`. So their column and row borders, the resize handle and double-click AutoFit didn't react, the rulers showed no table markers, and Table Layout › Cell Size found no drawn cell: it showed a 0 height for a row without a set height, which its box raised to its 0.02" minimum and wrote to the row as soon as the tab was shown.

## What changes
- **What the mouse reaches:** the header's and footer's tables while one of them is being edited, the rest of the page's otherwise, i.e. whatever isn't dimmed on screen. Their borders, the resize handle, double-click AutoFit and the ruler markers work as in the main text.
- **The caret table's handles** (shown while the caret is in a table): a header's or footer's table is drawn on every page that shows it, and its handles show only on the caret's page; there a press on the handle scales the table. On the other pages its borders still drag, and nothing shows or grabs at the handle's spot. It has no move handle (see Not in this PR).
- **Escape during a drag** on the page or the ruler (a table border, the table, an object, a link, a tab stop) goes no further than the drag: with the caret in a header it used to close the header too. Escape also ends Create Link's wait for a click when the pointer is off the page; with a menu or popup open, Escape closes only that.
- **Cell Size** finds the caret's cell in the header and footer too, measured on the caret's page (a header is not always drawn alike: another section's page width, a page number field), or on the first page that draws it when that one doesn't. Its boxes no longer clamp the value they show, so in Draft or Web Layout, where an open header's table isn't laid out, showing them writes nothing.

title: File › Close closes the document and keeps the window (#1712)
author: D13GOOOO
body:
Fixes #1712. This replaces #1725, which @Silvertree2010 closed so this branch could go in. Thanks!

## What was wrong

File › Close (Mod+W, Mod+F4) quit the whole app. `file.close` pushed a `close` UI request, and `handle_request` turned every such request into `quit_requested = true`, which is the same thing the window's close button does. In Word, Close closes the document and the window stays.

## Change (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`, no engine change)

`WordApp::execute` now handles `file.close` itself (`close_document`):

- After the usual Save / Don't Save / Cancel, the document is replaced by the placeholder blank document that marks "no document open" (#1129), and the Backstage closes. The window then shows no page, the ribbon is greyed out but for Help, and File › New or Open goes on from there, as in Word after closing its last document.
- The window's close button (`close_requested`) passes `{"quit": true}`, so it still asks first and then quits. The parameter travels with the prompt's pending command, so a Cancel leaves no state behind.
- With no document open, Close has nothing to close and does nothing. The window's close button still quits from there.
- The engine's `file.close` is untouched. That keeps this PR clear of #1391's `force` guard, which is now on `main`. That guard still applies: a programmatic close of unsaved work needs `force`, and then closes the document rather than the app.

## Tests

- `tests::close_asks_then_closes_the_document_and_keeps_the_window`: Cancel keeps the document. Don't Save closes it and the window stays. Closing the empty window asks nothing, a second Close does nothing, and File › New goes on.

author: dkhlapov

title: Zotero bridge edits respect protection and tracked changes (#1323)
author: dkhlapov
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"dkhlapov"} -->
_Requested by **Dima**_

Fixes #1323.

Before: the Zotero bridge edited the document model directly. Inserting, refreshing, converting or removing citations, bibliographies and Zotero preferences skipped Restrict Editing, content-control locks and Track Changes. So Zotero could change a read-only document, and its edits never became revisions that Reject could undo.

After: every Zotero call that changes the document runs through a new engine entry, `Session::guarded_edit`. It applies the same rules as normal commands and is one transaction: a refused call puts back the document, the selection, undo and the bridge's field ids.
- **Read-only and comments-only documents:** Zotero edits are refused, except inside the editable regions the user may change.
- **Forms protection:** edits are allowed only inside fillable content controls.
- **Locked content controls:** edits there are refused.
- **Track Changes, or the "tracked changes" protection:** Zotero's inserts and deletions are recorded as revisions, so Reject All restores the original text and Accept All keeps Zotero's text.

**Tests** (`crates/zotero/src/tests.rs`, real bridge calls; all 8 failed before the fix): `read_only_protection_refuses_every_zotero_edit`, `comments_protection_refuses_every_zotero_edit`, `read_only_exception_takes_a_citation_but_the_rest_refuses_one`, `forms_protection_refuses_zotero_edits_outside_fillable_controls`, `locked_content_controls_refuse_zotero_edits`, `track_changes_records_zotero_edits_as_revisions`, `tracked_changes_protection_records_zotero_edits_as_revisions`, `tracked_inserted_text_never_takes_a_deletion_mark`. `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps passed.

title: Zotero transport: write deadline and cumulative bounds (#1332)
author: dkhlapov
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"dkhlapov"} -->
_Requested by **Dima**_

Fixes #1332.

Before: the Zotero transport set a read timeout only. It looped over frames and kept every error, and the UI waited for replies with no limit and kept a method history until the command finished. A program on Zotero's port that stopped reading, trickled bytes, or sent calls or errors forever could keep WordCraft "busy" indefinitely and grow its memory without bound. The 32 MiB frame cap didn't bound a whole session.

After:
- **Time limits:**
  - 60 s to send a reply (the clock starts after the reply is built);
  - 60 s to finish a frame once its first byte arrives;
  - 60 min with no messages;
  - 4 h for a whole command.
  Zotero's own citation dialog can stay open for minutes; only the 60 min idle limit applies then.
- **Caps:**
  - 200,000 calls per command;
  - 20 stored errors of 500 bytes each, with the rest counted;
  - 200 history entries, each method name cut to 128 bytes (at a character boundary);
  - Zotero's question text cut to 2,000 bytes;
  - only the first 20 failed calls logged per command.
- **Cancel:** while a command runs, the status bar shows "Waiting for Zotero…" and a Cancel link (`ui.zotero.cancel`). It works with no document open, hangs up the connection and always clears the busy state, as does a connection thread that ends without reporting.

**Tests:** `crates/zotero/src/tests.rs` uses a local fake peer. The tests cover a peer that stops reading, a frame dripped byte by byte, endless calls, endless errors, the overall limit and cancel; all 6 failed (hung or grew without bound) before the fix. In `crates/ui-egui/src/zotero.rs`, three tests failed with their fixes reverted: Cancel clears busy and hangs up; the status bar cancels a running command; a thread that ends without reporting still clears busy. Also `the_call_history_is_bounded_in_count_and_bytes` and `a_transport_error_clears_busy`. The tests take about 1.2 s and were stable ov…

title: Tables: at-least rows taller than a page start on a fresh page; header rows follow (#1742)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1742.

## What was wrong
A table row with an "at least" height that was taller than a whole page was cut into whatever space was left at the bottom of the current page. Word moves it to a fresh page first and only splits it from there. Repeated header rows didn't follow a first row that moved on.

The basic case, an at-least row whose minimum fits on one page, was already fixed on main by #1618: it moves to the next page whole. This PR covers the rest of the issue.

## What changed (`crates/layout/src/lib.rs`, table placement)

- Repeated header rows go with a first row that moves on.
- A row already at the top of a page or column never moves on, so pagination always progresses. A row can move on at most once, and the existing loop cap stays.

title: The caret and clicks land between the letters of a ligature (#1974)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1974.

## What was wrong
When a font draws several letters as one shape (a ligature, such as "fi" or "ffi" in Calibri), the caret, mouse clicks and selection edges couldn't stop between those letters. The whole ligature's width sat on its first letter and the other letters had none, so the caret was always drawn after the whole shape. In Word, the caret goes between the letters (checked on Word for Mac 16.113.4).

## What changed (`crates/layout/src/para.rs`, `split_ligature_advances`)
- After shaping, the ligature's width, including each letter's character spacing, is split evenly among the letters it draws. The caret, clicks (to the nearest inner boundary) and selection highlight edges all use these split positions. The right arrow already moved one letter at a time, and now the caret visibly moves too.
- In right-to-left text (for example the Arabic lam-alef ligature) the split is mirrored, and the glyph still starts at the ligature's left edge.
- A grapheme cluster is never split. That covers a letter with a combining mark, an emoji ZWJ sequence and an Indic conjunct.
- The ligature's total width is unchanged, including with expanded or condensed character spacing, so line breaks don't move.

## Tests (`crates/layout/src/tests_ligature.rs`, `crates/engine/src/tests_typing.rs`)
Against main's code these fail, and they pass with this change:
- `caret_between_the_letters_of_a_ligature_is_inside_it`

author: dkhlapov
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"dkhlapov"} -->
_Requested by **Dima**_

Fixes #1670.

Before: a STYLEREF field in a header showing the Hebrew heading "פרק א" drew it backwards ("א קרפ"). A field's result was shaped as one unit, and its pieces were placed left to right in stored order, so the paragraph's bidi pass never reordered the inside of a field.

title: A mouse drag on a table no longer scrolls the view to the caret (#1738)
author: dkhlapov
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"dkhlapov"} -->
_Requested by **Dima**_

Fixes #1738.

Before: with the caret on page 1 and a table on page 2, dragging the table's column or row border to resize it made the view jump back to the caret, as did dragging the table's move handle. Every command except view, draw and a few others asked the canvas to follow the caret afterwards.

title: M1: input-method compositions are laid out in the text (#1888)
author: ngotuankhoi
body:
Fixes #1888.

## Problem
An input-method composition (the preedit) was drawn as an overlay at the caret. That caused three problems:
- It covered the text that follows the caret.
- It used the UI font instead of the document's font.
- Clicking elsewhere moved the composition along with the caret, because the preedit was never committed.

The composition also went stale when the window lost focus (for example, to a screenshot tool). After that, typed spaces landed before the uncommitted word.

## Fix
- **Engine** (`Session`): the new `set_composition` / `end_composition` / `composition` calls place the preedit in the document as a transient edit.
  - The edit is a snapshot plus `type_text`. It adds no undo step and doesn't mark the document dirty.
  - It is rolled back at the start of every `Session::run`, so commands, saves and undo never see it.
  - It reuses `EditSnapshot` / `restore`.
- **Canvas:**
  - Before layout, the canvas syncs the preedit into the session, so it is laid out like normal text: it uses the run's font and pushes the following text along.
  - It draws an underline from the selection rects.
  - The old overlay remains only for equations and protected documents, where a transient edit isn't allowed.
- **Keys:** the preedit is committed where it is when either of these happens:
  - a mouse press
  - `WindowFocused(false)` (macOS IMEs drop their composition when the IME is disabled on focus loss)
- `ui_shot` gains a `{"preedit": "…"}` script line for headless checks.
- `docs/typing-parity.md` gains an "Input methods" section, and `ROADMAP.md` has a progress-log row.

## Tests
- `tests_typing::composition_sits_in_the_text_until_committed`
- `canvas::tests::a_click_commits_the_composition_where_it_was`
- `canvas::tests::leaving_the_window_commits_the_composition`

`cargo xtask ci` passes all six steps (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

title: Copy puts list numbers and bullets in the clipboard's text (#2015)
author: D13GOOOO
body:
Fixes #2015.

## What was wrong

When you copied a numbered or bulleted list and pasted it into another program as plain text, the numbers and bullets were missing. Copy took its text from the copied fragment. Once that fragment becomes a document of its own (`Fragment::to_document`), it no longer has the source document's list definitions, so it has no labels to write.

## Change

**`Document::copy_text`** (`crates/doc/src/edit.rs`) builds Copy's plain text from the source document. Each copied list paragraph starts with its label and the character after it: `1.` and a tab, `•` and a tab, or a space or nothing, following the level's suffix.

- The labels come from `numbering::Counters`, counted from the top of the body in reading order (table paragraphs included), the same way layout counts them. So they read as the page shows them: start overrides, levels and restarts all apply.
- The label is inserted in the level's own font (`Level::chr`). A Symbol-font bullet such as `\u{F0B7}`, which is how Word documents store them, therefore comes out as `•` through the existing symbol mapping in `shown_text`.
- Which paragraphs get a label: a paragraph gets one when its start is copied along with some of its text. It gets none when it's copied from its middle, or when the selection only reaches its start. A selection inside a single paragraph gets the label only when it covers the whole paragraph.
- Not yet covered: paragraphs in tables, headers and notes keep their plain text without labels. Copy falls back to the old text there.

**Paste** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/paste.rs`) recognises our own copy by comparing the system clipboard's text with the text Copy actually put there (`s.clipboard_text`). It used to recompute that text from the fragment, so with labels the two would no longer match, and pasting a copied list back into WordCraft would have inserted `1.	Item 1` as typed text instead of the list. A column copy (`column.rs`) already stored a text different from the fr…

title: Copy a list with its numbers and bullets
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #2015.

## The bug

Copying a numbered or bulleted list and pasting it into another editor dropped the labels. The `.txt` export already wrote them, so the two disagreed about the same list:

```
clipboard (numbered)  "Item 1\nItem 2"
.txt export           "1.\tItem 1\r\n2.\tItem 2"
clipboard (bulleted)  "Item 1\nItem 2"
```

## The change

`blocks_text` takes the newline to use and reports whether it labelled anything; `export` is now one call to the line builder, and Copy is another with `\n`. So Copy and Save as `.txt` produce the same text apart from the line ending each of them wants — a test asserts that directly rather than restating the expected string twice.

Three things the route had to go around, each found by a failing test rather than by reading:

- **Layering.** `ListCounter` is in `formats` (L2) and `Fragment::clipboard_text` is in `doc` (L1), so the label cannot be added where the text walk lives. `copy` in `engine` can see both.
- **Resolved properties.** `from_doc` reads the *style-resolved* paragraph properties, so my first gate — `p.props.numbering.is_some()` in `engine` — missed a list applied through a style and labelled nothing. The exporter now reports what it labelled, which cannot drift from what it renders.
- **A `Fragment` carries no styles or numbering definitions.** Its `to_document()` builds a default `Document`, so `numbering.level(..)` returned `None` and no label resolved even once the gate was right. The labels are resolved against the document the copy came from, which `copy` still has in hand.

## Scoped to lists on purpose

With no list in the copy, Copy keeps `Fragment::clipboard_text()` unchanged. That guard is there for a reason I checked rather than assumed: the plain-text rendering of a table is not the same as the clipboard's — `"\t\r\n\t\r\nbefore\r\nafter"` against what the clipboard produces for the same selection — so an unconditional switch would have moved table copies too, which this issue does not ask for.

title: Insert › Shapes keeps the selected shape and text (#2019)
author: D13GOOOO
body:
Fixes #2019.

## What was wrong

Inserting a second shape removed the first. After an insert, the new shape stays selected, and `insert.shape` replaced the selection (`delete_selection`), so each shape replaced the one before it. The same command could also delete selected text.

## What Word does

Checked by hand in Word for Windows (Microsoft 365):

| | Word | WordCraft before | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Insert › Shapes twice | the second shape is drawn over the first, which stays | the first is gone | both kept |
| Insert › Pictures twice, with the first still selected | the second picture **replaces** the first | replaced | unchanged |

So the report holds for shapes. For pictures, replacing the selected one matches Word, and `insert.picture` is unchanged. #1664 pointed out the same picture case and left it alone. This PR doesn't change it either, but now there's a test pinning it.

## Change (`crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs`)

`insert.shape` no longer deletes the selection. The new shape goes after it and becomes the selection, so a selected shape or selected text stays. The ribbon's Insert › Shapes menu runs this command, so the app gets the fix too. A selected Drawing Canvas still takes the shape in (#344).

## Tests (`crates/engine/src/cmd/objects.rs`)

- `shapes_inserted_in_a_row_are_all_kept_and_keep_selected_text`:
  - three shapes in a row give three objects; with the old code only 1 of 3 is kept;
  - a shape inserted over selected text keeps the text, and the new shape is selected.
- `an_inserted_picture_replaces_a_selected_picture`: pins Word's picture behaviour.
- `docs/target-app-parity.md`: status line and revision history.

## Checked

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo xtask assets`, `layers` and `wasm` pass. `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` passes except for the two colour-emoji render tests. Those fail the same way on unmodified `main` on Windows; it's tracked as #1874 and fixed in #1983…

title: DOCX: a style ID defined twice is its last definition
author: Morzilla
body:
## What and why

Some generators write a placeholder Heading 1 and then their own,
under the same w:styleId. The reader kept the first definition and
skipped the rest, so headings came out in the placeholder's font,
size and colour. Word uses the last definition, whole: a synthetic
document with an italic red 20 pt first definition and a bold blue
12 pt second one shows bold blue 12 pt, with nothing of the first
(no italic, no centring), for a custom style and for Heading 1 alike.

The reader now replaces an earlier definition in place instead of
skipping the later one.

## Tests

title: A floating object's anchor takes no room on a line
author: Morzilla
body:
## What and why

A line's first item stays on it even when it is wider than the line;
markers before it don't count. A floating object's anchor (a zero-size
object cluster) did count, so a picture a little wider than the line,

title: Floating objects are drawn in their stacking order (relativeHeight)
author: Morzilla
body:
## What and why

Word stacks floating objects by wp:anchor/@relativeHeight, not by the
order of their anchors in the paragraph. The reader ignored the
attribute, so a panel anchored after the text boxes it frames, but
lower in the stack, was drawn over them and hid their text.

- wordcraft-doc: Float gets a `z` (0 = none, drawn in document order).
- wordcraft-docx: it is read from relativeHeight and written back as
  read; an object without one gets the next order above, as before.
- wordcraft-layout: place_objects collects each object's items with
  its order and emits them lowest first (stable, so objects without an
  order keep the paragraph's).

Four round-trip tests compare whole floats after a save; saving now
gives objects without an order one, so those tests compare without it
(`unstacked`). The order itself is covered by its own round-trip test.

## Tests

`anchor_stacking_order_is_read_and_kept` (`crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs`) reads relativeHeight and keeps it through a save; `floats_are_drawn_in_their_stacking_order` (`crates/layout/src/tests.rs`) checks the drawing order with and without orders.

title: Symbols keep their symbol font when the text font changes (#2036)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #2036 (follow-up to #776).

## What was wrong
A symbol from a DOCX `w:sym` (for example a Wingdings ✓) or from Insert › Symbol stored its symbol font as the run's ordinary font. If you then selected all text and changed the font, or used Clear Formatting, that font was overwritten and the symbols turned into boxes. The writer also never wrote `w:sym`, so Word showed boxes too.

## What changed
- **Model:** a character now remembers its symbol font separately from its text font, in a new optional field `CharProps.sym_font`. It's set by the DOCX reader for `w:sym` and by Insert › Symbol. Font commands still change the text font, and the symbol font survives. Old saved JSON without the field still loads.
- **Display and text output:** layout, PDF text, copy-as-text and TXT export map a symbol character through its own symbol font.
- **DOCX writer:** these characters are written back as `<w:sym w:font=… w:char=…/>`, so Word shows them whatever the run's font is. This applies only to printable characters (U+0020 and up).
- **Kept out of ordinary text:** the symbol font doesn't spread to other text through typing, the Format Painter, New Style / Update Style to Match (styles never give text a symbol font), Replace All, AutoCorrect dashes or AutoCorrect word replacements.
- **Phonetic guide:** a guide has one format for its whole base, so it keeps a symbol font only when every base character shares it. Known limit: a mixed base like "✓ab" shows the ✓ as a box. Before this change, the letters and the guide text showed as Wingdings symbols instead. A proper fix needs per-character base formatting, which is outside this PR.

## Tests
- Original fix: `a_sym_character_keeps_its_symbol_font_when_the_text_font_changes`, `an_inserted_symbol_keeps_its_font_when_the_text_font_changes`, `a_sym_character_round_trips_as_w_sym`, `format_painter_does_not_carry_a_symbol_font_to_text`, `symbol_font_is_optional_in_json_and_survives_font_changes`, `hostile_sym_fonts_never_panic`.

author: H0ruu1

## What changed

Two Word features that were catalog-only (`tools.dictate`, `review.translate`) now work, **on the user's own computer**, with model files the user downloads once. Nothing is sent anywhere and the app never downloads anything by itself (README: "Private … work offline").

**Dictate** (Home › Voice › Dictate, now a toggle)

- Dialog: target language, source (auto: script + document language), whole document or selected paragraphs, new untitled document (default, as Word) or this one; shows which model will be used; progress window with Cancel; the result is **one undoable step**. title: Paste Options: change the last paste in place (Keep Source, Keep Text Only, Merge, Picture) (#1747)
author: TheGaBr0
body:
Fixes #1747.

## What

After a paste that could have gone another way, a small **Paste Options (Ctrl)** button
appears under the end of the pasted text. Click it, or tap Ctrl, to redo the paste in place as:

- **Keep Source Formatting** (a paste starts here)
- **Keep Text Only**: plain words in the destination's formatting; table rows become
  comma-separated lines
- **Merge Formatting**: destination font and colour, keeping emphasis, lists and
  style-given bold
- **Picture**: the pasted content drawn as a cropped PNG

The current option is highlighted. The button hides on typing, Esc, moving the caret away,
or when it would fall outside the page area; the menu opens up or down by room. Plain text
shows no button.

## How

- `edit.pasteChange {"mode": "source" | "text" | "merge" | "picture"}`
  (`crates/engine/src/cmd/paste.rs`), enabled only while the offer stands. The engine keeps
  the last paste (range, source fragment, destination formatting from before the paste,
  current option) in `Session::last_paste`; the offer ends on any other edit.
- UI: `crates/ui-egui/src/paste_options.rs` (button, menu, Ctrl tap).
- Related fixes found while testing, in the same PR:
  - HTML import: `background-color: rgb(…)` (browsers' form) and the CSS `font:` shorthand.
  - Pasted paragraphs that state no alignment, indent or spacing take the destination's;
    a browser's computed `text-align: left` is not a choice.
  - HTML tables without widths follow their content (AutoFit) instead of full width.

## Not in this PR

- The options are not listed in the ribbon's Paste dropdown.
- Default paste behaviour per situation is #1727 / #1737, which this is compatible with.

## Tests

`cargo xtask ci` passes. New tests in `crates/engine/src/tests.rs`, `cmd/paste.rs` and
`crates/formats/src/html.rs`; `i18n` catalogs have "Paste Options" in every language.

title: Cmd/Ctrl+click for Independent Selection in Tables
author: eugenezimin
body: ### What was changed In a table's selection areas (above a column, left of a row, a cell's left edge), **Cmd+click** on macOS or **Ctrl+click** elsewhere adds that part to the selection, even when it isn't next to what's already selected, as in Word. - Cmd/Ctrl+click on a part that's already selected takes it out. - A Cmd/Ctrl+drag keeps the earlier selection and adds the cells it passes over. If it started on a selected part, it takes them out instead. - A plain click starts a new selection. Cmd/Ctrl+click inside a cell's text still selects a sentence. ### How - `CellRange` gets `picked: Option>`, which holds scattered cells. When it's set, `rows`/`cols` are the bounds. Rectangles keep `picked: None`, so existing callers are unchanged. - The new `table::select_set` selects any set of cells. A set that fills its bounding rectangle goes through `select_range` as before. - `table.selectAt` takes `"add": true`, so the CLI and MCP can do the same. - The UI sends `add` when `modifiers.command` is held. `table_pick` recognises separate whole rows or columns, which keeps the right-click menu correct. ### Behaviour with scattered cells | Works on just the selected cells | Refused (`Disabled`) | |---|---| | Formatting, shading, alignment, typing, copy, Delete Rows/Columns | Merge Cells, Insert Above/Below | A border drag ignores a scattered selection and moves the border for the whole column. ### Tests - Engine: - `ctrl_clicks_select_rows_apart` covers formatting, undo, shading, refused commands and deleting rows. - `ctrl_clicks_add_and_take_out_columns_and_cells` covers adding, removing, the drag base and the removing drag. - UI: `a_command_click_adds_to_the_selection`. - `cargo xtask ci` is green, and a headless `ui_shot` screenshot showed only the selected cells shaded.

title: Give the status bar zoom percentage a fixed width
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1975

## Cause
The zoom percentage label in the right-to-left part of the status bar was exactly as wide as its own text. When the number gained or lost a digit (9% → 10% → 100%), the label's width changed and moved the zoom buttons, slider, view-mode buttons and Focus to its left by several pixels.

## Fix
The label now always takes at least the width of "000%" plus a 4 px reserve, and its text is right-aligned in that space. Controls to its left stay put at every zoom from 10% to 500%.

title: Open HWPX (Hangul) documents
author: BBQ-MAN
body:
Opens Hancom Hangul **HWPX** documents (`.hwpx`, OWPML / KS X 6101), read-only. Hangul is the standard word processor in Korean government, schools and many companies, and Word does not open these files.

This is part 1 of 2, split as requested in review. The binary HWP 5 format (`.hwp`) follows in a separate PR that builds on this one.

**How**
- `crates/formats/src/hwpx.rs` reads the zip package (the `content.hpf` spine, `header.xml` and the section XML), written from the OWPML schema.
- `crates/formats/src/hangul.rs` is the shared mapping to the document model: character and paragraph shapes, border fills, the table grid built from cell addresses and spans, and page setup. The HWP 5 reader reuses it in part 2.

- `NOTICE` carries rhwp's MIT notice. Its source was consulted for HWPX's HwpUnitChar unit switch.

**What it reads**
- **Text and character formatting:** all text, Korean included. Hangul and Latin faces (the Hangul face goes in the East Asian slot), size, bold, italic, underline, strikeout, colour, shading, super/subscript, spacing and width ratio.

title: proof: compound words, NEEDAFFIX and BREAK in affix dictionaries (#735)
author: Skaywalker
body:
Second step of the `affix.rs` extension from #735, on top of #1859: compound words,
`NEEDAFFIX` and word breaks. The branch contains #1859's commit; the change here is the second
commit (`a040761`), and it rebases cleanly once #1859 is in. With it the Hungarian Hunspell dictionary (`hu_HU`, Magyar Ispell)
loads and checks Hungarian text. As before, nothing is bundled; WordCraft reads the dictionary
installed on the system. The Hungarian proofing module that uses it comes in the next PR.

## What changes

**Parsing a word** (`affix.rs`). Lookups now enumerate every reading of a word: a stem, a stem
with a prefix, one or two suffixes in a row, or a prefix and a suffix. The same bounds as before
apply, and each caller decides which readings count. A standalone word is one that isn't
`FORBIDDENWORD`, `ONLYINCOMPOUND` or a bare `NEEDAFFIX` stem. The Polish, Portuguese, Italian,
Croatian and Turkish behaviour is unchanged (their tests pass as they are).

**Compounds** (`affix/compound.rs`, new):
- `COMPOUNDFLAG`, `COMPOUNDBEGIN`/`FIRST`, `COMPOUNDMIDDLE`, `COMPOUNDEND`/`LAST`, on stems or
  on affixes' continuation classes; `COMPOUNDPERMITFLAG`, `COMPOUNDFORBIDFLAG`,
  `ONLYINCOMPOUND`, `COMPOUNDMIN`, `COMPOUNDMORESUFFIXES` (without it a part carries one suffix).
- Hungarian's 6–3 rule: `COMPOUNDWORDMAX` with `COMPOUNDROOT`, then `COMPOUNDSYLLABLE` and
  `SYLLABLENUM`. Inflections on the last part don't count. A form listed as a stem counts as the
  lemma its `st:` field gives, unless the entry is a derivation (`ds:`).
- `CHECKCOMPOUNDDUP`, `CHECKCOMPOUNDTRIPLE`, `CHECKCOMPOUNDCASE`, `CHECKCOMPOUNDPATTERN` and
  `CHECKCOMPOUNDREP` (on the whole word and on each pair of neighbouring parts). Two
  neighbouring parts that together are a listed word are read as that word.
- `COMPOUNDRULE` (`0*1`: numbers such as `1999-ben`).
- `BREAK`, with `^` and `$`. A listed `FORBIDDENWORD` stays wrong even when its sides are right
  (`Rákóczi-híd`). Only dictionaries that declare `BREAK`…

title: macOS: start on Macs whose Metal compiler is older than the OS
author: alecanales
body:
## Problem
On Macs running a macOS newer than their GPU's Metal shader compiler supports (e.g. patched macOS on unsupported Macs), wgpu picks an MSL version from the OS (`metal3.2`) that the compiler rejects. egui's pipeline then fails during startup and wgpu's default handler panics.

## Change
- `vendor/wgpu-hal` (wgpu-hal 30.0.1 + one patch in `src/metal/adapter.rs`, `supported_msl_version`): use the newest Metal language version the device's compiler accepts, not the OS's. Wired in via `[patch.crates-io]`; drop when upstream does the same.
- `apps/wordcraft/src/gpu_startup.rs` (macOS): create the wgpu device ourselves so uncaptured errors during renderer setup are recorded and shown as a message (suggesting `WGPU_METAL_MAX_MSL=3.1`) instead of panicking.
- `ATTRIBUTION.md` row for the vendored crate (MIT OR Apache-2.0).

## Testing
- Unit test for the startup error → message conversion.
- `cargo build --release -p wordcraft` succeeds; `cargo fmt --check` passes.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, assets and layers pass. `cargo test --workspace` has 2 failures, `breaks_menu::page_break_from_the_menu_adds_a_page` and `section_break_from_the_menu_splits_sections` (`crates/ui-egui/tests/breaks_menu.rs:31`); both fail identically on `main`, so they are not caused by this PR. The wasm step did not run because tests stopped the pipeline; the change is `cfg(target_os = "macos")` only.

## Try it
An unofficial, unsigned x86_64 test build of this branch is available for Intel Macs running a newer macOS than their GPU's Metal compiler supports (e.g. OpenCore Legacy Patcher): <https://github.com/alecanales/wordcraft/releases/tag/test-macos-msl-fix-x86_64> (SHA-256 attached). It is ad-hoc signed and not notarized; run `xattr -cr WordCraft.app` or open it with right-click → Open.

title: Legacy form fields are drawn: check boxes, and drop-downs' selected entry
author: Morzilla
body:
## What and why

Legacy form fields keep their w:ffData since the last round, but were
not drawn: a FORMCHECKBOX has an empty result, so a form of check
boxes came out with none, and a FORMDROPDOWN showed its saved result
rather than its selected entry.

- wordcraft-doc: `legacy_form` reads what layout needs from the kept
  w:ffData (kind, name, check box state and size, drop-down entries and

  and is drawn as Word draws it; a drop-down shows its selected entry
  (w:result, else w:default, else the first).

Measured on Word's PDF export with a synthetic document (Calibri):

  text size | Word square | WordCraft
  8 pt      | 7.44        | 7.45
  10 pt     | 9.96        | 9.89
  12 pt     | 12.36       | 12.33
  20 pt     | 22.08       | 22.09
  w:size 15 | 16.08       | 15.99

The square sits 1.16 pt inside the line height on every side (room on
the line within 0.2 pt of Word's), has a 0.72 pt border and, checked,
an X from corner to corner in 0.48 pt lines; w:checked beats
w:default. docs/file-format-parity.md is updated.

- `legacy_form_fields_are_drawn` (`crates/layout/src/tests.rs`): one square of the line's height inset 1.16 pt, X only when checked, `w:checked` wins, `w:size` scales it, a drop-down shows its selected entry.

author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #2069

Six layout tests assumed line heights or text widths that only hold with the usual fonts, so FreeBSD's CI fails them. On 2026-10-15, with only the bundled fallback fonts there, two failed; since 2026-10-16 the FreeBSD VM also has DejaVu, and four others fail instead. Each test now measures what it needs from a layout.

## What changes

- **`a_row_with_less_room_than_its_minimum_height_moves_on_whole`** (from #1618) left "two filler paragraphs' room" for a row with a 63.6 pt minimum height: 51.3 pt with the usual fonts, 69.4 pt with the fallback ones, where the row fit. - **`a_floating_table_ignores_a_paragraphs_empty_lines`** (from #1658) put 14 empty paragraphs after the text; with the fallback fonts only 12 fit, so the table went to page 2. It now counts how many fit and leaves two free.

title: #1934: middle-click paste toggle on Linux (File > Options > Advanced)
author: matstrange
body:
## Merged with main, and the paste is now plain text

`main` moved 553 commits ahead of this branch (`e05b7fe8` → `8e986366`), so the branch no longer
merged. `f8d13104` merges it: the 26 conflicts were the 22 interface catalogs, `ROADMAP.md`,
`docs/ui-parity.md`, `contributors/people.toml` and the `file.options` parameters, and each keeps
both sides — main's entries first, this change's after them. The four catalogs `main` has added
since the branch (`da`, `nl`, `ro`, `sl`) get the new row too. `main` has since changed the HTML
clipboard hook to carry a copy's MathML as well (#1297), so this keeps `main`'s three-argument form
and adds the primary-selection write beside it.

`f57042f9` changes what a middle click pastes: **the primary selection comes in as plain text,
always.**

The branch used to paste our own copy with its formatting and another program's selection as plain
text, telling the two apart by comparing the text: the primary selection still held what we last
put there, so the paste kept that copy's bold. Text equality is not proof of ownership — the
primary selection carries no owner at all, so a selection another program made that reads exactly
like our copy could not be told apart from ours, and it came in with that copy's bold against the
will of the program it came from. The only sound answer without an X11 selection-owner query (a new
dependency, X11 only, nothing on Wayland) is to treat every primary selection as what it is: text.
So the middle click now pastes plain text, and the formatting preservation goes with it.

The engine is untouched: `edit.paste` still reuses the saved rich copy for Ctrl+V and for the
agents, and the primary selection never reaches that path. The copy still puts its text on the
primary selection, so a middle click in another program pastes it as a browser's does.

## What

On Linux a middle click pastes the primary selection (the mouse selection) in every other program; in WordCraft it started the autoscroll gesture inst…

title: Tab strip never draws tabs over Comments / Editing / Share (#2026)
author: HyakoV3
body:
Fixes #2026.

## Problem
File, the active tab and contextual tabs were never dropped from the tab strip, so in narrow windows (about 520 pt and below) they were drawn under Comments / Editing / Share.

## Change
The strip is planned before anything is drawn (`plan_strip` in `crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs`). The buttons keep their room and the tabs give way in order:
1. tab padding
2. Comments and Editing labels (icon only, tooltip keeps the name)
3. Share label
4. plain tabs go into the » menu, from the end
5. labels of the active and contextual tabs are cut with …
6. last, the active tab goes into »

File always stays. The » button is highlighted when it holds the active tab, and the active tab is marked in its menu. Thresholds come from measured widths, so long languages work without fixed breakpoints.

Word is not installed on the dev machine, so the behaviour is based on public sources only (Word keeps these buttons in view and shrinks the tabs); the » menu is ours. Noted in `docs/ui-parity.md`.

## Tests
- `plan_strip_gives_way_in_order`, including hostile numbers (NaN, infinity, empty).
- `tab_strip_never_overlaps_the_right_buttons`: widths 300 to 1280 in en, pl and de with Table Layout active; no tab rect crosses a button, tabs stay in the window, File stays.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm).

Not in this PR: the status bar also overlaps at about 420 pt.

title: Proofing: a hyphenated word added to the dictionary is no longer flagged
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2082.

Add to Dictionary stores the whole word, hyphen included (`unigranrio-rj`), but the Portuguese check splits a hyphenated word and only looks up its parts (`unigranrio`, `rj`), so the entry the user just added is never matched and the word stays underlined. Polish, Italian, Croatian and Czech share the same branch; English and Russian already look up the whole word first, which is why it only shows in some languages. The fix looks the whole word up in the user dictionary in `accepted_by_options`, which every language's check already goes through, so the per-language modules stay as they are and the languages in the open proofing PRs (es, fr, pt-PT) get it too. Adding `Unigranrio` and `RJ` separately still works as before. I put the lookup there rather than in each module's hyphen branch to keep it in one place, happy to move it if you'd rather.

Validation:
- `pt::tests::user_dictionary_accepts_a_hyphenated_word_whole`: fails on main (`Unigranrio-RJ` is still flagged after `add_word("Unigranrio-RJ")`), passes here

title: fix(export): pictures marked decorative are skipped by screen readers
author: MyAIPlugins
body:
Follow-up to #1502 / #1526, as mentioned in my comment there.

A picture marked decorative (Alt Text › Mark as decorative, `adec:decorative` in DOCX) was still exported as content:

- **Tagged PDF:** a `Figure` with its alt text, or with "picture" when it had none, inline and floating. PDF/UA expects decorative content to be an artifact so screen readers skip it. `Draw::Image` now carries the mark, and the exporter tags a decorative picture (inline, rotated or floating) as `Artifact` instead of `Figure`.
- **HTML and Markdown** (and ODT, which reads the same model): the document keeps the description when a picture is marked decorative, and it was written as the alt text. A decorative picture now exports with an empty alt text (`alt=""` in HTML), the WCAG way to say "skip this".

Pictures not marked decorative are unchanged. Charts and diagrams stay figures, since they usually carry meaning.

**Rotated groups:** a rotated inline group is drawn inside one rotation, and its tag used to be chosen for the whole group (one Figure with the first picture's alt text). It is still turned as a whole, but each picture in it is now tagged on its own, so a decorative picture next to a described one no longer takes the other's Figure away.

**Not covered:** pictures inside turned text (a table cell's text direction) are part of the paragraph's content, as on `main` for every picture there; tagging them as figures or artifacts is left for a separate change.

**Tests:** `decorative_pictures_are_artifacts_not_figures` (pdf: inline, rotated inline, floating, rotated floating), `rotated_group_tags_each_picture_on_its_own` (pdf: a rotated group with a decorative and a described picture) and `decorative_picture_exports_with_empty_alt_text` (formats: HTML, Markdown). All fail without the change. `cargo test -p wordcraft-pdf -p wordcraft-formats -p wordcraft-render` pass; `cargo fmt --check` and clippy `-D warnings` are clean on the touched crates. `myanmar_prevowel_is_drawn_before_its_co…

title: #1885: dialog close box fills red on hover, whole box clickable
author: C00kieMonsta
body:
Fixes #1885.

In Word on Windows a dialog's close control is a rectangle at the right end of the title bar: the full title-bar height and about 1.6 times as wide, the whole rectangle clickable, red with a white cross while the pointer is over it. WordCraft's dialogs, the Read Aloud player and the file browser used egui's small close glyph instead: only the glyph was the hit area and hovering only changed its stroke colour.

title: #2055: Header & Footer contextual tab while editing a header or footer
author: C00kieMonsta
body:
Fixes #2055.

In Word, double-clicking a header or footer (or Insert › Header › Edit Header) selects a contextual Header & Footer tab with everything that can be set there; closing the header takes the tab away and returns to the tab that was showing. title: #2044: Remember the page view between runs
author: C00kieMonsta
body:
Fixes #2044.

Word keeps the zoom in the document (w:zoom) and otherwise reuses the last view, so One Page stays One Page from one launch to the next. title: #1878: Rulers thin out with the zoom and span the caret's page
author: C00kieMonsta
body:
Fixes #1878.

Before, every whole unit on the rulers got a number whatever the zoom, so zoomed out the numbers overlapped each other and the indent markers, and the margins were numbered backwards to the page edge. The rulers already followed the caret's page, but no test pinned that in One Page and Multiple Pages, and the vertical bar ran past the page's bottom. Word thins the numbers out as the page shrinks and keeps both rulers on the page with the caret.

Now the numbers come every 1, 2, 4, 8... units, the fewest that keep them at least 30 px apart, and the small ticks drop out below 4 px, with the text at its usual size. The margins get ticks only. A number gives way to an indent, tab stop (set, or being dragged to that spot) or table column/row marker sitting on it. The horizontal ruler spans the caret page's on-screen rect at that page's scale, the vertical one is pinned to the left edge over that page's height, both clipped to their strips, in every layout, and they follow the caret to another page of the row or the next row.

title: L10N-AR: Arabic interface (right-to-left chrome, catalog, bidi text)
author: Paymeet-Apps
body:
Adds an Arabic interface: a full Arabic catalog, right-to-left mirroring of the whole chrome, and bidi-correct drawing of mixed-direction text.

## What's in it
- **Text drawing (L10N-AR.1–3, 14):** pins epaint's Arabic shaping; `bidi::visual` draws mixed-direction interface text in visual order; RTL catalogs draw in visual order with `fmt` isolating inserted values; document and user text shown in the chrome (titles, panes, fields) draws in bidi order.
- **Font (L10N-AR.4):** Arabic interface face from craft-fonts when built with `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR`, otherwise from installed system fonts. No font files are added to this repo.
- **Language (L10N-AR.5, 15a–d):** Arabic joins the interface languages; the catalog covers the ribbon, menus, status bar, every dialog, panes, Backstage, style names, equation gallery, watermarks, paper sizes and preview tiles. A coverage test keeps it complete, and Arabic runs in the interface audit.
- **Mirroring (L10N-AR.6–13):** direction-aware layout helpers; mirrored title bar, Quick Access Toolbar, status bar, ribbon and keytips, menus, popups, tooltips, panes, Backstage, scroll bar and all dialogs; directional icons flip in right-to-left interfaces.
- **Docs (L10N-AR.16):** localization and UI parity docs, gaps, roadmap and progress log updated, with parity numbers after a side-by-side screenshot pass.

Latest `origin/main` is merged in.

## Checks
`cargo xtask` fmt, clippy, assets, layers and wasm pass. All tests pass except two render tests, `tests_color_glyphs::emoji_are_drawn_in_colour` and `emoji_keep_their_colours_on_a_dark_page`. They fail the same way on `origin/main` (fd0bb2f) on the Windows dev machine (the ✅ emoji isn't drawn with the colour emoji font), so they are not caused by this branch.

All icons are drawn in code; no Microsoft assets.

title: Opening a named pipe or a device no longer hangs or eats memory, whatever its name (#1444 follow-up)
author: asystemoffields
body:
#1444 (fixing #1440) made the app open a file whose name isn't valid Unicode. It reads that file with a plain `std::fs::read`. `file.open` on a path, which the CLI also uses, does almost the same: it checks the length and then calls `std::fs::read`. Neither one checks that the path is a regular file. So:

- a named pipe blocks the open until something writes to it. For the app, that means start-up hangs with no window.
- a device such as `/dev/zero` reports a length of 0 and never ends, so the read grows until memory runs out.

`read_regular_file` in `io.rs` already guards against both for HTML pictures (#98). This PR uses it for documents too.

Before (`upstream/main` fee9b98; `t/fif\xe9.txt` is a FIFO, `t/z\xe9ro.txt` a symlink to `/dev/zero`, `t/caf\xe9.txt` holds "Bonjour"):

```
$ wordcraft-cli text $'t/fif\xe9.txt'
exit 124                               # killed by `timeout 10`
$ wordcraft-cli text $'t/z\xe9ro.txt'     # under ulimit -v 4000000
wordcraft-cli: t/z�ro.txt: out of memory
exit 1
$ wordcraft-cli text $'t/caf\xe9.txt'
Bonjour
exit 0
```

Without the `ulimit` the `/dev/zero` read keeps growing until the machine runs out of memory, so I didn't run it that way.

After:

```
$ wordcraft-cli text $'t/fif\xe9.txt'
wordcraft-cli: t/fif�.txt: not a file
exit 1
$ wordcraft-cli text $'t/z\xe9ro.txt'     # under ulimit -v 4000000
wordcraft-cli: t/z�ro.txt: not a file
exit 1
$ wordcraft-cli text $'t/caf\xe9.txt'
Bonjour
exit 0
```

I did not launch the app with a display: on a FIFO it would hang before the window works. Instead, the app's unit test below calls `open_non_unicode`, the function that reads the file at start-up.

What changed:
- New `io::read_document(path)` in the engine. It checks the automation read root, refuses a path that isn't a regular file, refuses a file over 2 GB, then reads through `read_regular_file`. That function checks the opened handle again and stops after 2 GB whatever length the file reports.
- `open_path_in` (`file.open`, `word…

title: fix(pdf): shapes with a description are figures in tagged PDF
author: MyAIPlugins
body:
A shape with a description (Alt Text) was exported as an artifact like any other shape, so screen readers skipped it and the description was lost: an arrow or an icon drawn with shapes that means something was invisible to them.

A shape that has a description, is not marked decorative and shows no text is now a `Figure` with its description, inline (rotated too) and floating. Unchanged:
- shapes without a description and decorative shapes stay artifacts;
- a text box keeps its frame as an artifact and its text read as paragraphs: a `Figure` would replace the text with the description, so the description isn't used.

The rule lives in `shape_figure_alt` (layout). `Draw::Figure`'s `kind` becomes an `Option` (`None` for a shape), and `Placed::Shape` carries the description for floating shapes.

**Not covered:** a group's own description (a floating group is placed member by member, so wrapping it needs a change to how groups are placed), and shapes inside a Drawing Canvas. Shapes in a group that have their own description are covered.

**Tests:** `described_shapes_are_figures_with_their_description` (pdf: inline, rotated inline, floating, rotated floating; described, undescribed, decorative, text box). It fails without the change. `cargo test` passes for pdf, layout, render and formats, `cargo fmt --check` is clean, and clippy `-D warnings` is clean on those crates and ui-egui. `myanmar_prevowel_is_drawn_before_its_consonant` fails in my environment on `main` too (font-dependent), unrelated.

**Note:** #2086 changes the arm just before the `Draw::Figure` one in the same `match` in `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase; I'll do it. Both together pass the pdf, formats and render tests.

title: File: recovery copies and .json files store pictures as base64 (#586 follow-up)
author: asystemoffields
body:
Follow-up to #586 (local crash recovery, part of #518).

Recovery copies wrap the native JSON form of the document, and native JSON wrote `Document::media` and `Document::passthrough` with serde's default for bytes: an array of numbers, one per byte. A picture took about 3.6 times its size in a recovery copy. In a `.json` file, which `io::save_bytes` pretty-prints with one number per line, it took over ten times its size. A 27 MiB photo made a 96 MiB recovery copy every ten seconds and a 286 MiB `.json` file.

Each part is now one standard base64 string (`crates/doc/src/byte_store.rs`, using the workspace `base64` crate the DOCX reader already uses). It is encoded straight into the writer through `collect_str`, so no second copy of a large picture is held. Reading takes either form: base64 text, or the old array of numbers. Recovery copies and `.json` files written before this change still open with the same bytes. Anything else, such as bad base64, a number over 255 or an object, is an error and never a panic.

### Measured

Release build, a synthetic 27 MiB picture of incompressible bytes (xorshift noise, as a photo's are). `native_json_size_with_a_large_picture` (ignored, run on demand):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| compact (what a recovery copy wraps) | 96.4 MiB, written 252 ms, read 404 ms | 36.0 MiB, written 52 ms, read 46 ms |
| `.json` file (pretty) | 285.5 MiB, written 614 ms, read 533 ms | 36.1 MiB, written 57 ms, read 37 ms |

Through the recovery worker, with a 6,000-paragraph document plus that picture (the measurement test in the companion PR):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| recovery copy on disk | 99 MB | 39 MB |
| worker time per snapshot | 2.35 s | 0.26 s |
| worker's share of a core over a minute of typing (fixed 10 s interval) | 20.1% | 2.4% |
| start-up scan listing the copy | 1.03 s | 0.14 s |

### Tests

- `byte_store` unit tests: every length round-trips and writes canonical base64 (`"TWFu"`, `"TWE="`); old number arrays still …

title: File: crash recovery keeps its folder private, paces snapshots and leaves no stale copies (#586 follow-up)
author: asystemoffields
body:
Follow-up to #586 (local crash recovery, part of #518). These are defects found reviewing it on current `main`.

**What was wrong**

1. **Folder permissions.** The recovery folder was made with `DirBuilder::mode(0o700)`, but that mode applies only to folders it creates. An existing `recovery/` folder (or record folder) that others could read, say 0755 from an older build or a restored profile, stayed readable to them. Copy files were already 0600.
2. **CPU while typing.** Snapshots ran on a fixed ten-second interval whatever they cost. On a large document (6,000 paragraphs plus a 27 MiB picture, 1.7–2.3 s per snapshot on `main`) the worker was busy 17–20% of the time for as long as typing went on.
3. **Stale copies.** A saved document's copy was removed only by a later tick that saw the document clean. Save followed straight away by New or Open (the save prompt's Save, for one) replaced the document before that tick, and the copy was then offered as unsaved work at every later start. So was the copy of a document whose changes the user gave up with Don't Save.
4. **Exit ordering.** Dropping the session dropped the worker's channel but didn't wait for the worker. A snapshot under way at exit could be cut off, and a session started next (the next launch, or the next test) could find the record still locked and skip it. This is one source of flaky recovery tests.
5. **One bad record hid all others.** In the start-up scan, a record that failed a per-record check (more generations than discovery reads, an unreadable folder) returned an error through `?` and ended the scan. Every valid copy went unlisted.
6. **Untranslated.** File › Recover and its Discard dialog shipped in English in every language. Only "Recover" had a translation, and not in Korean. The interface audit didn't draw that page.

**What changed**

1. `Store::new` and each snapshot write tighten an existing recovery or record folder to 0700 (Unix) before anything is written into it.

title: Fonts: emoji prefer a colour emoji font on Windows (#1754, #1874)
author: kilter-ecnvs
body:
Fixes #1754. Fixes #1874.

**What was wrong:** on Windows, Segoe UI Symbol and Segoe UI Emoji are both installed. `SYSTEM_FALLBACKS` lists Segoe UI Symbol first, and fallback otherwise goes by load order, so ✅ (U+2705) came out black and white while 🧠 on the same line was in colour. The two tests in `render::tests_color_glyphs` failed on Windows, so `cargo xtask ci` couldn't pass there.

**The fix** is in the shared fallback path, so every caller gets it:
- `fonts::is_emoji(c)` is new. It returns true for the BMP characters with `Emoji_Presentation` (from emoji-data.txt) and for the whole U+1F000–U+1FAFF pictograph range.
- `script_fallbacks(c)` returns the colour emoji families (Segoe UI Emoji, Apple Color Emoji, Noto Color Emoji) for those characters. The system search therefore loads a colour font first.
- `loaded_fallback` ranks already-loaded faces by `fallback_rank` for emoji, so a symbol font that happens to be loaded no longer wins.
- Text-style symbols (✔ ☺ →) are not emoji by this test, so they keep the symbol fonts.

**Tests:**
- New: `fonts::script::tests::emoji_prefer_colour_emoji_fonts`. It doesn't depend on which fonts are installed.
- The two render tests that failed before now pass on Windows 11.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes on Windows 11 (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

One deliberate simplification: the whole U+1F000–U+1FAFF range counts as emoji, including a few pictographs that default to text style. It's marked with a comment in case one of them should draw in monochrome.

title: Proofing: Vietnamese spelling by syllable rules
author: ngotuankhoi
body:
## Problem
Vietnamese had no spelling check:
- `vi-VN` text was proofed as `Other`, so nothing was marked.
- A Vietnamese paragraph typed under the default English language was detected (`vi::looks_vietnamese`) and then left unmarked too.

## Fix
- **`ProofLang::Vi`**: the `vi`, `vi-VN` and `vie` tags map to it. Detected Vietnamese paragraphs under English are spelled as Vietnamese. Issues read "Có thể sai chính tả".
- **Spelling by syllable rules, no dictionary needed** (`crates/proof/src/vi.rs`). Every Vietnamese word is written as syllables. A syllable must be:
  - an onset;
  - one of the ~160 Vietnamese rhymes;
  - at most one tone mark.

  On top of that, spelling rules apply:
  - `k`, `gh` and `ngh` only before `i e ê y`;
  - `c`, `g` and `ng` never before them;
  - a stop ending (`c ch p t`) takes only the acute or the dot below.

  Marks may be precomposed or combining. Plain-ASCII English words (`email`, `file`) are accepted.

  This catches the common slips: `nghành`, `ngỉ`, `hoc`, `cinh`, and leftover Telex keys like `tieengs` and `vieejt`.
- **Optional list of syllables in use.** The rules alone still accept syllables nobody writes (`quyêm`).
  - When a `vi-syllables.txt` (one syllable per line, `#` comments) is in the dictionaries folder or a Hunspell location, a syllable must also be on it.
  - It is found the same way as the Hunspell dictionaries, reloaded by `set_dictionaries_folder`, and listed in Options › Proofing.
  - The file is size-capped at 4 MB. Entries that break the rules are dropped.
  - None is shipped. A good list can be extracted from the Vietnamese Wiktionary's page titles, but that list is CC BY-SA, so it stays outside the repo.
- **No suggestions or grammar for Vietnamese yet**: `suggest_in` and `check_grammar_in` return nothing for it, as for Bulgarian.
- **Docs and UI**:
  - Options › Proofing gets a "Vietnamese" label, added to every catalog.

title: Return 0 for SIGN(0) in table formulas
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/table_formula.rs:721` (no existing issue): Table formula SIGN(0) returns 1 instead of 0.

## Cause
The table formula `SIGN` function was implemented as `f64::signum()`. Rust's `signum()` returns 1.0 for +0.0 and -1.0 for -0.0, so `=SIGN(0)` and a cell holding 0 gave 1 or -1 instead of 0.

## Fix
`SIGN` now returns 0.0 when its argument equals 0.0, which covers both +0.0 and -0.0. It uses `signum()` for every other value. The regression test covers SIGN of 0, -0, a zero cell, 5 and -5.

## Verified
- Regression test `sign_of_zero_is_zero`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --lib sign_of_zero`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::deleted_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_without_markup`, `tests::hidden_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_when_not_shown`, `tests::tight_wrap_follows_an_ellipse`, `tests_pages::widow_control_moves_a_three_line_paragraph_whole`, which also fail on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
The other table formula functions are unchanged.

title: Translate Selection: right-click popup via Google Cloud Translation, or offline StarDict lookup
author: ngotuankhoi
body:
Right-click a selection › **Translate** opens a small popup under it with the translation. **Insert** replaces the selection; **Copy** copies the translation. The target language defaults to the interface language and the popup remembers the last one picked.

This complements #2046 (Translate Document with local OPUS-MT models) rather than replacing it. It covers quick, ad-hoc translation of a phrase in place. It uses its own command id, `review.translateSelection`, and leaves `review.translate`, the catalog row and the ribbon button to #2046 / #1307. Parity stays at 489/504.

## Without a key: offline word lookup
Users with no Google key get each selected word looked up in **StarDict** dictionaries (`.ifo` + `.idx` + `.dict` or `.dict.dz`) instead. They put the dictionaries in the dictionaries folder (File › Options › Proofing) or in any other folder searched for spelling dictionaries.

- If the whole selection is a headword ("look up"), the popup shows that entry. Otherwise it lists each word with its entry, up to 50 words.
- It strips simple English inflections (cats→cat, -ed, -ing, -ly).
- The popup offers Copy only, because a definition is not a translation to insert.
- The files are treated as untrusted. They are capped at 256 MB, every offset is checked, and gzip headers are parsed defensively.

## Privacy
Nothing leaves the machine unless the user does both of these:
1. Adds their own Google Cloud Translation API key in File › Options › Language. There is no key by default and the feature is off.
2. Picks Translate on a selection.

Only the selected text is sent, and it is sent only at that moment. The popup says so when no key is set. The key travels in the `X-Goog-Api-Key` header, never in the URL. `ui.inspect` on the control channel, and so MCP, never returns the key.

title: fix(render, pdf): fix vertical double and wave border rendering
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Summary
In crates/render/src/lib.rs and crates/pdf/src/lib.rs, vertical double and wave borders exhibited severe rendering defects:
1. **Vertical double borders (crates/render):** Draw::Line offset double strokes only along the Y axis (line(ctx, -w * 0.9) / line(ctx, w * 0.9)), causing vertical double lines (x0 == x1) to overlap completely on the same X coordinate instead of rendering side-by-side.
2. **Vertical wave borders (crates/render and crates/pdf):** wave_path assumed horizontal orientation ( = x0.min(x1),   = x0.max(x1)). When the border was vertical (x0 == x1),  == b caused the generation loop to terminate immediately, producing an empty path and making vertical wave borders completely invisible.

### Fix
- In crates/render/src/lib.rs, updated Double stroke rendering to compute normal perpendicular offset vector (nx, ny) from line direction (dx, dy), matching crates/pdf.
- In both crates/render and crates/pdf, updated wave_path to compute unit direction (ux, uy) and perpendicular normal (nx, ny), supporting wave strokes of any orientation including vertical.
- Added test in crates/render/src/cache_tests.rs verifying that vertical wave strokes generate path elements.

title: fix(engine): exclude carriage returns from word count character statistics
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Summary
In `crates/engine/src/cmd/review.rs:761`, `word_count` filtered out newlines when calculating `charactersWithSpaces` using `text.chars().filter(|c| *c != '\n').count()`.

When selected text contained CRLF (`\r\n`) or carriage returns (`\r`), `\r` was not filtered, improperly inflating character counts by treating carriage return control characters as printable characters or spaces.

### Fix

title: PDF export can write fillable form fields, as an export option
author: Morzilla
body:
PDF export can now write **fillable PDFs** for a document's form fields, as an export option. It is off by default, so existing exports are unchanged.

This is the first of two PRs, split as asked. The second one, for blanks drawn with underscores and dates, builds on this.

## What it does

`PdfOptions::form_fields` is a new option. It is available everywhere a PDF is written:

| Option | Command param (`file.exportPdf`, `file.save`, `file.saveAs`) | CLI (`wordcraft-cli convert`) |
|---|---|---|
| `form_fields` | `"formFields": true` | `--form-fields` |

Legacy form fields (`FORMCHECKBOX`, `FORMTEXT`, `FORMDROPDOWN`) and content controls the user may edit (text, rich text, date, check box, drop-down, combo box) become AcroForm fields.

- **Names:** each field is named after `w:name`, or the tag or title. Duplicates get the first free `_2`, `_3`, never a name another field already has. Viewers join fields that share a name.
- **Values:** each field holds the document's value as the page shows it: the check box state, the selected entry, or the text without hidden text or tracked deletions. Hidden or deleted fields are not made fillable.
- **Widgets:** they are opaque and sit exactly over what layout drew, including the check box square with its 0.72 pt border. A filled-in or flattened copy therefore shows the new value, not the old one underneath.
- **Font:** text and drop-downs use the standard PDF font closest to the document's text there, with its size, bold, italic and colour. Arial, Calibri and Aptos map to Helvetica; Times and Cambria to Times; Consolas to Courier. No font is embedded, and every viewer has these fonts.
- **Scaled or moved pages:** no fields are added when a selected page is drawn scaled or moved (Print Markup's comments, `paper`). With `pages`, fields follow their pages and are dropped with them.

## How

krilla has no form or widget annotations (`AnnotationType` is only `Link`). So `crates/pdf/src/forms.rs` adds the AcroForm to the finished P…

title: Ribbon tab clicks no longer scroll the page to the caret while a footer is edited (#2054)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2054.

Clicking a ribbon tab header (Design, Layout, References...) runs `ui.tab`, and `after_command` treated it like an editing command: it set `canvas.scroll_to_caret`, so the view jumped to the caret. With the caret in a footer, that showed up as the page moving a few pixels on every tab click.

`after_command` already skips caret-follow for `view.`, `document.`, `format.state` and `draw.` commands. This adds `ui.` to that list: every `ui.*` command only changes the app's chrome (tabs, dialogs, backstage, theme, keytips) and never moves the caret. Mouse clicks on tabs (`ribbon.rs`) and keytips both go through `ui.tab`, so both paths are covered.

Commands that edit the document still scroll to the caret as before.

Test: `ribbon_tab_click_does_not_follow_the_caret` runs `ui.tab` and checks the view stays put, then checks typing still scrolls to the caret. It fails without the fix.

title: fix(doc): strip negative sign when formatting numbers rounded to zero
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
When `format_number` in `wordcraft_doc::locale_number` formats fractional negative values close to zero (e.g. `-0.001`), `format!("{v:.2}")` yields `"-0.00"`, producing `"-0.00"` (or `"-0,00"` with decimal comma locales). A rounded zero should not carry a negative sign (mirroring `format_picture`).

### Solution
- When `format!("{v:.2}")` rounds to `"-0.00"`, strip the negative sign so the output becomes `"0.00"` (or `"0,00"`).
- Added tests verifying `format_number(-0.001, ...)` outputs `"0.00"` / `"0,00"` and `format_number(-0.0, None)` outputs `"0"`.

title: Opening a second document opens a new window instead of replacing the current one
author: k33ssa
body:
## Problem
A WordCraft window holds one document, and every open path replaces that document in place:
- Finder double-click, Open With, `open -a WordCraft file`
- File › Open, Recent, File › New and templates
- Cmd+O, Cmd+N
- drag-and-drop onto the window

If the current document is saved and unchanged, it is replaced **silently**. The user had one document open, opened a second one, and the first one simply disappeared. Nothing in the app could create a second window. Word on macOS opens each document in its own window.

## Change
- The opened or new document goes to a **new window** (a new app process), unless the current window is untouched and blank. Untouched blank means no path, not dirty, and empty. Only then is the window reused, as Word does.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`:
  - adds the `Services::new_window` hook, the `NewWindow` enum, and `window_is_reusable` / `new_window_for`;
  - `WordApp::run` routes `file.open` and `file.new` through the hook when the host provides it.
- `apps/wordcraft/src/new_window.rs` (new) starts the process:
  - macOS app bundle: `open -n <WordCraft.app> --args <path>`;
  - otherwise: the current executable.

  The child gets the file on its command line, so no `odoc` Apple Event loops back to the first process. `WORDCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT` is cleared for the child, so the two control ports don't clash.
- `apps/wordcraft/src/main.rs` registers the hook and adds `--new <template>`, which skips the Start screen and runs `file.new`.
- Each window keeps its own Save Changes prompt and its own Cmd/Ctrl+W, and closing one window never affects another. The prompt is never bypassed: the in-place path is reached only for a reusable window, which by definition is not dirty.
- Unchanged: the web build, the control channel and MCP (`engine.execute`), and pictures/fonts dropped onto the window.

## Tests
- `ui-egui`:
  - the reuse-vs-new-window decision;
  - a dirty document gets no prompt and stays intact when a file opens in a new window;
  -…

title: fix #2115: an encrypted .docx without dataIntegrity is refused, not opened unchecked
author: HyakoV3
body:
Fixes #2115.

`EncryptionInfo` is stored in the clear and `decrypt` only checked the HMAC when the `dataIntegrity` element was present, so removing the element (no password needed) turned the check off and a changed package still decrypted with the owner's password.

- `parse_info` now refuses an agile package without `dataIntegrity` (`the file has no integrity check…`); `decrypt` always verifies the HMAC. WordCraft already writes the element and Word 2010+ agile files carry it.
- Test `a_package_without_its_integrity_element_is_refused`: a file as written still opens; with the element removed, both an untouched and a changed package are refused (with or without a password). The hostile-input case that expected success without the element now expects failure; the existing wrong-HMAC test is unchanged.
- Password check, spin-count cap and MD5 / non-CBC rejection are unchanged.

I did not add an "open without an integrity check" option; the issue marks it as optional, and I can add it if real files omit the element. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: fix(engine): use table_formula parse_number for table sorting
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
`crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs` sorted table columns using `wordcraft_doc::locale_number::parse_number`, rather than `table_formula::parse_number`. As documented in `table_formula.rs` ("A cell's number as a formula or a sort key reads it: surrounding spaces, currency signs, thousands separators and % are ignored, and accounting negatives in parentheses count as negative"), `table_formula::parse_number` handles accounting negatives in parentheses `(50)`. Because `wordcraft_doc::locale_number::parse_number` does not handle parenthesized numbers, values like `(50)` were treated as text rather than negative numbers, causing them to sort after all positive numbers.

### Solution
- Change `table.rs` to import and use `super::table_formula::parse_number` for extracting cell sort numbers.
- Added a unit test verifying that table sorting correctly orders parenthesized accounting negative values (e.g. `(50)` before `10` and `20`).

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
