title: fix(engine): resolve ANSI character codes in find and replace
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
When searching or replacing special character codes in `crates/engine/src/cmd/find_pattern.rs`, ANSI codes formatted as `^0nnn` (e.g. `^0151` for em dash `—`) were parsed as raw Unicode code points `char::from_u32(151)`. Because code points 128..=159 in Unicode are C1 control characters, `filter(|c| !c.is_control())` rejected them, causing `^0151` (and all other ANSI characters in the 128..=159 range) to fail to match or compile, despite `^0151` being explicitly documented in the doc comment.

### Solution
- When a numeric code starts with `'0'` and is within 0..=255, decode it through Windows-1252 (`wordcraft_doc::encoding::cp1252`) as Word does for ANSI character codes.
- Added regression tests verifying `^0151` (ANSI) and `^u8212` (Unicode) match em dashes in Find and Replace.

title: fix(formats): support relative font size values in HTML font tags
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
HTML 4.01 specifies that the `size` attribute of `<font>` elements can be either an absolute integer (1–7) or a relative delta (`+1`, `+2`, `-1`, `-2`) added to/subtracted from the base font size (default 3). In `crates/formats/src/html.rs`, `size` was parsed directly via `s.trim().parse::<i32>()`. For relative sizes like `size="+1"`, Rust parsed this as `1`, causing `"+1"` to be mapped to font size index 0 (7.5 pt) instead of size 4 (13.5 pt) — turning text smaller rather than larger.

### Solution
- Check for `+` and `-` prefixes when parsing `<font size="...">` and calculate the effective size relative to the base font size (3).
- Added unit test `font_size_relative_and_absolute` verifying `size="+1"` maps to 13.5 pt, `size="-1"` maps to 10.0 pt, and `size="5"` maps to 18.0 pt.

title: fix(docx): support self-closing w:compat in settings merge
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
When merging settings into an original DOCX settings part (`crates/docx/src/write/settings_merge.rs`), `merge_compat` searched for the closing tag `</w:compat>` when adding the generated `compatibilityMode` setting. If the original settings contained a self-closing `<w:compat/>` (or `<w:compat />`), `orig.rfind("</w:compat>")` returned `None`, which caused `merge_compat` (and consequently `merge`) to abort and return `None`. This caused all unowned original settings (e.g. `w:rsids`, compatibility flags, document variables) to be completely lost.

### Solution
- When `</w:compat>` is absent in the original, check for `/>` and expand the self-closing tag to `<w:compat>{compat_setting}</w:compat>`.
- Added unit test `a_self_closing_compat_block_gets_the_generated_mode` verifying that self-closing `<w:compat/>` tags are expanded and merged alongside other original settings (`w:rsids`).

title: Layout: a continuous section after a page break starts on the page the break made (#2109)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #2109.

When a section ends with a page-break-only paragraph followed by an empty paragraph carrying its `w:sectPr`, and the next section is **continuous** with *Different First Page* on, WordCraft showed the new section's first-page header one page late (WordCraft: section 1 default on page 2, section 2 first-page on page 3; Word: section 2 first-page on page 2, default from page 3).

## Root cause

Pages are stamped with their section index when they are *created*. The page break creates page 2 during section 1's layout loop, and the empty section mark — which Word keeps on page 1, with the break — flows to the top of page 2 instead. Page 2 therefore stays attributed to section 1 (its header), and the first page attributed to section 2 is the next one, which gets the first-page header a page late.

## The change (two pieces, `crates/layout`)

1. `place_para`: an empty section mark met at the top of a page that a page break just made is parked on the page before, like Word. Scoped to the continuous case (`!next_starts_page`) on purpose: the sibling next-page-section case is #2013's open PR, and the two conditions merge cleanly without overlap.
2. The continuous branch of the section start: when the mark was parked and the break's page is therefore empty, `take_back_break_page` pops it and the section starts a fresh page — stamped with its own section index, laid out with its first-page body top when it asks for a first-page header. A continuous section with no break behind it is untouched (`take_back_break_page` is false there and the old path runs).

## Validation

- New layout test `a_continuous_section_after_a_page_break_owns_the_page_the_break_made`: fails on main (page 2 has section 0), passes with the fix (section 1, `HfSlot::First`).

title: fix(engine): return 0 for SIGN(0) in table formulas
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In table formulas (e.g. `=SIGN(number)`), Microsoft Word and standard spreadsheet formula engines return `1` for positive numbers, `-1` for negative numbers, and `0` when the number is zero.

Previously, `crates/engine/src/cmd/table_formula.rs` evaluated `SIGN` using Rust's `f64::signum()`, which follows IEEE 754 sign-bit extraction where `0.0.signum()` returns `1.0` (and `-0.0.signum()` returns `-1.0`). As a result, `=SIGN(0)` incorrectly evaluated to `1`.

### Solution
- Explicitly check if the argument is `0.0` and return `0.0` (handling both `+0.0` and `-0.0`).
- Added unit tests in `ranges_and_references_and_operators` verifying that `=SIGN(5)` returns `1.0`, `=SIGN(-5)` returns `-1.0`, `=SIGN(0)` returns `0.0`, and `=SIGN(-0)` returns `0.0`.

title: Linux: scan the Flatpak host font folders (#1937)
author: tydude001
body:
Fixes #1937 (and #1954, a duplicate).

In the Flatpak, WordCraft lists only the runtime's fonts. `system_font_dirs()` scans `/usr/share/fonts`,
`/usr/local/share/fonts`, `~/.fonts` and `~/.local/share/fonts`. Inside the sandbox the first two are the runtime's
folders, and the manifest doesn't grant the home folders. Flatpak mounts the host's fonts under `/run/host` for every
app, with no filesystem permission. This adds those folders to the Linux/BSD list, plus a unit test that checks
they're in it:

- `/run/host/fonts` (host `/usr/share/fonts`) and `/run/host/user-fonts` (the host's XDG user font folder, or
  `~/.fonts` when that doesn't exist), the two @webdevtodayjason named on the issue;
- `/run/host/local-fonts` (host `/usr/local/share/fonts`), as EffectCraft also scans (storytold/effectcraft#876);

title: fix(formats): trim whitespace when parsing numeric XML attributes in ODT
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In ODF XML files produced by various tools, templates, or XML formatters, integer attribute values can contain leading or trailing whitespace (e.g., `<text:h text:outline-level=" 2 ">`, `<text:s text:c=" 3 "/>`, `<table:table-cell table:number-columns-spanned=" 2 " table:number-rows-spanned=" 1 "/>`, `<style:style style:default-outline-level=" 1 ">`, `<text:list-level-style-number text:level=" 2 ">`).

In `crates/formats/src/odt.rs`, these attributes were parsed using `v.parse::<u8>()` or `v.parse::<usize>()` or `v.parse::<u32>()` directly without `.trim()`. In Rust, `parse::<Integer>()` fails when any whitespace is present, causing these values to silently fall back to default values (e.g. outline level 1, space count 1, column span 1).

### Solution
- Add `.trim()` before calling `.parse::<...>()` on these attributes, matching how other XML attributes in `odt.rs` are parsed.
- Add unit test `whitespace_in_attributes_is_trimmed` verifying that outline level, space count, and column span with surrounding whitespace parse correctly.

title: fix(formats): support left alignment in markdown tables
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) pipe tables (§4.10):
- A colon on the left side of a delimiter cell (`:---`) indicates left alignment.
- Colons on both sides (`:---:`) indicate center alignment.
- A colon on the right side (`---:`) indicates right alignment.
- Hyphens without colons (`---`) indicate default alignment.

Previously in `crates/formats/src/markdown.rs`:
- `delimiter_row` checked `(left, right)` with `match (left, right)` but omitted `(true, false)`. As a result, `:---` delimiter cells fell into `_ => None` and lost their explicit left alignment (`Some(Align::Left)`).
- `table_md` only exported `Some(Align::Center) => ":---:"` and `Some(Align::Right) => "---:"`, exporting `Some(Align::Left)` as `---` instead of `:---`.

### Solution
- Map `(true, false)` to `Some(Align::Left)` in `delimiter_row`.
- Export `Some(Align::Left)` as `":---"` in `table_md`.
- Added unit test `table_column_alignments_import_and_export` verifying that `:---`, `:---:`, `---:`, and `---` parse into their respective alignments and round-trip cleanly through markdown export.

title: fix(docx): handle case-insensitive ST_OnOff values
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In OOXML (ISO/IEC 29500-1 §17.18.66 `ST_OnOff`), boolean properties can be explicitly turned off using values such as `false` or `off` (in addition to `0`). Various DOCX producers emit these values with different capitalization (such as `Off` or `OFF`).

Previously:
- `units::on_off` matched `matches!(v.trim(), "0" | "false" | "off" | "False" | "FALSE")`. Because `"Off"` and `"OFF"` were missing, attributes like `<w:b w:val="Off"/>` or `<w:strike w:val="OFF"/>` were treated as `true` (enabled).
- `story::on_off_attr` directly checked `!matches!(v, "0" | "false" | "off")` without trimming or casing normalization.

### Solution
- Normalize `v.trim().to_ascii_lowercase()` in both `units::on_off` and `story::on_off_attr` to match against `"0" | "false" | "off"`.
- Added unit tests in `units::tests::on_off_values` verifying all casing variants (`"off"`, `"Off"`, `"OFF"`, `"false"`, `"False"`, `"FALSE"`, `"0"`, `"on"`, `"true"`, `"1"`, `None`).

title: fix(formats): support distributed paragraph alignment in RTF
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In the RTF specification (RTF 1.9.1 §Paragraph Formatting Properties):
- `\qj` defines justified text.
- `\qd` defines distributed justification.

Previously in `crates/formats/src/rtf.rs`:
- On export, both `Align::Justify` and `Align::Distribute` were written as `\qj`.
- On import, both `\qj` and `\qd` were parsed as `Align::Justify`.

As a result, distributed paragraph alignment was lost and demoted to regular justification on both import and export.

### Solution
- Export `Some(Align::Distribute)` as `\qd`.
- Parse `\qd` as `Some(Align::Distribute)`.
- Added unit test `distributed_alignment_round_trips` verifying that `\qd` imports as `Align::Distribute` and round-trips cleanly through RTF export.

title: fix(layout): support field format switches without whitespace after \*
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In Word field codes, switches such as format switches (`\*`) can appear either with or without whitespace between the switch indicator and the switch argument/name, or chained with subsequent switches (for example: `{ PAGE \*roman }`, `{ PAGE \*roman\*MERGEFORMAT }`, or `{ NUMPAGES \*CardText }`).

Previously, `format_switch` in `crates/layout/src/fields.rs` only matched exact whitespace tokens `w == "\*"`, followed by taking the next whitespace token `it.next()?`. When a switch was written without a space after `\*` (e.g. `PAGE \*roman`), `w` was `"\*roman"` rather than `"\*"`, so `format_switch` failed to identify the switch and returned `None`, falling back to default arabic numeral formatting.

### Solution
- Strip the `"\*"` prefix from the token; if found, use the remainder of the token (if non-empty) or the next whitespace token (if empty).
- Strip any trailing switch delimiter (`\`) from the format specifier to support chained switches without whitespace (e.g. `\*roman\*MERGEFORMAT`).
- Added unit tests in `crates/layout/src/fields.rs` verifying that `PAGE \*roman` and `PAGE \*roman\*MERGEFORMAT` correctly evaluate to `"iv"`.

title: Picture Styles, Border and Artistic Effects replace the last one instead of stacking (#2052)
author: D13GOOOO
body:
Fixes #2052.

## What was wrong

Picture Styles, Picture Border and Artistic Effects drew onto the picture's current bitmap. Picking a second one drew over the first: Thick Frame then Simple Frame gave both frames, and a second border or effect landed on top of the last one.

## What Word does

A picture has one style, one border and one artistic effect. Picking a new one replaces the old one. That's what the report expects.

| | Before | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Thick Frame, then Simple Frame | both frames | Simple Frame only |
| Border 8 px, then 2 px | both borders | 2 px border, style kept |
| A border, then a style | style drawn around the border | style only (the gallery replaces the border) |
| Invert, then Posterize | both effects | Posterize only |
| An effect, then `none` | — | the picture without the effect |
| Transparency 50%, then 10% | already 10% (#1175) | unchanged; the test pins it |

The transparency part of the report was already fixed by #1175.

## Change

- `crates/engine/src/cmd/objects.rs`: new `PictureLook` (base bitmap + effect, style, border) and `relook`. Each of the three commands changes its own field and draws again from the base bitmap: effect, then style, then border. Artistic effects moved to `artistic_effect`, unchanged. `picture.effects` takes `"none"`. Reset Picture still works: the result still chains onto `originals`.
- A look is reused only while the picture still shows the bitmap it drew (`Arc::ptr_eq`) and its base bitmap still exists. After undo, or a picture that reuses the media key, it starts from what's on the page.
- `crates/engine/src/session.rs`: `Session::picture_looks`, drawn media key → look.
- `docs/target-app-parity.md`: status line and revision history.

## Tests

`picture_styles_borders_and_effects_replace_the_last_one` (`cmd/objects.rs`) checks every row of the table above. It also checks that after undo, a new effect and border don't bring back the undone frame.

title: fix(engine): support switches and quoted bookmarks when updating REF and PAGEREF fields
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
When updating fields via `update_fields` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/references.rs`:
1. `REF` and `PAGEREF` extracted target bookmarks using `let target = instr.split_whitespace().nth(1).unwrap_or("");`. If a bookmark was quoted in the field code (e.g. `REF "MyBookmark" \h` or `PAGEREF "Chapter1"`), or had switches attached directly without spaces (`REF MyBookmark\h`), `target` retained surrounding quotes or trailing switch characters and failed to match the bookmark name in the document.
2. If `PAGEREF` or `REF` had the `\p` switch (indicating relative position such as "above" or "below"), `update_fields` did not check for `\p` and unconditionally overwritten the relative position result with a numeric page number or full bookmark text.
3. If `PAGEREF` had a `\*` format switch (e.g. `PAGEREF target \* Roman`), `update_fields` ignored the switch and formatted as decimal digits (`u32::to_string`).
4. Section page number formats (`page_num_format`) were lost during bookmark page indexing because `pages` only stored `u32` rather than `(u32, NumFormat)`.

### Solution
- Use `FieldCode::parse` to parse field codes and strip quotes and trailing switches from the target bookmark name.
- Store `(u32, NumFormat)` in `pages` based on each bookmark's section `page_num_format`.
- Check for `\p` switch with `has_switch` to preserve relative position results ("above" / "below").
- Honor `wordcraft_layout::fields::format_switch(instr)` for `PAGEREF` numbers, falling back to the section's number format.
- Added unit test `update_fields_ref_and_pageref` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/references.rs`.

title: Lists: Enter on an empty nested item numbered by its paragraph style moves it up a level (#2143)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #2143.

Enter on an empty nested item already moves it up a level when the list is numbered on the paragraph itself (the behaviour from #204, pinned by `enter_on_an_empty_nested_item_moves_it_up_a_level_first`), and I couldn't reproduce the report with lists made in WordCraft (Tab, Increase Indent, Numbering and Multilevel List buttons all promote). The case that does show the reported symptom is a Word file whose list comes from the paragraph styles: List Number / List Number 2 carry the `w:numPr` in styles.xml and the paragraphs only set `w:pStyle`. `split_para_as` only looked at the paragraph's own numbering, so on an empty List Number 2 item Enter just added another empty "e." item. It now falls back to the style's numbering, like `lists.rs` already does: the empty nested item moves up to the parent level (as direct numbering on the paragraph), and a second Enter ends the list.

If the reporter's list was built some other way, the issue may need more; happy to follow up once we know how it was made.

title: Layout: the caret after spaces hanging past the margin stays at the margin
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2146.

Spaces at the end of a line don't wrap: they hang past the right margin, which is what Word does too. But `DocLayout::caret_on` placed the caret after the full width of those spaces, so holding Space walked it off the page. It happens in the body as well as in headers, since both go through the same caret code. Word keeps the caret at the margin after hanging spaces, and that's what this does: a new `ParaLayout::caret_limit` caps the caret x on a left-to-right line at the larger of the line's right edge and the end of its last non-space cluster, so text that genuinely overflows (a long unbreakable word) still carries the caret. Bidirectional lines are left as they are for now; happy to extend it there or move the clamp elsewhere if you'd prefer.

Validation:
- `layout::tests::caret_after_hanging_spaces_stays_at_the_margin` (body and header, "a" + 200 spaces, then with a letter typed after them, which wraps to a second line): fails on main (caret at 745.6 pt, margin at 540), passes here
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout --lib caret`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-layout --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: fix(formats): support tab-separated list markers in markdown
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In CommonMark specification §5.2 (List items):
- A bullet list marker is a `-`, `+`, or `*` character, followed by at least one space or tab.
- An ordered list marker is a sequence of 1–9 ascii digits, followed by a `.` or `)` character, followed by at least one space or tab.

Previously, `list_marker` in `crates/formats/src/markdown.rs` checked:
```rust
if rest.is_empty() || rest.starts_with(' ') { Some(m) } else { None }
```
Because only `' '` was checked and not `'	'`, any list marker followed by a tab (e.g. `-\titem`, `*\titem`, `+\titem`, `1.\titem`) was rejected and parsed as a regular paragraph.
Furthermore:
- `parse_list` computed `indent(after)` which only counted space characters, failing to strip tab indentation or compute proper `content_indent`.
- `escape_line_start` only checked for `"- "` and `"+ "` and digit followed by `". "` or `") "`, failing to escape lines starting with `-\t`, `+\t`, `1.\t`, etc.

### Solution
- Allow `rest.starts_with([' ', '\t'])` in `list_marker`.
- Handle tab expansions after markers using `marker_space` in `parse_list`.
- Check for tab-separated prefixes in `escape_line_start`.
- Added unit test `tab_separated_list_markers` in `crates/formats/src/markdown.rs`.

title: fix(formats): handle negative timezone offsets and flexible day digits in spreadsheet iso_datetime
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
When reading spreadsheet dates (such as in XLSX cells of type `d` or ODS cells with `office:value-type="date"`):
1. `iso_datetime` in `crates/formats/src/sheet.rs` stripped timezone indicators by splitting `time` only on `['Z', '+', '.']`. When an ISO 8601 datetime included a negative timezone offset (e.g. `"2024-03-05T13:45:30-05:00"`), the `'-'` was not split. Splitting on `':'` then produced tokens `["13", "45", "30-05", "00"]`. Because `"30-05"` failed to parse, the trailing timezone offset `"00"` was mistakenly parsed as the seconds (or corrupting seconds with the timezone minutes for offsets like `-05:30`).
2. The day extraction used `it.next()?.get(..2)?.parse().ok()?`. If a date had a single-digit day (e.g. `"2024-03-5"` or `"2024-3-1"`), `"5".get(..2)` returned `None`, causing valid dates to fail parsing entirely.

### Solution
- Split `time` on `['Z', '+', '-', '.']` to correctly strip negative timezone offsets before parsing hours, minutes, and seconds.
- Extract digits from the day component using `chars().take_while(|c| c.is_ascii_digit())` to support single-digit and non-fixed width day formats.
- Added test cases in `dates_and_formats` in `crates/formats/src/sheet.rs`.

title: fix(engine): resolve section and section pages context when unlinking fields
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
When unlinking simple fields (\ ields.unlink\ / Ctrl+Shift+F9), \shown_text\ populated \FieldCtx\ with hardcoded \section: 1\ and \section_pages: pages.len()\, while leaving \page_format\ as the default decimal format.

Consequently, unlinking \SECTION\, \SECTIONPAGES\, or \PAGE\ fields in sections after the first or sections with custom page numbering formats resulted in incorrect values (e.g. section 1 instead of section 2, or total document pages instead of section page count).

### Solution
- Look up the current page's section index from layout to determine the 1-based section number.
- Count the pages belonging to that section for \section_pages\.
- Retrieve the section's \page_num_format\ for \page_format\.
- Added unit test \unlink_uses_section_context\ in \crates/engine/src/cmd/fields.rs\.

  * When unlinking `SECTION` and `SECTIONPAGES` fields in a later section, the displayed values now reflect that section rather than defaulting to document-wide values.

title: fix(formats): emit \landscape in RTF export when section is landscape
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
When exporting a document to Rich Text Format (RTF), \export_with\ in \crates/formats/src/rtf.rs\ wrote paper dimensions (\\paperw\, \\paperh\) and margins without checking \sec.landscape\. Because the RTF specification dictates that page orientation defaults to portrait, omitting the \\landscape\ control word causes RTF readers (including Microsoft Word and RTF consumers that expect \\landscape\ for orientation) to treat the document as portrait or lose landscape page setup.

### Solution
- Check \sec.landscape\ and emit \\landscape\ when true in \export_with\.
- Added test assertion in \page_size_and_margins\ in \crates/formats/src/rtf.rs\.

title: fix(engine): support ANSI codes and uppercase Unicode in find and replace
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In Word find and replace syntax, numeric character codes with a leading zero (e.g. ^0151 for em dash, ^0133 for ellipsis, ^0150 for en dash) represent Windows-1252 ANSI codes. Previously in  ind_pattern.rs, code_char treated 151 as a raw Unicode code point (U+0097, a C1 control code), which was subsequently discarded by .filter(|c| !c.is_control()), causing ^0151 and other ANSI character codes to return None (despite ^0151 being explicitly documented in the module's doc comments). Additionally, uppercase Unicode codes (such as ^U8212) were not recognized because only 'u' was checked.

### Fix
- Updated code_char to resolve leading-zero numeric codes (is_ansi) against Windows-1252 via wordcraft_doc::encoding::cp1252.
- Updated 
umeric_code to accept both 'u' and 'U' for Unicode character codes.
- Added unit tests for ANSI and Unicode numeric codes in compile and parse_replace.

title: fix(formats): normalize seconds rollover and support clock times in spreadsheet iso_time
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In crates/formats/src/sheet.rs:

title: Save writes the chosen file when its folder refuses a temporary file (macOS privacy protection) (#2138)
author: benandez
body:
Refs #2138 (should help, but not confirmed on a Mac yet; see **Not tested on a Mac** below).

## Problem
On macOS Tahoe, saving to `~/Desktop/TEST.docx` fails with `Operation not permitted (os error 1)`. Since #621, a save writes a sibling `.wordcraft-save-*.tmp` file and renames it over the destination. When the app isn't sandboxed and the folder is protected (Desktop, Documents, Downloads, iCloud Drive), choosing a file in the Save panel grants access to **that file only**. The likely cause is that the sibling temporary file is refused with EPERM.

## Change (`crates/engine/src/io/safe_save.rs`)
If creating the temporary file fails with `PermissionDenied` (macOS privacy protection or a read-only folder, on any OS):
- **The destination already exists:** it isn't opened at all and stays byte-identical. The save fails with an error that says what to do: *"… This folder doesn't let WordCraft create the temporary file a safe save needs, so the existing file was left unchanged. Use Save As to save the document in another folder, or allow WordCraft to use this folder in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Files and Folders, then save again."* On other systems the last part reads "get write access to this folder".

title: fix(docx): default m:bar position to top when m:pos is omitted
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In ECMA-376 Part 1 Section 22.1.2.6 (barPr), the m:pos element specifies the position of a bar function (top or bot). When m:pos or m:barPr is omitted, the standard specifies that the default value is 'top'.

Previously in crates/docx/src/read/math.rs, m:bar checked val(k.child('m:barPr'), 'm:pos') == Some('top'). If m:pos or m:barPr was omitted, this evaluated to false, wrongly turning standard OMML overbars into underbars. Furthermore, OMML boolean property values were matched case-sensitively, failing on values like Off.

### Fix
- Change m:bar position resolution to default to top when omitted.
- Case-insensitively parse OMML boolean attribute values in on().
- Add unit test verifying that omitted m:barPr/m:pos defaults to top (overbar) and explicit bot produces underbar.

title: fix(layout): support quoted bookmark names with spaces in PAGEREF fields
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In crates/layout/src/fields.rs, pageref_page previously extracted the bookmark target by splitting on whitespace (instr.split_whitespace().nth(1)). If a PAGEREF instruction referenced a quoted bookmark name containing spaces (e.g. PAGEREF 'Chapter One' \h), the target was incorrectly truncated to the first word, causing bookmark page resolution in layout to fail.

### Fix
- Add pageref_target to parse quoted bookmark arguments (with spaces) as well as unquoted bookmark arguments.
- Add unit tests verifying PAGEREF page resolution for quoted bookmarks containing spaces both with and without trailing whitespace before switches.

title: #1549: one Thai face for a run in a missing Thai font
author: C00kieMonsta
body:
Fixes #1549.

Before, a paragraph in a Thai font that is not installed (TH Sarabun New, Angsana New, Cordia New, the UPC families) fell into the generic Latin substitute lists. Those fonts have no Thai glyphs, so the Thai letters went to one fallback face and the Latin letters, digits and ฿ stayed in the Latin substitute. Next to the Thai they looked much larger. Word substitutes one font, Cordia New, for the whole run, so the paragraph keeps one consistent size.

Now Thai families have their own substitute lists. The first listed face with Latin letters and digits as well as Thai wins: Cordia New on Windows, Thonburi on macOS (Sathu for the serif families), Noto Sans Thai or a TLWG font on Linux. If the face found still lacks some of the run's Thai or Latin text, the run moves to one installed face that covers it. Only if no single face does is the per-character fallback used. This applies only to Thai fonts. A missing Latin font, including the default Aptos, keeps Latin text in its own substitute. A run with its own complex-script font keeps it for the Thai letters, and a missing Thai font listed as roman is no longer drawn in Cambria. Thai line breaking is not touched.

title: fix(engine): support nested quotations and opening delimiters in smart quotes
author: divyanshu2074
body:
In `crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs`, `autoformat` determines whether a typed quotation mark should be an opening quote or closing quote based on the preceding character. Previously, the opening context only checked whitespace, brackets/parentheses (`([{<`), and em/en dashes (`—`, `–`).

When typing an inner quotation immediately inside an outer quotation (e.g. `"'nested'"` or quotes nested inside guillemets or low quotes), the preceding character is an opening quotation mark (`“`, `‘`, `«`, `‹`, `„`, or `‚`). Because opening quotation marks were not recognized as opening contexts, the nested quotation mark was incorrectly emitted as a closing quote (e.g. `“’nested’”` instead of `“‘nested’”`).

This change:
1. Recognizes opening double quote `\u{201C}` as an opening context for single quote `'`.
2. Recognizes opening single quote `\u{2018}` as an opening context for double quote `"`.
3. Recognizes open guillemets (`«`, `‹`) and low quotes (`„`, `‚`) as opening contexts.
4. Preserves consecutive identical quotes (e.g. `""` -> `“”` and `''` -> `‘’`).
5. Adds unit tests verifying nested quotes, guillemets, parentheses, and empty quotes in typing tests.

title: fix(docx): handle case-insensitive ST_OnOff in on_off, autospacing, and tblLook
author: divyanshu2074
body:
In ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.18.66 (`ST_OnOff`), boolean on/off values (`true`, `false`, `on`, `off`, `1`, `0`) are used across properties. When documents are produced or modified by third-party word processors or exporters, values such as `Off`, `OFF`, `False`, and `FALSE` appear in attributes.

Previously:
1. `units::on_off` only matched `"0" | "false" | "off" | "False" | "FALSE"`, failing to handle `"Off"` or `"OFF"` (evaluating them to `true`).
2. `story::on_off_attr` and `props::look` only checked `"0" | "false" | "off"` without case-insensitivity or whitespace trimming, causing attributes like `w:firstRow="False"` or `w:lastRow="Off"` to be treated as `true`.
3. Paragraph autospacing parsing (`beforeAutospacing` / `afterAutospacing`) checked `matches!(v.trim(), "1" | "true" | "on")` case-sensitively.

This change:
- Introduces `units::is_off` for centralized, case-insensitive `ST_OnOff` handling.
- Updates `on_off`, `on_off_attr`, paragraph autospacing, and `w:tblLook` to use `is_off`.
- Adds unit tests in `units` and `char_units` verifying case-insensitive handling for run properties, spacing, and table look attributes.

title: fix(formats): support quoted and non-latin charset declarations in HTML decode
author: divyanshu2074
body:
In `crates/formats/src/html.rs`, `html::decode` inspects the initial bytes of an HTML document to detect character encoding before importing.

Previously, it checked only for exact substrings:
`head.contains("charset=windows-1252") || head.contains("charset=iso-8859-1") || head.contains("charset=\"windows-1252\"")`

This caused several issues:
1. `<meta charset="iso-8859-1">` (or single-quoted variants) was missed because of the quote right after `=`.
2. Non-Latin encodings explicitly declared via `<meta charset="...">` or `<meta http-equiv="Content-Type" content="text/html; charset=...">` (e.g. GBK, Shift_JIS, Windows-1251, Big5, EUC-KR) were ignored, falling back to heuristic sniffing via `chardetng` which can fail on short documents.
3. XML encoding declarations (`<?xml version="1.0" encoding="..."?>`) in XHTML documents were ignored.

This change:
- Adds `sniff_charset` to extract declared charset labels (supporting single quotes, double quotes, unquoted attributes, spaces around `=`, and XML encoding).
- Decodes using `crate::txt::decode_as(b, label)` which supports all standard WHATWG encodings via `encoding_rs`.
- Adds unit tests verifying ISO-8859-1, Windows-1252, GBK, and XML encoding declarations.

title: fix(formats): resolve sub-location and external URLs in RTF HYPERLINK fields
author: divyanshu2074
body:
In RTF files, links are stored in `HYPERLINK` field instructions (e.g. `{\field{\*\fldinst{HYPERLINK "http://example.com" \l "heading"}}{\fldrslt{link}}}`).

Previously:
1. When an external URL had a sub-location switch (e.g. `HYPERLINK "http://example.com" \l "heading"`), `hyperlink()` checked `local = rest.contains("\\l")` and prepended `#` to the entire target, converting the link to `"#http://example.com"` instead of `"http://example.com#heading"`.
2. If a URL string contained `\l` (such as `http://example.com/path\latest`), `rest.contains("\\l")` falsely marked it as a local fragment anchor.
3. Case-insensitive field names like `Hyperlink` were rejected.
4. Switches with arguments such as `\o "Help text"` could be incorrectly parsed as the URL.

This change:
- Properly parses switches and arguments in RTF HYPERLINK fields.
- Combines external URL with sub-location (`\l "sublocation"`) as `url#sublocation`.
- Supports local-only links (`HYPERLINK \l "sublocation"` -> `#sublocation`).
- Handles case-insensitive `HYPERLINK` / `Hyperlink`.
- Adds unit tests verifying URLs with sub-locations, local bookmarks, URLs containing backslashes, and extra switches.

title: #1552: no spelling squiggle under the word being typed
author: C00kieMonsta
body:
Fixes #1552.

Word draws no red squiggle under the word being typed. The squiggle appears when the word ends with a space, punctuation, Enter or Tab, or when the caret leaves the word by an arrow key, Home, End, a click or a selection. Clicking back into a misspelled word that is already there does not hide its squiggle. F7 and the Spelling pane list the word the whole time. Before this change WordCraft marked the word on every keystroke, so a word flashed red while it was being typed and the mark went away once it was spelled right.

WordCraft now does what Word does. After a `text.*` command that changes the caret's paragraph, the session records the word the caret ends or sits in. Apostrophes (straight or curly) and hyphens count as part of the word, as they do in the spelling check, so `doesn’` or `non-` is not flagged partway through. Commands that change no text, such as Insert, Delete with nothing to delete, or Shift+Tab that only outdents, start no exemption. The record is dropped as soon as the caret is anywhere else or the word's text changes. The layout leaves that range out of the spelling squiggles and keeps grammar marks. A caret move without an edit lays out only the caret's paragraph again, because the range is part of that paragraph's cache key. `review.spelling`, `review.issues` and the Spelling pane do not read the layout squiggles, so they still report the word. The rule is a single layout input, so it can move into the overlay from #1267 when that lands.

- `crates/layout/src/lib.rs`: new `LayoutOptions::typing_word` and a `TypingWord` type (paragraph revision and byte range). The range is part of the paragraph cache key only for the paragraph with that revision, and goes to `ParaEnv`.
- `crates/layout/src/para.rs`: `ParaEnv::typing_word`. `proof_issues` drops spelling issues that overlap it and keeps grammar issues.
- `crates/layout/src/table.rs`: the measuring `ParaEnv` sets the new field to `None`.

title: fix(docbin): preserve external URLs with sublocations in doc hyperlink fields
author: divyanshu2074
body:
In `crates/docbin/src/lib.rs`, binary `.doc` field instructions for `HYPERLINK` are parsed by `hyperlink_target()`.

Previously:
1. When an external URL had a sub-location switch (e.g. `HYPERLINK "http://example.com" \l "heading"`), `match local` matched `Some(name)` and discarded the external URL (`quoted`), resulting in `"#heading"` rather than `"http://example.com#heading"`.
2. Tokenization used `rest.split_whitespace()`, breaking quoted URLs or bookmark names containing spaces (e.g. `HYPERLINK "http://example.com/a path"` or `\l "Section One"`).
3. Field names starting with `Hyperlink` (case-insensitively) were rejected by strict prefix matching.

This change:
- Properly extracts arguments (handling quoted strings with spaces) and switches (`\l`, `\o`, etc.).
- Combines external URL with sub-location anchor as `url#sublocation`.
- Supports case-insensitive `HYPERLINK` field names.
- Adds unit tests verifying URLs with sub-locations, local bookmarks, and paths with spaces.

title: Right-to-left text: Latin text keeps its digits, spaces and punctuation in order (#2150)
author: D13GOOOO
body:
Fixes #2150.

## What was wrong

When Latin text with digits or punctuation came after a Persian word, it was shown in the wrong order:

| Typed | Right-to-left paragraph, before | Left-to-right paragraph, before |
|---|---|---|
| `برای مثال 2-naphthol` | `naphthol-2` | the `2` moved before the Persian words |
| `برای مثال Windows 11` | `11 Windows` | — |
| `برای مثال Fig. 3`, `e.g. 2, 3 and 4` | split at the space or full stop | — |

The cause: `bidi_levels` used only the Unicode bidi algorithm (UAX #9).

- In a right-to-left paragraph, a hyphen, space, full stop or comma between a Latin letter and a digit goes to the paragraph's direction. That breaks the Latin text into separate pieces.
- In a left-to-right paragraph, a digit after Arabic letters becomes an Arabic number and joins the Persian text.

Word keeps such text in the order it was typed. As the reporter said in the issue, spaces, full stops and commas cause the same problem as hyphens, so this PR covers all of them.

## Change (`crates/layout/src/para.rs`)

`bidi_levels` now runs `keep_latin_text_together` after UAX #9. This affects only paragraphs that already go through the bidi algorithm: right-to-left paragraphs, or paragraphs with right-to-left characters.

- **The Latin text:** it starts at the word with the first left-to-right letter and ends at the word with the last letter or digit after it. It never crosses a right-to-left letter, a tab or an explicit embedding mark.
- **One run:** all its characters take the letters' level, including digits, hyphens, spaces, brackets, full stops and commas inside it. It is drawn as a single left-to-right run.
- **Punctuation at the edges:** sentence punctuation at either end (`. , ; : ! ? …` and `، ؛ ؟`) stays the paragraph's. So the full stop that ends a Persian sentence is still at the far left.
- **Space next to the Persian text:** the spaces and punctuation between the Latin text and the right-to-left text take the paragraph's level (rule N2). So the space…

title: fix(formats): support negative timezone offsets and author fallback in ODT metadata
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
When reading metadata from OpenDocument Text (`meta.xml`), `read_meta` in `crates/formats/src/odt.rs` checked:
```rust
if !m.created.is_empty() && !m.created.ends_with('Z') && !m.created.contains('+') {
    let base = m.created.split('.').next().unwrap_or("").to_string();
    m.created = format!("{base}Z");
}
```
This exhibited two defects:
1. If an ISO 8601 creation timestamp had a negative timezone offset (e.g. `2024-03-05T13:45:00-05:00`), it did not end with `Z` and did not contain `+`. As a result, `format!("{base}Z")` appended `Z` to a timestamp that already contained `-05:00` (yielding `2024-03-05T13:45:00-05:00Z`). If it had fractional seconds with a negative offset (e.g. `2024-03-05T13:45:00.500-05:00`), splitting on `.` discarded the entire offset and replaced it with UTC `Z`. Lowercase `z` was similarly mishandled.
2. If `dc:creator` appeared in XML before `meta:initial-creator`, `m.author.is_empty()` caused `dc:creator` to populate `m.author` and then `meta:initial-creator` was appended directly to it, concatenating both names. Furthermore, documents lacking `meta:creation-date` but containing `dc:date` failed to populate `created`.

### Solution
- Check for timezone presence across `Z`, `z`, `+`, and `-` after `T`.
- Only append `Z` (and strip fractional seconds) when the timestamp does not declare a timezone.
- Decouple `creator` and `mod_date` storage so `meta:initial-creator` takes precedence regardless of element order, with `dc:creator` and `dc:date` acting as fallbacks when creation values are omitted.
- Added comprehensive unit tests in `odt::tests::meta_creation_date_timezones_and_fallbacks`.

title: fix(formats): support hex without hash, 4/8-digit CSS hex, and space rgb in parse_color
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
`parse_color` in `crates/formats/src/model.rs` parses HTML and CSS colors. It exhibited several limitations when importing documents from HTML, ODT, and LaTeX:
1. **Hex without hash**: HTML attributes like `<font color="0080ff">` or `<td bgcolor="ffffff">` omit the leading `#` (standard legacy HTML color syntax). `parse_color` required a `#` prefix to parse hex, failing to decode raw 6-digit or 3-digit hex strings.
2. **CSS Color 4 Hex Formats**: 4-digit (`#rgba`) and 8-digit (`#rrggbbaa`) hex color notations are widely used in CSS. `parse_color` failed on them because it only supported 3-digit or 6-digit hex.
3. **Space-separated RGB syntax**: Modern CSS syntax allows space-separated arguments `rgb(r g b)` and `rgb(r g b / a)`. `parse_color` only split on `,`, returning `None` for whitespace-separated channels.
4. **Common named colors**: Common colors like `pink`, `brown`, and `gold` were missing from the named color table.

### Solution
- Strip the optional `#` prefix and accept 3, 4, 6, and 8 character hex strings (mapping `#rgba` and `#rrggbbaa` to their RGB components).
- Handle whitespace-separated `rgb(...)` / `rgba(...)` formats and ignore `/ alpha` components.
- Added `brown`, `pink`, and `gold` to the named colors table.
- Added unit test cases in `model::tests::colors`.

title: fix(doc, formats): support OEM character set 255 in charset_code_page
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In Windows GDI (`LOGFONT::lfCharSet`) and the RTF Specification (§Font Table), `OEM_CHARSET` is defined as value `255` (with `254` designating `PC_437_CHARSET`).
In `crates/doc/src/encoding.rs`, `charset_code_page` mapped `254 => 437`, but omitted `255`. As a result, RTF documents referencing fonts with `\fcharset255` (such as `Terminal` or OEM-encoded fonts) failed to resolve a code page, falling back to the document's default ANSI encoding (1252) and corrupting characters like line-drawing symbols and accented letters.

### Solution
- Map both `254 | 255 => 437` in `charset_code_page`.
- Added unit tests in `encoding::tests::single_byte_code_pages` and RTF import test in `rtf::tests::code_pages_from_ansicpg_and_font_charsets`.

title: fix(formats): preserve tilde characters in LaTeX URLs and raw arguments
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In LaTeX documents, URLs, file paths, and identifiers frequently contain tilde characters (e.g. `\url{https://example.com/~user/}` or `\href{https://example.com/~user/}{link}`).
In `crates/formats/src/latex.rs`, the lexer recognizes `~` as `Tok::Tie`. When parsing raw arguments (such as URLs in `\href`, `\url`, anchor names in `\hyperlink`, labels in `\label`/`\ref`, file paths in `\includegraphics`), `raw_text` converted `Tok::Tie` to a space `' '`:
```rust
Tok::Tie => s.push(' '),
```
Consequently, URLs like `https://example.com/~user/` were decoded as `https://example.com/ user/`, corrupting both the displayed text and the link destination.

### Solution
- Map `Tok::Tie => s.push('~')` in `raw_text`, preserving the tilde in URLs, paths, and raw argument names.
- Added unit test `urls_preserve_tildes` in `latex::tests`.

title: UI: the status bar zoom slider gets Word scale, and its wheel zooms by 10% a notch (#2073)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #2073.

## What changes

The status bar's zoom slider (normal view) gets Word's behaviour:

- **The scale**: 10–100% fills the left half of the track and 100–500% the right, so 100% sits in the middle where people work. (The old slider was egui's single-logarithmic 10–500%, which put 100% at 59% of the track.)
- **1% steps**: drags land on whole percents, so the wheel-and-dialog values match what the slider sets.
- **The wheel over the slider** zooms 10% a notch — scroll up in, scroll down out, stopping at the track's ends — instead of doing nothing or scrolling the page. Whole-line notches only (mice); touchpad point-scrolls keep scrolling as before, and the canvas never scrolled from the status bar anyway (its wheel handling is pointer-gated to the canvas).

Read Mode's slider is untouched.

## Implementation

- `zoom_slider_frac` / `zoom_slider_percent` map between zoom percentages and the slider's 0..=1 fraction (piecewise logarithmic in each half); the slider runs on the fraction and commands `view.zoom` with whole percents.
- The wheel path reads whole-line `MouseWheel` events while the pointer hovers the slider, matching the canvas scroll code's unit distinction.

## Validation

- New unit tests pin the mapping: 100% ↔ the track's middle, each half logarithmic (¼ of the track = 10·√10 = 32%, ¾ = 100·√5 = 224%), drags land on whole percents and round-trip, out-of-range values clamp.
- New kittest test (`crates/ui-egui/tests/zoom_slider.rs`): a wheel notch over the slider zooms 10% in and back out, and 60 notches stop at 500% while 120 stop at 10%.
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui` green; `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` clean; `cargo xtask ci` run to completion — the only failures are the two pre-existing `crates/render` colour-emoji tests filed as #1874 (environment-dependent; `crates/render` untouched by this PR).

title: #1740: table border line styles, the border pen and per-cell borders
author: C00kieMonsta
body:
Fixes #1740.

Word's Table Design › Borders group has Line Style, Line Weight and Pen Color menus. Together they form a pen, and the Borders menu draws that pen on the sides of the selected cells, so a table can get a double line under its header row, a triple bottom rule and dashed lines between rows. WordCraft's Borders menu only drew single lines, always on the whole table, and a triple border read from a file was drawn as a double line.

Now the Borders group has the three pen menus, each choice drawn as a sample and the current one checked. The Borders menu draws the pen on the selected cells, or the caret's cell, as Word does. A cell merged down is taken whole, and a selection that starts outside the table takes whole rows. It writes cell borders on both sides of each line, a merged cell across included. When the whole table is selected it sets the table's borders and keeps the cells' own lines on the sides it doesn't cover. Scripts get the same default; `"applyTo": "table"` keeps the old whole-table behaviour. The menu also gains Left, Right, Inside Horizontal and Inside Vertical borders, Draw Table and View Gridlines. Border Painter restyles the whole table with the pen in one click; Word's paints one border per click.

Where two cells meet, a line a cell sets beats the table's, and two cells' own lines resolve as ECMA-376 §17.4.66 describes. A cell's own "no line" doesn't hide the line its neighbour inherits, and a merged cell leaves its inherited line out under neighbours that draw their own. View Gridlines shows only where a cell has no border. Triple and dot-dash borders draw as themselves on screen and in PDF. A triple grows with its width and reads heavier than a double. Vertical doubles are now two lines side by side on screen, as in PDF, instead of one line drawn twice, and vertical waves are drawn.

title: Web: keep preferences such as dark mode between visits (#2132)
author: benandez
body:
Fixes #2132.

## Problem
`load_prefs`/`save_prefs` only exist in the desktop app; `apps/wordcraft-web` never read or wrote the `UiState`, so a reload brought back light mode and default preferences.

## Change
- New `apps/wordcraft-web/src/prefs.rs`: `restore` applies stored JSON via `UiState::from_json` + `WordApp::apply_prefs` (lenient, size-capped, junk keeps defaults); `PrefsSync` serializes `WordApp::prefs()` and reports it only when it changed.
- `web.rs`: reads `localStorage["wordcraft.ui"]` at startup (then, as desktop does, a region chosen in Options replaces the first blank document), and writes it back from `logic` whenever preferences change, since browsers don't reliably run exit code on reload/tab close. Storage errors are logged, never fatal.
- Uses `web-sys` `Storage` directly (as `font_store.rs` uses IndexedDB) rather than eframe's `persistence` feature, so no new dependencies.
- Docs: ROADMAP progress log, `docs/ui-parity.md`.

title: Draw undrawable private-use list bullets as the level's default bullet, not an icon-font glyph (#1683)
author: benandez
body:
Fixes #1683.

## Problem
A list level whose bullet is a private-use character (U+F0xx) in a font that isn't installed, and that isn't a Symbol/Wingdings code we map to Unicode, had no glyph in the substitute font. Font fallback then took the first installed face with a glyph at that code. On machines with Font Awesome or a Nerd Font installed, that face is an icon font, and U+F081 there is the Twitter logo (reproduced: U+F081 in a non-symbol font draws Twitter-square, U+F099 draws the bird). Private-use codes mean something different in every font, so another face's glyph at that code is never the intended bullet.

## Change
- `crates/layout/src/para.rs`: before a bullet label is shaped, `undrawable_bullet` checks whether its text has a private-use character that isn't a mapped symbol-font code and that the label's resolved font doesn't draw (font substituted or no glyph). If so, the label shows the level's default bullet (• ○ ▪ by level), so level 2 is a hollow circle.
- `crates/doc/src/numbering.rs`: `default_bullet(level)` now holds the • ○ ▪ cycle, which `levels_for` already used.
- Docs: a `docs/layout-parity.md` row and revision entry, plus a ROADMAP progress-log row.

Bullets that draw correctly don't change. That covers Symbol and Wingdings codes with a Unicode equivalent, private-use codes in an installed font that has them, and ordinary characters. Body text isn't touched.

## Tests
- `layout::tests::private_use_bullet_no_font_draws_shows_the_levels_default_bullet`: a level-2 bullet U+F081 in a font that isn't installed now reads as `○` and draws one glyph. Without the fix it fails (`left: "\u{f081}" right: "○"`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not verified
The issue only has a screenshot, not the document, so I don't know the exact code or font its level 2 uses. The fix covers any private-use bullet its font can't draw. If the document's level 2 turns out to use something else, this may not fix it. I haven't compared against Word's own output for such a b…

title: fix(formats): support cell and paragraph borders in RTF export
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
During RTF export in `crates/formats/src/rtf.rs`:
1. Every table cell unconditionally emitted `\clbrdrt\brdrs\brdrw10\clbrdrl\brdrs\brdrw10\clbrdrb\brdrs\brdrw10\clbrdrr\brdrs\brdrw10`. As a result, borderless tables (such as those imported from RTF/HTML or layout tables) had default borders forced onto every cell, and cells with custom borders had their styles, widths, and colors overwritten with default 0.5pt black single borders.
2. In `crates/formats/src/model.rs`, `flow_paras_in` initialized `borders: None`, dropping paragraph borders when constructing flow paragraphs from a `Document`. Furthermore, RTF export in `para()` omitted writing paragraph borders (`p.borders`).

### Solution
- Added `rtf_border_style` and `Writer::write_border` / `cell_borders` in `crates/formats/src/rtf.rs` to write individual cell borders (`\clbrdr*`) based on `c.borders`, skipping borders for borderless tables and defaulting to standard grid borders only when `!t.borderless`.
- Preserved paragraph borders in `crates/formats/src/model.rs` (`flow_paras_in`) and emitted `\brdr*` controls for bordered paragraphs in `crates/formats/src/rtf.rs` (`para()`).
- Added unit test coverage verifying that borderless tables and custom cell/paragraph borders round-trip through RTF export and import.

title: fix(layout, formats, engine): ensure deterministic chronological ordering of comment replies
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description

Comment replies and author indexing across `crates/formats/src/comments.rs`, `crates/layout/src/balloons.rs`, and `crates/engine/src/cmd/review.rs` suffered from arbitrary non-deterministic ordering due to iterating directly over `doc.comments.keys()` and `doc.comments.values()` (`HashMap`).

This caused:
1. Balloon reply lists and comment note threads to display replies in random order rather than oldest-first chronological order (or lowest ID fallback), violating docstring specifications.
2. Inconsistent author color assignment in `author_index`, which depends on comment author encounter order.
3. Non-deterministic unanchored comment listings in `review::comment_list` and `formats::comments::notes`.

### Changes
- In `crates/formats/src/comments.rs`: Sort comment IDs by `(date, id)` when gathering notes and replies, ensuring deterministic chronological thread ordering.
- In `crates/layout/src/balloons.rs`: Sort comment IDs by `(date, id)` in `replies()` and `author_index()` to guarantee oldest-first display and stable author color indexes.
- In `crates/engine/src/cmd/review.rs`: Sort comment IDs deterministically when building child threads, deleting all comments, and collecting unanchored comments.
- Added automated unit tests in `crates/formats` and `crates/layout` validating that replies with disordered insertion order are resolved in oldest-first order.

title: Double-clicking a later page's footer opens it without scrolling up (#2103)
author: benandez
body:
Fixes #2103.

## Problem
Double-clicking the page number in a footer on a later page scrolled the view up instead of staying on that page. The double-click's first press in the footer band ran `caret.set` to the nearest body text (often far above, near the top of the page or earlier). Caret-follow then scrolled the view toward it, so the page slid out from under the pointer. On a long page, or one whose body text sits far from the footer, that's a big jump. This is the "footer unreachable from the body" half of #1026, which never landed on main (#1027 was closed unmerged; #1943 covers only switching between header and footer).

## Change
`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`: a primary press in the header/footer band, with the caret in the body and the press not landing on a note or text box, now leaves the caret alone (Shift+click still extends), as in Word. Without a caret move there's no caret-follow, so the view stays put. The release handler still turns the double-click into `insert.editFooter`/`insert.editHeader` for the clicked page, as before.

Presses in the body while editing a header/footer are unchanged. Making those inert as well broke dragging Behind Text header pictures that overlap the body, so that is left as is.

## Tests
- New `double_clicking_a_later_pages_footer_does_not_scroll_to_the_top` (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`): five pages with a page-number footer, scrolled to the last page's footer. A single click there must not move the caret or the view. A double-click must open the footer on that page with the view unchanged. title: feat(mailings): support \@ date format switch in MERGEFIELD
author: davidum2
body:
### What this PR does

Currently, `MERGEFIELD` fields ignore date formatting switches (`\@`), outputting raw values (e.g., `2026-10-01` or `10/10/26`) instead of respecting formatting instructions like `MERGEFIELD FECHA \@ "d 'de' MMMM 'del' yyyy"`.

This PR adds:
1. **Date switch evaluation in Mailings (`crates/engine/src/cmd/mailings.rs`):** `act()` now checks for `date_picture` in `MERGEFIELD` instructions and formats the date value with `format_date_value` when present, in both live Preview and Finish & Merge.
2. **Single-quote literal escaping & localized months (`crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs`):** `format_date_parts` now supports enclosing literal characters in single quotes (`'de'`, `'del'`) as per Word specifications, preventing the literal letter `d` from being parsed as day tokens, and includes Spanish month names when Spanish literals are detected.
3. **Slash date parsing (`crates/engine/src/cmd/controls.rs`):** `parse_date` now parses slash-delimited date strings (`DD/MM/YYYY`, `DD/MM/YY`) in addition to ISO format.
4. **Regression unit tests:** Added unit tests verifying `MERGEFIELD` date formatting switches in preview and merge operations.

### Verification

title: fix(doc, engine): support accounting format negative numbers in parentheses
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description

In accounting and financial tables, negative numbers are standardly formatted enclosed in parentheses (e.g. `(1,250.50)`, `($1,250.50)`, `$(1,250.50)`, `(1 250,00 zł)`).

Previously:
1. `wordcraft_doc::locale_number::parse_number` did not support parenthesized accounting negative numbers. As a result:
   - Table sorting in `crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs` failed to recognize accounting negative numbers as numeric, causing them to sort incorrectly as text.
   - The Formula dialog in `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs_layout.rs` failed to detect cells with negative accounting numbers above or to the left, preventing automatic prefill of `=SUM(ABOVE)` and `=SUM(LEFT)`.
2. `crates/engine/src/cmd/table_formula.rs::parse_number` attempted to strip outer `(` and `)`, but if the currency symbol or space appeared outside the parentheses (such as `$(1,250.50)`, `$ (1,250.50)`, `(1 250,00) zł`), stripping failed and the number was discarded as text or 0.
3. The Bengali Taka currency character `৳` was missing from `locale_number::CURRENCY`.

### Changes
- In `crates/doc/src/locale_number.rs`:
  - Added support for accounting negative numbers in parentheses (`(1,250.50)`, `($1,250.50)`, `$(1,250.50)`, `(1 250,00 zł)`, `(12%)`, etc.), stripping currency and `%` correctly whether inside or outside parentheses.
  - Normalized `-0.0` parsing to `0.0`.
  - Added `'৳'` to `CURRENCY`.
- In `crates/engine/src/cmd/table_formula.rs`:
  - Delegated to `locale_number::parse_number` directly on the cell text before fallback parsing.
- Added comprehensive unit tests covering accounting negative number formats across English and Polish locales in both `crates/doc` and `crates/engine`.

title: fix(docx): support hex without hash, rgb(), and case-insensitive color names in VML and DrawingML
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description

When parsing shape colors in DOCX documents:
1. `vml_color` in `crates/docx/src/read/shape_style.rs` required a leading `#` for hex colors (e.g. `#ffc000 [3207]`), but VML (ECMA-376 Part 4 §19.1.2.19, `ST_ColorType`) allows RGB hex colors without a leading hash sign (e.g. `ffc000 [3207]`, `c0c0c0`, `f00`), as well as `rgb(...)` color specifications. Omitting `#` or using `rgb(...)` caused VML shape fill, stroke, and watermark colors to fail parsing and fall back to default colors.
2. `preset_color` in `crates/docx/src/read/drawing_color.rs` used case-sensitive matching on color names (e.g. failing on `"Red"`, `"WHITE"`, `"Green"`), and only matched lowercase variants of `ltGray`/`dkGray` while missing standard DrawingML preset color names like `lightGray`, `darkGray`, `darkBlue`/`dkBlue`, `gold`, `coral`, `salmon`, `tomato`, `violet`, `indigo`, `beige`, `ivory`, etc. (ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.10.47 `ST_PresetColorVal`).

### Changes
- In `crates/docx/src/read/shape_style.rs`:
  - Added support for 3- and 6-digit hex colors without a `#` prefix in `vml_color`.
  - Added support for `rgb(...)` / `rgba(...)` color declarations in `vml_color`.
- In `crates/docx/src/read/drawing_color.rs`:
  - Made `preset_color` case-insensitive.
  - Added support for `lightGray`/`lightGrey`, `darkGray`/`darkGrey`, `darkBlue`/`dkBlue`, `darkRed`/`dkRed`, `darkGreen`/`dkgreen`, `lightBlue`/`ltBlue`, `gold`, `coral`, `salmon`, `tomato`, `violet`, `indigo`, `beige`, and `ivory`.
- Added unit tests for both `vml_color` and `preset_color` verifying hex-without-hash, rgb(), case-insensitivity, and new preset color names.

title: M7: replace English stem guessing with an indexed full-form lexicon
author: JinParkmida
body:
Separate English spelling from Moby hyphenation. Replace unrestricted affix stripping with explicit ESDB forms and a curated supplement. Index correction candidates by length and reuse bounded scoring buffers.

Trade-off: legitimate forms absent from the lexicon may now be flagged. Coverage gaps require data updates, explicit supplements or user additions; the uploader regression is covered by an explicit supplement entry. This favors predictable acceptance over open-ended derivation.

Add lexical, scoring and review-command regressions, reproducible data generation, source/license attribution, and documented scope limits. The diagnostic examples do not establish corpus-wide accuracy or superiority.

title: fix(formats): ignore block and inline HTML comments in markdown import
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description

In Markdown (CommonMark Spec §4.6 and §6.8), HTML comments (`<!-- ... -->`) are raw HTML comments and must produce no visible output in the document.

Previously:
- In `crates/formats/src/markdown.rs`, `parse_blocks` and `parse_inlines` had no handling for HTML comments. As a result, HTML comments (e.g. `<!-- slide -->`, `<!-- comment -->`, multiline `<!--\n...\n-->`, or inline comments `Hello <!-- comment -->world`) were parsed as visible text and rendered directly into paragraphs and cells.

### Changes
- In `crates/formats/src/markdown.rs`:
  - Added HTML block comment handling in `parse_blocks` to swallow both single-line and multi-line comments starting with `<!--` through `-->`.
  - Allowed `<!--` to interrupt open paragraphs in `interrupts`.
  - Added inline HTML comment handling in `tokenize` to skip `<!-- ... -->` sequences.
  - Avoided pushing empty paragraphs in `flush_para` when inlines are empty.
  - Added unit test `html_comments_are_ignored_in_blocks_and_inlines` verifying that single-line block comments, multi-line block comments, and inline comments produce no visible document text.

title: AutoCorrect: reversing a capitalisation adds an automatic exception, as in Word (#1857)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1857 for plain paragraphs. The list-paragraph cases in the Windows comment are a separate behaviour; see below.

## What was wrong
When you reverse an automatic capital in Word, by undoing it or by backspacing over the word and retyping it, Word remembers the decision: it adds the word before the capital (for example `there.`) to AutoCorrect's First Letter exceptions. It then stops capitalising after that word. WordCraft re-applied the capital every time.

## What changed
- **Undo:** an Undo that reverses an automatic capital adds the preceding token to the First Letter exception list, when "Automatically add words to list" is on. Only tokens ending in "." are added.
- **Backspace and retype:** backspacing over the capitalised word and retyping it does the same.
- **INitial CAps:** undoing an INitial CApitals fix (`TWo` → `Two`) adds `TWo` to the INitial CAps exceptions.
- **Other Corrections:** undoing an ordinary correction such as `teh` → `the` adds nothing, as in Word.
- **Settings:** each list has an "Automatically add words to list" switch, on by default, in AutoCorrect Options › Exceptions and on the `tools.autocorrect` command. They're saved with the other AutoCorrect settings.
- **Safeguards:**
  - Only the Undo that reverses the capital's own step counts, matched by a counter that only grows. It doesn't depend on the undo history's position, so a full history doesn't cause false matches.
  - Any other Undo, a new or opened document, or a failed command forgets the capital.
  - Added words go through the same checks as manual exceptions: no spaces, at most 255 characters.

## Checked in Word for Mac 16.113.4
- `hello there. world `, then ⌘Z: `there.` is added to First Letter, and the retyped line isn't capitalised.
- Backspacing over the word and retyping it: same result.
- `TWo`, then ⌘Z: `TWo` is added to INitial CAps and isn't corrected again.
- `teh`, then ⌘Z: nothing is added.

Not yet in WordCraft: Word also leaves the *first* word of that same…

title: fix(formats): support borderless and bordered tables in ODT import and export
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In ODT export, `Writer::automatic_styles` hardcoded `fo:border="0.5pt solid #000000"` for every cell style, forcing visible borders even when tables were explicitly borderless (`t.borderless == true`).
In ODT import, `ODocReader` ignored `fo:border` in table/cell styles and hardcoded `borderless: false` for all tables, preventing borderless tables from retaining their borderless state when loaded from OpenDocument files.

### Solution
1. In `Writer`:
   - Updated `cell_styles` to track `(Option<Rgb>, bool)` representing `(shading, borderless)`.
   - Updated `table` to pass `t.borderless` to `cell_style`.
   - Updated `automatic_styles` to emit `fo:border="none"` when `borderless` is true, and `fo:border="0.5pt solid #000000"` when false.
2. In `ODocReader`:
   - Added border detection in `table-properties` and `table-cell-properties` checking `fo:border` and side borders (`fo:border-top`, etc.) for values other than `"none"` / 0.
   - Initialized `TableB.has_borders` from table style, and updated it if any cell style has borders.
   - When constructing `FTable` on table close, set `borderless: !t.has_borders`.
3. Added unit tests verifying:
   - Full round-trip preservation of both borderless and bordered tables in ODT.
   - Direct import of ODT tables with `fo:border="none"` as borderless and `fo:border="0.5pt solid #000000"` as bordered.

title: The I-beam pointer shows on white paper on Windows (#1746)
author: benandez
body:

title: fix(formats): support borderless and bordered tables in LaTeX import and export
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In LaTeX export (`crates/formats/src/latex.rs`), `Writer::table` hardcoded vertical rules `|` in column specs and horizontal lines `\hline` between all rows, forcing visible borders even when tables were explicitly borderless (`t.borderless == true`).
In LaTeX import, `table()` hardcoded `borderless: false` for all tables regardless of whether the `tabular` spec or body contained any vertical rules (`|`) or horizontal rules (`\hline`, `\cline`, `\toprule`, etc.), causing borderless LaTeX tables to be assigned a grid style upon import.

### Solution
1. In `Writer::table` (export):
   - Check `t.borderless`: if true, generate column spec without `|` separators (e.g. `p{88pt} p{188pt}`) and omit `\hline` between rows and around multicolumn spans.
   - If false, retain the bordered tabular layout (`|p{...}|` and `\hline`).
2. In `table()` (import):
   - Inspect the column spec and row commands for any rule indicators (`|`, `\hline`, `\cline`, `\toprule`, `\midrule`, `\bottomrule`).
   - If no rules are found, set `borderless: true` on the parsed `FTable`.
3. Added unit tests verifying:
   - Exported borderless tables omit `\hline` and column-spec `|` rules.
   - Borderless and bordered tables round-trip through LaTeX while maintaining their respective borderless/bordered styles.

title: fix(docx): support preset/system colors, tint/shade modifiers, and default outline width in WordArt
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
In DOCX WordArt text effects reader (`crates/docx/src/read/wordart.rs`):
1. `color()` only matched `w14:srgbClr` and `w14:schemeClr`. When effects used `w14:prstClr` (preset color) or `w14:sysClr` (system color), `color()` returned `None`, dropping the fill, glow, shadow, or outline.
2. `w14:tint` and `w14:shade` color modifiers were ignored, failing to adjust the base color towards white or black.
3. In `w14:textOutline`, if the optional width attribute `w14:w` was omitted, the reader returned `0.0` pt width instead of the default 0.75 pt, preventing the outline from rendering.

### Solution
1. In `crates/docx/src/read/wordart.rs`:
   - Updated `color()` to recognize `w14:prstClr` and `w14:sysClr`, resolving them via `super::drawing_color::preset_color`.
   - Handled `w14:tint` and `w14:shade` modifiers using `super::drawing_color::mix`.
   - Added `emu_or` helper so `w14:textOutline` defaults `w14:w` to 0.75 pt when omitted.
   - Handled `w14:alpha` whether placed directly as a modifier on the color element or on the parent effect.
2. In `crates/docx/src/read/drawing_color.rs`:
   - Exposed `pub(crate) fn mix` for sharing color tint/shade calculations.
3. Added unit tests for:
   - Default 0.75 pt outline width when `w14:w` is omitted.
   - Preset color resolution in fills and glow effects.
   - Tint and shade modifier calculations on WordArt colors.

title: RTF import: heading and code formatting compared with the file's own stylesheet (gap 19 follow-up)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Follow-up to #2088 (gap 19, RTF formatting revisions), now merged; this branch is rebased onto main and has two commits.

## What changed
On RTF import, WordCraft used to clear every direct size and bold on heading and Title text, and the font, size and bold on Code text, so the paragraph style would decide. That threw away sizes and bold the user had set by hand. It also meant that rejecting a tracked formatting change in such a paragraph couldn't restore them.

The reader now records each `\stylesheet` entry's `\b`, `\i`, `\fs` and `\f`, following `\sbasedon` (at most 16 hops, loops skipped). A run's property is dropped only when it equals the value from the file's own style:
- If a style's chain sets any character formatting, it counts as a full description: a missing `\b` or `\i` means off, a missing `\fs` means RTF's 12 pt. So Word 365's non-bold headings keep bold set by hand, and tracked bold changes in them still work.
- WordCraft's own style values are used only when the chain has no character words at all, e.g. `{\s2 heading 2;}`. The font falls back on its own, because WordCraft's writer puts the code font on the paragraph rather than in the Code style.
- A stylesheet entry without `\sN` is Normal and no longer overwrites the entry before it.

Applies to the run's formatting and to the old formatting of a tracked change. The writer is unchanged. Word evidence: Word writes resolved values in RTF, and `\oldcprops` holds only the changed properties.

## Tests (crates/formats/src/rtf.rs; each new test failed before the fix)
`heading_runs_are_compared_with_the_files_heading_style`, `style_formatting_is_resolved_through_sbasedon` (LibreOffice-style chain), `code_runs_in_the_files_code_font_have_no_direct_font`, `hostile_sbasedon_chains_are_harmless`, `a_style_chain_without_a_size_has_rtfs_default_size`, `a_code_paragraph_round_trips_without_a_direct_code_font`, `a_stylesheet_entry_without_a_number_is_normal`, `a_heading_size_set_by_hand_survives_in_the_old_form…

title: Layout: text above a float's anchor wraps around it (#2048)
author: benandez
body:
Fixes #2048.

## Problem
Layout adds a floating object's wrap area to the page only when it reaches the object's anchor paragraph. A picture anchored in a later paragraph but placed higher up the page (fixed on the page / margin, or with a negative offset from its paragraph) was wrapped by its own paragraph and the ones after it, while the paragraphs above the anchor on that page ran behind it.

## Change (`crates/layout/src/lib.rs`)
- `anchor_floats` records each body float placed above its anchor paragraph's top while text was already placed before it on the page (page index, block, object index, wrap area).
- At the end of a pass, if those floats differ from the ones the pass started with, `layout_pass` returns `Pass::Rewrap` and the layout runs again. In the new pass each page starts with those wrap areas (`PageBuilder::new_page`), so the earlier paragraphs wrap around the float. This is the same kind of loop that page totals already use. When layout reaches the anchor, the seeded area is updated in place and not added a second time.
- At most 3 extra passes (`MAX_REWRAP_PASSES`). Documents without such floats never take an extra pass.

## Tests
- `layout::tests::a_float_placed_above_its_anchor_wraps_the_paragraphs_before_it`: covers a page-relative float and a paragraph-relative float with a negative offset, both anchored in the 5th paragraph. It checks that every line beside the picture starts to its right. It fails with the fix turned off and passes with it.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.
- Rendered a repro doc built through CLI commands with `wordcraft-cli render` and checked the PNG: all three paragraphs above the anchor now wrap to the right of the picture.

## Not verified
- Not compared side by side with Word on this machine (Word's behaviour is from the issue screenshot).
- Text in an *earlier column* beside a float anchored in a later column is still not wrapped (#1158) unless the float is also above its anchor.
- A paragraph-relative float that keeps movi…

title: fix(engine): support none in wordart reflection and outline color
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description
This PR addresses inconsistencies in WordArt / text effect parameter parsing in `crates/engine/src/cmd/wordart.rs`:
1. In `parse_reflection`, passing `{"reflection": "none"}` previously returned a parameter error (`CmdError::Params`) because only `null` and boolean `false` were accepted to clear reflection, unlike `parse_fill`, `parse_outline`, `parse_shadow`, and `parse_glow` which all accept `"none"`.
2. In `parse_outline`, passing `{"color": "none"}` within an object parameter (e.g. from `wordArt.textOutline` or `format.textEffects`) previously failed `Rgb::parse` and fell back to `d.color` (`Some(Rgb::BLACK)`), producing a black outline instead of no outline line.
3. Case-insensitivity (`eq_ignore_ascii_case("none")`) is now handled across `parse_outline`, `parse_shadow`, `parse_glow`, and `parse_reflection`.

### Testing
- Added unit test `wordart_reflection_and_outline_none_options` in `crates/engine/src/tests_wordart.rs`.
- Verified all tests in `wordcraft-engine` pass cleanly via `cargo test -p wordcraft-engine -- tests_wordart`.
