title: fix(doc): support accounting negative format, trailing minus, and expanded currency symbols

title: fix(doc): format hex number format as uppercase hex and support millions in cardinal text
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Summary of Changes

1. **`NumFormat::Hex` Formatting (`crates/doc/src/section.rs`)**:
   - In ECMA-376 §17.18.59, `hex` specifies that numbering sequences consist of uppercase hexadecimal digits (e.g. `10` -> `A`, `15` -> `F`, `16` -> `10`, `255` -> `FF`).
   - Previously, `NumFormat::Hex` was omitted from formatting and fell through to decimal `n.to_string()`, incorrectly outputting decimal strings.
   - Added `NumFormat::Hex => format!("{n:X}")` branch and removed it from decimal fallback list.

2. **Million and Billion Ranges in `cardinal_text` and `ordinal_text`**:
   - Previously, `cardinal_text` clamped inputs to `999_999`, converting any value $\ge 1,000,000$ (such as character count / word count fields formatted with `\* Cardinal` or `\* Ordinal`) to "nine hundred ninety-nine thousand nine hundred ninety-nine".
   - Expanded words generation to support `1_000_000..=999_999_999` (millions) and $\ge 1,000,000,000$ (billions), enabling proper formatting of large numbers (e.g. `1_000_000` -> "One Million", `ordinal_text` -> "One Millionth").

3. **Testing**:
   - Added unit test cases verifying `NumFormat::Hex` for values `10` ("A"), `15` ("F"), `16` ("10"), `255` ("FF"), as well as `CardinalText` and `OrdinalText` for 1,000,000 and 2,000,000,000.
   - All tests pass cleanly.

title: fix(doc): handle start 0 list counters and preserve literal %0 placeholders
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description
This change resolves two bugs in document list numbering counters (`crates/doc/src/numbering.rs`):
1. **List levels starting at 0:** `Counters` previously stored raw `u32` values where `0` was treated ambiguously as both an unstarted level sentinel and the counter value. If a list level had `start: 0`, the first call set `*v = 0`, and subsequent calls saw `*v == 0`, resetting it to `0` repeatedly. Using `[Option<u32>; 9]` properly distinguishes an unstarted level (`None`) from a level initialized to `0` (`Some(0)`), allowing `0`, `1`, `2`, ... to advance as expected.
2. **Literal `%0` placeholders:** Template string interpolation matched `%` followed by any digit (`\d`), consuming `%0` as a level reference (`k = 0`, level 1). ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.9 defines level placeholders as 1-based `%1` through `%9`. Matching is now restricted to `(1..=9).contains(&d)`, preserving literal `%0` (and characters following `%`) correctly.

### Testing
- Added unit tests:
  - `start_zero_counters_increment_properly`: verifies that list levels with `start = 0` advance from 0 to 1 to 2.
  - `placeholder_percent_zero_is_preserved_as_literal`: verifies that `%0` is preserved as literal text in list labels.
- Passed all unit tests in `crates/doc`.

title: Fix numbered list levels that start at 0 or are overridden to 1
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/doc/src/numbering.rs:319` (no existing issue): Numbered list level with "Start at: 0" labels every item 0 (0., 0., 0., …) instead of counting up.

## Cause
`Counters::next_label` used a counter value of 0 to mean "this level has not started yet". A level with `start = 0` therefore reset to its start on every item and was labelled `0.` each time. A `startOverride` of 1 is stored as 0, so it was also read as "not started" and fell back to the level's own start.

## Fix
`Counters` now keeps a separate per-level flag for whether the level has counted yet, plus the pending start-override value. An override sets the value of the level's first item. Counting up, restarting deeper levels and rendering `%N` placeholders use that flag instead of testing for 0.

## Verified
- Regression tests `a_level_starting_at_zero_counts_up`, `a_start_override_of_one_or_zero_is_honoured`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-doc --lib numbering::tests::a_`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The public `Counters::values` still reports 0 for a level that has not counted yet. How the DOCX reader parses `w:start` and `startOverride` is unchanged.

title: fix(formats): preserve paragraph spacing in flow and support RTF distributed alignment
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description
This change resolves several issues across the shared flow model (`crates/formats/src/model.rs`) and the RTF importer/exporter (`crates/formats/src/rtf.rs`):
1. **Flow Paragraph Spacing and Borders Preservation:** `model::flow_paras_in` previously initialized paragraphs with `spacing: Spacing::default()` and `borders: None`, entirely discarding the document's paragraph margins (`space_before`, `space_after`), line spacing, indents (`left`, `right`, `first`), and borders when mapping from `Document` to `Flow`. Spacing and borders are now preserved across flow conversions and internal page break splits.
2. **RTF Distributed Alignment:** RTF specifies `\qd` (and Word 2000's `\qk`) for distributed text alignment (`Align::Distribute`). Previously, `\qd` was conflated with `\qj` (justify) on import and export wrote `\qj`. `\qd` / `\qk` are now mapped to `Align::Distribute`, and `Align::Distribute` exports as `\qd`.
3. **RTF Paragraph Spacing & Indents Export:** Normal paragraphs in RTF now export their spacing (`\sb`, `\sa`) and indents (`\li`, `\ri`, `\fi`) rather than silently omitting them.
4. **RTF Special Characters & Surrogates:** Added support for named control words `\thinspace` (`\u{2009}`), `\nonbreakingspace` (`\u{00A0}`), `\optionalhyphen` (`\u{00AD}`), and `\nonbreakinghyphen` (`\u{2011}`). Additionally, fixed Unicode escape processing so orphaned or consecutive high surrogates emit the replacement character `\u{FFFD}` instead of being silently dropped.

### Testing
- Added unit tests:
  - `distribute_align_and_paragraph_spacing`: verifies import of `\qd` and `\qk` as `Align::Distribute`, paragraph spacing/indent properties, and their round-trip export into RTF control words.
  - `special_characters_and_surrogates`: verifies decoding of named spaces/hyphens and correct replacement character handling for orphaned high surrogates.
- Passed full test suite across `wordcraft-formats`.

title: Fonts: fallback no longer keeps unneeded font families in memory
author: arcanii
body:
## What it does

A character no loaded font covers (an emoji, a CJK character, a symbol) made `FontDb::system_fallback` load every installed family in the fallback list, in order, until one covered it. The families that didn't cover it stayed loaded for good, since faces are never unloaded.

- **On a Mac,** every CJK family in `SYSTEM_FALLBACKS` is installed. One emoji loaded PingFang, Hiragino Sans, Apple SD Gothic Neo, Heiti SC, STHeiti and Arial Unicode MS (about 330 MB) before Apple Color Emoji.
- **On Windows,** an emoji loaded Arial, Segoe UI, Microsoft YaHei, Yu Gothic, Malgun Gothic and Segoe UI Symbol first.

Now a preferred family loads only when one of its files maps the character. The fallback order is unchanged, and a family that has the character still loads whole, with all its styles.

## How

- **The check:** `system_fallback` asks the coverage index (#605) before it loads a preferred family (`family_maps`). A family none of whose files maps the character is skipped. It isn't marked as tried, so it still loads later for a character it has.
- **Character maps only:** the index now reads only each file's character maps (`cmap`), not the whole file (`file_coverage`).
  - The reads go through a `TableReader` that `file_face_names` now uses too.
  - The index therefore also covers files over the 40 MB limit, which the preferred families need: PingFang is 75 MB, Apple Color Emoji 183 MB.
  - Indexing a file costs kilobytes instead of the whole file.
  - `indexed_fallback` still loads only files up to 40 MB.
- `CoverageIndex::reads` now counts character-map reads.

**How it was measured:**
- macOS 27.0.1 on an Apple M3 Max, release builds of `main` (`86adfd3`) and of this branch, run side by side.
- Synthetic one-line documents.
- Physical footprint (Activity Monitor's "Memory") from `proc_pid_rusage`: the kernel's peak for the CLI, and the settled value for the headless `ui_shot` window.

| One-line document | `info` | `convert` to PDF | Interface |

title: fix(txt): support UTF-32 LE/BE BOMs and detect unmarked UTF-16 on odd-length input
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description
This change resolves two text encoding issues in the plain text importer (`crates/formats/src/txt.rs`):
1. **UTF-32 LE and BE BOM Support:** UTF-32 LE documents start with byte order mark `FF FE 00 00`. Because `decode` and `is_text` previously only checked for the 2-byte prefix `FF FE`, UTF-32 LE files were mistakenly treated as UTF-16 LE with leading NUL characters, corrupting every decoded code point. Furthermore, UTF-32 BE (`00 00 FE FF`) was unrecognized. Added `utf32` decoding and explicit checks for both 4-byte BOMs before 2-byte BOMs per the Unicode Standard §3.10.
2. **Unmarked UTF-16 with Odd Lengths:** `unmarked_utf16` previously required `b.len().is_multiple_of(2)`, rejecting valid UTF-16 files that contain a stray or truncated trailing byte. Since `utf16` already handles chunking via `as_chunks::<2>()`, `unmarked_utf16` now evaluates the sample without rejecting odd overall buffer lengths.

### Testing
- Added unit tests:
  - `utf32_bom_decoding`: verifies correct detection and decoding of UTF-32 LE and UTF-32 BE files with BOM.
  - `unmarked_utf16_with_odd_trailing_byte`: verifies that an odd-length UTF-16 sample is correctly detected and decoded.
- Passed all unit tests in `wordcraft-formats`.

title: OpenType ligatures follow w14:ligatures: model, DOCX read and write, shaping
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
OpenType ligatures follow `w14:ligatures`: a document that asks for none, or for historical and discretional ones, is now drawn that way, and the setting survives saving.

Word stores the Font dialog's Advanced ▸ Ligatures choice (None, Standard Only, Standard and Contextual, Historical and Discretional, All) as `w14:ligatures` in run properties, styles and document defaults; the value is any combination of the four flags, 16 names in [MS-DOCX]. This PR reads and writes the property at all three levels, inherits it like the other run properties, and maps each flag to its OpenType feature when shaping: standard `liga`, contextual `clig`, historical `hlig`, discretional `dlig`. `rlig` (Arabic lam-alef) and `calt` are left alone; contextual alternates are a separate Word option (`w14:cntxtAlts`). An unknown value is ignored, and nothing is written when the document has no value.

One choice I'd like your view on: without the property Word draws no ligatures, while WordCraft has always drawn standard and contextual ones. Here a missing value keeps WordCraft's current default, so no existing document reflows. The alternative is to follow Word, as was done for kerning (`w:kern`: no value means unkerned, and new documents get Kerning for fonts from the default stylesheet, `styles.rs:475`). In that version a missing value would mean no ligatures, and `Document::new()` would put `standardContextual` in the defaults, so new documents keep them and Word draws them too. The cost is that every .docx without the property, which is most files saved before Microsoft 365, would lose its fi/ffi ligatures and could wrap differently. Happy to switch.

Left out: the Ligatures entry in the Font dialog (it goes next to Kerning, after #2295), contextual alternates, stylistic sets and number forms.

title: fix(comments): case-insensitive extension matching, case-insensitive body tag, and cycle guard
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description
This PR addresses three issues in `crates/formats/src/comments.rs`:

1. **Cycle guard in `root()`**: If comments form a cyclic parent relationship (e.g. comment 1 points to 2 and comment 2 points to 1), `root()` previously iterated up to `MAX_PARENT_CHAIN` (64 times). Because 64 is even, starting at 1 ended back at 1 (`root(&doc, 1) == 1`), erroneously reporting the cyclical comment as its own root. Tracking visited comment IDs via a `HashSet` allows cycle detection and stops immediately.
2. **Case-insensitive and dot-tolerant format extension matching in `append()`**: `ext` can be passed as `".html"`, `"HTML"`, `".md"`, `".TXT"`. Cleaning `ext` with `ext.trim_start_matches('.').to_ascii_lowercase()` ensures files with uppercase or dot-prefixed extensions have their comments properly appended.
3. **Case-insensitive `</body>` tag detection**: When appending comments into HTML, `s.rfind("</body>")` was case-sensitive, missing closing `</BODY>` or mixed-case tags and appending comments after `</html>` at `s.len()`. A case-insensitive reverse finder ensures comment sections are always placed before the closing body tag.

### Testing
- Added unit tests in `crates/formats/src/comments.rs`:
  - `append_handles_case_insensitive_extensions_and_body_tag`: checks uppercase extensions `.HTML`, `.MD`, `.TXT` and uppercase `</BODY>` tag.
  - `comment_cycle_does_not_loop_or_falsely_become_root`: verifies cyclical comments do not falsely identify as roots or loop.
- Verified test suite passes via `cargo test --lib -p wordcraft-formats`.

title: fix(math): parse array column specs, support starred operatorname and tag, preserve delim sep in latex
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description
This PR fixes several LaTeX math parser and exporter issues in `crates/doc/src/math_latex.rs`:

1. **`array` / `tabular` arguments and column specs**:
   - `\begin{array}` requires a column specification argument (e.g. `{lcr}`) and accepts an optional position `[pos]`. Previously, `environment` did not consume these arguments and immediately began parsing cells with `self.seq(false)`, causing `{lcr}` to be mistakenly parsed as the contents of the first cell (`"lcr a"`), corrupting table structure.
   - Now parses the optional `[pos]` argument, extracts the column specification `{spec}`, and populates `col_jc` with corresponding `ColJc::Left`, `ColJc::Right`, and `ColJc::Center` values.
   - Also skips the optional `[pos]` argument in `\begin{aligned}[pos]`.
2. **`\operatorname*` and starred operators**:
   - LaTeX's `\operatorname*{argmin}_{x}` displays limits underneath (like `\lim`). Previously, the `*` remained unparsed in the token stream as a multiplication operator and subscripts were treated as regular indices rather than limits under the operator.
3. **`\tag` and `\tag*` support**:
   - Added support for `\tag{...}` and `\tag*{...}` equation numbers, converting them to WordCraft equation number markers (`# (...)` or `# ...`).
4. **Custom delimiter separator in `to_latex`**:
   - When exporting `MNode::Delim`, the custom separator `sep: Option<char>` was previously ignored and hardcoded to `\middle|`. It now respects `sep` (e.g. `Some('‖')` produces `\middle\|`).

### Testing
- Added unit tests in `crates/doc/src/math_latex.rs`:
  - `array_column_specs_and_aligned_optional_args`: verifies column alignment parsing and cell content isolation in `\begin{array}{lcr}`.
  - `operatorname_starred_and_tag`: checks `\operatorname*` with limits and `\tag` equation numbering.
  - `delim_preserves_custom_separator`: verifies `\middle\|` for double bar separators.
- Verified test suite passes cleanly via `cargo test --lib -p wordcraft-doc`.

title: fix(latex): export combining accents as math commands, expand symbols and allow standard math commands
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description
This PR addresses several issues in `crates/formats/src/latex.rs` when translating between linear format equations and LaTeX math:

1. **LaTeX Export of Combining Accents in Math**:
   - `latex_to_linear` converts commands like `\vec{a}` and `\hat{x}` into unicode characters with combining accents (`a⃗`, `x̂`).

Standard TeX engines (like pdfLaTeX) cannot compile combining accents in math mode and throw `inputenc` errors.
   - Added `wrap_last_atom` which correctly transforms combining marks back into proper LaTeX commands (`\vec{a}`, `\hat{x}`, `\bar{x}`, `\dot{x}`, `\ddot{x}`, `\tilde{x}`).
2. **Expansion of Allowed Math Commands (`MATH_COMMANDS`)**:
   - `known_math_command` guards which commands from linear text may be written out without escaping `\`.
   - Commands such as `\text`, `\vec`, `\hat`, `\bar`, `\boxed`, `\dot`, `\ddot`, `\binom`, `\tag`, and `\phantom` were missing from `MATH_COMMANDS`, causing them to be incorrectly escaped as `\backslash text`, `\backslash boxed`, etc.
   - Added these standard math commands to `MATH_COMMANDS`.

title: Home › Font: a collapsed caret and the Font box at the caret follow Word (#1418)
author: dkhlapov
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"dkhlapov"} -->
_Requested by **Dima**_

Fixes #1418.

Before: with the caret inside a word that mixes fonts, sizes or weights (no selection), the Font box, the Size box and the Bold/Italic buttons went blank. With the caret in Chinese, Japanese or Korean text, the Font box showed the Latin font (`w:ascii`) instead of the East Asian one (`w:eastAsia`).

After, checked in Word for Mac 16.113.4:
- **At a caret inside a word,** the Font and Size boxes and the on/off buttons show the character before the caret. In "Hel" (Courier New 20) + "lo" (plain), the caret in the first part shows Courier New / 20, and in the second the default font and size. A mixed selection still shows blank.
- **Toggles follow the button shown:** with the caret in the bold part, ⌘B makes the whole word plain; in the plain part, it makes the whole word bold. The same goes for Italic, Underline and the rest.
- **Whole-word formatting is unchanged:** Bold, a font or a size with the caret inside a word still formats the whole word, as Word does with its default "Select entire word when selecting text" setting. title: fix(smart_art): normalize layout and color identifiers and preserve item text with leading whitespace

title: fix(docx): support fill color on v:fill, broader watermark IDs, and modulo 360 diagonal check
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Summary of Changes

1. **Watermark Fill Color Detection**:
   - In DOCX VML (`vml_watermark`), watermark shape colors can be declared either via `fillcolor` on `<v:shape>` or via `color` on a child `<v:fill color="#...">`. The reader previously only inspected `shape.attr("fillcolor")`, causing watermarks using `<v:fill color="..."/>` to revert to default color. Now checks `<v:fill color="...">` as a fallback.

2. **Broader Watermark ID Matching**:
   - Word and third-party tools (LibreOffice, WPS) emit watermarks under various ID schemes (e.g., `WordWatermarkObject`, `WordPictureWatermark`, `Watermark`). Previously only `id.starts_with("PowerPlusWaterMarkObject")` was matched. Now matches any ID containing `"watermark"` (case-insensitive).

3. **Modulo 360 Diagonal Rotation Check**:
   - Rotations such as `rotation:360` or `rotation:0` represent horizontal orientations. Previously, `diagonal` was determined strictly by `deg != 0.0`, mistakenly classifying a 360-degree rotation as diagonal. Updated to check `deg.rem_euclid(360.0)` within `(1.0..359.0)`.

### Verification
- Added automated unit test in `crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs` verifying watermarks with child `<v:fill color="...">`, `WordWatermarkObject` ID, and `rotation:360`.
- All fixture and roundtrip watermark tests pass cleanly.

author: divyanshu2074
body:

title: fix(docx): make doc and docx property parsing case-insensitive and whitespace-tolerant
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description

In DOCX files produced by various word processors and third-party tools, enumerated attribute values such as paragraph alignment (`w:jc/@w:val`), tab stops (`w:tab/@w:val`, `w:tab/@w:leader`), cell vertical alignment (`w:vAlign/@w:val`), run text vertical alignment (`w:vertAlign/@w:val`), table layout and sizing (`w:tblLayout/@w:type`, `w:tblW/@w:type`), section start type (`w:type/@w:val`), and highlight/underline/border styles are frequently capitalized or padded with whitespace (e.g. `Center`, `Right`, `MiddleDot`, `Restart`, `Fixed`, `YELLOW`, `SINGLE`).

Previously:
1. `Underline::from_ooxml` matched aliases case-sensitively and defaulted unknown values to `Underline::Single`, turning explicit `"0"`, `"false"`, or `"off"` values into `Underline::Single` instead of `Underline::None`.
2. `Highlight::from_ooxml` and `BorderStyle::from_ooxml` matched case-sensitively and failed on padded strings or uppercase styles (e.g., `"YELLOW"` or `"None"` or `"0"`).
3. `align(v)` in `crates/docx/src/read/props.rs` matched case-sensitively, causing `"Center"`, `"Right"`, and `"Both"` to fall through to `Align::Left`.
4. `tab_stop`, `w:vertAlign`, `w:vAlign`, `w:vMerge`, `w:hMerge`, `gap_width`, and `sectpr` attributes were checked case-sensitively against lowercase strings without trimming whitespace.

### Fix
- Updated `Underline::from_ooxml`, `Highlight::from_ooxml`, and `BorderStyle::from_ooxml` to be case-insensitive, trim whitespace, and correctly map boolean-off values (`"none"`, `"0"`, `"false"`, `"off"`) to `None`.
- Normalized alignment, tab stop kind and leader, cell vertical alignment, merge flags, and section properties in `crates/docx/src/read/props.rs` using whitespace-trimmed and ASCII-lowercased matching.
- Added comprehensive unit tests in `crates/doc/src/props.rs` and `crates/docx/src/read/props.rs` verifying case-insensitive and whitespace-tolerant parsing.

title: fix(rtf): support column break (\column) and escaped nonbreaking space in RTF import and export
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description

In RTF specifications (RTF Specification 1.9.1), `\column` denotes a column break, matching Wordcraft's `wordcraft_doc::para::COLUMN_BREAK` (`\u{000E}`), and `\ ` (backslash followed by space) denotes an escaped non-breaking space (equivalent to `\~`).

Previously:
1. When exporting text to RTF, `esc(s)` did not handle `\u{000E}`, causing it to be swallowed by `c if c.is_ascii_control() => {}` and completely omitted from the output.
2. When importing RTF, `r.word` did not recognize `"column"`, so `\column` control words were silently ignored rather than parsed as column break characters.
3. The control symbol parser did not handle `\ ` (backslash space), treating it as an unrecognized control symbol and dropping the space entirely.

### Fix
- Added `'\u{000E}' => o.push_str("\\column ")` in `esc`.
- Added `"column" => self.ch('\u{000E}')` in RTF reader's control word matching.
- Added `b' ' => { r.ch('\u{00A0}'); i += 2; }` in `parse_full` control symbol handling.
- Added automated unit tests verifying column break and escaped space export and import.

title: fix(latex): support soft/non-breaking hyphens and page/column breaks in LaTeX export and import
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description

When exporting text to LaTeX, special hyphenation and break characters were either emitted as raw Unicode characters unhandled by standard LaTeX engines or discarded:
1. `\u{00AD}` (soft/discretionary hyphen) was emitted directly as raw UTF-8 `\u{00AD}`, which causes compilation errors in standard LaTeX (`! Package inputenc Error: Unicode character \u00AD not set up for use with LaTeX`). In LaTeX, the discretionary hyphen command is `\-`.
2. `\u{2011}` (non-breaking hyphen) was also emitted directly, causing inputenc errors. In standard LaTeX without extra packages, it is represented as `\mbox{-}`.
3. `\u{000C}` (page break) and `\u{000E}` (column break) were classified as ASCII control characters and discarded by `c if c.is_control() => {}`.
4. In LaTeX text import, `\-` was matched in `text_symbol` as an ignorable command returning `""`, dropping the soft hyphen rather than preserving it as `\u{00AD}`.

### Fix
- In `escape_text`, mapped `\u{00AD}` to `\-`, `\u{2011}` to `\mbox{-}`, and `\u{000C}` / `\u{000E}` to `\newpage\n`.
- In `text_symbol`, mapped `"-"` to `"\u{00AD}"` and `"textnonbreakinghyphen"` to `"\u{2011}"`.
- Added automated unit tests verifying round-trip and escaping of soft hyphens, non-breaking hyphens, and breaks.

title: DOCX: a w:u without w:val draws no underline
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2362.

The DOCX reader turned a `w:u` with no `w:val` into a single underline. In the schema `w:val` on `CT_Underline` is optional with no default (unlike `w:color`, which defaults to `auto`), and Word leaves those runs plain, as the reference PDF in the issue shows. Now a missing `w:val` sets no underline, so the run inherits whatever its style says, and the colour is still read. The writer used to drop that colour when there was no underline, so a colour-only `w:u` now saves back as `<w:u w:color="…"/>` instead of being lost (before this change it was saved as a single underline). title: proof: Hungarian spelling, suggestions, grammar and hyphenation (#735)
author: Skaywalker
body:
Hungarian proofing, the last step of #735's affix work: spelling, suggestions, grammar and
hyphenation for text in Hungarian (`hu`, `hu-HU`). It builds on #1859 and #2070 (the affix engine
reading the Hungarian dictionary); the branch contains their commits, and the change here is the
last commit.

## What changes

**`crates/proof/src/hu`** (new), in the shape of the Polish and Turkish modules:
- **Spelling** against the Hungarian Hunspell dictionary installed on the system (Magyar Ispell,
  `hu_HU.aff`/`.dic`: OS package, Homebrew, LibreOffice or the Dictionaries folder; not bundled).
  Compounds (`almafa`, `házkulcsban`), the 6–3 rule and hyphenated forms (`SMS-ben`,
  `Petőfi-vers`) follow the dictionary through the affix engine. Numbers, short capitals and
  other scripts are accepted as in Polish, and the user dictionary applies.
- **Suggestions**, adapted from the Polish ones: missing accents first (`hazban` → `házban`),
  the dictionary's `REP` table (`hejesírás` → `helyesírás`), a missing space (`nemis` → `nem
  is`), one typo, then a stem scan when nothing nearer was found. Candidates are looked up
  without compounding first; compound checks are budgeted per call and rank a compound after a
  plain word. With the real dictionary a call takes 5–40 ms. `AffixDict::contains_simple` is new
  for this.
- **Grammar**, with Hungarian messages: repeated word, space before punctuation, double space,
  sentence capital (Hungarian abbreviations, ordinals and dates: `3. fejezet`, `2026. október`),
  a missing comma before `hogy`, `mert`, `hanem`, `de`, `ha` and the relative pronouns (not after

Fixes #1743.

## What was wrong
On Linux and BSD the canvas fakes touchpad momentum, and wheel notches ease in over a few frames. Ctrl/⌘+wheel events were skipped by `CanvasScroll::frame`, but they didn't stop a glide that was already running. So a coast or a queued notch kept scrolling the page on top of the zoom's "keep the point under the pointer" correction (#1223), and the page crept while you zoomed.

## Fix
- `crates/ui-egui/src/scroll.rs`: a hovered Ctrl/⌘+wheel event drops momentum and queued notches, and the frame scrolls nothing.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`: any applied zoom (Ctrl+wheel or pinch) cancels the glide first.

The #1223 anchor correction is unchanged.

## Tests
- `ctrl_wheel_zoom_does_not_scroll_the_document` (ui-egui lib): a touchpad coast, then Ctrl/⌘+wheel. The point under the pointer stays put within 1 px.
- `scroll::tests::zoom_modifier_wheel_clears_queued_notches`: the zoom frame returns zero and nothing keeps gliding.

Both fail with `scroll.rs` and `canvas.rs` reverted. They pass with the fix, and `cargo xtask ci` passes.

Docs: `docs/ui-parity.md` (zoom row) and `ROADMAP.md` progress log.

title: DOCX: positional tabs (w:ptab) keep their alignment, base and leader and go to the margins or indents, as in Word (#2367)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
DOCX: positional tabs (`w:ptab`) keep their alignment, base and leader, and are laid out where Word puts them

Word's positional tabs (Insert Alignment Tab; the ones its header and footer designs use) go to the left edge, centre or right edge of the margins or of the indents, whatever tab stops the paragraph has, and the text after them lines up there (ECMA-376 §17.3.3.23). When the text has already passed that place, the tab moves to the next line and goes there. This PR reads `w:ptab` into a new `InlineObject::PositionalTab`, writes it back with its three attributes, and lays it out as a left, centre or right stop at that place, with its leader. Plain-text export, copy and word counts see it as a tab. A `w:ptab` whose alignment or base the spec doesn't define stays a plain tab, as before.

Not checked against Word, happy to switch: on a line narrowed by a floating object the position still follows the spec (margins or indents, not the narrowed span); `relativeTo="indent"` uses the left indent on the first line too; right-to-left paragraphs get no special handling. Out of scope: RTF/ODT/HTML export of the tab (they see a plain tab or nothing), and a command to insert one.

Closes #2367

Validation:
- `positional_tabs_keep_their_alignment_base_and_leader` (three ptabs: right/margin/dot, center/indent/none, left/margin/underscore): fails on main (no objects, all three saved as `w:tab`), passes here
- `right_positional_tab_ends_text_on_the_right_margin`, `center_positional_tab_relative_to_indents_centres_between_them`, `positional_tab_behind_the_text_moves_to_the_next_line`: fail on main (the text lands right after the text before it), pass here
- `a_positional_tab_with_an_unknown_alignment_is_a_plain_tab`, `positional_tab_after_only_a_bookmark_stays_on_its_line`: regression guards, already green on main
- `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-doc -p wordcraft-docx -p wordcraft-layout --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Fonts: restore missing strokes in hint-reliant Chinese fonts
author: xyz9516
body:
Documents using Windows DFKai-SB (標楷體) render Chinese characters with missing or misplaced strokes. For example, `中文契約` becomes fragments while the same text in PMingLiU or Microsoft JhengHei is legible. This reproduces in v0.7.0, and the unconditional unhinted outline path is still present on main at `eae2421`.

`FontFace::glyph_outline` currently draws every font unhinted. Some legacy CJK fonts use TrueType instructions to assemble their contours, so these instructions are required for correct geometry rather than merely small-size rasterization.

This change uses skrifa's `require_interpreter()` detection and its recommended `Engine::Interpreter` / `Target::Mono` configuration. The interpreter is cached per face at units-per-em size, so output stays in the font units expected by the existing outline cache and zoom transforms. Fonts that do not require the interpreter keep the existing unhinted path. Document text, font selection and advance metrics are unchanged.

The opt-in regression uses an already installed, locally licensed `kaiu.ttf` to check that representative characters have complete horizontal/vertical bounds and remain cached. No proprietary font binaries, private documents or user screenshots are included. Progress/parity documentation records the measured scope without changing readiness estimates.

### Reproduce

1. On Windows with DFKai-SB installed, create a blank document and type `中文測試：本契約之締結而揭露相關技術、程式、資料與智慧財產權。`.
2. Set its East Asian font to DFKai-SB / 標楷體, 16 pt.
3. Compare with the same text in PMingLiU and Microsoft JhengHei. Before this patch, the Kai line has missing strokes; after it, the characters are complete. This was verified in both the application window and `ui.render` output using a synthetic DOCX and a locally rebuilt v0.7.0 application.

title: PDF export: lam-alef drawn as two glyphs at the same x extracts in reading order (#2310)
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #2310. Refs #1773.

## What

PDF export: right-to-left clusters drawn at the same x are now written in reverse text order, so the run's text ranges still decrease and krilla marks it `/ReversedChars`. Viewers then extract, search and copy the word in reading order.

Fonts hit this with lam-alef: the static Noto Naskh Arabic builds (2.004, 2.012) shape لا as a lam and a zero-advance alef, each with its own cluster, at the same x. `visual_order` sorted clusters by x with a stable sort, so the tie kept logical order (lam, alef). The run's ranges then weren't strictly decreasing, `/ReversedChars` was dropped, and السلام extracted as السالم. @Sriram-PR's repro in #2310 shows this in poppler, mupdf and PDFium.

## How

`visual_order` (`crates/pdf/src/lib.rs`) breaks an x tie between clusters by where their text starts: later text first in a right-to-left cluster, earlier text first otherwise. Clusters at different x, and glyphs inside one cluster, are ordered as before. No change to krilla; its `/ReversedChars` check is the same in the craft-libs copy.

## Checks

- New `clusters_at_the_same_x_go_in_reading_order` (synthetic glyphs, no installed fonts needed): a lam and a zero-width alef at one x come out alef first, and two left-to-right clusters at one x keep their order. Without the fix it fails with `[1, 2, 0]`.
- Windows, with only Noto Naskh Arabic 2.012 visible (system fonts hidden): before the fix, `wordcraft-cli convert` of the #2310 sample gave one `/ReversedChars` run and `right_to_left_text_extracts_in_logical_order` read back السالم. With the fix it gives three runs and reads back السلام. (That test still misses the Hebrew words in this setup, because no Hebrew font is visible.)
- Linux, Noto Naskh Arabic 2.004: the same test read back السالم before the fix and passes with it. This was checked on main before the craft-pdf switch.

title: #1534: more preset shapes and picture fills
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1534.

## What's new
**Eight more preset shapes** in Insert › Shapes: Hexagon, Octagon, Regular Pentagon, Decagon, Parallelogram, Trapezoid, Cross and Chevron. Each uses the DrawingML default proportions (ECMA-376 presetShapeDefinitions).

- In `crates/docx/src/read/props.rs`, `sectpr` now delegates `w:vAlign` to `PageVAlign::parse`, and performs whitespace-tolerant case-insensitive matches for `w:type`, `w:orient`, and `w:lnNumType` restart.

title: Layout: automatic space between Asian text and Latin text or digits (autoSpaceDE, autoSpaceDN) (#2358)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Chinese and Japanese text now gets Word's automatic space next to Latin letters and digits ("法院 94 年度"), following `w:autoSpaceDE` and `w:autoSpaceDN`.

Neither ECMA-376 nor Microsoft's docs give the amount, so I measured it on Word's PDF attached to the issue: in the unjustified heading at 16 pt the gaps are 4.05 to 4.15 pt, so a quarter of the font size. That also matches JIS X 4051's quarter em. The space follows the first of the two characters and works across runs. It takes the Asian character's size. A field result is classed by the text it shows. Word's PDF leaves CJK punctuation alone ("5、" and "、8"), so the space only comes between ideographs, kana or bopomofo on one side and a letter or ASCII digit on the other. It is not added next to Hangul, Latin punctuation or an existing space. At the end of a line it takes no room, so a justified line still ends flush. On a character grid the paragraph snaps to, it is skipped so the text keeps its cells. Both flags were already on by default when absent (as in the spec, and the issue's file has neither), so existing documents that mix CJK and Latin text will now lay out differently, as they do in Word. Left out: Word also widens these gaps when it justifies a line (4.87 pt on one justified line of the reference). `autoSpaceLikeWord95` is also left out, and so is `characterSpacingControl` punctuation compression, which is why line 2 of the issue's page still wraps one character early. Happy to switch the size source or the Hangul choice if you see it differently.

Closes #2358

title: PDF: pin craft-libs main, whose Krilla leaves out simple-text — no more rustybuzz or ttf-parser (#1365)
author: rabis7575
body:
## What

Moves the shared `storytold/craft-libs` pin (the `craft-pdf` dependency and the root Krilla patch) from `c3487320` to current craft-libs `main`, `8f5a2831`. That revision already turns Krilla's default features off in the shared workspace and keeps only `raster-images` ("make backend text shaping opt-in"), so Krilla's `simple-text` feature — the only path to the unmaintained `rustybuzz` 0.20.1 (RUSTSEC-2026-0206) and `ttf-parser` 0.25.1 (RUSTSEC-2026-0192) — is no longer built.

Closes #1365

## Why it is safe

`simple-text` only gates Krilla's `Surface::draw_text` and `text::TextDirection` (naive shaping with rustybuzz). WordCraft never calls them: it shapes text itself and hands Krilla positioned glyphs (`Font`, `GlyphId`, `KrillaGlyph`, `draw_glyphs`), which don't depend on the feature. JPEG and RGBA images still go through `raster-images`, which stays on.

Between the two revisions the vendored Krilla is unchanged and `craft-pdf`'s writer (`src/write.rs`) is unchanged; the new commits add the shared reader/rasteriser behind features WordCraft does not enable (`read`, `interpret`, `raster`) and touch `craft-print`, which WordCraft pins separately (`d27646a`, not changed here, like `craft-ui`). Rust 1.95 is still the minimum.

## Result

- `cargo tree -i rustybuzz --target all`, `-i ttf-parser`, `-i unicode-properties`: "did not match any packages".
- `cargo tree -e features -i krilla`: only `raster-images`, through `craft-pdf/write`.
- `Cargo.lock` loses 6 packages: `rustybuzz`, `ttf-parser`, `core_maths`, `unicode-bidi-mirroring`, `unicode-ccc`, `unicode-properties`.
- `docs/shared-pdf.md`: the new revision and the Krilla features.

title: fix(txt): support unicode line separators and preserve form-feed page breaks
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description

When importing plain text documents in `crates/formats/src/txt.rs`:
1. Unicode standard line and paragraph separators (`\u{0085}` NEL, `\u{2028}` Line Separator, `\u{2029}` Paragraph Separator) were previously not normalized to `\n` before the control character filter. Because `\u{0085}` is classified as a control character, it was stripped out entirely instead of breaking lines, while `\u{2028}` and `\u{2029}` were left as single inline characters without creating paragraphs.
2. Form-feed characters (`\u{000C}`) in plain text documents denote page breaks. While `\u{000C}` was allowed through the control filter, `Document::from_text(&clean)` does not set `page_break_before` on the following paragraph.

### Changes
- Normalized `\u{0085}`, `\u{2028}`, and `\u{2029}` to `\n` in `txt::import` alongside `\r\n` and `\r`.
- Normalized documents containing `\u{000C}` through the model representation (`model::to_doc(&model::from_doc(&doc))`) so that `page_break_before` is accurately set on paragraphs following page breaks.
- Added automated unit test `txt_unicode_newlines_and_page_break` in `crates/formats/src/tests.rs`.

title: fix(ui): borrow fallback fonts and preserve visual order for recent files (#2067)
author: harshpsi9194
body:
Fixes #2067

### Problem
1. **Missing Glyphs (Tofu/Squares):** In a fresh session with a blank document, recent file paths containing non-Latin scripts (Arabic, Hebrew, Urdu, etc.) were never scanned for system fallback fonts. As a result, faces like Arial/Segoe UI were not registered in `canvas.ime_faces`, rendering characters as boxes `□□□□□` or `?????`.
2. **Reversed Extensions & Digits:** Mixed RTL/LTR strings drawn directly to `ui.painter().text(...)` were rendered without base-direction BiDi reordering, reversing extensions (e.g. `xcod.6202` instead of `.docx`) and misplacing Arabic numbers.

### Solution
1. **Fallback Font Discovery:** Added `WordApp::ensure_recent_fonts()` to scan `self.ui.recent` on startup/change and register fallback faces into `canvas.ime_faces`. Cached via `recent_fonts_for` to avoid per-frame scanning.
2. **Visual Reordering:** Added `bidi_display()` in `canvas.rs` using `unicode_bidi` with an explicit LTR base direction (`unicode_bidi::Level::ltr()`) for visual display in Backstage, preserving standard file extensions and number ordering.
3. **Preserved Raw Paths:** Unmodified filesystem paths remain bound to `file.open` click actions.

### Testing & Quality Gates
- Added unit tests:
  - `bidi_display_preserves_extensions_and_numbers` (testing Latin, Arabic, and mixed filenames with years/extensions).
  - `recent_documents_borrow_fallback_faces`.
- All 553 `wordcraft-ui-egui` tests pass.
- Verified clean `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm).

title: fix(latex): support table column alignments, multicolumn alignment, and line alignment commands
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description

When importing LaTeX documents in `crates/formats/src/latex.rs`:
1. `tabular` column specifications (such as `l`, `c`, `r`, `J`, `X`, `S`, or repeated specs `*{n}{...}`) were parsed only for column count and column width (`spec_widths`), discarding the column alignments. Consequently, table cells were always imported with `align: None` rather than the intended column alignment (e.g. `c` -> `Align::Center`, `r` -> `Align::Right`).
2. `\multicolumn{n}{spec}{content}` parsed `n` but discarded `spec`, leaving multicolumn cells with whatever default alignment rather than the cell's overridden alignment (e.g., `\multicolumn{2}{|c|}{Header}` should center the cell paragraphs).
3. Classic TeX line alignment commands `\centerline{...}`, `\leftline{...}`, and `\rightline{...}` were unrecognized and dropped as generic commands rather than creating paragraphs with centered, left, or right alignment.
4. Several standard LaTeX symbols were missing from `text_symbol`: `\checkmark` (✓), `\circledR` (®), `\thickspace` ( ), `\textminus` (−), `\textcelsius` (℃), `\textperthousand` (‰), `\textpertenthousand` (‱), `\textrupee` (₹), and `\maltese` (✠).

### Changes
- Implemented `spec_cols` and `spec_cols_at` to extract column alignments alongside column widths, correctly propagating `Align::Left`, `Align::Center`, `Align::Right`, and `Align::Justify` through column specifications and `*{n}{...}` repeats.
- Added `parse_align_from_spec` to parse the column alignment specifier in `\multicolumn{n}{spec}{content}` and apply it to the cell's paragraphs.
- Handled `\centerline`, `\leftline`, and `\rightline` in `Parser::command`.
- Added standard symbol mappings in `text_symbol`.
- Added automated unit tests `table_column_and_multicolumn_alignments` and `centerline_and_symbols` in `crates/formats/src/latex.rs`.

title: fix(docx): support none merge types and normalize cell margins, valign, and alignment
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Description

When reading OpenXML table cell properties (`w:tcPr`) and table properties (`w:tblPr`) in `crates/docx/src/read/props.rs`:
1. In ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.85 (`w:vMerge`), the attribute `w:val` specifies the merge type: `"restart"`, `"none"`, or `"continue"` (default when omitted). Previously, `w:vMerge` only checked `if k.attr("w:val") == Some("restart") { VMerge::Restart } else { VMerge::Continue }`, which erroneously treated `w:val="none"` as `VMerge::Continue`, causing unmerged cells to be vertically merged into the row above.
2. In ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.19 (`w:hMerge`), `hcont` was set to `k.attr("w:val") != Some("restart")`, which similarly treated `w:val="none"` as a merge continuation.
3. In `margins`, margin elements (`w:top`, `w:left`, `w:bottom`, `w:right`, and modern `w:start`/`w:end`) were queried via `e.child(...)` with specific hardcoded prefixes rather than checking child elements by their local name (`k.local()`).
4. Cell vertical alignment (`w:vAlign`) and paragraph/table alignment (`align`) values were not trimmed or normalized for case insensitivity.

### Changes
- Updated `tcpr` to recognize `w:val="none"` for `w:vMerge` (yielding `VMerge::None`) and `w:hMerge` (yielding `hcont = false`), with case-insensitive value handling.
- Normalized `w:vAlign` values to lowercase and trimmed whitespace.
- Updated `margins` to match sub-elements by `k.local()` (`top`, `left`/`start`, `bottom`, `right`/`end`), matching the approach used by `borders`.
- Normalized `align` input strings with `trim()` and `to_ascii_lowercase()`.
- Added unit tests `tcpr_merges_and_alignments` and `margins_and_align_tolerance` in `crates/docx/src/read/props.rs`.

title: AltGr types ś, ł, ż… instead of opening KeyTips on Linux (#2388)
author: D13GOOOO
body:
Fixes #2388 (and the Linux side of #1748).

## What was wrong

On Linux under Wayland, AltGr + S on a Polish layout opened the ribbon KeyTips, and the letter went to the badges instead of typing ś. The same happened with ł, ż and other AltGr characters.

This is the event sequence (the issue's `wev` trace, as winit 0.30 and egui-winit 0.36 forward it):

1. `Key AltRight ↓`, then `ModifiersChanged` with no Alt. AltGr is `ISO_Level3_Shift` (Mod5), not Alt. winit sends a `ModifiersChanged` for every `wl_keyboard.modifiers` event, and egui-winit forwards each one.
2. `Key S ↓` + `Text("ś")`.

The KeyTips logic (`keytips::alt_transition`) read the `ModifiersChanged` in step 1 as "Alt let go with nothing pressed in between". So it opened KeyTips while AltGr was still held, and `S` went to the badges.

On Windows, AltGr is Ctrl+Alt, so the chord check already stopped it there.

## Change (`crates/ui-egui/src/keytips.rs`, `lib.rs`)

- **Key tracking:** a new `UiState::alt_key_down` records whether an Alt key is down, according to key events. While it is down, a `ModifiersChanged` without Alt doesn't end the press; the key-up does.
- **Modifier check:** a new `UiState::alt_modifier_seen` records whether the Alt modifier was on during the press. A release opens KeyTips only if it was. Left Alt always counts.
  - A bare AltGr tap doesn't open KeyTips, as on Windows.
  - Right Alt that is real Alt (US layout) still opens them.
- **Reset:** both flags are cleared when KeyTips are suppressed or the window loses focus, the same as `alt_pressed`.

Unchanged:
- every case in `native_alt_taps_toggle_once_in_either_event_order`: key and modifier events in either order, modifier-only backends, a tap within one frame;
- Alt chords, Alt+drag and Alt numpad codes;
- macOS (Option never opens KeyTips there).

## Tests

`keys::tests::altgr_types_its_characters_without_keytips` drives `keytips::logic` and `canvas_events` with the Wayland event sequence. It checks that:
- AltGr held through S…

title: fix(docx): support sym hex prefixes and normalize break types and note references
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
1. In DOCX reader (`crates/docx/src/read/story.rs`), `w:sym` parsing called `u32::from_str_radix(h.trim(), 16)` directly. If XML generators format `w:char` with prefixes like `0x`, `0X`, `U+`, `u+`, or `#x` (common in XML/HTML entity escaped attributes), `from_str_radix` returned `Err`, failing to decode the symbol character.
2. `w:br` type attribute parsing strictly matched `"page"` or `"column"`. In case-insensitive DOCX XML files where generators output `"Page"` or `"Column"`, they fell back to simple newline breaks (`\n`) rather than page breaks (`\u{000C}`) or column breaks (`\u{000E}`).
3. References to footnotes and endnotes used exact tag string matching rather than prefix-agnostic local name matching (`k.local()`).

### Solution
1. In `read_run`, clean `w:char` prefixes (`0x`, `0X`, `U+`, `u+`, `#x`, `#X`) before parsing hex into `u32`.
2. Normalize `w:type` on `w:br` by trimming and lowercasing to handle arbitrary casing.
3. Use `k.local()` for footnote and endnote reference tags.
4. Add unit test verifying hex prefix stripping and break casing normalization.

title: Layout: a paragraph running into a column of another width is broken for it
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2382.

With Word's Left and Right column presets the two columns have different widths, and a paragraph often runs from one into the next on its own, with no column break. `place_para_in_flow` broke the whole paragraph once, for the column it started in, so narrow lines went down the wide column (Left), or wide lines ran over the narrow column and into the margin (Right), and on later pages over the other column's text. #934 already rebreaks the text after a column break; this covers the case without one. The paragraph env gets a `width_from` map (from this text offset on, break for this width), lent to the paragraph only while it is laid out, the same way as `page_from` for #1352. When the rest of a paragraph lands in a column of another width, only the lines from that point on are broken again. The lines already placed stay as they were, so the rest still starts at the same line, and the paragraph's floats stay where they were anchored. The wrap (#1374) and PAGE-field (#1352) relays run with the map, and the column-break branch from #934 starts from an empty map, since it lays the paragraph out afresh for its new column. Equal columns never get relaid.

One limit, the same one #1374 and #934 have: widow/orphan control decides how many lines stay in the first column from the rest broken at that column's width, before it is broken again for the next one. Happy to look at that separately if you think it matters.

One more limit of the same kind: a display equation (and the footnote separator) in lines that ended up in a narrower column is still laid out for the first column's width. Rare, happy to cover it next.

title: fix(formats): support table cell vertical alignment in rtf, html, and odt
author: divyanshu2074
body:
### Problem
1. In `crates/formats/src/model.rs`, `Cell` lacked vertical alignment (`valign: Option<VAlign>`), leaving cell vertical alignment dropped when importing or converting between documents and formats.
2. In RTF reader/writer (`crates/formats/src/rtf.rs`), cell vertical alignment control words `\clvertalt` (top), `\clvertalc` (center), and `\clvertalb` (bottom) were completely ignored on import and never written on export.
3. In HTML reader/writer (`crates/formats/src/html.rs`), `valign` attributes and CSS `vertical-align` (`top`, `middle`/`center`, `bottom`) on `<td>`/`<th>` were ignored on import, and HTML export hardcoded `vertical-align:top` on every cell regardless of the cell's actual vertical alignment.
4. In ODT reader/writer (`crates/formats/src/odt.rs`), `style:vertical-align` on `style:table-cell-properties` was ignored on import and omitted on export.

### Solution
1. Add `valign: Option<VAlign>` to `model::Cell` and map it to/from `wordcraft_doc::CellProps.valign` in `from_doc` and `to_doc`.
2. In RTF, parse `\clvertalt`, `\clvertalc`, and `\clvertalb` in `CellDef` and output them during table cell export.
3. In HTML, parse `valign` attributes and `vertical-align` CSS property for table cells on import, and output appropriate `vertical-align` CSS on export.
4. In ODT, parse `style:vertical-align` in `style:table-cell-properties` and generate cell styles with `style:vertical-align` on export.
5. Add automated unit tests in `rtf.rs`, `html.rs`, and `odt.rs` verifying table cell vertical alignment round-tripping.

title: Refresh DATE/TIME fields when opening .doc/.dot by extension
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/io.rs:183-187 (read_bytes, the "doc" | "dot" arm returns before opened() is called)` (no existing issue): Opening a .doc/.dot by extension skips the open-time refresh of DATE/TIME fields, but the same bytes opened as .docx get it.

## Cause
The "doc" | "dot" arm of `read_bytes` called only `doc.ensure_nonempty()` and returned early, so `opened()` never ran and the stale cached results of unlocked DATE/TIME fields were kept. The same bytes under a `.docx` name go through `open_by_content`, which does call `opened()`.

## Fix
The "doc" | "dot" arm now calls `opened(&mut doc)`, as every other open path does. This makes sure the document isn't empty and refreshes unlocked DATE/TIME fields. The regression test builds a minimal Word 97-2003 file with a stale DATE field and checks that `.doc` and `.dot` give the same result as `.docx`.

## Verified
- Regression test `binary_doc_opened_by_extension_refreshes_date_fields`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --test date_fields binary_doc_opened_by_extension_refreshes_date_fields`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::deleted_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_without_markup`, `tests::hidden_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_when_not_shown`, `tests::tight_wrap_follows_an_ellipse`, `tests_pages::widow_control_moves_a_three_line_paragraph_whole`, which also fail on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
The other open paths, including the encrypted-package and open-by-content paths, already call `opened()` and are unchanged. The refresh logic itself is unchanged.

title: Layout: text overflowing into an unequal column takes its width (#2382)
author: PanSHIgg
body:
Fixes #2382.

Word 2024's **Left** and **Right** preset column layouts — in the issue's files a narrow 118 pt column beside a wide 272 pt one — overflowed in WordCraft: a paragraph that fills the narrow column and continues into the wide one kept the narrow width for its remaining lines. On **Left** the wide column's text ran a word or two wide (4 pages against Word's 3); on **Right** 21 lines ran past the right margin, by up to 91 pt.

**Cause** — `place_para_in_flow` breaks a paragraph's rest again for the column it lands in only after a *column break* (#934). A natural overflow into a column of another width kept the lines as broken, drawn at the new column's x.

**Change** — an overflow that lands the rest of a paragraph in a column of another width now re-lays that rest for it (new `resume_relaid` and `MAX_WIDTH_RELAYS`, run before the wrap-area relay). Unlike a break, the new width can cut the resume line mid-way: the line's tail from the resume point then opens the new column (`xs` rebased to the continuation indent, leaders kept from the cut). Bidirectional lines are left as they were — the tail cut does not reorder `vis`, and those are rare in unequal columns.

**Evidence** — this machine, `wordcraft-cli convert` on the files attached to the issue, text positions read from the exported PDFs (no Word needed for the before/after numbers; the Word columns are the issue's reference PDFs):

| file | pages before → after (Word) | farthest text right edge before → after (Word) | lines past the margin before → after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Left.Column.layout.docx | 4 → **3** (3) | 510.0 → 510.0 (509.9) | 0 → 0 |
| Right.Column.layout.docx | 3 → 3 (3) | **601.5 → 509.4** (509.3) | **21 → 0** |

The wide column's continuation lines now end at ~450–509 pt (Word 473–509), and the Left file lays out in Word's page count.

title: Paste: plain text keeps the formatting of the paragraph it lands in
author: seif9116
body:
Closes #2423.

## What was wrong

Paste (Ctrl+V, Home › Paste) of plain text from another program gave every line after the first
a paragraph with default formatting. `paste_fragment` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/paste.rs`) turned
the text into a fragment with `Fragment::from_text`, whose paragraphs carry no formatting.
`Document::insert_fragment` keeps the target's paragraph formatting only in the first pasted
paragraph. The middle lines went in as they were, and the last line took the place of the
paragraph after the caret, so the text after the caret lost its formatting too.

So pasting several lines into a right-to-left paragraph turned all of them but the first
left-to-right, and lost the paragraph's style, alignment, indents and spacing. In a list, the
lines after the first were no longer list items. Keep Text Only already pasted the same text
correctly.

## What changed

- `paste::paste_content` says what a Paste brings in: a fragment (WordCraft's own copy, or
  another program's HTML or RTF) or plain text. It picks between them as `paste_fragment` did.
- Paste inserts plain text the way Keep Text Only does (`paste::insert_text`, through
  `cmd::paste_text`). Each line after the first splits the paragraph as Enter does, so it takes
  that paragraph's direction, style, alignment, indents, spacing and list, and the text after the
  caret keeps them. Empty lines become empty paragraphs with the same formatting. The text takes
  the character formatting just before the caret. This is what Word does with text that carries
  no formatting, as Microsoft describes Keep Text Only
  ([Control the formatting when you paste text](https://support.microsoft.com/office/20156a41-520e-48a6-8680-fb9ce15bf3d6)).
- A paste is still one undo step.
- Paste of WordCraft's own copy and of HTML and RTF is unchanged, so it keeps the formatting it
  carries. Merge Formatting, Paste Special and Keep Text Only are unchanged. `paste_fragment`
  stays, for Merge Formatting.

body:

The Navigation pane's Headings tab was a flat, read-only list of every heading. It is now the
document's outline, the shape an online editor (Tencent Docs, WPS) gives it:

* headings indent under their parent, and a triangle folds a section shut;

* the right-click menu acts on the whole section — Promote, Demote, Delete, Do Not Show in TOC,

title: Diagram: edit a draw.io diagram where it sits, in a window over the page
author: renlixing87
body:
## What this does

Double-clicking a picture whose PNG carries a draw.io diagram in its `tEXt`/`zTXt` chunk (which is
what draw.io writes when a diagram is exported with a copy of it in the file) opens draw.io in a
child window over the document area. What draw.io exports comes back as the picture, in place of
the one that was edited, as one undo step; Exit without a change leaves the document alone.

The draw.io web app is served from the app itself. `packaging/fetch-drawio.sh` fetches it into

It needs a native window, so the feature is there on macOS and Windows and absent in the browser
build, where `diagram::unsupported()` says so and a page cannot host a second browsing context in

and `ui.editDiagram` commands, `crates/ui-egui/src/diagram/` (the editor), and the `editor_page`

title: DOCX: keep Word's Table of Contents content control around a TOC the writer doesn't rebuild
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2427.

Since #392 the reader drops every Table of Contents content control on open, on the understanding that the writer puts it back around the TOC (`TOC_SDT_OPEN` / `toc_span`). Since #617, though, a TOC is only folded into the heading-and-entries form when it matches it exactly; any other TOC (no `TOCHeading`, unstyled entries, the field ending in a paragraph of its own, as in the repro) keeps its explicit field range, `toc_span` doesn't see it, and the `w:sdt` is gone after a save. Now the reader keeps the control as an ordinary block control, and hands it to the TOC only when, with the markers taken out, the writer's own `toc_span` would wrap exactly the same paragraphs. So Word-shaped TOCs behave as before (one control, Update Table still works), and every other TOC keeps its `w:sdt` with its `w:id` and `w:sdtEndPr` as read. Thanks @vangel76 for the content control work this builds on.

One thing left as it was: when the TOC goes back to the writer's rebuilt control, its `w:id` and `w:sdtEndPr` are still the writer's (none), as before this change. Happy to carry them over too if you'd like.

Validation:

title: #1843: Read Aloud speaks Russian text with a Russian voice
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1843.

## What was wrong
On Windows, Read Aloud always used the default voice (usually English) and handed it the sentence through a text channel that doesn't decode UTF-8. Russian came out as single letters ("Е А В В").

## What changes
- **Windows:** the sentence is read from standard input as raw bytes and decoded as UTF-8, so every character arrives intact. When the sentence's language differs from the default voice's, an installed voice for that language is chosen; with none installed it falls back to the default voice. The text is never part of the script, so it can't run as code.
- **Language of a sentence:** the run's language tag, unless its script disagrees with the letters (Word writes en-US on almost every run, even for Cyrillic text). Mixed text goes to the non-Latin script when it has at least a fifth of the letters.
- **macOS and Linux:** the same language choice (`say -v`, `espeak-ng -v`).
- **Nothing changes for text the default voice already reads:** English text under en-US keeps the user's own voice on all three systems (no novelty voices on macOS). On Linux a voice `espeak` doesn't know no longer means silence; it retries with the default voice.

## Tests
Speech tests cover the language and script detection, the Windows script (UTF-8 input, voice choice, no text in the script, still no console window), the macOS and Linux arguments, the en-US-keeps-the-default rule, and the retry decision. The regression tests were shown to fail before the fixes. `cargo xtask ci` passes all 6 steps, and the Windows target passes clippy.

## Needs a manual check
I can't run Windows here, so the PowerShell was checked by reading and unit tests only. On Windows 11 with a Russian voice installed: type "Привет как твои дела?", start Read Aloud, and expect Russian speech. The macOS code is covered by GitHub's macOS build and unit tests, not run on a Mac.

## Follow-ups

title: DOCX: strict line heights with a unit are points under auto (#2329)
author: PanSHIgg
body:
Fixes #2329.

Word 2024 saves **Strict Open XML** documents (`w:conformance="strict"`, the `purl.oclc.org` namespaces) that write measures out with their unit: the attached file's paragraph defaults are `w:spacing w:after="8pt" w:line="13.90pt" w:lineRule="auto"`. The reader fed `13.90` straight into the `auto` branch (240ths of a line, 240 = single), so 13.90pt became a 13.9 **multiple** — a 13.9× line height, 191.8 pt lines, and the file laid out as 10 pages here against Word's 1.

**Cause** — `crates/docx/src/read/props.rs` `w:spacing`: `measure(line, 240.0)` returns a universal measure in points (13.9), and the `auto` arm used it as a multiple of single spacing.

**Change** — `units::line_multiple`: under `auto`, a bare number still counts 240ths of a line (240 = single, the transitional form); a measure with a unit (ISO 29500 strict `ST_SignedTwipsMeasure`: `13.90pt` = 278 twips) reads through twips, exactly as Word renders it (the strict `wml.xsd` types `w:line` as `ST_SignedTwipsMeasure`; there is no percent form). `exact`/`atLeast` already read units as points.

**Evidence** — `wordcraft-cli convert` on the issue's file, text positions read from the exported PDFs, with Word's own PDF as the reference:

| | pages | body line advance | paragraph advance (8 pt after) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Word's PDF (reference) | 1 | 16.10 / 15.96 | 24.00 |
| main | 10 | 191.80 | — |
| this PR | 1 | 15.98 | 23.99 |

Baselines line up with Word's to ≤0.3 pt across the page (e.g. `764.16` vs `764.28`, `748.18` vs `748.18`, `685.16` vs `685.18`) and table-cell lines match too (12.65 against 12.60/12.72). A save-and-reopen of the fixed file keeps the spacing.

title: DOCX: opening no longer copies the document's pictures
author: arcanii
body:
## What it does

Opening a DOCX copied every picture out of the unzipped package into the document. Each embedded-object part and macro part kept for saving was copied the same way. So a document with pictures held them twice while it opened, and the package's copies were left behind as freed memory.

Now the document shares the package's bytes. Nothing changes in what is read or saved.

## How

- **Shared parts:** `Package` holds its parts as `Arc<Vec<u8>>`, the type the document already keeps `media` and `passthrough` parts in. `Package::get_shared` hands a part over, and `get` is unchanged for everything else.
- **Callers:**
  - `Reader::media_for` takes pictures with `get_shared` instead of `Arc::new(bytes.to_vec())`;
  - the VBA project, VBA-related parts and embedded-object parts do the same;
  - `keep_unmodelled` searches the main document part in place instead of copying it first.
- **`from_parts`** keeps its signature (Flat OPC, Word 2003 XML).

**How it was measured:**
- macOS 27.0.1 on an Apple M3 Max, release builds of `main` (`eae2421`) and of this branch.
- A synthetic 92 MB document with 20 PNG pictures (2400×1800), 89 pages, and a text-only 74-page one.
- Physical footprint (Activity Monitor's "Memory") from `proc_pid_rusage`, and `vmmap --summary` / `footprint` once the document is open in the desktop app. The app ran in its own profile (`WORDCRAFT_PROFILE_DIR`), driven over the control channel. Two runs each.

| Opening the picture document | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop app, once open | 862–866 MB | 772 MB |
| Of which freed large blocks still counted | 206 MB | 118 MB |
| Desktop app, peak | 915–932 MB | 821–823 MB |
| `wordcraft-cli info`, peak | 319 MB | 231 MB |

The text-only document is unchanged (182 → 179 MB once open).

title: fix(ui): AutoSave writes off the UI thread, so typing never waits for the disk
author: christestet
body:
AutoSave previously serialized and wrote the document on the UI thread, freezing typing during each disk write. The UI now stamps and copies the document, and a worker serializes and writes that snapshot.

- Split engine saves into `prepare_save` and `write_prepared`; explicit engine saves retain their existing behavior.
- Keep one AutoSave in flight. Rejected submissions return their snapshots, clear the dead worker, and write inline. Failed inline writes restore unsaved state.
- Wait for pending AutoSave before Save/Save As, rename, or document replacement, so an older write cannot overwrite a newer save.
- Apply AutoSave failures before deciding whether closing needs a save prompt. A five-second timeout keeps the worker busy and defers the operation.
- Report worker disconnection during a pending save as a failure.
- Remove the temporary `autosave_probe` example.
- Merge upstream main at `e05b7fe8`, preserving its comment-draft handling and document-close behavior.

- Headless rendered UI: typed through egui input, waited for natural AutoSave, used Ctrl+S, saved a copy, autosaved that copy, reopened it, cancelled the close prompt, saved, closed the document, and reopened it again. Verified actual DOCX contents and dirty/dialog states.

title: perf(layout): cache the keep-with-next lookahead shape through the paragraph cache
author: christestet
body:
## The bug

Typing into a large document with headings lagged badly — ~100 ms per keystroke on a
281-page/157k-word document with 100 headings, growing with the number of headings and the
length of the paragraph after each.

The cause is in `next_first_line` (crates/layout/src/lib.rs): for every keep-with-next block
(Word's built-in Heading 1 has keep-with-next, so every real document with headings qualifies)
it laid the paragraph *after* the block out with a fresh `para::layout_para`, bypassing
`LayoutCache.paras`. That shape is recomputed on every pass, is invisible to the hit/miss
counters, and scales with the number of keep-with-next blocks × the length of the paragraphs
after them — effectively O(document) re-shaping per keystroke.

## The fix

The lookahead now goes through the paragraph cache, using the same key the paragraph gets when
it is placed:

- label-less (a lookahead doesn't take its list label, as before),
- with proofing participating as usual, so a cache entry first created by a lookahead still
  carries the proofing marks,
- **without advancing the equation counter** — a lookahead doesn't count (`para_key` grows an
  `advance_eq` flag for this; its two existing callers are unchanged).

The shape computed for the lookahead is therefore reused by the placement and by every later
pass; repeated lookaheads are pure cache hits.

## Measurement (release builds, layout after one keystroke, warm cache; new `cache_probe` example)

| Document | pages | headings | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| long paragraphs + 100 headings + tables | 281 | 100 | 96.4 ms | **3.4 ms** (28×) |
| short paragraphs + headings + tables | 342 | 60 | 14.0 ms | 11.1 ms |
| long paragraphs + 6 headings | 280 | 6 | 6.2 ms | 3.7 ms |
| short paragraphs | 42 | 7 | 1.0 ms | 0.6 ms |

Cache counters confirm the mechanism: 1 miss / 415 hits before, 1 miss / 464 hits after on the
281-page document (the additional hits are the reused lookahead shapes). The edit itself was
measured…

title: Copy: a selection across table cells stays a table (#2398)
author: saad-mughal435
body:
Towards #2398.

### What happens

`Document::copy_blocks` has two paths. When both ends of the selection share a
parent it handles tables, cloning a `Block::Table` whole. When they do not, it
falls through to:

```rust
for p in self.paths_between(&a, &b) {
    if let Some(para) = self.para(a.story, &p) { ... out.push(Block::Para(q)); }
}
```

which collects paragraphs and nothing else. Selecting across the cells of a row
puts the two ends in different cells, so their paths have different parents and
the row is flattened into loose paragraphs.

That single defect produces both halves of the report:

- `text_of` already writes a table's cells separated by `\t`, but only for an
  actual `Block::Table`. Loose paragraphs are joined by `\n`, which is the
  reported "all cells on separate lines".
- `export_fragment` likewise writes a table as a table, so the HTML flavour lost
  its `<table>` for the same reason.

### The change

`table_slice` copies the rectangle of cells between the two ends and cuts the
grid to match, returning a `Block::Table`. Word selects whole cells once a
selection leaves one, and this follows that. Both clipboard flavours then come
out right without touching the serialisers.

A selection inside a single cell returns `None` and keeps the existing
paragraph path, so ordinary copying is unchanged.

### Tests

- `copying_across_a_table_row_keeps_its_cells_tab_separated` (doc): the copy is
  still a table and its clipboard text is `Col 1\tCol 2\tCol 3`.
- `copying_a_table_row_offers_tsv_text_and_an_html_table` (engine): through
  `edit.copy`, the result's `text` is TSV and its `html` holds one `<table>`
  with three `<td>`.

I checked the first test fails before the change, on the assertion that the copy
is still a table, so it catches the defect rather than passing alongside it.

### What this does not cover

The report also notes that `wl-paste --list-types` shows no `text/html` at all on
Wayland. I traced that path: `set_clipboard_html` is wired in t…

title: DOCX: HYPERLINK fields read as links, so Word for the web TOCs keep their tabs and page fields (#2174)
author: Nghiathan13
body:
Fixes #2174.

**The bug.** Word for the web writes each table of contents entry as a `HYPERLINK` complex field. The field holds the heading's text, a tab and a `PAGEREF` field:

```xml
<w:fldChar begin/> HYPERLINK  \l  "_Toc1675065987" <w:fldChar separate/>
  Intro <w:tab/> <w:fldChar begin/> PAGEREF _Toc1675065987 \h <w:fldChar separate/> 1 <w:fldChar end/>
<w:fldChar end/>
```

The DOCX reader buffered the whole field into one field object with a flat text result, `"Intro\t1"`. That caused three problems:
- The tab was drawn as a box instead of reaching the dotted right tab stop, which is what the issue's screenshot shows.
- The page number was no longer a field of its own.
- The link could not be followed, because nothing treats a `HYPERLINK` field object as a link.

The .doc reader (`docbin`) and the RTF reader already read `HYPERLINK` fields as linked text. Only the DOCX reader did not.

**Proof.** I rendered the issue's `toc_test.docx` with `wordcraft-cli` on main (eae2421) and got the same picture as the reporter's 0.7.0 screenshot. As a control, I rewrote only the six `HYPERLINK` fields in `document.xml` as `<w:hyperlink w:anchor="…">` around the same runs. With that change, WordCraft draws the TOC as Word does: dot leaders, and page numbers at the right margin.

**The fix.** `crates/docx/src/read/story.rs`: a `HYPERLINK` field, complex or simple, now reads the way a `w:hyperlink` does. Its result stays ordinary content carrying the link, and nested fields such as `PAGEREF` are kept.
- The target is `url`, `url#bookmark` (`\l`) or `#bookmark`, matching how `w:hyperlink` is read.
- On save the link is written back as `w:hyperlink`. The tooltip (`\o`) and target frame (`\t`) are dropped, since the model has nowhere to keep them; the `w:hyperlink` reader drops `w:tooltip` too.
- A `HYPERLINK` field with no target stays a field.
- Only a code whose first word is `HYPERLINK` is split into words. Field codes can be up to 2 MB.

title: #2456: wait for the next edit after an over-limit recovery snapshot
author: C00kieMonsta
body:
Part of #2456.

Before: a recovery snapshot over the 256 MiB cap, or over what was left of the folder's 2 GiB budget, failed at the limit, deleted its temporary file and was tried again at the next tick. A document that can't fit wrote about 256 MB every 10 to 12 seconds for as long as it had unsaved changes, even after typing stopped.

After: the worker reports a size-limit failure as a typed error (`Failure::TooLarge`), and `Recovery::poll` keeps the attempted revision. A snapshot over the cap is tried again only after the next edit, at the usual interval, so a document that can't fit costs at most one attempt per change. A full folder depends on other copies, so it is also tried again when another copy is discarded or the list is refreshed. After a size failure the store measures the next snapshot in memory before it creates or locks the record, so a document that stays too large touches no file after its first failed attempt. File › Recover says the document is too large for a recovery copy, or that the recovery folder is full, in all 22 interface languages. The message stays until the next attempt, a save or another document, so Refresh does not clear it. The log gets one `warn` per document with the size and the limit, and no document content. Other failures, such as I/O errors or a locked record, are still retried at the next interval.

This PR leaves out the storage format change the issue proposes (parts as files, a v2 snapshot), so a document over the limit still gets no recovery copy. That design is to be agreed with the maintainers and the authors of #2101 and #2102, as the issue asks. This change also touches the retry path that open PR #2102 changes (`Event`, `Recovery::poll`, `tick`, the worker's job match and the limits paragraph of `docs/recovery.md`), so whichever lands second needs a small rebase. The new catalog rows go at the end of each file, away from #2102's catalog hunk.

title: #2449: drag selected text to move it, Ctrl or Option to copy
author: C00kieMonsta
body:
Fixes #2449.

In Word you can press on selected text, drag it and drop it somewhere else in the document. A dotted caret shows where it will land. Holding Ctrl (Option on a Mac) copies the text instead of moving it, and Esc cancels the drag. Until now WordCraft treated a press on the selection as a new click: the selection collapsed and a new drag-select started, so text could not be moved with the mouse.

Now a press on the selection holds it. Dragging shows a dashed drop caret, drawn in the caret's colour for that spot so it reads on light and dark pages, and scrolls the view near its edges. Releasing moves the text through the new `edit.moveText` command (one undo step, the moved text stays selected), or copies it with Ctrl or Option held. A drop back on the selection, or a click on it without dragging, puts the caret there. Esc, or a release over the ruler, the ribbon or outside the window, leaves the text in place. A selection running from text into a table, or out of one, is not picked up, because it takes whole rows and moving it would empty their cells; a whole table between two ends in body text moves intact. With Track Changes on, a moved sentence or paragraph is a tracked move and a word is a deletion plus an insertion, the same as cut and paste. Repeat (F4) does not replay a drop. File › Options › Advanced › "Allow text to be dragged and dropped" turns the mouse gesture off.

- `crates/engine/src/cmd/drag_drop.rs`: new `edit.moveText` command (`{"to": Pos}` or `{"page","x","y"}`, `copy`). It refuses an empty selection, whole cells, a column, a selection whose ends are in different containers, a drop inside the selection, into a text box or note the text carries, or into a comment from outside it; locked content controls and protected documents refuse it through the usual checks. It shifts the drop point when the text before it leaves. Tests.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs`: registers the module.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/moves.rs`: `take_tracked` splits …

title: #2458: turn a rotated text box's text with the box
author: C00kieMonsta
body:
Fixes #2458.

In Word, a rotated text box turns its text with it. The text is laid out in the unturned frame and the whole frame turns about its centre. Flips never mirror the text: a horizontal flip leaves it as it is and a vertical flip turns it upside down. Format Shape's Do not rotate text (`wps:bodyPr upright="1"`) keeps it level. Before this change WordCraft turned the box's outline but drew its text upright, and clicks, the caret and the selection ignored the turn.

Now a rotated or flipped text box draws its text turned with the box, on screen, in page renders and in PDF, for boxes in groups, headers and footers, and for warped boxes. In PDF the text stays real, tagged paragraph text. Do not rotate text is read, written and honoured. A click lands on the turned word and the caret leans with the text. Up and Down follow the turned lines. Column selection, links, equations, content control frames and change bars follow the turn. The selection, including selected table cells, is shaded turned. An unturned box draws exactly as before.

title: DOCX: two lines in one and horizontal in vertical (`w:eastAsianLayout`) survive a save
author: imachus
body:
Opening a .docx that uses two lines in one (warichu) or horizontal in vertical (tate-chu-yoko) and saving it again dropped the `w:eastAsianLayout` run property, so the saved file had lost those settings for Word too. This reads the element into a new `CharProps::east_asian_layout` (`EastAsianLayout`: `id`, `combine`, `combine_brackets`, `vert`, `vert_compress`, each `None` when the file doesn't say; `CombineBrackets` for `ST_CombineBrackets`) and writes it back after `w:lang`, in `CT_RPr`'s order. It goes through `rpr`/`rpr_inner` like the other run properties, so it is kept in runs and in styles, and it overlays and `minus`es like them. Values the schema doesn't allow (an id outside `xsd:int`, an unknown bracket, an on/off that isn't one) are left unset rather than guessed, and an element with nothing valid writes nothing. On/off attributes are written as `1`/`0`.

Layout doesn't change: the text still shows as ordinary text. Laying out horizontal in vertical in vertical sections, and then two lines in one, would be follow-ups; this keeps the files intact first. Source: ISO/IEC 29500-1 §17.3.2.10 (`CT_EastAsianLayout`, `ST_CombineBrackets`); no Word observation.

Docs: `file-format-parity.md` splits the row (`w:eastAsianLayout` ✅/✅, `w:fitText` stays ❌), the East Asian typography row in `target-app-parity.md` (no percentage change), and the ROADMAP progress log.
