title: Layout: In Front of Text objects draw over the whole page's text (#1993)
author: Nghiathan13
body:
Part of #1993: the text drawn over the picture. The anchor indicator is the issue's other request and is not changed here.

## What was wrong
On `main` (eae2421), insert a picture into the sample document, set Wrap Text › In Front of Text, and move it over the text (`arrange.position {"preset":"topCenter"}`).
- **In Front of Text:** the picture covered its own paragraph (the title) only. Every paragraph after it showed through: the subtitle and the first body paragraph were drawn on top of the picture.
- **Behind Text,** for comparison: correctly under all the text.

**Root cause:** `place_objects` returned In Front of Text objects in the same `front` layer as inline and square-wrapped ones. All three callers appended that layer right after the anchor paragraph's lines (`items.extend(front)`). Paragraphs laid out later on the page were drawn after it. Behind Text objects were already inserted at the front of the page, so they stayed under everything.

## What changed (`crates/layout/src/lib.rs`)
`place_objects` returns a third layer, `top`, for In Front of Text: the object's drawing, its `Placed::Object` frame for hit testing, and its text box's text.

**Body pages.** `PageBuilder.on_top` holds the layer per page, beside `behind`.
- When the page is left (`new_page`, and at the end of layout), `lift_on_top` appends it to the page's items. This runs after `apply_valign` and before the footnotes.
- Vertical alignment moves the layer too:
  - centre and bottom by the same offset as the body;
  - justified by the gap of the object's own block. Each entry records where its paragraph's items start, counted like `block_marks`.
- `Snap` saves the last page's layer and restores it, like `behind`. A page that was left and then taken back has the lifted items truncated with the rest.
- `take_back_break_page` doesn't treat a page holding only such an object as empty.

**Boxes** (table cells, headers, footers, text boxes; `layout_box`): the layer goes after the box's other items…

title: Text boxes: Wrap text in shape off, and a box that fits such text takes its size (part of #2191)
author: Nghiathan13
body:
Part of #2191: the figure caption box (points 3 and 6 of the issue). The line and arc shapes, the gradient fill, the SmartArt arrow and the font fallback are left as they are.

**The bug.** On page 1 of `vaccines_history_chapter`, the "(Figure 1.1) A time line of …" caption is a floating, square-wrapped text box. It sets two things in `wps:bodyPr`:
- `wrap="none"`: Wrap text in shape is off.
- `a:spAutoFit`: Resize shape to fit text is on.

The size stored in the file is an old 144 × 144 pt square. Word lays the caption out on one line and sizes the box to that line (about 363 × 17 pt in its PDF). So the text beside the box starts at the margin.

WordCraft ignored `wrap="none"` and never sized a box to its text. The caption wrapped into three lines inside the 144 pt square. That square pushed "The Beginning" and the first four body lines to the right, and moved the page breaks that follow. The issue reads this as a `wrapNone` box being treated as an obstacle. In fact the box is `wrapSquare`, so wrapping around it is right; its size is what's wrong.

**Proof** (WordCraft main eae2421 against Word's `reference.pdf`):

| x of "The Beginning:" | |
|---|---|
| Word | 93.5 |
| main | 230.4 |
| main, with only the box's `wp:extent` and `a:ext` changed in the XML to Word's 363 × 17.5 pt | 93.7, with the same line breaks as Word |

Changing `wrap="none"` to `wrap="square"` gave the same PDF on main, so the attribute was ignored.

**The fix.**
- **Model and DOCX:** `TextBody::no_wrap` is read from `wps:bodyPr wrap="none"` and written back.
- **Layout (`crates/layout/src/textbox.rs`):**
  - A box whose text doesn't wrap keeps each paragraph on one line, past the box's side if need be.
  - A floating box that also resizes to fit its text takes the size of its widest line and the depth of its text, inside its margins (`fitted_size`). This size is used where the body, headers, footers, cells and boxes place their floats. Drawing, hit testing and handles take the rectangle from th…

title: M12: Markdown source view (view.markdownSource)
author: alehel
body:
A .md document switches between the formatted view and its file's own text (View › Views › Markdown Source, or the status-bar button), one paragraph per line in a monospaced face.

- Source view shows the text the file was opened with while the document is unchanged; after formatted edits it shows the document written as Markdown.
- Typing is literal: no AutoFormat or AutoCorrect; Paste keeps text only.
- Saving as .md/.txt writes the text byte for byte; other formats save the document the text describes; native JSON keeps the view.
- The flag lives on the document, so Undo steps across the switch, and switching alone leaves no unsaved changes.
- Formatting, styles, tables and objects are unavailable there (Session::unavailable, used by the ribbon and control channel); grammar marks are off, spelling stays.

title: Fonts: Times New Roman and Book Antiqua keep their own substitutes, not Cambria (part of #2191)
author: Nghiathan13
body:
Part of #2191 (the "Times New Roman falls back to Caladea" item; the text-box items are in #2496).

## Problem
Word's font tables class Times New Roman, Book Antiqua, Courier New, Symbol… as *roman*. Since #1613, `lookup_family` draws any missing roman font in Cambria, so on Linux (no Times New Roman installed) these documents were set in Caladea instead of Liberation Serif, which moved line breaks.

## Fix
- `wordcraft_fonts::word::has_own_substitutes(family)`: true when the font (or the font its charset name stands for, e.g. `Times New Roman Cyr`) has a substitute list of its own rather than the generic one.
- `layout::para::lookup_family` only applies the Cambria fallback to roman fonts **without** their own substitutes, i.e. fonts we don't know. Word has the fonts we do know, so it never draws them in Cambria.

## Tests
- `fonts_known_by_name_have_their_own_substitutes` (fonts): known fonts vs unknown names.
- `a_roman_font_with_its_own_substitutes_keeps_them` (layout): Times New Roman and Book Antiqua marked roman resolve to their own substitute face.
- `a_missing_roman_font_is_drawn_as_word_draws_it` still passes: unknown roman fonts still go to Cambria.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, tests, assets and layers pass; `cargo xtask wasm` passes (16/16 crates).

title: #2233, #2234: inline pictures drag to a dashed insertion cursor and stay inline
author: Nghiathan13
body:
Fixes #2233. Fixes #2234.

Dragging a picture whose layout is In Line with Text dropped it as a floating picture with Square wrapping (#2234). While you dragged, only the see-through copy showed, so you couldn't tell where it would land (#2233). In Word an inline picture moves within the text: a dashed insertion cursor follows the pointer, and the picture lands there, still inline.

The two issues are fixed together because an insertion cursor would be misleading if the drop then floated the picture somewhere else.

## What changes

- **While dragging** an In Line with Text picture, shape or text box, a dashed insertion cursor follows the pointer through the text of the object's own story. Its colour has the same contrast with the paper as the normal caret. Inline drags don't snap to alignment guides any more, because they don't place the object by coordinates.
- **On drop**, the object moves to that text position and stays In Line with Text. It keeps its character formatting, stays selected, and the move is one undo step. Ctrl/⌘+drag drops a copy there. Dropping it back on itself does nothing and adds no undo step.
- **Floating objects** drag exactly as before.
- **Engine:** `arrange.bounds` and `arrange.copyTo` take `{"to": Pos}` for inline objects, so scripts, the CLI and MCP can do the same move. `x`/`y` keep their old meaning, so existing scripts don't change. title: Word's Spike: Ctrl+F3 collects cuts, Ctrl+Shift+F3 inserts them
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Word's Spike: Ctrl+F3 cuts the selection and collects it, Ctrl+Shift+F3 inserts everything collected and empties it (⌘F3 / ⌘⇧F3 on macOS).

In Word the Spike is an AutoText entry called "Spike". Ctrl+F3 cuts the selection and adds it to the end of the Spike, with a paragraph mark after each piece, and leaves the clipboard alone. Ctrl+Shift+F3 inserts the whole Spike at the insertion point, in the order the pieces were collected and with their formatting, and then empties it. Inserting it from the AutoText gallery leaves it full. This PR works the same way: the Spike is the `"Spike"` entry in `building_blocks`, so it shows up in Insert › Quick Parts, and `insert.autoText {"insert":"Spike"}` inserts it without emptying it. The two new commands are `edit.spike` and `edit.insertSpike`. Each is one undo step. The cut goes through `delete_selection`, so Track Changes and content controls are respected, and the insert goes through Paste's own path. A piece that already ends with a paragraph mark doesn't get a second one. Text boxes inside the pieces keep their own stories. If Restrict Editing refuses one of the two commands, `Session::run` now puts the Quick Parts back too, so the Spike never ends up half-changed.

Choices and limits, happy to switch any of them:
- The Spike lasts for the session: it survives File › New and Open in the same window. Word keeps it in Normal.dotm, so there it is global and survives a restart. Saving Quick Parts between launches would be a separate change.
- Undo of Ctrl+F3 puts the text back and keeps the piece in the Spike, the same way undoing Cut leaves the clipboard. Undo of Ctrl+Shift+F3 doesn't refill the Spike.
- With nothing selected, Ctrl+F3 is disabled, like Cut. With the Spike empty, Ctrl+Shift+F3 is disabled.
- After Ctrl+Shift+F3, the rest of the paragraph where you inserted takes the paragraph formatting of the last piece's paragraph. That comes from how `insert_fragment` joins paragraphs.
- Inserting the Spike from the Quick Pa…

title: Layout: field results mixing scripts draw each glyph in its own face (#2491)
author: Nghiathan13
body:
Part of #2491: the Chinese text that showed as blanks or wrong glyphs. The TOC entries' dot leaders and right-aligned page numbers have a separate cause and are not changed here (see "What's left").

## What was wrong
I reproduced the issue on `main` (eae2421) with a synthetic .docx of my own, generated from the issue's description with Python's standard library. It has:
- a cached `TOC \o "1-3" \h \z` field with four entries, each holding a nested `HYPERLINK \l` field and a nested `PAGEREF`;
- the same strings as headings, as body text and in a `w:hyperlink`.

`wordcraft-cli render` showed the TOC entries as `1`, `2`, `3`, `4 CPU`. The Chinese was blank space, while the headings, body text and hyperlink drew it correctly. Both `宋体` and `Noto Sans CJK SC` as the East Asian font reproduce it.

**Narrowing it down:**
- `wordcraft-cli inspect` shows the nested HYPERLINK read as one buffered field whose result is the string `"1 春日花园\t1"`.
- A HYPERLINK field whose result is all Chinese drew correctly.
- A Latin-then-Chinese result did not.

**Root cause** (`crates/layout/src/para.rs`):
1. `shape_atomic` shapes a field result through `shape_with`, which picks a face per character: Times New Roman for `"1 "`, the East Asian font or a fallback for the Chinese.
2. It then merges every glyph into one cluster and keeps `first.style`.
3. Display draws a cluster's glyphs in its style's face. The Chinese glyph ids were therefore drawn in the Latin face, where they mean nothing or another letter.

This affects every buffered result that mixes faces, not only TOC entries: a `DATE` field in a CJK format, or a HYPERLINK field with Latin and Chinese text. Enclosed characters and ruby base text go through the same function.

## What changed
**`para.rs`**
- New `ParaLayout.faces`: for each cluster drawn in more than one face, each face's style and glyph range (`FaceRun`).
- `shape_atomic` fills it, and `shape_overstruck` carries it into the cluster it builds.
- The enclosure measuring …

title: #2209: a first start takes the system account's name as the user name
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #2209

## What changes

On a first start, WordCraft now takes the name of the system account running it as the user name
(the account badge, comments, tracked changes, *Last modified by*) instead of "WordCraft User".
A name set in File › Options › General always wins and is saved as before.

| System | Name used | How |
|---|---|---|
| Windows | the account's first and last name, else its display name (only a domain or work account has one), else the logon name (`USERNAME`) | Windows Runtime `Windows.System.User` / `KnownUserProperties.FirstName`, `LastName`, `DisplayName`: a safe API (the Win32 `GetUserNameExW` needs `unsafe`); the `windows` crate is already a dependency, so no new crate and no `Cargo.lock` change |
| Linux, BSDs | the full name in the account's `/etc/passwd` entry (GECOS up to the first comma, `&` = capitalised logon name), else the logon name (`USER`, then `LOGNAME`) | plain file read, capped at 4 MiB |
| macOS | the logon name (`USER`) | the full name is in Directory Services, which nothing in our build reads safely |
| Web | unchanged ("WordCraft User") | — |

## Design notes

- **Only while the name is the default.** `use_system_user_name` (apps/wordcraft) runs after the
  preferences load and does nothing when the session's name isn't `Session::DEFAULT_AUTHOR`. Every
  run used to save the default into `ui.json`, so preferences holding "WordCraft User" (or a blank
  name) count as "no name chosen" and take the system's; that is what makes it work for existing
  installs too.
- **Asked once.** The name is saved with the preferences like one typed in Options, so the system
  is not queried again (Word keeps the name it first starts with as well).
- **Same cleaning as a typed name.** The name goes through `file.setAuthor` (trim, no control
  characters, 255 chars, blank refused). It's `pure`: no undo step, the document isn't dirty.
- **Can't hold up the start.** The Windows lookup runs on its own thread with a 2 s timeout;
  failures, an …

title: Linux: scan fontconfig's font folders; Load System Installed Fonts rescans on the desktop (#2499)
author: Nghiathan13
body:
Fixes #2499.

On Linux, WordCraft already scans `/usr/share/fonts`, `/usr/local/share/fonts`, `~/.fonts` and `~/.local/share/fonts` at startup. Two gaps remained, and they match points 1 and 2 of the request:

1. **Load System Installed Fonts… did nothing on the desktop.** It only showed "All system fonts are already available.", so a font installed while WordCraft was open (then `fc-cache`) didn't show up until a restart.
2. **Folders added in the fontconfig configuration weren't scanned.** Packages add their own folders through `conf.d` (TeX Live's `/usr/share/texmf/fonts/opentype/...`), and users add theirs through `~/.config/fontconfig/fonts.conf`. `fc-list` shows those fonts and WordCraft didn't.

## Changes

- **`crates/fonts/src/fontdb/fontconfig.rs`** (new): reads the `<dir>` and `<include>` entries of the fontconfig configuration, following fonts-conf(5):
  - The configuration starts at `$FONTCONFIG_FILE`, then `$FONTCONFIG_PATH/fonts.conf`, then `/etc/fonts/fonts.conf`.
  - A `conf.d` folder contributes its `[0-9]*.conf` files, in name order.
  - A leading `~` means the home folder. `prefix="xdg"` means `$XDG_DATA_HOME` for a `<dir>` and `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` for an `<include>`. `prefix="relative"` starts from the file's own folder.
  - It reads nothing else, never runs `fc-list` and doesn't link libfontconfig.
  - Hostile configurations stay bounded: at most 512 files of 1 MB each, include chains 16 deep and 256 folders. A file that includes itself is read once.
- **`system_font_dirs`** adds those folders after the built-in ones, without repeats. Not on wasm.
- **`FontDb::load_system_fonts`**: a rescan clears the cached fallback answers and the remembered uncovered characters, then moves `FontDb::generation`. The UI's existing `watch_fonts` hook then lays text out again and refreshes the font lists and previews.
- **`ui-egui` `load_system_fonts`**: without a web hook, it rescans and reports "Loaded {count} system fonts." with the number of new families. With…

title: #1031: Ctrl+drag adds to the selection (multiple selection)
author: matteo-andreuzza
body:
Closes #1031

## What changes

As in Word, Ctrl (⌘ on macOS) now adds to an existing selection instead of replacing it:

- **Ctrl+drag** adds the text dragged over; the pieces already selected stay.
- **Ctrl+click** adds the sentence.
- **Ctrl+double-click** adds just the word, in place of the sentence the first click added.
- With nothing selected, Ctrl+click still selects the sentence (#549), as before.

With several pieces selected:

- Bold, italic, font, size, colour, highlight and the other character formatting apply to every piece.
- Paragraph formatting and styles apply piece by piece. The commands that move or renumber paragraphs act on the last piece.
- Copy, Cut and Delete take every piece, in one undo step.
- Typing and pasting replace the piece added last and let the others go.
- The status bar counts the words of every piece.
- Moving the caret drops the pieces.

## How

- A new command, `select.add` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/multi.rs`), catalogued under *Editing › Selection*. It takes `{"anchor","focus"}` (a drag) or `{"pos","unit"}` (a click or a double-click). `replaceLast` swaps the piece added last while a drag goes on. Like every command, it is drivable from the CLI, the control channel and MCP.
- The pieces are stored as a `ColumnBlock` with a new `ranges` field: the pieces as made, the last one being `Session::sel`. Their `segments` are the pieces split paragraph by paragraph and merged where they overlap. Painting, word count, Copy, Cut, Delete and character formatting reuse the column-selection (Alt+drag) paths unchanged. `multi::dispatch` handles only what differs: paragraph formatting and styles go piece by piece, and other edits act on the last piece.
- `canvas.rs`: a Ctrl press with text already selected starts an `AddDrag`. Moving calls `select.add` with `replaceLast`. Releasing without moving adds the sentence, on release so a drag doesn't flash it. A Ctrl+double-click swaps that sentence for the word.
- Hostile params are capped: at most …

title: Text frames in the body go where their frame puts them (#2406)
author: D13GOOOO
body:
Fixes #2406

### What was wrong
The form in the issue is built from text frames: nearly every paragraph has a `w:framePr` that puts it at a spot on the page, with zero page margins. `layout_box` already places frames in headers, footers, cells and text boxes (#935), but body paragraphs ignored their frame and were laid out in line. The whole form ran down the left edge of the page, in document order (`docs/layout-parity.md` listed this: "body frames still lay out in line").

### What Word does
A framed paragraph sits where its frame's anchors, offsets and alignment put it, and the text around wraps around the frame; the frame takes no room in the flow. Consecutive paragraphs with the same frame properties share one frame, stacked one under the other (the attorney/address block in the issue's file is 12 paragraphs in one frame).

### Change
`place_para` now hands a framed body paragraph to a new `place_framed_para` (`crates/layout/src/lib.rs`), which:
- finds the run of neighbouring paragraphs with the same resolved frame (bounded to 64), measures them at the frame's width (or their widest line when the frame has none) to get this paragraph's offset in the frame and the frame's height (exact / at-least / auto);
- places the frame with the existing `frame_float` + `float_rect`, relative to the page, margins or column and paragraph as its anchors say;
- adds the frame's wrap area once (from its first paragraph), so the text around keeps clear of it;
- pushes the paragraph's lines and objects there and leaves the flow position and spacing untouched.

List labels are counted once, when each paragraph is placed; the measuring pass lays out without them. Web view keeps frames in line as before. Frames inside text boxes (#2383) are not touched.

Rendering the issue's `test.docx` with `wordcraft-cli render` now gives the page of Word's PDF: the heading, the parties, the "On Appeal" rules, the attorneys' block on the right and the footer in their places. Remaining differences…

title: Keep leading U+3000/NBSP in Markdown import and round trip
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/formats/src/markdown.rs:253 (join_lines); also the trim_start() calls at lines 229, 311, 426 and 432, against escape_line_start at line 1077` (no existing issue): Markdown import and round trip drop leading U+3000 and NBSP from paragraphs, and read an NBSP before a marker as a heading or list.

## Cause
The Markdown importer stripped leading whitespace with `str::trim_start()`, which removes all Unicode whitespace (U+3000, NBSP), while CommonMark only strips spaces and tabs. As a result, indents were lost on import. A marker after an NBSP or U+3000 was also read as a heading, list or quote, because `escape_line_start` only skips spaces and tabs and so did not escape it.

## Fix
The importer's leading-whitespace stripping now removes only ' ' and '\t' (`trim_start_matches([' ', '\t'])`) in the paragraph joining, block detection and list parsing. U+3000 and NBSP stay in the paragraph text and no longer start blocks. This matches what `escape_line_start` already assumes.

## Verified
- Regression test `leading_unicode_whitespace_is_kept_and_does_not_start_blocks`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-formats --lib leading_unicode_whitespace_is_kept_and_does_not_start_blocks`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::deleted_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_without_markup`, `tests::hidden_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_when_not_shown`, `tests::tight_wrap_follows_an_ellipse`, `tests_pages::widow_control_moves_a_three_line_paragraph_whole`, which also fail on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
`escape_line_start` is unchanged. It already skips only spaces and tabs, which now matches the importer.

title: #1876: Web Layout text fills the window width
author: dkhlapov
body:
Part of #1876 (the width; the blur is the same as #1762 / #1531, already covered by #1736).

## What was wrong
View › Web Layout laid the text out in a fixed 800-point column, so the page never filled the window, unlike Word's Web Layout.

## What changes
- **Web Layout fills the work area** from side to side and re-wraps when the window is resized or the zoom changes. The width is clamped, so a tiny or huge window never gives a zero, negative or absurd width.
- **While the window edge is dragged**, the layout waits until the size has been steady for 0.16 s (the same settle logic Read Mode uses, now one shared piece of code), so a long document isn't laid out again on every frame. Entering Web Layout or changing the zoom applies at once. After a re-wrap the caret's line is brought back into view.
- **Draft and Outline** keep their fixed 800 pt column and never pick up a leftover width from Web Layout.
- **Not saved:** the window-derived width is never written into a file or the preferences. The headless engine (CLI, MCP, tests) keeps 800, so headless layouts don't change.
- Print Layout and Read Mode are unchanged.

## Tests
New tests: Web Layout wraps at the window width (and more lines when the window is narrower); no relayout in the middle of a window drag; the settle logic as a pure function; 200% zoom halves the width; Draft after Web Layout stays at 800; the width isn't saved. Each regression test was shown to fail before its fix. `cargo xtask ci` passes all 6 steps. The reviewing agent looked at screenshots of Web Layout at two widths and at 200% zoom.

## Follow-ups
- After a Ctrl+wheel zoom, the view keeps the caret in view rather than the point under the pointer (Read Mode anchors to the first visible line).
- The blurry rendering from the same report is #1736's job.

title: Fonts Word embeds as subsets lay out the text set in them (#2240)
author: D13GOOOO
body:
Fixes #2240

### What was wrong
Embedded fonts have been loaded on open since #1176, but each face was registered under the family name inside the font file. When Word embeds only the characters used, the subset it writes carries a made-up family inside, and the document asks for the font by the font table's name. Nothing answered to that name, so the text fell back to a substitute as if no font were embedded.

From the court form attached to #2406 (de-obfuscated `name` tables):

| font table `w:name` | family inside the file |
|---|---|
| `OBRBWW+Century Schoolbook` | `___WRD_EMBED_SUB_46` |
| `WFMBOK+Century Schoolbook Bold` | `___WRD_EMBED_SUB_44` |
| `VUKLGA+Old English Text MT` | `___WRD_EMBED_SUB_56` |
| `Calibri`, `Old English Text MT` (full embeds) | same as the table |

So almost all of that form's text (148 runs in `OBRBWW+Century Schoolbook`) was drawn in a substitute, and "Before the" in a sans face instead of Old English.

### Change
- `wordcraft_docx::embedded_fonts` returns `EmbeddedFont { name, data }`: each file with its `w:font/@w:name`.

- `add_font` and the font-folder loader pass no name and behave as before.

With this, `wordcraft-cli render` of the #2406 form draws its text in the embedded Century Schoolbook (regular, bold and italic) and "Before the" in Old English, as in Word's PDF.

title: Text effects: legacy outline, shadow, emboss and imprint are drawn (#2534)
author: naxvog
body:
Fixes #2534.

The legacy run properties `w:outline`, `w:shadow`, `w:emboss` and `w:imprint` were already read, resolved and written back on save, but nothing in layout drew them, so they showed as plain text (the `format.outline` / `format.shadow` / `format.emboss` / `format.engrave` commands had no visible effect either).

## Fix

`wordart::run_effects` maps the four flags onto the `TextEffects` that WordArt already uses, and `display.rs` asks it instead of reading `rc.text_effects` directly. Screen and PDF both draw `Draw::Art` through `art_layers` already, so render and pdf needed no change. The real glyphs stay in place, invisible, so PDF text extraction is unchanged.

- Outline: hollow letters with a 0.5 pt stroke in the text colour.
- Shadow and Emboss: a sharp grey copy offset down-right by size/20.
- Imprint: the same copy offset up-left.
- Word's PDF export gives Emboss and Imprint a slightly doubled look; this is an approximation, noted in the parity doc.
- `w14` text effects on the same run take precedence (`TextEffects::overlay`).

Edge cases found in review:

- Colour-glyph faces (emoji) have no outlines, so they skip the art path and keep drawing as normal glyphs.
- Synthetic bold: `embolden` widens the outline, or adds one in the solid fill's colour and transparency, so bold text in a face without a bold variant keeps its weight. This applies to WordArt too. Gradient fills get no added outline yet (marked `shortcut:`).
- Vertical text: in a top-to-bottom frame, runs with upright East Asian characters skip the art path, since `Draw::Art` isn't turned upright. Everything else in turned frames keeps its effects.
- With markup shown, tracked insertions and deletions keep their legacy effects; WordArt runs still turn plain in the reviser colour as before.
- Dark page: `Draw::Art` carries the run's highlight or shading (`text_bg`), and the letter layers (fill, outline) are inked with `ink_text` like plain glyphs (#1252), so effect text on a dark highlight s…

title: #1653: RTF import decodes the East Asian multibyte code pages (932/936/949/950)
author: midasdf
body:
## What this fixes

Fixes #1653 — *RTF import ignores the font code page (`\cpg` / `\fcharset`): Cyrillic and Japanese text becomes mojibake*.

`crates/doc/src/encoding.rs` mapped charsets to **single-byte** code pages only and decoded one byte at a time, so a Japanese, Korean or Chinese RTF (charset 128/129/134/136 or `\ansicpg932`/`936`/`949`/`950`) came out as mojibake: a Shift-JIS lead byte and its trail byte were decoded separately.

- `charset_code_page` now maps 128 → 932 (Shift-JIS), 129 → 949 (UHC), 134 → 936 (GBK), 136 → 950 (Big5), 255 → 437; `MULTIBYTE_CODE_PAGES`, `is_multibyte_code_page()`, `multibyte_encoding_name()` and `is_text_code_page()` are new, and `\ansicpg`/`\cpg` accept those pages.
- The RTF reader streams 8-bit text through one `encoding_rs` decoder per code page (`new_decoder_without_bom_handling`, U+FFFD for invalid sequences, the rest kept), so a lead byte and its trail byte decode together across text words, group boundaries and chunks, and the decoder never switches to UTF-8/UTF-16 on a BOM-like byte sequence. A raw run decodes in one pass (ASCII body text and picture hex no longer go byte by byte; picture hex skips the decoder entirely) and a code-page switch (`\f`, `\fcharset`, `\cpg`, `\ansicpg`), a group end and end of document finish the run.
- Single-byte code pages, `\uN`/`\ucN` escapes, font tables, and the whole Windows-1252 path are unchanged byte for byte.

`encoding_rs` was already a `wordcraft-formats` dependency (`Cargo.toml` line 64), so no dependency change; `wordcraft-doc` stays free of it.

## Tests

`cargo test -p wordcraft-formats -p wordcraft-doc` → **200 + 174 passed, 0 failed** (doctests 0); `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-formats -p wordcraft-doc --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean.

```

title: Layout: a left tab whose text doesn't fit moves to the next line with it (#2531)
author: naxvog
body:
Fixes #2531.

When the text after a tab doesn't fit on the line, Word moves the tab to the next line together with that text. There the tab starts again from the indent and takes the first stop. Since this PR was opened, main has done this for right, centre and decimal tabs and for left tabs past the right indent (#1840, which fixed #1839). An ordinary left tab still broke after itself, so its text started the next line at the margin.

In the docxide-pdf `leading-tab-two-tabs` and `leading-tab-visible-prefix` fixtures, the greeting doesn't fit after the second tab on line 1. Word carries that tab to line 2, where it reaches the centre stop at 250.9 pt and centres the greeting on it (x = 268.4 pt in the reference). WordCraft drew it at the left margin (x = 72 pt).

## Fix

`break_lines` (`crates/layout/src/para.rs`): main's wrap rule for a right/centre/decimal tab now applies to any tab. The tab stays on its line in three cases:

- Nothing that takes room precedes it (markers, floating objects' anchors).
- It's at the first line's hanging-indent stop (`[1]<tab>long URL`).
- The word after it wouldn't fit after the first stop on the next line either, which would leave the tab a line of its own.

A centre, right or decimal tab laid out again on the next line now starts with no width. Before, the width it had on the line before shifted its text left; this was latent in main's right-tab path too.

## Word measurements

@OPUZZLES reproduced this independently and measured Word for Mac 16.114 (compatibility mode 15):

- The leading-tab case puts the greeting at x = 271.77 pt.
- A mid-line left tab (`PrefixPrefixPrefixPrefix<TAB>Synthetic greeting`, left stops at 108 and 431.25 pt) is carried along too: the greeting lands at x = 180 pt on line 2.

Their DOCX round-trip regression is included unchanged as `crates/engine/tests/leading_tabs.rs`, and they are credited as co-author.

title: #2543: the table eraser erases what a click or a drag touches, as in Word
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #2543

The table eraser took only single clicks on a line between two cells. It now works like Word's: a click or a drag erases every border it touches, in one undo step.

## What changes

- **Click:** erases the border nearest it, within about 6 screen points at any zoom. A line between two cells wins over the table's outside.
- **What lights up is what goes:** the preview and the command take the reach from one function, so a border lit while the button is down is the one the release erases, at every zoom down to the smallest page scale.
- **Drag:** a thin red rectangle follows the pointer, and the borders it touches show thick. On release they are all erased in one undo step. Cells that make one rectangle merge (across a row, down a column, or a block corner to corner); other lines are hidden.
- **Outside borders:** erasing the table's outside hides that stretch, a one-cell table's too.
- **Cells that don't line up:** where a wide cell sits under narrow ones, only the stretch they share is hidden.
- **Esc** during a drag drops only the drag; the eraser stays on.
- **A click off the table** puts the eraser down.
- **Gridlines** show while the eraser or Draw Table is on, so hidden borders stay visible. View Gridlines clicked while a tool is on takes effect at once and stays after the tool stops, also when you switch between Draw Table and the eraser.
- **Nothing lights up on hover**, only while the button is down.
- **Pointer:** our own eraser, drawn in code, with a pink end and a white sleeve like the Eraser button (one pink constant shared with the icon). It stays drawn during a drag over the rulers and the ribbon, and after Esc while the button is still down. The status-bar hint is updated in all 26 catalogs.

## Engine

`table.eraser` also takes a drag (`x0`, `y0`, `x1`, `y1`) and an optional `reach` in page points (a default when it is left out). Borders are found from the layout, table by table, nested tables included.

title: #2544: Draw Table draws nested tables and rows, and a line splits every cell it crosses
author: rabis7575
body:
**Draft until #2554 lands:** this PR is stacked on #2554, so until then its diff also shows #2554's three commits; this PR's own commits are the last three. Once #2554 is merged I'll rebase this onto `main` and mark it ready for review.

Refs #2544

As asked in the review, the floating-table placement that was here is split off: it follows as its own PR once this one lands.

With Draw Table, a rectangle inside a table drew nothing, a line split only the cells it ran along for half their length, and a border the eraser took between two rows couldn't be drawn back. title: #1681: HTML export and import keep furigana (ruby)
author: midasdf
body:
## What this fixes

Fixes #1681 — *Furigana (ruby annotations) are lost during HTML export.*

The flow model (`crates/formats/src/model.rs`) had no ruby variant at all, so a `wordcraft_doc::InlineObject::Ruby` was dropped when a document was converted for export — the annotation *and* its base text never reached any writer. This makes ruby survive the conversion and round-trip through HTML:

- **Export**: `Inline::Ruby` → `<ruby>base<rt>reading</rt></ruby>`, wrapped in exactly the run's formatting tags that `Inline::Text` gets (the tag block moved into a `fmt_tags()` helper so both use it); base and reading go through the existing `text_html` escaper.
- **Import**: `<ruby>` is read with a bounded sub-parser (like the existing `read_math`): `<rb>`/text outside `<rt>` = base, `<rt>` = reading, `<rp>` fallback parentheses are dropped, inner tags ignored, an unclosed element is closed by the next block-level tag and that token is handed back to the main reader so following paragraphs are not swallowed, 4096-token cap, whitespace collapsed as body text does. Half-marked ruby (no base or no reading) becomes plain text — the inner text is never lost.
- **Defaults on import** (`model::ruby_object`, matching the Phonetic Guide command `crates/engine/src/cmd/phonetic.rs`): align = `RubyAlign::default()` (center), base size = the run's size else 10.5 pt, ruby size = `(base.floor()/2).max(1)`, raise = `ruby_raise(0.0, base_size, size)`. HTML cannot express the guide's align/size/raise or the ruby's own run props, so they reset to those defaults on re-import.
- Formats that have no ruby markup keep the base text as before (one arm each in RTF and LaTeX; ODT and Markdown go through a `ruby_as_text()` helper so their text paths and styles still apply).
- **Tracked changes**: ODT export reads the insertion/deletion marks from a ruby's formatting too (not just from text runs), so an inserted or deleted phonetic guide keeps its `text:change-start`/`text:change` range around the base …

title: Layout: 行頭禁則 lists small kana and the prolonged sound mark (JIS X 4051 §4), with the emergency-break gap documented
author: midasdf
body:
## What this changes

`crates/layout/src/kinsoku.rs` implements the paragraph's 禁則処理 on top of the Unicode line-break opportunities (UAX #14). Its module doc promises that "the lists make sure of it for the standard Japanese/Chinese sets", but `NO_START` was missing the **小書きの仮名** (`ぁぃぅぇぉっゃゅょゎゕゖ`, `ァィゥェォッャュョヮヵヶ`, the katakana phonetic extensions U+31F0…U+31FF, the halfwidth `ｧｨｩｪｫｬｭｮｯ`) and the **長音記号** (`ー`, `ｰ`).

The list now holds them, grouped and documented as JIS X 4051 §4 and Word's default 禁則処理 do — 小書きの仮名 / 長音記号 / 繰り返し記号・濁点 / 閉じ括弧類 and the rest — with the module doc updated to say what the set covers and why. Still one `&str` constant consulted by `apply()`; `kinsoku = false` (a break may fall between any two East Asian characters) and the `word_wrap = false` path are unchanged, and no other character's behaviour moves.

## An honest finding: this is a contract fix, not a visible bug fix

Probing the actual dependency (`unicode-linebreak` 0.1.5, Unicode 15.0): it classes these characters `CJ` and its pair table resolves `CJ` like `NS`, so break opportunities are **already** absent before them — `linebreaks("漢っ漢ゃ…")` offers a break only before each 漢. A control experiment (temporarily reverting only the `NO_START` data, tests kept) confirmed the two behaviour tests pass either way and only the membership test fails.

So the rule already holds in normal-width paragraphs today, and this change makes our own list state it: it matches the documented contract above, and it keeps the result correct if the line-break data ever resolves `CJ` as `ID` (UAX #14's relaxed default) or the dependency changes.

## The gap this leaves (repro included, deliberately not fixed here)

The emergency break in `crates/layout/src/para.rs::break_lines` — the "No opportunity: break here" fallback taken when no break opportunity exists on the line — ignores kinsoku entirely, because `kinsoku::apply()` can only filter opportunities that exist. At a very narrow line width a Japanese pa…

title: #537: test that System pins the title bar to the desktop's light/dark answer on Linux
author: benandez
body:
Refs #537

## What
Adds a regression test, `system_theme_pins_the_title_bar_to_the_desktop_answer` (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`). It checks that with the interface theme on **System**, when winit reports no OS theme (Linux), the app uses the desktop portal's light/dark answer and sends `SetTheme(Light|Dark)` to the window. It also checks that a theme switch made while the app is running is followed.

## Why
#537 was reported on v0.5.0. On GNOME, winit draws the title bar itself (sctk-adwaita) and reads the portal's `color-scheme`, so it went dark. The app couldn't read the desktop's setting at that point and stayed light. #298 (v0.6.1) fixed this: System now follows the desktop and passes that answer to the window, so the title bar matches. Nothing tested that path, so this PR adds a test.

The KDE screenshot in the issue shows KWin's server-side title bar in the user's own KDE colour scheme. The app doesn't control that.

## Testing
- New test passes; `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).
- **Not checked visually on GNOME:** I tested on KDE Wayland, which uses server-side decorations, so the sctk-adwaita title bar never appears. @DeveloperX-debug, @jakubiszon26: could you confirm on v0.7.0 that the title bar now matches the app on GNOME?

## What
Each Windows release also ships a **just-me installer**, `wordcraft-<ver>-windows-user-<arch>.msi` (x64, x86, arm64), next to the existing all-users MSI. It installs WordCraft into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\WordCraft` for the current user without a UAC/administrator prompt. Start Menu shortcut, file associations ("Open with", Default apps) and App Paths all work for that user.

## How
- **One WiX source, two builds.** `wordcraft.wxs` takes `-d Scope=...` (default `perMachine`, so the existing MSI's scope is unchanged). `package.ps1` builds it again with `Scope=perUserOrMachine`. In WiX v5 that sets `ALLUSERS=2` + `MSIINSTALLPERUSER=1` ([source](https://github.com/wixtoolset/wix/blob/v5.0.2/src/wix/WixToolset.Core/Compiler_Package.cs)). That makes a dual-purpose package that installs per-user by default. Windows redirects Program Files to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs` and the Start Menu to the user's own.
- **`HKLM` → `HKMU`** for all 45 registry values. HKMU is HKLM in a per-machine install and HKCU in a per-user one, so the all-users MSI writes exactly what it wrote before.
- Both share the UpgradeCode. Each one upgrades its own earlier versions, because Windows Installer only matches products installed in the same context. If someone installs both, they get two separate installs.
- **Why not `Scope="perUser"` like craft-launcher?** A pure per-user package can't key components on files (ICE38) and needs RemoveFolder entries (ICE64), so WordCraft would need a second WiX source. The dual-purpose route keeps one source.
- **File name:** `windows-user-<arch>` rather than `windows-<arch>-user`. The shared `windows-arm64.yml` installs the *first* `dist/*.msi` and checks Program Files, and this name keeps the per-machine MSI sorting first.
- No release workflow change is needed: it uploads `dist/release/*`.
- README download table, `docs/releasing.md` and the ROADMAP progress log are updated.

title: Gap #8: Romanian proofing (ro-RO spelling, suggestions, grammar)
author: Moogabe
body:
## Romanian proofing (gap #8)

Adds Romanian (`ro`, `ro-RO`, `ro-MD`) as a proofed language, following the Italian/Croatian pattern.

**Spelling** comes from the Hunspell `ro_RO` dictionary installed on the system. Rospell works, including LibreOffice's `dict-ro`. The dictionary is never bundled because it is GPL/LGPL/MPL-licensed. It is read by the existing affix engine.
- Cedilla `ş`/`ţ` (old fonts and keyboards) are read as the standard comma-below `ș`/`ț`, so legacy text isn't flagged word by word.
- Hyphenated forms (`într-o`, `s-a`, `dă-mi`, `nord-est`) are checked part by part. The dictionary lists the clipped pieces (`într`, `s`, `n`) as words.

**Suggestions** (`ro/suggest.rs`), in this order:
1. Missing diacritics first (`stiinta` → `știință`, `si` → `și`) and the pre-1993 `î` inside words (`cîine` → `câine`).
2. The dictionary's `REP` table.
3. A missing hyphen (`intrun` → `într-un`, `sa` → `s-a`) or space.
4. One typo.
5. A stem scan.

**Grammar** (`ro/grammar.rs`) is conservative and reports in Romanian:
- Repeated word, with the emphatic doubles allowed (`încet încet`).
- Space before punctuation, double space, doubled punctuation.
- Sentence capitals, knowing Romanian abbreviations and `„`.
- `nici un`/`nici o` → `niciun`/`nicio` per DOOM, except in the correlative `nici unul, nici altul`.
- A missing comma before `ci` and before the conjunction `dar`. The noun (`un dar`) is not flagged.

**UI:**
- Romanian is listed in Review › Language, in the Language dialog and in File › Options › Proofing (installed dictionary).
- "Romanian" is translated in every catalog.

**Not included:**
- Romanian hyphenation patterns: words fall back to the English patterns, as Czech does.

author: sirmmo
body:
## What this changes

WordCraft gets an add-in system, compatible with the one in GridCraft (storytold/gridcraft#1123) and DeckCraft (storytold/deckcraft#919), plus what is built on it: Office (Office.js) add-ins, VBA macros run by an external add-in, live co-editing with document chat, and editing inside Nextcloud. WordCraft starts them and talks JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdin/stdout, so an add-in that crashes or hangs never takes the document with it (never-crash rule: timeouts, restarts, `failed` after 3 failures, bounded input everywhere, no panics). The protocol is shared with GridCraft and DeckCraft, so one add-in can serve all three apps. The cross-app specs (co-editing, chat, add-in requirements) live in [sirmmo/craft-collab](https://github.com/sirmmo/craft-collab).

1. **Add-ins, protocol 1** (66488f7): `plugin.json` manifests, commands answered with engine commands and run as one undo step, ribbon groups and context-menu items, Options › Add-ins, install from GitHub (release zip picked by platform, size and path limits, confirmation first), `plugins.*` commands, `--plugin DIR`.

title: Read Mode keeps the keyboard and shows whole, unobscured columns (#1772)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #1772.

The report was vague ("Read Mode glitches"), so I reproduced Read Mode headlessly (`ui_shot`: enter, page forward/back, resize, change width/size/spacing, leave) and fixed the three glitches that were real:

1. **Keys did nothing until a click.** Right after entering Read Mode, arrows, Page Up/Down and Escape were ignored: the canvas got a new widget id in Read Mode's layout and lost keyboard focus. The canvas now has a fixed id. Test: `reading_mode_keys_turn_columns`.
2. **The page-turn bar covered the last lines of a column.** Columns now end 44 px above the bar. Test: `reading_columns_end_above_the_page_turn_bar`.
3. **A column was cut off at the right edge** after changing column width, text size or window size. Read Mode now shows only whole columns, centred. Test: `reading_viewport_shows_whole_columns` (also sweeps widths 300–4000 px and four zoom levels so it can't silently drop a column).

All three tests failed before the fix and pass after. Docs: `docs/ui-parity.md`, `ROADMAP.md`.

**Review:** independent review found one bug in my first fix (rounding could drop a column in the default layout, e.g. 800 px at 100% showed 2 columns instead of 3). Fixed with a tolerance and a stronger test. A second review found that shrinking the window by a pixel or two could drop a column and keep it dropped (800 px → 799 px showed 2 columns instead of 3); a column up to half a point too wide is now kept, with a new test (`reading_viewport_keeps_columns_when_the_window_shrinks_a_little`) that failed before. title: Control/MCP: no replay of mutations with unknown outcome; queued requests honour timeouts (#1326, #1331)
author: vangel76
body:
Closes #1326
Part of #1331

Both issues are source audits against an older main (159b84f). Checked against current main: all points still applied.

## What changes

**#1326: no replay of an ambiguous mutation** (`crates/mcp/src/backend.rs`)
- The bridge now tells "not sent" (connect or write failed, so the app cannot have run it) from "outcome unknown" (the request was written, then the read failed, timed out or the reply was lost).
- Read-only methods (`document.inspect`, `engine.commands`, `ui.inspect`, `ui.parity`, `ui.render`, `ui.screenshot`) and not-sent requests still retry once on a new connection.
- Any other method with an unknown outcome returns an explicit `outcome unknown: ...` error and is never sent again.
- Reply lines are capped at 128 MiB (a bigger one is an unknown-outcome failure, not unbounded memory).

**#1331: deadline / cancellation for queued control requests** (`apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs`, `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs`, `lib.rs`)
- `ControlRequest` carries a shared state (queued / started / cancelled). The UI calls `start()` before running it; the waiting connection thread calls `cancel()` when its 60 s wait ends. Whoever comes first wins, so a request that timed out in the queue is dropped and never runs.
- The caller gets `timeout before execution: the request was not run and never will be` or `timeout: outcome unknown, the request had started ...`.
- Unauthenticated connections are capped (64); extra ones are closed at once. Threads are created with `thread::Builder` (a failure closes that connection instead of panicking).

**#1331: bounded MCP stdio line** (`crates/mcp/src/server.rs`): request lines over 32 MiB are dropped without being buffered and answered with an error; the next line is served.

## Not part of this PR (why #1331 is only "Part of")
- Write deadlines and a total response deadline for partial/drip-fed replies on the bridge.
- Bounded queue depth for control requests.
- Cancelling a request that is already r…

title: Font list: entries of tall-ascent fonts are no longer cut off (#2570)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #2570.

**What was wrong.** Each entry in the font list is a small picture of the font's name, drawn into a fixed 22 pt box with its baseline placed by the font's "ascent". Fonts with a very tall ascent break that: Amiri sits low, and Amiri Quran (ascent 1.815 em) lands below the bottom of the box, so only the tops of its letters show (the half-cut row). The low-sitting rows also made the list look like two lists. Reproduced with the real Amiri fonts; the screenshot matches the report.

**Fix.** `render_text_line` now centres each entry's capital letters in the row instead of using the ascent. The cap height is clamped (0.3–1.0 em) and a non-finite value falls back to 0.7 em, so a bad font can't push the text out. Ordinary fonts move by about a pixel at most.

**Test.** `a_tall_ascent_font_list_entry_sits_where_the_others_do` (crates/render): a copy of Source Sans 3 with a 1.815 em ascent must draw in the same rows as the normal one, uncut and centred. It failed before the fix (ink rows 33–43 vs 12–33) and passes now. Docs: `docs/ui-parity.md`, `ROADMAP.md`.

**Review:** independent Opus review approved. Deferred minors: the clamp limits and the missing-cap-height fallback have no test of their own; the test leaves its renamed font in the process-wide font list (test process only); the ROADMAP progress-log table was already malformed.

**Word check:** none; centring each entry in its row is an assumption.

CI: all 6 steps pass (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

title: #959: the Assistant, Nib: tips, cheeky sayings and agent messages
author: benandez
body:
Fixes #959

"Bring back Clippy", but our own: **Nib**, an original fountain-pen nib with eyes, drawn in code (no Microsoft artwork, names, animations or wording; CLAUDE.md asset rule). It floats over the window with **Tips**, deliberately cheeky **Sayings**, and **messages from agents**.

## Behaviour
- **Off by default.** Nib introduces itself once ("Keep me around" / "Not now"), then stays off unless turned on: Help › Assistant, File › Options › General › Assistant, or its right-click menu. Never appears in tests, headless runs or the CLI.
- **Tips** (each at most once a session; "Don't show me this tip again" remembered): letter ("Dear …" → Envelopes, Letter template), list started (→ Restart at 1), keyboard shortcut after the same ribbon command 3×, tip of the day, save reminder (AutoSave off, 20 min unsaved). Buttons run commands by id and only appear when enabled. A newer Tip replaces an open one.
- **Sayings**: idle, mass delete, Save spam, lorem ipsum, word-count milestones, undo streaks. Level **Off / Sometimes** (default, ≤1 per 15 min) **/ Annoying** (≤1 per 3 min).
- **Never in the way**: the Balloon never takes keyboard focus (typing with it open goes to the document; a click on it hands focus back); nothing new appears over dialogs, menus, Backstage, Focus or Read mode. Sayings fade after 8 s, Tips after 20 s of typing on.
- **Nib**: six poses (idle bob/blink, wave, write, startled, doze, bow), all still when animations are off. Drag to move (remembered); right-click: Hide, Sayings, Mute agent messages, Reset tips, Options.

title: Equations: quoted text is normal text with its spaces; a fraction waits for its denominator (part of #2581)
author: Nghiathan13
body:
Part of #2581. It fixes the two parts that are clearly bugs and leaves the rest as it is: spaces typed outside quotes are still build-up spaces that separate operands, as in the linear format.

## What was wrong
Typing `Giro dos Estoques = Custo das Vendas (CMV) / Saldo Médio dos Estoques` in an equation gave `GirodosEstoques=(CustodasVendas(CMV))/()SaldoMédiodos Estoques`:
1. **No way to type words with spaces in math mode** other than the Normal Text toggle. In the linear format (UnicodeMath), text in `"…"` is ordinary text, but WordCraft kept the quotes as characters, and build-up dropped the spaces between them.
2. **`x/` then a space left the denominator empty** and put the caret *after* the fraction, so everything typed next landed outside it.

## What changed
- `crates/doc/src/math_linear.rs`: a closed `"…"` pair parses to one normal-text run (`nor`, upright), spaces kept; `""` gives nothing, and an unclosed quote is still a character. `clean()` and `operand_start` no longer treat a normal-text run (e.g. a quoted `" "`) as a build-up space or operator.
- `crates/doc/src/math_edit.rs`:
  - `"` triggers build-up, but an **open** quote doesn't build up, so spaces typed inside it stay.
  - When build-up re-reads a structure (e.g. a fraction) before the caret, normal-text runs inside it are written back as `"…"`, so rebuilding keeps them, along with their spaces.
  - A fraction built with an empty denominator puts the caret in that denominator.

## Result
Typed key by key through `equation.type`:
- `"Giro dos Estoques"="Custo das Vendas (CMV)"/ "Saldo Médio dos Estoques" ` → Giro dos Estoques = (Custo das Vendas (CMV)) / (Saldo Médio dos Estoques), all upright normal text with spaces; LaTeX `\text{…}`.
- The issue's text without quotes now puts "Saldo Médio dos Estoques" **in** the denominator (it was empty, with the text after the fraction). Words before the last build-up are still joined, unchanged by this PR.

title: #1273: equations from Word files keep all their content
author: benandez
body:
Refs #1273

## What

#1273 says some equations in Word documents go missing and others come out incomplete. We don't have the reporter's file, so I wrote OMML test documents by hand (one for each ECMA-376 §22.1 construct plus the usual Word wrappers), rendered them with `wordcraft-cli render` and compared each against the expected structure.

Every §22.1 element was already read and laid out. The content was lost in the places around the math:

- **Math straight in a story.** `m:oMathPara`/`m:oMath` directly in `w:body` or a `w:tc` (allowed: EG_BlockLevelElts → EG_RunLevelElements → EG_MathContent) was skipped, so the whole equation disappeared. It now gets a paragraph of its own.
- **`mc:AlternateContent Requires="m"`.** The math prefix wasn't in the reader's known list, so we drew the fallback (a picture or placeholder) and not the equation. We now read the equation.
- **Wrappers inside an equation.** EG_PContentMath allows `w:hyperlink`, `w:fldSimple`, `w:dir`, `w:bdo` and `mc:AlternateContent` inside `m:oMath`. Their runs were dropped, so `p=` showed where the file had `p=q`. They're kept now, and nesting depth is still bounded by `MAX_DEPTH`.
- **Symbols.** `w:sym` in a math run (for example Symbol `F061` = α), Symbol-font text and `w:noBreakHyphen` were dropped or drawn as private-use code points. They're mapped to Unicode with the existing `symbol_fonts` table.
- **Layout.** An n-ary operator, delimiter, accent or group character that the math font doesn't have was drawn as a missing-glyph box. It now comes from a fallback font (`char_glyphs`).

## Coverage before → after

| Construct (§22.1) | Import before | Render before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| f (bar, skw, lin, noBar), sSup, sSub, sSubSup, sPre, rad (deg / degHide) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| nary (chr, limLoc, subHide/supHide, grow) | ✅ | ✅, but ⬜ box if the font lacks the operator | ✅ fallback font |
| d (beg/end/sep chars, empty chars), m (mcs/count/mcJc), eqArr, cases | ✅ | ✅, but ⬜ for delimiters the font …

title: #1297: copied equations go in the MathML clipboard formats Word reads
author: benandez
body:
Refs #1297 (follow-up to #816 / #1147). Doesn't close it yet: the paste into Word still needs a person to try it (see "Not verified").

## What

When you copy or cut **one equation on its own**, WordCraft now also puts its MathML in the platform's MathML clipboard formats, beside the HTML (with MathML, from #1147) and the linear text that were already there:

- **Windows:** `MathML` and `MathML Presentation` (registered formats, UTF-16LE text with a terminating NUL)
- **macOS:** `public.mathml.presentation` and `public.mathml` (added to arboard's pasteboard item with the safe `NSPasteboard::setString_forType`)
- **Linux/BSD/web:** unchanged. Word doesn't run there, and arboard can't serve extra MIME types. The HTML still carries MathML.

If the copy has text around the equation, these formats are left off. Word reads them before anything else, so including them would paste only the equation and drop the text. That copy keeps HTML+MathML and text, as before.

## How, and why MathML formats rather than OMML

The issue asks for OMML. I looked for a public way to put OMML on the clipboard and found none. Microsoft documents MathML formats as the way Office apps take math from the clipboard:

- Microsoft Learn, *MathML Support in Microsoft 365*, "Clipboard support" (https://learn.microsoft.com/office/math/mathml#clipboard-support). When the apps (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, OneNote) paste math, they check first for `MathML` or `MathML Presentation`, then for MathML in `CF_UNICODETEXT`. The data is UTF-16LE. The same page says the importer handles Presentation MathML 3, uses the first child of `<semantics>` and ignores annotations, and supports `display="block"`. It also describes MathML inside pasted HTML, but only from Microsoft 365 Version 2606 / Mac 16.110 on, which is why the HTML alone may not be enough on older builds.
- W3C MathML 3, §6.2.4 *Transferring MathML* (https://www.w3.org/TR/MathML3/chapter6.html). Defines the flavour names: Windows `MathML` / `MathML Prese…

title: Gap 9: open AES-encrypted Word files (Standard encryption)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Closes part of docs/gaps.md row #9 (password-protected `.doc` files using AES).

## What changed
- **Scope finding:** [MS-OFFCRYPTO] defines AES only for ECMA-376 *encrypted packages* (a compound file with `EncryptionInfo` + `EncryptedPackage`). For Word 97-2003 binary files ([MS-DOC] §2.2.6.2) only XOR, RC4 and RC4 CryptoAPI exist, and `fAES` "MUST be 1 only for ECMA-376 documents". The engine already routes encrypted packages named `.doc`/`.dot` to the docx decryptor, but that decryptor only knew the **agile** method. Files using the **Standard** method (AES-128/192/256, SHA-1, 50,000 spins, the method Word 2007 wrote) couldn't be opened. That is the AES case this PR fixes.
- `crates/docx/src/crypt.rs`: Standard encryption decryption from the public spec: §2.3.4.5 (binary `EncryptionInfo`), §2.3.4.7 (key derivation), §2.3.4.9 (AES-ECB password verifier, constant-time compare) and §2.3.4.4 (`EncryptedPackage` StreamSize, checked and then truncated). `decrypt()` picks agile or Standard from the version and flags. A missing or wrong password gives the same errors as agile files, under any Word extension (`.docx`, `.doc`, `.dot`, or none).
- `crates/docbin/src/crypt.rs`: a binary `.doc` whose table-stream header claims AES is still refused, now with a message saying AES is only defined for the newer encrypted-package format.
- `crates/engine/src/io.rs`: doc comment updated.
- Docs: `docs/gaps.md` row 9 (narrowed; nothing left to build), `docs/file-format-parity.md` (the duplicate combined encryption row is removed and the totals are re-summed from the rows), `ROADMAP.md` progress log. Each with its status line and revision history.

  - docx unit tests: key derivation, verifier, round trip;

title: #763: LanguageTool checks each run in its own language
author: dkhlapov
body:
Fixes #763.

**Stacked on #672 — merge that first.** (The diff against main also shows #672's commits until it merges.)

LanguageTool no longer checks a whole paragraph in its first run's language. A paragraph whose runs have different languages (e.g. English with a `fr-FR` quote) is sent to LanguageTool once per language, as the full paragraph, and from each answer only the issues inside that language's runs are kept. Sending the whole paragraph (not cut-off spans) avoids false "sentence should start with a capital" marks at the cuts. Single-language paragraphs behave as before. Blank runs (spaces, deleted text) join their neighbour so they don't split a sentence.

Code: `crates/ui-egui/src/languagetool.rs` only (plus docs: gaps.md, target-app-parity.md, ROADMAP.md).

Tests: `languagetool_checks_each_run_in_its_language` (accents and emoji before the French run; offsets land right), `languagetool_mixed_paragraph_keeps_sentence_context` (fake server flags lowercase sentence starts; none appear at language cuts), `language_spans_merge_blank_runs`. title: Clipboard: copy and paste RTF
author: dkhlapov
body:
Closes the docs/gaps.md "By kind › UI/UX gaps" item: RTF on the system clipboard ("RTF on macOS and X11 … RTF on the clipboard is not written yet"). No GitHub issue exists for it.

## What changed
- **Copy and Cut also produce RTF** (engine, `edit.rs`): the copied fragment goes through the existing RTF writer (`wordcraft_formats::rtf::export`), is kept on the session beside the HTML, and is returned as `"rtf"` in the command result. Agents and the CLI get it too.
- **UI**: the host service `set_clipboard_html(html, text)` becomes `set_clipboard_rich(text, html, rtf)`. If the host can't set it, egui's text fallback still runs.
- **Writing RTF, per platform** (`apps/wordcraft/src/clipboard.rs`):
  - Windows: after arboard sets text and HTML, "Rich Text Format" is added with `clipboard-win`'s `set_without_clear`.
  - macOS: after arboard, `public.rtf` is added through `NSPasteboard`. These are safe objc2 calls, with no `unsafe`.
  - Wayland (data-control): one offer covers text, HTML and `text/rtf` through `wl-clipboard-rs`. Without the protocol it falls back to arboard as before.
  - **X11: not done.** arboard owns the X11 selection and can't offer extra formats. Adding RTF would mean writing our own selection owner, so on X11 a copy still holds text and HTML.
- **Reading RTF on paste**: added for macOS (`public.rtf`) and X11 (`text/rtf`, then `application/rtf`). The X11 read uses `x11rb`, gives up after 1 s, enforces the size cap, and refuses large copies that arrive in pieces (INCR). Windows and Wayland already read RTF. The order of preference between HTML and RTF on paste is unchanged.
- **Dependencies**: no new crates. `objc2-foundation` and `x11rb` were already in the build through arboard at the same versions; they are now listed directly, and objc2-app-kit gains the `NSPasteboard` feature.

title: Perf: redraw only the changed band of a page on an edit (#1109)
author: maxm11
body:
## What

A keystroke re-rendered whole pages on the CPU: every visible page (or every visible tile of it) was
re-rasterised and the whole texture re-uploaded, for a change of one line. This makes an edit redraw
**only the vertical band of the page its text moved**, and patch that band into the page's existing
texture with `TextureHandle::set_partial`.

`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` now keeps each page's *item bands* — one `(fingerprint, top, bottom)`
per drawn `Placed` item, in page order — beside the raster, together with the content fingerprint,
view and raster scale the raster was made from. After a layout change it diffs old against new and
redraws the union of the **old and new** extents of the items that changed (so deleted and moved ink
is wiped), padded by 32 pt for ink that reaches past its geometry (outlines, shadows, italics), then
snapped outward to whole raster rows and clamped to the page.

Why the diff is sound: an item is fingerprinted by exactly the hash the texture cache already used
(paragraph Arc + line range + position for text, the drawn fields for everything else), so an item
that compares equal draws the same pixels — a band path can never be *less* current than the old
whole-page path, which never re-drew an unchanged page either. Highlights:

- **Fallbacks stay conservative.** Another scale or view, another page size, a non-finite
  (hostile) extent, a change covering more than 75% of the page, a missing texture, or a band raster
  whose size isn't the texture's all draw the page whole, exactly as before.
- **Tall tiled pages** (Web/Draft) keep their native-resolution tiles: the changed band is clipped
  to each tile, and a tile the change misses keeps its raster (it is only re-tagged).
- **Zoom is unchanged** — a zoom step is still whole pages at the new scale (reported below).
- No per-frame hashing was added: the snapshot is taken once per page per layout, where the content
  fingerprint was already computed (#811's invariant is intact …

title: Keep explicit text:s spaces at paragraph ends on ODT import
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/formats/src/odt.rs:1480 (finish_para calls p.trim()); crates/formats/src/model.rs:188 (Para::trim)` (no existing issue): ODT import strips explicit leading and trailing spaces (text:s) from paragraphs, so indentation is lost on round trip.

## Cause
`finish_para` in the ODT reader called `Para::trim` on every untracked, non-code paragraph. That strips all leading and trailing spaces and tabs, including real spaces that came from `<text:s/>`. Indentation written with `text:s` was lost on import.

## Fix
The reader no longer trims paragraph ends with `Para::trim`. XML whitespace at the start of a paragraph is already collapsed away while the text is read. The reader now records whether the last text ended in a space collapsed from XML whitespace, and `finish_para` removes only that one trailing space. Spaces from `text:s` and tabs are kept.

## Verified
- Regression test `explicit_spaces_at_paragraph_ends_are_kept`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-formats --lib explicit_spaces_at_paragraph_ends_are_kept`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::deleted_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_without_markup`, `tests::hidden_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_when_not_shown`, `tests::tight_wrap_follows_an_ellipse`, `tests_pages::widow_control_moves_a_three_line_paragraph_whole`, which also fail on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
`Para::trim` and its use in other formats. Tracked-change and code paragraphs are handled as before. A trailing `text:line-break` or `text:tab` is now kept as well; the old trim stripped it.

title: Fields: Japanese era and numeral picture items in DATE fields (和暦)
author: midasdf
body:
## What this adds

Word's date field picture switch (`{ DATE \@ "ggge年M月d日" }`, Insert ▸ Date & Time) supports Japanese era and Japanese-numeral picture items beyond the Gregorian ones. WordCraft's `format_date_parts` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs`) handled `y`/`M`/`d`/`h`/`m`/`s`/`am/pm`/`dddd`, so a 和暦 picture fell through as literal text and a Japanese document could not show 令和8年10月17日. The items of **[MS-OE376] Part 4 §2.16.4.1, Date and time formatting** (<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oe376/e03ea6ec-7739-461f-ba7f-d11e2058e818>) are now implemented:

| picture item | shows (2026-10-17) |
|---|---|
| `g` / `gg` / `ggg` (and longer runs) | `R` / `令` / `令和` — the era's Latin initial, one kanji, full name |
| `e` / `ee`, and their other spelling `n` / `nn` | `8` / `08` — the era year |
| `A` / `O` / `C` / `I` | day, month, seconds, minutes in Japanese counting-form numerals (`十七`, `十`, `三十一`) |
| `aaa` / `aaaa` | `土` / `土曜日` |

- **Day-accurate era boundaries**: 大正 began 1912-07-30, so 1912-07-29 is `明治45年`; 1989-01-07 is `昭和64年`, 1989-01-08 `平成1年`; 2019-05-01 begins `令和`. Before 明治 1868-01-25 there is no era: the era items render nothing and the rest of the picture still renders (`ggge年M月d日` for 1868-01-24 → `年1月24日`).
- **Era year 1 stays a number** (`令和1年`, `ee` → `01`): the reference defines `e`/`ee` as year numbers and has no 元年 form (its own examples show `令和27年`-style output). Noted in a code comment and here rather than inventing one.
- Works from `insert.dateTime` and from unlocked `DATE` fields refreshed on open (`references::update_fields`), which share the formatter.
- **Lowercase `m` remains minutes** (as `h:mm am/pm` requires), so the era-year/month/day picture is `ge.M.d` → `R8.10.17`; `ge.m.d` shows the minute. Both are pinned in the tests.
- **`A/P`** (and `a/p`) is now read as Word's other AM/PM spelling, before `A`; a bare `A` is the Japanese day numeral. Note the deliberate consequence: a picture that used…

title: Keep custom footnote/endnote marks as text inside the note on DOCX save
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/docx/src/write/story.rs:512-530 (InlineObject::NoteRef, the `current_note == Some(..)` branch)` (no existing issue): DOCX save writes a footnote/endnote with a custom mark as an auto-numbered note, so the mark in the note text changes from the custom mark to the number.

## Cause
When the DOCX writer reached a note's own `NoteRef`, it always wrote the bare `<w:footnoteRef/>` or `<w:endnoteRef/>` placeholder and ignored `custom`. Word replaces that placeholder with the automatic number, so a note with a custom mark such as `*` showed `1` after reopening, though the body reference kept `*`.

## Fix
In `crates/docx/src/write/story.rs`, a note's own marker with a non-empty `custom` is now written as a plain `<w:t>` run holding the custom text. Notes without a custom mark still get `footnoteRef`/`endnoteRef`. The regression test covers footnotes and endnotes.

## Verified
- Regression test `custom_note_mark_stays_in_the_note`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-docx --test roundtrip custom_note_mark_stays_in_the_note`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::deleted_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_without_markup`, `tests::hidden_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_when_not_shown`, `tests::tight_wrap_follows_an_ellipse`, `tests_pages::widow_control_moves_a_three_line_paragraph_whole`, which also fail on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
The reader is unchanged. A note's own custom mark is now written as plain text, so when the file is read back it is ordinary note text and not a `NoteRef` marker. That is how Word writes custom marks. A note read back that way still gets the automatic `footnoteRef` placeholder when it is saved again, because the writer adds one to any note that has no own reference. I did not change that.

title: Promote the cell below when deleting a vertical merge's first row
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/doc/src/table.rs:129 (Table::delete_row), called from crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs:526 (del_row)` (no existing issue): Delete Rows on the first row of a vertically merged cell leaves an orphan 'Continue' cell at the top of the table.

Before removing the row, `delete_row` finds each `Restart` cell in it. If the cell below (same grid column) is `Continue`, it becomes `Restart` when more `Continue` rows follow, and `None` otherwise. The regression test covers a 2-row merge and a 3-row merge.

title: Floating objects stack in Word's order, not the text's (#2638)
author: D13GOOOO
body:
Fixes #2638

## What was wrong
Word stacks anchored drawings by `wp:anchor/@relativeHeight` (ECMA-376 Part 1, §20.4.2.3): the higher one is drawn over the lower, wherever each sits in the text. WordCraft never read the attribute. It drew objects in text order, and on save it renumbered `relativeHeight` in text order too.

In the reporter's file all eight drawings are anchored in one paragraph. In the pasted set the canopy comes before the trunk in the text, but its `relativeHeight` is higher (251662336 against 251661312). Text order therefore drew the trunk over the canopy. In the original set the text order happens to match the stacking order, so it looked right. The rectangles and ellipses also happen to match, which is why only the freeforms showed the bug.

## Change
- **Model:** `Float::z: Option<u32>` holds the stacking order. `None` is an object made in WordCraft, which stacks above every object that has an order, in text order.
- **DOCX read:** `relativeHeight` is read into `z`. An invalid value is ignored, since the spec makes it an unsigned int.
- **DOCX write:** a `z` read from a file is written back unchanged. Objects made here get numbers above the highest one in the document (`Document::top_z`), so they still save on top. Before, everything was renumbered from 251658240 in text order.
- **Layout:** `place_objects` now keeps each object's items together (its picture or shape, its hit area, its text box text). It then puts the floating objects in stacking order with a stable sort, both behind the text and in front of it. Inline objects keep their places.

**Not changed:** objects anchored in *different* paragraphs still stack in text order. Sorting them would mean moving items across paragraphs after pagination, which is a bigger change. The VML `z-index` and ODF `draw:z-index` are not read either.

## Tests
- `layout::tests::floating_objects_are_drawn_in_their_stacking_order`: five shapes, two behind the text and three in front, one of them with no orde…

body:
Resolves #2072.

### Summary
1. **Background (Triage findings for #2072)**:
   In v0.7.0, new documents in non-US regions automatically start as A4 under #838. In v0.7.0, the \Layout › Size\ dropdown had no checkmark indicating the active paper size (\mi\ instead of \mi_check\). Selecting A4 on an already-A4 document changed nothing visible on screen and gave no visual feedback, leading the user to perceive that A4 wasn't working. title: Fix stray leading space in RTF list items on export
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/formats/src/rtf.rs:269-272 (Writer::para)` (no existing issue): RTF export puts a stray space before the text of every bulleted or numbered paragraph, so list items come back with a leading space.

## Cause
Writer::para in the RTF writer always pushed a ' ' after the paragraph preamble. For list paragraphs the preamble ends with `{\listtext ...\tab}`. A space after a closing `}` is literal text in RTF, so every list item gained a leading space on export and on re-import.

## Fix
The delimiter space is now written only for paragraphs without a list label. In that case it ends the preceding control word. List paragraphs go straight from the closing `}` of the label to the item text. The regression test round-trips bullets, numbering, multilevel and defineBullet lists through .rtf and checks the text is unchanged.

## Verified
- Regression test `rtf_list_round_trip_keeps_text`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --lib rtf_list_round_trip_keeps_text`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The space before `{\listtext` is unchanged. It is a control-word delimiter, so it is harmless. The reader and the other formats are unchanged.

title: Shapes, pictures and text boxes inside a drawing canvas are selected and moved on their own (#2637)
author: D13GOOOO
body:
Fixes #2637

## What was wrong
A Drawing Canvas behaved as one static object. A click anywhere in it selected the whole canvas, so the shapes, pictures and text boxes inside it could not be selected, moved, resized, formatted or deleted, and the text of a text box inside it could not be edited. The only way to change a member was the `canvas.member` command, by index.

## Change
**Engine** (everything goes through commands, so it also works from the CLI, the control channel and MCP):
- **`select.member {"index": n | null}`** picks one member of the selected canvas on its own. The canvas stays the selection in the text. Its state is `Session::member`, which records the selection it was picked in. Any other selection change, caret movement or undo clears it.
- **`objects::selected` and `edit_obj`** see the picked member. So Shape Fill, Shape Outline, Change Shape, Shape Effects, Size, Rotate, Alt Text and Picture Format change the member and not the canvas.
- **`arrange.bounds` (Move or Resize) and `arrange.nudge`** move and resize the member inside the canvas. They turn the page point the frame gives into the member's offset in the canvas, and the canvas keeps its frame.
- **Delete, Backspace, Cut and Copy** act on the member alone. A copied member is pasted as a picture or shape of its own.
- **Commands that don't apply to a member** (Wrap Text, Position, Align, Bring Forward / Send Backward, Move with Text, Ctrl+drag copy) are disabled, with the reason, because the canvas places its members.

**UI** (`ui-egui/src/objects.rs`):
- A press inside a canvas finds the topmost drawn member under the pointer (`InlineObject::member_rects`, clipped to the canvas) and picks it.
- The member gets the frame, handles and rotation handle, with the canvas's frame drawn around it. Dragging moves, resizes or turns it, each drop one undoable command. Alignment guides and Ctrl+copy stay off for members.

title: Fonts: Times New Roman keeps Liberation Serif under the roman-font rule (#1613)
author: xmaks82
body:
#1613 draws a missing font in Cambria when the font table classes it as roman, as Word does. Times New Roman is `w:family w:val="roman"` in every font table, so since #1613 every Times document on a machine without Times New Roman (Linux, the web build) is drawn in Caladea instead of Liberation Serif. Word itself always has Times New Roman, so it never applies that rule to it.

What it did to real files: at 12 pt every line was 2.1 pt taller than in Word (15.9 pt against 13.8 pt), and the line breaks moved because Caladea is set wider.

**Change.** The rule now skips a font whose substitutes are chosen by its name: a metric-compatible clone or the same design under another name (Times New Roman, Times, Arial, Helvetica, Courier New, Consolas, Palatino / Book Antiqua, the symbol fonts, Hebrew and Persian fonts). Fonts with no clone of their own still go to Cambria: Cambria, Georgia, Garamond, brand fonts and the like. `word::has_named_substitutes` exposes the distinction, and `substitutes` is unchanged.

**Checked.** 251 real documents (Russian home and office files: `.docx`, `.doc`, `.rtf`), each converted with `wordcraft-cli convert` and compared page by page with a PDF saved by Word 2016 on Windows:

| | `main` eae2421 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| exact page count | 201 / 251 | 229 / 251 |
| page breaks at the same word | 45.4 % | 51.9 % |
| words missing against Word | 0.29 % | 0.26 % |

37 documents improve and 3 get worse. In those 3, Caladea happened to fit one more line before a page break than the true metrics do.

Tests: `a_missing_roman_font_with_its_own_substitute_keeps_it` (layout) and `fonts_with_a_clone_have_named_substitutes` (fonts). `a_missing_roman_font_is_drawn_as_word_draws_it` still passes. `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-fonts -p wordcraft-layout --all-targets -D warnings` is clean, and the tests of both crates pass.
