title: RTF: tables placed as Word places them (row edge, cell margins, vertical alignment)
author: xmaks82
body:
The RTF reader ignored where a table row sits: `\trleft`, `\trgaph`, the `\trpadd…` cell margins, and `\clvertal…` on cells. Every RTF table was drawn with WordCraft's default 5.4 pt cell margins against the page margin. Three things went wrong as a result:

- the text sat 5.4 pt to the right of Word's when the file states no `\trgaph`;
- rows that state a top margin came out 10 pt too high;
- cells centred vertically were drawn at the top.

These are common files. CV services such as hh.ru export résumés as RTF with a `.doc` extension, laid out in tables like this, and 38 of the 44 `.doc` files in my corpus are exactly that.

**Measured in Word 2016 on Windows**: each case saved as PDF by Word through COM, then measured. Word opens RTF in compatibility mode 11 (`Document.CompatibilityMode`), and in that mode:

- the left border stands at `\trleft`;
- the left and right cell margins are `\trpaddl` / `\trpaddr` when their unit is twips (`\trpaddfl3` / `\trpaddfr3`), otherwise `\trgaph`. A file with no `\trgaph` has zero margins;
- the top and bottom margins are only `\trpaddt` / `\trpaddb` in twips;
- each row keeps its own margins.

**Change**
- `rtf.rs` reads these words per row. The table takes its first row's indent and margins; a row whose margins differ gives its cells their own (`CellProps::margins`).
- `\clvertalt` / `\clvertalc` / `\clvertalb` set the cell's vertical alignment.
- RTF opens in compatibility mode 11 (`RTF_COMPAT_MODE`), where `tblInd` is the first cell's text position, as in Word.
- `formats::model::FTable` gains `indent` and `cell_margins`, and `Cell` gains `margins` and `valign`. The other readers construct them with `..Default::default()`.

**Checked**
- 10 synthetic rows (no `\trgaph`; `\trgaph` 108 / 300; `\trleft` −108 / 500 with and without `\trgaph`; `\trpaddl` and `\trpaddt` with and without their unit) plus `\clvertalc` and `\clvertalb`. Text and border positions match Word's PDF within 0.4 pt. Before this change they were 5.4 to 25 …

title: Layout: a Symbol bullet's line keeps Symbol's height without the font
author: xmaks82
body:
Word sizes a line by the fonts in it, and a bullet in Symbol (Word's default bullet, U+F0B7) has a taller ascent than Calibri or Times New Roman. So in Word a bulleted line is taller than the same line without its bullet.

Where Symbol isn't installed (Linux, macOS without Office, the web build), WordCraft draws the bullet as its Unicode equivalent from another face (#776). It also took that face's height, so every bulleted line came out shorter than in Word.

**Measured in Word 2016 on Windows** (synthetic lists saved as PDF by Word):

| line | Word | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| Calibri 11 pt, 1.08 spacing, Symbol bullet | 15.08 pt | 14.49 pt | 15.07 pt |
| Times New Roman 12 pt, 1.08 spacing, Symbol bullet | 15.72 pt | 14.89 pt | 15.75 pt |
| Calibri 11 pt, no bullet / Wingdings bullet | 14.52 pt | 14.49 pt | 14.49 pt |

**Change.** `word::symbol_font_metrics` gives Symbol's and Wingdings' ascent and descent: the `/Ascent` and `/Descent` that Word's own PDFs state for them (Symbol 1.005 / 0.216 em, Wingdings 0.899 / 0.205 em). A run in one of these fonts takes those metrics when the font isn't installed. The list label's ascent now comes from its style instead of being re-read from the face, so the existing rule (the label's extra ascent is added unscaled by the spacing multiple) receives them. Glyphs are unchanged.

**Checked.** I compared 251 real documents (Russian home and office files) page by page with PDFs from Word. Page breaks at the same word went from 45.4 % to 50.1 %: 19 documents improve and 6 get worse. Together with #2673 (Times New Roman) and #2676 (RTF tables), the figure is 57.6 %, and exact page counts go from 201 to 230 out of 251.

The test is `a_symbol_bullet_sizes_its_line_by_the_symbol_font`, which is skipped where Symbol is installed. Clippy is clean, and the tests of `wordcraft-layout` and `wordcraft-fonts` pass.

title: #2634: a table inserted in right-to-left text is right to left, so Tab moves left
author: benandez
body:
## What
`insert.table` now makes a right-to-left table (`w:bidiVisual`) when the caret's paragraph reads right to left (resolved `bidi`, incl. style/defaults), as Word does.

## Why (root cause)
Tab was not the bug: it already moves to the next cell in reading (logical) order, and right-to-left tables are stored logically and mirrored by layout (first cell at the right). But a table inserted while writing RTL text (e.g. after typing Arabic/Hebrew, which makes the paragraph RTL) came out as a **left-to-right** table, so the next logical cell sat on the visual right. Making the table take the paragraph's direction fixes Tab and Shift+Tab without touching navigation code. LTR tables are unchanged.

## Tests
- `tests_typing::tab_in_a_table_inserted_in_right_to_left_text_moves_left`: RTL paragraph → table is `bidiVisual`, Tab goes to cell 1 laid out left of cell 0, Shift+Tab returns; LTR paragraph → LTR table, Tab moves right. Failed before the fix.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps pass.

Docs: `docs/typing-parity.md` (Text direction + revision history), `ROADMAP.md` progress log.

Note: Word's behaviour (table direction from the insertion paragraph) was not re-observed side by side for this change. Existing documents with LTR tables containing RTL text keep their direction (as in Word); use Table Layout › Right-to-Left Table.

Fixes #2634

title: #2625: recovery does not retry a snapshot that cannot be copied until the document changes
author: benandez
body:
## What
`Recovery::poll` cleared `revision` on every worker error, so `tick` re-snapshotted an unchanged dirty document every `INTERVAL`, writing up to 256 MiB each time for an over-limit document.

Now the worker classifies save failures (`SaveError { message, permanent }`):
- **Permanent** (caused by the snapshot itself): size limit / disk budget hit in the `Limited` writer, recovery folder full (record limit), or a copy that does not decode back to the same document. `revision` is kept, so no retry until the document changes.
- **Transient** (locks, I/O, anything else): unchanged behaviour, retried at the next interval.

`docs/recovery.md` describes this; ROADMAP progress log row added.

## Tests
- New `snapshot_that_cannot_be_copied_is_not_retried_until_the_document_changes`: a document whose snapshot always fails (NaN page width, which the format cannot keep) fails once, is not re-queued on later ticks with no change (`recovery_wait` is `None`, no job queued), and is snapshotted successfully after the next edit. Failed before the fix.
- `size_limit_and_lossy_values_fail_without_committing` now also checks the limit flag and that the lossy failure is permanent.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps passed (Linux).

Not tested: a real 256 MiB over-limit document (logic is shared with the tested path via the `Limited` writer's `exceeded` flag); macOS/Windows.

Fixes #2625

title: #2617: centre equation-array rows without &
author: benandez
body:
## What
Equation arrays (`m:eqArr`) now centre a row that has no `&` alignment mark, and such a row no longer widens the aligned columns.

## Why
In Word's built-in "First Property of Radicals" equation, the first case row (`a,  n odd`) has no `&` but the second (`|a|,  &n even`) does. WordCraft put the lone row in the first column and right-aligned it there. That widened column 1 to the whole row, so `|a|,` was pushed far to the right of the brace. Word's PDF in the issue shows the lone row centred over the aligned row: both rows have the same centre, to within 0.01 pt. The "Absolute Value" equation was fine because every row in it has a `&`.

An array where no row has `&` is now centred too. Before, its rows were effectively left-aligned, even though the code meant to centre them.

## Tests
- New `math::tests::eq_array_rows_without_ampersand_are_centred` in `crates/layout` (synthetic OMML nodes): the lone row is centred in both the mixed and the all-unaligned case, and it doesn't widen the aligned columns. It failed before the fix (row at 42 pt instead of the centred 25 pt).
- I rendered the issue's document with `wordcraft-cli convert`. The layout now matches Word's PDF: brace, `a,` over `|a|,`, `n odd` over `n even`.
- `cargo xtask ci` passed (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

Not covered: the spacing of the literal spaces in math text still differs slightly from Word's. That is a separate issue.

Fixes #2617

title: Undo: steps share the style sheet and list definitions (1.2 GB → 21 MB at the limit)
author: arcanii
body:
## What it does

Every undo step keeps a clone of the `Document`. Blocks, pictures and the text of parts were already `Arc`-shared, as the doc crate describes, but the clone copied the whole `StyleSheet` and `Numbering`. A `Style` holds a full `ParaProps` and `CharProps` inline, about 3.5 KB even when mostly empty. So typing into a document with 600 styles and 60 lists cost 2.4 MB per undo step, and 1.2 GB at the 500-step limit (`MAX_UNDO`). Even a plain document paid about 70 KB a step for the default style sheet.

Now undo steps share the style sheet and the list definitions. A command that changes them copies them once.

## How

- **The fields:** `Document::styles` is `Arc<StyleSheet>` and `Document::numbering` is `Arc<Numbering>`.
- **Writes:** each place that changes them uses `Arc::make_mut`, about 155 places in 36 files, most of them tests. Reads are unchanged, through `Deref`.
- **Saved forms:** the JSON form is unchanged (serde's `rc` feature), so recovery copies and `.json` files read and write as before.
- **Per-keystroke paths:** none of the new copy-on-write sites runs on every keystroke. They are style, list, template and theme commands, and AutoFormat's list start.

**How it was measured:**
- `wordcraft-cli run` on macOS 27.0.1 (Apple M3 Max), release builds of `main` (`eae2421`) and of this branch.
- Peak physical footprint (`proc_pid_rusage`).
- Synthetic documents of 74 pages of text, plus one kind of thing an office document carries in quantity.
- An undo step is typing a word and moving the caret (`text.insert`, `caret.left`): typing alone stays one step.

| Document | `main`, 500 steps | This branch, 500 steps | Per step |
|---|---|---|---|
| + 600 styles, 376 latent entries, 60 lists of 9 levels | 1,180 MB | 21 MB | 2,390 → 16 KB |
| Plain text | 46 MB | 14 MB | 80 → 14 KB |
| + 300 comments | 123 MB | 91 MB | 233 → 168 KB |
| + 20 sections with headers and footers, 300 footnotes | 72 MB | 40 MB | 129 → 66 KB |
| All of the above | 1,283 MB | 1…

title: #2702: a missing font is drawn in its font table's altName, as Word does
author: Nghiathan13
body:
Closes #2702.

## Problem
When a document asks for a font that isn't installed, Word draws it in the alternate the font table names (`w:font/w:altName`, ECMA-376 §17.8.3.1). WordCraft dropped `w:altName`, so the font went to the generic substitutes. [`go_math_grade4_guide`](https://github.com/sverrejb/docxide-pdf/blob/main/tests/fixtures/scraped/go_math_grade4_guide/input.docx) (docxide-pdf corpus) is set in Museo Sans 300 with `altName` Calibri: Word draws Calibri and lays out 26 pages, WordCraft drew Arial and laid out 53.

## Fix
- **docx** (`read_font_families`): reads `w:altName` with the family classes into the new `Settings::font_alt_names` (font, alternate). Same name-length and table-size limits as `roman_fonts`. An empty alternate, or one that repeats the font's own name, is skipped.
- **layout** (`lookup_family`): for a font that isn't installed, tries the alternate first. Like Word, the whole value is one name, not a comma-separated list (MS-OE376 2.1.264). The run's East Asian font goes through the same lookup. An alternate is used when it is installed, has substitutes of its own, or is Calibri (the generic sans list is Calibri's: Carlito first). Then comes the roman rule (Cambria, #1613), then `resolve()` as before.
- **fonts**: `has_own_substitutes`, the same function and position as #2504, so the two merge cleanly.
- The run's font name is unchanged and the font table is written back as before (#770), so a saved file keeps the original name and its `altName`.

## Rule order, measured in Word 2024 for Windows (16.0.17932)
A synthetic five-paragraph fixture, each paragraph in a font no machine has. Font embedded in Word's PDF, and in WordCraft's before and after:

| | Font table entry | Word 2024 | main | this PR |

title: fix: a dragged picture, shape or text box is no longer left behind on its page
author: GavinQiEr
body:
<!--
Paste-ready PR text for https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft (branch: main @ eae2421).
Everything below the rule is the PR body. The image line is a placeholder: drag
upstream-mid-drag.png (same folder) into the GitHub editor to upload it. Full command transcript:
verify-log-main.txt in the same folder.

---

## What the user sees

Press a picture, shape or text box and drag it — floating already, or still inline in the text: the
object shows up **twice**. One copy stays exactly where it was, fully opaque; the other follows the
pointer, lighter. Let go and it snaps back to being a single object at the new place.

## Root cause

Pages are drawn once into a texture and reused. The cache key is
`(page content, view_key(kind of view), raster scale)`:

- `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs:1070` — a page is only rendered again when that key changes
  (`fresh` is false);
- `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs:614` — `view_key()` hashes marks, dark mode, page colour, watermark,
  dimming and media. **It has no notion of a drag.** So while an object is dragged, the page's
  raster is still the one drawn with the object in place, at full opacity;
- `crates/ui-egui/src/objects.rs:209` — when the drag first moves, the preview is made once: the
  object drawn alone (`objects.rs:461`), then painted under the pointer at
  `PREVIEW_OPACITY = 170` (`objects.rs:33`, `objects.rs:535`).

Two drawings of the same object: the cached page still has it where it was, and the preview draws
it again under the pointer. Nothing was ever asked to leave it out of the page.

This is not the same bug as #1010 / #1097 (that fix made the *preview* the object alone instead of
a cut of the page); it is the second copy, on the page itself.

## Fix

Leave **exactly one object** out of **one page** while it is being moved, and let the preview stand
in for it:

- `crates/layout/src/display.rs` — `DisplayOptions::hide_object: Option<Pos>`; `page_display()`
  resolves it once into a `Hidden` (the object's ide…

title: LanguageTool: key results by run languages too — same text with different language marks, mixed-language paragraphs (#2679, #763)

#672 now stores LanguageTool results by paragraph text plus the checker language, which already stops two identical paragraphs in different single languages from overwriting each other. This PR keeps what #672 does not cover:

title: File: recovery keeps each picture once per record, as a file, and doesn't retry a size failure until the document changes (#2624, #2625)
author: asystemoffields
body:
Closes #2624, closes #2625. Follow-up to #2456 and #586 (part of #518).

**Builds on #2101 and #2102 and should land after them.** This branch is #2102's head with #2101's head merged in (their only conflict, the `docs/recovery.md` paragraph and the `ROADMAP.md` status line and log rows, resolved keeping both), plus one commit. Once both land, its diff against `main` is that commit alone. Reviewing that commit (`git show HEAD`) shows only what this PR adds.

This is the design @arcanii proposed in #2624, built as proposed. We had already built it in our fork; this is that work adapted to `main` as it stands with #2101 and #2102. The fork also encrypts copies of password-protected documents. That is a separate concern and is left out here: a protected document still gets no recovery copy, as on `main`.

**What was wrong**

1. **No copy for documents with large pictures (#2624).** A snapshot held every picture inside its JSON, and `MAX_BYTES` (256 MiB) capped that JSON. With byte arrays, any document with more than about 70 MB of pictures got no recovery copy. With #2101's base64 the cut-off moves to about 190 MB, but it is still there.
2. **Every snapshot rewrote every picture.** A snapshot that did fit still wrote, then read back and decoded, every picture at every interval.
3. **Failures retried at every interval (#2625).** `poll` cleared `revision` on any error. A snapshot over the limit was written again every interval, up to 256 MB each time, even when nothing had changed. #2102's pacing spaces these attempts out but doesn't stop them.

**What changed** (`crates/engine/src/recovery/desktop.rs`, `recovery.rs`)

1. **Parts as files.** A version 2 snapshot moves `Document::media` and `Document::passthrough` out of its JSON. Each part is written once per record as `parts/<sha256>` (temporary file, `sync_all`, rename, then a directory sync), the first time a snapshot needs it. The JSON names it: `"parts": {"media": {"media/image1.png": {"part": "<sha256>", "len": N}}…

title: #1270: pasted HTML blockquote is an indented paragraph, not Quote
author: benandez
body:
## Cause

Not ribbon-specific: Ctrl+V, the ribbon's Paste and the context menu's Paste all run the same command (`edit.paste` → `paste_fragment` → `rich_fragment`), and the clipboard's HTML wins over its RTF.

The clipboard dump in the issue shows the real trigger. LibreOffice puts a paragraph indented on both sides on the clipboard as HTML `<blockquote>`, with its margins in the page's stylesheet (`blockquote { margin-left: 1cm; margin-right: 1cm }`). Our HTML reader maps `<blockquote>` to the **Quote** style, which is centred, italic and grey. That is why the paragraph that differs from the others came out italic and centred. The first pasted paragraph merges into the paragraph at the caret and takes its formatting, which is why the problem seemed to depend on the paragraph's position.

## Change

- **Paste only** (Paste, and Paste Special > HTML): a pasted `<blockquote>` becomes a Normal paragraph indented on both sides. The indents come from the payload's `<style>` `blockquote` margins (`margin-left`/`margin-right`/`margin`), else 0.5 in each side. Bold and other run formatting are kept. (`crates/engine/src/cmd/paste.rs`: `import_html`, `blockquote_margins`)
- Opening an `.html` file still maps `<blockquote>` to Quote, so HTML import and export round-trip as before.
- `html::css_len_pt` is now `pub` so paste can reuse it.
- Clipboard HTML is hostile input: the scan is linear and bounded by the existing 16 MB paste cap, slices are taken only with `get`, and indents are clamped to 0–22 in.
- Docs: `docs/file-format-parity.md` (HTML row and revision history), ROADMAP progress log.

## Tests

- `pasted_blockquote_is_an_indented_paragraph_not_a_quote`: a synthetic LibreOffice-style CF_HTML payload (plain paragraph, bold `<blockquote>`, plain paragraph), pasted with Paste and with Paste Special > HTML. It asserts the paragraph is not Quote, not centred and not italic, stays bold, and is indented 1 cm left and 2 cm right as the stylesheet says. Without a stylesheet the…

title: Layout: a line can break after a hyphen before a digit, like Word (#2712)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #2712.

Word breaks a line right after a hyphen-minus even when a digit follows (`2016-` / `2022`); WordCraft never did — UAX #14's LB25 (`HY × NU`) suppresses that opportunity, so a range like `2016-2022` moved whole or split inside a number.

## The change

`crates/layout/src/para.rs` takes its break opportunities from `unicode_linebreak::linebreaks` and already overrides UAX #14 where Word differs (no break right after a `/` before a letter or digit). This adds the sibling override in the other direction: the position after a `-` (U+002D) followed by an ASCII digit is a break opportunity again.

Scoped exactly as the issue asks: only U+002D before ASCII digits is added here — a non-breaking hyphen (U+2011) and a minus sign (U+2212) stay unbreakable, other dashes keep their ordinary UAX #14 breaks, and soft hyphens / automatic hyphenation are untouched. The spec is unconditional, so a space-preceded `"-2016"` now wraps as `-` / `2016` — which is Word's behaviour too (the issue's own sweep shows `Deed is -` / `2022`), even where the hyphen reads as a minus sign.

## Validation

- New layout test `a_hyphen_before_digits_is_a_break_opportunity_like_word` sweeps the text width over `Deed 2016-2022` and pins the first wrap: it must break after the hyphen (`Deed 2016-` / `2022`), like the Word column of the issue's table — not move the range whole (`Deed ` / `2016-2022`, which is exactly what main produced) and not split inside a number. A second test pins the scope: with U+2011 or U+2212 the first wrap stays at the space and the range moves whole.
- `docs/layout-parity.md` (line-breaking row, revision history) and the ROADMAP progress log updated per the project's doc obligations.
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout` green (333 passed — including the slash override, kinsoku, auto-hyphenation and justification tests around the same code); `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` clean; full `cargo xtask ci` run — the only failu…

title: #2726: AccessKit focus guard — every tree update carries its focused node
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2726.

`accesskit_consumer`'s `validate_global` panics on the UI thread when a `TreeUpdate`'s focus is not in its node list (`Focused ID #… is not in the node list`), which closes the window on Windows. egui can send an update that drops a focused widget's node, and a screen reader's focus request can target a node the next frame no longer carries.

**Fix:** the `a11y::FocusGuard` plugin runs on every update egui produces, before it reaches the adapter: a focus the update does not carry falls back to the root, so the reader starts from the top of the document instead of the process dying. Registered from `WordApp::logic`, so desktop, web and ui_shot all get it.

**Red without the fix:** the raw update breaks `accesskit_consumer::Tree::new` (the consumer 0.35.0 the Windows adapter runs, pinned as a dev-dep to the version kittest already brings into the tree).

**Tests:**
- `a_focus_the_update_does_not_carry_falls_back_to_the_root` — the raw update panics, the guarded one is accepted.
- `every_update_the_app_sends_is_valid_for_the_consumer` — idle frames, typing, lists, tables and a screen reader focus request feed the real consumer without breaking its contract.

Gates: `cargo xtask ci` green (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm); ui-egui 553 tests. ROADMAP progress log row.

  * Improved accessibility focus handling so screen-reader focus requests remain reliable across app updates and frames.

title: #2729: Layout tests use pinned bundled fonts
author: vangel76
body:

`wordcraft-fonts/test-support` exposes a one-time initializer that must run before any global lookup. The fixed families are Source Sans 3, Source Serif 4, Inter and JetBrains Mono. Carlito is not required: its optional integration is still in #1024, and relying on it would leave clean checkouts without the fixture. The default Aptos request therefore uses the existing Source Sans 3 substitute. These are fixed metrics, not Calibri metrics. Existing guards for scripts not covered by these fonts still apply; details and the setup convention are in `docs/testing.md`.

Two pagination fixtures needed adjustment: the floating table's empty filler count, and the minimum-height row's filler count. The latter now uses a pinned count instead of deriving its available room from layout. The widow sweep shifts the filler immediately before the target paragraph. body:
Count a preceding row's painted bottom border when the next cell has no visible top border.

- Include the band in text clearance and minimum row height instead of making the table too short.
- Match overlapping grid spans and exclude internal vertical-merge edges.
- Preserve exact row heights and borderless tables.

This corrects downstream keep-with-next decisions without changing keep-chain rules.

Existing border conflict selection remains. When combining with #2607, retain the effective band in `CellPart.top` for split rows. No document-specific offsets or private fixtures are included.

title: Hungarian proofing: hu_HU (Magyar Ispell) spelling via spellbook
author: Jano79
body:
Before: Hungarian text gets no spelling marks. The Hungarian interface exists, but Review › Language has no Hungarian entry, and new documents in the Hungarian interface aren't tagged as Hungarian.

After: Hungarian runs (`hu`, `hu-HU`, `hun`) are spell-checked against the installed Hunspell `hu_HU` dictionary (Magyar Ispell). The dictionary is read at runtime and never bundled, like the Polish, Czech and Italian ones. You get squiggles, F7, suggestions (`helyesirás` → `helyesírás`, `szamitogep` → `számítógép`) and generic grammar checks with Hungarian messages. Review › Language and Options › Proofing list Hungarian. The status bar shows "Hungarian (no dictionary)" when `hu_HU` is missing. The Hungarian interface writes new documents in `hu-HU`.

Magyar Ispell relies on compounding (`COMPOUNDFLAG`, `COMPOUNDRULE`, `ONLYINCOMPOUND`…), flag aliases (`AF`/`AM`), `NEEDAFFIX` and `ICONV`. `affix.rs` deliberately rejects all of these. Rather than grow the affix engine, the dictionary is read by [spellbook](https://github.com/helix-editor/spellbook). It is a pure-Rust, Hunspell-compatible checker (MPL-2.0, no C dependency), and it is used only by the new `hu` module.

**How**
- `crates/proof/src/hu/`: the dictionary handling, mirroring `cs` (`dictionary`, `install_dictionary`, `reload_dictionary`, `installed_path`, `is_correct`, `suggest`). There is also a `grammar.rs` with the generic repeated-word and spacing checks in Hungarian.
- **Magyar Ispell quirk:** the `.aff` says `SET UTF-8`, but its ~250 flags are raw bytes, mostly above 0x7F (`SFX \xff Y 3`), and its header comments are ISO 8859-2. So the file isn't valid UTF-8, and a lossy decode would merge distinct flags. `byte_flags_to_long` rewrites every flag field (`AF`, `PFX`/`SFX`, flag directives, `COMPOUNDRULE`) as two hex characters under `FLAG long`. `FLAG num` would also work in Hunspell, but spellbook skips the `AF` alias lookup for numeric flags. I checked with `hunspell -l` that the rewritten file gives the s…

title: Layout: build author colour index once; binary-search STYLEREF (WC-10, WC-26)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Two quadratic hot paths in `wordcraft-layout` from the security audit. Rendered output is unchanged.

**WC-10: author colour index rebuilt per tracked run (#2754).** `display.rs` recomputed a revision's author index for every tracked run and tracked paragraph mark. Each time it walked all revisions with a `Vec::contains` dedupe, so painting cost tracked runs × revisions × distinct authors. `balloons::add` did the same for every comment balloon. Now `page_display` and `object_display` create a small `Authors` helper that builds a per-revision index once, lazily, on the first tracked change drawn. Pages without markup pay nothing. `balloons::add` builds the comment author map once. Colours stay the same: authors are numbered by first appearance, and an unknown revision is author 0. Tests: `author_indices_follow_first_appearance` checks the numbering for revisions and comments. `many_revision_authors_paint_quickly_in_their_colours` paints 20,000 revisions by distinct authors with 600 tracked runs: about 94 s with the old code, well under the 5 s bound now, and every author colour still appears. `many_comment_authors_lay_out_balloons_quickly` lays out 200 balloons with 20,200 comment authors.

**WC-26: STYLEREF in headers is fields × pages × paragraphs (#2767).** `StyleIndex::eval` walked the body entries backwards and then forwards for every header STYLEREF on every page, on each layout pass. `StyleIndex` now keeps the ascending list of entries for each paragraph style and each character style. `eval` finds the first candidate in the same search order (on the page, first or last with `\l`; else the nearest before; else the nearest after; for body fields, at or before, then after) with `partition_point`. The old walk stays as a `#[cfg(test)]` reference, `eval_scan`. Tests: `indexed_search_matches_the_walk` compares the two for 12 instructions × about 1,900 positions. These cover paragraph and character styles, `\l`, `\p`, `\n`, `\s`, heading levels, missing styles, page…

title: Bound formats importers: ODT spaces, Markdown tables and inlines, trim, font names and links (WC-04/05/09/16/17)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Fixes five findings from the security audit (#2744) in the `formats` importers: amplification bombs and quadratic hangs that hostile `.odt`, `.md`, `.html`, `.rtf` or `.tex` input (or a paste) could trigger. Each fix has its own commit and regression test. **WC-04: ODT `` had no total expansion budget** (`odt.rs`). Each tag was clamped to 1000 spaces, but nothing capped the total, so a 6 KB file expanded to over 100 MB and a larger one aborted out of memory. All the `text:s` tags in a document now share a 4 Mi-space budget (`MAX_SPACES`). Once it's spent, each tag gives one space, which is no more than the tag's own size in the file. Test: `odt::tests::space_runs_have_a_document_budget` (10,000 × `c="1000"`; checks the exact total, and that ordinary tags before and after the flood still behave). **WC-05: Markdown table rows were padded to the header's width before any cap** (`markdown.rs`). Every body row was resized to the header's column count and turned into cells. `MAX_COLS` and `MAX_ROWS` only applied later, in `to_doc`. Now the column count is cut to `MAX_COLS` as soon as the header matches its delimiter row. Rows past `MAX_ROWS` still count as part of the table but no longer produce cells. Test: `markdown::tests::tables_are_capped_before_cells_are_made` (a 50,000-column header, and a table with `MAX_ROWS + 100` rows). **WC-09: Leading-whitespace trim was quadratic** (`model.rs`). `Para::trim_with` dropped each leading blank span with `Vec::remove(0)`. Blank spans in alternating formats don't merge (`

`… from HTML, ODT or LaTeX, including paste), so this was O(n²). The blank spans are now removed with a single `drain`. Test: `model::tests::trim_drops_many_leading_blank_spans_at_once` (200,000 spans, plus edge cases: a leading non-text inline, an all-blank paragraph). **WC-16: Font names and link targets of any length were copied into every run** (RTF, HTML, Markdown, ODT, LaTeX). The fix caps them at the source with two …

title: Bound embedded fonts: check WOFF1 sizes before decoding, cap faces per file (WC-07, WC-18)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Two fixes from the security audit for fonts that a document embeds (`load_embedded_fonts` runs on every docx open). Both changes stay inside `crates/fonts`.

**WC-07: WOFF1 is now size-checked before it is decompressed (#2751).** `wuff::decompress_woff1` calls `Vec::with_capacity(orig_length)` for each table, with `orig_length` taken from the file. `decode_font_file` only compared the decoded output with `MAX_DECODED_BYTES` after decoding, so a few bytes of zlib could make it reserve gigabytes. `decode_font_file` now reads the WOFF1 header and table directory first (`woff1_sfnt_size`). It refuses the file with `TooLarge` when `totalSfntSize`, or the sfnt header plus directory plus every table padded to 4 bytes, comes to more than 128 MB. Each table counts the larger of `origLength` and `compLength`, because the decoder copies a stored table whole. A cut-off directory is reported as `BadWebFont`. Test: `woff1_sizes_are_checked_before_unwrapping` builds the WOFF1 files in code and covers four cases: one table claiming 2 GB behind an 8-byte zlib stream, four 40 MB tables that add up to more than the cap, a header that lies about its size, and a truncated directory. All four are refused without decoding. A real font still unwraps.

**WC-18: limits on the faces read from one font file (#2761).** `enumerate_faces` turned every member of a TTC, and every named instance of a variable font, into a face. A file could declare millions of members that share one table directory. Named instances were deduplicated with an O(n²) scan. In `add_fonts`, each new face was checked against every face already loaded. The 256-faces-per-file limit only applied to fonts the user installs.
- `enumerate_faces` now returns at most `MAX_FACES_PER_FILE` (256) faces. Collection members and named instances count against the same limit, and the faces come back in file order. Each file also looks at no more than 1024 named instances, because an instance whose name is missing or repeated costs a `name…

title: docbin: bound .doc tab stops, hyperlink targets, repeated anchors and picture decode work (WC-11..14)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Security-audit fixes for the legacy `.doc` (docbin) reader: four places where a small hostile file could cost minutes of CPU or gigabytes of memory. One commit per finding, each with a regression test built synthetically in code (no Word-produced files).

**WC-11: uncapped style tab stops, re-applied per child style (#2755).** Each `sprmPChgTabsPapx` adds up to 64 stops, but nothing capped how many sprms a papx holds, so one style could pile up tens of thousands of stops, and each new stop scanned all the others. `stylesheet()` also re-walked the whole base chain for each of up to 4,096 styles. Tab stops are now capped at Word's 64 (`fmt::MAX_TABS`, `Clear` stops included). Each style is now resolved once, as its parent's resolved properties plus its own grpprls, memoised by istd. A base cycle is cut where it closes. This replaces the old 16-deep chain walk, so deeper chains now inherit fully. Tests: `style_tab_stops_are_capped_and_each_style_resolved_once` builds a ~64 KB tab papx base with 2,047 children plus a 2,048-deep chain. It checks that every style has at most 64 stops, that inheritance reaches the root, and that the run takes under 5 s (in practice about 0.1 s). `style_cycles_resolve_without_looping` covers cycles.

**WC-12: HYPERLINK target cloned per result character (#2756).** The target was cloned into every result character's props and compared again on each push. That is O(target × result), and neither part was capped. Field instructions are now capped at 8 KB. The target is set once per run of equally formatted result text, through a new `ParaBuild::push_str` that does one comparison per run. The first run's copy is already paid for by the instruction's characters. Each later run's copy is charged against the walk budget, and once that budget is spent the rest of the result stays as unlinked text. Test: `hyperlink_target_is_capped_and_set_once_per_run` uses a 20 KB URL over a result whose formatting alternates on every character. It checks that the …

title: Harden automation file access: UNC/device paths, checked-path I/O, dictionariesFolder, PNG-only export, app --automation-*-root
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Hardens what automation (the MCP server and the desktop app's control channel) can reach on disk. Part of the security audit tracked in #2744.

### WC-01 (#2745): unconfined agent file access; `file.exportPng` writes any path
- **Problem:** `file.exportPng {"path": "~/.bashrc"}` replaced any file with PNG bytes; the desktop app's control channel (and so `mcp --connect`) could not be confined at all; the `open_document` tool description invited agents to open "any other text file".
- **Change:** `file.exportPng` requires a `.png` extension (any case), and so does `ui.screenshot`, which now writes through `io::write_file` (roots, safe save). The Export dialog adds `.png` to a name typed without it, so people are not affected. `wordcraft --control PORT --automation-read-root DIR --automation-write-root DIR` holds every control-channel request to those folders, parsed by the same parser as `wordcraft-cli mcp` (a malformed flag, a missing folder, or roots without `--control` exit with status 2). Control requests always run inside `file_access::confine`. The `open_document` description no longer says "any other text file". `docs/mcp.md` and `docs/control-protocol.md` document the app flags and say plainly that the default is unconfined.
- **Also (audit Minor):** `file.exportPng`'s page index uses `usize::try_from(..).unwrap_or(usize::MAX).saturating_sub(1)`, so a huge page on a 32-bit target is "no page" instead of wrapping. The identical MCP site (`crates/mcp/src/lib.rs:49`) is left to the MCP PR.
- **Tests:** `export_png_writes_only_png_files` (engine), `control_requests_are_held_to_the_automation_roots` and the screenshot check (ui-egui), `root_flags_open_the_roots_or_refuse_to_start` (app).
- **Not done here, proposed as a follow-up:** making the headless MCP server confined by default (for example to the working directory, with an explicit `--unconfined`). That changes behaviour for every existing MCP client config, so it is a maintainer decision. Hence `Refs #2745` …

title: Audit F: hyperlink and export safety (WC-20, WC-28, WC-29, WC-30, WC-38)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Security-audit fixes for hyperlinks and export (PR "F" of the audit tracker).

**WC-20 (#2762), PDF link schemes.** PDF export wrote every hyperlink target as a URI action, including `javascript:`, `file:` and UNC (`\\host\share`) targets. Every other exporter already filters through `wordcraft_doc::link::is_safe_href`. The PDF exporter now does the same, so an unsafe target keeps its text and loses its link. Test: `pdf::tests::unsafe_link_targets_are_not_exported` exports `javascript:`, `\\host\…`, `//host/…`, `file:` and `ms-msdt:` links plus one https link. It checks that the uncompressed PDF bytes contain none of the unsafe targets and still contain the https `/URI`. The test fails without the fix.

**WC-28 (#2769), strict link parsing.** Ctrl/⌘+click only compared the scheme before `:`, then handed the raw string to `webbrowser`. When `Url::parse` fails, `webbrowser` retries the string as a local file path. So `http://x:99999/../../home/u/Downloads/evil.html` could open a local file. The `url` crate is in the tree only through eframe's `webbrowser`, which is native-only. I did not add it to the L1 `doc` crate. Instead, `wordcraft_doc::link::followable_link` is a careful hand-rolled parser that returns a normalised string:
- `http`/`https` must be followed by `//` and a valid host: domain labels, an exact dotted-quad IPv4 (no octal or hex forms) or a bracketed IPv6.
- The port, if any, must be in 1–65535.
- User info (`good@evil`) and backslashes are refused.
- Spaces, non-ASCII and stray `%` in the path, query and fragment are percent-encoded.
- Control characters, surrounding whitespace and links over 8 KiB are refused.

On native builds, `ui-egui` then parses the result once more with `url::Url` (the parser `webbrowser` uses), adding it as a native-only dependency that was already in the lockfile. It requires http(s) with a host, or mailto, and opens `parsed.as_str()`. An IDN host is punycoded by that parser, so nothing `webbrowser` can't parse ever reaches i…

title: Harden the MCP bridge and control channel (WC-03, WC-31, audit minors)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Security-audit fixes for the MCP bridge and the control channel.

**WC-03 (#2747): the bridge sent the control key to any loopback peer.** `may_send_key` accepted any loopback peer, so `[::1]` and `127.0.0.2` counted, and `localhost` could resolve to `::1` first. The app binds `127.0.0.1` only (`apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs`), and any local user can bind those other addresses on the same port without privileges. Now the key goes only when the `--connect` address names `127.0.0.1` (also as `::ffff:127.0.0.1`) or `localhost`, *and* the connected peer is exactly `127.0.0.1`. `localhost` is no longer resolved: it connects to `127.0.0.1` only. The warning text and the docs say this. The `may_send_key` test table now refuses `[::1]`, `127.0.0.2` and `localhost` → `[::1]`. New tests: `localhost_means_127_0_0_1_only` (a pure check of the connect targets) and `no_key_to_a_listener_on_ipv6_loopback` (a real `[::1]` listener never sees a key; skipped where there is no IPv6). Follow-up, out of scope here: challenge-response (an HMAC over a server nonce), so the key never travels on the wire.

**Minor: key file ACL on Windows (finishes WC-03).** The key file was mode 0600 on Unix only. On Windows it inherited the folder's ACL. That is fine under `%APPDATA%`, but not when `WORDCRAFT_PROFILE_DIR` points to a shared folder. Setting a DACL directly needs `unsafe` Win32 calls, and no safe wrapper is in `Cargo.lock`. So the key-file writing moved into `wordcraft-control-key` (`write_key_file`, `make_private`), which runs the system's own tools by absolute path from `%SystemRoot%\System32`, never through `PATH`, with no console window and a 10 s timeout:
- `whoami.exe /user /fo csv /nh` gives the user's SID. It is used only if it parses as `S-` followed by digits and dashes.
- `icacls <file> /reset` drops explicit entries. On this machine a sandbox service adds one to every new file, so `/inheritance:r` alone left a second entry.
- `icacls <file> /inheritance:r /grant:r *<SID>:…

title: CI #1358: guard mutable workflow refs and document shared-release trust
author: maxm11
body:
## Summary

Part of #1358. The release workflow calls `storytold/craft-common-actions` at `@main` on purpose (the decision is recorded in storytold/craft-common-actions#6; re-litigating it here would just reopen a closed decision). This PR makes that exception explicit and enforceable, fixes the one remaining unpinned third-party action, and documents the controls the shared branch needs.

Prior-work check: #1358 overlaps [craft-common-actions#6](https://github.com/storytold/craft-common-actions/issues/6) (closed as intentional) and [craft-common-actions#7](https://github.com/storytold/craft-common-actions/issues/7) (open; signing secrets during build and `contents: write`). This PR does not duplicate #7.

## What changed

- `cargo xtask workflows` scans `.github/workflows/*.yml` and rejects any external `uses:` that is not a full 40-character commit SHA or an immutable Docker `sha256:` digest. Local `./` actions pass. The command is part of `cargo xtask ci`.
- `packaging-lint.yml` has a `workflow-refs` job that runs the check on PRs and pushes that touch workflows, so the guard is enforced before merge.
- The four intentional `storytold/craft-common-actions@main` calls are the only allowlisted exception, in `xtask/src/workflows.rs`, with the reason and links to #1358 and craft-common-actions#6.
- `printing.yml` used `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`; it now uses the same pinned SHA as the shared workflows (`683b588c...`, v1) with `toolchain: stable`. This was the last unpinned third-party ref.
- `docs/releasing.md` documents the shared-workflow trust model: what is pinned, what is intentionally mutable, why pinning the caller alone would not freeze the shared workflow's own `@main` composite actions, and the branch-protection/review controls the shared repository needs.
- `README.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and `AGENTS.md` list the new gate with the rest of `cargo xtask ci`.

title: Engine work budgets for Finish & Merge and regex Find; normalise recovery restores (WC-27, WC-33, WC-37)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Three security-audit fixes in the engine: work budgets for Finish & Merge and regex Find, and the run repair for recovery restores that `.json` documents already get.

**WC-27 (#2768): Finish & Merge amplification.** `MAX_MERGED_BLOCKS` counted only top-level blocks, and every record deep-copied the body (`merge_blocks` calls `Arc::make_mut` on every block). So one big table or a megabyte paragraph, merged over up to 100k records, could need tens of GB. `finish` now:
- sizes one copy with `merge_units`: text bytes, plus one per paragraph and one per table cell, nested tables included, as deep as the merge goes;
- multiplies that by the copies (records, divided down by unconditional NEXT fields) and refuses before copying anything above 50M units;
- also counts what it actually copies, merged field values and per-letter header/footer copies included.

The error tells the user to merge fewer records with From and To. The old block cap stays. Tests: a 1 MB paragraph over 100 records, a 200 × 50 table over 3000 records (2 top-level blocks per copy, so the old cap never fired) and 11 records of 5 MB values are all refused, and the document is left unchanged. A From/To range that fits still merges.

**WC-33 (#2773): regex Find has no work budget.** Building the pattern now goes through `find_pattern::Compiled::matcher`, which also builds the Thompson NFA to count its states. Before searching anything, `search_full` refuses a search whose story bytes × NFA states exceed 2^34. That is the PikeVM worst case: measured at about 2·10⁹ to 7·10⁹ state-bytes per second, so 2–8 s at most natively. Before this, `(?:[^\r]{0,99}\b){9}\p{Lu}{2}` (Unicode `\b` over Cyrillic, so PikeVM) took 11 s per Find on a 3 MB paragraph here. Now it is refused in milliseconds.
- **NFA limit not lowered:** I measured the suggested ~64 KB against everyday patterns. 64 KB rejects a 1000-character literal and Ignore punctuation on any phrase over about 16 characters. 512 KB still rejects a 90-character …

title: docx reader limits: attribute caps, one part per name, bounded zip reads, linear scans (WC-06/08/23/24/25/39)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Fixes the docx-reader findings from the security audit (#2744). Each one was checked in the code before it was fixed. Every change is in `crates/docx`, apart from the few lines in the engine's `file.open` that show WC-23's report of unreadable parts. Each comes with a regression test.

**WC-06: no attribute cap per XML element.** `xml::parse` capped nesting and element count but not attributes, and it reads them with `with_checks(false)`. So one element with millions of duplicate attributes built a tree hundreds of times the size of the part. The parser now refuses more than 1,024 attributes on one element and more than 16M in one part (`DocxError::Limit`). Parsed chart and diagram trees stay alive for the whole read, so they are also capped at 32 MB of input per file (`MAX_GRAPHIC_PART_BYTES`). Test: `xml::tests::attribute_floods_are_refused` (one element over the cap, and many elements that add up).

**WC-08: case-variant part names defeated the caches.** `Package::get` matched names case-insensitively, but the reader's caches (pictures, charts and diagrams, kept parts, headers and footers) were keyed by the target as written. N spellings of one 256 MB part therefore made N copies, and a save wrote case-duplicate zip entries. Now:
- The package keeps one part per lowercased name. A case-duplicate entry is dropped and logged.
- Names resolve through a lowercase index (`Package::canonical`).
- Part bytes are handed out as a shared `Arc` (`Package::shared`), not copied.
- Every cache and the kept-part manifest (including the VBA-related parts) uses the stored name.

Tests: `package::tests::case_variant_names_are_one_part`, plus `tests/reader_limits.rs`:
- 64 spellings of one picture give `doc.media.len() == 1`, and the saved package has no case-duplicate entries.
- A chart reached through 16 spellings is one graphic.

**WC-23: failed zip entries were not charged against the total.** An entry that inflated in full and then failed its CRC was skipped before its bytes w…

title: WC-21: guard every command step and make the never-panic test detect caught panics
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Problem

Audit finding WC-21: the never-panic safety net and the test meant to prove it had gaps.

- `Session::run` turns a panic caught in a command body into `Err(CmdError::Failed("{id} panicked: …"))`. `hostile_params_never_panic` threw that result away (`let _ = s.run(spec.id, j);`), so **it passed even when a command panicked**. It only failed on panics outside `catch_unwind`.
- Some code that runs on every command was outside `catch_unwind`: `(spec.enabled)(self)`, `protect::check_before`, and the post-command bookkeeping (`protect::outside_unchanged`, `fmt_revisions::record`, `connectors::reroute`, `clamp_selection`, `outline::after_command`). A panic in any of these crashed the app.
- The test skipped `file.*`, `insert.picture` and `insert.textFromFile`. Its junk values had no huge counts, no long strings and no file paths.

## Changes

**`crates/engine/src/session.rs`**
- New `guarded(id, f)` helper wraps `catch_unwind` and produces the existing `"{id} panicked: {msg}"` error, so the message format is unchanged.
- The `enabled` check and the Restrict Editing pre-check now run inside `guarded`. Neither one mutates the session.
- The post-command bookkeeping now runs inside its own `guarded` block, together with the protection diff that was already there. Behaviour does not change when nothing panics: a protection violation is still `Disabled` and rolls back. If the bookkeeping panics, the result becomes the panic error and the usual rollback runs (document, selection, undo/redo stacks, typing group, evictions, column state). The dirty flag goes back to its value before the bookkeeping, the equation-edit state is dropped, and for a non-mutating command the selection goes back to where it was before the command.
- Under `cfg(test)`, every caught panic is also recorded in a per-thread log (`take_caught_panics()`). Panics in nested commands are recorded too, even when the outer command throws away the inner error.

title: Interface font setting, with the system font through fontconfig on Linux (#1375)
author: maxm11
body:

- **File › Options › General now has an Interface font setting** (`ui.interfaceFont`): Inter (the embedded default), System default, or any installed family. The choice is saved in `ui.json` and survives restarts.

title: #1503: touch screens pan with one finger; a long press selects (#2155)
author: maxm11
body:
## What changed

Touch input arrives twice: `Event::Touch` and the pointer events eframe/egui-winit synthesize from it. The scroll path only read `MouseWheel`, so a finger produced no scroll, and `canvas::mouse()` treated every primary press as a caret plus drag-select. This adds one shared gesture in `ui-egui`:

- **Pan** — a one-finger drag follows the finger 1:1 and coasts on release. It has its own `Momentum`, so it works on the web, macOS and Windows where the system sends no momentum for a touch screen.
- **Tap** — still places the caret (on press, as before).
- **Long press** — holding still for `InputOptions::max_click_duration` starts a selection; dragging then extends it.
- **Pinch** — a second finger hands the gesture to the existing pinch zoom and puts back the selection the first finger's press replaced.
- **Read Mode** — horizontal finger travel turns reading columns.

The web wrinkle is handled too: eframe runs a frame inside `pointerdown`, which comes before `touchstart`, so a press is remembered and adopted when its `Touch Start` arrives a frame later; the text drag it started is cancelled, and the selection it replaced is restored if the finger pans. A pointer release can arrive before `touchend` (web) or with `PointerGone` (native), so its click/double-click still run — double-tap still selects a word.

## Tests

- Unit tests for the gesture: 1:1 pan and coast, tap, long press, pinch cancelling, web adoption, hostile numbers.
- App-level kittest coverage for both event orders: native drag pans without selecting; web drag adopts the `pointerdown` frame and keeps the selection; tap places the caret; long press + drag selects; double-tap selects a word (including a native release with `PointerGone`); pinch zooms without selecting; mouse drag is unchanged; reading-column turns.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, workspace tests, assets, layers, wasm).

title: Keytips: right Alt (AltGr) never arms keytips, so AltGr+letter types (ą, ę, ł) on Linux
author: avengerpol
body:
Fix AltGr+letter typing Polish letters (ą, ę, ł…) on Linux
Problem

On Linux, typing a character with AltGr (right Alt) on a Polish layout
doesn't insert it. AltGr+A doesn't type "ą"; the letter goes to the
ribbon keytips instead, and it takes several presses to get the
character. The same layout works in every other application. Left and
right Alt behaved the same way in WordCraft.

Seen on CachyOS with WordCraft 0.7.0 (AppImage), Polish layout, with
and without WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND=1.
Cause

AltGr is level 3 (Mod5), not Alt (Mod1). The backend can send the
AltRight key press and then a ModifiersChanged event without alt
before the letter arrives. alt_transition() reads that as a bare Alt
release, so keytips arm before the letter is typed. While keytips show,
the letter is consumed by them and the Text event is dropped, so
nothing reaches the document.
Fix

In keytips::logic, a right Alt press is treated as part of a chord
(alt_chord_used = true) on platforms other than Windows and macOS, so
it never arms keytips. Windows already reports AltGr as Ctrl+Alt (a
chord), and macOS never arms keytips from Alt.

The left Alt key and F10 still open keytips.

Trade-off: on layouts without AltGr (e.g. US), a right Alt tap no
longer opens keytips. Left Alt does.
Tests

    Added altgr_letter_does_not_arm_keytips: AltRight press, optional
    ModifiersChanged without alt, then a letter, then release; keytips
    must stay off.
    Adjusted native_alt_taps_toggle_once_in_either_event_order: a right
    Alt tap no longer arms keytips (except on Windows/macOS).

Tested manually on CachyOS (Polish layout): AltGr+letter now types
ą, ę, ł, ó, ś, ż, ź, ć, ń as expected.

title: Format Painter: double-click keeps it on, armed and sticky look different (#2785)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2785.

The engine already supports a sticky painter (`edit.formatPainter` with `{"sticky": true}`), but the ribbon always sent `{}`. This PR covers both points of the issue:

- **Double-click keeps it on.** egui reports `clicked()` on both clicks of a double-click, so the first click armed the painter and the second turned it off again. On `double_clicked()` the ribbon now turns off anything left armed and runs `edit.formatPainter` with `{"sticky": true}`. Esc (existing handler in `keys.rs`) or another click on the button turns it off.
- **Armed and sticky look different.** A single-use painter draws only the accent border. A sticky painter uses the full checked look (fill and border) that `small` already draws for toggled buttons, using the same stroke as `widgets::bg`.

The change is only in `crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs`. The engine command and the keytip path are unchanged.

Test: `double_click_on_format_painter_makes_it_sticky` runs the two clicks of a double-click, then the double-click handler, and checks that the painter ends up sticky.

title: Use the Default Paragraph Style font when importing ODT (#2804)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2804.

LibreOffice keeps the body font of a document in the Default Paragraph Style (`style:style style:name="Standard"` in `styles.xml`) or, when the user never changed it, in `style:default-style style:family="paragraph"`. The ODT importer skips the Standard style when it applies paragraph styles to the text and never read `style:default-style`, so the text fell back to the built-in body font (Aptos).

The importer now takes the font from the Standard style, else from the paragraph default style, and sets it as the document's default character font (`styles.default_chr.font`). The text keeps no direct font formatting, and the ODT export already writes `default_chr.font` as the body font, so the font survives a save and reopen. Monospace fonts are not taken as the default, which matches how the style reader treats them (as code formatting).

Test: `default_paragraph_style_font_becomes_document_font` in `crates/formats/src/odt.rs` covers both cases (a font on Standard wins over the default style; with only the default style, its font is used). It fails without the fix.

title: Keep the ODT paragraph 'Keep with next' option on import and export (#2813)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2813.

LibreOffice saves "Keep with next paragraph" as `fo:keep-with-next="always"` on the paragraph style. The ODT reader never read that attribute, so the paragraphs lost the option on import. The writer never wrote it either.

What changed:

- The ODT style reader now reads `fo:keep-with-next`: `always` turns the option on, and `auto` turns it off. The nearest style in the parent chain wins, so a style can switch off what its parent turns on.
- `Para` gets a `keep_next` flag. The builder maps it to `ParaProps.keep_next`, and the ODT export path reads it back from there.
- The ODT writer puts `fo:keep-with-next="always"` on the paragraph's automatic style, next to `fo:break-before`.
- A heading's own style is not counted. WordCraft's built-in Heading styles already keep with next, and this is the same rule the reader uses for the text formatting of kind styles.
- `docs/file-format-parity.md`: the ODT row now lists keep with next.

Test: `keep_with_next_survives_import_and_export` in `odt.rs` imports a paragraph that keeps with next, a child style that turns it off with `auto`, and a plain paragraph. It then exports and imports the document again and checks the flags each time. Without the fix the first paragraph comes in as `None`, so the test fails.

title: fix: dropping an object near the top of the next page no longer sends it back
author: GavinQiEr
body:
## What happens

Drag a floating object (picture, shape or text box) to the **top** of the next page: the preview follows the pointer to page 2, but releasing the mouse puts the object back on page 1. Dropping in the middle of the next page works, which is why this looks inconsistent.

## Root cause

`move_object` (in `crates/engine`) anchors the object to the paragraph under the drop point and computes the offset from that paragraph origin. With a `Square`-wrapped object the text around its old position reflows as soon as it moves, so the first paragraph of the target page - the anchor chosen when dropping near the top - slides back to the previous page, and the object is placed with it.

Measured on a two-page document: `arrange.bounds { page: 1 }` with y = 60/72/95 lands on page 0, while y = 99/105/400/700/760 lands on page 1. So it is not a wrong page number being passed; the placement is undone by the reflow.

## Fix

Split `move_object` into a small wrapper plus `move_object_once`. After placing across pages, check that the object really ended up on the target page and re-anchor if it did not (at most three attempts; each attempt sees the reflow caused by the previous one). Same-page moves still place exactly once, so resize and nudge are unchanged, and if three attempts are not enough the last placement is kept rather than reporting an error.

## Tests

- `objects::tests::a_shape_dragged_onto_the_next_page_is_dropped_there` - a kittest that presses, moves and releases onto the top of the next page and asserts the object stays on the page under the pointer. Fails without the fix (`left: 0 / right: 1`), passes with it.

## Verification

On a clean checkout of `main` with this patch applied:

- `cargo build -p wordcraft-ui-egui` ✅
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui --lib` → `552 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored`
- `cargo check -p wordcraft-ui-egui --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` ✅
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` ✅

title: WC-19: bound picture decodes and page raster area
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Fixes audit finding **WC-19** (no GitHub issue): large pictures were decoded again on every paint, page rasters had no area cap, and PDF export decoded every picture at full size.

**Pictures on screen (`crates/render`).** `decode_pixmap` used the default 512 MB `max_alloc`, then `to_rgba8()` (up to 4× for a grey image) and a premultiplied copy. A pixmap bigger than the cache's half-budget was never cached, so it was decoded again on every paint: a 22000×22000 grey PNG (about 470 KB) cost about 4.3 GB at peak on every repaint. Now the header is read first. The decoder's `max_alloc` is sized from the declared size (16 bytes a pixel plus 16 MB for metadata, never more than the old 512 MB). A picture over the budget is shrunk uniformly as it decodes (`thumbnail_exact`, an averaging filter), so it still shows instead of vanishing. The budget is 24 Mpx (a 24-megapixel photo stays at full size), reduced when the source bytes are large so the pixmap and its source still fit the cache together. That means the shrunk pixmap is cached and decoded only once. A tiled page background keeps its natural tile size when its pixmap was shrunk. Pictures within the budget decode exactly as before (`into_rgba8` now moves an RGBA buffer instead of copying it).

**Page rasters.** `render_page` / `render_region` / `render_items` clamped each side to 16000 but not the area, so one raster could reach 1 GB (and `to_png` copies it again). Rasters are now capped at 64 Mpx (`MAX_RASTER_PIXELS`) by scaling both sides alike. `render_page` lowers the scale so the whole page still fits, and `render_region` / `render_items` scale their view to match as a backstop. Normal pages are unaffected: 64 Mpx is 8192², far more than any page at normal zoom.

**PDF export (`crates/pdf`).** `load_image` decoded every picture (up to 30000², with the default `max_alloc`) and converted it to full-size RGBA. It now uses the same header-sized `max_alloc` and shrinks pictures over 64 Mpx (256 MB of RGBA) before embedd…

title: WC-15: cap total spreadsheet text in recipient lists; linear sheet field names and cell text
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Spreadsheet recipient lists (`crates/formats/src/sheet.rs`, `sheet/xls.rs`): a total-text budget, plus two quadratic/cubic hotspots made linear. No GitHub issues exist for these; audit IDs below.

**WC-15: spreadsheet cell multiplication.** Repeats and shared strings multiplied cell text without a total limit. One ODS cell of 32,767 characters with `number-columns-repeated="1000"` in a row with `number-rows-repeated="1000000"` came to about 2 M cells × 32 KB, roughly 65 GB, when picked as a mail-merge source. XLSX `t="s"` and XLS `LABELSST` cells copied a shared string on every reference in the same way. Now there is `MAX_TOTAL_TEXT` (64 MiB) of cell text in all, and every repeat and every shared-string use counts. `Grid` has a `TextBudget` that `Grid::push` charges for each row copy before making it (the last copy is moved, not cloned). The ODS row builder checks repeated values against what is left before it extends the row. The XLSX sheet walk and XLS `put` charge each kept cell. Once a value doesn't fit, the budget is spent: that row and every row after it are dropped, so the list ends at a row and has no holes, like the existing row and cell caps. Tests: `repeated_long_cells_stop_at_the_text_budget` (the audit's ODS scenario keeps 2 whole rows; a single row of 1,000 × 98 KB is never built), `shared_strings_count_against_the_text_budget_per_use` for XLSX (3,000 references to a 32 K shared string keep 2,048 rows) and XLS (2,100 `LABELSST`s).

**Minor (audit §5): `sheet::field_names` was O(cols³).** Each repeated header retried `Name k` from 2 and rescanned every name taken so far. Now it keeps a set of taken names (ASCII-lowercased) and the next number to try for each base. Every lower number was already taken and still is, so the result is the same and the cost is linear. Test: `field_names_number_repeats_in_linear_time` covers the numbering cases (literal `a 2` headers, case, blanks) and 20,000 identical headers.

title: WC-01: confine headless MCP to the working directory by default
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**This changes default behaviour, and maintainers should decide whether to take it.** Up to now, `wordcraft-cli mcp` with no flags let an agent read and write any file the user can. After this PR it reads and writes only inside its working directory. Anyone whose MCP client starts the server somewhere other than the folder the agent works in (or who relies on the agent opening files elsewhere) has to add `--automation-read-root`/`--automation-write-root`, set the client's `cwd`, or pass `--unconfined`.

This is the rest of WC-01 (audit §5 WC-01, §8.1 item 5). #2805 already did the PNG-only `file.exportPng`, the tool description and `--automation-*-root` for the desktop app's `--control`. This PR makes headless MCP confined by default.

### WC-01: headless MCP is confined by default

**Problem.** Without root flags, the headless server put no limit on paths. A prompt-injected agent could open `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` or `~/.aws/credentials`, read it back with `get_text`, or save over any file the user can write.

**Change** (`apps/wordcraft-cli/src/main.rs` only; `crates/engine/src/file_access.rs` is untouched):
- `wordcraft-cli mcp` with no `--automation-read-root`/`--automation-write-root` now makes the working directory both the read root and the write root (`AutomationRoots::new(Some(cwd), Some(cwd))`). It then runs exactly like `--automation-read-root . --automation-write-root .`: links are followed, `..` is resolved, and `confine_process` applies to every thread.
- `--unconfined` is a new flag that keeps the old behaviour. It is mutually exclusive with the root flags: giving both is a usage error with **exit status 2** (new `Failure::Usage` variant; every other error still exits 1). If the working directory can't be read, the server stops with an error that names both ways out. It never falls back to running unconfined.
- At start, one stderr line names the roots in force (`wordcraft-cli: files confined: read root …, write root …`), or says the server is not confine…

title: WC-40: zip 9, deny.toml + cargo xtask deny, control-key/xtask lints, parser overflow checks
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Audit **WC-40** (Info: dependencies and misc; no GitHub issue): supply-chain hygiene and lint uniformity from audit §3 (`cargo audit`, `cargo deny`) and §8.3.

**zip 3.0.0 → 9.0.5.** `cargo audit` flagged RUSTSEC-2026-0367/0368/0369 in zip 3. None is reachable (WordCraft never calls `ZipArchive::extract`; parts are read into memory), but the upgrade removes them. zip 9's MSRV is 1.88 (workspace: 1.95) and it still builds for wasm32. The only API change we hit is `ZipFile::name()`, which now returns `ZipResult<Cow<str>>` (decoded on demand: UTF-8, else CP437). `docx::Package::open_limited` falls back to a lossy decode of `name_raw()` if decoding fails, so an odd name never fails the document (mechanical, three-line change in `package.rs`). Tests call `.name().unwrap()`. One behaviour difference: zip 9 enforces each entry's declared uncompressed size, so an entry that inflates to more than it declares now fails a byte past its declared size instead of running on to our own budget. That is strictly safer. `odt::tests::pictures_over_the_budget_are_not_inflated` asserted the old behaviour (a lying entry used up the whole picture budget); it now asserts that the lying entry costs at most its declared size + 1 and doesn't block later pictures, and adds a case where the declared size is over the budget. New test `docx/tests/malformed.rs::entry_names_that_are_not_utf8_do_not_stop_the_package` patches an entry name into invalid UTF-8 and checks that the document still opens and writes.

**`deny.toml` + `cargo xtask deny`.** A root `deny.toml`:
- a licence allow-list matching what the tree actually uses (`cargo deny list`): 0BSD, Apache-2.0 (+ LLVM exception), BSD-2/3-Clause, BSL-1.0, ISC, MIT, Unicode-3.0, Unlicense, Zlib. OFL-1.1 and Ubuntu-font-1.0 are allowed only for `epaint_default_fonts`. Copyleft (GPL/LGPL) appears only as an alternative in `OR` expressions, so it is not allowed.
- `[sources]`: unknown registries and git sources are denied, and `allow-git` lists only `…

title: WC-40: keep embedded document fonts per document (no cross-document font leak)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Security audit, Minor finding "Fonts are global and leak" (part of **WC-40**, no GitHub issue).

**Problem.** Opening a document that embeds fonts (`w:embedRegular`…, #1171) added its faces to the process-wide `FontDb` face list. From then on every lookup by family name saw them. So document A's embedded "X" drew, or could pass itself off as, "X" in document B, in any new document, in B's PDF export, and in the character fallback for all text. Because faces are never unloaded (`FaceRef` is a `&'static` handle), the faces also stayed loaded for the rest of the process.

**Change.**
- New `crates/fonts/src/fontdb/document.rs`. Embedded fonts go into a store of their own, kept apart from `faces`. `FontDb::add_document_fonts(files)` now returns a **font scope** (`u32`, 0 = none). The engine stores it in a new non-serialized `Document::font_scope` (`#[serde(skip)]`), set in `io::open_bytes_in`, the one place embedded fonts are loaded.
- Lookups take that scope: `FontDb::face_in` / `has_family_in`, and `word::resolve_in(scope, …)`, which shares `resolve`'s memo with the scope in the key. `word::resolve` is `resolve_in(0, …)`, so it never sees embedded fonts. Layout uses the document's scope for paragraph text, complex-script and East Asian fonts, the roman-font check and text in graphics. Render and PDF use it for the watermark, `format.font` for its East Asian check, and WordArt sizing. The scope is also in layout's `env_hash`, so a cache never reuses another document's faces.
- Inside its own document, behaviour is as before: a face already available (bundled, user or installed) with that family and style is kept, and an embedded face fills in only a family or style nothing else provides.
- On the leak: faces still can't be unloaded, because `FaceRef` stays `&'static`. Making it `Arc` would bring back the shared refcount traffic that made parallel composition scale negatively. So the store is **bounded** instead:
  - Files are deduplicated by content (hashed, then compa…

title: audit minor: docx/docbin hardening (part names, WordML 2003 limits, spin count, .doc fixes)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Fixes the docx/docbin items of the security audit's §5 "Minor" list (no GitHub issues exist for them). Each fix has a regression test.

**audit minor: part names re-emitted unchanged.** Zip entry names were not checked against OPC part-name rules, so a name like `..\..\x` was kept as a single segment and written back into saved zips. That is a zip-slip hazard for other extractors. A new helper, `package::part_name_ok`, rejects empty names and empty segments, segments made only of dots and spaces (`.`, `..`, and `.. `, which Windows trims to `..`), backslashes, a drive letter in the first segment (`C:`) and control characters. The zip read loop skips such entries, `Package::from_parts` (Flat OPC) drops them, and `zip_entries` never writes them. Test: `package::tests::unsafe_part_names_are_dropped_on_read_and_never_written`.

**audit minor: WordML 2003 conversion skipped `MAX_PART`.** The converted parts (document, styles, notes, headers, rels, content types) were stored without any size check; only pictures were counted. Every part now goes through one `Conv::store` that enforces the same per-part and total limits as a zip package. A `convert_limited` variant lets the test use small limits. Test: `wordml2003::tests::converted_parts_obey_the_package_limits`.

**audit minor: quadratic comment ids.** For each comment without a usable numeric id, `read_comments` searched `comment_map.values()` again on every step of the free-id search. A `HashSet` of ids already handed out makes this linear. Test: `fixtures::comments_without_numeric_ids_get_distinct_ids` (5,003 comments, colliding and non-numeric ids).

**audit minor: agile spin count.** Decryption accepted the specification's maximum of 10,000,000 SHA-512 rounds per password attempt. Encrypted packages are now limited to 1,000,000 rounds, ten times the 100,000 that Word and other producers write. Anything higher is refused before any hashing, and `encrypt_with_spin_count` clamps to the same bound so WordCraft never writ…

title: audit minor: quadratic hotspots, attached-template path, web loading error
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Fixes the remaining "Minor" items from the security audit's §5 that have no GitHub issue: four quadratic hotspots, the attached-template path check, and the web loading error. Output stays the same in every case. Each item has a regression test.

**audit minor: print-markup comment quotes** (`crates/formats/src/comments.rs`). `notes` recounted each open comment's quote (`q.chars().count()`) for every character the comment spans. The quote also gained one space per paragraph without any limit, so a comment left open over a long document cost O(chars × paragraphs). The fix keeps a character count next to each quote and stops adding paragraph spaces once the cap is reached. Past the cap no other character is kept, and trailing spaces are removed later anyway, so the quote is unchanged. Tests: `long_open_comments_quote_quickly` (8 open comments over 20,000 paragraphs, under 5 s, quote still the first 200 chars plus "…") and `paragraph_breaks_count_toward_the_quote` (pins the old behaviour where paragraph breaks count toward the cap).

**audit minor: behind-text `insert`** (`crates/layout/src/lib.rs`, the body and outline-view paragraph placement). A paragraph's behind-text objects were added to the front of the page with one `Vec::insert` each, and every insert shifted the whole page. Now one `splice(0..0, behind)` adds them all, in the same order: the later paragraph's objects come first, and each paragraph keeps its own order. This removes the O(k²) cost for one paragraph with k such objects. Remaining: each paragraph that has behind-text objects still moves the items already on its page once. In print layout the page size bounds that; in Web Layout (one long page) it is O(items) per such paragraph, the same order as the existing per-object `covers_text` scan. Making it fully linear would mean changing how pages hold behind-text items, so I left it out. Test: `behind_text_objects_go_in_front_of_the_page_in_order` checks the order across two paragraphs. It also lays ou…

title: CI: make cargo test --workspace green on Windows (colour emoji fallback, locale, recovery and control-server timing)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Makes `cargo test --workspace` pass reliably on a Windows dev machine (German interface, Segoe UI Emoji installed, heavy parallel load). These tests failed or flaked on upstream/main there; see the audit's §3 (#2744).

**Colour emoji fallback (a real bug, render `tests_color_glyphs::emoji_*`).** ✅ (U+2705) was drawn in black. title: fix(macos): skip wgpu indirect validation on Intel Macs so launch no longer exits (#2652)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes storytold/WordCraft#2652

## Problem
On Intel Macs (reported: MacBookAir6,1, Intel HD Graphics 5000, macOS Big Sur 11.7.11, no OCLP), WordCraft 0.7.0 exits on launch. The crash report in the issue shows `MTLCompilerService` aborting in Intel's IGIL backend while wgpu compiles its **indirect-call validation** compute pipeline inside `request_device` (`wgpu_core::indirect_validation: ... Compiler encountered an internal error`, then `Parent device is lost`). Ordinary compute pipelines compile fine on that GPU; only wgpu's indirect-validation shader triggers it.

## Fix
Same approach as PhotoCraft's merged storytold/PhotoCraft#3171: on x86_64 macOS builds, leave `InstanceFlags::VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL` out of the wgpu instance eframe creates. WordCraft issues no indirect draws or dispatches, so nothing depends on that validation. Apple silicon, Windows and Linux keep wgpu's default, and `WGPU_VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL=1` still turns it back on (`.with_env()`).

- `apps/wordcraft/src/graphics.rs`: `skips_indirect_validation` + `configure_indirect_validation`, with a regression test.
- `apps/wordcraft/src/main.rs`: the module is now also compiled on macOS; the skip is applied before eframe creates the instance.

This is an app-side change, not a craft-libs bump: the PhotoCraft fix lives in PhotoCraft's own `gpu_startup.rs`, and WordCraft's craft-libs pin only covers `craft-pdf`/`krilla`.

Not covered here: the macOS 15 / OCLP `-std=metal3.2` rejection class (#2567, #644), which is a different failure.

## Testing
- `cargo test -p wordcraft --bin wordcraft graphics::tests` (Windows host): 6 passed, including the new `intel_macs_skip_the_indirect_validation_shaders`.
- Not run: a macOS build or `cargo xtask ci`, and no test on Intel Mac hardware. A test build for the reporter would confirm the fix.
