title: WC-32: bound Zotero sessions and add Cancel
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Fixes audit finding **WC-32** (Zotero-port squatter; no GitHub issue).

**Problem.** Any local process that binds Zotero's connector port (23116) before Zotero does gets a session with a 1 h idle timeout, unlimited calls, and 32 MiB frames. `Field_setText` / `Document_insertText` payloads are parsed as RTF/HTML on the UI thread, and nothing could end the session: every Zotero button stayed disabled until the peer let go.

**Change.**
- `wordcraft_zotero::client::Limits` (in `Options`) bounds one command: 100,000 frames, 128 MiB received, and 4 MiB for a rich-text call (`Field_setText`, `Document_insertText`). A rich-text call over the limit gets an `ERR:` reply and never reaches the bridge/parser. Going over the call or byte budget ends the session with a protocol error. Every frame counts, including txid-0 frames, so a peer can't flood no-op frames. The numbers leave plenty of room for real use: a refresh makes a few calls per citation, a citation code is a few KB, and a bibliography entry is a few hundred bytes of RTF, so even a 5,000-entry bibliography comes to about 2 MB.
- `wire::MAX_FRAME` (incoming) drops from 32 MiB to 8 MiB. Replies keep 32 MiB (`wire::MAX_REPLY`) because `Document_getFields` returns every field code in the document. `read_frame` now grows the buffer as bytes arrive instead of allocating the length the header announces.
- The idle timeout drops from 60 to 30 minutes, which is still long enough for Zotero's own dialogs that wait on the user. A 60 s write timeout is added, so a peer that stops reading ends the session.
- `client::Cancel` + `run_cancellable`: cancelling shuts the socket down, which wakes the session wherever it is blocked (read, write, or waiting for the UI's answer). The session and `Cancel` share one `Arc<TcpStream>` rather than a `try_clone`d handle. On Windows, under the full ui-egui test run, `shutdown` on a duplicated handle failed with WSAENOTCONN and the session did not end. The result is `Outcome { cancelled: true }`.…

title: WC-36: classify file commands under Restrict Editing
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Fixes audit finding **WC-36** (Restrict Editing bypass via `file.*`; no GitHub issue).

**Problem.** `protect::always_allowed` let every `id.starts_with("file.")` command run in a protected document. Some of those commands change the document: `file.inspect {"remove": ["comments", "revisions", "properties", "hidden", "headers"]}`, `file.properties {…}` and `file.privacyOptions {…}` all ran without the password. In "comments" mode, the comment deletion that Inspect Document runs internally was allowed too, so the comments were stripped. `file.privacyOptions`' own comment said it was "refused on a protected document", but the prefix check let it through.

**Change** (only in `crates/engine/src/cmd/protect.rs`):
- `FILE_ALLOWED` lists the file commands that leave the document as it is: open, new, save, Save As, export, print, close, info, options, recover, and the other session-level ones. These keep running, as Word's Restrict Editing still allows Save As, export and print even in "No changes (Read only)". `file.protect` stays allowed because it is `review.restrict` under File › Info, and that command guards it.
- `FILE_EDITS` lists `file.inspect`, `file.properties` and `file.privacyOptions`. Each is refused in every enforced mode, tracked changes included, when its params ask for a change: a non-empty `remove`, any property key, or any privacy option. The error says "stop protection before …". The same calls without those params only read, so they still work. This matches Word, which blocks property edits and Document Inspector removal until Stop Protection.
- A `file.*` command in neither list falls through to the normal edit checks (default deny).
- `docs/file-format-parity.md`: the Restrict Editing row, the status line and the revision history are updated.

**Tests.**

title: Format Painter: double-click keeps it on (sticky), armed vs. sticky button state (#2785)
author: miltonjrd
body:
Fixes #2785

## What
- The engine already supports a sticky painter (`edit.formatPainter` with `{"sticky": true}`), but the ribbon never passed it. A double-click fires two clicks, so the second one toggled the painter back off.
- On `double_clicked()` the ribbon now re-arms the painter as sticky. The selection hasn't changed between the clicks, so it picks the same formatting.
- Button state: armed (single click) draws only a blue border; sticky (double-click) draws the full checked look (fill and border).
- Esc or another click on the button turns it off, as before.

The ribbon and engine are shared by desktop and web, so both get the change.

## Tests
- New engine test `a_double_click_makes_the_format_painter_sticky` (click, click, re-arm sticky, paste keeps the painter on, toggle off).
- Manually checked on a Windows x64 release build: single click shows the border and turns off after one use; double-click shows the fill and stays on across several applications; Esc and a click on the button turn it off.
- `cargo xtask ci` steps: fmt, clippy, assets, layers and wasm pass.
- `cargo test --workspace`: one failure, `tests_complex::myanmar_prevowel_is_drawn_before_its_consonant` in `wordcraft-layout`. It fails the same way on a clean `main` in my environment (Linux/WSL), so it looks font-dependent and unrelated to this change.

## Not in this PR
- A plain click on a word (no drag) still doesn't apply the painter on mouse up, although `edit.pasteFormat` supports a collapsed selection.
- The paragraph-formatting rule (`a.off == 0`) only approximates "selection includes the paragraph mark".

title: File page: the back arrow no longer ends WordCraft when accessibility is on
author: arcanii
body:
## What it does

On Windows, WordCraft 0.8.0 ends without a word after **Blank document**, then **File**, then the back arrow at the top of the File page, whenever accessibility is active (a screen reader, or any UI Automation client). The log in `%APPDATA%\WordCraft\logs` has the panic reported in #2726:

```
panic at …\accesskit_consumer-0.35.0\src\tree.rs:71:13: Focused ID #5743185116967667151 is not in the node list
```

After this change the arrow closes the File page, the page has the keyboard again as before, and nothing ends.

This removes one cause of #2726, found with steps that reproduce it every time. It does not replace #2742, which guards every update in general; the two fit together (see below).

## How

**The cause:**
- `refocus_after_chrome_click` hands the keyboard straight back to the page after a click outside it, with `memory.request_focus` on the page's widget id from the last frame that drew it.
- When the click is the File page's back arrow, the File page closes in the same pass, so that pass did not draw the page.
- egui keeps focus on a widget that has just gained it even when the pass did not use it ("recently gained focus" in `Focus::end_pass`). Its AccessKit update then names a focused node that is not in the update.
- `accesskit_consumer` rejects the tree with that panic, which ends the program.

**The fix:**
- The page's id is now kept with the pass that drew it (`CanvasState::widget_id: Option<(Id, u64)>`, from `cumulative_pass_nr`).
- Focus is requested by id only in that pass. Otherwise `want_focus`, which the back arrow already sets, hands the keyboard over in the next frame, when the page is drawn.
- The same path covered File › New › Blank document with a document open.

**With #2742:** its guard moves a focus that an update doesn't carry to the root, so the program survives any such update. This change stops this click from producing one: focus never names a page that the pass didn't draw. The new test passes with or without the…

title: DOCX: a missing font is drawn in the font table w:altName (#2702)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #2702.

## What changes

When a document asks for a font that isn't installed, layout now draws it in the alternate name the document's font table gives (`w:font/w:altName`, ECMA-376 §17.8.3.1) — as Word does — before the roman-family rule (#1613) and the generic substitute list.

- `crates/docx/src/read/mod.rs`: the font table reader keeps the name → alternate pairs (same `MAX_TABLE_FONTS` / `MAX_FONT_NAME` caps and empty-name drops as the rest of the table).
- `crates/doc`: the pairs live in `Settings::alt_fonts` (serde default/skip, like `roman_fonts`), so they are document state.
- `crates/fonts/src/word.rs`: new `substitutes_available(family)` — true when the family, a Windows charset alias of it, or one of its own substitutes is installed; false only at the last-resort fallback. It lives next to the substitute lists it reasons about.
- `crates/layout/src/para.rs`: `lookup_family` (the seam where the roman rule lives) resolves installed → **font-table alternate, when the alternate is itself available** → roman rule → the font as asked. The name stored on the run is unchanged, so saving keeps the original.

## Validation

title: fix: CMD pressed during macOS scroll momentum no longer turns it into a zoom
author: egkodin
body:
## What
Pressing CMD while a touchpad / Magic Mouse scroll is still gliding (momentum) turned the rest of that plain scroll into a zoom.

## Why
egui stamps every wheel event with the modifiers held *now*. macOS keeps sending momentum events after the fingers lift, so CMD pressed mid-glide made egui read them as Cmd+wheel. #2386 cancels the app's own momentum when a zoom starts but does not stop the system's momentum events from becoming a zoom.

winit (macOS) reports only the edges of a gesture: `Start` (fingers down, or momentum begins) and `End` (fingers lift, or momentum ends). Inside momentum every event is `Move`, same as under the fingers, so the phase alone can't tell them apart.

## Change
- `scroll::GestureLock` follows the phase sequence `Start` (fingers) … `End` (lift) → `Start` (momentum) … `End` (momentum over). A `Start` right after the lift (within 0.15 s) is momentum and keeps the gesture's mode; any other `Start`, including one right after the momentum's `End` (fingers landing on a gliding page), is a new gesture and reads CMD afresh.
- Every event of a gesture, momentum included, carries CMD as it was at the start: a plain scroll never zooms, and a CMD gesture keeps zooming if CMD is released.
- Applied in `WordApp::raw_input_hook` on macOS, before egui computes the zoom. Wheels without phases (classic mouse) are not locked; CMD is read live.
- Tests in `scroll.rs` cover CMD pressed mid-momentum, a CMD gesture interrupting momentum (also right after the momentum's `End` and in the same frame), CMD released mid-zoom, and unphased wheels.

## Reviewer notes
- Trade-off: a lift with no momentum followed by a new touch within 0.15 s is taken as that gesture's momentum.
- Uses `InputOptions::default()` for the zoom modifier (the app never overrides it).
- Not verified on a real trackpad / Magic Mouse; the phase sequence comes from winit 0.30.13 source.

## Checks
`cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui --lib` (613 passed), fmt, clippy, `cargo xtask layers` OK…

author: PanSHIgg
body:
Fixes #2640.

**Manage Sources** gains **Import…**, and `references.sources` an `"import": path` parameter: it reads a Word bibliography file — Word's own `Sources.xml`, i.e. any `b:Sources` document in the bibliography namespace (ECMA-376) — into the document's sources. title: Keep the Insert SmartArt dialog within the window (#2832)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2832.

The picker lays out its three columns (categories, layouts, preview) in `ui.horizontal_top`, with `ui.separator()` between them. In a horizontal layout a separator is a vertical line as tall as `ui.available_size_before_wrap().y`, and inside the dialog window that is the whole window height. So the two separators made the dialog as tall as the window, and centering it pushed the title bar and the OK/Cancel buttons off the top and bottom edges.

- The columns row is now drawn by a small `picker_row`, which caps the row at `PICKER_HEIGHT` (three rows of 96 pt tiles plus the 8 pt gaps, 304 pt) before `horizontal_top`. The separators now stop at the tallest column, and the dialog is only as tall as its content plus the buttons.
- The content already fits in that height: the 8 layouts make at most 3 tile rows, and the category list and preview column are shorter. So nothing needs to scroll, and the layout is the same as before, only without the stretched separators.

Only the SmartArt picker is changed; the other Insert dialogs use horizontal separators in vertical layouts, which take the width, not the height.

Test: `the_picker_row_stays_within_its_height` runs `picker_row` with a separator in a 1920x1080 egui frame and checks that the row stays within `PICKER_HEIGHT`. Without the cap the separator takes the full screen height and the test fails.

title: DOCX: Word 2007 WordArt (VML textpath) in the body is shown as text, not dropped (#2875)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2875.

Word 2007 writes WordArt as a VML `v:shape` with a `v:textpath` inside `w:pict`. Only Word's header watermark read that textpath (#1290); any other WordArt shape fell through `read_vml_shape` and was dropped, so the text vanished and the paragraphs below moved up.

What changed (`crates/docx/src/read/story.rs`, `read_vml_shape`):

- A `v:shape` whose `v:textpath` is on and has a non-empty `string` now becomes a text-box shape holding that string. The header watermark is still taken before this, so it doesn't change.
- Text: the textpath's `font-family` (quotes trimmed, the same way the watermark reader does it), the shape's `fillcolor` (its own, else its shapetype's) as the text colour, and a size taken from the shape's height, since WordArt letters fill their box (`fitshape`). The box has no fill, no outline and no inner margins, with the text centred vertically. The letters are the art.
- Warp: the shape's WordArt preset (`o:spt` 136-175, its own, its shapetype's, or from Word's `_x0000_tNN` id) maps to the DrawingML text warp of the same shape (`textArchUp`, `textWave1`, `textCanDown`…). That puts it on the shape's existing `extra.warp`, which layout already draws and the writer already saves, the same as DrawingML WordArt (#416).
- Limits match the watermark reader: string capped at 200 chars, font name at 100. The existing `MAX_STORY_DEPTH` check still applies.

Not covered: VML WordArt outline (`strokecolor`), shadow and 3-D effects. The text is drawn plain in its fill colour. `docs/file-format-parity.md` now says so; it used to say body WordArt was dropped.

Test: `vml_textpath_in_body_is_shown` in `crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs`. It checks that a body WordArt shape becomes one text shape with the right size, text, font and colour. It also checks that Arch Up (144) and Can Down (175) get their warps, and that a textpath turned off or with an empty string gives nothing. Without the fix the shape is dropped, so the test fails.

title: Decode ISO 8859-1 Hunspell dictionaries so the original pt_BR works (#2824)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2824.

The original VERO `pt_BR.aff` (the LibreOffice extension, and the Arch `hunspell-pt-br` package that installs it as-is) starts with `SET ISO8859-1`. `hunspell::decode` only knew UTF-8, ISO 8859-2, KOI8-R and Windows-1251, so it returned "unsupported encoding ISO8859-1" and Portuguese text got no spelling marks at all.

- `crates/proof/src/hunspell.rs`: `decode` accepts `ISO8859-1` / `ISO-8859-1` (the same two spellings the ISO 8859-2 arm takes). ISO 8859-1 maps every byte to the code point of the same value, so `decode_latin1` is one line next to `decode_latin2`.
- `docs/spelling-dictionaries.md`: the list of encodings now includes ISO 8859-1.

Test: `decodes_latin1` decodes an `.aff`/`.dic` pair with `ç` (0xE7) and `á` (0xE1) in ISO 8859-1, under both `SET` spellings. Without the fix, `decode` returns the "unsupported encoding" error and the test fails.

ISO 8859-15, which the issue mentions as cheap to add, is left out: no dictionary in the issue uses it.

title: Keep the selection's font when typing over a backward selection
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #2879

## Cause
`Session::typing_props` took its formatting from the run just before the caret (`sel.focus`), even when text was selected. When a selection is made right to left, the focus is at the start of the selection, so text typed over it took the formatting of the text before the selection, for example the old font.

## Fix
If text is selected and no caret formatting is waiting, `typing_props` now uses the formatting of the first selected character, taken from the start of the selection in document order, as Word does. A hyperlink or footnote/endnote reference style on that character is dropped, the same way as at a caret. The new behaviour and its test are listed in docs/typing-parity.md.

## Verified
- Regression test `typing_over_backward_selection_keeps_its_font`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --lib typing_over_backward_selection_keeps_its_font`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::deleted_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_without_markup`, `tests::hidden_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_when_not_shown`, `tests::tight_wrap_follows_an_ellipse`, `tests_pages::widow_control_moves_a_three_line_paragraph_whole`, `tests::the_font_box_lists_recently_used_fonts_first`, which also fail on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
`caret_props` (Reveal Formatting and the inspector, which already handle selections on their own) and the behaviour with a collapsed caret are unchanged.

title: Fit inline text boxes with Resize shape to fit text to their text
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #2791

## Cause
An inline drawing's line height always came from its saved extent (`wp:extent`). For a text box with `a:spAutoFit`, `body.auto_fit` only turned off clipping of overflowing text and never resized the box, so a stale saved height took room that Word doesn't give it and pushed the following content onto another page.

## Fix
Layout now measures inline, unrotated, horizontal, unlinked auto-fit text boxes: their text is laid out at the box's width, and the text's depth plus the top and bottom insets is used in place of the saved height. The height is worked out once per layout, passed to paragraph layout through `ParaEnv::fitted` and included in the paragraph cache key. The box's frame, its drawing and the placement of its text all follow the fitted height.

## Verified
- Regression test `inline_box_that_resizes_to_fit_takes_its_texts_height`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-layout --lib inline_box_that_resizes_to_fit_takes_its_texts_height`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::legacy_font_effects_are_drawn`, which also fails on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
Floating, rotated, vertical-text, linked and grouped text boxes keep their saved size. Auto-fit width (wrap="none") is not handled.

title: UI: the Full Screen button leaves full screen on a second click (#2864)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #2864.

## Problem

The View tab's **Full Screen** button enters full screen, but clicking it again does nothing — the only way out is Escape.

## Root cause

The button is a mode toggle, but it was drawn with the one-shot `big()` helper, which takes the *menu* flag as its last argument:

```rust
big(ui, app, "fullScreen", "Full\nScreen", "view.fullScreen", json!({}), v.full_screen);
```

The fullscreen state was therefore passed as `menu`. Inside `big_button`, a click only runs the command when `!menu` — so while full screen was on, the button swallowed its own clicks. (F11 worked because the key handler passes `{"value": false}` explicitly.)

## Fix

- Draw the button with `big_toggle`, which exists exactly for "a large ribbon button for a mode that stays on (`checked` draws it pressed)": the state now renders as the pressed look instead of masquerading as a menu arrow, and clicks always run `view.fullScreen`.
- The button also had no accessible name (big ribbon buttons are drawn without one), so a screen reader announced nothing there; it now carries "Full Screen" via `widget_info`, the same pattern `small()` buttons already use. Scoped to this one button: labelling every `big_button` makes ribbon buttons duplicate their status-bar twins ("Web Layout", "Focus") in the accessibility tree, which breaks `get_by_role_and_label` uniqueness elsewhere.

## Test

`the_full_screen_button_toggles_out` (kittest): switch to the View tab, click **Full Screen** — asserts the window gets `Fullscreen(true)` and the state flips — then click it again — asserts `Fullscreen(false)` and the state flips back. Red on main (the second click sends nothing); green here.

Validation: `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui --lib` — the two chrome-focus tests that a blanket labelling of all big buttons had broken (`clicks_on_ribbon_and_status_bar_chrome_keep_typing_in_the_document`, `focus_hides_the_ribbon_and_escape_brings_it_back`) pass again; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo cli…

title: speech: Read Aloud on Linux falls back to Speech Dispatcher and says what to install
author: Skaywalker
body:
## Summary

On Linux, Read Aloud only tried `espeak-ng` and `espeak`. Many desktops ship Speech Dispatcher (`spd-say`, usually with the espeak-ng module) but not the `espeak-ng` command, and there Read Aloud stopped at the first sentence with "couldn't start the speech program: No such file or directory". The module docs already named `spd-say`, but the code never tried it.

- **Speech Dispatcher fallback.** When neither `espeak-ng` nor `espeak` is installed, Read Aloud talks to Speech Dispatcher directly over its socket (SSIP, `crates/engine/src/speech/ssip.rs`), starting the server once if it isn't running, as `spd-say` does. One connection speaks one sentence: client name, end and cancel events, rate (1× = 0, 0.5× = -50, 3× = 100), the sentence's language from #2430 (English included, since Speech Dispatcher's default language is its own setting), the text, then the wait for the end event.
  - The sentence is always message data: `spd-say -e` would run a line starting with `!-!` as an SSIP command, so a document could have sent commands. Line breaks become spaces and a leading `.` is doubled, so the text can't end the message early either.
  - Stopping, skipping or changing the speed sends `CANCEL self`, which stops only WordCraft's own message; `spd-say -C` would have silenced every client, a screen reader included.
- **A message that says what to install.** When none of the programs exists, the player and the status bar show "Read Aloud needs a speech program: install espeak-ng or Speech Dispatcher from your distribution's packages" instead of the OS error. Other spawn errors keep the old message.
- **Packages.** The `.deb` recommends `espeak-ng | speech-dispatcher` (one of the two) and the `.rpm` recommends `espeak-ng`, so apt and dnf install a speech program with WordCraft by default.
- **Docs.** README (Linux) says what Read Aloud needs and how to install it for the AppImage and the tarball; `docs/hardware-parity.md` records the Linux state.

title: speech: choose the Read Aloud voice
author: Skaywalker
body:
## Summary

Read Aloud always used the speech program's default voice (or, since #2430, the voice of each sentence's language). Word lets you pick the reading voice; this adds that.

- **`readAloud.voice`** without `value` lists the installed voices (`id`, `name`, `lang`) and the chosen one. The system is asked once, on a background thread, so the settings page never waits on a slow program; `pending` is true until the answer arrives.
  - Linux / BSD: `espeak-ng --voices` (or `espeak`), else Speech Dispatcher's `LIST SYNTHESIS_VOICES` over the socket from #2934 (plain voices only; every variant of every voice would be thousands). MBROLA voices are left out unless `mbrola` is installed, since espeak-ng can't speak them without it.
  - macOS: `say -v '?'`, without the novelty voices.
  - Windows: the enabled System.Speech voices.
- **`readAloud.voice`** `{"value": id | null}` chooses one (`null` = Automatic) and answers with the same list. One command keeps the label to "Voice", which every catalog translates already. The chosen voice reads the sentences in its own language and those without a language; a sentence in another language keeps its language's voice, so a Hungarian voice doesn't read a Russian quotation.
- **Options › Accessibility › Read Aloud › Voice**: Automatic, then the installed voices as "name (language)". The choice is saved with the other Read Aloud settings.
- Passing the voice: `espeak-ng -v <file>`, `SET SELF SYNTHESIS_VOICE <name>` to Speech Dispatcher, `say -v <name>`, and `SelectVoice('<name>')` on Windows, the name quoted as a PowerShell literal with `'` and the typographic quotes ‘ ’ ‚ ‛ doubled (PowerShell ends a single-quoted string at any of them). A voice that fails falls back to the default voice, as for the language voices; a saved voice that isn't installed is simply not used.

title: A Word 2003 XML or web page saved as .doc opens by what it holds (#2853)
author: D13GOOOO
body:
Fixes #2853

## What was wrong

The attached `soulsoul.txt.doc` is not a Word 97-2003 binary file. It is a **Word 2003 XML Document** (`<?mso-application progid="Word.Document"?>`, root `w:wordDocument`) saved with a `.doc` name.

WordCraft picks the reader by extension. It only opens a file "by what it holds" when the file starts with a ZIP, OLE or RTF signature that contradicts the extension. XML matched none of those, so the file went to the binary `.doc` reader, which refused it:

```
not a Word document (compound file): Invalid CFB file (wrong magic number): [3c, 3f, 78, 6d, 6c, 20, 76, 65]
```

The window then showed an empty page. WordCraft already reads Word 2003 XML and Flat OPC (`.xml`, #548); the file just never got there.

A web page saved as `.doc` hits the same path. Report generators do this, and so does Word's own Save as Web Page under a `.doc` name.

## Change

`crates/engine/src/io.rs`:
- `signature_contradicts` also recognises:
  - a Word XML Document, Word 2003 or Flat OPC, by its root element through the existing `sniff_xml`. Only text that starts with markup (after a BOM and white space) is parsed.
  - a web page: `<!DOCTYPE html` or `<html`, after a BOM, an XML declaration and comments.
- Under a `.doc`, `.dot`, `.docx`, `.docm`, `.dotx`, `.dotm` or `.rtf` name, such a file now goes to `open_by_content`:
  - Word XML opens with the Word XML reader;
  - a web page opens with the HTML importer, pictures fitted as for `.html`.
- The extension is checked first, so files of other formats don't pay for the sniffing.
- A web page under an unknown extension (`.log`…) still opens as plain text, and XML that isn't a Word document is still refused.

Docs: `file-format-parity.md`, the `.txt` row on mismatched extensions, the status line and the revision history.

**Overlap with #1104:** #1104 adds an MHT reader (`wordcraft_formats::mht`). An earlier version of this branch had its own MHTML reader for `.doc` files that hold an MHT message. I took it out s…

title: Render: fade dimmed headers and footers as one layer
author: dfgodvan
body:
Fixes #2946.

## Problem
Dimmed headers and footers (and the dimmed body while a header is edited) get the 0.45 alpha on every draw item separately. Where items overlap, the alpha is applied twice, so a header table's borders turn darker along shared cell edges and nearly black where they cross. The undimmed view and the PDF export look right.

## Fix
- `crates/layout/src/display.rs`: the per-story loop of `page_display` moves into `stories_display`. The new `page_layers` returns a page's draws as two layers (headers/footers, body) at full strength, each with the opacity to draw it at. `page_display` is unchanged.
- `crates/render/src/lib.rs`: `render_region` draws a dimmed layer inside a single `push_opacity_layer`, so the layer is faded once, as Word dims it. Undimmed layers are drawn as before, without a layer. `background_at` blends a dimmed layer as a whole, the same way.

## Before / after
Dimmed header, 8×, left: main, right: this PR.

## Testing
- New test `dimmed_header_borders_dont_darken_where_they_meet`: a 2×2 table in the header, rendered dimmed and undimmed. Every dimmed pixel is the undimmed one faded by 0.45 (±2). It fails on main (`(216, 107): 137 dimmed, 156.45 wanted (36 at full strength)`) and passes here.

title: Clipboard: WordCraft Fragment, so another window pastes a copy with its formatting
author: TarasDzia
body:
## What this changes and why

Copying in one WordCraft window and pasting in another loses most of the formatting. Each window is a process of its own; the copy's rich fragment (`Session::clipboard`) lives only in the window it was made in, so another window gets the system clipboard's HTML, which can't carry paragraph and character styles, the document's own Normal and defaults, list definitions, or spacing and indents that come from styles. The HTML was also exported in the built-in styles (`Fragment::to_document()`) and with no paragraph spacing at all, so even the source's Normal font and its spacing before/after and line spacing were lost — in Word and LibreOffice too.

Five commits, and merges of `main` (latest 254351c; conflicts only in the progress docs' status lines and revision tables):

### 1. Clipboard: WordCraft Fragment

- **Copy / Cut** also put the copy on the clipboard as JSON (`{"format":"wordcraft-fragment","version":1,"text","doc","media","whole"}`): the copied blocks and text box stories as a `Document` with the source's styles, numbering and revisions, plus only the pictures the copy shows (base64), capped at 64 MB. Windows: registered format `WordCraft Fragment`, added after arboard's text and HTML with `clipboard-win`'s `set_without_clear`. Wayland reads `application/x-wordcraft-fragment`; writing it there needs a data-control offer of our own (the RTF work in #2630 builds one), so it's left out here. macOS and X11: not yet.
- **Paste, Merge Formatting and Paste Special › Formatted Text** take it as a new `wordcraft` param (the desktop UI fills it from `Services::clipboard_native`):
  - this window's own copy (payload hash = `Session::clipboard_native_id`) pastes the session fragment as before;
  - another window's copy is adopted like HTML/RTF (styles it lacks, lists, pictures), and — as Word's *Keep Source Formatting* — wherever a style it uses resolves differently here (another Normal font, Heading size, docDefaults spacing), the source's …

title: Selection rectangles walk only the paragraphs the range reaches
author: dfgodvan
body:
## Problem
`Document::paths_between` lists every paragraph of the story, including every cell paragraph of every table, and then keeps those between the two ends. So each `selection_rects` call costs the whole document, however short the range. The canvas calls it on every frame for each Find reading highlight (up to 5,000), for content control frames, for Read Aloud and for the hyperlink under the pointer. In a long document with big tables this adds up to whole frames.

## Fix
`crates/doc/src/lib.rs`: `walk_between`, a version of `walk` that skips the blocks, rows and cells outside the two paths. `crates/doc/src/edit.rs`: `paths_between` uses it.

## Numbers
A one-paragraph range in a document of 26,000 paragraphs (2,000 paragraphs and four 1,500 × 4 tables): `paths_between` takes 2.6 µs instead of 1.0 ms (mean of 200 calls, dev profile, macOS). With 1,000 Find highlights, that is about 1 s less work per frame.

## Testing
- New test `paths_between_matches_every_path_filtered`: a document with tables and a nested table. For every pair of paragraph paths, `paths_between` must equal the old filter over `para_paths`.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, assets, layers and wasm pass; `cargo test --workspace` passes except `legacy_font_effects_are_drawn` and `script_file_name_need_not_be_unicode`, which fail the same way on an unmodified main on this macOS machine (a font-dependent check, and APFS refusing a non-UTF-8 file name).


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Improvements**
  * Document path-range results now include the paths within the requested range, including paths in nested tables. The results remain consistent with filtering all paragraph paths in the document, while handling ranges that end before later content.

title: #2950: Prefer native Wayland when Fcitx is set up
author: C00kieMonsta
body:
Fixes #2950.

Before: on a Wayland session with an X server (DISPLAY set), WordCraft always ran through XWayland unless WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND was set to any value. Fcitx then reached it through XIM, which garbled Vietnamese Telex typing (#2932).

After: when Fcitx is set up, the window runs on native Wayland. Fcitx counts as set up when XMODIFIERS names `fcitx` or `fcitx5` after its first `@im=`, or GTK_IM_MODULE, QT_IM_MODULE, QT_IM_MODULES or SDL_IM_MODULE names one of them. Native Wayland reaches fcitx5 only when the compositor connects it: GNOME through fcitx5's IBus frontend, KDE when Fcitx 5 is picked under Virtual Keyboard, wlroots compositors and niri directly. IBus and other input methods stay on XIM through XWayland; stock GNOME sets up IBus, so it keeps XWayland, file drag-and-drop and GNOME's title bar. `WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND=1` forces native Wayland and is the opt-in for IBus users. `WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND=0` forces XWayland (it used to mean native Wayland, like any other value). The log records the choice and why on a line containing `display:`.

Trade-offs: fcitx5 users on Wayland lose file drag-and-drop (#220), and on GNOME they get winit's plain fallback frame (#78) until #282 or #2188 lands; `WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND=0` brings both back. Some fcitx5 setups give the compositor no route to fcitx5 (ChromeOS Crostini, #1061; KDE without Fcitx 5 under Virtual Keyboard) and need `WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND=0`. Related work: #1978 rewrites the same lines in `main.rs` to make native Wayland the default, so the two will conflict; #2184 (a display-server setting) would plug into `display_backend::choose`; the X11-side fix for #2932 is in progress separately.

- `apps/wordcraft/src/display_backend.rs`: new module. `choose(env)` picks Wayland or X11 from the environment and gives the reason for the log. Tests cover every rule, stock GNOME with IBus, junk values, long values and values that aren't UTF-8.

title: Ruler: margin handles on even mirrored pages edit the visible edge's stored margin (#2914)
author: dhruvLearner8
body:
Fixes #2914.

With Mirror margins (or Book fold) on, `mirror_even_pages` lays an even page out reflected: its visible left edge is the stored **right** margin and its visible right edge is the stored left margin plus gutter. The ruler's handles still mapped the visible left edge to `margin_left`, so on an even page dragging the left handle changed the opposite margin and the edge did not follow the pointer.

`margin_drag` (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`) now maps a drag to the stored edge: on an even page of a mirrored layout it reflects the pointer (`page_w - x`) and swaps Left/Right, then uses the existing `dragged_margin` (so snapping, the one-inch minimum text width and the gutter are unchanged). Top/bottom and odd or unmirrored pages are unchanged. `rulers` decides "mirrored" from `mirror_margins` and the page's displayed number being even, the same rule the layout uses.

Test: `ruler_margin_drags_on_even_mirrored_pages_move_the_visible_edge` (two-page mirrored document; dragging each visible edge of page 2 edits the right stored margin; the left margin and the odd page follow). fmt, clippy -D warnings and the whole `wordcraft-ui-egui` suite pass; I did not run the full `cargo xtask ci` and did not drive the ruler by hand.

title: #2948: the mouse wheel over the ribbon switches tabs
author: C00kieMonsta
body:
Fixes #2948.

In Word for Windows, turning the mouse wheel over the ribbon or its tab names moves to the next tab (wheel down) or the previous one (wheel up). It skips File and stops at the first and last tab, and a setting in File › Options › Advanced turns it off. Until now the wheel over WordCraft's ribbon did nothing.

Now each wheel notch over the tab strip or the ribbon body switches one tab, in tab order, with contextual tabs included. Touchpad input adds up to a notch, and one gesture moves at most one tab. A page scroll that is still coasting when the pointer reaches the ribbon switches nothing, so a click right after scrolling the page lands on the tab you were looking at. Shift+wheel and sideways scrolling still scroll the ribbon. Open menus and a text box on the ribbon, such as the font box, keep the wheel; text boxes elsewhere don't block it. The Styles, Table Styles and Equation symbol galleries scroll with the wheel instead of switching tabs, each with its own count. A collapsed ribbon stays collapsed. File › Options › Advanced › Display has a check box to turn this off, and `ui.wheelTabs` does the same for scripts; it is on by default and kept between runs. In a browser, and with high-resolution wheels that report parts of a notch, a quick spin moves one tab, like a touchpad.

- `crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs`: wheel notch counting (`WheelNotches`: whole notches count at once, finer input adds up, input that started elsewhere is held off until it rests), tab stepping (`wheel_tab`), separate wheel state for each gallery (`gallery_wheel`), wiring into the tab strip and ribbon body, the Table Styles gallery scrolling sideways, and tests.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/previews.rs`: the Styles gallery scrolls one row of tiles per notch.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/equation_tab.rs`: the Equation symbols strip scrolls one row per notch.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`: `UiState::wheel_tabs` (on by default, persisted), the `ui.wheelTabs` command (also usable with no document…

title: speech: Read Aloud in the browser through the Web Speech API
author: Skaywalker
body:
## Summary

Read Aloud in the web version stopped at once with "Read Aloud isn't available in the browser". Browsers have speech synthesis built in (the Web Speech API), so this speaks there too.

- **`speech/web.rs`** (wasm only) speaks one sentence at a time, like the desktop backends: a `SpeechSynthesisUtterance` per sentence, in the sentence's language (#2430), at the reading speed, in the chosen voice when it suits the sentence (#2937). Its `end` event moves on to the next sentence; an `error` event other than `interrupted`/`canceled` stops with the browser's error code.
- Every change to the player (pause, skip, stop, a new speed or voice) cancels the utterance and, if still playing, speaks the current sentence again, as the desktop worker does. The generation and the sentence index an utterance was started for keep a late event of a cancelled one from moving the player.
- The utterance and its handler are kept until the next sentence (an utterance the page no longer references may be collected before its `end` event fires), and a handler that ends a sentence isn't dropped while it starts the next one.
- **Voices:** `readAloud.voice` lists the browser's voices (`getVoices()`, id = voice URI). Browsers load them after the page, so the list is `pending` until they arrive or a few seconds pass without any.
- No speech synthesis in the browser: the player stops with "Read Aloud isn't available in this browser".
- `crates/engine` gets `wasm-bindgen` and the `web-sys` speech features for wasm32 only (`xtask layers` allows them; the web app already uses both).

title: proof: bundle Hungarian spelling with MPL attribution and LibreOffice updates
author: kalmarr
body:
Hungarian text currently receives no spelling checks on `main`. This adds offline `hu-HU` spelling and suggestions using a bundled Magyar Ispell 1.9 dictionary from LibreOffice. For example, `muszály` suggests `muszáj`, while `árvíztűrő`, `tükörfúrógép` and `házainkban` are accepted. Hungarian is available in the proofing language selectors, and a Hungarian interface uses it for new documents.

The contribution also includes basic repetition/spacing checks with Hungarian messages and a maintainer command, `cargo xtask update-hungarian <full-LibreOffice-commit>`. Updates preserve the original dictionary bytes, check the upstream MPL license statement, parse and smoke-test the candidate, and record its immutable revision and SHA-256 checksums before replacement. Publication uses an OS lock, private staging, whole-directory renames, installed-byte verification and recovery of interrupted updates; recovery instructions are documented. No document text is sent anywhere and no background dictionary downloads occur.

title: #2945: Ctrl+click a cross-reference to go to its target
author: C00kieMonsta
body:
Fixes #2945.

In Word, the Cross-reference dialog's "Insert as hyperlink" box (on by default) adds `\h` to the REF, PAGEREF or NOTEREF field. Ctrl+click (Cmd+click on Mac) on such a reference moves the caret to its target and scrolls there. Before this change WordCraft already wrote `\h`, but a click on the reference did nothing, so a reader could not jump from "Figure 1" in the text to the figure.

Now Ctrl/Cmd+click on a reference with `\h` puts the caret at the start of its bookmark and scrolls there. The bookmark can be in the body, a note, a header or footer, or a text box. Go Back (Shift+F5) returns to the reference. The hover tip names the target ("Figure 1", the heading text, or "Bookmark: name"), not the hidden `_Ref` name. A reference without `\h` is plain text. If the bookmark is gone, the caret and the view stay where they are, and the tip and the status line say the target is no longer in the document. The dialog has "Insert as hyperlink", on by default, and `insert.crossReference` takes `"hyperlink"`. Above/below references now write `\p`, so updating fields keeps "above" or "below". PAGEREF and NOTEREF links are kept in PDF exports, as REF links already were. The new `edit.followLink` command follows a link for scripts and agents; run from command search or a shortcut, it also opens web and email links.

- `crates/layout/src/fields.rs`: `reference_link` is public and covers REF, PAGEREF and NOTEREF.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs`: `Link`, `link_at`, `link_under`, `link_destination` and the `edit.followLink` command, with tests.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs`, `crates/engine/src/cmd/references.rs`: bookmarks are found in every story (`find_bookmark`), so Go To, follow and Update Field reach notes, headers and text boxes.

title: Layout: a word after a slash wraps whole, like Word (#2963)
author: Faabyy
body:
Fixes #2963.

UAX #14 (LB13) forbids a break between a space and a slash, and the break after a slash is dropped on purpose (Word keeps "and/or" whole). Together, "caption /word" had no break opportunity at all, so on a line too short for both the word was filled letter by letter and split (`/заполняетс` / `я`).

This adds the break before a slash that follows whitespace and starts a word. "and/or", URLs and a spaced " / " are unchanged.

Test: the issue's caption (slash in its own run), swept over widths; every line but the last must end at a space. It fails on main at margin 364 with the split from the report.

Checked: fmt, clippy, layout tests (four fail the same way on main: deleted/hidden-text opportunity tests, tight wrap ellipse, widow control). I did not compare against Word or LibreOffice here, and the test uses a plain paragraph rather than a table cell.

title: #2914: ruler margin handles edit the visible edge's stored margin on mirrored even pages
author: maxm11
body:
Fixes #2914.

## The bug

With `w:mirrorMargins`, an even page's text area is the odd page's reflected: its left edge is the stored `margin_right` and its right edge the stored `margin_left` plus the inside gutter. The ruler's horizontal margin handles stored the dragged edge by its visual name, so on an even page dragging the visible left edge edited `margin_left` — the text edge jumped away from the pointer (and symmetrically on the right).

## The fix

In `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` only:

- New `margin_drag(edge, at, sect, mirrored)` beside the existing `dragged_margin`: on a mirrored even page it reflects the pointer across the page (`page_w - at`) and swaps Left/Right, then delegates to `dragged_margin` for snapping, the minimum text width and the gutter. Top/bottom and the vertical ruler are unchanged (pass `false`).
- `rulers` computes `mirrored = settings.mirror_margins && page.number.is_multiple_of(2)` — the same test the layout uses to mirror a page — and passes it to the two horizontal handles.
- `margin_handle` now runs `layout.margins` with the stored edge's param instead of the visual one.

Odd pages and unmirrored layouts behave exactly as before; Book fold layout and Page Setup are untouched (#2414 is separate).

## Tests

Three regression tests in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`:

1. `mirrored_margin_drags_swap_the_stored_edge` — the mapping itself: unmirrored unchanged, even mirrored swaps with the gutter off the stored left margin, top/bottom never swap, NaN keeps the current margin.
2. `ruler_margin_drags_on_odd_and_even_mirrored_pages_move_the_visible_edge` — a two-page mirrored document with an 18pt gutter; both handles on both pages go through the same mapping and `layout.margins` command `margin_handle` uses, and the laid-out text area is asserted to land under the pointer each time.
3. `ruler_margin_handles_on_even_mirrored_pages_follow_the_pointer` — the real interaction: an `egui_kittest` harness presses and drags the actual ruler handl…

title: #2963: a slash opening a word travels whole to the next line
author: maxm11
body:
Fixes #2963.

## What was wrong

In a narrow fixed-layout cell, `…толтырылады /заполняется…` filled letter by letter (`толтырылады /заполн` / `яется в случае`) instead of moving `/заполняется` to the next line whole as Word and LibreOffice do.

Two UAX #14 rules met to make the whole `word /slashed` run unbreakable:

- **after** the slash: the `no_line_break_right_after_a_slash` guard removes the break (keeps `and/or` and URLs whole);
- **before** the slash: LB13 forbids a break before `/` *even after a space*, so the space before it was no break point either.

With no break opportunity anywhere in `толтырылады /заполняется`, the line filler hit its emergency path and broke mid-word. The control cell without the slash has a normal space break and wrapped correctly.

## The fix

`crates/layout/src/para.rs`: after the `linebreaks` loop, a `/` that **opens a word after a plain space** (next char alphanumeric) gets a break opportunity at the slash. So the space before it becomes a break again, the trailing space hangs as usual, and the line starts with the complete `/заполняется`.

- No space before the slash → nothing changes: `and/or`, `https://…` stay glued both ways; the `after_slash` guard is untouched, so `no_line_break_right_after_a_slash` still passes.
- The word after the slash is never breakable between its letters (the guard still suppresses `/`→letter).
- A slashed word wider than the line still takes the emergency break (nothing in the break decisions changed for that path).

Only UAX #14 opportunities are touched: Thai/ICU breaking, kinsoku, hyphenation and the #2712/#2739 numeric paths are unchanged.

## Test

`layout::tests::a_slash_opening_a_word_travels_with_it_to_the_next_line` uses the issue's shape — a fixed 2 × 1800-twip table, 7 pt italic, centred, the slash in its own run — and asserts:

- a line starts with the complete `/заполняется` and every line holds whole words;
- the no-slash control cell wraps in whole words, unchanged;
- a `/` + word wi…

title: #2505: Dutch (nl) spelling proofing
author: Jeroentjj
body:
Closes the spelling part of #2505 (Dutch spelling and hyphenation). Hyphenation and Dutch grammar rules are not in this PR.

## What it does

Dutch spelling reads the installed Hunspell `nl_NL` dictionary at runtime, the same way Czech, Polish and Indonesian do. The dictionary is OpenTaal's: Debian/Ubuntu ship it as `hunspell-nl`, LibreOffice as `dict-nl`, and it can also come from the Dictionaries folder or `WORDCRAFT_DICTIONARIES`. Nothing is bundled. Without a dictionary, Dutch text gets no spelling marks. OpenTaal's dictionary covers Belgium too, so `nl-BE` uses it as well.

- `ProofLang::Nl` for `nl`, `nl-*`, `nld` and `dut`.
- Suggestions use the dictionary-driven Czech ranking. They run on the dictionary's `ĳ` spelling and are shown back with `ij`. Splits with a lone letter (`werkzaamheden n`) and dangling compound hyphens are dropped.
- Generic repeated-word and spacing checks, with Dutch messages. The doubles Dutch grammar produces itself are allowed: `dat dat`, `die die`, `haar haar`, `zijn zijn`, `had had`.
- Review › Language, the status bar, Set Proofing Language and File › Options › Proofing list Dutch. Load errors go through `note_load` (#2830).

## Affix engine changes

OpenTaal's `nl_NL` uses Hunspell features the engine rejected, so the engine now supports them:

- **`FLAG long`**: each two-character flag maps to one private-use `char`, so the rest of the engine keeps `char` flags.
- **Flags that only stems carry** (no rule or directive uses them) get no bit. This keeps nl_NL's 148 flags under the 128-bit limit (125 of them are used). Existing dictionaries behave the same, because such a bit never did anything.
- **`ICONV`/`OCONV`** (nl_NL stores `ij` as the letter `ĳ`) and **`KEEPCASE`**.
- **Compounding**, in the new `affix/compound.rs`. Dutch writes compounds as one word, and the dictionary builds them from parts instead of listing them all. Supported:
  - `COMPOUNDRULE` (with `*` and `?`)
  - `COMPOUNDBEGIN`/`MIDDLE`/`END` with `COMPOUNDPERMITF…

Before: Design › Watermark offered text only. Custom Watermark had a text box and Diagonal or Horizontal, with no way to pick a picture and no control over transparency. A text watermark was either Semitransparent or opaque. Word's dialog has three choices: No watermark, Picture watermark (Select Picture, Scale, Washout) and Text watermark (with a Semitransparent check box). Word stores a picture watermark as a VML picture in each header, with gain and blacklevel on the picture when Washout is on.

After: Custom Watermark has the same three choices. A picture watermark is drawn centred in its section's margins behind the text, at Auto (fitted to the margins) or at a percentage of the picture's size. Washout fades it the way Word does, on screen and in PDF. The faded copy is made from at most 4096 px on the picture's longer side, so a large photo is decoded once and keeps PDFs small. Text watermarks get a transparency percentage next to Semitransparent, and the two stay in step (Semitransparent is 50 %). DOCX saves a picture watermark as Word's picture watermark in every header, each sized for the first section that shows it.

Reading DOCX: a Word picture watermark becomes the document's watermark only when every page shows the same one. Each must be centred on the margins, behind the text, shown, not moved, turned, flipped or stretched, and carry Word's Washout values or none; their scales must agree (all Auto, or all the same 1 to 500 %); and no footer may have a watermark. Otherwise each stays a picture in its header, as before: for example a cover page without it, a section with another picture or scale, or a footer with a text watermark. A text watermark's `v:fill` opacity round-trips at any value. A picture's transparency has no form Word reads in its VML watermark, so pictures get Washout only, as in Word. `design.watermark` takes `picture` ({path|data|media}), `scale` (kept to tenths of a percent), `washout`, `transparency` and `semitransparent`…

title: #2956: Stacking order for floating objects and shape fill transparency
author: C00kieMonsta
body:
Fixes #2956.

Word stacks floating pictures and shapes by an order saved as `relativeHeight`. Bring Forward and Send Backward move an object one step, Bring to Front and Send to Back move it to the top or bottom, and Bring in Front of Text and Send Behind Text move it across the text. Shape fills can be made see-through. WordCraft had none of this: its Bring Forward and Send Backward only changed the wrapping, objects were drawn in document order, and an object in front of the text could be covered by later paragraphs.

Now every floating object has a stacking order. Behind-text and in-front objects are drawn bottom to top in their own layer, in-front objects sit above all the text, comment balloons above them, and a click where objects overlap picks the one on top. Bring Forward and Send Backward step past the nearest object of the same layer that overlaps it, or the next one when none does. The six commands sit in Bring Forward and Send Backward split buttons on the Layout, Shape Format and Picture Format Arrange groups, and in Bring to Front and Send to Back submenus on the right-click menu, greyed for an object in line with the text. Group keeps its members' stacking order, layer first. Pasted objects, Quick Parts and Text from File go on top, as new objects do. Shape Fill has a Transparency submenu (0, 25, 50, 75 % and an exact value) that keeps the colour. The order (also read from a VML `z-index`, higher on top as in CSS) and the transparency are saved in DOCX and drawn on screen and in PDF; PDF structure tags keep reading order.

`arrange.bringForward` and `arrange.sendBackward` change meaning: they used to set the wrapping to In Front of Text or Behind Text, and now move the object one step in the stacking order and are disabled for inline objects. Scripts that want the old behaviour use `arrange.bringInFrontOfText` or `arrange.sendBehindText` (documented in `docs/mcp.md`).

title: Size the text cursor by the font, not the line spacing (#2920)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2920.

The caret took its height from the whole line box (`caret_metrics` returned `baseline - top` and `top + height - baseline`), so any extra line spacing made it taller. With multiple spacing the leading sits below the text, so the caret grew downwards; with at-least and exact spacing it sits above, so the caret grew upwards.

Each layout `Line` now keeps the text's own ascent and descent (`text_asc`, `text_desc`: the tallest font on the line, plus an inline picture above the baseline), measured before line spacing is applied. `caret_metrics` uses those, kept inside the line box, so the caret is as tall as the font, as in Word. An exact spacing smaller than the font still clips the caret to the line, as before.

Lines that end with a line break and leave an empty last line get the paragraph mark's metrics, so the caret there behaves the same way.

Tests:
- `caret_height_ignores_line_spacing`: the caret is the same height at single spacing as at double, at-least 40 pt and exactly 40 pt. Fails without the fix.
- `paragraph_relative_floats_start_above_the_space_before` used the caret's bottom as the bottom of the first line. With the default 1.15 spacing those are no longer the same, so the test now reads the line's bottom from the layout.

title: Opening a missing recent file keeps File open and shows the error (#2938)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2938.

Clicking a file in the Recent list (File > Home and File > Open share it) threw away the result of `file.open` and always closed File. When the file had been deleted or moved, that left the greyed-out no-document window with no explanation.

Now File closes only when the open succeeds, the same way a successful pick from Browse does. If the open fails, File stays open and the error (for example, file not found) shows in red above the Recent list. The message is cleared after the next successful open, and also when File closes, so it does not show up again later. A save prompt or a password prompt still closes File as before, because those return `Ok` with a pending dialog.

The missing file stays in the Recent list. Removing it is left to the maintainers.

Test: `opening_a_missing_recent_file_keeps_file_open_with_the_error` opens a path that does not exist through the Recent handler. It checks that an error comes back and that File stays open.

title: file.rename keeps one extension when the name already has it (#2983)
author: tyrel
body:
Fixes #2983.

## What changed

`file.rename {"name": "renamed.docx"}` on `in.docx` produced `renamed.docx.docx`: the command always appended the file's extension to the name. Agents and scripts usually pass a full file name, so now:

- a name that already ends in the file's own extension, in any case, keeps a single extension, normalised to the file's (`renamed.docx` → `renamed.docx`, `Loud.DOCX` → `Loud.docx`);

- a different extension stays part of the name, so the format is kept (`notes.docm` on a `.docx` → `notes.docm.docx`), and a name that is only the extension (`.docx`) is not stripped.

The result's `name` is the stem that was used, and the params doc says the extension may be typed. Docs: `docs/ui-parity.md` (Rename paragraph, status line, revision history) and `ROADMAP.md` (progress log, status line, revision history).

title: IME: the composition is drawn in the text's font and size, and CJK in it no longer shows boxes
author: arcanii
body:
## What it does

Two problems with how an input method's composition (the text an IME shows before it is committed) is drawn on the page, both seen with the Microsoft Japanese IME on Windows:

- **Boxes instead of Japanese.** In a build without craft-fonts' CJK interface faces (a build from source without `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR`), the composition showed a box until it was committed. The committed text was drawn correctly. A Chinese IME shows the same boxes, seen again on 2026-10-25 in a build of `main` at `c72e1ca`.
- **Latin letters look bold.** While typing romaji, the letters looked larger and heavier than the same letters once committed. The composition was drawn in the interface font (Inter) at 0.8 of the line's height.

Now the composition is drawn as Word draws it: in the font and size of the text it goes into, on that text's baseline, and CJK characters in it are drawn.

## How

**Boxes.**
- The composition is interface text. For a script the interface fonts lack, it borrows a document fallback face (#565), but only one of 16 MB or less.
- On Windows, WordCraft's document fallback for kana and Han is Microsoft YaHei (`msyh.ttc`, 19 MB), so nothing was borrowed. A release build has craft-fonts' CJK faces built in and hid this.
- A CJK composition now asks for the CJK UI font, as the window caption and the comment balloons already do (`want_system_cjk`), and borrows no document face for CJK (`caption_char_covered`).

It returns `None` in turned text.

title: Render: small text in a minified picture stays crisp
author: kevin2y
body:
…ays crisp

A 1920x1080 screenshot placed across a page is drawn about 2.2x smaller than its pixels. vello_cpu's bilinear sampler reads 2x2 taps, so at that reduction one-pixel glyph strokes broke into colour speckle: the same picture read clearly in WPS and poorly here.

Resample every picture that would be minified to the exact device pixel size first, then draw it 1:1 so the sampler never minifies. The resample is a single-pass 2D fractional-coverage box average in sRGB space: integer bins at a non-integer ratio would alternate 2-px and 3-px wide, making a 1-px line pulse as it crosses bin edges. Premultiplied values average correctly on their own, so a partly transparent picture stays right.

An exact area average also flattens stroke contrast, so a mild zero-sum 3x3 unsharp pass follows it: the weights sum to zero, so flat colours and the picture's overall brightness are untouched and only local slopes steepen. Measured on that screenshot: gradient energy 5.96 to 6.78, mean brightness 179.8 to 179.7, RMSE against a reference render 32.5 to 21.7.

Averaging in linear light is deliberately not used: under a screen of thin white glyphs the white carries far more linear energy than its sRGB value suggests, so dark backgrounds lift and a black window turns grey (measured: mean 179.8 to 184.8, shadows 17.4 to 21.6). A Mitchell-Netravali cubic was tried too and blurred more than the box: its support is twice as wide at the same scale.

A tiled background keeps its 96-dpi tile period: the tile's page footprint comes from the original pixels, so resampling cannot shrink the repeat. Only the axes that are actually minified are resampled -- an axis that would have to grow keeps its source pixels and is left to the sampler, so an anisotropic picture cannot allocate a huge intermediate bitmap. And the unsharp pass clamps r/g/b to the sharpened alpha, so a partly transparent edge cannot end up with r > a.

Results are cached by media name and target size, under the byte and …

title: #2999: a file dialog that "cancels" at once asks again without a parent, then shows the built-in browser
author: benandez
body:
Closes #2999 (pending the reporter's confirmation).

**Problem:** on some Linux desktops, Save As, Export and Open do nothing at all. On Linux, rfd asks the xdg-desktop-portal FileChooser for a dialog. When the portal fails to show one, it answers with a failure response code, and rfd turns any non-success code into "cancelled" (`parse_response` in rfd 0.17's `portal/mod.rs`). So WordCraft sees a cancel, finishes quietly and logs nothing. GridCraft goes through the same portal and works on the reporter's machine. The main difference is that WordCraft passes its window as the dialog's parent (`set_parent`), which on Wayland goes through xdg-foreign.

**Fix** (`apps/wordcraft/src/file_dialogs.rs`):
- A "cancelled" answer within 300 ms, quicker than anyone can see a dialog and dismiss it, is treated as a failure.
- The dialog is then asked for once more **without a parent window**, as GridCraft does.
- If that also comes back at once, the app gets an error and shows its **built-in file browser**. That path already exists for setups with no portal at all (#576).
- Each step logs a warning, so the next report's log shows what happened.
- `ponytail:` comment on the heuristic. A portal that fails more slowly than 300 ms still reads as a cancel. The real fix would be for rfd to expose the response code.

**Tests:** `an_instant_cancel_retries_then_falls_back` covers a real pick; an instant cancel followed by a successful retry; both instant, which gives the built-in browser; and a slow real cancel on either attempt, which isn't retried.

**Tested by hand** on CachyOS KDE (Wayland), where the portal works:
- Save As and Export › PDF open the KDE dialog as before.
- Cancel closes the dialog and nothing is saved.
- `WORDCRAFT_FILE_DIALOG=builtin` shows the built-in browser.

I can't reproduce the reporter's compositor locally. I've asked for their compositor, portals and log on the issue, and offered them `WORDCRAFT_FILE_DIALOG=builtin` as a workaround.

title: Insert Table of Figures: a dialog with the caption label (Table, Equation, your own) (#3013)
author: tyrel
body:
Closes #3013.

## What changed and why

**References › Insert Table of Figures** always built a list of Figures: the ribbon sent `{}`, so the label defaulted to Figure, and there was no way in the interface to build a list of tables or of a custom label.

- **Table of Figures dialog** (`crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs_refs.rs`). It offers:
  - **Label**: Figure, Table, Equation, the user's own labels from New Label…, and any label the document's captions use
  - **Include label and number**
  - **Include page numbers**
  - **Page numbers at the right margin**
  - **Tab leader**
  - a preview of the list

  The ribbon button, the KeyTip and command search all send `{}` and now open the dialog, the same way Insert Caption and Insert Index already do (`input_dialog` in `lib.rs`). Commands sent with parameters still run directly.
- **`references.tableOfFigures`** takes `includeLabel`, `pageNumbers`, `rightAlign` and `tabLeader` and writes the TOC switches for them (ECMA-376 §17.16.5.68):
  - `\c "<SEQ identifier>"` lists the captions with that label
  - `\a "<id>"` lists them without their label and number
  - `\n` leaves page numbers out
  - `\p " "` puts the page right after the text

  A multi-word label uses its SEQ identifier (`Photo_Plate`), as captions do.
- **Updating a list:**
  - Captions are matched on their whole label (SEQ identifier, any case) rather than a text prefix, so `Figures 2: …` no longer appears in the list of Figures.
  - A table of figures in a file from Word, which writes its switches in a different order (`TOC \h \z \c "Figure"`), is recognised and updates.
  - Update Table keeps each list's tab leader, as the table of contents does.
- **Table of contents code** (`references.rs`) uses a new `FieldCode::is_table_of_figures` (`\c` or `\a`) in place of the old `!has('c')` checks, so a table of figures built with `\a` is never treated as the table of contents.

author: jcagudelo12
body:
Fixes #3049.

**Problem:** with only a picture on the clipboard, Ctrl+V pasted nothing when Ctrl was released
before V — the natural one-hand Left Ctrl+V motion. Releasing V first (e.g. with Right Ctrl)
worked, so it felt like a delay. egui-winit keeps the Mod+V press, so WordCraft pastes a picture on
V's release, and `is_paste_release` required `modifiers.command` at that moment.

**What changed** (`crates/ui-egui/src/keys.rs`, `canvas.rs`):
- A plain V press arrives as a Key event; a Mod+V press doesn't (egui-winit eats it). So a V
  release with no V press seen since the last one was Mod+V.
- The canvas remembers the modifiers last held with Mod and uses them for that release, so
  Mod+Shift+V and Mod+Alt+V stay apart.
- The remembered state is cleared on any other key press and on window focus changes, so a V

V, Ctrl+B then a stray V release, and Ctrl+Shift+V don't; V released first still pastes) and
`paste_release_modifiers_fall_back_to_those_held_with_mod`. The first fails without the fix (0
pictures). `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui`: 707 unit tests pass.

**Verified by hand:** Ubuntu, GNOME Shell 50.1, Wayland, Left Ctrl+V released Ctrl first now pastes.

title: Paste: a copied picture file wins over the name beside it
author: renlixing87
body:
## What happens

Copy a picture in Finder (or any file manager) and paste: the **file's name** arrives as text and the picture never does.

```
Screenshot 2026-10-14 at 13-08-08.png
```

Copying pixels — a screenshot tool, Preview's Copy — works. That is why this reads like a clipboard problem, but on this path the clipboard is fine.

## Why

A file manager's Copy leaves two things on the pasteboard: the file itself (`public.file-url`) and the file's **name** as `public.utf8-plain-text`. `system_clipboard::fill` reads the text first and fills `text`; the picture branch below only runs when `text` is absent, so the name wins and the file is never looked at.

`names_picture_files` does exist for this, but it only recognises `file://…` or an absolute path, and Finder puts a bare name there.

## Fix

`edit.paste` now asks the clipboard for **copied files** before it reads its text (`paste_picture::paste_copied_files`) and inserts the pictures among them. It only takes over when the clipboard really holds files *and* at least one of them is a picture:

- a copy of `notes.txt` still pastes `notes.txt`
- text that merely names a picture is not a copy of one, and still pastes as text
- pixels and encoded images keep the existing path — `edit.paste` and the paste event from Ctrl/Cmd+V both go through `fill`

`paste` was split into `read` + `insert` so the clipboard is read once, and `paste_copied_files` reuses the same insertion code.

## Tests

- `system_clipboard::tests::copied_picture_files_win_over_the_name_beside_them`
- `system_clipboard::tests::a_copied_file_that_is_not_a_picture_pastes_its_name`
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui --lib`: **707 passed, 2 ignored**

## Verified on a real build

Built macOS 0.8.0 from this branch and drove the app through its control port with real key events:

| Clipboard | Result |
| --- | --- |
| only a file (`«class furl»`) | picture inserted |
| written the way Finder does it (file URL **and** the file name as text) | picture inser…

title: Keep a single trailing space when exporting a paragraph to ODT
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/formats/src/odt.rs:354-390 (plain_inlines)` (no existing issue): ODT export loses a single trailing space at the end of a paragraph.

## Cause
In `plain_inlines`, a run of trailing spaces at the end of a paragraph was flushed as one literal space plus `<text:s/>` for the rest. The ODF whitespace rules, which the importer follows, drop a literal space at the end of a paragraph. A paragraph ending in exactly one space (e.g. "trail ") therefore lost it on re-import.

## Fix
When the text run is the last inline of the paragraph, `plain_inlines` now flushes its trailing spaces as if the previous character were a space. The last space is written as `<text:s/>` and survives re-import. The regression test round-trips "trail " and "trail  ".

## Verified
- Regression test `odt::tests::explicit_spaces_at_paragraph_ends_are_kept`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-formats --lib odt::tests::explicit_spaces_at_paragraph_ends_are_kept`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Trailing spaces in runs that are followed by another inline in the same paragraph. The importer already keeps them, so they are still written as before.

title: Rendering reuses one render context, so typing starts no threads (#3027)
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #3027

Every page, area and icon render built its own multi-threaded vello_cpu `RenderContext`, and with it a rayon thread pool that started, spin-waited and was torn down again: a few threads per keystroke while typing. Renders now share one kept context, reset to each render's size, so typing starts no threads at all.

## What changes

- **One kept context** (`crates/render/src/context_pool.rs`): a render takes the kept context, reset with `reset_and_resize` to its size (the way vello_cpu is meant to be reused), and gives it back when done. Its worker threads live as long as the app.
- **`render_region`** (pages, areas, thumbnails, previews) and **`icon_lib::render`** take and give back that context; nothing else in them changes, so the page drawing code is untouched.
- **Overlapping renders still work:** while one render holds the context (another thread, or a render inside a render), the next one builds its own, as before; only one is kept afterwards.
- **A render that panics** never gives its context back, so a half-drawn context (a layer still pushed) is dropped, not reused. The lock is only held to take or put back the context, never while drawing, so it can't be poisoned by a draw.
- `render_text_line` and `render_items` already render single-threaded (no pool) and are unchanged.

## Measured (Windows, debug build)

Typing `a` through the control channel (`text.insert`, ~150 characters in 15 s) into a new blank document, counting the app's threads by id and start time every ~1 ms:

| | Idle 15 s | Typing 15 s | CPU time while typing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` (two runs) | 18 threads | 388 / 295 threads | 2.27 s / 3.19 s |
| this PR (two runs) | 21 threads | 21 threads | 1.58 s / 1.62 s |

The three extra threads are the kept context's workers; while typing no thread is created.

Not checked here: macOS (the report's M3) and Linux; the change is the same code on every platform. The web build renders single-threaded and is unaffected apart from reusin…

title: Add Thai Distributed and Khmer Justify paragraph alignments
author: inmean
body:
## What

- **Thai Distributed** (`w:jc="thaiDistribute"`) is now its own alignment. It was read as plain Distribute and written back as `distribute`, so the round trip lost it. A wrapped line's spare room is spread evenly between Thai/Khmer clusters; the last line is not stretched.
- **Khmer Justify** is a new alignment for Khmer, which has no spaces between words. Room goes to phrase spaces first (cap 0.5 em), then word boundaries (ZWSP, ។ ៕, script changes; 0.2 em), then orthographic syllables (0.06 em). Leftover is shared evenly so lines still reach the margin. Nothing is added inside a syllable or coeng stack.
- **File format:** Khmer Justify is written as `thaiDistribute` plus an ignorable `wc:khmer="1"` attribute (`urn:wordcraft:ext`, in `mc:Ignorable`). Word shows Thai Distributed; WordCraft restores Khmer Justify. Files from Word have no mark and stay Thai Distributed. RTF uses `\qt` for both.
- **U+200B** is an invisible zero-width marker whatever the font has: Khmer OS Battambang/New have no glyph for it.
- Commands `para.thaiDistribute` and `para.khmerJustify` (`Mod+Alt+J`), Paragraph dialog entries, Thai Distributed in the parity catalog, `docs/khmer-justify.md` (script rules and font study).

## Scope

Per review, this PR is the alignments only. The Mod+Enter page-break change and the Khmer font substitution that were briefly on this branch are removed; they will be separate PRs.

## Tests

New tests in `doc` (khmer, thai), `layout` (`khmer_just`, `tests_khmer.rs`), `docx` (round trip, Thai vs Khmer kept apart), `formats` (RTF `\qt`) and `ui-egui` (Paragraph dialog Harness test). title: Linux X11: Vietnamese input over XIM no longer garbled; typing doesn't move the IME spot (#2932)
author: Nghiathan13
body:
Fixes the X11/XIM part of #2932 (garbled Vietnamese input). The Wayland part is #2950 / #2974.

## Problem

On X11 (and XWayland), input methods talk to the window over XIM. A Vietnamese fcitx5 engine that fixes a word by forwarding BackSpaces and then committing the new letters, such as Ngó Sen's default mode, typed garbled text: `tieengs vieetj cos daaus` came out as `Tigếgv ieêt caâuấu` or `Ieêngếng vi eêtệuấ`.

WordCraft moved the IME spot to the caret after every keystroke. egui-winit sends that as `set_ime_cursor_area`, and winit 0.30 turns it into a synchronous `XSetICValues` once it handles the next X event. Forwarded BackSpaces that arrive during that wait are filtered again and sent back to the input method. So they reach WordCraft late, after the committed letters, and the engine sees a BackSpace nobody typed. A bare winit window shows the same thing, without egui or WordCraft (details in #2932). I've reported it to winit: rust-windowing/winit#4777.

## Fix

- **`crates/ui-egui/src/ime_spot.rs`** (new): over XIM, the spot stays where it is once keys come in, and catches up with the caret at the next click, tap or window focus. Every frame notes its keys and clicks, including frames that don't place the caret.
- **`canvas.rs`**: both places that report the IME rect (the text caret and the equation caret) go through `ime_output`, which asks `ImeSpot` for the rect.
- **`Services::xim`**: the desktop app sets it when the window's display handle is Xlib or Xcb. Windows, macOS, native Wayland and the web keep moving the spot with the caret, as before.

The first version moved the spot once typing had paused for 300 ms. That fixed fast typing, but words typed about 350 ms apart still came out garbled. The app learns of a key only after the input method has handled it, and that late notice plus frame timing put the "paused" move right on the next key. An fcitx5 XIM log showed `SET_IC_VALUES` arriving 30 to 40 ms after a key, while the input method was still forwa…

title: Keep page border offsetFrom, display and zOrder on save
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3075

## Cause
The writer hardcoded `w:offsetFrom` as `text` on `w:pgBorders`, and the reader kept only the four sides. As a result `offsetFrom` was always rewritten as `text`, and `w:display` and `w:zOrder` were dropped.

## Fix
The section model now stores the three page-border attributes. The reader fills them in, treating a missing `w:offsetFrom` as the schema default `text`; such a border is written back with an explicit `text`, which has the same meaning. The writer emits the attributes as read. Borders created in WordCraft save with `offsetFrom` set to `page`.

## Verified
- `page_border_attributes_round_trip` and `new_page_border_is_measured_from_the_page_edge` fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it.
- `text_offset_is_kept` and `missing_offset_from_is_not_written_as_page` also pass on `main`. They guard against the fix writing the wrong value for text-measured borders.
- All four pass with the fix: `cargo test -p wordcraft-docx --test section_page_borders`.

## Verified
- Regression tests `page_border_attributes_round_trip`, `new_page_border_is_measured_from_the_page_edge`, `text_offset_is_kept`, `missing_offset_from_is_not_written_as_page`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-docx --test section_page_borders`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Layout still ignores these attributes, and the `firstPage` and `notFirstPage` display modes are still not implemented. Both are tracked separately.
