title: #1549: a Thai run with Latin finds one installed font covering it all
author: mikael2
body:
## Problem

On Linux with Noto Sans Thai installed, a Thai run mixing Latin letters, digits and ฿ was split across two faces. The run fallback loaded the script's preferred family (Noto Sans Thai, which has no Latin letters) and stopped: every character then had *some* face, so an installed font mapping the whole run (here IBM Plex Sans Thai) was never tried.

Three tests failed deterministically on such a machine (Ubuntu 26.04 with `fonts-noto-core` and IBM Plex):
- `fonts::fontdb::tests::a_thai_run_with_latin_falls_back_to_one_face`
- `layout::tests_complex::a_missing_thai_font_draws_the_whole_run_in_one_thai_face`
- `layout::tests_complex::a_thai_substitute_without_latin_hands_the_run_to_one_face_covering_it`

GitHub's runners probably have no Thai font, so these tests skip there.

## Fix (`crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs`)

When no loaded face covers the run, `search_run` now looks through the coverage index for the first installed file that maps the whole run.
- **Whole family:** it loads that file's whole family, and marks the family's files as used in the index so no file is loaded twice. Path order can reach `…-Bold.ttf` before `…-Regular.ttf`, and the fallback order prefers the regular weight.
- **Concurrent searches:** it looks at the loaded faces again even when it loaded nothing itself. A concurrent search may just have loaded the font and taken its files off the index; without the re-check, the miss was cached for good. This made the layout Thai tests fail in 13 of 15 runs before the fix.

`indexed_fallback` (one character) works as before; it now shares `load_indexed` with the run search. `family_paths` is factored out of `load_cataloged`.

## Tests

- New: `fonts::fontdb::tests_sysfonts::a_run_no_preferred_face_covers_whole_loads_an_installed_font_that_does`. It uses synthetic patched Source Sans 3 files, so it doesn't depend on installed fonts. It fails without the fix, and also fails when only the matching file (Bold) is loaded instead of the whole famil…

title: Page borders honour w:offsetFrom and measure from the text by default (#3073)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3073.

Page borders were always placed `w:space` points from the page edge, whatever `w:offsetFrom` said. ECMA-376 §17.6.10 makes `"text"` the default, so a border with no `w:offsetFrom` (or `"text"`) has to be measured from the text margins.

**Cause:** the DOCX reader read `w:pgBorders` with the shared `borders()` helper, which keeps only the sides, and `page_border_rules` in `crates/layout/src/lib.rs` always measured from the page edge.

**Changes**

- `SectionProps` gets `page_borders_from_page` (false by default, so `"text"`). It is skipped in JSON when false, like `page_num_set`.
- The reader sets it from `w:offsetFrom="page"`.
- Layout: when the borders are measured from the text, each side sits `space` points outside the text margin (gutter included), clamped to the page. With the repro (72pt margins, `w:space="24"`) the border is now 48pt from the page edge, not 24pt.
- Mirrored margins: borders measured from the page edge stay where they are on even pages, as before. Borders measured from the text now move with the margins.
- Writer: `w:offsetFrom` used to be written as `"text"` every time. It now writes `"page"` when the file said so. Without this, saving a page-edge document after the layout fix would move its borders. This covers only the `offsetFrom` part of #3075; dropping `w:display` and `w:zOrder` is left for that issue.
- `docs/layout-parity.md`: the page borders row now names the behaviour and the tests, and there is a revision entry.

**Tests**

- `layout::tests_pages::page_borders_follow_offset_from`: the default (text) border is at 48pt on all four sides, and at 24pt with `page_borders_from_page`. Before the fix it was 24pt in both cases.
- `layout::tests_pages::text_measured_page_borders_follow_mirrored_margins`: 108/36pt margins with mirror margins put the border at 84pt / page width − 12pt on odd pages and the other way round on even pages.

title: #2802: Delete on whole table cells leaves one empty paragraph in each
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #2802

Delete with whole table cells selected cleared the text of each paragraph but kept the paragraphs, so a cell that held three paragraphs was left with three blank lines. Now each cell is emptied to one paragraph, as in Word.

## What changes

- **Delete on selected rows, columns, the whole table or one cell** (and Backspace where it clears rather than deletes, e.g. one cell of several): each selected cell is left with exactly one empty paragraph, however many it had.
- **Formatting:** that paragraph keeps the paragraph and mark formatting of the cell's last paragraph, whose mark is the end-of-cell mark (a cell whose last line was right-aligned stays right-aligned).
- **Nested tables** inside the cleared cells go too.
- **One undo step** brings everything back. The caret goes to the start of the first cleared cell, also when that cell started with a nested table.
- **Unchanged:** Backspace on whole rows, columns or the table still deletes them (#1844); with Track Changes on, Delete still marks the cells' text deleted as before.

## Engine

`text.delete` (and `text.backspace`, `text.deleteWordBack`, `text.deleteWordForward`) with whole cells selected now go through `table::clear_cells`: one `delete_range` per cell, from its first paragraph's start to its last paragraph's end, bottom up. Content-control locks are checked for every cell before anything is deleted; markers of controls that reach outside a cell are kept, as for any delete. No new commands or parameters.

## Checked against Word (2019, Windows)

A 3×3 table with several paragraphs in a cell (centred, left, right-aligned) and a table nested in another cell: Delete on a selected row, on a selected column and on the row holding the nested table. Each cell is left with one empty paragraph with the last paragraph's alignment; text typed there afterwards is plain; the nested table is removed.

title: Saving and exporting: SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH stands in for the clock
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #3083.

## The problem

```console
$ wordcraft-cli convert in.txt out1.pdf && sleep 2 && wordcraft-cli convert in.txt out2.pdf
$ cmp out1.pdf out2.pdf   # 88 bytes differ, same size, pages identical
/ModDate(D:20261019091517Z)   vs  …091519Z)
<xmp:ModifyDate>…T09:15:17…   vs  …09:15:19…
<xmpMM:InstanceID>…           vs  …
```

So a PDF cannot be checked by its hash, cached by content, or compared between runs.

## Where the date actually comes from

Not where it looks. `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs` has what seems to be the fallback:

```rust
let date = parse_iso(&c.created).or_else(|| now_unix().map(civil));
```

Making **that** honour `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` changes nothing, which I established by trying it — the exported dates stayed on the clock. Instrumenting it says why:

```
DBG metadata(): c.created="2026-10-19T09:50:00Z"  SDE=Some("1791208980")
```

`c.created` is already set by the time the export runs. `Session::stamp_save` writes the document's `created` and `modified` properties with `cmd::now_iso()`, and the convert path goes through it, so the clock enters the **document** before any export reads it. (`wordcraft-cli info in.txt` reports `created: ''` beforehand, which is what sent me to the wrong place first.)

## Change

`saved_iso()` provides what a saved or exported file records: `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` when it holds a non-negative whole number of seconds, else the clock, per the [reproducible-builds specification](https://reproducible-builds.org/specs/source-date-epoch/). `stamp_save` uses it.

**`now_iso()` keeps the clock, and keeps its callers.** A comment, a tracked change and a version are events that happened at a time; pinning those would misdate real edits, and the variable has no business doing it. Only what a file records follows it — the same line I drew in storytold/vectorcraft#2947, where the encryption seed and the recovery heartbeat stayed on the real clock.

```
pinned, 1s apart   PDF   identical, date reads D:20261005140300

title: Page text on Linux is hinted like FreeType's hintslight
author: mikael2
body:
## Problem

Page text on Linux looked soft next to Firefox and other apps. Glyph outlines were drawn unhinted, so baselines, x-heights and cap heights fell between pixel rows, and every horizontal edge was smeared over two rows. Example: a 4K screen at 145% KDE scaling, where XWayland gives the window native pixels.

## Fix

On Linux and BSD, on-screen page rasters are now hinted the way FreeType's `hintslight` draws text:
- **`crates/fonts`:** `FontDb::hinted_outline` returns glyph outlines hinted with skrifa's Light target, keeping linear metrics, in device pixels. Outlines and hinting instances are cached per face and size, with bounded caches. The engine follows FreeType's light mode: the autohinter for TrueType outlines, even when they carry their own instructions; the font's own hinting for CFF fonts and for fonts that need their instructions to assemble glyphs.
- **`crates/render`:** a new `RenderOptions::hinting` option, off by default. Each glyph's baseline goes on a whole pixel and its hinted outline is drawn. Rotated, mirrored or unevenly scaled views and colour glyphs stay unhinted.
- **`crates/ui-egui`:** `screen_render_options` turns hinting on for `unix` targets other than macOS. macOS, Windows, wasm and exports are unchanged.

Nothing moves sideways, so line breaks don't change.

## Measured

| | Ink (first line) | Row-profile distance to Firefox |
|---|---|---|
| headless Firefox, Arial 21.27 px | 323k | — |
| before | 330k | 18k |
| hinted with the font's own TrueType instructions | 338k | 25k |
| **hinted with the autohinter (this PR)** | **320k** | **4k** |

title: Layout: with multiple line spacing a page's last line may hang its leading
author: pick2510
body:
## Summary

Word fits a page's last line once its **text** fits: the leading that multiple line spacing (above single) adds under the text may run past the bottom margin. Exact and at-least spacing still need the whole line.

WordCraft required the whole spaced line to fit. Double-spaced papers therefore broke a line early, and widow control then often moved two lines, so documents drifted a page or two over their length.

## Measurement

Measured in Word for Mac 16.113 (compatibility mode 15) with synthetic documents: 60 one-line paragraphs of 12 pt Times New Roman, widow control off, and the bottom margin set so that 24 lines fit plus a given slack for the 25th.

| Line spacing | Slack for line 25 | Word: lines on page 1 |
|---|---|---|
| double / 1.5 (auto) | 2, 6, 10, 12, 13.4, 13.7 pt | 24 |
| double / 1.5 (auto) | 13.9, 14, 16, 20, 24 pt | 25 |
| exactly 27.6 pt | 14, 20, 27 pt | 24 |
| at least 27.6 pt | 14, 20, 27 pt | 24 |

The single line is 13.8 pt. All 26 probes now match Word; on main, every multiple-spacing case whose slack lies between 13.8 pt and the whole spaced line (20.7 pt at 1.5, 27.6 pt at double) put 24 lines.

On a real double-spaced paper Word reports the page's last two lines at 717.95 pt and 746.35 pt with the bottom margin at 769.9 pt, so the last line's box ends about 4 pt inside the margin.

## Changes

- `crates/layout/src/para.rs`: `Line::hang`, the leading multiple spacing adds under the text (zero for exact, at-least or document-grid spacing, and under a picture taller than the text).
- `crates/layout/src/lib.rs`: the body line-fit check subtracts `hang` unless the page has footnotes, where the existing rule (keep the last line's space after clear of the separator) applies.
- `crates/layout/src/tests.rs`: `multiple_spacing_lets_the_last_line_hang_into_the_bottom_margin` sweeps the probe cases (it fails on main); `space_after_may_overflow_the_bottom_margin_without_notes` now lets the last line's leading pass the margin as well as its…

title: Layout: justified lines shrink their spaces by Word's measured limits
author: pick2510
body:
## Summary

Word 2013+ (compatibility mode 15) fits one more word on a justified line by shrinking the line's spaces (#109). Measured in Word, the limit has two parts:

- the line's spaces give up **at most a quarter** of their width (WordCraft: a fifth), and
- the word now ending the line, with the space before it, may overrun the line by **at most 0.355 of its own width** (WordCraft: no such limit).

So WordCraft wrapped long words too early and pulled short words onto lines Word wraps. Real-world justified paragraphs drifted by a word or two per line from Word's breaks.

## Measurement

Word for Mac 16.113, synthetic justified paragraphs of one repeated word. Each paragraph's right indent leaves room for N words plus one more that fits only if the spaces shrink by x%; x is swept from 0% to 30% in 0.5% steps. The table gives the largest x Word accepts and the overrun that means.

| Last word | Spaces | Largest shrink Word accepts | Overrun | ÷ (word + space) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `i` (2.67 pt) | 12 × 3.33 pt | 5.0% | 2.0–2.2 pt | 0.33–0.37 |
| `n` (6.67 pt) | 12 × 3.33 pt | 8.5% | 3.4–3.6 pt | 0.34–0.36 |
| `nn` (13.35 pt) | 12 × 3.33 pt | 14.5% | 5.8–6.0 pt | 0.35–0.36 |
| `nnn` (20.02 pt) | 12 × 3.33 pt | 20.5% | 8.2–8.4 pt | 0.351–0.360 |
| `nnnn`, `nnnnnn`, `mmmmmmmm` | 12 × 3.33 pt | 24.5–25.0% | (quarter of the spaces) | — |
| `i` / `n` / `nnn` | 12 × 6.67 pt (24 pt spaces) | 4.0 / 5.5 / 11.5% | 3.2–3.6 / 4.4–4.8 / 9.2–9.6 pt | 0.34–0.39 / 0.33–0.36 / 0.345–0.36 |

Varying the font size (8, 12, 20 pt), the font (Arial, Times New Roman) and the number of spaces (4–30) gives the same picture. The wide-space rows rule out a constant-plus-word cap and confirm (word + space). The other findings:

- **Only justified text shrinks.** Left, centred and right lines don't.
- **A paragraph's last line shrinks too.**
- **Compatibility modes 14, 12 and no mode never shrink.**

With this change WordCraft matches Word on every paragraph of the 13 probe documents (41–61 …

title: Word signature lines stay signable after saving a .docx
author: Axxxxpirine
body:
## Cause
Word stores a signature line (Insert › Signature Line) as a VML picture in a `w:pict`: a `v:shape` whose `v:imagedata` is a metafile of the line, its X and the suggested signer, plus an `o:signatureline` element (signer, title, e-mail, instructions) that makes it signable. The DOCX reader read only the picture, so saving wrote a plain DrawingML picture and dropped `o:signatureline`. After a save in WordCraft, Word no longer offers to sign the line.

## Fix
A `w:pict` whose single VML drawing is a `v:shape` with an `o:signatureline` is now read like an OLE object (`read_object`): it is still shown as its picture, and its markup is kept with `keep_embedded` in the image's `ole` field. The writer already writes that markup back through `embedded_xml`, with the relationship ids remapped and the `v:shape` style and alt text updated to the size set in WordCraft. The writer itself is unchanged. Any other `w:pict` is read as before. The doc comments on `InlineObject::Image::ole` and `Embedded::xml` now mention signature lines.

## Verified
- New regression test `signature_line_round_trips` (`crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs`): it fails on `main` and passes with the fix. A resized signature line is written back as a `w:pict` with its `o:signatureline` (signer and title), its shapetype, the new size and its picture part. A plain VML picture in the same paragraph still becomes a DrawingML picture.
- A real contract made in Word (private, not attached) with three signature lines: all three come back as `w:pict` with `o:signatureline` and their signers after `wordcraft-cli convert in.docx out.docx`. The anchored logo is still a `w:drawing`.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
- Signature lines are not signable in WordCraft, and their properties can't be edited.
- The signer's name and X inside the picture are EMF text records, which are not drawn yet; that is #1915.
- Word writes a `v:shapetype` only once, at its first use. A later signature line that uses it relies…

title: Layout: a paragraph of only a page break moves when it doesn't fit
author: pick2510
body:
**Merge after #1172.** This branch is now based on `main` and holds only its own commit (it used to carry #3093, which I've closed as a duplicate of #1172). It's a draft until #1172 lands. Without #1172's last-line rule, a double-spaced break-only paragraph needs its whole line to fit, while Word keeps it once its mark's text fits.

## Summary

Word treats a paragraph holding **only** a page break as an ordinary line. When its mark's text doesn't fit at the bottom of a full page, it goes to the next page, and its break leaves that page blank. Only a break **with text after it** in its paragraph stays on the full page, which #534 established and which this keeps.

WordCraft kept both kinds on the full page. On a real 74-page paper, Word moves the break paragraph before the references onto a page of its own, so the references start on page 52. WordCraft started them on page 51.

## Measurement

Word for Mac 16.113 (compatibility mode 15), Letter page, a full page of 12 pt Times New Roman lines, then either a break-only paragraph followed by "After", or a paragraph starting with the break and then text.

| Lines | Room left | Break-only paragraph | Break, then text |
|---|---|---|---|
| exactly 24 pt | 0 pt | 3 pages (moves) | 2 pages (stays) |
| exactly 24 pt | 10 pt | 3 pages | 2 pages |
| double | 13.2 pt | 3 pages | 2 pages |
| double | 23.2 pt | 2 pages (fits) | 2 pages |

Sweeping the room for a double-spaced break-only paragraph puts the edge at its mark's text height: 13.76–14.26 pt for a 12 pt Times New Roman mark (single line 13.8 pt), and below 28.8 pt for a 24 pt mark (single line 27.6 pt). The break run's size makes no difference. That is #1172's last-line rule (the leading may hang into the bottom margin). Together with that rule, WordCraft matched Word on 28 of the 30 probes. The other two have a mark with no font in a package with no styles part, so Word draws them in its built-in default font, which real files always override.

title: Keep an ordered list's start number in Markdown import
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/formats/src/markdown.rs:160-161,463 and crates/formats/src/model.rs:111 (ListInfo)` (no existing issue): Markdown import ignores an ordered list's start number ("5. a" becomes "1.").

## Cause
The Markdown parser read an ordered list's start number into `Marker.start`, but `ListInfo` had no start field. The number was dropped when the list was built, so every ordered list was numbered from 1.

## Fix
`ListInfo` now has a `start` field. The Markdown parser fills it in, and the list numbering takes the level's start from it. The text and Markdown exporters count from that start, so `5. a\n6. b` and `3. a\n- b\n4. c` keep their numbers. Other importers set `start: 1`.

## Verified
- Regression test `markdown::tests::ordered_list_keeps_start_number`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-formats ordered_list_keeps_start_number`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Two adjacent ordered lists that merge into one numbering instance (for example `1.` followed by `1)`) use the first list's start. A nested list that restarts after its parent item is still numbered from 1 in the text export. A list that starts at 0 still shows 1.

title: A dimmed header fades as one group, so its borders keep one tone where they meet (#2946)
author: GabrielMatozo
body:
Fixes #2946.

`page_display` gave every header, footer and body draw item the dimming alpha (0.45) on its own, so wherever two of them overlapped the alpha was applied more than once: the borders of a table in a dimmed header met at 0.55² of the background and read near-black, and a border two neighbouring cells share read darker grey than the outer ones, while the lines around them were 0.55 of it. Double-clicking into the header or exporting to PDF (which does not dim) showed one tone, as Word does.

The dimming is now on the group: each story's items are collected and wrapped in `Draw::Faded { alpha, items }`, which is drawn as one opacity layer, so a crossing and a shared border keep the tone of the lines. The body dims the same way while a header or footer is edited, and a group is left out when its story draws nothing. title: Fix Paragraph::sentence_at at the first character of a sentence
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/doc/src/para.rs:1397-1427` (no existing issue): Paragraph::sentence_at returns the whole text up to that point when the offset is exactly at the start of a sentence.

## Cause
`sentence_at` scanned the sentence start only over characters with index `< off`, so a sentence starting exactly at `off` was never seen and the start stayed at 0. The end scan also began at `off`, so it missed a terminator right before `off`.

## Fix
The start scan now includes the character at `off`. The end scan starts with `ended` set when the text before `off` ends in `.`, `!` or `?`. It reads that text with `t.get(..off).unwrap_or("")`, like the existing `t.get(off..)`, so it can't panic. The regression test also covers an out-of-range offset.

## Verified
- Regression test `para::tests::sentence_at_sentence_start`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-doc --lib sentence_at_sentence_start`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I left `clamp` and the other selection helpers (such as word selection) unchanged.

title: Write large whole numbers without decimals in format_number
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/doc/src/locale_number.rs:114` (no existing issue): format_number writes whole numbers of 1e15 or more with a ".00" decimal part.

## Cause
`format_number` only took the whole-number branch when `v.abs() < 1e15`. Whole values of 1e15 or more fell through to `format!("{v:.2}")` and got a ".00" suffix. The cutoff was arbitrary, because the `v as i64` cast is safe up to about 9.2e18.

## Fix
Raise the whole-number bound from 1e15 to 9.2e18, which is safely inside the i64 range. Whole values below that bound now print without decimals. A regression test covers 1e15, 2.5e15, -1e15 and 9e18, and checks that 1e15 + 0.5 still gets two decimals.

## Verified
- Regression test `locale_number::tests::large_whole_numbers_have_no_decimals`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-doc --lib large_whole_numbers_have_no_decimals`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Whole numbers at or above 9.2e18 still use the two-decimal format. The bound keeps a margin below i64::MAX (about 9.223e18), so the cast cannot overflow. I did not change the decimal-separator handling or the negative-zero handling.

title: Task panes: draw them with craft_ui::panes; Styles docks left or right or floats
author: aiongg
body:
## What

WordCraft's ten task panes are drawn by `craft_ui::panes` (`PaneHost`, `SidePolicy::Columns`). Each pane gets the shared title bar (title, ▾ menu, ×), a resize edge with pointer and arrow keys, and F6 / Shift+F6 to move between the panes and back to the document. F6 past the last pane (or Shift+F6 past the first) gives the document keyboard focus (`to_document` sets `canvas.want_focus`), so typing goes on in the page.

WordCraft routes F6 itself (`panes::route_f6`; the host's own F6 is off). F6, Shift+F6, Alt+F6 and Alt+Shift+F6 cycle the panes only when nothing is open (a dialog, which includes Customize Keyboard, a file dialog or browser, the colors dialog, a content-control popup, a Zotero alert, keytips or an egui popup) and the keymap doesn't bind that combination. So F6 in a dialog stays in the dialog, and a user's F6 binding runs. Global shortcuts (Ctrl+S, Ctrl+P, Ctrl+H, F7, …) run while a pane title bar or other non-text widget has focus. A focused text field keeps its keys, and so does a focused widget in an open dialog or popup, so Ctrl+Z on a dialog button doesn't undo the document behind it.

Every pane can dock left or right or float (#1756), through the host, and keeps that place between runs. This takes over #2584's behaviour without its own drag, snap and float code.

Commands, command ids and i18n keys stay as they are. `nav_pane` in `ui.json` is unchanged.

## How it maps to panes

| WordCraft | `craft_ui::panes` |
|---|---|
| `panes::Pane`, one variant per pane | `P` |
| `panes::open`: built from the `ViewState` flags (and `restrict.open`) in the order the panels were drawn before: SmartArt Text Pane (only while SmartArt is selected), Navigation, Clipboard at `Start`; Styles, Style Inspector, Accessibility, Alt Text, Restrict Editing, Comments at `End` | `open` |

title: feat(layout, proof): Khmer dictionary line breaking and balanced justification (#604)
author: touchde
body:
## Summary
Khmer is written continuously without spaces between words within a phrase or clause. Previously, Khmer text could only wrap at spaces or risk splitting character clusters.

This PR adds dictionary-based word segmentation and line breaking for Khmer (Unicode UAX #14) and balances justification spacing so lines do not produce unnaturally wide gaps.

Part of #604.

## Key Changes

title: Pointer zoom stretches page rasters until it stops
author: mikael2
body:
> **Stacked on #3090.** This branch contains #3090's commits. The changes for review here are the last two commits: `d5cfc4f5` (the stretch) and `8423a532` (only a raster of what the page shows now stands in, from review). Once #3090 merges, the diff will show only those.

## Problem

While a Ctrl/⌘+wheel zoom eased in, or a pinch followed the fingers, every frame rendered up to two pages again at an in-between size that was shown for a single frame.

Measured on a 4K screen at 145% (2649×1490 window, release build, sample document): **11–15 ms of CPU per zoom frame**, and one wheel notch rendered the page 12 times. A maximised window has about twice the pixels.

## Fix (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`)

While such a zoom moves, each page's last raster is stretched to the new size instead of re-rendered. It is rendered:
- once the zoom stops (drawn hinted, as #3090 does), or
- again mid-zoom whenever the stretch would pass `STRETCH_MAX` = 1.5×, so a long zoom stays legible.

These are still rendered at once:
- **pages with no raster yet;**
- **zooms that aren't gestures:** the Zoom dialog, the slider, a fit zoom;
- **wheel steps with animation effects off:** they land finished in their own frame, as `zoom_steps_land_finished_with_animation_effects_off` requires. "Moving" now means eased (animation effects on) or a pinch. This also corrects #3090's unhinted-frame rule for that case.

Very long Web/Draft pages drawn in tiles still render every frame. Stretching tiles needs their geometry kept apart from the scale; not done here.

## Measured after

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| frames during a zoom | 11–15 ms | 0–1 ms |

| renders for a 1.8× zoom | one per frame | 2–3 |

title: ODT: read an embedded equation's own MathML instead of its undecodable metafile preview
author: matteo-andreuzza
body:
Fixes #3099.

## Root cause

The attached `test_equation_wordcraft.odt` embeds its equation as ODF normally does: a `draw:frame` with a `draw:object` child pointing at a formula sub-document (`Object 1/`, media type `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.formula`) whose own `content.xml` is presentation MathML —

```xml
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block">
  <semantics>
    <mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="italic">mc</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow>
    <annotation encoding="StarMath 5.0">E=mc^2</annotation>
  </semantics>
</math>
```

— plus a `draw:image` replacement preview (`ObjectReplacements/Object 1`) for apps that can't read the object, in LibreOffice's own "StarView Metafile" (SVM) format (`file` reports `StarView MetaFile, version 256`). SVM is **not** WMF/EMF, so #1994 (which teaches the WMF reader to draw its text records, for Equation Editor/MathType OLE objects embedded in **DOCX**) doesn't apply to this bug — different container format, different embedding mechanism.

`crates/formats/src/odt.rs` never had a handler for `draw:object` at all: it only read `draw:image`, and fed those bytes to `make_img`, which calls `sniff_image` (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP/BMP only). SVM bytes don't match any of those, so `make_img` returned `None` and the whole frame was dropped — the equation rendered blank, exactly as reported.

## Fix

`crates/formats/src/odt.rs`:
- On `draw:object`, read the pointed-at sub-document's `content.xml` and scan it for a `math:math` element (`read_formula`, bounded the same way as other XML parsing in this file: depth-capped, node-capped).
- Feed that element to the MathML reader already used for HTML equations (`crates/formats/src/mathml.rs::read`) to get `(linear, display)`.
- At the end of the frame, prefer the equation over the `draw:image` fallback; only fall back to decoding the replacement image when the object holds no math (some other OLE object kind, or malformed input).

No new dependencies. Equati…

title: Content controls: typed text takes the control's formatting, in any language
author: pick2510
body:
## Summary

Filling a form made in German Word, the entries stayed **grey** in WordCraft, on screen and in the saved file. Word shows them in the form's input style (bold black here). There were two causes:

1. **The placeholder style was known only by its English id.** German Word writes the style id `Platzhaltertext`, while the name stays `Placeholder Text`. `content_props` removed only `PlaceholderText`, so typed text kept the grey placeholder style. Restoring a placeholder also added a second `Placeholder Text` style. The style is now found by its built-in name, with the English id as fallback.
2. **The control's own run properties were ignored.** `w:sdtPr/w:rPr` is "the run properties … applied to the text entered into the parent structured document tag in replacement of placeholder text" (ECMA-376 §17.5.2.27). WordCraft kept it only as raw XML to write back, so typed text took the placeholder's formatting instead. The reader now also parses it into `ContentControl::run_props`, and typing over a placeholder uses it. The raw XML is still what's written back.

## Evidence

A real protected form from German Word for Mac (not shareable: 72 content controls, placeholder style `Platzhaltertext`, every control's `w:rPr` naming the input style `Eingabe`, bold black):

- **Word:** in a copy filled in Word, each of the 17 entered values carries exactly the style its control's `w:rPr` names (16 × `Eingabe`, 1 × another).
- **WordCraft before:** text typed over a placeholder (selected, or with the caret inside it) was `rStyle Platzhaltertext`, grey, on screen and after saving.
- **WordCraft after:** the same text is `rStyle Eingabe`. It renders black in the app (headless `ui_shot` with real keyboard input) and in the PDF, untouched placeholders stay grey, and the document keeps a single `Placeholder Text` style.

title: #2986: Search and three other boxes stop resetting the input method every frame
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #2986

On Linux under X11 (also XWayland), WordCraft reset the input method on every frame while the Search box was open. Each reset makes the X11 backend destroy and recreate the XIM input context, which can leave fcitx passing no more keys until WordCraft restarts. Now the box asks for the keyboard only while it lacks it, so the input method is reset once, when focus moves.

## What changes

- **Search** (the title bar's box, Alt+Q): its text box keeps the keyboard as before, but requests focus only when it doesn't have it.
- The same applies to the three other boxes that requested focus on every frame: **Go To › Page**, the **Icons** search box and Caption's **New Label** box.
- **Unchanged:** the box still takes the keyboard back if something else in the dialog took it, now with one reset rather than one per frame. The test covers Tab; a click elsewhere in the dialog goes through the same check (the box no longer has focus). Typing, Enter and Escape behave as before.

## Engine

None: the change is in `crates/ui-egui` (`dialogs.rs`, `dialogs_refs.rs`). In egui 0.36, `request_focus` always interrupts IME, even for a widget that already has focus. egui-winit turns that into `set_ime_allowed(false)` and `set_ime_allowed(true)` in the same frame, and winit's X11 backend recreates the XIM input context for each. The canvas avoids the same thing for Space and Enter since #1179 (#1169). The boxes now check `r.has_focus()` first, as the password and field-code boxes already do.

## Checked on Linux with fcitx5

X11 with fcitx5 5.1.7 over XIM (`XMODIFIERS=@im=fcitx`), on a separate Xvfb display. A script typed in the page, clicked Search, typed `insert table`, pressed Escape, clicked the page and typed again. fcitx5's own log (`--verbose '*=5'`) counted the XIM requests in one run:

| | `XIM_CREATE_IC` | `XIM_DESTROY_IC` | key events forwarded |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 118 | 118 | 81 |
| this PR | 8 | 8 | 81 |

title: #2184: Linux: setting to choose the display server (Wayland / X11)
author: Yasas-Sri
body:
Closes #2184.

## Problem
On Linux the only way to choose between native Wayland and XWayland was the `WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND` environment variable, which is awkward for anyone who launches WordCraft from a desktop entry, the ArtCraft launcher or Flatpak. Each mode has bugs that only happen in that mode (XWayland: #1382, #1240, #1956, #2066; native Wayland: no file drag-and-drop #220, plain title bar on GNOME #78), so people need an easy way to switch.

## What this adds
**File › Options › Advanced › Linux display server**: Automatic (default), Wayland, or X11 (XWayland).

- Stored in `ui.json` (`displayServer`) and read before the window opens, alongside the saved window geometry, so a change applies at the next launch. A note under the option says so.
- **Precedence:** `WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND` → the setting → Automatic. Existing setups that use the variable keep working.
- **Automatic keeps today's behaviour** (XWayland whenever there's an X server, for file drag-and-drop). This PR doesn't change the default, so it composes with #1978 / #2974: whichever heuristic lands becomes the Automatic branch of `uses_x11()`.
- **Fallback instead of failing to start:** X11 is only forced when `DISPLAY` is set; otherwise winit picks Wayland when it's available and X11 when it isn't. So choosing X11 without an X server runs on Wayland, and choosing Wayland without a Wayland compositor runs on X11.
- The log records the choice and why, e.g. `display: native Wayland; the setting asks for wayland`.
- Shown on Linux and the BSDs only; hidden on Windows, macOS and the web.
- `ui.displayServer` (`{"value": "auto"|"wayland"|"x11"}`; no value reads it) for agents and the control channel. Works with no document open, like the other settings.

## Behaviour changes
- `WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND=0` (also `false`, `no`, `off`, any case) now asks for X11. Before, any value meant Wayland. This matches #2974.
- An empty `DISPLAY` is treated as unset, as winit already does.

title: Rename: a name given with the document's extension keeps it, once
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #2983.

`file.rename` appended the document's extension unconditionally:

```rust
destination.set_file_name(format!("{name}.{}", ext.to_string_lossy()));
```

so `{"name": "renamed.docx"}` produced `renamed.docx.docx`. The Rename field in the ribbon edits the stem, which is why it was written that way, but a script or an agent passes a whole file name — as the report says.

### What changed

A name that already ends in the document's extension is taken as the whole file name, whatever its case. Anything else still gets the extension, including a name that merely contains a dot (`Report.2026` → `Report.2026.docm`) and the extension on its own (`.docm` → `.docm.docm`, since that is a stem rather than a file name). The params line now says the extension may be given or left off.

### Tests

Added to `rename_document_preserves_saved_contents_and_rejects_collisions`:

| `name` | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Report.docm` | `Report.docm.docm` | `Report.docm` |
| `Report.2026` | `Report.2026.docm` | `Report.2026.docm` |
| `.docm` | `.docm.docm` | `.docm.docm` |
| `Report.DOCM` | `Report.DOCM.docm` | `Report.DOCM` |

On `main` the first row fails with `Report.docm.docm`. The existing collision, confinement, trimming and case-only-rename assertions are untouched, and the renamed file still holds the original bytes.

`cargo xtask ci`: all steps pass.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Renaming a saved file now accepts its current extension, including case variations, without appending the extension twice.

body:

title: fix(odt): read and write paragraph indents (#2542)
author: irvingoh999
body:
Closes the paragraph-indent half of #2542.

`style:paragraph-properties` was read for alignment, page breaks, keep-with-next, page numbering and the paragraph rule, but never for `fo:text-indent`, `fo:margin-left` or `fo:margin-right`, so an opened ODT lined every paragraph up at the margin whatever its own styles said. The writer never emitted them either, and the shared doc-to-model conversion left `Spacing` empty, so an indent could not survive a save in any direction.

The `test.odt` attached to #2542 has every paragraph indented by its own style. Converting it to .docx emitted no `w:ind` element at all before this change; after it, 62 paragraphs carry their 4.001cm box indent and 2 carry their 3cm first line, and the values survive a round trip through ODT.

Changes:

- `StyleInfo` gains `spacing`; the reader fills `left`/`right`/`first` in points, dropping anything past the widest page (22in) as hostile input, as the page-layout reader clamps its own values.
- `Styles::para` returns the indents along with kind and alignment, and they follow the whole style chain the way the alignment does.
- `para_style_at` writes `fo:margin-left`, `fo:margin-right` and `fo:text-indent` beside the alignment it already wrote.
- `flow_paras_in` carries `indent_left`/`indent_right`/`indent_first` into `Spacing`, including for the paragraph a page break splits off.

Test: `odt::tests::paragraph_indents_survive_import_and_export` covers a first-line indent, a box indent, a hanging indent and a plain paragraph, then the round trip back out to ODT (compared to the two-decimal points the writer emits, which is what ODT itself holds).

Checks: `cargo test -p wordcraft-formats` 184 passed, `cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --test odt_sections` passed, `cargo fmt --all --check` clean, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-formats --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, `cargo xtask layers` clean.

The headers and footers half of #2542 is not touched here.

title: Crop any part of a picture: a side can take 95% of the source, not 45% (#3135)
author: SlavenDj
body:
Closes #3135.

The crop was capped at 45% of the source per side in three places — `picture.crop`, the canvas crop handles and the Picture Format L/T/R/B fields — so a crop could only keep a window around the picture's middle. Keeping the leftmost tenth, say, was impossible: dragging the right side in stopped at 45%, and the left crop could not pass 45% either.

Word crops to a sliver, and the renderer already drew at most 95% of a side away, keeping at least 5% of an axis (`crates/render/src/lib.rs` clamps the crop to 0.95 and floors the visible part at 5%). The command, handles and fields now follow that:

- `picture.crop` clamps each side to 0–0.95 and the two sides of an axis to 0.95 together (left/top honoured first; a side left out is still uncropped). The source-size math used when a crop and a new size arrive together, and `cropped_original_size` (Reset, the original size in the Size dialog), use the true visible part down to 5% instead of stopping at 10%.
- Crop handles: a side can be dragged to 95% of the source; the two sides of an axis stop at 5% (or at the 1 pt minimum display size, as before).
- Picture Format › Crop L/T/R/B: the fields go to 95%, and a field stops where the opposite side already leaves its 5%.
- The crop preview keeps drawing the whole source at the right scale down to that 5%.

### Behaviour
- `picture.crop` takes each side as a fraction 0–0.95: `{"left": 0.9}` keeps the rightmost tenth. `{"left": 0.9, "right": 0.9}` stops the right at 0.05, so an axis always keeps 5% of the source. A side past 0.95 stops at 0.95.
- Documents cropped within the old 45% limit are unchanged; only the ceiling moved.

### Tests
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/objects.rs`: `a_picture_can_be_cropped_to_any_part_of_itself` (90% off the left, the right then stops at 0.05, the original size follows down to 5%, 4.0 clamps to 0.95); the existing clamp test now expects 0.95.

title: Caption a floating picture in a text box under it (#3129)
author: RatkoR
body:
Fixes #3129

## Why
Insert Caption on a floating picture (Square, Tight, In Front of Text…) added the caption as a normal paragraph in the text, so it ended up on the left side of the page, not under the picture. Word puts the caption of a floating picture in a text box right under the picture.

## What
Three commits. Please merge them together: the first one alone would make these captions disappear from cross-references and the Table of Figures.

1. **Caption a floating picture in a text box under it.** The caption goes in a text box with no fill, outline or margins. The box is as wide as the picture, placed under it (or over it with "Above selected item") and wraps like the picture. Caption numbering counts captions in text boxes in document order. Captions of inline pictures work as before.
2. **Find captions and bookmarks in text boxes.** Cross-references, the Table of Figures and bookmark lookups now also look in the body's text boxes, so captions from commit 1 (and those Word makes) can be referenced and listed.
3. **Fit floating text boxes with "Resize shape to fit text" to their text.** Word saves its caption boxes almost 0 pt tall and grows them to fit the text. WordCraft did this only for inline boxes, so the selection frame of a Word caption was a thin line above the text. Floating boxes now fit too, and the text of a one-line box can be clicked into (before, the whole small box acted as its border).

## Testing
- New tests for each commit; each fails without its change.
- I tested it by hand in WordCraft with a real .docx document made in Word: a new caption sits under the floating picture (and over it with "Above selected item"), the Word-made caption's frame covers its text, and clicking its text puts the caret there for editing.
- `cargo xtask ci`: everything passes except `fontdb::tests::a_thai_run_with_latin_falls_back_to_one_face`, which fails on `main` too and isn't related.

title: Borders: dotted, dashed and dash-dot borders take Word's dash patterns
author: abweil-fsspx
body:
## Summary

Paragraph, cell and table borders were dashed, but not with Word's patterns: dots were one width on and two off (Word: one and one), dashes four on and two off (Word: three and one), and dash-dot was drawn as plain dashes.

## Changes

- layout: borders use their own strokes (`Stroke::BorderDotted`, `BorderDashed`, `BorderDotDash`); `Stroke::dashes` gives every pattern in line widths. Underlines and the other dotted lines keep theirs.
- pdf, render: lines are stroked with `Stroke::dashes`.

## Evidence

Word figures come from PDFs that Word for Microsoft 365 produced (through Microsoft Graph conversion) from synthetic documents written for each check; nothing from Word is committed.

Checked against Word for Microsoft 365 (ink along each border, on synthetic documents): borders 0.5, 1 and 2.25 pt wide, dotted / dashed / dotDash, are 1-1, 3-1 and 3-1-1-1 widths in Word; before 1-2, 4-2 and 4-2; after as Word (2.25 pt dashes: 6.72 on / 2.28 off in both).

## Related

- Shape outline dashes (`a:prstDash`) are already drawn since #2661; this PR only touches paragraph, cell and table borders.

title: Fonts: single line spacing from the OS/2 metrics, as Word for Windows
author: abweil-fsspx
body:
## Summary

A line at single spacing took its ascent and descent from the hhea table, the line gap above the ascent. Word for Windows measures it from OS/2, as GDI does:

- a font whose `fsSelection` has USE_TYPO_METRICS (bit 7) set gets its typo values: sTypoAscender plus the whole sTypoLineGap above the baseline, -sTypoDescender below;
- any other font its usWinAscent and usWinDescent, with the external leading (the part of the hhea line gap the win metrics don't already cover) above the ascent;
- the hhea values only when OS/2 has no usable metrics.

The two agree for most fonts (Arial, Times New Roman, Segoe UI, Georgia), not for Calibri (win 1950 / 550, hhea 1536 / -512 / 452), nor for a font whose win metrics are much taller than hhea (a sans with win 955 / 205, hhea 740 / -200 / 70: lines 1.16 em apart in Word, 1.01 here), nor for a font with the flag set (TeX Gyre Pagella: typo 726 / -281 / 0, win 1212 / 419; lines 1.007 em apart in Word's rule, 1.631 with the win metrics).

## Changes

- fonts: `word::line_metrics` reads the tables in `font_line_metrics` (so tests can feed it font bytes): `typo_line` when the flag is set and the values are usable (positive ascent, at most twice the em), else `win_line`, else `hhea_line`.

Word figures come from PDFs that Word for Microsoft 365 produced (through Microsoft Graph conversion) from synthetic documents written for each check; nothing from Word is committed.

author: abweil-fsspx

A cell must end with a paragraph, so a cell holding a nested table ends with an empty one after it. Word for Windows gives that paragraph no room: the row is as tall as the nested table. WordCraft laid it out as a blank line, so every nested table added one. Report exports nest their content this way (hundreds of nested tables, nearly each closed by such a paragraph), and a synthetic 45-row case that Word lays out on 3 pages took 5.

title: Tables: autofit widths follow the content as in Word (room beside the table, automatic cells under a preferred width)
author: abweil-fsspx
body:
## Summary

**Tables: a column too narrow for its longest word widens into the room beside the table**

In a table whose widths follow its content (not tblLayout fixed), a column narrower than its longest word widens so the word stays whole. WordCraft took the whole difference from the other columns, down to their own longest words, even with room to spare beside the table: in a 40/200/40 pt grid with two long words, the middle column fell from 200 to 25 pt. Word, for a table without a preferred width, grows the table into the room first and the other columns keep their widths; only what does not fit comes from the columns that can spare it (equal shares each, the rule of #2464).

**Tables: a table with a preferred width and automatic cells shares it by content**

A table whose layout follows its content (not tblLayout fixed), with a preferred width (`tblW` in percent or points) but none for its cells (`tcW` auto), kept its grid in WordCraft: one grid column for six cells (a template whose columns repeat) came out as six equal columns, and so did six equal grid columns. Word ignores the grid there and shares the table's width by the cells' content, as browsers do for an automatic table layout.

## Changes

- layout: `table::autofit` takes the room beside a table without a preferred width (up to the margins; before compatibility mode 15, up to the cell margins beyond them, the first cell's text standing at the margin) before taking from the other columns; the cap on the fitted width follows. Tables with a preferred width (dxa or percent) and fixed tables are unchanged.
- layout: `table::autofit` takes the table's target width. When no cell asks for a width, each column gets its widest line scaled to fill the target if the widest lines fit, else its longest word plus the same share of what its widest line needs beyond it, else its longest word. Tables without a preferred width, and those with cell widths, are unchanged.

title: CLI: run without --file uses the region's paper, like convert (#3152)
author: naxvog
body:
Fixes the first part of #3152: `wordcraft-cli run` without `--file` wrote a Letter page whatever the region, while `convert` and `run --template` used the region's paper (A4 for fr-CH, en-GB, de-DE …).

## Cause

`run` without `--file` and without `--template` built its session from `Document::new()`, which is always Letter. It never went through `file.new`, the path that puts a blank document on the system region's paper. `run --template` already did.

## Fix

The two "no `--file`" arms in `run` (`apps/wordcraft-cli/src/main.rs`) are now one: it runs `file.new`, passing the template only when one was given. With no template, `file.new` gives the same blank document as before (same styles, theme, fonts and compat settings), only on the region's paper. It adds no undo step and doesn't mark the document as changed, and `--author` still applies afterwards.

## Test

`every_run_session_follows_the_region` (`apps/wordcraft-cli/tests/convert_region.rs`) gains a bare `run --cmd text.insert=… --save` case. It fails before the fix (Letter in it-IT) and passes after.

End to end in the CI container, using the command from the issue (`run --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"x"}' --save r.docx`):

| `WORDCRAFT_REGION` | `w:pgSz` |
|---|---|
| fr-CH | `w:w="11906" w:h="16838"` (A4) |
| en-US | `w:w="12240" w:h="15840"` (Letter) |

`cargo test --workspace` shows the same seven font-dependent failures as `main` (e6c5a701) in the same image, and no new ones. fmt, clippy, layers and wasm pass. No rendering change, so no docxide bench.

## Not in this PR

- The issue's second point, `styles.xml` keeping `en-US` as the default language for every region, is left alone: it's unclear whether it should follow the region.
- Headless `wordcraft-cli mcp` (no `--connect`) has the same Letter-page problem. It builds `Session::new(Document::new())` without setting `system_region` (`crates/mcp/src/lib.rs`). That's a separate fix.

title: Fonts: configurable font folders and font aliases (family, regular and bold styles)
author: abweil-fsspx
body:
## Summary

A server renders with fonts it brings along, not installed ones, and documents name fonts it doesn't have under their commercial names. WordCraft read only the platform's folders (on Linux /usr/share/fonts and $HOME/.fonts, so a server had to fake HOME), and a missing family fell to the hard-coded substitutes: "Century Std Book" became Liberation Sans, a sans for a serif, with no way to name the house's own cut.

## Changes

- `WORDCRAFT_FONT_DIRS` (a PATH-style list) adds font folders to the process-wide database, independent of HOME; `FontDb::add_font_dir` does the same at run time (rescans, bumps the generation so memoised resolutions are redone).
- Font aliases: `word::set_aliases` / `word::aliases`, or a file named by `WORDCRAFT_FONT_ALIASES` (`Requested = Family; regular = Style; bold = Style`, parsed by `word::parse_aliases`, errors name the line). An alias applies when the requested family isn't available and its own family is; regular and bold text get the styles it names, italic is matched or synthesized. `word::resolve_in` resolves in a given database with a given alias (testable without the global state). The resolution cache stays bounded and is also cleared when the aliases change.
- Book faces known by name (Century, Garamond, Minion, Caslon…) get the serif substitutes instead of the sans default.

## Evidence

Word figures come from PDFs that Word for Microsoft 365 produced (through Microsoft Graph conversion) from synthetic documents written for each check; nothing from Word is committed.

Measured with the CLI: a document in "Century Std Book" was set in Liberation Sans; now Liberation Serif with no fonts provided, and the house cut with the folder and the alias `Century Std Book = <house family>; regular = Book`. "Verdana = DejaVu Sans" draws a letter in DejaVu Sans instead of Liberation Sans.

title: Hyphenation: liturgical Latin TeX patterns (hyph-utf8)
author: abweil-fsspx
body:
## Summary

Latin runs (`la`, `lat`) fell back to ProofLang::Other and so to the English patterns: "mis-er-i-cor-dia", "mag-nif-i-cat". They now get their own ProofLang variant with hyph-utf8's hyph-la-x-liturgic patterns (the Latin of liturgical books, Solesmes conventions), bundled unmodified, under MIT. Like Bulgarian, Latin is hyphenation only: no spelling or grammar marks, as before.

## Changes

- A letter outside the pattern alphabet is read without its accent; a word still outside it gets the generic heuristic, each part separately around an apostrophe the patterns don't know. The pieces (`tex_patterns`, `core_breaks_tex`) take further hyph-utf8 languages with one line each.
- ui-egui: the dictionary-name match lists the new variant (no dictionary, so no new interface string).

title: Options › Language names the proofing language at the caret (#3150)
author: naxvog
body:
Fixes #3150: File › Options › Language, under *Proofing language*, always said "Spelling and grammar are checked in English (United States).", whatever the text's language. It was a fixed sentence (`crates/ui-egui/src/options.rs`) left over from before WordCraft could proof other languages. Since this PR was opened, #2632 replaced it with the document's default language. This PR now builds on that by showing the language at the caret, which falls back to the document default, so after *Set As Default* it still names the new default. It also covers the cases where nothing is checked.

## Fix

The note now describes the text at the caret, the same way the status bar does. It shows the first of these that applies:

1. The text is marked *Do not check spelling or grammar* → "The text at the insertion point is marked Do not check spelling or grammar." (the caret's own resolved formatting, read like its language: `ribbon::caret_no_proof`).
2. WordCraft doesn't proof the language at all (Bulgarian, Swiss German, `x-none` …) → "{language}: WordCraft doesn't check spelling or grammar in this language yet." This uses `proof::has_dictionary`, the same test the spell checker applies.
3. The language's dictionary is installed but couldn't be read → the status bar's existing "couldn't be read, so it isn't checked" sentence.
4. No dictionary for the language → the status bar's existing "No spelling dictionary for {language} is installed, so it isn't checked…" sentence.
5. Otherwise → "Spelling and grammar are checked in {language}.", using `ribbon::caret_language`.

Cases 2–4 matter because a plain "checked in Polish" would be false when nothing is checked. The two dictionary sentences moved from the status bar's tooltip into `chrome::dictionary_problem`, which both places call. Their msgids are unchanged, and the status bar behaves as before.

title: Dragging a picture near the bottom of a page moves it off the page (#3169)
author: RatkoR
body:
Fixes #3169.

**Cause.** When an object is dropped, `move_object_once` anchors it to the paragraph under its top edge and works out its offset from that paragraph's top. To find that top, it first put the object at offset 0, that is at the top of its paragraph, and laid the document out. Near the bottom of a page, a tall Square-wrapped object there pushes the paragraph's text past the page end, so the paragraph moves to the next page. Its top then reads as the top of that page. The offset worked out from it puts the object about a page below the drop point once the paragraph moves back. The object is still part of the old page, so it is cut off at the page edge and only its selection box shows, over the next page.

**Fix.** The object is first placed on the page exactly where it was dropped, so the text wraps around it as it will in the end. Its paragraph's position is read from that layout, and only then is the object given its offsets from the paragraph's column and top. Drops that are positioned on the page (no paragraph starts on it) stop after the first step, as before.

**Not changed.** A picture dropped so that only its bottom runs past the page end still hangs over the edge, because the drag only keeps a corner on the page. Word's behaviour there hasn't been observed yet, so it's left as is.

**Testing**
- `engine::tests::an_object_dropped_near_the_bottom_of_a_page_lands_there`: a 450 × 300 box dropped at y 400, 600 and 760 on page 1 of a two-page document lands exactly there. Without the fix, the drop at 760 lands at y 1237.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes, except `fontdb::tests::a_thai_run_with_latin_falls_back_to_one_face`, which fails on `main` too.
- I tested it by hand in WordCraft with a real .docx: dragging a picture down page 1 step by step, it now lands where it is dropped, including near the bottom of the page.

title: Expose the document canvas as an editable text area so macOS Zoom follows the caret (#2970)
author: SlavenDj
body:
Closes #2970.

The canvas was exposed to macOS accessibility as `Role::Document` (`AXGroup` / `AXDocument`), which AccessKit treats as read-only, so macOS Zoom (picture-in-picture, "Follow keyboard focus") queried the caret but never followed it — it follows only elements it considers editable text. The canvas node is now `Role::MultilineTextInput` (`AXTextArea`), which keeps the text ranges and makes `AXValue` settable. It is deliberately **not** marked read-only.

`SetValue` / `ReplaceSelectedText` requests are intentionally not handled — edits go through the command registry — and a regression test pins that a `SetValue` request leaves the document unchanged.

title: #2986: Search and three other boxes stop resetting the input method every frame
author: vangel76
body:
## Rebase note
This is #3122 rebased onto current main; the status-line conflicts in ROADMAP.md (progress chain and revision rows duplicating entries already on main) are resolved with both kept.


Closes #2986

On Linux under X11 (also XWayland), WordCraft reset the input method on every frame while the Search box was open. Each reset makes the X11 backend destroy and recreate the XIM input context, which can leave fcitx passing no more keys until WordCraft restarts. Now the box asks for the keyboard only while it lacks it, so the input method is reset once, when focus moves.

## What changes

- **Search** (the title bar's box, Alt+Q): its text box keeps the keyboard as before, but requests focus only when it doesn't have it.
- The same applies to the three other boxes that requested focus on every frame: **Go To › Page**, the **Icons** search box and Caption's **New Label** box.
- **Unchanged:** the box still takes the keyboard back if something else in the dialog took it, now with one reset rather than one per frame. The test covers Tab; a click elsewhere in the dialog goes through the same check (the box no longer has focus). Typing, Enter and Escape behave as before.

## Engine

None: the change is in `crates/ui-egui` (`dialogs.rs`, `dialogs_refs.rs`). In egui 0.36, `request_focus` always interrupts IME, even for a widget that already has focus. egui-winit turns that into `set_ime_allowed(false)` and `set_ime_allowed(true)` in the same frame, and winit's X11 backend recreates the XIM input context for each. The canvas avoids the same thing for Space and Enter since #1179 (#1169). The boxes now check `r.has_focus()` first, as the password and field-code boxes already do.

## Checked on Linux with fcitx5

X11 with fcitx5 5.1.7 over XIM (`XMODIFIERS=@im=fcitx`), on a separate Xvfb display. A script typed in the page, clicked Search, typed `insert table`, pressed Escape, clicked the page and typed again. fcitx5's own log (`--verbose '*=5'`) counted the XIM requests…

title: ODT: read an embedded equation's own MathML instead of its undecodable metafile preview
author: vangel76
body:
## Rebase note
This is #3115 rebased onto current main; the revision-history conflict in docs/file-format-parity.md (both sides adding rows at the table top) is resolved keeping every row. Local cargo xtask ci: fmt/clippy ok; the workspace test step hits exactly one failure, the known pre-existing fontdb flake (a_thai_run_with_latin_falls_back_to_one_face), untouched by this branch — GitHub CI will run the full suite on the PR branch.


Fixes #3099.

## Root cause

The attached `test_equation_wordcraft.odt` embeds its equation as ODF normally does: a `draw:frame` with a `draw:object` child pointing at a formula sub-document (`Object 1/`, media type `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.formula`) whose own `content.xml` is presentation MathML —

```xml
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block">
  <semantics>
    <mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="italic">mc</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow>
    <annotation encoding="StarMath 5.0">E=mc^2</annotation>
  </semantics>
</math>
```

— plus a `draw:image` replacement preview (`ObjectReplacements/Object 1`) for apps that can't read the object, in LibreOffice's own "StarView Metafile" (SVM) format (`file` reports `StarView MetaFile, version 256`). SVM is **not** WMF/EMF, so #1994 (which teaches the WMF reader to draw its text records, for Equation Editor/MathType OLE objects embedded in **DOCX**) doesn't apply to this bug — different container format, different embedding mechanism.

`crates/formats/src/odt.rs` never had a handler for `draw:object` at all: it only read `draw:image`, and fed those bytes to `make_img`, which calls `sniff_image` (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP/BMP only). SVM bytes don't match any of those, so `make_img` returned `None` and the whole frame was dropped — the equation rendered blank, exactly as reported.

## Fix

`crates/formats/src/odt.rs`:
- On `draw:object`, read the pointed-at sub-document's `content.xml` and scan it for a `math:math` element (`read_formula`, bounded the same wa…

title: Dark-theme interface text on Linux no longer looks semi-bold
author: vangel76
body:
## Rebase note
This is #3101 (stacked on the #3090 FreeType-hintslight work) rebased onto current main; the ROADMAP.md status-line conflicts are resolved keeping every entry. Local cargo test hits only the known pre-existing fontdb flake (a_thai_run_with_latin_falls_back_to_one_face), which fails identically on a clean upstream/main checkout on this host; GitHub CI runs the full workspace suite on this branch.


> **Stacked on #3090.** This branch contains #3090's commits. The changes for review here are the last three commits: `db80f133` (ui_shot scale), `8df61fb9` (dark-theme interface text) and `cb7c5df3` (ui_shot clamp, from review). Once #3090 merges, the diff will show only those.

## Problem

On Linux, WordCraft's interface text in the dark theme looked semi-bold. egui's default colour transfer for dark visuals, `2c − c²`, thickens every light-on-dark glyph edge.

## Measured

Same text, Inter, rendered at the UI's body size (18.1 px) and small size (15.2 px) at 1.45× (a 145% desktop), in egui and in headless Firefox:

| Interface text | Ink vs Firefox | Row-profile distance |
|---|---|---|
| light theme, as is | −0.4 % | 5k |
| dark theme, egui default | **+21 %** | 49k |
| dark theme, plain coverage | 0 % | 5k |

title: Layout: a paragraph of only a page break moves when it doesn't fit
author: vangel76
body:
## Rebase note
This is #3100 rebased onto current main; the status-line conflict in docs/layout-parity.md is resolved with both entries kept. The layout suite passes (441/0 on this branch); the only local failures are the two pre-existing Thai font-DB flakes that fail identically on a clean upstream/main checkout on this host (hostile font state), unrelated to this change.


**Merge after #1172.** This branch is now based on `main` and holds only its own commit (it used to carry #3093, which I've closed as a duplicate of #1172). It's a draft until #1172 lands. Without #1172's last-line rule, a double-spaced break-only paragraph needs its whole line to fit, while Word keeps it once its mark's text fits.

## Summary

Word treats a paragraph holding **only** a page break as an ordinary line. When its mark's text doesn't fit at the bottom of a full page, it goes to the next page, and its break leaves that page blank. Only a break **with text after it** in its paragraph stays on the full page, which #534 established and which this keeps.

WordCraft kept both kinds on the full page. On a real 74-page paper, Word moves the break paragraph before the references onto a page of its own, so the references start on page 52. WordCraft started them on page 51.

## Measurement

Word for Mac 16.113 (compatibility mode 15), Letter page, a full page of 12 pt Times New Roman lines, then either a break-only paragraph followed by "After", or a paragraph starting with the break and then text.

| double | 13.2 pt | 3 pages | 2 pages |
| double | 23.2 pt | 2 pages (fits) | 2 pages |

Sweeping the room for a double-spaced break-only paragraph puts the edge at its mark's text height: 13.76–14.26 pt for a 12 pt Times New Roman mark (single line 13.8 pt), and below 28.8 pt for a 24 pt mark (single line 27.6 …

title: Word signature lines stay signable after saving a .docx
author: vangel76
body:
## Rebase note
This is #3097 rebased onto current main; the status-line conflicts in ROADMAP.md and docs/file-format-parity.md (duplicate change entries and revision rows already on main) are resolved with every entry kept.


## Cause
Word stores a signature line (Insert › Signature Line) as a VML picture in a `w:pict`: a `v:shape` whose `v:imagedata` is a metafile of the line, its X and the suggested signer, plus an `o:signatureline` element (signer, title, e-mail, instructions) that makes it signable. The DOCX reader read only the picture, so saving wrote a plain DrawingML picture and dropped `o:signatureline`. After a save in WordCraft, Word no longer offers to sign the line.

## Fix
A `w:pict` whose single VML drawing is a `v:shape` with an `o:signatureline` is now read like an OLE object (`read_object`): it is still shown as its picture, and its markup is kept with `keep_embedded` in the image's `ole` field. The writer already writes that markup back through `embedded_xml`, with the relationship ids remapped and the `v:shape` style and alt text updated to the size set in WordCraft. The writer itself is unchanged. Any other `w:pict` is read as before. The doc comments on `InlineObject::Image::ole` and `Embedded::xml` now mention signature lines.

## Verified
- New regression test `signature_line_round_trips` (`crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs`): it fails on `main` and passes with the fix. A resized signature line is written back as a `w:pict` with its `o:signatureline` (signer and title), its shapetype, the new size and its picture part. A plain VML picture in the same paragraph still becomes a DrawingML picture.
- A real contract made in Word (private, not attached) with three signature lines: all three come back as `w:pict` with `o:signatureline` and their signers after `wordcraft-cli convert in.docx out.docx`. The anchored logo is still a `w:drawing`.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
- Signature lines are not signable in WordCraft, and their properties…

title: Layout: justified lines shrink their spaces by Word's measured limits
author: vangel76
body:
## Rebase note
This is #3096 rebased onto current main. Two conflicts were resolved: docs/layout-parity.md status line (both entries kept) and a real code conflict in crates/layout/src/para.rs, where a sibling branch had extended the hyphen-break condition (the some_and cluster guard) and this branch added the word_from tracking; the merge keeps both changes in that else-if chain. Local note: layout suite passes except the two pre-existing Thai font-DB flakes that fail identically on a clean upstream/main checkout on this host (PR #3078 covers that); this branch adds its own passing tests. GitHub CI runs the full workspace suite on this branch.


## Summary

Word 2013+ (compatibility mode 15) fits one more word on a justified line by shrinking the line's spaces (#109). Measured in Word, the limit has two parts:

- the line's spaces give up **at most a quarter** of their width (WordCraft: a fifth), and
- the word now ending the line, with the space before it, may overrun the line by **at most 0.355 of its own width** (WordCraft: no such limit).

So WordCraft wrapped long words too early and pulled short words onto lines Word wraps. Real-world justified paragraphs drifted by a word or two per line from Word's breaks.

## Measurement

Word for Mac 16.113, synthetic justified paragraphs of one repeated word. Each paragraph's right indent leaves room for N words plus one more that fits only if the spaces shrink by x%; x is swept from 0% to 30% in 0.5% steps. The table gives the largest x Word accepts and the overrun that means.

title: DOCX: majorBidi/minorBidi theme fonts follow the theme font language
author: vangel76
body:
## Rebase note
This is #3088 rebased onto current main; the status-line and revision-table conflicts in docs/file-format-parity.md are resolved keeping every entry.


## Summary

Word draws a `majorBidi`/`minorBidi` theme slot (`w:asciiTheme`, `w:hAnsiTheme`) in:

1. the theme's font for the script of `w:settings/w:themeFontLang/@w:bidi` (`a:font script="Arab"` for `ar-SA`, `Hebr` for `he-IL`, `Arab` for `ur-PK`…), or its `a:latin` font when that language is written in Latin;
2. else the theme's `a:cs`;
3. else Times New Roman.

With no bidi language in the settings it draws Times New Roman whatever the theme says. The run's own `w:lang` and the inherited fonts play no part.

WordCraft read `a:cs` only and let an empty one inherit. Office's usual theme has an empty `a:cs` and `Arab` → Times New Roman, so research papers set in `majorBidi` with `themeFontLang w:bidi="ar-SA"` came out in Calibri Light (Helvetica Neue on a Mac without Carlito) instead of Times New Roman. This corrects the empty-`a:cs` rule recorded with #1619. That rule fits a template whose bidi language has no script entry, which falls through to `a:cs` here as well.

## Measurement

title: #2802: Delete on whole table cells leaves one empty paragraph in each
author: vangel76
body:
## Rebase note
This is #3087 rebased onto current main; the ROADMAP.md status-line conflict is resolved with both entries kept. fmt/clippy clean; GitHub CI runs the full engine suite (typing tests included) on this branch.

Delete with whole table cells selected cleared the text of each paragraph but kept the paragraphs, so a cell that held three paragraphs was left with three blank lines. Now each cell is emptied to one paragraph, as in Word.

title: A display operator without a cataloged size variant still enlarges (#3208)
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
Fixes #3208.

The issue described two symptoms with display-mode n-ary operators (∫, ∬, ∭, ∮, also checked against ∑):

## 1. A display operator with no cataloged size variant stays at its plain (inline-sized) glyph

`crates/layout/src/math.rs`'s `op_atoms` sizes a display-mode n-ary operator by picking the cataloged `MathVariants` vertical size variant nearest a target height. When the font's MATH table has **no** vertical construction cataloged for the glyph at all, the fallback used to set `adv = want` (the *target* size standing in for the glyph's own natural size), so the scale factor always computed to `want / want == 1.0` — exactly undoing what the code's own comment said it did ("scale the nearest one").

I confirmed this empirically: WordCraft's bundled substitute math font on this machine (`DejaVu Math TeX Gyre`) has full vertical-variant data for every n-ary operator I checked, so I couldn't reproduce the exact letter-height symptom here — this font never hits that fallback path. But the defect is real and demonstrable on its own merits (new test below), and it's plausible the font WordCraft resolved to on the reporter's macOS install lacks complete variant data for some operator and does hit it.

Fixed by falling back to the glyph's own measured ink height (`glyph_bounds`) instead of `want`, consolidated into a small `scaled_fallback` helper shared by both the "real stretch (variant/assembly) failed" and "no cataloged variant at all" paths.

## 2. A display operator doesn't grow further to match an unusually tall operand (equation 2 in the issue, a nested stacked fraction)

This **did** reproduce for me. It's `m:grow`, and this codebase's docx reader already gives `m:naryPr`'s `grow` the correct OOXML spec default of **off** when absent (`crates/docx/src/read/math.rs:154`) — correctly different from `m:dPr`'s default of **on** (line 172), a real difference in the spec, not an oversight.

title: A successful native print returns to the document (#3210)
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
Fixes #3210.

## Root cause

`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`'s `poll_printing` turns a terminal print message (`Submitted`/`Failed`/`WorkerStopped`) into a status-bar line, but never closed the Print backstage page:

```rust
let text = printing::feedback(&message, |label| i18n::t(label).to_owned());
self.status(text);
```

On desktop, printing goes straight to the spooler through `services.print_native` (`crates/ui-egui/src/printing.rs`'s architecture comment: "Native printing submits the selected queue on a worker; the browser owns its dialog") — there's no separate OS print sheet on macOS/Windows/Linux that the user interacts with afterward. WordCraft's own File › Print backstage page *is* the whole flow, so once the job is submitted successfully, staying on that page (as reported) means the user has to click Back manually to get back to their document, even though there's nothing left to do there.

I confirmed the actual async submit/poll state machine lives in the shared `craft-ui` library (`State::begin`/`poll`), while "what WordCraft's own UI does when a print job finishes" is this repo's own concern in `poll_printing` — so the fix stays here, not in the shared library.

## Fix

Close the backstage specifically on a successful submission (`Feedback::Submitted`), matching Word's own behavior of returning to the document once a print job is away (the same as after Save). A failed submission still leaves the Print page open, so the error and the settings to fix it stay visible — only success returns to the document.

## Testing

Added `a_successful_native_print_returns_to_the_document`, which fakes `services.print_native` with a channel that resolves immediately to either `Ok` or `Err`, opens the Print page, submits, and checks the backstage closes only on success. Verified it fails without the fix and passes with it.

`cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, full test suite, assets, layers, wasm) aside from a pre-existing, environment-dependent Thai-font test failure u…

title: Status bar names footnotes and endnotes, not just header/footer
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
Found while investigating #3057 ("editing a footnote dims the whole document") against current `main`: that specific issue is already fixed (landed via #2562, after the v0.8.0 build the report used), confirmed with a headless `ui_shot` screenshot of editing a footnote — no dimming. But that same screenshot showed the status bar saying **"Editing header/footer"** while editing a footnote, which is a separate, still-live bug.

## Root cause

`crates/ui-egui/src/chrome.rs`'s `status_bar`:

```rust
if app.session.sel.focus.story != StoryRef::Body && !crate::canvas::in_text_box(app) {
    st(ui, tl!("Editing header/footer"));
}
```

This only checks "not the body, not a text box" — it doesn't look at *which* part it actually is. A footnote or endnote satisfies that condition too, so it always said "Editing header/footer" regardless.

## Fix

Branch on the part's actual kind (`crate::canvas::part_kind`, made `pub(crate)` to reach it from `chrome.rs`): `Footnote` → "Editing footnote", `Endnote` → "Editing endnote", anything else (Header/Footer) → the existing text. title: Compare: don't let a character-level diff scramble a reordered digit run
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## What

Fixes #3094. The compare/combine feature's character-level diff (`lcs_ops` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs`) is a textbook LCS, which finds the *longest common subsequence* — mathematically minimal, but not the most readable edit script. On two short strings that happen to share a few characters in a different order (very common with dates, IDs, phone numbers), it faithfully threads a chain of single-character matches through what a reader expects to be one clean replacement.

Reproduced the reporter's exact case: comparing `"...01.09.2026..."` against `"...19.10.2026..."` at character level. `".2026"` is the genuine common suffix (correctly stripped before the DP table even runs), but the remaining `"01.09"` vs `"19.10"` happen to share the characters `0`, `1`, `.` in a different order — the LCS table finds that 3-character subsequence and the backtrack emits `Del('0') Same('1') Ins('9') Same('.') Ins('1') Same('0') Del('9')`: a scrambled, alternating chain, matching the garbled screenshot in the issue (real Word instead shows one clean `01.09` deletion and one clean `19.10` insertion).

## Fix

Added `collapse_noise_matches`, called only when the compare is at character granularity (`level: "character"`):
- It folds a short (length-1) matched run that sits *strictly inside* a run of edits back into the surrounding delete/insert, flattening that whole region into one clean delete followed by one clean insert — matching what Word's compare visibly does.
- A matched run that opens or closes the entire sequence is the genuine common prefix/suffix `lcs_ops` already stripped before building its table (not a coincidence), so it's left untouched regardless of length.
- Gated on character granularity only: at word granularity, a single matched *token* (a whole word) is essentially never a coincidental match and must survive — the same length-1 threshold would be wrong there (tested explicitly: `compare_at_word_level_still_matches_a_whole_unchanged_word`).
