title: TOC: leave the caret after the table, not inside its own title
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## What

Fixes #3227. `references.toc` (Insert › Table of Contents) builds the TOC's title paragraph, field and entries, but never moves the selection afterward — it stays wherever it was before the command, which for a brand-new TOC on an otherwise-empty (or TOC-first) document is offset 0 of the `TOCHeading` paragraph itself, right before "Contents":

```
wordcraft-cli run --template blank --cmd 'references.toc={"levels":2}' --print
# references.toc: {"anchor":{"off":0,"path":[0],...}, ...}  <- inside "Contents", not after it
```

**Confirmed against real Microsoft 365 Word** (16.0.20527.20054, via a `Claude_Win11` VM I use for this kind of comparison): Insert › Table of Contents › Automatic Table 1 on a document with no headings (Word warns but still creates an empty table) leaves the caret in a fresh paragraph right after the table's "No table of contents entries found." line — typing immediately lands cleanly below the table, not inside it. Screenshot evidence is in the linked issue.

## Why this matters beyond the caret itself

The natural workflow this breaks: insert a TOC placeholder at the top of a new document, write the headings and body text, then call Update Table once done. In WordCraft today, anything typed right after `references.toc` lands *inside* the TOC's own title paragraph — and the later `references.updateToc` call, operating on that now-tangled paragraph, splices the "Contents" title text out of its own paragraph and onto whatever body paragraph happened to end up immediately before the entries, leaving the `TOCHeading` paragraph blank. Full repro with intermediate state is in #3227.

In `crates/engine/src/cmd/references.rs`'s `insert_toc`, after `regenerate_toc` builds the title/field/entries, move `s.sel` to a paragraph right after the table's range (`toc_range`'s `end`) — reusing one that's already there, or inserting an empty one if the table ends the document, matching what I observed Word do.

title: Generated lists: leave the caret after the list, not inside its title
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## What

Fixes #3229, a follow-up to #3227/#3228. The same caret-placement bug found in `references.toc` exists in all its siblings — **Bibliography**, **Table of Figures**, **Table of Authorities**, and (through `references.index`'s first-creation path) **Index** — because they all share `generated_list` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/citations.rs`. That function builds the title paragraph, the field and the entries, but never moves the selection afterward:

```
wordcraft-cli run --template blank --cmd 'references.bibliography={}' --print
# references.bibliography: {"anchor":{"off":0,"path":[0],...}}  <- inside "References", not after it
```

Confirmed the same result for all four commands (see #3229 for the exact repro of each). This is exactly the #3227 scenario on a different References-tab button: insert the list, then keep writing the document — anything typed right after lands inside the list's own title paragraph instead of after it, and a later "Update" call on that list can splice stray text out of its title into whatever body content ends up adjacent.

## Fix

Same shape as #3228: after `update_generated` finishes building the title + field + entries, scan forward past the list's own entries (`ENTRY_STYLE`-styled paragraphs) and move the selection to the paragraph right after — reusing one that's already there, or inserting an empty one if the list ends the document.

title: #2038: a click below a floating table goes to the text, not its last row
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #2038

A table dragged to the right by its move handle floats, and the empty paragraph after it moves up into the room left of the table. A click below the table then landed in a cell of its last row (the nearest line), so the text after the table couldn't be reached with the mouse, and Enter only added lines inside that cell. Now a click below a floating table goes to the paragraph beside or after it, as in Word.

## What changes

- **A click below a floating table** (just below it, far below it, or below it at the left margin) puts the caret in the text beside or after the table, not in a cell of its last row.
- **A click inside the table's area** still lands in the cell under it, also low in a cell of the last row.
- **Vertical sections** (text running down the page): the same, for the turned text there.
- **Which tables:** floating tables in the main text (`w:tblpPr`), dragged there by the move handle or opened from a .docx. Tables in the text flow, and tables in headers, footers and text boxes, are hit as before.
- **Unchanged:** Down from the last row and Ctrl+End already reached the paragraph; they still do.

## Engine

`Page` now lists the top-level body tables placed on it as floating tables (`float_tables`, their paths). `DocLayout::hit` leaves out the lines of a floating table's cells when the point is outside the area its cells cover on the page, as long as other lines are left; on a page of turned text (a vertical section) the nearest turned line is chosen the same way. Everything that places the caret from a point goes through it (`caret.set`, drag selection, Draw Table's start), so they all follow. No new commands or parameters.

## Checked against Word (2019, Windows)

A 3×3 table at the top of a blank document, and again after a paragraph of text, dragged by its move handle to the right and a little down so it floats (Around): the empty paragraph after it moves up beside it, on the left. A click just below the table, far below it and below it…

title: DOCX: packages may unpack to 1 GiB on the desktop; the total limit is named as such
author: pick2510
body:
A real 100 MB manuscript opens in Word, but WordCraft refuses it with:

```
limit exceeded: part word/media/image48.emf decompresses past the size limit
```

That picture is only a few MB. The package holds 45 EMF figures (11 of them over 10 MB, the largest 39 MB), 580 MiB unpacked in all. That is over `MAX_TOTAL` (512 MiB), and the error names whichever part happened to cross it.

## Change
- `MAX_TOTAL` is 1 GiB on the desktop. The web build keeps 512 MiB, because an out-of-memory in 32-bit wasm is a trap, not an error. `MAX_PART` (256 MiB per part) and `MAX_ENTRIES` are unchanged, so a decompression bomb is still bounded.
- `Package::open_limited` says which limit was hit: `part … decompresses to more than 256 MiB` or `the parts decompress to more than 1024 MiB in all`.

## Evidence
| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `wordcraft-cli convert` of that manuscript | refused | 37 pages (Word: 37), 3.0 s, peak RSS 0.97 GB |

The file is private, so the test is synthetic: `the_total_limit_is_reported_as_the_total` uses two pictures, each within the part limit, that together pass the total.

`cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Collation: Vietnamese alphabet, canonical equivalence of Latin letters, accented letters next to their base, and Sort options (case sensitive, sorting language)
author: nhdai111983
body:
Builds on the language-aware sorting of #836/#837 (#844).

### What this changes

Sorting in WordCraft (Table > Sort, Home > Sort, the index, the bibliography, Edit Recipient List) now uses a collation that handles Vietnamese and Unicode canonical equivalence. Behaviour you will notice:

- **Vietnamese (`vi`, `vi-VN`, `VI_vn`…)** sorts in the CLDR `vi` standard order: `a ă â b c d đ e ê … o ô ơ … u ư`. Tones are a second-level difference (`ma < mà < mả < mã < má < mạ`), so `Hoà` (tone on `a`) sorts before `Hòa` (tone on `o`).
- **Accented Latin letters sort next to their base letter in every language**, including the ones that no per-language table lists (`Ánh` sits beside `Anh`, not after `z`). Languages whose alphabets treat a letter as its own (Polish `ą`, Swedish `å`, Czech `ch`…) are unchanged.
- **Precomposed and decomposed Latin letters compare equal.** This covers the Latin letters U+00C0–U+024F and U+1E00–U+1EFF with combining marks from U+0300–U+036F: a letter typed precomposed (`ậ`) and as base plus marks gets the same key, and marks of **different** combining classes match in either order (marks of the same class keep their order, as Unicode requires). Other scripts are not unified yet (see Known limits). Sorting never rewrites the text; it only orders it.
- **Mail merge uses the document's language collation.** "Contains" conditions match whole letters (`e` does not match inside `ễ`, even when the text is decomposed), and precomposed/decomposed forms match each other. The recipient sort (Edit Recipient List, Filter and Sort) and the less/greater/equal filters compare text in the document's language too, not only the Edit Recipient List sort and `contains`: tailorings such as Czech/Hungarian/Croatian digraphs apply (`ch` after `h`), and `equal` is canonical-equivalence aware.

title: fix(linux): honour desktop DPI scale on X11 and clamp restored window…
author: ccsimenson
body:
## Summary

On Linux, WordCraft runs through the X11 backend (`with_x11()`) so file drag-and-drop works under both X11 and XWayland. However, when `WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR` is unset, `winit`'s X11 backend ignores desktop scaling (`Xft.dpi` / `GDK_SCALE` / `QT_SCALE_FACTOR`) and computes the DPI scale factor directly from the monitor's EDID physical millimeter dimensions reported by XRandR.

On displays whose EDID reports aspect-ratio placeholders (e.g., `160 mm × 90 mm` for 16:9 on many HDMI monitors/TVs), `winit` calculates an inflated scale factor (`3.17x` on a `1920×1080` screen), causing the default `1440×920` window to open larger than the physical monitor and saving oversized `WindowGeometry` dimensions to `ui.json`.

## Changes

1. **`apps/wordcraft/src/main.rs` (`ensure_x11_scale_factor`)**:
   - When `DISPLAY` is set, `WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND` is unset, and `WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR` is not already set, query `Xft.dpi` via `xrdb -query` (`dpi / 96.0`), falling back to `GDK_SCALE`, `QT_SCALE_FACTOR`, or `"1"`.
2. **`apps/wordcraft/src/main.rs` (`saved_window`)**:
   - Clamp restored window width/height when larger than the saved monitor dimensions and pull off-screen coordinates back within monitor bounds.
3. **`contributors/people.toml`**:
   - Add `[people.ccsimenson]` entry.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Improved window restoration by fitting oversized windows to the available monitor area, enforcing practical minimum sizes, and re-centering windows that would otherwise appear partially off-screen.
  - Improved display scaling on Linux and other Unix systems by detecting and validating desktop scaling settings, with a safe fallback for invalid or unavailable values.
  - File-open failures now provide clearer feedback through the application’s status message.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: Layout: Times and Courier take Times New Roman's and Courier New's line spacing
author: pick2510
body:
Apple's **Times** and **Courier** are one em tall (hhea ascender 0.75, descender -0.25, no line gap), so WordCraft spaced their lines at exactly the font size. Word for Mac spaces them like **Times New Roman** (1.15 em) and **Courier New** (1.13 em). Real manuscripts set in "Times" came out a page shorter than in Word.

## Change
`fonts::word::line_metrics`: the faces of the families Times and Courier take the line (ascent with the gap above it, descent) of Times New Roman (hhea 1825 / -443, gap 87 per 2048) and Courier New (1705 / -615, no gap), scaled to their own em. Glyphs and advance widths are unchanged. On Windows, Word draws a "Times" document in Times New Roman anyway, so the rule holds on both platforms.

## Evidence
Word for Mac (compatibility mode 15). Synthetic documents with five one-line paragraphs per font, single spacing, no spacing before or after; distance between paragraph tops from Word's `vertical position relative to page`:

| font | own hhea | Word 11 pt | Word 20 pt | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Times | 1.000 | 12.675 | 22.938 | 11.000 / 20.000 | 12.650 / 23.000 |
| Times New Roman | 1.150 | 12.675 | 22.938 | 12.650 / 23.000 | unchanged |
| Courier | 1.000 | 12.425 | 22.688 | 11.000 / 20.000 | 12.475 / 22.650 |
| Courier New | 1.133 | 12.412 | — | 12.450 | unchanged |
| Hoefler Text | 1.000 (typo/win 1.25) | 11.025 | 19.900 | 11.000 / 20.000 | unchanged |
| Palatino | 1.100 (win 1.656) | — | 22.06 | 22.000 | unchanged |

Other Mac fonts whose hhea is one em (Hoefler Text) keep it in Word, and fonts whose OS/2 metrics differ from hhea (Palatino, Monaco, Futura) follow hhea, as WordCraft already does. So only these families are special. **Helvetica** (1.21 em at 11 pt, 1.198 at 20 pt) and **Symbol** (1.22) are also spaced wider in Word than their own one-em metrics, but they match no counterpart cleanly, so this PR leaves them alone.

title: Align opens a menu with Left, Center and Right, not just center (#3242)
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## Summary

Closes #3242.

The Picture Format / Shape Format "Align" button ran `arrange.align` directly with no `value` param. `arrange.align`'s own handler defaults a missing `value` to `"center"` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/objects.rs`), so the button only ever centered the selected object — there was no way to reach Left or Right from the ribbon short of dragging the object by hand (or holding arrow keys), exactly as reported.

`arrange.align` itself already correctly supports `"left"`/`"center"`/`"right"` and already converts an inline object to floating (`Wrap::Square`) when aligning it — confirmed by calling it directly with `{"value": "left"}` via `wordcraft-cli run`, which floats and left-aligns an inline picture as expected. ## Fix

Added `align_menu` (mirrors the existing `rotate_menu` / `group_menu` pattern next to it), which opens a menu with Align Left / Align Center / Align Right, each calling `arrange.align` with the matching `value`. Replaced the three identical `small(ui, app, "align", …, "arrange.align", json!({}), false)` call sites (Picture Format and two Shape/Text Box Format "Arrange" groups — the same bug was duplicated three times) with `align_menu`.

title: #1899: a picture cropped to a sliver is drawn at the size the file gives
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #1899

In T.docx (attached to the issue) the header's red bar is a picture cropped to 2.7% of the height of a page-sized WMF. WordCraft never kept less than 5% of a picture's axis, so it stretched a wider band over the frame: the bar came out half as tall (8.8 pt instead of 16 pt) and the white name in the text box over it ("د. هيثم الأحمر", and the page number beside it) fell below the bar, white on the white page. Now a crop keeps what the file says, down to a sliver, and the bar is as tall as the file makes it.

The pale look in the screenshots is not this bug: the header and footer are dimmed while the body is being edited.

## What changes

- **A picture cropped to under 5% of its source** (on either axis) is drawn at the size the file gives: the kept part fills the picture's frame. Bitmaps and metafiles (WMF, EMF), on screen and in PDF export.
- **Junk crops** (NaN, infinite, past 0–1, two sides that overlap) still draw something finite: each side is taken as 0–1, and when the two sides of an axis leave less than 0.5%, the left (top) side stands and 0.5% shows.
- Crops that keep 5% or more draw as before.

## Engine

No command or file-format change: the DOCX reader already kept `a:srcRect` as it is. Every place that turns a crop into the part of the picture shown now uses one function, `wordcraft_metafile::crop_window`, which keeps down to 0.5% of an axis. That floor keeps a whole source within the placement limit (±1,000,000 pt) on the largest frame layout makes (4000 pt), so a metafile item the crop shows is never left out as far off the page.

| `metafile` `Picture::fit` | metafile pictures, on screen and in PDF | `crop_window` |

title: Reject non-digit characters in numeric HTML entities
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/formats/src/html.rs:29-32 (decode_entity)` (no existing issue): HTML numeric entity decoding accepts a leading '+' sign (&#+65; becomes 'A').

## Cause
decode_entity passed the text after `&#` or `&#x` straight to `u32::from_str_radix` and `str::parse::<u32>`. Both accept a leading '+', so `&#+65;` and `&#x+41;` decoded to 'A' instead of staying literal.

## Fix
decode_entity now checks that every character after the prefix is a digit in the right radix (ASCII digits, or hex digits after `&#x`). If any character isn't, it returns None and the text stays literal. The regression test also checks that `A` and `A` still decode.

## Verified
- Regression test `html::tests::numeric_entity_rejects_sign`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-formats --lib numeric_entity_rejects`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::deleted_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_without_markup`, `tests::hidden_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_when_not_shown`, `tests::tight_wrap_follows_an_ellipse`, `tests_pages::widow_control_moves_a_three_line_paragraph_whole`, which also fail on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
Named entity handling and the code-point mapping (0, the 0x80..=0x9F range, invalid scalar values) are unchanged.

title: The close prompt's Save on a lossy format keeps the prompt with the reason (#3236)
author: rahul05ranjan
body:
## What's wrong

Editing a `.md` document and closing it traps you in a loop (#3236):

1. Press Ctrl+W (or the window's close button) → "Do you want to save changes to `name.md`?" appears.
2. Click **Save**. The `.md` is written correctly, but `file.save` only marks a session saved for formats that keep everything (`["docx", "docm", "dotx", "dotm", "odt", "rtf", "json", "xml"]` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs`), so `Session::dirty` structurally can never clear for a `.md` save.
3. `answer_save_changes` turned the resulting `PromptSave::NotSaved` into a plain "don't go on": the dialog closes (it was `take`n at the top of the answer), Close is refused, and the only explanation is the status-bar line "That format doesn't keep everything…" that appears **after** the dialog is gone — where nobody is looking any more.

Repeat forever: **Save** in this dialog can never actually let the document close.

## What the fix does

`PromptSave::NotSaved` from the prompt's Save now calls `prompt_again` with that same message, exactly as a *failed* save already does (#1445) — the machinery is already there: `Dialog::SaveChanges` renders `message` in red in the dialog, and `save_failed`/`settle_async_saves` already use this path for errors. The message string is the existing catalog entry (byte-identical literal, so all translations apply unchanged).

The user now sees the reason *in the dialog*, with **Don't Save** and **Cancel** still at hand, instead of a dialog that silently eats the click. No engine semantics change: a lossy save still leaves the document unsaved, and the held-back command still refuses to run.

The Save As path picked from the close prompt (a document with no path, or a legacy `.doc`) is untouched, so `a_save_that_drops_content_does_not_continue` keeps its meaning; this change only affects the arm where the document already has a lossy path and Save was writing + refusing.

title: Russian and Czech dictionaries are reported, not just checked (#3226)
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## Summary

Partially addresses #3226 — specifically "Russian does not appear in the Options dictionaries list."

`installed_dictionaries()` (`crates/proof/src/lib.rs`) never included Russian or Czech at all. The reason: neither `crates/proof/src/ru` nor `crates/proof/src/cs` had an `installed_path()` function for it to call — every other proofed Hunspell language (Polish, Portuguese, Italian, Croatian, Turkish, Indonesian) already did. Added `installed_path()` to both `ru` and `cs`, mirroring the existing pattern used by every other language (`crate::hunspell::find(NAMES).map(|(_, dic)| dic)`), and added both to `installed_dictionaries()`.

The actual spell-checking dispatch (`is_correct_in_with`) already routed Russian and Czech to `ru::is_correct`/`cs::is_correct` correctly before this change — that part of the pipeline wasn't broken. title: Subpixel (LCD) page text on Linux and the BSDs
author: mikael2
body:
> **Stacked on #3090**, whose hinted outlines this uses. Review the last two commits:
> - `afc3f0f1` **Render: optional subpixel text.** The render crate only, off by default, so on its own it changes nothing.
> - `3a3921e2` **The wiring:** the desktop setting, File › Options, the canvas, translations and docs.
>
> Once #3090 merges, the diff shows only those two. This PR is independent of #3101 and #3111. If #3111 merges first, this needs a small rebase in `canvas.rs`, which I'll do.

## Why

On Linux, the desktop's font settings usually ask for subpixel (LCD) text. KDE Plasma does by default, and GNOME can be set to. Firefox and other fontconfig-based apps then draw text with RGB subpixel edges. WordCraft's pages were greyscale, so next to those apps they looked softer.

## What

**Render** (`crates/render/src/subpixel.rs`, `RenderOptions::subpixel`):
- **Glyphs:** each glyph is rasterised at 3× horizontal resolution from its hinted outline (#3090). It's smoothed with FreeType's default LCD filter (8, 77, 86, 77, 8)/256 and blended per colour channel. RGB and BGR orders.
- **Drawing order:** text runs wait to be blended, and vello_cpu's drawing waits to be rendered. A section is rendered (and the text blended onto it) only when something is drawn *over* waiting text, so drawing order holds and most pages need a single section.
- **Lines and fills over text:** straight solid lines and fills drawn over waiting text (table borders, cell shading) wait with it as rectangles. They use vello_cpu's own coverage and rounding, so their pixels are bit-identical to vello_cpu's.
- **Clips:** open clips are closed for a section render and reopened afterwards, because vello_cpu renders only without open layers. Text is clipped to the clips' device rectangles.

title: Clipboard: a copied picture goes on the clipboard as HTML, so another document pastes it (#2909)
author: albayazid
body:
## What this fixes

#2909 — the sub-problem where an image copied inside WordCraft is lost: it reaches neither
another document nor another program.

Copying a picture (or a shape) gives no text, only HTML with the picture in it. Three things
kept the picture from travelling:

1. `system_clipboard::put()` emptied the clipboard's text for such a copy (#2276) and returned
   before the HTML was published, so the copy left the system clipboard holding an empty text and
   nothing else.
2. The HTML export of a copy had no media: the copied fragment's objects point at the source
   document's media, and the export was given a document without it — so the export wrote the
   picture's alt text (or nothing) instead of the picture.
3. Our own copy (the fragment WordCraft keeps) outlived the document it came from: the next
   document holds neither its text nor its pictures, so a paste there inserted a picture with no
   image in it.

## How

- `crates/ui-egui/src/system_clipboard.rs` — `put()` offers the HTML to the host whenever there is
  one, before the text-only fallbacks. A copy with text is unchanged; a copy with only HTML (a
  picture or a shape) now reaches the clipboard as HTML with an empty text beside it, as every
  other copy does. The text is still emptied, so the text copied before it is not pasted instead
  (#2276 keeps holding).
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs` — the export is given the document's media, so the picture is in
  the HTML.
- `crates/formats/src/html.rs` — the picture's size travels in the style, in points (the width and
  height attributes are in pixels, as HTML has them), so the picture comes back at the size it had
  instead of a third larger.
- `crates/engine/src/session.rs` — a new document takes our own copy with it: the new document
  holds neither its text nor its pictures.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/paste.rs` — the paste keeps using our own copy while the system clipboard
  holds it. A copy of a picture has no text, only the HTML with th…

title: Find box and Results list borrow a document font for Georgian etc. (#3248)
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## Summary

Closes #3248.

The Find box and the Navigation pane's Results list draw the typed query and document excerpts around each match with the interface faces (Inter, Source Sans 3, plus the embedded CJK faces) — nothing else. Georgian text typed into the search box, or found in the document and shown in a result's surrounding context, was drawn as boxes, exactly as the issue's screenshot shows (the document canvas itself renders Georgian fine — it has full system font fallback via `FontDb`; the UI chrome's own text widgets don't).

This isn't Georgian-specific: Armenian, Thai, and anything else outside the bundled interface faces' coverage and the embedded CJK faces would hit the same thing in these two widgets.

## Fix

This exact class of problem was already solved for two other places interface faces draw arbitrary text — the window caption (`ensure_caption_fonts`, #565) and comment balloons/the Comments pane (`ensure_comment_fonts`) — both borrow a document font's fallback face for characters the interface faces can't draw, via `theme::faces_for_preedit`. Added `ensure_find_fonts()` following the identical pattern: scan the Find query and the currently visible results' surrounding text (same ±30/+40 byte window the Results list itself uses to build its snippet) for characters the interface faces can't draw, and borrow a fallback face for them. Cached by `(query, result count)` so it only rescans when either actually changes, not every frame.

- New regression test `georgian_find_text_is_drawn_in_the_navigation_pane`: a Latin query/result needs no extra face; a Georgian search that actually finds a match borrows a face covering it (added once, cached on repeat frames); and separately, just typing a Georgian query with no match yet still gets a fallback face (covers the search-box half of the bug, not just the results-list half).

title: Docs: control protocol's Methods table renders again
author: mikael2
body:
Docs only, one file (`docs/control-protocol.md`). Found while reviewing #3253.

## Problem

The Methods table's `engine.execute` row lists the UI commands with unescaped `|` inside code spans, for example `"system"|"on"|"off"` and `true|false`. GitHub-flavoured Markdown splits table cells on every unescaped pipe, even inside code spans. So the row renders as 32 cells in a 3-column table and is cut off. title: Unstyle TOC entry links whose Hyperlink style has a localized id
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3239

## Cause
`unstyle_toc_links` removed the Hyperlink character style from TOC entry links only when the run's style id was exactly "Hyperlink". Non-English Word versions (for example Spanish `Hipervnculo`) and older files (`Hyperlnk`) give that built-in style a different id, so TOC entries kept its blue, underlined formatting.

title: #2828: the window comes back where it was left
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #2828

WordCraft saved the window's size and place correctly, but two things undid it at the next launch:

1. **A window sized to fill the screen was shrunk and centred again.** The check that fits a too-big window on its screen (#1215) kept 48 pt free on every side for the taskbar, also for a window the user had sized and placed themselves. On a small screen (the issue's 1600 × 900) a window sized to fit the screen is always past that margin, so every launch it came back at the same smaller, centred size.
2. **With an Interface size other than Auto the window crept and moved to the middle.** The geometry was saved in egui points, which the Interface size scales, but the window opens before the app sets its Interface size. At 125 % on a 100 % display the window shrank by a fifth at every launch (down to the minimum size), and its monitor, saved in points too, looked like another monitor, so it was also moved to the middle.

## What changes

- **A window restored on the monitor it was saved on keeps its size and place** while what shows of it fits on that monitor. This is what browsers do: outside macOS, Chromium's window sizer only shrinks a saved window when the screen's work area has changed. "What shows" is the frame less its side and bottom borders, which Windows draws mostly invisible, past the screen's edges when a window is dragged to them.
- **Saved geometry is in the units the window opens with** (the system's display scale, without the Interface size), so it reopens the same at any Interface size.
- Unchanged: the first window (no saved geometry) and a window saved on a different monitor are still fitted with the taskbar margin (#1215); a window whose monitor is gone is still moved on screen; a maximized window still opens maximized and keeps its normal size for un-maximizing.

title: Layout: text in an earlier column wraps around a shape anchored in a later column (#1158)
author: DevCoderMax
body:
Fixes #1158.

## Problem

In a multi-column section, a floating object anchored in a later column can be placed over an earlier column (for example a square-wrapped shape anchored at the start of column 2 but sitting on column 1's side of the page). Layout added the object's wrap area only when it reached the anchor paragraph, by which time the earlier column had already been laid out. That text therefore ran through the shape instead of wrapping around it.

`crates/layout/src/tests.rs` gets a regression test with two columns, a column break in paragraph 7, and a square-wrapped shape anchored at the start of column 2 over column 1. It asserts that no line of the earlier column crosses the shape.

## Change (`crates/layout/src/lib.rs`)

- `zone_hits_earlier` detects when a block adds a wrap area that overlaps lines already placed on the same page by earlier body blocks. Only lines of body blocks from the page's first block up to the anchor's block qualify, so another story or a turned line cannot narrow a column.
- When that happens, the page is laid out again from its start with the new wrap areas pre-seeded. `PageBuilder::seed` is keyed by the index of the page being replayed, applied when that page is created again or when the replay resumes on it, and dropped once the flow has moved past it; the existing `Snap` restores the state at the page start.
- Seeds are kept per block: they are cleared when the output moves to another page and replace the same block's zones when the anchor is laid out again, so a moved anchor does not leave a stale wrap area behind.
- Boxes discarded by a replay are counted in `boxes_discarded`, keeping the totals consistent.
- Bounded and scoped: this runs only in multi-column flow, at most 3 replays per page. When a replay fired, column balancing sits that section out rather than replaying a stale state.

`docs/layout-parity.md` and `ROADMAP.md` record #1158 (synthetic tests; not compared with Word).

title: Markdown import: reference-style links
author: Hamza0101
body:
Part of #3238 — the reference-style links only. The ticket bot asked for one problem per ticket, so task lists and footnotes are left for their own changes; this does not touch them.

### What was wrong

None of the three reference forms was read, and the definition line was not consumed either, so the markdown showed up twice. From the issue's own repro:

```
Reference link: [click here][ref1] Footnote: some text[^1]
[ref1]: https://example.com/ref [^1]: Footnote body
```

The link scanner required a `(` after the closing bracket, so `[text][ref]` fell through to literal text; nothing collected `[ref]: url` lines, so they stayed as a paragraph.

### After

```
Reference link: click here
```

One paragraph, the definition gone, and the destination attached. All three forms, measured:

| written | text | destination |
|---|---|---|
| `[click here][ref1]` | click here | `https://example.com/ref` |
| `[ref1][]` | ref1 | `https://example.com/ref` |
| `[ref1]` | ref1 | `https://example.com/ref` |
| `[click here][  REF1  ]` | click here | `https://example.com/ref` |
| `[nope]` | — | not a link, stays text |
| `[x](https://inline.example)` | x | `https://inline.example` (unchanged) |

### How

Definitions are taken out of the lines before parsing, into a map that is threaded to the inline parser beside the formatting it already carries.

Details worth reviewing:

- **Label matching** follows CommonMark §4.7: case-folded with every run of white space collapsed to one space, so `[  REF1  ]` finds `[ref1]`. The first definition of a label wins.
- **Destinations** may be wrapped in `<...>`; a title in `"…"`, `'…'` or `(…)` is read and discarded. A line whose tail is neither is not a definition, so it stays text rather than being eaten.
- **Fenced code is left alone** — a definition inside a fence is code and defines nothing. There is a test for it.
- **An undefined label stays text**, so an ordinary bracketed phrase is unaffected. That is what makes the shortcut form safe to a…

title: #3003: Save to a NAS share mounted by GVFS keeps working when it refuses a mode change
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
Fixes #3003.

## Cause

Saving over an existing file writes a sibling temporary file, gives it the original's Unix mode (`File::set_permissions`), then renames it over the original (`crates/engine/src/io/safe_save.rs`). If that mode change fails, the whole save fails.

On Linux, a NAS opened from the file manager (`smb://…`) is mounted by GVFS under `/run/user/<uid>/gvfs/smb-share:…`. GVFS's SMB backend refuses every mode change. `do_set_attribute` in `daemon/gvfsbackendsmb.c` accepts only `time::modified`, and its `unix::mode` branch is compiled out (`#if 0`). Everything else fails with `G_IO_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED`, which `gvfsfusedaemon.c` (`errno_from_error`) turns into `ENOTSUP`. That is the same "Operation not supported" that `cp -p` prints onto such a share.

So every save of an existing document on the share failed. That matches the report: the close prompt's Save stays open and nothing is written. Save As to a local folder works, because a local folder accepts the mode change.

## Fix

`keep_permissions` treats "not supported" as "there is no mode to keep" and lets the save continue. That means `ENOTSUP`/`EOPNOTSUPP`, plus `ErrorKind::Unsupported`. Any other failure to set the mode (for example `EACCES`) still stops the save and leaves the original untouched, as before.

std reports `ENOTSUP` as `ErrorKind::Uncategorized`, not `Unsupported` (only `ENOSYS` maps to that). The new test caught this, so the check matches the raw OS codes per platform: Linux 95; macOS 45/102; FreeBSD/DragonFly 45; OpenBSD 45/91; NetBSD 45/86. I didn't add a `libc` dependency for these few constants.

## Tests

- `a_folder_without_unix_modes_still_takes_the_save`: a refused (unsupported) mode change still replaces the file and leaves no temporary file. A permission-denied mode change still fails and keeps the previous bytes.
- `enotsup_from_the_os_is_an_unsupported_mode_change`: a raw `ENOTSUP` from the OS is tolerated, and a raw `EACCES` is not.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes locally on …

title: #3176: File › Home and New name each template and recent document for screen readers
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
Part of #3176: the "start-page tiles are unnamed" half. Launch focus is not changed here; it can follow separately, as the triage bot suggested splitting the issue.

## Cause

In `crates/ui-egui/src/backstage.rs`:

- **Templates:** `template_tile` allocated the thumbnail with `allocate_exact_size(…, Sense::click())` and no `widget_info`, then added the caption as a separate clickable `Label`. AccessKit exposed an unnamed node and a plain text node, so NVDA had no button role and no name to announce.
- **Recent documents:** each row in `open_list` was an unnamed click area, with its file name and path painted as text.

## Fix

- **Templates:** each template is one click area covering the thumbnail and its caption, with `WidgetInfo::labeled(Button, …)` named by the caption (translated, as shown). The caption is painted unwrapped, and the tile is as wide as its caption when that is wider than 150 pt, as the label made it before. Home and New look the same; I compared headless `ui_shot` screenshots before and after.
- **Recent documents:** each row reports a button named by its file name.

title: macOS accent menus type one letter and the accent replaces it (#2253)
author: SlavenDj
body:
Fixes #2253.

## What changes

Holding a key for macOS's accent menu typed the letter repeatedly (`cccccc`) while the menu opened, and the picked accent was appended after those letters (`ccccç`). Now:

- the repeats macOS sends while its menu opens aren't typed, so holding `c` types one `c`, as in native apps;
- a press long enough to open the menu (at least 0.4 s) marks the letter it typed, and the accent committed afterwards **replaces** it — together with the digit macOS types to pick the variant — in one Undo step.

## Why this is a workaround

macOS inserts the chosen accent through `insertText:replacementRange:`, naming the letter it replaces. winit drops that range (its `Ime` event has no variant for it) and reports `selectedRange` as a caret at 0, so all the app receives is "insert ç". The proper fix needs winit to report the replacement range, which requires surrounding-text support (rust-windowing/winit#3617).

Also, winit 0.30.13 ignores text inserted with no marked text (`insert_text` commits only with marked text), so on stock winit the accent isn't delivered at all and only the repeat suppression applies. With a winit that forwards it (rust-windowing/winit#4749, #4666) the replacement runs.

Known limitation: macOS also types the selector digit into the document; the app erases it with the letter when the commit arrives, so it is visible for about half a second.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui --lib keys::tests` — 25 pass (stock dependencies).
- New `the_accent_menu_replaces_the_run_the_long_press_typed`: repeats, release, preedit/commit, cancel, dead key, one-step Undo.
- New `the_accent_menu_replaces_the_run_after_the_selector_digit`: release → digit → commit.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

title: Control channel: a document-replacing command doesn't discard unsaved work
author: matstrange
body:
Programmatic calls never show the Save prompt, so discarding unsaved work has to be explicit. The control channel enforced that for a dirty document on `file.close` alone, while the interactive path used the full `discards_document` list — so an agent that saved nothing lost the open document and its undo history through `file.new`, `file.open`, `file.recover {"restore"}` and the mailings merges, and got `ok: true` back. `app.quit` bypassed the close prompt too.

Both paths now share one predicate, so the prompt and the refusal cover exactly the same commands. `{"force": true}` still discards, and forms that leave the document alone (a merge written to a file, an envelope added to the current document) are never refused.

Closes #3274.

Three tests asserted the old behaviour and are updated: two keep their original purpose (no prompt is ever shown; a stale prompt never acts on a replaced document) with the corrected expectation, and the mailings one now checks both the refusal and that `force` still runs the command.

title: Restrict Editing: the file commands, the user name and the post-check
author: matstrange
body:
`always_allowed` waved through every `file.*` id by prefix, so on a protected document the file commands that do change it went unchecked: the privacy options and the properties wrote document settings, and the inspector's removals deleted content. The privacy options' own comment already said they were "refused on a protected document"; that wasn't true.

This also fixes the protection around a protected document:

- The allow-list now names the file commands that don't change the open document, and the ones that do are checked like any other command. Reading the document stays allowed: the inspector without removals, the privacy settings, the info, and saving a version snapshot. The properties and the privacy options are refused outright, before the command runs: they are document-wide state and they aren't tracked, so under tracked changes they changed the document with no revision to show for it.
- The user name can't change while the document is protected. It is the identity a named `w:permStart w:ed="…"` exception is checked against, and the author the new revisions and comments are recorded under.
- The protection of a protected document only changes through the explicit stop (`review.restrict {"stop": true}`, which is what the pane's Stop Protection button sends). The "none" mode is the shorthand for it and doesn't stop a protected document, and the mode of a protected document can't be switched.
- Restoring a stored version replaces the whole document, including the content the protection kept read-only, so it needs the protection stopped first, password included when the document has one. The live document's protection wins over the snapshot's stale one, so a restore can't lock the user out of their own document either.
- The post-check that rolls a command back now compares the document's settings, metadata, custom properties, the comments' resolved flags, the list definitions and the bibliography sources as well as its text and formatting. `doc.revisions…

title: The inspector's removals are tracked, and a version snapshot belongs to its document
author: matstrange
body:
Two smaller gaps in the same area, found by a source audit.

The Document Inspector's removals delete straight from the document, so they aren't tracked. On a document that tracks changes — which is what `review.restrict {"mode": "trackedChanges"}` turns on — the text goes with no revision to show for it and the revision trail is broken behind the user's back. The removals are now refused while the document tracks changes; reading the document is still allowed, and a document that isn't tracking is inspected exactly as before.

A version snapshot belonged to no document: `Session::set_document` resets everything about the open document except the snapshots, so a snapshot taken of one document survived `file.new` and `file.open` and a restore then put the previous document's content into the open one. The snapshots go with the document they were taken from.

Closes #3277, closes #3281.

title: #2428: table.properties: text wrapping, positioning, percent widths and cell options
author: rabis7575
body:
Refs #2428 (the engine part of Table Properties; split out of #2452, which keeps the dialog).

`table.properties` set a table's alignment, width and indent and the caret's row, column and cell, but a table couldn't be made to float with text around it, widths couldn't be a percentage, a column couldn't go back to automatic, and a cell couldn't have its own margins. title: M15: fix Russian ё ordering and decomposed Cyrillic keys
author: LQRD
body:
Russian documents currently sort ёж and ёлка after яблоко because ё falls back to its Unicode code point. Give ё the same primary weight as е and a secondary diaeresis difference, matching the [CLDR Russian order](https://unicode.org/cldr/charts/42/collation/ru.html).

Compose the Russian pairs е + U+0308 → ё and и + U+0306 → й before building sort keys. Precomposed and decomposed words then compare equally and have matching index headings. Document text is unchanged; no dependencies are added. This is a narrow correction, not full Cyrillic/CLDR normalization.

Two new regression tests fail before the production change and pass afterwards. They cover representative word order, ru/ru-RU/RU_ru, case, canonical pairs and index headings. Progress and localization docs are updated.

title: Fix table formula ROUND erroring on large numbers with many digits
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/table_formula.rs:728-734` (no existing issue): Table formula ROUND errors for large numbers with many digits instead of returning the number.

## Cause
ROUND computes `(x * 10^digits).round() / 10^digits`. For a large finite x and a large digit count, `x * scale` overflows to infinity, and the `finite()` check turns that into a "not a number" error.

## Fix
When `x * scale` is not finite, ROUND now returns x unchanged. A value that large has no fractional part at that precision, so rounding changes nothing.

## Verified
- Regression test `cmd::table_formula::tests::round_large_values_return_input`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --lib round_large_values_return_input`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::deleted_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_without_markup`, `tests::hidden_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_when_not_shown`, `tests::tight_wrap_follows_an_ellipse`, `tests_pages::widow_control_moves_a_three_line_paragraph_whole`, which also fail on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
The digit clamp of ±15 and the rounding behaviour for values that don't overflow are unchanged. Other functions are untouched.

This PR adds spelling for **Bulgarian, Romanian, Slovenian, Albanian, Lithuanian and Bosnian**. Each one reads its installed Hunspell dictionary (`bg_BG`, `ro_RO`, `sl_SI`, `sq_AL`, `lt_LT`/`lt`, `bs_BA`), the same way Czech and Indonesian already do. title: Map Windows-1255 byte 0xCA to U+05BA
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/doc/src/encoding.rs:82 (CP1255 table, entry for byte 0xCA)` (no existing issue): Windows-1255 (Hebrew) byte 0xCA decodes to U+FFFD instead of U+05BA.

Set the CP1255 table entry for 0xCA to 0x05BA. Added a unit test that checks `windows_byte(1255, 0xCA)`.

No other code page tables were changed. The other unassigned slots in the CP1255 table stay as they are.

## Summary

- The comment balloons worked around this by reordering words by hand (`visual_row`).

Draft #20 by @generativimt12 started Hebrew with RTL. Thanks for that start. Its author notes they couldn't verify it on Windows, and it has conflicts with `main`. This PR is a complete take on the same goal:
- every catalog key
- a mirrored ribbon
- the bidi fix underneath

It could supersede #20, or the two can be combined, whichever the maintainers and @generativimt12 prefer.

`vendor/epaint` is epaint 0.36.2, patched in via `[patch.crates-io]` and excluded from the workspace. `VENDORED.md` lists exactly what changed:
- Shaping always runs in logical order. A new pass runs UAX #9 (via `unicode-bidi`, already a workspace dependency) on every laid-out row that holds right-to-left text.
- Glyphs keep their logical order in `Row::glyphs`, so cursor indices, selection and copying are unchanged. Only their x positions move to visual places.
- Clusters (a letter and its points) move as one unit. Brackets mirror inside RTL runs.
- New field `Glyph::rtl`. The caret sits on the leading edge of RTL characters, and hit-testing handles rows whose glyph x order isn't monotonic.
- Rows without RTL text take exactly the old code path. All 47 epaint tests still pass.

The same patch is proposed for GridCraft in storytold/gridcraft#2043, where it fixes cells, the formula bar and dialogs.

title: Read Aloud: Piper and cloud voices, voice roles, text rules, paragraph or page at a time
author: alex-ctms
body:
## Summary

Read Aloud gets natural voices, voice roles, text rules and chunked reading. The user can select the system voice, a neural voice that runs on the computer (Piper), or an OpenAI-compatible cloud voice. The sentence that Read Aloud reads stays highlighted with every engine.

![Read Aloud player: voice role and paragraph progress, highlighted sentence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-ctms/wordcraft/pr-assets-read-aloud/pr-player.png)

## Why this is needed

- **Hardware parity.** `docs/hardware-parity.md` rates *Speakers: Read Aloud* at 75%. Its only voice was the system speech program (`espeak-ng`, `say`, SAPI). On Linux and BSD, espeak is hard to listen to for long text. Word's Read Aloud uses natural voices. A local neural voice closes most of that gap without a cloud account.
- **Openness and agent control** (`AGENTS.md`: "going further on speed, openness and agent control"). Every new behaviour is a command (`readAloud.settings`, `readAloud.voices`), so the ribbon, CLI, control channel and MCP drive it the same way. The local engine takes any program that writes a WAV file, not only Piper.
- **Never crash** (`craftrules/standards/never-crash.md`). Settings from agents and `ui.json` are hostile input: strings are capped, numbers clamped, regex patterns size-limited, endpoints must be `https://` (or localhost), and a bad value changes nothing. A sentence that a neural or cloud voice cannot render is read by the system voice, so a missing program or a network error never means silence.

title: Keep footnotes and endnotes in plain text, Markdown, HTML and RTF exports (#3272)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3272. The flow model that the text formats export from turned a note reference (`InlineObject::NoteRef`) into nothing, so neither the mark nor the note text reached `.txt`, `.md`, `.html` or `.rtf`. The CLI `text` command goes through the plain-text export, so it lost the note too. Now `model::from_doc` keeps each reference as a new `Inline::NoteMark`. Notes are numbered in the order they are first referenced, the note's custom mark is kept as its label, and the note's text is joined onto one line. `model::flow_notes` lists the notes for the formats that write them after the body: - **Plain text** (`wordcraft-cli text` too): `Main sentence.[1]`, then a blank line and `[1] Note text.` - **Markdown**: `[^1]` in the text and `[^1]: Note text.` after the body. - **HTML**: a superscript link `1`, then `
` and one `

` per note, each linking back to its mark. RTF import still skips `\footnote` groups; #1053 / #1056 cover reading them. ODT, LaTeX and the flow-to-document builder ignore `NoteMark`, which is what they did with note references before. title: Reject signs and repeated '#' in Rgb::parse
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/doc/src/props.rs:49-56 (Rgb::parse)` (no existing issue): Rgb::parse accepts '+' signs inside hex colour pairs ("+1+2+3" parses as rgb(1,2,3)).

## Cause
Rgb::parse only checked that the string was 6 ASCII bytes. It then used u8::from_str_radix, which accepts a leading '+', so "+1+2+3" parsed as a colour. trim_start_matches('#') also removed any number of leading '#'.

## Fix
Rgb::parse now strips at most one leading '#' and requires all 6 characters to be ASCII hex digits. A regression test covers the rejected and accepted inputs.

## Verified
- Regression test `props::tests::rgb_parse_rejects_non_hex`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-doc rgb_parse_rejects_non_hex`).

## Not changed
model::parse_color and the colour commands are unchanged. They call Rgb::parse, so they pick up the stricter check. I added no separate test for them.

title: wasm: use the browser clock only on wasm32-unknown-unknown, not on WASI
author: alexwine36
body:
## Problem

#230 moved the clock to `js_sys::Date::now()` on the web, gated on `target_arch = "wasm32"`. That gate also matches the WASI targets (`wasm32-wasip1`, `wasm32-wasip1-threads`). There js-sys has no JavaScript host to call, so it panics:

```
cannot call wasm-bindgen imported functions on non-wasm targets
```

`layout()` times itself with `now_ms()`, so on WASI **every** document aborts during layout. We hit this embedding `wordcraft-docx` → `wordcraft-layout` → `wordcraft-render` in a napi-rs WASI build, which is what runs in the browser for us.

## Fix

Use the browser clock only on `all(target_arch = "wasm32", target_os = "unknown")`, the gate `wordcraft-docx` already uses for its own js-sys dependency. `std::time::{Instant, SystemTime}` work on WASI. The same pattern is changed in the four library crates that have it: `now_ms` in layout, and `now_unix` in engine, formats and pdf. Both the `Cargo.toml` target table and the `#[cfg]` change together. `ui-egui` is untouched: it only runs in a browser.

wasm32-unknown-unknown builds exactly what it did before.

## Checked

- `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` and `--target wasm32-wasip1-threads` for all four crates.
- `cargo tree --target wasm32-wasip1-threads -i js-sys` comes back empty for them.
- `cargo fmt --check`.
- A WASI build of layout + render now lays out and renders documents that panicked before.

`cargo clippy -D warnings` on rustc 1.95 reports two errors already on `main` and outside this change (`crates/proof/src/affix.rs:288`, `crates/layout/src/lib.rs:4113`), so I left them alone.

`cargo xtask wasm` only checks wasm32-unknown-unknown, which is why this didn't show up. Happy to add a wasm32-wasip1 check there too if you'd like.

title: Packaging: pin the signing client and appimagetool, and check their hashes
author: aiongg
body:
Both release tools were downloaded at whatever version was current, with no check. They are now pinned the same way as in designcraft:

- `packaging/windows/sign.ps1` downloads Microsoft.Trusted.Signing.Client 1.0.95 from NuGet and stops unless its SHA-256 is `3bfcf1e0a3cb42af1692f0a8ed45c15de070c2de86f28a59b2795d904d8a920f`. The working folder gets a random name and must not exist yet.

- The runtime hashes were checked against the 20251108 downloads for both architectures.

title: #3282: a flow table starts below a floating table a twip lower
author: RatkoR
body:
Fixes #3282.

## Problem
A table in the text flow right after a floating table anchored to the text with a tiny offset (`w:tblpPr w:vertAnchor="text" w:tblpY="1"`, `w:tblOverlap w:val="never"`) was drawn over the floating table instead of below it. On page 6 of the FCFCOA *Application for Consent Orders* kit, item 22's "Child 2" block covered item 21 and left its own place below "Child 1" empty.

## Cause
`below()` in `crates/layout/src/lib.rs` moves a flow table below the floats in its way, but only counted a float whose top was at the table's own `y` (within 0.01 pt). `tblpY="1"` puts the float one twip (0.05 pt) lower, so it was missed.

## Fix
`below()` / `below_floats()` take the height of the table's first row: a float counts as in the way when it reaches into that row. Only the first row is used, not the whole table, so a long flow table is not pushed below a float further down the page that a later row will meet. Both callers (body tables and tables in text boxes) pass it.

## Tests
In `crates/layout/src/tests.rs`:
- `a_flow_table_starts_below_a_float_a_twip_down`: the #3282 case (float at `y` = 0.05 pt); fails on main.
- `a_flow_table_starts_above_a_float_lower_down`: a float 200 pt down does not push the flow table below it.

## Verification
- Tested by the developer in the app: the tables in the consent orders kit are now rendered correctly.
- Rendered with `wordcraft-cli` before and after and compared text positions (`pdftotext -bbox`) on every page of the consent orders kit, two other real documents and the four built-in templates: the only page that changed is the kit's page 6 (PDF page 20), now laid out as in Word.
- Rebased on current `main` (only the docs conflicted; the code change is unchanged). `cargo xtask ci` steps: fmt, clippy, assets, layers and wasm pass; `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` passes (3,896 tests, 0 failed).

title: M15: correct Cuban and Peruvian Spanish decimal separators
author: MMexicann
body:
Table formulas and numeric sorting read `1.234` as `1234` in Cuban and Peruvian Spanish (`es-CU`, `es-PE`), and formula results use a decimal comma. Add the two missing decimal-point exceptions, matching WordCraft's existing region settings and the locales' CLDR inheritance.

The regression covers decimal values, grouped numbers and result formatting for both locales, with Spain controls preserving decimal commas. Required gap, parity and progress docs are updated.

Data references: [CLDR 49 Spanish decimal symbols](https://www.unicode.org/cldr/charts/49/summary/es.html#4ec3d1b99830ad07) and [CLDR parent locales](https://github.com/unicode-org/cldr/blob/main/common/supplemental/supplementalData.xml) (`es-CU`/`es-PE` inherit `es-419`, without decimal-symbol overrides).

Validation:
- Confirmed the new regression fails before the fix: `Some(1234.0)` versus `Some(1.234)`.
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-doc`: 174 passed; doctests passed (0 tests).
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh `cargo xtask ci` at `1b71286`: formatting and strict workspace/all-target Clippy passed. The unfiltered workspace run passed 2,680 tests (one existing ignored) and stopped at three color-emoji renderer tests on Windows. All 782 engine tests passed.

title: #3331: closing the header or footer returns to the body selection
author: RatkoR
body:
Fixes #3331.

## Problem
With the caret on a later page, entering the header or footer and leaving it with **Esc** (or the **Close Header and Footer** command) moved the caret to the start of the document, so the view jumped to page 1. Leaving with a double-click on the body kept the page only because the canvas moved the caret to the clicked spot afterwards.

## Cause
`insert.closeHeader` always set the caret to `start_of(StoryRef::Body)` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs`). Esc (`keys.rs`), the ribbon button, command search and MCP all run that command.

## Fix
- `Session::run` remembers the body selection when a command moves the caret from the body into a header or footer (new `Session::hf_return`, `Session::in_header_footer()`), so every way in is covered: Edit Header/Footer, a double-click on the margin, Page Number, MCP.
- `insert.closeHeader` puts that selection back, as Word does. If the caret is no longer in a header or footer (it left some other way), the saved selection is not used, and closing falls back to the start of the document as before.
- A double-click on the body still puts the caret where clicked.

## Tests
- `cmd::insert::tests::close_header_returns_to_the_body_selection` (engine): a selection on page 2 comes back after closing a written header, and after closing an empty footer that is taken away again (#960).
- `tests::escape_from_the_header_stays_on_the_page` (UI): with the last page in view, entering the header and pressing Esc leaves the selection and the scroll position unchanged.

Both fail without the fix.

## Verification
- Tested by the developer in the app: leaving the header with Esc now stays on the page.
- fmt, clippy, assets, layers and wasm pass; all engine (789) and UI (721) tests pass. `cargo test --workspace` fails only `fontdb::tests::a_thai_run_with_latin_falls_back_to_one_face`, which depends on the installed fonts and fails the same way on main (this change does not touch `crates/fonts`).

title: File: mark missing recent documents without blocking the UI (#3314)
author: LQRD
body:
Fixes #3314.

Home/Open > Recent now dims missing files and shows a localized “File not found” label. The full path and status are available on hover, and the row's accessible name includes the status. Rows remain clickable, preserving the existing open-error feedback.

title: #3341: the scrollbar page tip stays on one line
author: RatkoR
body:
Fixes #3341.

## Problem
While the vertical scrollbar is dragged, the tip beside the pointer (#2551) starts as "Page 1 of 40" but breaks into two lines ("Page 10 of" / "40") and then three ("Page 1" / "of" / "40") as the page number grows.

## Cause
An `egui::Area` keeps its size from the previous frame and lays its contents out within it. The label in `scrollbar_page_tip` (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`) wrapped to that width, so when the number gained a digit the text no longer fit and wrapped. The wrapped tip was narrower, so the next time the number grew it wrapped again.

## Fix
The label no longer wraps (`egui::Label::new(text).extend()`), so the tip grows to fit its text. Its position, layer, and when it shows and hides are unchanged. Other areas in the UI hold widgets of a fixed size, not growing text, so they are not affected.

## Tests
`canvas::tests::dragging_the_scrollbar_names_the_page_at_the_top` now uses a 12-page document and goes on dragging from a one-digit page to a two-digit one, checking that the tip is one row of body text tall. It fails without the fix (the tip is two lines, 30 px) and passes with it.

## Verification
- Tested by the developer in the app: the tip stays on one line while dragging through the document.
- fmt, clippy, assets, layers and wasm pass; all UI tests pass (720, 2 ignored). Only `crates/ui-egui` changes.

title: Read Aloud: read one paragraph, one page or the whole document at a time
author: alex-ctms
body:
Part 1 of 5 of the split of #3308. Parts: 1. #3346 chunked reading · 2. #3347 text rules · 3. #3348 voice roles · 4. #3349 local neural voice · 5. #3350 cloud voice. It applies to `main` on its own: `0d105326`, then the review fix `a6b0de7a`. Each part can be reverted on its own (later parts first).

## Summary

Read Aloud reads one chunk at a time: one paragraph (the default), the paragraphs that start on one page, or the whole document. Before, `review.readAloud` built the sentence queue for the whole rest of the document when reading started.

- The queue holds the sentences of the current chunk. The player loads the next chunk when it gets to the end of the current one.
- **Next Sentence** and **Previous Sentence** cross chunk edges.
- New `readAloud.settings` command. It validates every value, and a bad value changes nothing. The settings are kept in `ui.json`.

- Reading long documents: the work at the start no longer grows with the document length.
- `readAloud.settings` is the settings path that the next parts use (text rules, voice roles, voice engines).

title: Read Aloud: text rules for odd characters, web addresses and skipped text
author: alex-ctms
body:
Part 2 of 5 of the split of #3308. Parts: 1. #3346 chunked reading · 2. #3347 text rules · 3. #3348 voice roles · 4. #3349 local neural voice · 5. #3350 cloud voice. It builds on #3346 and carries its commits until that one is merged: review only its own commits, `05869fbc` and the review fix `4ff5bec2`. Each part can be reverted on its own (later parts first).

## Summary

Text rules change the spoken text of each sentence. The text on the page does not change, and the highlight stays on the words as written.

- Invisible characters (zero-width spaces, direction marks, soft hyphens) are always removed.

- Can be skipped: emoji, symbols (on by default), markup characters, `[brackets]`, `(parentheses)`, and four or more repeated punctuation marks (on by default).

title: Read Aloud: OpenAI-compatible cloud voice
author: alex-ctms
body:
Part 5 of 5 of the split of #3308. Parts: 1. #3346 chunked reading · 2. #3347 text rules · 3. #3348 voice roles · 4. #3349 local neural voice · 5. #3350 cloud voice. It builds on #3349 and carries its commits until that one is merged: review only its own commits, `eb1b732e` and the review fix `751dde42`. Each part can be reverted on its own (later parts first).

## Summary

A third voice engine, `cloud`, posts each sentence to an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` endpoint through the system `curl`. No HTTP or TLS library is added, and wasm is unaffected.

This PR sends document text off the machine, so it is kept separate for its own review of the endpoint check, the key handling and the opt-in wording.

## Endpoint

- It must start with `https://`, or `http://` to `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`.
- It may not contain whitespace, control characters or quotes. `http://localhost.evil.com` is rejected.
- It goes to `curl` after `--url`.

## API key

- WordCraft reads it from an environment variable (`OPENAI_API_KEY` by default) and never saves it. `ui.json` holds only the variable name.
- It goes to `curl` as a `header = "Authorization: Bearer …"` config line on stdin (`-K -`), so it is not on any command line.
- Only printable ASCII without quotes or backslashes is accepted.
- The sentence goes in a temporary request file, not in an argument.

## Opt-in

- The choice reads **Cloud voice (sends the text to a service)**. Its tooltip, a note under the fields and the docs (a CAUTION before the set-up steps) say that the text goes to that service.
- `readAloud.settings` can't switch the cloud voice on and can't change `cloud.endpoint` or `cloud.apiKeyEnv`. Otherwise a control-channel or MCP client could send the document and the key to its own server. Only File › Options and `ui.json` can.
- A command may leave the cloud voice on or switch it off.

If the service fails (no key, network, HTTP error), the system voice reads that sentence and the player shows why.

title: Spelling & Grammar button now shows suggestions
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3340. The Review tab's **Spelling & Grammar** button and the Home tab's **Editor** button both run `review.spelling`, which only moves the selection to the next spelling/grammar issue. With no way to see or apply a suggestion from there — just the generic selection toolbar — the button looked broken.

Running `review.spelling` now also opens the same suggestions popup that Shift+F10 and a Control-click already open for the word at the caret.

## Where the fix lives

The fix is in `WordApp::run()` (the single chokepoint every UI command path — ribbon click, keytip, keyboard shortcut — goes through), next to the existing `insert.picture`/`insert.icon` → `select_inserted_picture` post-command side effect:

```rust
if id == "review.spelling"
    && let Ok(v) = &r
    && v.get("done").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_bool) != Some(true)
{
    self.canvas.context_menu_from_keys = true;
}
```

I first tried adding `.clicked()` checks directly at the two ribbon button call sites, but reverted that: keytips (Alt-key access) call `app.run(id, params)` directly, bypassing a ribbon button's own `.clicked()` check, so that approach missed the keytip path entirely.

## Side effects this uncovered

Making the suggestions popup reachable from a ribbon click exposed two latent gaps the i18n audit hadn't caught before (nothing previously made this popup's content reachable from the audit's ribbon-click sweep):

- The popup's dictionary/grammar-rule suggestion words (e.g. "brown" for "brwn") aren't interface text, so I added an `Exempt` case in `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/audit.rs`, matching the existing treatment of font names and the user dictionary.

title: Keep '&' in LaTeX \href and \url addresses on import
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/formats/src/latex.rs:2526-2545 (raw_text)` (no existing issue): LaTeX import drops '&' from \href and \url addresses.

## Cause
The LaTeX tokenizer emits `Tok::Amp` for an unescaped `&`. `raw_text`, which reads the argument of `\href`, `\url` and similar commands, had no arm for it, so the `&` was dropped. A link like `https://e.com/a?b=1&c=2` became `https://e.com/a?b=1c=2`.

## Fix
Added a `Tok::Amp => s.push('&')` arm to `raw_text` in `crates/formats/src/latex.rs`. The regression test checks both `\href{...}{link}` and `\url{...}`. For `\url` it checks the link target and the visible text.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::latex_href_keeps_ampersand`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-formats latex_href_keeps`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::deleted_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_without_markup`, `tests::hidden_text_adds_no_line_break_opportunity_when_not_shown`, `tests::tight_wrap_follows_an_ellipse`, `tests_pages::widow_control_moves_a_three_line_paragraph_whole`, which also fail on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
Other token kinds that `raw_text` skips, and the LaTeX export code, are unchanged.

title: AutoFormat: a list marker typed in front of existing text makes that line a list item (Fixes #3352)
author: Claudio911015
body:
Fixes #3352.

**Cause:** `list_autoformat` only fired when the paragraph was exactly the marker (`"- "`, `"* "`, `"1. "`, …) with the caret at its end. Typing `- ` in front of a line that already had text did nothing, so turning a typed passage into a list meant leaving a blank line first.

**Fix:** the marker is now the text between the start of the paragraph and the caret, and only that part is removed; the rest of the line stays as the list item. A marker that is not at the start of the paragraph (`word - `, `x- `) still stays plain text.

**Tests:** new `list_autoformat_triggers_before_existing_text` (a `- ` on the only line, a `1. ` on the second line of a document) and `list_marker_not_at_the_start_of_the_paragraph_stays_text`. The test on the first one failed before the change. The 790 tests of `wordcraft-engine` pass; `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean. Not tried by hand in the running app.

**Open question:** I believe Word also converts a line when the marker is typed in front of existing text, but I have not checked it against Word itself.

title: List AutoFormat triggers in front of already-written text
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3352. "- ", "* ", "1. " and the rest of the list-AutoFormat triggers only turned into a real bullet or numbered item when they were the **entire content** of the paragraph (the code required the caret to be at the paragraph's end). Going back to the start of an already-written line and typing "- " to bulletize it — a completely ordinary way to build a list — left it as literal text instead, matching the report exactly: a dash with a space, never becoming a bullet, "unless I leave a blank line first" (a blank line is the one case where the paragraph genuinely has no other content).

## Verified against real Word

I wasn't confident this was actually a bug rather than intentional — WordCraft's own `docs/typing-parity.md` flags this exact AutoFormat behavior as not yet keystroke-checked against Word. So I checked it for real (Word for Windows, Microsoft 365): typed a line of plain text, went back to its start, typed `- `, and it became a real bullet, with "First paragraph" (or in my actual test, the reporter's own French sentence) kept right after it — same screenshot content as the issue's attachments. Updated `docs/typing-parity.md`'s revision history and header accordingly.

## Fix

`crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs`, `list_autoformat()`:
- Was: match the trigger pattern against `para.text.as_str()` (the whole paragraph) and require `f.off == para.len()` (caret at the very end).
- Now: match the trigger pattern against `para.text.get(..f.off)` (just the text up to the caret) with no end-of-paragraph requirement, and strip only that matched prefix (`para.delete(0, f.off)`) instead of the whole paragraph's text.

This still only fires at the very start of a paragraph (the match requires the prefix to begin at offset 0), still respects the `bullets`/`numbering` AutoCorrect preferences, still only overrides a paragraph with no existing active numbering, and the arrow-bullet (`-> `, `=> `) 3-character patterns still can't be confused with the 2-character …

title: Linux: native Wayland by default; XWayland opt-in, X11 libraries optional
author: bmh129
body:
## Summary

On Linux, WordCraft forced the X11 backend whenever `DISPLAY` was set, so on every Wayland desktop with XWayland it ran through XWayland (#220). That choice was made for one reason: winit 0.30 supports dropping files into the window only on X11. It has two costs.

1. **It breaks installs without the X11 libraries.** The deb and rpm only *recommend* libX11 and friends, because the binaries load them at runtime. When weak dependencies are skipped (minimal installs, `install_weak_deps=False`, image-based systems), a Wayland desktop still has `DISPLAY`, the backend is forced to X11, and the app fails to start. The rpm also never listed `libX11-xcb`, which winit opens and Fedora ships as its own package. The deb already lists `libx11-xcb1`.
2. **XWayland is the cause of a run of open Linux issues:** blurry or oversized windows at fractional scales (#1382, #68), input methods over XIM (#2932, #2933, #1169; #2950 proposes preferring native Wayland when one runs), wrongly sized dialogs (#1240), and typing on GNOME 50 (#1213).

This PR makes native Wayland the default on Wayland desktops and turns XWayland into an opt-in for file drag-and-drop:

- `WORDCRAFT_X11=1` runs through XWayland, as the default did before; only the value `1` does, so `0` or an empty value leaves it off. `WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND=1` is now the default behaviour and has no effect.
- Before forcing X11, the app checks that the libraries winit's X11 backend opens can be loaded (libX11, libXcursor, libX11-xcb, libXi; libX11-xcb brings in libxcb; and libxkbcommon-x11, which winit loads for the keyboard and panics without). If any is missing, it logs a warning and stays on native Wayland instead of failing to start.
- The rpm recommends `libX11-xcb` and `libxkbcommon-x11`; the deb recommends `libxkbcommon-x11-0`.

**Trade-off:** on native Wayland, files can't be dragged in from the file manager until winit supports it there. The README says so and names `WORDCRAFT_X11=1` as the way to get drag-and-drop…

title: Zero-pad hh in date/time pictures
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs:857 (format_date_parts)` (no existing issue): Date/time picture "hh" is not zero-padded to two digits.

## Cause
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs:857 (format_date_parts)` (no existing issue): Date/time picture "hh" is not zero-padded to two digits.

In `format_date_parts`, the `'h'` match arm used `_` for the repeat count, so `hh` was treated like `h` and the 12-hour value was never padded to two digits. The `H`, `m` and `s` arms already padded on `2..`.

## Fix
Added a `('h', 2..)` arm that formats the 12-hour value with `{:02}`. The `('h', _)` arm still writes the unpadded hour, so `hh:mm AM/PM` at 9:05 gives `09:05 AM` and `h:mm` still gives `9:05`.

## Verified
- Regression test `cmd::insert::tests::date_picture_hh_is_zero_padded`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --lib date_picture_hh_is_zero_padded`).
- CI runs on this PR.

## Verified
- Regression test `cmd::insert::tests::date_picture_hh_is_zero_padded`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --lib date_picture_hh_is_zero_padded`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The `H`, `m`, `s`, date and AM/PM handling are unchanged.

title: Header & Footer contextual tab while editing a header or footer
author: miltonjrd
body:
Closes #3366

## What

While the caret is in a header or footer, the ribbon now shows a **Header & Footer** contextual tab, selected on entry. Closing the header returns to the tab that was showing.

Groups:

- **Header & Footer:** Header, Footer, Page Number (the same group as Insert, now shared in code).
- **Navigation:** Edit Header, Edit Footer, Previous Section, Next Section, Link to Previous.
- **Options:** Different First Page, Different Odd & Even Pages.
- **Position:** distance from the page edge to the header and to the footer.
- **Close:** Close Header and Footer.

## Wrong-section bug

Page-setup commands (`layout.differentFirstPage`, `layout.pageNumberFormat`, and the others that go through `with_sect`) took the section from the caret's block index. In a header that index belongs to the header's own story, so the command could change a body section that has nothing to do with it. They now act on the section the header belongs to. For a header shared by linked sections, the page being edited tells which one.

## Commands

New `crates/engine/src/cmd/hf.rs` replaces the four commands that were in `tools.rs`:

- `hf.next` / `hf.previous` walked every header and footer part in one list, mixing headers and footers. They now move between the sections' own headers (or footers, whichever the caret is in) and skip sections that show the same part.
- `hf.position` clamps to half the page height instead of 300 pt, and acts on the header's section.
- `layout.linkToPrevious` unlinks into a copy of what the section showed, or relinks and drops the section's own parts. One undo step. Alt+Shift+R and the `footer` param (from the body) are kept. It refuses the first section.

## Not in this PR

- Key tips for the new tab.
- Previous/Next Section go to the default header or footer, not the first-page or even-page ones.
- Position is in points; Word shows inches.
- The buttons reuse labels already translated in every catalog (Edit Header, Header, Footer), so no new catalog…

title: #3376: Save as Picture writes the picture's original bytes
author: SlavenDj
body:
Fixes #3376.

Word's picture right-click menu has **Save as Picture…**; ours stopped at Change Picture…, Reset Picture and Size and Crop…, so getting an image out meant copying it (broken for pictures right now, #3328) or unzipping the `.docx`.

**What this adds**

- Right-click a picture → **Save as Picture…**. The Save dialog suggests the document's name with the picture's own extension.
- The file is the picture's **original encoded bytes**, at its original resolution: a JPEG stays a JPEG, a PNG stays a PNG. No re-encode and no page screenshot, so cropping or adjusting the picture in the document does not change what is saved (Word's "as shown" is a follow-up).
- `picture.saveAs` takes `{"path": "..."}` for scripts; without a path it asks the UI for one, like `file.exportPdf` (#2313).
- Only exactly one picture can be saved; a shape, a text selection with no picture, or several pictures are refused. Cancelling writes nothing. Saving is `.pure()`: no undo step and no dirty flag.
- The extension follows the picture's format, so a hand-edited `.png` name can't end up holding JPEG bytes (`jpg`/`jpeg` and `tif`/`tiff` compare as the same).
- The menu item, command label and status strings are in all 22 interface catalogs; `docs/ui-parity.md` records the new context-menu item.

No document-model change: the picture's bytes are already in `Document::media` under the key `InlineObject::Image { media, .. }` stores, so the command only looks the key up and writes it.

**Tests (local)**

- `cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --lib save_picture` — 2 passed: original bytes written, a path is requested when none is given, a hand-edited extension is corrected, a shape is refused, saving adds no undo step.
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui --lib save_picture` — 1 passed: the dialog suggests `Document1.png`, cancelling writes nothing, saving writes the exact bytes.

The `zh-hant` interface shares `prefer_hans` with Simplified Chinese, so its first CJK face is the

mainland glyph shapes: 說, 資, 這, 為, 戶 and others look wrong to Taiwan readers.
