title: Resizing a picture names the page it or the next item moves to
author: SlavenDj
body:
Fixes #3375.

While a resize handle on a **body picture** is dragged, a small label follows the pointer and says what the drag would do to pagination:

- `Moves to page {page}` / `Moves up to page {page}` when the picture itself moves.
- `Pushes the next picture to page {page}` / `Pulls the next picture up to page {page}`.
- The same for the next table, or `the text after it`.

It uses the displayed page number (`Page::number`), so a section that restarts numbering shows the number the drop will produce. The picture's own move wins; otherwise only the first changed follower is named. Nothing is shown when no page assignment changes.

## How

- **Engine:** `Session::speculative_layout()` factors the view's `LayoutOptions` out of `Session::layout()` and lays out a cloned document without touching the on-screen layout. `Session::resize_preview()` clones the document, resizes the one picture with the same `clamped_size()` that `arrange.bounds` uses, touches only its paragraph, runs the speculative pass, and compares first pages by `(story, path)` / `(story, path, off)` / table path. No document mutation, dirty flag, undo entry or `Session::layout` replacement.
- **UI:** the preview runs only after the drag threshold and while the pointer is inside the canvas, at most about 10 times a second — about 4 when a pass takes over 8 ms. A still size does not lay out again. The label is painted after the canvas handles the pointer, sits right of the pointer, flips left near the right edge, is clamped vertically, and is non-interactable. Release, Esc, and leaving the canvas hide it immediately.
- Strings go through `tl!` + `i18n::fmt`; catalog entries are left for the translation follow-up the issue lists as out of scope.

title: fix(engine): find and select reach the main text from a footnote (#3270)
author: wwewtech
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3270. `edit.find` and `select.text` no longer search only the story the caret is in: with no `story` selector and the caret in a note, the main text is searched after the caret's story, so text that exists in the body is found from a footnote, the way Word's Find covers the main document as well as notes.

The issue's reproduction: after `references.footnote` (which leaves the caret in the note), `edit.find={"text":"Main"}` reported `count: 0` and `select.text` failed with "not found", although the text is in the body; `caret.set` back into the body was the workaround.

## The change

- `crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs`: a `search_reach` helper next to `search` — the caret's story, and the body too when the caret is elsewhere; a `story` parameter searches only that story, as `story_param` already provides. `edit.find` uses it for its result list.
- `edit.findNext`/`edit.findPrevious` (`step`) merge the body matches behind the caret story's own matches and sort them by position, so the document order of the results and the wrap behaviour stay sane.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/caret.rs`: `select.text` walks the same two stories without a `story` selector (occurrence numbering continues into the body); with `story` it searches only that story as before.
- `edit.replace` and `edit.replaceAll` keep the caret's story: their scope is tracked separately (#3298, #3300), and #3300 has an open PR.

title: ci: Dependabot groups Cargo minor/patch updates; breaking bumps by crate family (#2973)
author: Nghiathan13
body:
### Why
`.github/dependabot.yml` puts every Cargo update into one group (`patterns: ["*"]`), so one breaking change holds back all of them. #2973 (19 updates, open since 2026-10-18) has failed to compile on all three systems since harfrust 0.13 → 0.14 dropped types `crates/fonts` uses. As a result the safe updates in it (`serde_json`, `sha2`, `proptest`, `arboard`, `winresource`) can't land either. In his review of #2973, @FredApps asked to close the group PR and have Dependabot split the updates, so that `egui*`, `harfrust`/`skrifa` and `hayro*` come in by hand with their code changes, and so that file-reading crates such as `zip` and `quick-xml` each get their own PR and test run.

### What changes
Only the Cargo entry in `.github/dependabot.yml`; GitHub Actions stays as it is.

- `cargo-dependencies` keeps its name but only takes `minor` and `patch` updates.
- Breaking bumps leave the catch-all group:
  - Crates that must move together get one group each: `egui` (`egui`, `egui_*`, `eframe`, `winit`), `fonts` (`skrifa`, `harfrust`) and `hayro` (`hayro-*`). A PR that bumped egui without eframe, or harfrust without skrifa, could not compile.
  - Every other breaking bump gets its own PR.
- A dependency goes to the first group it matches, so the family groups come before the catch-all.

### Why `update-types` is enough for 0.x crates
Most of our dependencies are 0.x. For cargo, Dependabot counts a 0.y bump as **major**, not minor, the same way Cargo does (`Cargo::Version.update_type` in [`cargo/lib/dependabot/cargo/version.rb`](https://github.com/dependabot/dependabot-core/blob/main/cargo/lib/dependabot/cargo/version.rb); since dependabot-core#13349). So egui 0.36 → 0.37 or harfrust 0.13 → 0.14 doesn't end up in the minor/patch group. Updates a group's `update-types` rejects get individual PRs, [as documented](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/dependabot-options-reference#groups--). That also works while the group PR is open,…

title: A document takes minutes to open: too many relationships, or a word with no break opportunity
author: matstrange
body:
Two ways a document could take minutes to open, both found by a source audit and both measured before and after.

**A document with many relationships.** The reader looks for each relationship's id in the main document's part, to know which parts the markup already refers to, so it doesn't carry them over twice. That was a full pass over the part, once per relationship: the open cost was the part's size times the number of relationships, where parsing the same part costs its size once. With the reader's limits (a 256 MiB part, 1024 relationships) that is about 256 GiB of byte comparisons for one document. The ids are now taken from the relationship attributes of the main document the reader has already parsed — the ids the markup names, the same rule the embedded objects use — so the open costs the part's size once and nothing more. One thing changes with it: an id that only appears as text is not a reference. The text names no part, and treating it as one lost the part on save, so a part whose id a paragraph only mentions is now carried over instead of dropped.

**A word with no break opportunity in it.** Laying out a line beside a floating object measures the word that starts on it, to tell whether the word fits the full line. The measurement walked to the end of the paragraph every time, so a word with no break opportunity in it — which takes a line per few characters — walked the paragraph once per line, and the layout was quadratic in the word's length. The measurement now stops once the word is clearly wider than the room there is: the answer is known by then, and the advances are widths, so the rest of the word could only make it wider — unless a font pulls a glyph back with a negative advance, and then the measurement carries on only as far as the rest of the word could take the width back. The same answer, the same layout, one line's worth of clusters per line instead of a paragraph's.

title: doc: a start override restarts only its own level
author: urbanij
body:
Fixes #3416

## What

`Counters::next_label` applied all of a num's `startOverride`s on the num's first use, whatever level that first paragraph was at. The counters are shared by every num of the abstract list, so a num that overrides every level — Word templates often give `Heading5`–`Heading9` their own num of the heading list, with `startOverride 1` on levels 0–8 — reset the chapter counter at its first deep heading, and every chapter after it was numbered from 1 again.

Now a num's override for a level applies once, when that level of that num is first used, and only to that level (ECMA-376 Part 1, §17.9.27). `seen` is keyed by `(num, level)` instead of `num`.

## Test

`numbering::tests::a_start_override_restarts_only_its_own_level_of_a_shared_list`: one abstract list, a plain num for chapters and a second num overriding every level, first used at level 5 inside chapter 2. Chapter 3 must still be `3.`. Fails before the change (`1.1.1.1.1.` instead of `2.1.1.1.1.`), passes after.

Checked on a real 140-page specification with this shape: the body heading numbers now match all 122 entries of the file's cached table of contents (before: chapters restarted at 1 halfway through).

On Windows/Linux, the back arrow in the File (Backstage) page's side panel was clickable across the whole 200px-wide row, not just the chevron icon drawn at its left edge (`crates/ui-egui/src/backstage.rs`). Clicking anywhere in that row — plain sidebar background to a user's eye — closed the File page the same as clicking the arrow itself, with no visual cue that spot was clickable. title: #3415: banded rows shade the same rows in Word and WordCraft (table style band sizes)
author: Nghiathan13
body:
Closes #3415.

## Problem
In the test document attached to #3415, WordCraft shades the "Etching press" and "Large-format printer" rows, and Word leaves every body row white.

That document was saved by WordCraft. Its `GridTable4AccentBlue` style has a `band1Horz` fill, but its `w:tblPr` has no `w:tblStyleRowBandSize`. The two programs read that differently:
- **ECMA-376** says a missing row band size means one. That's what WordCraft did (`band_size` unset → 1), so it banded the rows.
- **Word** reads it as zero, and at zero it applies no banded-row formatting. [MS-OE376 §2.7.5.7](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oe376/068c4488-4dbb-4c75-a8fb-e7b1e3597e0b): "Word uses 0 as the default for tblStyleRowBandSize… If tblStyleRowBandSize is set to 0, Word does not apply any banded row conditional formatting." [MS-OI29500 §17.7.6.5](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/6998fa34-5ceb-40a7-b3b5-ac4591c2f09e) says the same for `tblStyleColBandSize`.

The DOCX writer only wrote `w:tblStyleRowBandSize` when a style set one, and none of our built-in table styles did. It never wrote `w:tblStyleColBandSize`. So every banded table WordCraft saved lost its bands in Word.

## Changes
- **Model** (`crates/doc/src/styles.rs`):
  - An unset or zero band size now means no bands, as in Word.
  - Column bands get their own size, `col_band_size`.
  - `PartSet::of_cell` takes both sizes. The layout and the table style dialog's preview pass them, with an unset size counting as zero.
- **Our styles**: the banded built-in styles (Plain Table, Grid Table 4 and the others) set both sizes to one. `table.newStyle` does the same unless the style it's based on sets them. So their rows band as before, and Word now bands them too.
- **Writer**: writes `w:tblStyleRowBandSize` and `w:tblStyleColBandSize` (zero included) in schema order.
- **Reader**: reads both sizes, zero included. It used to drop zero.
- **Docs**: `docs/file-format-parity…

title: Equations: part of an equation can be selected, as in Word
author: pick2510
body:
> #3419 (the frame around the equation being edited) is merged, and this branch is rebased onto main. It holds only its own two commits: selecting part of an equation, and dragging the equation by the frame's grip.

## Summary

Until now an equation held only a caret: you couldn't select part of it with the mouse or the keyboard. Now part of an equation can be selected, as in Word:

- **Making a selection:**
  - drag inside the equation being edited (the selection follows the pointer even outside the equation);
  - Shift+click in it;
  - Shift with the arrows, Home or End.
- **Word's rule:** the selection lies in the argument holding both ends, and an end inside a structure there takes the whole structure. Dragging from inside the numerator into the denominator selects the whole fraction, as Word does.
- **Look:** the selection is highlighted at the frame's full height, or at an argument's height when it lies inside a structure. While something is selected there is no caret and no grey shading of the current argument.
- **Acting on it:**
  - typing, a symbol or a structure replaces it;
  - Backspace and Delete remove it;
  - Copy and Cut take it as an equation of its own, so its MathML goes on the clipboard too.

Each of these is one undo step. Selecting changes nothing in the document, and moving without Shift ends the selection.

## The grip drags the equation

The second commit makes the frame's grip work as in Word:
- **Drag:** a dotted caret shows where the equation will land. On release it moves there in one undo step and stays in edit mode. With tracked changes, the move shows as a deletion and an insertion, inserted first so the original's offset is still right.
- **Ctrl+drag (Option+drag on the Mac):** copies the equation instead of moving it.
- **Click without moving:** selects the whole equation.

title: A document with many content controls saves in the time they take
author: matstrange
body:
Saving a document with many content controls was quadratic in the number of controls: 32,000 of them took four seconds to save, and doubling that took four times as long again.

Two loops in the DOCX writer (`crates/docx/src/write/sdt.rs`) caused it:

- The plan that decides where each control is written collects the inline markers of every control in one set, then, for each paragraph, looks for that paragraph's markers by filtering the whole set. The cost of one paragraph's answer was therefore the size of the document's marker set, so the save cost paragraphs × markers.
- To find the block-level controls that clash (one that opens in the block another closes in), every control was compared with every other control.

**The fix** groups the markers by paragraph once, so a paragraph's markers are a lookup rather than a filter over every marker, and groups the block-level controls by the block they end in — each group keeping the two earliest closes, which answers the clash question the same way in one sweep.

| 32,000 controls | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| one control per paragraph | 3.58 s | 0.09 s |
| a control around every two paragraphs | 0.87 s | 0.17 s |

Both curves quadruple per doubling before the change and double after it.

**What is written does not change.** Checked three ways, byte for byte:

- ten shapes of control nesting — inline, around paragraphs, chained (the shape that makes controls clash) and nested — produce identical packages before and after;
- 400 documents with random control nestings (1,781 controls written across them) produce identical packages, with the old code put back in the tree for the comparison;
- the same 400 with the control kinds mixed (rich text, `w:docPartObj` gallery, `w:docPartList` gallery, plain text, check box) are identical too.

**Tests** — `crates/docx/tests/content_control_save_cost.rs`:

- two timing tests: the cost of four times the controls against a bound of 8.0 — 4.6× with the fix, 16.1× and 13.0× without…

title: PDF export can turn blanks drawn with underscores into fillable fields
author: Morzilla
body:
**Builds on #2120**, which adds the form fields this PR extends. Only the last commit is new here; until #2120 is merged, the diff also shows its commit.

This is the second of the two PRs split from #2120. It turns blanks typed as underscores into fillable text fields. That is the usual way of making a Word "form" without form fields.

## What it does

`PdfOptions::blank_fields` is a new option, off by default:

| Option | Command param (`file.exportPdf`, `file.save`, `file.saveAs`) | CLI (`wordcraft-cli convert`) |
|---|---|---|
| `blank_fields` | `"blankFields": true` | `--blank-fields` |

- **What counts as a blank:** a run of four or more `_` (`Ref. No. ________`), a date (`__/__/20__`, `__/__`), or a year with its century printed (`20__`).
- **Names:** fields are named after the words before the blank (`Ref_No`, `Code`). Names stay unique, as in #2120.
- **Dates and years:** each underscore group is its own field (`…_day`, `…_month`, `…_year`).
  - Each is as long as its underscores (`/MaxLen`) and centred.
  - Only digits can be typed. The day must be 1-31 and the month 1-12. A keystroke script and a validate script check this; Acrobat, Chrome, Edge and Firefox run them. Other viewers still apply the length limit.
  - The slashes and the printed `20` stay on the page.
- **Appearance:** the widgets are transparent, so **the page looks as before**, underscores and highlight included. Each field has 1.5 pt of room above and below its line, so viewers keep the typed text at the document's size. The font is the label's, as for form fields.
- **Skipped:** blanks already filled in by hand (`__JOHN SMITH______`, `__04/05/2025___`) and tracked deletions. A filled-in value must touch the underscores with a letter or digit on both sides; the search goes back at most 40 characters and stops at `:`, a tab or two spaces.

Fields are not added when the pages are drawn scaled or moved, as in #2120.

- **`form_fields_are_fillable` extended:** a blank and a date. The…

title: Layout: superscript and subscript lines are as tall as full-size text
author: pick2510
body:
## Summary

Word sizes a superscript or subscript's line as if the text were at full size, and leaves the vertical alignment's raise or drop out of the line height. WordCraft did two things differently:

- It added the subscript drop (0.14 × size) to the line's descent, and the superscript rise to its ascent. A line with a subscript beside normal text therefore came out taller than Word's.
- It sized the run's line at its shrunk drawing size (0.65 ×). A line holding only sub- or superscript, or whose largest text is a sub- or superscript, therefore came out shorter than Word's.

Now `StyleRun::line_extent` gives a run's line extent at the full font size. Only `w:position` raises or lowers it, and that is unchanged and matches Word.

## Word for Mac measurements

Synthetic documents, single spacing unless noted, distance between line tops measured over five lines:

| Line | Word | WordCraft before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 11 pt Arial, plain | 12.675 | 12.650 | 12.650 |
| 11 pt Arial + 11 pt subscript run | 12.675 | 13.375 | 12.650 |
| 11 pt Arial + subscript, double spacing | 25.35 | 26.75 | 25.30 |
| 12 pt Arial ×1.158 + subscript | 15.975 | 16.900 | 15.975 |
| 11 pt subscript alone | 12.675 | 9.775 | 12.650 |
| 24 pt subscript alone | 27.638 | 21.300 | 27.600 |
| 11 pt text + 24 pt superscript | 27.638 | 25.875 | 27.600 |
| 11 pt text + run with `w:position` +6 pt | 18.625 | 18.650 | 18.650 |
| 11 pt text + superscript with `w:position` +3 pt | 15.600 | 15.650 | 15.650 |

## Effect on real documents

I ran a private corpus of 181 real Word documents (papers and reports). For each one I measured the page of every paragraph in Word for Mac and compared it with WordCraft, current main with and without this change.

- The change moves paragraphs in 26 documents. In those, **52 more paragraphs start on the same page as in Word** (1548 → 1600).
- 9 documents get better, the best by 18–19 paragraphs.
- 4 get worse by 1–2 paragraphs each:
  - two of them are set in fo…

title: Layout: hanging punctuation (overflowPunct) and line-start punctuation compression (topLinePunct)
author: midasdf
body:
## What changed

`w:overflowPunct` (Word's **Allow punctuation to extend past text margin**, on by default) and
`w:topLinePunct` (**Compress punctuation at the start of a line**, off by default) were read from and
written to DOCX, set by the Paragraph › Asian Typography dialog and `para.asianTypography` (#269),
but line breaking ignored them. `crates/layout/src/para.rs` now honours both.

**句読点のぶら下げ (`w:overflowPunct`)** — a closing punctuation mark that would start the next line
hangs past the line's right margin instead, as long as it starts on the line (one mark, its own width
at most). The line's text ends before it, so alignment and justification measure the line up to the
last text: justified text does not shrink spaces to pull the mark in, and centred or right-aligned
text sits at the margin with the mark overhanging. The line may end after the hanging mark. The caret
before it sits at the margin, a click on its ink reaches it, and the caret after it (at the end of the
paragraph) plus the selection box follow the ink past the margin. Rendering and PDF export draw glyphs
from the line's cluster positions, so they need no clipping change. With the flag off the old
push-out is unchanged: the character before the mark moves down with it.

**行頭の句読点の圧縮 (`w:topLinePunct`)** — a line whose first visible character is closing
punctuation (kinsoku off, a manual break, or a mark that cannot hang) sets it at half its advance, so
the text after it comes half a character earlier and one more character may fit. Only closing
punctuation is affected; opening brackets and Latin punctuation are unchanged. Both flags are fully
implemented, not partially.

The character set is the existing `kinsoku::NO_START` sentence-end list, exposed as
`kinsoku::closing_punct` and reused by the line breaker.

## Limitations (honest list)

- Word applies both settings to Chinese, Japanese and Korean runs only, and its per-language
  character lists are narrower than the sentence-end list for som…

title: fix(ui): preserve Ctrl+Alt+Q and allow typing @ on German layout
author: divyanshu2074
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3424.

On German (and other European) keyboard layouts, `@` is typed using `Ctrl+Alt+Q` (or `AltGr+Q`). Previously:
1. egui's default quit shortcut matched `Ctrl+Alt+Q` (since `matches_logically` ignores extra Alt/Shift and treats `Ctrl+Alt` as matching `Command`), requesting window closure.
2. In `canvas_events` and equation typing, `Event::Text` events were suppressed if `m.command || m.ctrl`, which dropped `@` because `Ctrl+Alt` sets both `ctrl` and `command` on Windows/Linux.

This fix:
- Ensures `quit_shortcuts` is kept configured so only macOS uses `MAC_CMD + Q`, and `zoom_with_keyboard = false` is maintained.
- Allows `Event::Text` when `m.alt` is held alongside `m.ctrl` / `m.command` (AltGr / Ctrl+Alt national character typing) in canvas and equation editing.
- Adds an integration test in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` verifying `Ctrl+Alt+Q` does not close the window and correctly types `@`.

title: Layout: apply w:eastAsianLayout vert (縦中横/horizontal-in-vertical) in vertical text
author: midasdf
body:
## What changed

`w:eastAsianLayout/@w:vert` (horizontal in vertical, 縦中横) was read from and written to DOCX and
kept on round trip, but the layout never applied it: digits and short Latin text in vertical writing
were drawn lying on their side along the line, and `ROADMAP.md` said so. This PR draws the run as
the horizontal text it is in top-to-bottom vertical text.

**縦中横 rendering** — a run with `vert` on in top-to-bottom vertical text is drawn with its
characters standing upright, side by side across the line, reading left to right, inside the length
the run takes along the line: a pair of half-width digits fills exactly one character's height.
Each glyph is drawn on its own in a frame turned -90° about its em square, which the page's own
+90° turn cancels (the same counter-turn that stands East Asian characters upright; ISO/IEC
29500-1 §17.3.2.10 and [MS-OI29500 §2.1.75](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/efbc3ed1-1349-4572-93a0-a4e0f71e2a8b),
which records that Word rotates the text 90° left and ignores `vertCompress`). Glyph slots are
centred on the em square, and each glyph's own advance centres its ink in its slot.

- `crates/doc`: `ResolvedChar` carries the resolved flag (`vert`, off when `combine` is set — Word
  ignores `vert` then); the `CharProps` comment no longer says the layout leaves it alone.
- `crates/layout/src/display.rs`: the vertical-text run path draws such a run glyph by glyph; text,
  byte ranges and links stay per glyph so the PDF text layer keeps its order. The layout itself is
  unchanged — advances, line breaking, carets, clicks and selection are exactly as before — so this
  PR only changes how a `vert` run is drawn. The WordArt outline path and the layout-span
  decorations (underline, strikethrough) are skipped for such a run, since a line along the run's
  span would cut across the upright glyphs.

I checked it on a rendered page: with `vert`, "12" in a vertical line stands upright side by side;…

title: Layout: apply w:eastAsianLayout combine (割注/two lines in one)
author: midasdf
body:
## What changed

`w:eastAsianLayout/@w:combine` (two lines in one, 割注/warichu) was read and written but never laid
out: the run ran on one full-size line. It now sets 割注 — the standard Japanese annotation — on two
half-size sub-lines inside the line's own height, with the opening bracket above and the closing one
below so they enclose both.

**割注**: a run with `w:combine` is split at grapheme boundaries into two halves (one grapheme more
on the upper sub-line); each half is shaped at half the run's size; the upper line sits after the
opening bracket and the lower line under it, so the run takes one line's width instead of both
sub-lines end to end. The line does **not** grow: its height is the run's full-size ascent and
descent, as in Word. `w:combineBrackets` selects `round` (Word's default when the attribute is not
given), `square`, `angle`, `curly` or `none`; a run in a vertical section becomes two small columns
side by side, the first half on the right, with the brackets standing upright with the text.

- **`crates/doc`**: `props.rs` documents what is applied and what is kept for round trip only;
  `ResolvedChar` gains `combine: Option<CombineBrackets>` and `resolve.rs` fills it from the run's
  `eastAsianLayout` (`combine` true → the given brackets, or round when they are not given).
- **`crates/layout/src/para.rs`**: a combined run becomes one `Cluster` (`warichu: true`) whose glyphs
  are the two half-size sub-lines plus the brackets, positioned in the line's coordinates; its
  `obj_h`/`obj_d` carry the run's full-size line metrics so the vertical metrics keep the normal
  line height. The cluster's text is recorded in `ParaLayout::shown` with one byte range per glyph
  (empty for the brackets), which keeps copy and PDF text extraction in the run's order. The line
  cannot break inside the cluster, and the caret, selection and click offsets stop before and after
  the notation (see the limits for the character-level caret inside it).
- **`crates/layout/src/di…

title: fix(doc, layout): preserve comment anchors on partial deletion and ignore orphaned comment ends
author: divyanshu2074
body:
## Description
Fixes #3504.

When deleting the first line (or any leading portion) of a commented paragraph, `delete_range` previously only preserved content control markers via `kept_control_markers`. As a result, `CommentStart` was deleted while `CommentEnd` remained, leaving an orphaned `CommentEnd`. In layout display (`crates/layout/src/display.rs`), `open.take().unwrap_or(0)` subsequently assumed any `CommentEnd` without a preceding `CommentStart` in that paragraph started at character offset 0, resulting in a persistent, phantom highlight covering the remainder of the paragraph.

### Solution
1. **Preserve Range Markers on Partial Deletion** (`crates/doc/src/edit.rs`):
   - Introduced `kept_markers`, which preserves `CommentStart`/`CommentEnd` (and `BookmarkStart`/`BookmarkEnd`) markers whose partner is outside the deletion range.
   - When deleting the leading text of a commented paragraph, `CommentStart` is retained at offset 0 of the remaining text, keeping the comment anchored to the rest of the text rather than breaking.
2. **Handle Orphaned / Nonexistent Comment Ends in Layout** (`crates/layout/src/display.rs`):
   - Added `has_comment_start_before` to verify whether a multi-paragraph comment actually started in an earlier paragraph before falling back to `(0, off)`.
   - Verified that `doc.comments.contains_key(id)` so orphaned or nonexistent comment markers are never highlighted.
3. **Tests Added**:
   - `crates/doc/src/edit.rs`: `deleting_the_start_of_a_commented_range_keeps_comment_start`.
   - `crates/layout/src/tests.rs`: `orphaned_comment_end_does_not_highlight`.
   - `crates/engine/src/cmd/review.rs`: `deleting_first_line_of_commented_paragraph_keeps_comment_on_remainder`.

title: ci: pin GitHub Actions to full commit SHA (SonarCloud S7637)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Pins third-party GitHub Actions to full-length commit SHAs (with version comments) instead of mutable tags or branches.

Resolves SonarCloud rule **githubactions:S7637** (Security). Mutable refs like `@v2` or `@stable` can be silently repointed by an action maintainer (or attacker who gains access), so pinning to an immutable commit SHA prevents supply-chain tampering.

- `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` → `@b725eda…` `# stable`
- `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly` → `@2c76c03…` `# nightly`

- `EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@v2` → `@3c63498…` `# v2.1.1`

## Notes
- Already-pinned actions (e.g. `actions/checkout`) were left untouched.
- `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`/`@nightly` track moving branches; pinning freezes the toolchain commit. Bump the SHA + comment to update.

title: security: enforce HTTPS on curl downloads (SonarCloud S6506)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Enforces HTTPS on `curl` downloads flagged by SonarCloud rule **S6506** (`shell:S6506`, `docker:S6506`, `githubactions:S6506`, Security).

These `curl` calls use `-L`/`-fsSL` (follow redirects). A redirect could transparently downgrade to plaintext HTTP, exposing the download to MITM tampering. Adding `--proto '=https'` forces curl to refuse any non-HTTPS protocol, including across redirects, without changing behavior for the legitimate HTTPS endpoints already in use.

## Change
`curl <args>` → `curl --proto '=https' <args>` on each flagged line.

title: Table gridlines: draw only on cell edges without a border (#3432)
author: alexanderalber
body:
With Table Layout › View Gridlines on (the default), the canvas stroked a rectangle around every table cell, on top of the cell's borders. A styled table therefore showed the blue gridline instead of its own border colour (Grid Table 4, borders `C1E4F5`, looked strong blue, and the header cells were split by blue lines). Word shows gridlines only as an aid where a table has no border.

**Change** (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, UI only):

- `gridline_segments` takes the cell edges of `gridline_cells` and removes every stretch along which a border `Placed::Rule` is drawn on the page (body, header, footer). The borders are bucketed by line (horizontal by y, vertical by x, sorted, binary search) and subtracted as intervals.
- Because it works on the laid-out rules, it does not matter whose border it is: the cell's own, its neighbour's on a shared edge, the table's, a style part's or a row exception's. Merged cells, partially bordered edges and rows split across pages fall out of the same geometry.
- The canvas draws the remaining segments with `line_segment` in the same stroke as before.

Layout and rendering are unchanged; printing and export were never affected.

**Tests**

- `table_gridlines_skip_edges_with_borders`: synthetic page; no borders gives all edges, a border on a shared edge hides it for both cells, a half-length top border leaves the other half, a fully bordered cell gets no gridlines.
- `table_gridlines_follow_the_table_borders`: through the real layout; a new 2x2 table (bordered) has no gridlines, `table.borders` `none` gives all 16 edges, `outside` leaves the 8 inside edges.
- Checked headlessly with `ui_shot`: a 3x3 table with outside borders `C1E4F5` shows the light border outside and gridlines only inside.

title: Files: a template the platform hands the app starts a new document, and the template is never written over (#3433)
author: albayazid
body:
## What this fixes

#3433 — opening a Word template from the file manager overwrote the template.

Double-clicking a `.dotx` opened the template **as the document**, so the document kept the template's path. **Save** then wrote straight back to the template:

```
file.open  -> session path: Some("...T.dotx")
file.save  -> template bytes changed: true
```

The template was overwritten without notice, and the new document never got saved as a plain document.

## What Word does

Opening a template from the shell (double-click, the command line, a drop on the window) gives a **new untitled document based on the template**:

- the document has no path of its own — the title is `Document1`, and Save asks where to write;
- the template is recorded as the attached template (`settings.attached_template`);
- the template on disk is never modified.

**File › Open** on a `.dotx`/`.dotm` still opens the template itself, which is Word's way of editing one. That is unchanged here.

## How

The rule lives in one place, `WordApp::open_from_shell` (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`), and every path the platform can hand a file goes through it: the command line and a file whose name isn't valid Unicode (`apps/wordcraft/src/main.rs`), macOS Finder double-clicks, Open With and drops on the Dock icon (`apps/wordcraft/src/apple_events.rs`), and a drop on the window (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`).

- `crates/engine/src/io.rs` — `is_template_name` names a Word template by its extension (`.dotx`, `.dotm`, and the Word 97-2003 `.dot`).
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs` — `file.newFromTemplate` records the template as the attached one, so "Update Styles from Template" still finds it, and it takes a `password` and the file's `data` like `file.open` does.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs` — the password dialog retries **the command that asked for the password**. It used to always run `file.open`, which for a protected template would have opened the template as the document, undoing the fix.

title: Table formulas: read the Panamanian balboa B/. in numbers
author: alosslessdev
body:
## Summary

WordCraft already reads international currency signs around numbers in table sort and table formulas (`crates/doc/src/locale_number.rs`): single-character signs (`$`, `€`, `£`, `¥`, `₽`, …), short currency words (`zł`, `kr`) and ISO codes (`PLN 12`), with the document language's decimal and group separators. The Panamanian balboa (ISO 4217 `PAB`) was missing.

This adds the balboa's `B/.` as a multi-character sign, with Word's own rules, confirmed in Word 16.0 on Windows:

| Cell text | Word `=SUM(ABOVE)` | WordCraft |
|---|---|---|
| `B/. 1,250.50` | 1250.5 | 1250.5 |
| `B/.` + no-break space + `1,250.50` | 1250.5 | 1250.5 |
| `1,250.50 B/.` | 1250.5 | 1250.5 |
| `B/.1,250.50` | text (0) | not a number |
| `B/ 1,250.50` | text (0) | not a number |
| `PAB 1,250.50` | 1250.5 | 1250.5 (already worked) |

The `B/.` sign must be whitespace-delimited, matching Word; the ISO code `PAB` was already read as a currency word, so only the symbol needed adding.

## Changes

- `crates/doc/src/locale_number.rs`: multi-character currency signs (`B/.`), matched only as a word of their own, as Word does.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/table_formula.rs`: tests, including `=SUM(ABOVE)` over a balboa cell and the `es-PA` locale.
- `docs/localization-parity.md`: documents the behaviour and the Word observation.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p wordcraft-doc locale_number` — 4 passed
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-engine numbers_read_currency_and_separators_but_not_letters` — 1 passed
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: Table formulas: read Latin American currency signs
author: alosslessdev
body:
Closes #3550.

## Summary

WordCraft already ignored `$` and three-letter ISO codes around numbers in table sort and table formulas. This adds the missing Latin American currency signs, with the spacing rules observed in Word 16.0 on Windows (table cells read with `=SUM(ABOVE)`):

| Currency | ISO | Signs added | Word's spacing |
|---|---|---|---|
| Argentine peso | ARS | `Arg$` | touching or spaced |
| Bolivian boliviano | BOB | `Bs.`, `Bs` | space required |
| Brazilian real | BRL | `R$` | touching or spaced |
| Cuban peso | CUP | `CUP$` | touching or spaced |
| Dominican peso | DOP | `RD$` | touching or spaced |
| Guatemalan quetzal | GTQ | `Q` | space required |
| Honduran lempira | HNL | `L` | space required |
| Mexican peso | MXN | `MX$` | touching or spaced |
| Nicaraguan córdoba | NIO | `C$` | touching or spaced |
| Peruvian sol | PEN | `S/.`, `S/` | space required |
| Uruguayan peso | UYU | `$U` | space required |
| Venezuelan bolívar | VES | `Bs.S`, `Bs.` | space required |
| US dollar (Ecuador, El Salvador, Puerto Rico) | USD | `US$` | touching or spaced |

`S/` is accepted as CLDR writes the Peruvian sol even though Word 16.0 reads only `S/.`. ISO codes (`ARS 1,250.50`, `BOB 1,250.50`, …) already worked through the generic three-letter currency word.

### Regional separators and whole amounts

Numbers follow the cell text's language and region (the repo's existing CLDR-based `decimal_separator`, not the system locale):

| Separator | Regions | Example |
|---|---|---|
| decimal point | `es-MX`, `es-PA`, `es-PE`, `es-CU`, `es-DO`, `es-GT`, `es-HN`, `es-NI`, `es-SV`, `es-PR` | `S/. 1,250.50` |
| decimal comma | `es-AR`, `es-BO`, `es-CL`, `es-CO`, `es-CR`, `es-PY`, `es-UY`, `es-VE`, `pt-BR` | `R$ 1.250,50` |

Whole amounts without cents (`R$ 1.250`, `S/. 1,250`) parse as integers, and whole results show no decimals (`format_number`), while fractional results use the region's separator (`1250,50` / `1250.50`).

This also corrects `es-PE` and `es-CU`, which we…

title: wordcraft-web: postMessage host bridge (`?host=parent`)
author: halldave
body:
Lets a same-origin page that frames WordCraft in an `<iframe>` (a file manager, a document
store) open documents in it and receive what it saves, mirroring GridCraft's web bridge.

With `?host=parent` and a same-origin parent window:

- `wordcraft:ready {version}` is posted once the app listens;
- `wordcraft:open {name, bytes}` (ArrayBuffer or Uint8Array) opens like File › Open or a drop;
- every Save, Save As and export that would download posts `wordcraft:save {name, bytes}`
  (transferred ArrayBuffer) instead, and the native save marks the document clean;
- `wordcraft:dirty {dirty}` reports unsaved changes; `wordcraft:failed {error}` a failed start;
- `?author=` names the user for comments and tracked changes.

In host mode the page starts on a blank document (no File › Home), and the parent guards leaving
the page, so there is no unload prompt. Only the parent on the page's own origin is heard or
answered. Without `?host=parent` nothing changes.

Files: `apps/wordcraft-web/src/host.rs` (new), `src/web.rs`, `src/main.rs`, `Cargo.toml`
(web-sys features `MessageEvent`, `UrlSearchParams`; no new crates).

title: IME: the caret follows the composition text
author: aiongg
body:
While an input method composes (Japanese, Chinese, ...), the caret and the candidate window now sit at the input method's cursor inside the marked text, or at its end when the input method reports no cursor. Before, both stayed at the start of the marked text, and the caret jumped to the end on commit.

### Cause
`keys.rs` kept the `Preedit` text but dropped `active_range_chars`. The canvas drew the caret bar and set the IME `cursor_rect` at the document caret, which the marked text (drawn as an overlay to its right) doesn't move.

### Change
- `CanvasState` keeps the input method's range with the preedit; both commit paths clear it.
- The canvas lays out the preedit once, paints it, and moves the caret bar, the caret glide target and `cursor_rect` to the cursor's x in that galley. The range comes from the OS, so it is clamped to the text (`preedit_cursor_chars`); a reversed or out-of-range value can't panic or land inside a char.
- `docs/typing-parity.md`: Input methods row.

### Test
`canvas::tests::the_caret_follows_the_input_method_cursor_in_the_composition` (egui_kittest) composes "にほん" and checks `cursor_rect` for no range, `0..0`, `1..1`, out-of-range and reversed ranges, and that commit clears the range. It fails without the change.

`cargo xtask ci` passes.

### Related
#2021 lays the composition out in the paragraph instead of drawing it over the text, and #3022 changes the font it is drawn in. Both touch the same drawing code. This is the minimal fix for the caret position in the current overlay; if #2021 lands, it replaces this.

title: Header and footer: a click in the other band edits it there
author: aiongg
body:
While a header is being edited, a single click in the footer (or in another page's header or footer) now moves editing there, with the caret where clicked. Before, the click put the caret at the nearest point in the header being edited and the view scrolled back to it, so a double-click into the footer rarely landed unless both bands were on screen at once.

### Cause
A press in the margin bands was hit-tested against the story already being edited. Only the release of a double-click switched to the other header or footer, and by then the first click had scrolled the view.

### Change
- `canvas.rs`: a press in another header/footer band runs `insert.editHeader` / `insert.editFooter` for that page (creating it when the page has none, as the double-click does), then places the caret there without scrolling. The `hf_enter` check moved into `enters_header_footer` so the press can use it.
- The second press of a double-click after such a switch doesn't select a word, so a double-click into the other band still only places the caret.
- Clicks in the body are unchanged: a double-click there leaves header/footer editing, and a single press from the body into a margin band still leaves the caret and view alone (#2103).
- `docs/ui-parity.md`: the header/footer row lists this, and its two copies are combined into one row.

### Test
`tests::a_click_in_the_footer_while_editing_the_header_moves_there` edits page 1's header, scrolls until only the footer is on screen, clicks the footer, then clicks page 2's header, and checks the story, the page and that the view didn't scroll each time. It fails without the change. The existing header/footer double-click and Esc tests pass.

`cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Tables: an older-mode table moves out by its default cell margin, not the first cell's own (#3407)
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
Fixes #3407.

## What was wrong
In a document below compatibility mode 15 (including a .docx with no `settings.xml`, like the attached repro), WordCraft moves a table out past its indent so cell text lines up with the surrounding text. It used the **first cell's own** left margin (`w:tcMar`) for that distance. Word uses the **table's default** left cell margin (`w:tblCellMar`, else the table style's, else its own default).

With `w:tblCellMar` left/right = 0 and every cell given 144 twips (`w:tcMar`), as in the report, WordCraft shifted the whole table 7.2 pt left. The per-cell padding was applied, but the shift cancelled it, so the text landed on the page margin.

## Fix
`crates/layout/src/table.rs`: in older mode the outdent is `default_margins(..)[1]`, the table's default left margin. The same value feeds the paragraph-anchored positions in `lib.rs` through `first_cell_left_margin`. Word 2013 mode (≥ 15), which doesn't outdent, is unchanged.

## Verified
- The reporter's `repro-table-hyphen-slash-wrap.docx` → PDF: first-column text at **x = 63.9 pt** (was 56.7), matching the attached Word PDF (56.7 margin + 7.2 padding).
- Synthetic files using `w:left`/`w:right` and `w:start`/`w:end`: same result.
- New test `legacy_table_outdent_ignores_the_first_cells_own_margin`: fails on main (offset 0), passes here (7.2). It also checks that Word 2013 mode still insets.
- `cargo test --workspace`: 3893 passed, 0 failed; clippy `-D warnings` clean.

The hyphen-before-slash line break from the same file is #3408 and is not touched here.

title: #3360, #3553: Spanish proofing (es-ES, es-MX, es-419, es-UY)
author: FedeOlivares
body:
Fixes #3553. Fixes #3360. Closes #3530. Closes #1695.

## Why Spanish wasn't checked

`ProofLang` had no Spanish variant, so every `es-*` run resolved to `ProofLang::Other`, which by design gets no spelling or grammar marks (as confirmed in #3360). That is the "nothing gets underlined, no suggestions" both issues describe.

A second cause, the affix engine refusing the RLA-ES dictionaries LibreOffice ships because of their `☎️` flag (`☎` + U+FE0F), was fixed on `main` meanwhile by #2164. This branch had the same fix; on merging `main` it takes #2164's version.

## What this adds

Spanish follows the English dialect pattern (`En`/`EnGb`/`EnCa`): one `ProofLang` per variety, chosen from the tag's region, each reading its own installed Hunspell dictionary (nothing is bundled, as for the other Hunspell languages).

| Variety | Tags | Dictionary, then fallbacks |
|---|---|---|
| `ProofLang::Es`: Spain | `es`, `es-ES`, `spa`, any other region | `es_ES`, `es-ES`, `es_ANY`, `es` |
| `ProofLang::EsMx`: Mexico | `es-MX` | `es_MX`, `es-MX`, `es_419`, `es-419`, `es_ANY`, `es` |
| `ProofLang::Es419`: Latin America | `es-419`, its M.49 parts, and the other countries of the Americas (`es-AR`, `es-CO`, `es-US`…) | `es_419`, `es-419`, `es_ANY`, `es`, `es_US`, `es_MX`, `es_AR`, `es-AR` (LibreOffice ships no `es_419`) |
| `ProofLang::EsUy`: Uruguay | `es-UY` | `es_UY`, `es-UY`, `es_AR`, `es-AR`, `es_419`, `es-419`, `es_ANY`, `es` |

- **Spelling** (`crates/proof/src/es`): the variety's dictionary; hyphenated compounds part by part; short acronyms accepted; message "Posible error ortográfico".
- **Uruguayan `vos` forms** (`es/voseo.rs`): imperatives (`vení`, `tené`, `andá`), imperatives with pronouns (`decime`, `fijate`, `andate`, `decímelo`) and the present (`tenés`, `querés`, `venís`) are accepted when the dictionary has the verb's infinitive. title: Thai run fallback test: skip where no installed font covers the run, allow an embedded Thai face (#3561)
author: MatRanc
body:
Fixes #3561.

## What changed
Test only: `fontdb::tests::a_thai_run_with_latin_falls_back_to_one_face` in `crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs`. No library code changes.

1. **No installed font covers the whole run.** Fedora's Thai fonts (Noto Sans Thai, Noto Serif Thai, Droid Sans Thai) have no Latin, so `fallback_for_run` is right to return `None` and the test's `expect("one face covers the run")` panicked. When the result is `None`, the test now checks every font file in the catalog with `coverage_ranges`. If one maps the whole run, the test fails and lists it, because the search missed that file. Otherwise it skips with a message. Systems with a Thai font that has Latin, like CI, still run the full assertions.
2. **Built with `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR`.** craft-fonts embeds Noto Sans Thai with Latin, so the bundled-only database does find a face for the run. The last check now expects that face, which must cover the run, when a Thai font is embedded, and `None` otherwise. title: The end of a line wrapped short by an inline object is a caret stop
author: supikachu
body:
## Summary
A long inline object that does not fit the room left on its line (a wide equation, for example)
moves whole to the next line, leaving the line above short. That end was unreachable with the
caret: `off_at_x` skipped the wrap offset, so `→` from the last character jumped to the start of
the next line, and a click at the line's end landed before its last character.

The same offset now has two visual stops, as in Word: the end of the previous line (upstream,
after its last character) and the start of the next line (downstream). `Session` keeps the caret's
affinity; layout offers `caret_on_affinity`, `hit_affinity`, `at_wrap_end`,
`line_bounds_affinity` and `vertical_affinity`; the UI draws, clicks and drags with the affinity.
Programmatic `caret.set` accepts `"upstream"`, and `document.layout` reports it for headless
checks.

- `→` onto a wrap end shows it upstream; `→` again goes to the next line's start; `←` comes back.
- `Home`/`End`, `↑`/`↓`, clicks, drags and page moves keep the correct stop.
- Bidi lines keep their previous behaviour.

## Tests
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout` — 490 passed
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-engine` — 868 passed (plus 39 in integration tests, 1 ignored)
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui` — 824 passed, 2 ignored (plus 10 in integration tests)
- New regression tests: `crates/layout/src/tests.rs::the_end_of_a_line_shortened_by_a_wrapped_object_is_a_caret_stop`
  (a picture wider than the room left on its line) and the same test in `crates/engine/src/tests.rs`
  (Right / Right / Left / End / Home and a click at the line's end).
- `cargo fmt` clean. `cargo xtask ci` still stops at pre-existing clippy lints on this toolchain
  (Rust 1.95) in code untouched by this change.

## Related

title: G14: Romanian (ro-RO) spelling and grammar proofing
author: vioreltus
body:
Adds Romanian (`ro-RO`) spelling and grammar proofing, the same way Czech and Indonesian work: the installed Hunspell `ro_RO` dictionary is read at runtime, nothing is bundled.

## What this changes

**Proofing (`crates/proof/src/ro/`)**
- `ProofLang::Ro` for `ro`, `ro-RO`, `ro-MD`, `ron`, `rum` and the retired `mo`/`mol` (Romani `rom` and Romansh `rm` stay `Other`).
- Spelling from `ro_RO` (Debian/Ubuntu `hunspell-ro`, LibreOffice `dict-ro`, the Dictionaries folder, `WORDCRAFT_DICTIONARIES`). Without one, no marks, and the status bar shows **Romanian (no dictionary)** (`missing_dictionary` / `unreadable_dictionary` now name `ro_RO`).
- **Cedilla vs comma below.** A word typed with `ş`/`ţ` (old keyboards, text pasted from old documents) is flagged when the dictionary spells it with `ș`/`ț`, with its own message (*Se scrie cu ș și ț cu virgulă, nu cu sedilă*), and the comma-below form is the first suggestion. An old cedilla-only dictionary still accepts the comma-below spelling.
- Suggestions: the comma-below form, then `sînt`/`sîntem`/`sînteți` → `sunt`/`suntem`/`sunteți` (MAP alone would offer the unrelated `sânt`), then the dictionary-driven ranking Czech uses (MAP/REP/TRY/KEY of the loaded file: `pana` → `până`, `cînd` → `când`).
- Hyphenated forms accepted whole or by parts, elided forms and clitics counting as known (`într-o`, `dintr-un`, `dă-mi`, `s-a`, `ADN-ul`, `SMS-uri`).
- Conservative grammar with Romanian messages: repeated word (`da da`, `încet încet`, `tic tac` allowed), space before punctuation, double space, sentence capital (Romanian abbreviations such as `str.`, `nr.`, `art.`, `alin.`, `prof.`, `etc.`; initials; Roman numerals; a quotation ending in `?`/`!` goes on in lower case), doubled punctuation. No agreement or comma rules.
- Hyphenation keeps the English fallback.

**Interface**

title: Reject signs and non-digits in parse_date fields
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/controls.rs:113-123 (parse_date)` (no existing issue): parse_date accepts '+' signs inside the month and day fields.

## Cause
parse_date cut the year, month and day out as fixed-width slices and passed each one straight to `str::parse`. That function accepts a leading '+', so input like `2024-+1-+5` or `+123-01-01` was read as a valid date instead of being rejected.

## Fix
Each slice must now be made up only of ASCII digits before it is parsed. Anything else makes parse_date return None, so set_date and the other callers reject it with 'date: YYYY-MM-DD'.

## Verified
- Regression test `cmd::controls::tests::parse_date_rejects_signs_and_non_digits`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --lib parse_date_rejects_signs_and_non_digits`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The range checks and the handling of full ISO date-times (anything after the 10th character is still ignored) are unchanged. No command-level set_date test was added, because the unit test covers the shared parser that set_date calls.

title: Return None from parse_number when the value overflows f64
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/doc/src/locale_number.rs:104` (no existing issue): parse_number returns infinity for a very long digit string.

## Cause
`parse_number` accepts digit strings up to 400 bytes and parses them with `str::parse::<f64>`. That call returns infinity on overflow instead of an error, so a 350-digit cell produced `Some(inf)`. The inf then went into table sort and formulas, and `format_number` printed it as "0".

## Fix
After parsing, `parse_number` now returns `None` when the value is not finite. Large values that still fit in an f64, such as 300 digits, still parse as before.

## Verified
- Regression test `locale_number::tests::overflowing_digit_strings_are_not_numbers`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-doc --lib overflowing_digit_strings_are_not_numbers`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The 400-byte input limit and `format_number`'s handling of non-finite values are unchanged.

title: #3584: patterned shading (w:shd pctN, solid) is drawn as the colour it averages to
author: dpkruse
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @dpkruse (Kruse Legal)._

Fixes #3584.

A `w:shd` percentage pattern is now drawn as the colour it averages to: the pattern colour over the fill at the pattern's coverage, as Word draws it. Before, only `w:fill` was read, so `<w:shd w:val="pct80" w:color="auto" w:fill="FFFFFF"/>` (80% black dots on white, a dark grey bar in Word) was drawn white. The Australian family court's published forms use this for their Part heading bars.

### Cause
`PropCtx::shd_fill` (`crates/docx/src/read/props.rs`) returned `w:fill` whenever it parsed, and used the pattern colour only for `solid` with no fill. `pctN` was never looked at, and `solid` with a fill drew the fill.

### Fix
Following ECMA-376 §17.18.78 (`ST_Shd`): for `solid` and `pct5`…`pct95` (`pct12`/`pct37`/`pct62`/`pct87` are the eighths, 12.5%…87.5%), the shading is `ink × p + fill × (1 − p)`:

- `ink`: `w:color`, a theme colour (`w:themeColor`/`Tint`/`Shade`) first; automatic is black.
- `fill`: `w:fill`, a theme fill first; automatic is white.

`clear`, `nil` and the stripe and cross patterns are unchanged (their fill). Every `w:shd` (run, paragraph, cell, table and table style) is read through this one function, so all of them are covered.

On save the shading is still written as `clear` with a fill, now the blended colour, so a saved file looks the same in Word. Writing the pattern back unchanged would be a separate change.

### Tests
- `crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs`, `patterned_shading_is_drawn_as_the_colour_it_averages_to`: 10 cells (`pct80`→`333333`, `pct25`→`BFBFBF`, `pct50` red→`FF8080`, `solid` with a white fill→black, `pct10` all automatic→`E6E6E6`, `pct12`→`DFDFDF`, clear, clear-auto, a stripe pattern, a theme pattern colour), plus a paragraph's and a run's pattern.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes locally (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

title: #3585: automatic text is white on dark cell and paragraph shading
author: dpkruse
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @dpkruse (Kruse Legal)._

Fixes #3585.

Automatic text is now drawn white on a dark cell or paragraph shading, as Word (and LibreOffice) draw it. Before, it stayed black: on the Australian family court's *Affidavit* form, "COURT USE ONLY" on its black cell was black on black.

### Cause
`text_color` (`crates/layout/src/display.rs`) already turns automatic text white on a dark background, but `lines()` passed it only the run's own `shading.or(highlight)`. The cell's `w:tcPr/w:shd` and the paragraph's `w:pPr/w:shd` are drawn as `Placed::Fill` items before the lines, and were never considered.

### Fix
- `stories_display` keeps the backgrounds it has drawn so far: cell and paragraph fills, and the mostly opaque fill (under 50% transparent) of an unturned rectangle or text box (`display::ground`). A gradient counts as its colour averaged along its length. Each line is drawn against the newest one under the middle of the line, after the run's own shading or highlight. A white text box over a dark cell therefore keeps black text, and an unfilled box shows what's under it.
- PDF export draws each placed item alone (`Pdf::draws`, for tagging). `Exporter::page` now keeps the same running list of backgrounds for each list (header, footer, body) and passes it through `display::page_display_over(doc, page, opts, behind)`. `page_display` is `page_display_over` with nothing behind.
- Turned (vertical) lines and warped text are unchanged.

**Known limitation:** a gradient whose stops fade to transparent over another dark fill is treated as its opaque colours only. Following a gradient's opacity across the shape is left for a separate change if a real document needs it.

### Tests
- `crates/layout/src/tests.rs`, `automatic_text_on_dark_cell_and_paragraph_shading_is_white`. Text on a black cell and on a dark paragraph is white. Text on a grey cell, and a red run on a black cell, keep black and red. Each is checked twice: the who…

title: #3009: a paragraph opening with a page or column break moves once, whatever it keeps
author: dpkruse
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @dpkruse (Kruse Legal)._

Fixes #3009.

A paragraph that opens with a page or column break is now moved by its break only, as Word does. When it also had **keep with next** or **keep lines together**, or the paragraph before it kept with next, WordCraft moved it twice: once for the keep, to the next column, and then again for the break. A column was skipped, or a blank page appeared.

#3009 has no sample file. The Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia's *Application for Consent Orders* kit (https://www.fcfcoa.gov.au/fl/forms) shows it. On page 8, a two-column section, the "Relevant legislation" heading is a `Heading2` (keep with next) that starts with `<w:br w:type="column"/>`. Word puts it at the top of column 2. title: Fix spurious 零 after a group's trailing zeros in Chinese numerals
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/doc/src/cjk_numbers.rs:47-55 (Counting::format)` (no existing issue): Chinese counting numerals add a wrong 零 when a group ends in zero and the next group starts with a thousands digit.

## Cause
In Counting::format, trailing zeros at the end of a four-digit group set zero_pending. The flag stayed set across the 万/亿 boundary, so a 零 was written before the next group's thousands digit, as in 201000 → 二十万零一千.

## Fix
zero_pending is now cleared after each nonzero group is written. Trailing zeros no longer count as a gap, and 201000 gives 二十万一千. All-zero groups still skip before that line, so a real gap such as 一亿零一 keeps its 零.

## Verified
- Regression test `cjk_numbers::tests::chinese_no_zero_after_group_trailing_zeros`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-doc --lib chinese_no_zero_after_group_trailing_zeros`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The Japanese and Korean formats, which have no zero character, and the existing handling of zeros between nonzero digits. The regression test also checks that 100100, 100000001, 100010000 and 120000001 are unchanged.

title: #3603: legacy form fields can be filled in, under forms protection too
author: dpkruse
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @dpkruse (Kruse Legal)._

Part of #3603. This is the engine half; typing into a field on the page and Tab between fields will follow in a second PR built on this one.

A Word form built from legacy form fields (`FORMTEXT`, `FORMCHECKBOX`, `FORMDROPDOWN`) and protected for **Filling in forms** opened read only in WordCraft: every edit was refused, because forms protection only counted content controls as fillable. Every Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia form is built this way (https://www.fcfcoa.gov.au/fl/forms): the 12 we use hold about 2,000 text fields, 850 check boxes and 8 drop-downs, and only one of them has any content controls.

### What's new
- **`developer.fillFormField`** fills in a legacy form field, named by `field` (its `w:name`), by `at`, or the one at the selection:
  - a text field takes `text`: one line, at most `w:maxLength` characters; cleared, it shows five en spaces, as an unfilled field does;
  - a check box takes `checked`, or toggles: `w:checked` is written last in `w:checkBox`, as the schema orders it (ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.16.7);
  - a drop-down takes `index` or `entry`: `w:ddList/w:result` is written first in `w:ddList` (§17.16.9), and the result shows the entry.
  Nothing else in `w:ffData` changes.

title: Format Page Numbers: the command opens its dialog instead of doing nothing (#1443, #3608)
author: akamusti
body:
## The problem

**Insert › Header & Footer › Page Number ▸ Format Page Numbers…** did nothing: no dialog
appeared, and the only visible effect was that the document was marked as edited. The same
happened when **Format Page Numbers** was run from the command search (Help › Commands).

## The cause

`layout.pageNumberFormat` is the *dialog's* command: the number format and the start are the
Format Page Numbers dialog's fields (#1113, PR #3071). A call without them means "nothing to
apply", and the command took that as a call that changed nothing — but still marked the document
as edited. That is the symptom in #1443 (and #3608, the same report).

The dialog was written for the ribbon item alone, so every other way of reaching the command (the
command search, the keytips) still fell into the same dead end.

## The fix

- **`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`** — `input_dialog` maps `layout.pageNumberFormat` (no `format`, no
  `start`) to the `pageNumbers` dialog. This is the path every other command with a dialog takes
  (`insert.symbol`, `insert.field`, `table.formula`, …), so the ribbon item, the command search and
  the keytips all reach the dialog. `{"start": null}` is an answer (the pages number on from the
  section before), so only a call without the key at all opens the dialog.
- **`crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs`** — the ribbon item runs the command (`layout.pageNumberFormat`)
  instead of naming the dialog, so the ribbon and the command search share one path and the item
  answers to the id the feature catalog and the keytips know. The menu items moved into
  `page_number_items`, next to the other testable menu helpers.
- **`crates/engine/src/cmd/page.rs`** — a call with neither a format nor a start is refused
  (`` `format` or `start` is required ``) instead of silently doing nothing and marking the
  document as edited. A call with a format and/or a start applies it as before: `start` left out
  keeps the section's start, `{"start": null}` numbers on from the sectio…

title: Layout: a page break at the end of the document or of a section starts no blank page
author: cyril265
body:
**Problem:** a page break that is the last thing in a document (at the end of its last paragraph, after text or alone) starts a blank last page with only the footer on it, and `NUMPAGES` counts it. A page break followed only by the empty paragraph that holds a next-page section break starts a blank page between the two sections. Word starts neither page.

**Cause:** `place_para_in_flow` in `crates/layout/src/lib.rs` starts a new page after every page break. At the end of the body that page stays empty; before a section break the empty closing paragraph takes it, and the next section starts one more.

**Fix:** such a break starts no page when `break_starts_no_page` says so, following Word for Mac 16.114 (compatibility modes 12 and 15 agree):
- A page break that is the last thing in its section's last paragraph (only bookmarks and other markers after it) starts no page. The next section starts its page as usual; a continuous one goes on on the same page.
- An empty paragraph closing a section before one that starts a page gets no page of its own after a page break. An empty paragraph before it, text or a shape in it, or a column break instead keep the usual pages.
- That closing paragraph ignores its page break before, draws no list label and doesn't count in its list.
- Editor: a page break inserted at the end of the document (Ctrl+Enter, Insert › Page Break, Layout › Breaks › Page) goes into a paragraph of its own followed by an empty paragraph with the last paragraph's formatting, as Word's Insert Page Break leaves it; Backspace there removes the second page.

| Body | Word | main | branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AAA`, a paragraph of only a page break | 1 page | 2 | 1 |
| `AAA` + page break, an empty paragraph | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| `AAA`, a break paragraph, an empty paragraph with a next-page section break, `BBB` | 2, `BBB` on p2 | 3, p3 | 2, p2 |
| the same, next section `evenPage` | 2, p2 | 3, p3 | 2, p2 |

title: DOCX: VML rectangles and text boxes filled with a picture are drawn with it
author: cyril265
body:
**Problem:** a VML rectangle or text box filled with a picture (`<v:fill type="frame" r:id="…" o:title="…"/>`) is drawn as a plain shape in its fill colour, without the picture. Logos and letterhead backgrounds made this way come out as empty white boxes, or as nothing when the outline is white too.

**Cause:** the VML reader in `crates/docx/src/read/story.rs` takes only the colour from such a fill (`Fill::Solid`); the picture its `r:id` points to is not read.

**Fix:** `read_vml_all` and `vml_group_members` (`v:group` members, read since #1662) pass each shape to `vml_picture_fill`, which gives what Word draws, in this order: the fill colour, the picture stretched over the shape's box, the outline and the text.
- Only a frame fill with an `o:title` attribute (empty or not) is drawn as a picture; without it Word draws the fill colour. `opacity` 1, `aspect` `ignore`, an `r:id` that resolves to a picture, and a rectangle or text box unturned or turned by quarter turns, not flipped.
- The fill colour stays under the picture and shows through transparent pixels; it is left out under a JPEG or a PNG without alpha or `tRNS`. The picture stays upright on a turned shape.
- For a shape of its own the result is a picture, or a group of the layers marked `picture_fill` (document model, set only here and when such a group is read back). A text box that fills such a marked group is its hit target (`framing_text_box` in `crates/layout`), so a click inside still edits the text; any other group, a `v:group` with such members included, is taken whole, as on `main`.
- Saving writes a DrawingML picture or `wpg` group; the VML is not kept, as for every other VML shape. title: Layout: objects in headers and cells are placed from their paragraph's top above its space before
author: cyril265
body:
**Problem:** a picture or shape in a header, footer, table cell or text box that is placed relative to its paragraph or line (`wp:positionV relativeFrom="paragraph"` / `"line"`, VML's default `mso-position-vertical-relative:text` / `line`) stands lower than in Word by its paragraph's space before. **Cause:** `layout_box` in `crates/layout/src/lib.rs`, which lays out headers, footers, cells and text boxes, measured a paragraph's floating objects from below its space before. In the body `anchor_floats` measures from above it, and Word does that everywhere.

**Fix:** `layout_box` places a paragraph's floating objects from its top above the space it adds before (`y - applied_before`), and gives `place_objects` the same origin (for objects not placed yet and for offsets when an object is dragged). Only the space the paragraph adds counts, after it collapses with the space after above. | second in a table cell | 104.6 | 140.6 | 104.6 |

title: Layout: text before a floating table or shape on its page wraps around it
author: cyril265
body:
**Problem:** a paragraph that comes before a floating table (`w:tblpPr`) on its page stays where the flow put it, under the table. Word lays all the text on the page out around the float, so that paragraph moves below it, or beside a narrow one. Letters that start with an empty paragraph and a full-width letterhead table placed on the page had their body one line higher than in Word. For shapes #2237 (for #2048) does this, but where the text before no longer fits it pushes that text down; Word moves the anchor paragraph with its shape to the next page.

**Cause:** pagination places each block once, top to bottom, so a float's wrap area only reaches the blocks after it. #2237's extra layout pass handles floating objects only.

**Fix:** a new module, `crates/layout/src/float_before.rs`:
- While a page is filled (only in documents with a floating table or a wrapped floating object), the pagination state before each block is kept. When a floating table or a paragraph's floating objects land on lines placed before them on their page, the blocks from the first covered one are laid out again with the page's wrap areas known; the floats stay where they were.
- The new layout is kept only when the text before still ends on that page and the float's paragraph keeps its first line there (widow control counted). Otherwise the old layout stays and a paragraph with objects starts the next page, as in Word.
- `w:tblpY` 0 without `w:tblpYSpec` places a page- or margin-anchored table at the text, as Word does.
- Floats handled here skip #2237's extra pass; the others still get it. At most 512 blocks before a float and 16 floats per page are laid out again.
- A line with exact or at-least spacing is checked against floats with its whole height, not just the font's own line, before and after a float's anchor (`para.rs`). Word keeps that height clear: in Calibri 11 pt with 17 pt lines a full-width table or square-wrapped shape whose top lands 16.5 pt into a line moves it below; before,…

author: cyril265
body:

Turned text fits the width the same way. This replaces #2912's rule under its names (`Ctx::fitted_boxes`, `ParaEnv::fitted`).
- The fitted size is used for the fill and outline, the wrap area, alignment, the object's rectangle and an inline box's line; the stored extent is saved unchanged. A VML shape with `stroked="f"` has no outline width (was 0.75 pt), and an outline that isn't drawn is saved with its width.

title: Tests: group members with the group's fill, as Word draws them
author: cyril265
body:

title: Save As and Export: Browse in WordCraft when the system dialog doesn't appear (#3535)
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
Fixes #3535. For #3467 it gives a way to save: Ctrl+S on a new document still asks for the system dialog first, but File › Save As › Browse in WordCraft… now works even after that dialog hangs.

### The problem

On some Linux desktops the system file dialog never appears (#3467 is the AppImage on CachyOS, #3535 is niri). It fails in one of two ways. Either the portal takes the request and never answers, or it answers at once as if the user had cancelled. In the first case `ask_file` keeps the request pending, so every later pick only says "A file dialog is already open." From then on Save, Ctrl+S, Save As and Export all do nothing. The host can't tell either case from a real dialog, so the automatic fallback from #576 never starts. File › Open has had a manual way out since #576; Save As and Export had none.

### The change

- **File › Save As** gets Browse in WordCraft… under Browse…, on Linux and the BSDs (the same condition as Open). It runs `ui.fileBrowser {"purpose": "save"}`, which gives up a pending system dialog first and saves through WordCraft's own browser.
- **The export formats** (File › Export, and below the settings on the Print page) end with the same button, which runs the new `ui.fileBrowser {"purpose": "export"}`.
- **Exporting in the built-in browser** lists Export's formats as the types, starting on the one asked for. Choosing another type switches the export format and the extension on the file name. The automatic #576 fallback for an export gets the same list.
- **No new interface strings.** The button reuses the Open page's label and the types reuse the export format labels, so the nine complete catalogs need nothing.
- `EXPORT_FORMATS` and `export_file_ext` move out of `export_formats` and `export_dialog`, so the page and the browser share one list.

### Tests

title: Fonts: a missing font is drawn in the font table's alternate name, as in Word
author: cyril265
body:
**Problem:** when a document names a font the machine doesn't have, WordCraft draws its own substitute for the name even if the font table names an alternate (`w:altName`). `HelveticaNeue` with altName Arial comes out in Helvetica Neue on macOS and Carlito on Linux; Word draws Arial, so lines wrap differently.

**Cause:** the DOCX reader doesn't read `w:altName`, and `lookup_family` in `crates/layout/src/para.rs` picks the substitute from the name alone.

**Fix:**
- The reader keeps each entry's alternate (`Settings::font_alt_names`). The font table is already saved unchanged.
- `word::document_family` (`crates/fonts`): the font if it is there, else the alternate if that is there, else the fallback as before. An alternate that isn't there counts as none: the font is found exactly as without one. Run, complex-script and East Asian fonts use it, as do equation text, chart text, watermarks and the check whether a bullet's private-use character can be drawn. A new WordArt box is sized in the font its text is drawn in (Cambria for a missing roman font, as its text).
- A font Word ships counts as there when its metric-compatible open font is installed (Carlito, Caladea, Liberation, Arimo, Tinos, the Palatino look-alikes). `substitutes` now tries Arimo and Tinos before Helvetica and Times, so such a font is drawn in its clone.
- Embedded fonts and full names (`Arial Bold`) count as installed. A PostScript name (`ArialMT`) doesn't when the font has a usable alternate. Without one it is found by that name, as on `main`, so an installed font named by its PostScript name and classed roman stays itself instead of Cambria.

title: Gap 19: ODT format changes keep their author and date
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
Part of gap 19 (RTF and ODT depth): the "ODT formatting revisions left" item.

### What ODF allows

ODF 1.3 Part 3 §5.5.6 defines `text:format-change` as a record of who changed the formatting and when, over a range marked by `text:change-start`/`text:change-end`. It says outright that the element "does not contain formatting changes that have taken place". So an ODT file never holds the formatting from before the change. WordCraft read these regions as no change, and saving to ODT dropped every formatting revision.

### The change

- **Import:** text inside a format-change range opens with a formatting revision, keeping the region's author and date. Since the old formatting is unknown, the revision's old formatting is the current one. A paragraph whose mark is inside a range (the range runs past the paragraph's end, the way this file already marks an inserted paragraph mark) opens with a paragraph formatting revision the same way. Accept and Reject both clear the mark and leave the formatting as it is, and the Reviewing Pane lists it as "Formatted". That holds in headings too: where the style's size replaces a span's, the old formatting drops the span's size as well.
- **Export:** character formatting changes are written as format-change ranges around their runs. A paragraph formatting change is a range over the paragraph mark: it opens at the end of the paragraph's content and closes where the next paragraph begins. It reopens on the paragraph, also when the paragraph is empty, when its text has changes of its own, or when it is joined to the next one at a tracked deleted mark (the change is then written inside the deletion's region, over that mark).
- **Region order:** a change mark inside deleted content (an insertion, or a format change over a deleted paragraph mark) may name a region listed after the deletion's own region, since ODF 1.3 doesn't fix the order of `text:changed-region` elements. When a file has tracked changes, the reader now reads every region's…

title: Tables: a row fits on a page only with room for the border below it (#3814)
author: dfgodvan
body:
Fixes #3814.

## Problem
`place_table` breaks the page before a row when `pb.y + row.height` passes the bottom margin. The border under a row belongs to the next row's top band, so it isn't in `row.height`, but Word wants it on the page too: a row that ends less than that border's width above the margin moves on. WordCraft kept such a row, so a page could hold one row more than Word's.

## Fix
`crates/layout/src/table.rs`, `crates/layout/src/lib.rs`:
- `RowLayout::edge`: the width of the bottom border of a row that another row follows (the widest of its cells' bottom bands; 0 for the last row, whose border is already in its height).
- `place_table` checks `pb.y + cur.height + cur.edge` against the bottom. The check that keeps repeated header rows from staying alone at the foot of a page (#1705) counts the edge too, otherwise the two disagree: the first row "fits" for the header check, then moves on in the loop, and the header stays alone (`a_repeated_header_is_never_left_alone_when_the_table_starts_mid_page` fails without it).
- The part of a split row left on the page has no edge (it ends the page); the rest keeps the row's.

## Result
The repro of #3814 (A4, 60 rows, 3 pt borders), rows on page 1:

| bottom margin | Word for Mac | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 77.8 pt | 41 | 41 | 41 |
| 78.2–81.0 pt (8 steps) | 40 | 41 | 40 |
| 81.4 pt | 40 | 40 | 40 |

The last row's text ends at the same place as in Word (743.9 pt here, 743.7 pt in Word, the 0.2 pt is the font's line height).

## Testing
- New `a_row_leaves_room_for_the_border_below_it` (`crates/layout/src/tests.rs`): tables with 0.5 and 3 pt borders after 20–39 filler lines; the last row on page 1 ends at least its border's width above the margin. Fails on main (`border 3, 23 filler lines: the last row ends at 717.04834, the margin at 720`).
- Existing table tests pass, including the repeated-header ones. `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout -p wordcraft-engine -p wordcraft-pdf`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo c…

title: Layout: keep with next takes the 0.01 pt of slack the other fit checks take
author: dfgodvan
body:
## Problem
`place_para_in_flow` moves a paragraph kept with the next one to a new page when `pb.y + need > pb.bottom`, while every other fit check in the layout (lines, rows, floats, the header-row check) allows 0.01 pt. A kept paragraph whose need comes to a rounding error over the bottom moves on alone, though its lines would have fit.

## Fix
`pb.y + need > pb.bottom + 0.01`, as elsewhere.

## Testing
New `keep_with_next_fits_to_the_hundredth_of_a_point`: exact line spacing fills the page to 0.005 pt over the bottom with a kept paragraph and the next one's line; the kept paragraph stays on page 1. Fails on main.
