title: Drop U+FFFE and U+FFFF from ODT export text
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/formats/src/odt.rs:49-63 (fn x, the ODT text escaper; filter at line 58)` (no existing issue): ODT export writes U+FFFE/U+FFFF into content.xml, producing a malformed file.

## Cause
The ODT text escaper `x()` only filtered characters where `char::is_control()` is true. The noncharacters U+FFFE and U+FFFF are not control characters but XML 1.0 forbids them, so they were written raw into content.xml and made it malformed.

## Fix
`x()` now drops U+FFFE and U+FFFF, as the DOCX writer's escaper already does. A unit test covers the escaper.

## Verified
- Regression test `odt::tests::escaper_drops_noncharacters`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-formats escaper_drops_noncharacters`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The DOCX writer and the importers. A .txt or RTF import can still produce these characters in a document. The ODT writer now drops them on export.

title: DOCX: a malformed main document part is an error, not a truncated document (#3599)
author: fluorine
body:
## What

A `.docx` whose `word/document.xml` is not well-formed opened with only the text before the first error. There was no warning, `wordcraft-cli` exited 0, and saving wrote the truncated text as a valid DOCX, so the lost text was gone for good.

The cause is the shared XML reader. It does not check end-tag names, ignores an end tag with nothing open, and closes elements still open at the end of the data. That suits small secondary parts, but not the main document.

The main part is now read strictly (`xml::parse_strict`, used by `Package::xml_strict`). A mismatched end tag, or an element left open at the end of the data, returns `DocxError::Xml`. The document does not open. The user sees an error, as in LibreOffice, and nothing is overwritten.

Fixes #3599

## Not changed

- Secondary parts (styles, numbering, headers, footers, notes, comments) still read leniently and a broken one is skipped with a log line, as before. A malformed header or footer can still lose its content silently. I left that for a separate change because a stricter reader there would stop a whole document from opening over a small part.
- The ODT, XLSX and ODS readers have the same pattern (#3767, #3768). Open PR #1862 already fixes those two.

## Tests

- `a_malformed_main_part_is_an_error_not_a_truncated_document` covers the three cases of the issue: a `<` in a run, a paragraph left open, and a mismatched end tag. It also checks that well-formed text with `<-` still reads whole. It fails without the fix.
- `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-docx --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.

title: Layout: no ligatures unless the document asks (w14:ligatures), as in Word
author: jpc7k1
body:
### What

When a run has no `w14:ligatures`, shaping left the shaper's own defaults on, so standard and contextual ligatures (fi, fl, ffi) were drawn. Word draws **none** unless the document asks (Font › Advanced › Ligatures defaults to None). The narrower ligature glyphs made WordCraft fit more text per line than Word in long justified paragraphs, which shifts line and page breaks.

### How it was observed (black-box, synthetic document)

A synthetic one-paragraph document (Garamond 12, justified, double-spaced; the sentence below repeated six times) was exported to PDF by Word for Mac 16.114, once as is and once with `w14:ligatures="none"` on the run:

> The firm filed the official affidavit; the fiduciary flatly refused fifty office files, finding the conflict difficult and the effort inefficient.

- Word: identical line breaks with and without `w14:ligatures="none"`, so Word's default is no ligatures.
- WordCraft before this change: two of the eight lines break differently from Word.
- WordCraft with ligatures off: identical to Word.

### Change

- `crates/layout/src/para.rs`: every ligature feature (`liga`, `clig`, `hlig`, `dlig`) is set explicitly; with no `w14:ligatures` they are off. Kerning is unchanged.
- `ligatures_follow_w14_ligatures` now asserts one glyph per letter without `w14:ligatures` ("as in Word") and that `standard` draws them.
- The caret-inside-a-ligature tests (`tests_ligature.rs`, `right_arrow_moves_through_a_ligature_one_letter_at_a_time`) now ask for standard ligatures explicitly, since that is what they exercise.

### Results

title: Tables: a file with no default table style gives its tables no cell margins
author: naxvog
body:
## What was wrong

Since #2434, a cell whose `w:tcMar` sets only some sides takes the other sides from the table's default cell margins. When neither the table nor its style sets any, those defaults fall back to 5.4 pt left and right (`DEFAULT_MARGINS` in `crates/layout/src/table.rs`).

Word's 0.08" (108 twips) comes from its Normal Table style. Every Word-written file carries that style as the default table style (`w:type="table" w:default="1"`). A file with no default table style gets no cell margins in Word. In the docxide-pdf fixtures `case212`–`case219` (no table styles at all; each cell sets only `w:right` = 108), Word puts the cell text at the page margin, in both compatibility mode 14 and 15. WordCraft has put it 5.4 pt further right since #2434. `case204`–`case211` (no `w:tcMar`) and the fixtures without a styles part show the same thing; WordCraft got those wrong before #2434 too. In `case109` (no styles part), for example, Word's inside border sits at 322.0 pt = 85.05 pt margin + 236.8 pt first column, so the table isn't moved out by a cell margin.

## Fix

The DOCX reader notes whether the styles part names a default table style (a missing styles part counts as none). If it doesn't, a table with no `w:tblCellMar` whose style chain sets no cell margins gets explicit zero margins. They are stored as the table's own because saving writes a default Normal Table, which would otherwise bring back 0.08" on reopening.

Test: `no_default_table_style_means_no_cell_margins` (`crates/docx/tests/cell_margin_inheritance.rs`):
- no styles part, a styles part without a default table style, and Word's usual Normal Table;
- a table whose own style sets margins;
- a save and reopen that keeps the zeros as `w:tblCellMar`.

## Bench (docxide-pdf suite, 390 fixtures, against main 00bc6a4b)

## Summary

GridCraft (`apps/gridcraft-web/src/host.rs`) and PdfCraft (`apps/pdfcraft-web`, `mod host`) can be framed by a same-origin page that keeps the files, such as a Nextcloud app or a personal file server. WordCraft's web build had no such bridge, so a framing page could not hand it a document or store what it saves. This PR adds one with the same protocol:

| Message | Direction | Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `wordcraft:ready` | to parent | `{ version }`: sent once the app is running and listening, so send a file now |
| `wordcraft:open` | from parent | `{ name, bytes }` (an `ArrayBuffer` or `Uint8Array`): opens like File › Open or a dropped file |
| `wordcraft:save` | to parent | `{ name, saveAs, bytes }` (a transferred `ArrayBuffer`): Save, Save As, File › Export and Export as PDF |
| `wordcraft:dirty` | to parent | `{ dirty }`: sent when unsaved changes appear or go away |
| `wordcraft:failed` | to parent | `{ error }`: the app couldn't start (no WebGPU or WebGL2) |

The bridge is only active with `?host=parent` and only inside a frame whose parent is on the page's own origin. It ignores messages from anywhere else and posts only to that origin. As in PdfCraft (#2167 there), a cross-origin parent leaves the bridge off, so saves never disappear silently. Without `?host=parent`, nothing changes.

## Behaviour in host mode

- **Saving goes to the parent.** Save, Save As and Export hand their bytes to the parent instead of `showSaveFilePicker` or a download, so no save finishes later and `async_saves` is unused.
- **Save writes the opened file back** under its own name and format, as the desktop app's `file.save` does. Plain web Save always suggests `<stem>.docx` (fine for a download), but a host would otherwise turn every Save of `report.odt` or `notes.md` into a new `.docx`. An import-only Word 97–2003 file (#2445) is still saved as `.docx`. A format that doesn't keep everything (Markdown, text, HTML) leaves the document unsaved, as on the desktop.

title: Layout: in older documents, tabs behind a float keep their text on the row
author: naxvog
body:
## What was wrong

#1840 made a left tab whose stop lies past the line's right edge start the next line, so a TOC entry's page number keeps its leader. Beside a floating picture, though, that edge is where the float cuts the line, not the paragraph's right indent.

The docxide-pdf fixture `ut_koer_annual_meeting_minutes` (Word 2010 mode) has a header with a centred logo (`wrapTight`) between two names, e.g. "Penningmeester" + 10 tabs + "Secretaris". Since #1840, every name after the tabs moves to a line of its own: the header grows from five lines to nine, pushes the body down, and the document gets a fourth page.

## What Word does

In Word's PDF of that file, the tab stops behind the logo are counted as if the logo weren't there, and the text after them starts in the span past the logo, at the stop it reached (or the span's left, whichever is further right). "Penningmeester" + 10 default stops + 15 spaces = 423.3 pt; Word puts "Secretaris" at 423.45 pt. The other two header lines fit the same rule exactly.

`belgian_youth_program_certificate` (body, Word 2013 mode, a signature picture between the tabs) behaves differently. There Word matches #1840's rule: the tab starts the span past the float and goes to the first stop there. I checked all 390 docxide-pdf fixtures, plus the 417 that upstream docxide-pdf has added since, with both rules. These two are the only documents where the rules differ. The likely switch is the compatibility mode (14 vs 15), but the two documents also differ in header against body. That's noted in the code and in `docs/layout-parity.md`, so a Word comparison can settle it.

`break_lines` (`crates/layout/src/para.rs`): before Word 2013 mode, a left tab whose stop lies behind a float takes no room and goes to its stop. title: Print and PDF export use the Numeral setting (#3784)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3784.

With File › Options › Advanced › Numeral set to Hindi, the screen showed Eastern Arabic-Indic digits, but printing produced Western digits. Only the screen layout (`Session::layout`) passed the Numeral setting to the layout. Every output layout used the default, which is Western digits.

The fix covers every way a copy of the document is made:

- **Print, File › Export › PNG and the print preview:** `Session::export_layout_with` now resolves `view.numeral` the same way the screen layout does (`System` is resolved against the system locale).
- **File › Export PDF, Save As .pdf and the web download:** these go through `cmd::file::export_options` and `io::save_*`, which use only the document and so never saw the setting. `io::ExportOptions` gets a resolved `numeral` field, filled in by `export_options`. It is passed to `wordcraft_pdf::export` through a new `PdfOptions::numeral` field (default `Arabic`, which is the old behaviour) and to `io_ext::render_png`.

Headless conversions with no session (`wordcraft-cli convert`) keep Western digits, because nothing sets a Numeral mode there. This is display only, like on screen: the PDF's text layer and the saved document keep the digits as they were typed.

Tests (both fail without the fix):
- `export_layout_follows_the_numeral_setting`: the print/export layout of "Year 2024" draws different glyphs once Numeral is Hindi.
- `pdf_and_png_copies_follow_the_numeral_setting`: the PDF and PNG copies made by `export_options` + `save_bytes_opts` change when Numeral is Hindi. The creation date is pinned so the PDF bytes depend only on the layout, and the test first checks that two Western exports are byte-identical.

title: fix(docx): write and read a turned object's effect extent as Word does
author: arc-uri-el
body:
Saving a .docx with a picture turned 90° makes Word crop it, and the text after it moves up. WordCraft measures the turned picture's overhang in `wp:effectExtent` against its unturned frame, which for a 254 × 337 pt picture gives +41.5 pt left and right and -41.5 pt top and bottom. From 45° up to 135° and from 225° up to 315°, Word measures against the frame with width and height exchanged, so a quarter turn records zero, and it draws negative top and bottom extents as a crop. I checked what Word writes for that picture at 30, 44, 45, 60, 90, 120, 134, 135, 224, 225, 270, 314 and 315°, inline and floating; the switch is exactly at those angles.

Reading had the same mismatch the other way: a picture Word turned 60° got about 43 pt of extra space above and below.

`Float::effect_spin_pad` gives Word's measure, and the docx reader and writers use it. Layout keeps `spin_pad`. Two existing tests asserted the old values and now use Word's. The new test uses the extents Word writes at 90° and 60°.

title: picture.corrections: a tiny sharpen value no longer panics in the blur (#3646)
author: fluorine
body:
## What

`picture.corrections` with a very small negative `sharpen` (for example `-1e-40`) panicked inside `image::blur`. title: Layout: a paragraph kept with a table needs its header rows and the start of its first row
author: dfgodvan
body:
## Problem
`next_first_line` asks a table that follows a paragraph kept with the next (`w:keepNext`, a table caption typically) for a flat 24 pt. Word keeps the paragraph with the table's repeated header rows and the start of its first row: when they don't fit under it, the caption goes over with the table. With a taller header or first row WordCraft left the caption alone at the foot of the page, and the table started on the next.

The first row need not fit whole. In compatibility mode 15 Word splits it under the caption with the least it can leave on the page: two lines of a cell's text (widow/orphan control in the cells), a whole row it can't split. #3154 also replaces the 24 pt, with the header rows and the whole first row; that keeps the caption on its page less often than Word does when the first row is long (the second table below: Word keeps the caption with 2 of the row's 4 lines from 85 to 105 pt, where the whole row doesn't fit).

title: Layout: tables at the foot of a page before Word 2013 layout (compatibility mode 12 and 14)
author: dfgodvan
body:
Stacked on #3832: the first commit is #3832's, the second (ae7cd83a) is this PR's.

## Problem
Before Word 2013 layout (compatibility mode 12 or 14, and a .docx that doesn't state a mode) Word breaks a table at the foot of a page differently from mode 15:
- a row split across pages divides its cells' text at any line: there is no widow/orphan control in the cells, a single line of the first row may stay on the page;
- the repeated header rows stay alone at the foot of a page when no line of the first row fits under them (the rule of #1705 holds in mode 15 only);
- so a paragraph kept with the table (a caption with `w:keepNext`) goes over only when the header rows don't fit under it.

WordCraft applied the mode 15 rules in every mode: where Word keeps the caption with the header row and one line of the first row, or with the header row alone, WordCraft left the caption alone at the foot of the page (main) or moved it to the next page (#3832).

## Fix
- `crates/layout/src/para.rs`: no widow/orphan control for a paragraph in a table cell before mode 15.
- `crates/layout/src/lib.rs`: the header-rows check in `place_table` (#1705) applies in mode 15 only; before it `table_start_need` asks for the header rows only.

body:

title: Slovak proofing: sk-SK spelling from the installed Hunspell dictionary
author: TheGreatOneYouKnow
body:
## Slovak proofing (sk-SK)

Closes #3806.

Adds Slovak (`sk`, `sk-SK`, `slk`, `slo`) as a proofed language, following the Czech and Indonesian pattern. It also teaches the affix engine `CIRCUMFIX`, which the current Slovak dictionary needs to load.

**Spelling** reads the system Hunspell `sk_SK` dictionary at runtime (`hunspell-sk` on Debian/Ubuntu, LibreOffice's `dict-sk`, the Dictionaries folder or `WORDCRAFT_DICTIONARIES`). Nothing is bundled: the common `sk_SK` is GPL/LGPL/MPL. Without it, Slovak has no spelling marks, as for the other Hunspell languages.

**CIRCUMFIX** (second commit). The current sk-spell `sk_SK` (2.4.x, what LibreOffice ships) uses `CIRCUMFIX` for the `naj…ší` superlatives. The engine listed it as unsupported, so that dictionary was reported unreadable (the blocker noted in #3296 and #3806). The engine now reads it the way Hunspell does:

- An affix whose continuation classes carry the flag is only a word with a prefix and suffix that both carry it: `najrýchlejší` and `najrýchlejšia` are words; `najrýchly` and a paired suffix alone are not.
- The pairing applies only when a suffix is involved, so a stem carrying the prefix flag takes the prefix bare: `krajší/F` → `najkrajší`, which libhunspell accepts.
- The flag gets a bit even though it is only a continuation class. The compact format keeps it, and `forms` lists no unpaired halves.
- Without `CIRCUMFIX` declared, nothing changes for any other dictionary.

**Hyphenated Slovak words** are right as a whole (`najbielo-čiernejší`, listed in the dictionary) or part by part, as Hunspell checks them.

**Suggestions** reuse Czech's dictionary-driven ranking (`cs::suggest::suggest_in`), like Indonesian. One Slovak-specific fix:

- The older `sk_SK` 2.03 has no `MAP` table, only single-letter `REP` pairs.
- REP restores one diacritic per suggestion, so `pocitac` could never reach `počítač`.
- `AffixDict::with_default_map` fills in the Slovak diacritic groups (`aáä`, `oóô`, `lľĺ`, `cč`, …) **only when …

title: Layout: a multiple-spaced line stays on the page while its text fits, as in Word
author: jpc7k1
body:
### What

Multiple line spacing above single puts its extra leading below the text (`baseline_offset`). Word lets that leading of a page's **last** line run into the bottom margin: only the text has to fit above the margin. WordCraft required the whole line box to fit, so multiple-spaced pages ended up to a line early. Double-spaced documents (common in court filings) lost a line on many pages, which compounds into different page counts.

### How it was observed (black-box, synthetic documents)

Synthetic pages of justified Garamond 12 text, widow control off, each pushed down a little more by the space before the first paragraph, exported to PDF by Word for Mac 16.114:

| Spacing | Steps | Word holds one more line than WordCraft did | With this change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Double (`line="480"`) | 14 × 2pt | 7 of 14 steps | 14 / 14 page breaks match Word |
| 1.5 (`360`) | 12 × 1pt | 2 of 12 | 12 / 12 |
| 1.15 (`276`) | 12 × 1pt | 2 of 12 | 12 / 12 |

In every case Word's cutoff is where the last line's *text* reaches the margin, not its full line box.

**Only the bottom margin takes the leading.** On a page whose footer is taller than the bottom margin (so the footer, not the margin, limits the body), Word keeps the whole line clear of the footer; a document with a four-line footer only kept Word's page breaks with that limit. Pages with footnotes are unchanged (the whole line stays clear of the notes).

### Change

- `crates/layout/src/lib.rs` (`place_para_in_flow`): for `LineSpacing::Multiple(m)` with `m > 1`, when the page's limit is the bottom margin and there are no footnotes on the page, a line fits if its text (`baseline - top + text_desc`) ends above the limit; otherwise unchanged.
- New test `a_page_ends_when_a_multiple_spaced_lines_text_no_longer_fits` (1.15, 1.5 and double; fails before this change).
- `space_after_may_overflow_the_bottom_margin_without_notes` now checks the last line's **text** against the margin, since the leading may run past it (its p…

title: ODT import: text:s spaces have a budget for the whole document (#3700)
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
Fixes #3700.

Each `<text:s text:c="n"/>` in an ODT added up to 1,000 spaces, and nothing limited how many such elements a file could hold. The audit's 11.6 KB file with 200,000 of them came out as 200 million spaces and a 1.2 GB peak.

The spaces an element adds beyond the one it stands for now come out of a budget for the whole document: 4 Mi (4,194,304), the figure the issue suggests. Once the budget is spent, each element is one space, so the text grows only with the file and the words on either side stay apart. Documents use `text:s` for runs of a few spaces, nowhere near the budget.

### Tests

- `text_s_spaces_have_a_budget_for_the_whole_document`: 5,000 elements asking for 1,000 spaces each give exactly 5,000 + 4 Mi spaces, the text before and after is kept, and an element in a later paragraph gives one space. Without the budget it fails (5,000,002 against 4,199,306).
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-formats --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p wordcraft-formats` (247 passed), `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p wordcraft-engine` (covers wordcraft-formats).
- App (a dev build with my other audit fixes merged, driven over the control channel with a throwaway profile): the audit's case, an 11.9 KB `.odt` with 200,000 `text:c="1000"` elements, opens in 0.15 s as a paragraph of 4,394,312 characters. The app went from 226 MB to 723 MB, saved the document as `.json` and stayed responsive.

title: Markdown import: table cells past the document's limits are not built (#3701)
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
Fixes #3701.

The Markdown importer padded every body row of a table to the header's width, with a parsed paragraph in each cell, before the document builder's row and column caps applied. The audit measured 2.28 GB from a 33.6 KB file with a wide header.

The parser now stops where the document stops anyway: 63 cells per row (`MAX_COLS`), header included, and 32,767 rows (`MAX_ROWS`). Rows past the last one are still read as part of the table, so whatever follows it parses as before. Short rows are still padded with empty cells up to the 63, as GitHub-flavored Markdown says.

### Tests

- `table_cells_past_the_document_limits_are_not_built`: a 50,000-column header with three rows gives 63 cells per row and keeps a short row's text; a one-column table of 32,777 rows keeps 32,767, and the paragraph after it is still a paragraph. It fails without the caps.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-formats --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p wordcraft-formats` (247 passed), `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p wordcraft-engine` (covers wordcraft-formats).
- App (a dev build with my other audit fixes merged, driven over the control channel with a throwaway profile): the issue's suggested input (220 KB: a 50,000-column header and 10,000 rows of `|`) opens in about 1 s as a 63-column table of 10,001 rows, 228 pages. Before, the parser alone would have built 500 million cells.

One thing this doesn't solve: laying out the 630,000 cells that are left still takes the app from 226 MB to 6.3 GB. A table that size costs the same from any format, since no reader has a total cell budget for document tables (charts and spreadsheets have one), so I'd treat that as its own issue rather than lower the document's limits here.

title: RTF: a semicolon in a font name stays in the name (#3740)
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
Fixes #3740.

In `\fonttbl` a `;` ends the font name, and the writer put names through `esc` unchanged. A run in "Semi;Colon" came back in "Semi", and two names sharing a prefix up to the semicolon became one.

- **Writer:** font names go through a new `esc_font`. A `;` is written as `\'3b`, and control characters, which `esc` would turn into `\line` or `\tab` inside the table, are dropped.
- **Reader:** an escaped semicolon (`\'3b`, or `\u59` with its fallback) belongs to the name; only a literal one ends the entry. This holds in multibyte code pages too, where `\'3b` goes through the decoder instead of `ch`.
- **Reader, text after `\uN`:** while fallback bytes were pending, the reader sent the whole rest of that text run through its byte path one byte at a time, so a literal `;` there looked escaped. Only the fallback bytes are skipped that way now, and the rest of the run is read as ordinary text, as it already was without a pending fallback. Body text comes out the same either way.
- `commit_font` no longer strips trailing semicolons: a literal one never reaches the name, and an escaped one is part of it.

### Tests

title: HTML export: font names are written as CSS strings (#3739)
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
Fixes #3739.

A run's font name went into `font-family:'...'` with only single quotes removed. `esc` escapes for HTML, not CSS, so a name holding a newline, a semicolon or a backslash could end the declaration and add CSS of its own inside the `style` attribute. As the issue says, the attribute itself couldn't be closed.

- **Writer:** `css_font_name` writes the name as a quoted CSS string. Quotes, backslashes and control characters become hex escapes (CSS Syntax 3, section 4.3.7), and so do `;` and `,`, because a reader that splits declarations or the family list on them would cut the name there. WordCraft's own reader does. Ordinary names come out as before: `font-family:'Times New Roman'`.
- **Reader:** `css_unescape` decodes CSS escapes in the first family, so names round-trip, apostrophes included. The old writer dropped those.

The issue also suggests an allow-list of characters. I chose escaping because real font names use characters an allow-list would strip, such as the `+` in "M+ 1p".

### Tests

- `font_names_are_written_as_css_strings`: names with a newline and `;position:fixed`, with a backslash, with quotes and with a comma, plus "Times New Roman" and "M+ 1p". Every `style` attribute with a `font-family` holds one declaration and two quotes, and every name reads back unchanged. Reverting either side fails it.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-formats --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p wordcraft-formats` (247 passed), `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p wordcraft-engine` (covers wordcraft-formats).
- App (a dev build with my other audit fixes merged, driven over the control channel with a throwaway profile): a run set to `O'Brien "Sans";position:fixed` and saved as HTML gets `style="font-family:'O\27 Brien \22 Sans\22 \3b position:fixed'"`, and reopening the file gives the name back unchanged.

title: Field codes: Rules and Mark Entry keep quotes in the text they write (#3681, #3669)
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
Fixes #3681. Fixes #3669.

Both issues come from field codes built out of typed text without quoting it, so they share one small helper.

**Mail Merge Rules (#3681).** `mailings.rules` put the value and the IF texts between quotes as typed. A quote inside one ended it early: a then text of `Dear "friend"` printed `Dear`, and the comparison used the wrong text. They are now written as field-code text with `\"` and `\\` (ECMA-376 Part 1, 17.16.1), and a merge field name with a space, a quote or a backslash is quoted the same way. The merge evaluator found the texts by splitting at every quote. It now reads them with the same word splitting as `FieldCode::parse`, so the escapes come back, and it still takes only the quoted texts.

**Mark Entry (#3669).** The bookmark was looked up as given but written trimmed, so `{"bookmark": " Intro"}` was refused although `Intro` exists. It is trimmed first now. A bookmark name read from a file can hold a space, a quote or a backslash, and it went into the XE field as it was, where it could split or add switches (`\b`, `\t "..."`). Such a name is quoted now; an ordinary one is written bare, as before.

**Shared code.** The word splitting in `FieldCode::parse` moves into `field_words` (`references.rs`), which the merge evaluator uses too. `quoted` and `field_arg` write text that `field_words` reads back. The mailings module's own `quote`, which only quoted names with spaces, is gone.

title: Tests: hostile_params_never_panic fails on a caught panic (#3718)
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
Fixes #3718.

`Session::run` turns a panic inside a command into `CmdError::Failed("... panicked: ...")`, and `hostile_params_never_panic` threw the result away, so the test only failed when a panic escaped the guard.

I matched on the message instead of adding a `CmdError::Panicked` variant, the issue's other option, because `CmdError` is public and matched in other crates. No command panics on the current junk, so nothing else had to change.

Separately, I ran a wider fuzz locally (not part of this PR): every command with each of its own documented params set to subnormal, huge and odd values, from 14 starting states (pictures, tables, shapes, text boxes, charts, equations, headers, tracked changes, comments and others). The one panic it found was `picture.corrections` with a subnormal `sharpen` (#3646), which #3830 fixes. This test doesn't reach that one either way, since its junk has no `sharpen`.

title: Insert Picture: a huge width can't make the size infinite (#3619)
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
Fixes #3619.

`place_picture` scaled both sides by the requested width before fitting the picture to the column. On a picture taller than it is wide, `insert.picture` with `width: 3e38` overflowed the height to `+inf`. A `.json` save wrote it as `null` and could not read it back, and AutoRecover then refused every snapshot of the document.

The requested width is now clamped to 22 inches (1584 pt) before scaling, as Insert Icons already clamps its size. Text is never wider than that, because page widths are capped at 22 inches, so a picture still comes out at the column's width and nothing else changes.

This covers the case the issue reproduces. Its wider suggestions (one length helper for every command, f64 arithmetic, sanitizing floats on `.json` open) would be separate changes.

### Tests

- `a_huge_picture_width_keeps_the_size_finite`: a 2 x 400 px PNG inserted with width 3e38 keeps a finite size and its 1:200 shape, and the document's `.json` save reopens. Without the clamp it fails.

- App (a dev build with my other audit fixes merged, driven over the control channel with a throwaway profile): `insert.picture` with `width: 3e38` on that PNG gives a 468 x 93,600 pt picture, and the `.json` save reopens.

title: References: TOC, index and list page numbers follow the section's number format
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #3856

A table of contents, a table of figures, a table of authorities, an index and an inserted page cross-reference now write each page number the way the page shows it: `ii` in front matter numbered i, ii, iii; `V` in a section numbered in upper-case roman from IV; `c` in one numbered a, b, c. Sections numbered in decimal don't change.

All five read the page number from the layout and printed it as a decimal. Now there's one small helper, `cmd::PageNumbers`. It looks up the layout once and returns the number together with its section's `NumFormat`. TOC, index, table of figures, table of authorities and Insert Cross-reference all use it, and so does Update Field for `PAGEREF`, which already got it right with its own copy of the same lookup. An inserted page cross-reference now matches what F9 writes afterwards.

An index page range (`\r`) now compares where the two pages are in the document, not their numbers, because numbering can restart inside the range: a range from page ii of the front matter to page 1 of the next section is `ii–1`, not just `ii`.

On Word's behaviour: for PAGEREF, Word's field reference says the `\*` switch "overrides the numeral style selected in the Number format box in the Page Number Format dialog box" (https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/word/field-codes-pageref-field), so without it the section's format applies. For the TOC, this accepted answer says the same: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/a/10480471. I think INDEX and TOA follow the same rule, but I found no source for them and haven't checked them in Word.

Tests:

- `toc_page_numbers_follow_the_section_number_format`: a lower-roman front section with a decimal main section restarting at 1 (`Preface ii`, `Alpha 1`, `Bravo 2`), and upper-roman from IV with lower-letter from c (`Preface V`, `Alpha c`, `Bravo d`). Both cases are saved as DOCX, reopened and updated again, with the same result.

title: Audit fixes for 13 issues: import limits, escaping, link schemes, table depth
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
This puts the fixes from #3838 to #3848 into one PR, so the batch can be reviewed and merged together. Each fix is its own commit. The CodeRabbit follow-ups from those PRs come right after the fix they belong to, and their messages name the PR the review was on, so every change still reads and reverts on its own. Based on main at 9130181a.

Fixes #3700, fixes #3701, fixes #3740, fixes #3739, fixes #3681, fixes #3669, fixes #3718, fixes #3743, fixes #3744, fixes #3675, fixes #3717, fixes #3619. Part of #3618.

## Fixes

**ODT import: `text:s` spaces have a budget for the whole document (#3700).** Each `<text:s text:c="n"/>` added up to 1,000 spaces, and nothing limited how many a file held: the audit's 11.6 KB file became 200 million spaces and a 1.2 GB peak. The extra spaces now come out of one budget of 4 Mi (4,194,304) per document, the figure the issue suggests, shared by headers, footers and the body. Past the budget each element is one space, so words stay apart.

**Markdown import: table cells past the document's limits are not built (#3701).** The importer padded every row to the header's width before the document's caps applied (2.28 GB from a 33.6 KB file). It now stops at 63 cells per row (`MAX_COLS`) and 32,767 rows (`MAX_ROWS`), and rows past the last one are still read as part of the table. Wide lines turn only the first 63 cells into strings; the header and the delimiter row are still checked at full width.

**RTF: a semicolon in a font name stays in the name (#3740).** In `\fonttbl` a `;` ends the name, so "Semi;Colon" came back as "Semi". The writer escapes it as `\'3b` and drops control characters, and the reader keeps an escaped semicolon in the name. Text after a `\uN` fallback used to go through the reader's byte path, where a literal `;` looked escaped; only the fallback bytes are skipped that way now.

title: Security: bound layout memory (linked text boxes, repeated headers, crops, gridAfter)
author: benandez
body:
## Summary

Part of #3692.

Fixes for the findings from the automated security audit (tracker #3692), against `00bc6a4b`. Each row is its own commit with a regression test.

| # | CWE | Problem → fix | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | 400 | A linked text-box chain re-laid the head box's whole story for every box. The story is now laid out once per distinct width, up to 16 widths. | aa8971b9 |
| 11 | 400 | Repeated header rows cloned every item onto every page. This is capped at 500,000 copied items. | 800f15ee |
| 35 | 789 | `gridAfter` from the model was trusted. It is now clamped to `MAX_COLS` (63), as the DOCX reader does. | fb04cf48 |
| 38 | 400 | A picture with many crops was decoded once per crop. It is now decoded once, within a per-layout budget of 2^28 pixels. | a17c2af0 |

Ultrareview findings 6 and 7 apply here (see §4).

**Limits introduced:** `MAX_FLOW_WIDTHS` 16, `MAX_HEADER_ITEMS` 500,000, `MAX_DECODED_PIXELS` 2^28 per layout, `gridAfter` ≤ `MAX_COLS` (63).

**Fixed after review (CodeRabbit CLI + a multi-agent review of all 12 security PRs merged together):**

Past 16 widths, a box reuses the nearest existing layout (same direction, the widest that fits, else the narrowest), so the story is still laid out at most 16 times.

author: benandez
body:
## Summary

| 12 | 400 | A note's fields were re-expanded per field. Each note is now listed once, within a field and code-byte budget. | c88a26f5 |

Only a listener confirmed as another uid's is refused; an unlisted listener falls back to the loopback rule. If our own socket's row is missing, our uid comes from the owner of `/proc/self`.

## What changed

- **Status bar:** a one-word document reads “1 word”; the note names the footnote or endnote actually open; items with no action behind them (the editing note, Track Changes) are labels with a hover cursor instead of buttons; Read Mode’s zoom percentage no longer pretends to open a dialog.

When rerouting a partially attached group connector, unresolved/free endpoints are derived from its unrotated frame. The reroute then clears rotation, moving the free endpoint even though the user only moved an attached target.

## Coverage

Synthetic model regressions cover straight, elbow and curved connectors, either free endpoint, rotations/flips, unresolved targets, invalid sites, fully unresolved and fully attached cases, and idempotence. External public-API smoke exercises an attached start with a 90-degree rotated free end.

title: doc: decode numeric XML references in legacy form labels
author: mrzv
body:
## Problem

`LegacyForm::parse` resolves the five named XML entities but leaves decimal and hexadecimal character references literal. The DOCX XML serializer itself emits numeric tab, newline and carriage-return references, so selected drop-down labels can display XML notation rather than their text; field names are affected too.

## Change

Decode valid XML 1.0 numeric references along with named entities in one pass. Do not recursively decode escaped reference text; malformed/invalid references remain literal. Raw field XML remains the save source, so roundtrip preservation is unchanged.

## Coverage

A public model regression covers numeric field names, decimal whitespace, supplementary Unicode, all named entities, escaped reference literals, invalid XML scalars, malformed digits and missing terminators. An external public-API consumer checks the resulting selected label. The new regression fails on current main before the fix.

Related open PR #3778 adds legacy-form editing/state APIs; this narrowly fixes the existing decoder and does not duplicate that work.

title: doc: apply Turkic casing to collation and index headings
author: mrzv
body:
## Problem

Default Unicode lowercasing maps capital `I` to dotted `i` before Turkish/Azerbaijani collation tailoring. This groups `I` with the wrong letter instead of dotless `ı`, and dotted lowercase index entries receive `I` rather than `İ` headings.

## Change

Apply Turkic dotted/dotless casing without losing whole-string contextual lowercasing or existing supported composed/decomposed equivalences. Preserve current default-locale and Russian behavior. Public signatures and tailoring tables remain unchanged.

## Coverage

API regressions exercise Turkish/Azerbaijani language-tag forms, dotted/dotless case pairs, decomposed dotted I, ordering, headings, combining marks, contextual Greek final sigma, supported accented-I equivalences, default locales and Russian tailoring. An external consumer exercises actual sort keys, comparisons and index headings.

Open PR #3237 adds Vietnamese/canonical collation handling and mechanically overlaps this file, but its default lowercasing does not fix Turkic I. This is a narrow independent correction, not a replacement for that PR.

title: doc: preserve manual equation breaks during run normalization
author: mrzv
body:
## Problem

`math_edit::tidy` coalesces identically formatted runs even when the incoming run carries a manual equation break (`brk`) and alignment position. Editing/cleanup can silently remove that break and later saving loses it.

## Change

Keep incoming manual-break runs separate, while allowing ordinary continuation text to coalesce. Run splitting must keep the break only on the original left-hand run, rather than duplicating it on a right-hand suffix.

## Coverage

Synthetic model regressions cover manual breaks at alignment positions 0 and 2, ordinary following text merging into a continuation, and typing/build-up inside an existing continuation without adding a second break. The direct tidy regression fails on current main before the fix. External public-API smoke checks preservation of the break/alignment and normal continuation merging.

title: Mini toolbar: the alignment buttons mark the alignment seen on the page, as the ribbon does
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #3579.

The mini toolbar lit its alignment buttons from the paragraph's logical alignment, where `Left` is the start edge, so a start-aligned right-to-left paragraph, which sits on the right, lit Align Left. The ribbon already marks the alignment as seen on the page (`r.align.visual(r.bidi)` in the Paragraph group), and the `para.align*` commands behind both bars already set it that way, so this makes the bar read the same value the ribbon does. The text context menu shows the same bar, so it's fixed there too. Alignment is the only control on the bar with a direction, so nothing else needed the change.

This also matches Word, where a right-to-left paragraph that starts at the right edge reports right-aligned: [Selection.RtlPara](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/vba/api/word.selection.rtlpara) says that turning a left-aligned left-to-right paragraph right-to-left "sets its paragraph alignment to right-aligned".

title: Save, export and print keep the view where it is
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #3864.

`after_command` sets `scroll_to_caret` after every command that isn't `ui.`, `view.`, `document.`, `format.state` or `draw.`, so Save (Ctrl+S or the button) pulled the view back to the caret, pages away from where the reader was. Save As, Export PDF/PNG, Print, Print to PDF, Save as Template, Properties, Rename, Encrypt with Password and the other File › Info/Options commands that touch neither the caret nor the text did the same. This leaves the view alone for those, as Word does; commands that replace or edit the document (New, Open, New from Template, Recover, Inspect Document) still show the caret. `file.versions` also still follows the caret, saving a version included, because the same id restores one. AutoSave was already fine: it runs `file.save` on the session and never reaches `after_command`.

I listed the commands explicitly rather than excluding the whole `file.` prefix, so a document-replacing command added later still follows the caret; happy to switch to the prefix with a short exclusion list if you prefer.

title: Font: a selected text box's Font commands format all its text
author: pakiat
body:
## What's wrong

With a text box selected as an object (its frame, not the text in it), choosing a font, size, Bold and so on did nothing to the box's text: `format::apply` formatted only the selection's range, which for a selected object is the box's anchor character (U+FFFC) in the paragraph around it.

There was no other easy way either:

- **Select All** doesn't reach a floating text box's text. This matches Word, where Ctrl+A also leaves floating text boxes alone.
- A text box **behind text** can't be clicked into where body text covers it (`hit.rs` `story_at` / `object_at_in`), and Word does the same: the click goes to the text over the box.

So in a real document (a Thai government memo whose "วันที่" heading is a behind-text text box over a dotted-leader line), Select All → TH Sarabun New changed everything except that box, and there was no way to change it short of moving things around.

## What Word does

Observed black-box on a synthetic document: when a text box is selected as a shape and a font is chosen, all of the box's text takes the font, and the body text is left as it was.

## The change

- `crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs`: `selected_text_box` returns the whole story of a text box that is selected as an object. `apply` uses it ahead of `target`, and so does `resolved`, so toggles like Bold read the box's current formatting and a second press turns Bold off. This is the same thing `wordart.rs`'s `box_story` / `apply` already do for the WordArt text commands.
- `format.changeCase`, `format.clear` and `format.resetChar` (which don't go through `apply`) take the same range. In Word, with a text box selected, they work on the box's text and leave the body alone. Before, Clear could reset the paragraph around the box while the box kept its formatting.
- With an empty box selected, `resolved` reads the box's paragraph mark (what `apply` formats), not the anchor's run in the body. So Bold on an empty box sitting in bold body text turns Bold on.

title: Ruler: dragging a margin edge leaves the view where it is
author: pakiat
body:
## What's wrong

Dragging the bottom margin's edge on the vertical ruler could move it much further than the pointer went. In a real A4 memo, dragging about 1 cm up set a 2.00 cm bottom margin to 8.10 cm. While dragging, the view jumped up the page.

Cause: `margin_handle` (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`) runs `layout.margins` on every frame of the drag. `after_command` then sets `scroll_to_caret`, as it does for most commands. When the caret is off screen, which is the usual case when you drag the bottom margin while the text you're editing is higher up, the view scrolls to it mid-drag. The margin is computed from the pointer's distance to the top of the page (`y0`), so when the page slides under a pointer that hasn't moved, that distance changes, and the next frame's margin overshoots, and so on.

## The change

`margin_handle` runs the command with `run_keep_view`, as the table border drags already do (#1738). This covers all four margin edges on both rulers, since they share the handle. Typing and other commands still bring the caret into view as before.

## Tests

- New test `canvas::tests::dragging_the_bottom_margin_on_the_ruler_keeps_the_view_and_follows_the_pointer` does a real mouse drag in the kittest harness. It scrolls page 1's bottom margin into the middle of the window with the caret off screen, then drags the vertical ruler's bottom edge 36 pt up in five moves. It checks:
  - the scroll offset doesn't change during or after the drag;
  - the margin grows by 36 pt (within the 1/16 inch snap);
  - the drag is one undo step.
- On `main` it fails at the second move: the offset goes from 418 to 104.5. With the change it passes.

title: Layout: inline equations wrap within available width; framed paragraphs in a cell stack vertically (#3461, #2357)
author: albayazid
body:
## What this fixes

**#3461** — Inline equations overflow the column width instead of wrapping.

**#2357** — Framed paragraphs in a table cell that share the same frame overlap each other instead of stacking vertically.

## Root causes

1. **Inline equation overflow**: In `crates/layout/src/math.rs`, the `layout_equation` function used `cx.arg()` for inline equations, which lays out the entire equation on a single line without considering the available column width. Display equations correctly used `cx.wrapped()` which wraps at the available width.

2. **Frame stacking in table cells**: In `crates/layout/src/lib.rs`, the `layout_box` function placed each framed paragraph independently at the frame's absolute offset. When multiple consecutive paragraphs shared the same `w:framePr` (as in a letterhead's signature block), they all drew at the same position, overlapping each other. Word stacks such paragraphs vertically inside the frame.

## Fixes

### 1. Inline equation wrapping (`crates/layout/src/math.rs`)
- Added `inline_wrapped` function that reuses the display equation's wrapping logic (`cx.wrapped`)
- Inline equations now call `cx.inline_wrapped` which wraps at the available column width
- Updated test `long_display_equations_wrap_before_operators_and_indent` to verify inline equations now wrap (previously they were expected not to wrap)

### 2. Frame stacking in cells (`crates/layout/src/lib.rs`)
- Added `frame_run` state tracking in `layout_box`
- When consecutive paragraphs share the same frame key (position, size, anchors), they are stacked vertically: the first goes at the frame's position, subsequent ones follow below the previous one
- The frame's offset is applied only to the first paragraph; subsequent ones stack below it

### 3. Test coverage
- New test `paragraphs_sharing_a_text_frame_in_a_cell_stack_inside_it` verifies frame stacking in a table cell (RED/GREEN verified)
- Existing test `paragraphs_sharing_a_text_frame_stack_inside_it` still passes for…

title: CI: shared gate workflow; FreeBSD nightly and on release
author: aiongg
body:
Switches WordCraft's CI to the suite's shared gate workflow and takes the slow platform builds off the pull-request path. **Depends on storytold/craft-common-actions#69**; merge after it. Until then this PR's CI fails, because `gate.yml` doesn't exist yet.

- `ci.yml` calls `storytold/craft-common-actions/.github/workflows/gate.yml@main`. That workflow brings the cached apt install, nextest, rust-cache saved only from main (keyed on the root `Cargo.toml`, so profile changes start a fresh cache), and a check that `Cargo.lock` is unchanged. Every push to main now runs to the end, and pushes to a PR branch cancel their older run. The apt package list and the craft-fonts pin (the same commit as `release.yml` and `freebsd.yml`) are the old file's.

title: #3734: ui.resize refuses sizes that aren't positive and clamps to the GPU's limit
author: mercuryVM
body:
## Problem

The control channel's `ui.resize` turned `width`/`height` into `f32` and sent them to the viewport with no check. Zero and negative sizes went through, and so did huge ones (`1e300` becomes `inf` after the cast). A window larger than the largest texture the GPU can draw gives wgpu a surface configuration over its limit, and that validation error is a panic outside `Session::run`'s guard.

## Fix

- `window_geometry::requested_size` refuses sizes that aren't positive and finite (NaN, and `1e300`, which is infinite once read as `f32`) and clamps the rest to the app's minimum (`MIN_SIZE`, the same 760 × 480 the desktop window sets as its minimum inner size) and to the largest texture side in points, capped at 16384 like restored window sizes are. The GPU's limit wins over the minimum, and a limit that isn't positive refuses the resize.
- `ui.resize` replies with an error for a refused size, and otherwise with the `width` and `height` it asked for, so callers can see the clamp.
- `docs/control-protocol.md` gives `ui.resize` its own row with its parameters and behaviour.

Fixes #3734

## Tests

- `tests::control_resize_rejects_bad_sizes_and_clamps_huge_ones` (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`) runs `control::handle` inside a frame and reads the `InnerSize` commands it sends: `-5`, `0 × 0`, a negative height and `1e300` are refused and send nothing; `1e9 × 600` sends the GPU's limit × 600; `10 × 10` sends the minimum; `1200 × 800` is sent unchanged. It fails on `main` (the `-5` width is accepted with `{"ok": true}`).
- `window_geometry::tests::requested_sizes_are_positive_and_fit_the_gpu` covers the helper, including NaN and infinite input and GPU limits below the minimum.

Gates: `cargo xtask ci` passes locally (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm) on Windows.

title: Khmer: ignore w14:ligatures when shaping Khmer text
author: inmean
body:
## Problem
Khmer documents saved by Word carry `w14:ligatures="historicalDiscretional"` on every run. WordCraft mapped that to `liga` off and `clig` off. Khmer OS fonts build their syllables in those features, so pre-base vowels and stacked signs were drawn in the wrong order (`ស៊ើបអង្កេត` came out as `សីបអង្កតេ`, `ផ្តន្ទាទោស` lost its `ោ`). Word renders the same file correctly.

Checked on a 6-page sample: removing `w14:ligatures` fixes it. `liga` only on fixes it; `clig` only on does not, so `liga` is the feature that matters.

## Fix
Runs containing Khmer characters are shaped with the font's default features; the ligature setting still applies to all other text.

## Tests
`tests_complex::khmer_ignores_the_ligature_setting` shapes Khmer OS Siemreap text with `historicalDiscretional` and `none` and expects the same glyphs as with no setting. It fails without the change. `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout`, `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` pass. I did not run the full `cargo xtask ci`.

Not covered: Myanmar and Indic scripts may have the same problem.

title: #3639: Header and footer commands change the section of the header the caret is in
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
Fixes #3639.

## Cause

While the caret is in a header or footer, `s.sel.focus.story` is `StoryRef::Part(id)` and `s.sel.focus.path.0[0]` counts that header's paragraphs. These commands still passed it to `Document::section_mut` as a body block index:

- `layout.linkToPrevious` and `hf.position` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs`)
- `hf_part`, used by `insert.header` / `insert.footer` and the page-number paths, and the no-page fallback of `edit_hf` (`insert.editHeader` / `insert.editFooter`) (`crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs`)
- `design.pageBorders` with `applyTo: "section"` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/design.rs`). This one isn't in the issue, but it has the same pattern.

Header block 0 is body block 0, which is in section 1. So with the caret in section 2's header, Link to Previous cleared section 1's headers, and so on.

## Fix

- `page::section_end_of_focus` maps `section_index_of_focus` to the section's last body block, which is what `section_mut` takes. `section_index_of_focus` already resolves a header, footer or note to its owning section; it was added for Page Setup in #2072.
- The commands above now use it. `edit_hf` picks the section by `section_index_of_focus` directly.

The other `focus.path.0.first()` call sites in `crates/engine/src/cmd` are body-only, or already go through `section_index_of_focus` outside the body.

## Tests

- `header_and_footer_commands_change_the_section_of_the_header_the_caret_is_in` (`crates/engine/src/tests.rs`) builds two sections with their own headers, "H1" and "H2". With the caret in H2, it runs `hf.position`, `design.pageBorders`, `insert.footer`, `insert.editFooter` and `layout.linkToPrevious`. Each change lands on section 2, and section 1 is unchanged.

title: #3637: A table cell span from a .json file no longer overflows
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
Fixes #3637.

## Cause

`CellProps::span` is a plain `u32`. The `.docx` reader clamps `gridSpan` to 1..=63, but a `.json` document (or a recovery snapshot) can hold any value. `Cell::span()` clamps it for reading, yet three edit primitives in `crates/doc/src/table.rs` did arithmetic on the raw field:

- `insert_col`: `c.props.span += 1` on a cell the new column goes through
- `merge_right`: `first.props.span += c.props.span.max(1)`
- `delete_col`: `c.props.span -= 1`. It can't underflow (it is guarded by `span() > 1`), but it leaves a huge raw span huge.

With a span at or near `u32::MAX`, Insert Column or Merge Cells panicked with "attempt to add with overflow" in debug builds. In release the value wrapped to a small number, and the cell silently lost its span.

## Fix

All three compute from the clamped `span()` and cap the result at `MAX_COLS` (63), the most columns a table has:

```rust
c.props.span = (c.span() + 1).min(MAX_COLS) as u32;
first.props.span = (first.span() + c.span()).min(MAX_COLS) as u32;
c.props.span = (c.span() - 1) as u32;
```

In a consistent table, the spans of a row add up to at most 63, so the cap only changes rows that were already out of step with the grid. A raw span of 0 now counts as 1 in a merge, as `span()` reads it.

The issue also suggests a sanitising pass on `.json` load. I left that out to keep this change to the overflow. Reading already clamps, and every edit path now writes back a value in range.

## Tests

- `a_huge_span_from_a_file_does_not_overflow` (`crates/doc/src/table.rs`): a 1×2 table whose first cell has `span = u32::MAX`.
  - `insert_col(1)`, through the spanning cell, gives span 63.
  - `merge_right` with one huge cell, and with two, gives 63.
  - `delete_col(0)` gives 62.
- With the fix reverted, the test panics with `attempt to add with overflow` at `table.rs:197`.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes locally on macOS: fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm.

## Docs

title: #3663: "NaN" in the Font dialog's Size box no longer closes the app
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
Fixes #3663.

## Cause

The Font dialog's preview size was `size.trim().parse::<f32>().unwrap_or(12.0).clamp(6.0, 72.0)` (`crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`). `f32::from_str` accepts `"NaN"`, so `unwrap_or` doesn't replace it, and `clamp` returns NaN for NaN. The NaN size reached `FontId::new`, and epaint 0.36.2's glyph cache asserts on it.

I confirmed it with the new test on the old code. Typing `NaN` in the Size box and drawing one frame panics:

```
panicked at epaint-0.36.2/src/text/font.rs:181:9:
Bad px_scale_factor: NaN
```

That panic is in UI painting, which `Session::run`'s guard doesn't cover, so it ends the app (in builds with debug assertions).

## Fix

A small `preview_size(&str) -> f32` drops non-finite values before the clamp, so `NaN`, `inf` and `-infinity` preview at 12 pt, like any other text that isn't a size. Both the regular and the bold preview fonts use it.

As the issue asked, I checked the UI's other `parse::<f32/f64>()` boxes:

- The table style, chart and caret-glide boxes already check `is_finite`.
- The ribbon and mini-toolbar size boxes, and the dialog's OK, send the number to `format.size` / `format.set`. A NaN becomes JSON `null` there and is ignored.

## Tests

- `font_dialog_preview_ignores_a_size_that_is_not_a_number`:
  - Unit checks of `preview_size`: "NaN", "nan", "inf", "-infinity" and "" give 12; "10.5" gives 10.5; "200" gives 72.
  - A kittest harness then opens the Font dialog with "NaN" in the Size box and runs four frames. The dialog stays open.
- With the old line restored, the harness part fails with the panic above.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes locally on macOS: fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm.

## Docs

`ROADMAP.md` (progress log, status line, revision history) and `docs/ui-parity.md` (status line, revision history).

title: #3934: keep with next stops at a next-page section break
author: dpkruse
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @dpkruse (Kruse Legal)._

Fixes #3934.

Keep with next now stops at a next-page section break. The paragraph that closes a section before a new page keeps with nothing: Word leaves it at the bottom of its page, and a kept heading before it stays too. WordCraft moved it to a page of its own, and the next section then started one more: a blank page. This is the blank page 2 of the court's *Financial Questionnaire* and the blank page 9 of its *Application for Consent Orders* kit (with #3604), whose section-closing paragraphs are empty and in a heading style that keeps with next.

- `next_first_line` needs no room for an empty paragraph closing a section before a new page: it stays on a full page anyway (#1614's `closing_mark`), so a kept heading before it doesn't move for it.
- In `place_para_in_flow` the flag is cleared before the keep check, on a copy of the shared layout made only in that case. Done this way so this PR doesn't touch the keep condition #3604 changes; the two merge in either order.
- The continuous case is left as it was: there a continuous section starting on a full page has its own problem (its first line can be drawn below the bottom margin), which I'll report separately.

title: #3907: continuous sections running off a page go onto the next; empty section marks in a row stack to the page bottom
author: benandez
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3907.

Two layout bugs with continuous section breaks.

**1. Continuous sections never started a new page.** Each continuous section moves the column top down to just below the text above it. `at_top()` then returned true at the start of every new section, so a paragraph that didn't fit was placed anyway, as if it were on an empty page. A run of one-line sections ran off the bottom of page 1.

```diff
 fn place_para_in_flow
-  if over && l1 == l0 && !pb.at_top() …   // true at every mid-page section start
+  if over && l1 == l0 && !pb.fresh() …    // at the top with nothing above on this page
```

`fresh()` is used only for the decisions about whether a paragraph fits: line fit, widows and orphans, overflow, and keep lines together. `at_top()` still drives the spacing rules, which are unchanged. Keep lines together now measures against the next column, or against the next page's body when it is in the last column.

**2. Empty section-break paragraphs in a row took no room.** Only the first empty mark right after text stays quiet; that case was measured before and is unchanged. Each later mark in a run takes its line while it fits. Once the page is full, the rest stay at its bottom, so the text after the run starts the next page.

```text
place_para(mark)
  first mark after text  → quiet (no room), as before
  mark after a mark      → its line while it fits, else it stays at the page bottom
```

## Evidence

Measured in Word on synthetic files I made: "Start", then N empty paragraphs each ending a continuous section, then "End". No Word-produced files are used or committed.

| N | Word | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | about 9 cm down page 1 | right under Start | 8.5 cm down page 1 |
| 50 / 100 / 200 | first line of page 2 | page 1 | first line of page 2 |
| 100, 24 pt marks | first line of page 2 | page 1 | first line of page 2 |
| 100, no spacing | first line of page 2 | page 1 | first line of page 2 |

title: Keep inline content and formatting in Convert Text to Table
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3751

## Cause
`table.fromText` read each selected paragraph with `plain_text()` and rebuilt every cell as `Paragraph::with_text(..., Default::default())`. Before removing the source paragraphs, this dropped pictures, footnote references and other objects, turned fields into static text, removed character and paragraph formatting and links, and made tracked-deleted text live again.

## Fix
A new helper, `text_table_paras`, splits each source paragraph at the separator positions in its stored text and cuts each field out with `Paragraph::split_off`, trimming surrounding white space. The cells now hold the original runs, objects, tracked-change marks and paragraph properties, but not the section break. Row and column counting, and the 63-column and row limits, are the same as before.

## Not changed
`text_table_lines` and `text_table_cells` stay plain-text based, because the Convert Text to Table dialog uses them to count rows and columns. Quick Tables and the other `with_text` table builders are unchanged because they don't convert existing content.

title: RTF import: numeric parameters of 11+ digits leak their digits as text
author: MoriartyPuth
body:
## What

Importing an RTF file with a control-word parameter of 11+ digits left the digits past the tenth in the imported text. The parameter itself still took effect (it was parsed and clamped), but the remainder was brought in as literal body text — and survives open → edit → save.

Repro (one file):

```rtf
{\rtf1\ansi\li999999999999 x}
```

Open it in WordCraft (or `wordcraft-cli convert repro.rtf out.docx` and read the text back): the document contains `99 x` instead of `x`. The RTF spec's parameter is a run of digits ended by a delimiter, so a reader that stops mid-run mis-scans the file; WordCraft's scanners reject such splits. (I have not tested Word's exact behaviour on this input, so I am only claiming what the spec's grammar and this import show.) The same split reaches every control word that takes a number, including negative parameters, and it also shifts the counted-payload offset when `\bin` gets a zero-padded count of 11+ digits (the count digits and the payload came in as text).

## Root cause

`crates/formats/src/rtf.rs`, in the control-word scanner (diff base `3a4770e`):

```rust
let d0 = k;
while bytes.get(k).is_some_and(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()) && k - d0 < 10 {
    k += 1;
}
```

The 10-digit cap keeps the following `parse::<i64>()` infallible, but it sits on the *scan*, so with a longer run the cursor stops mid-run and `i = k` resumes the text loop at the eleventh digit. The value is already clamped to i32 a few lines below, so lifting the scan cap changes no valid behaviour. Zero-padded `\bin` counts hit the same split: the count parsed from the first 10 digits only, and the digits that were not part of the parameter — along with payload bytes — were imported as plain text.

## Fix

Consume the whole digit run; bound the *parse*, not the scan:

```rust
let v = std::str::from_utf8(bytes.get(d0..d0 + (k - d0).min(15)).unwrap_or(b"0"))
    .ok()
    .and_then(|s| s.parse::<i64>().ok())
    .unwrap_or(0);
```

The value is parsed from the first 15…

title: Parse the Flat OPC part root tag once when inheriting namespaces
author: Silvertree2010
body:

title: #3943: Layout's paragraph fields leave out-of-range values alone
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #3943

Just showing the Layout tab rewrote a paragraph whose indent or spacing lay outside the range of the Paragraph group's fields: a −1000 pt left indent became −792 pt, spacing above 1584 pt became 1584 pt, each time with an undo step. The fields clamped the value as they were drawn and reported that as an edit, which they then applied. Now they show the value as it is and change it only when it is typed or dragged.

## What changes

- Layout › Paragraph's Left, Right, Before and After fields are built with `clamp_existing_to_range(false)`, as the Picture Format, Shape Format and Chart Design size fields already are. A value typed or dragged is still kept within the range; only a value the document already has is left alone.
- Such values come from files (indents and spacing are read without an upper bound) and, for indents, also from `para.indents`, which takes −1584 pt to 1584 pt while the fields start at −792 pt.

## Engine

No change: the commands already accepted these values; only the ribbon rewrote them.

## Checked by hand

On Windows, in the app window with points as the unit: the first paragraph given a −1000 pt left indent, Layout shown: the Left field reads −1000 pt, and a single Undo takes the indent back to 0 pt with nothing left to undo, so showing the tab added no step.

## Not in this PR

- Table Layout › Cell Size has the same problem (a column wider than 22 mm shrinks with millimetres as the unit); #1995 already turns the clamp off there.
- Picture Format's crop fields: #2027 already turns the clamp off there.

title: Rename kept docx parts whose names are not valid OPC part names
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3691

## Cause
The docx writer wrote kept parts (embedded objects, custom XML, unmodelled parts) back under the name they had in the input zip whenever that name was free. Names containing a backslash, empty or dot segments, or percent-encoded separators were saved unchanged, so the output could contain entries like `word/..\..\x.bin`.

## Fix
`EmbedWriter::alloc` now normalises the original name before allocating it. It replaces backslashes and percent-encoded `/` and `\` with `_` and drops empty, `.` and `..` segments. A name that ends up empty falls back to the default embedded-part name. The normalised name then goes through the existing free-name and reserved-name logic. A regression test covers backslash, dot-segment and encoded-separator names.

## Verified
- Regression test `write::embed::tests::kept_part_names_are_valid_opc_names`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-docx kept_part_names_are_valid_opc_names`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Part-name reading in package.rs and `resolve` are unchanged. Only names on the write path are normalised. Dropped parts are renamed, not removed.

title: Fix .doc bookmark table desync on names longer than 40 characters
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3690

## Cause
`sttb_strings` cut each string's length to 40 and then moved forward by that shorter length, so the rest of a long name was read as the next entry. It also always assumed the extended UTF-16 form and never skipped the `cbExtra` bytes, and if any entry ran past the end of the buffer, the whole table was thrown away.

## Fix
The reader now moves forward by the stored `cch` plus `cbExtra` and cuts only the kept text to 40 characters. It checks `fExtend` (0xFFFF) and reads the non-extended form as 1-byte lengths with Windows-1252 text. A truncated entry now ends the list and keeps the names read before it, instead of throwing away the whole table.

## Verified
- Regression tests `notes::tests::long_bookmark_name_does_not_desync_table`, `notes::tests::sttb_extra_data_is_skipped`, `notes::tests::non_extended_sttb_reads_byte_strings`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-docbin --lib notes::tests`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The 40-character limit on kept bookmark names is unchanged. `parse_bookmarks` and the PLC parsing are not changed.

title: Bound MCP stdio request and bridge reply line reads
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3685

## Cause
The MCP stdio loop used `lines()` and the `--connect` bridge used `read_line` on the app's reply. Neither limits line length, so a peer sending a huge line with no newline could grow the buffer until allocation failed and the MCP process aborted.

## Fix
Added a bounded line reader that buffers at most `max + 1` bytes with `take` and `read_until`, and discards the rest of an over-long line. The stdio loop caps requests at 1 MiB and answers an over-long line with an error reply (code `INVALID_REQUEST`, message `request line too long`), then keeps serving. The bridge caps replies at 256 MiB, enough for screenshots and `document.inspect`, and returns an I/O error for a longer one.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::over_long_request_line_is_rejected_and_serving_continues`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-mcp over_long_request_line_is_rejected_and_serving_continues`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The app's control server, which already bounds its lines. No direct test of the bridge reply limit; only the stdio path has a new regression test.

title: Cap the number of VML path commands parsed from a path attribute
author: Silvertree2010

## Cause

## Not changed

title: Skip quoted attribute values when scanning settings.xml tags
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3682

## Cause
`children` in `settings_merge.rs` ended each tag at the next `>`, even when that `>` was inside a quoted attribute value, which XML allows. The tag was cut short, so the element depth never returned to 0 and `children` returned `None`. `has_unowned` then reported nothing to keep, and the merge fell back to the generated part, which dropped the unmodelled settings.

## Fix
Added a `tag_end` helper that skips `"..."` and `'...'` sections when looking for a tag's closing `>`. `children` uses it for both the root start tag and its child tags. A regression test covers `>` in double-quoted and single-quoted values, on self-closing and open/close elements.

## Not changed

title: DOCX: VML horizontal rules take their line
author: Morzilla
body:
A web page's `<hr>` pasted into Word becomes a VML horizontal rule: `<v:rect style="width:0;height:1.5pt" o:hr="t" o:hralign="center" o:hrstd="t"/>`. WordCraft took the `width:0` as written and drew a **1 pt dot** where Word draws a line across the page. Documents made from web content often use these rules as section separators.

## What Word does

Measured on Word (Microsoft 365) with a synthetic document. Here is where each rule is drawn, A4 page with 2 cm margins, so the text runs from 56.7 to 538.6 pt:

| Rule | Word | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `width:0`, no `o:hrpct` | 56.7–538.5 | 56.7–538.6 |
| `o:hrpct="500"` centred | 177.1–418.1 | 177.2–418.1 |
| `o:hrpct="500"` right | 297.6–538.5 | 297.6–538.6 |
| `o:hrpct="500"` left | 56.7–297.6 | 56.7–297.6 |
| `width:100pt`, `o:hrpct="0"`, centred | 247.6–347.5 | 247.6–347.6 |
| `fillcolor="#c00000" stroked="f"`, 4 pt | red, no outline | red, no outline |
| paragraph indented 72 pt | 128.6–538.5 | 128.7–538.6 |

So:

- With no width and no `o:hrpct`, a rule spans the line, inside the paragraph's indents.
- `o:hrpct` is a share of the line, in tenths of a percent.
- `o:hrpct="0"` keeps the shape's own width.
- `o:hralign` places a shorter rule.

## Changes

- **wordcraft-doc:** `ShapeExtra::hr: Option<HorizontalRule>` holds the share, the alignment and Word's standard look (`o:hrstd`).
- **wordcraft-docx:** reads `o:hr`, `o:hrpct`, `o:hralign` and `o:hrstd`.
  - A rule is written back as the same VML `v:rect`, since DrawingML has no rule. A fixed-size `wps:wsp` would lose the line-wide width.
  - Word opens a file re-saved by WordCraft with the same lines, checked by exporting it to PDF from Word.
- **wordcraft-layout:**
  - A rule's cluster takes the whole line, and `display::inline_rect` draws it at its share and alignment.
  - When a table column is measured (an unbounded line), a rule asks for no width, so it follows its column instead of widening the table.

**One deliberate difference:** Word draws a rule insid…

title: Bound control-channel replies and MCP bridge exchanges with deadlines
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3758

## Cause
The control server writes replies with a blocking `writeln!` and no write timeout, and removes its read deadline after authentication. A client that stops reading a large reply could hold its connection thread forever. On the bridge, `Remote::roundtrip` used only a 90 s per-read timeout, so a peer sending a byte every few seconds kept one tool call open indefinitely.

## Fix
The app now writes every reply, error replies included, through `write_reply`. It writes in chunks, and each chunk waits only for the time left of one overall 30 s deadline. The connection closes when that deadline passes, and an oversize-line drain is skipped if its error reply missed the deadline. The bridge now gives each exchange (request write plus whole reply) one overall deadline, using a `Timed` reader and a deadline-bounded write, so `Remote::call` returns an error instead of hanging.

## Verified
- Regression tests `control_server::tests::a_client_that_does_not_read_its_reply_is_dropped`, `backend::tests::a_drip_fed_reply_hits_the_exchange_deadline`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft --bin wordcraft control_server::tests::a_client_that_does_not_read_its_reply_is_dropped && cargo test -p wordcraft-mcp --lib backend::tests::a_drip_fed_reply_hits_the_exchange_deadline`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The MCP server's stdout writes to its client pipe still block as before. Turning a timed-out exchange into an explicit "outcome unknown" result is left to #3754.

title: Refuse arrange.group when members exceed the group child cap
author: Silvertree2010
body:

title: #3955: Format Shape's Angle field leaves an angle above 359.9° alone

body:

Just showing the Format Shape pane rewrote a shape whose linear gradient angle lay between 359.9° and 360°: an angle of 359.95° became 359.9°, with an undo step. title: Pick free drawing ids when a shape already uses u32::MAX
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3673

## Cause
`next_shape_id` returned `max.saturating_add(1)`, so a shape with id 4294967295 made it return that same id. The writer also started fresh `docPr` ids at `next_shape_id() - 1` and saturated at `u32::MAX`. Every new connector glue and every fresh drawing therefore reused an existing id.

## Fix
`Document::shape_ids()` now collects every shape id in the document. When the highest id is `u32::MAX`, `next_shape_id` returns the lowest unused id. The writer no longer derives its `docPr` ids from `next_shape_id()`. It takes them from the set of ids already in the document and skips any that are used.

## Verified
- Regression tests `tests::next_shape_id_avoids_a_shape_at_the_largest_id`, `fresh_docpr_ids_skip_used_ids_with_a_shape_at_the_largest_id`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-doc next_shape_id_avoids_a_shape_at_the_largest_id && cargo test -p wordcraft-docx --test drawing_ids`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Connector glue code in the engine (`ensure_id`) is unchanged, because it uses `next_shape_id` and gets the fix through it. Ids are not renumbered when a file is opened. I did not add an engine-level connector test. The docx test covers the saved `docPr` ids (a shape at `u32::MAX` plus shapes at 1 and 3 and two shapes with no id).

title: Ignore docx chart number-format codes longer than 255 bytes
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3729

## Cause
Chart number-format codes were read from category caches, value caches and the axis `c:numFmt` with no length limit. Every formatted label then re-tokenised the code, with one heap `String` per literal character. A crafted multi-MB code therefore cost huge amounts of memory and time per tick and label.

## Fix
Added `MAX_FORMAT_CODE` (255 bytes, the spreadsheet limit). The category cache, value cache and axis `c:numFmt` read sites now ignore longer codes, so those labels fall back to the plain value text. Regression tests cover each of the three sites, with a code just under the limit as a control that still applies.

- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The tokeniser still runs once per formatted value. I did not cache tokens per axis or series, and I did not merge literal runs into one token.

title: Proofing options reach the Czech, Croatian, Indonesian, Italian, Polish and Portuguese checks
author: FedeOlivares
body:
## The bug

File › Options › Proofing › "Ignore words in UPPERCASE" and "Ignore words that contain numbers" had no effect on short words in Czech, Croatian, Indonesian, Italian, Polish and Portuguese. `is_correct_in_with` dispatches these languages as `accepted_by_options(word, opts) || <lang>::is_correct(word)`, and each `is_correct_with` accepted, unconditionally, every word in capitals of up to six letters and every word with a digit. With either option off, a misspelling like `ŠKULA`, `LIBRRO` or `praya2` was still accepted.

The same issue was raised by CodeRabbit on the new Spanish module in #3562 and fixed there. These six modules share the pattern on `main`, so they get the same fix here.

## The fix

- Each of the six modules gains `is_correct_with_options(word, opts)` and a private `check(d, word, opts)` that applies the capitals and digits rules only when `opts.ignore_uppercase` / `opts.ignore_numbers` are on, as Spanish does. `is_correct` and `is_correct_with` keep Word's defaults (both on).
- `lib.rs::is_correct_in_with` routes the six languages through `is_correct_with_options`.
- Indonesian also accepted a capitalised part of up to six letters in a hyphenated word (`KTP-nya`); that rule follows Ignore words in UPPERCASE too, so with it off `RUMHA-nya` is flagged like `RUMHA`.

Not changed here: Turkish (`tr/mod.rs`) still accepts words with digits regardless of the option, and Russian (`ru/mod.rs`) short words in capitals.

## Testing

- New `proofing_options_reach_the_<language>_check` test per language, on its synthetic test dictionary: a short all-caps misspelling is accepted by default and flagged with Ignore words in UPPERCASE off, the correct all-caps spelling still passes, `<misspelling>2` is flagged with Ignore words that contain numbers off, and numbers alone stay correct. All six fail without the `lib.rs` change.
- `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p wordcraft-proof` (241 passed).
