title: Load ui.json with many unknown keys in linear time
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3659

## Cause
`options::overlay` inserted every key into the settings tree, then cloned the whole tree and deserialised it to validate that one key. Unknown keys deserialise without error, so they stayed in the tree and every later key paid for them too. Load time grew as O(keys²).

## Fix
A key with no slot in `T`'s default tree is now checked while it is temporarily in the tree, then removed. It is re-added once after the loop if it passed. The tree stays the size of `T` during validation, so load time is linear. The regression test loads 20k unknown keys plus one valid setting and asserts a time bound and that the setting is kept.

## Verified
- Regression test `options::tests::unknown_settings_keys_load_in_linear_time`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui unknown_settings_keys_load_in_linear_time`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I did not cap the size of the `ui.json` read in `apps/wordcraft/src/main.rs`. I did not make `saved_window` and `load_prefs` share one read. I did not change `lenient` to deserialise per field.

title: Reconcile inline objects with U+FFFC markers on .json open
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3678

## Cause
Opening a `.json` file only repaired runs (`Document::normalize_runs` → `Paragraph::normalize`). Nothing checked that a paragraph's `objects` matched the U+FFFC markers in its text. Objects are paired with markers by position, so with too few objects a delete removed markers but kept objects, and the later objects moved to earlier markers. With too many objects, the extra ones stayed in the model where no marker could reach them.

## Fix
Added `Paragraph::reconcile_objects`, which drops objects that have no marker and deletes markers that have no object, last first, through `delete` so the runs stay consistent. `Document::normalize_runs` now calls it for each paragraph after the run repair, so `.json` open fixes these counts.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::normalize_runs_reconciles_objects_with_markers`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-doc --lib normalize_runs_reconciles_objects_with_markers`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`Paragraph::normalize` stays a runs-only pass, because edit paths call it while text and objects are briefly out of step. Unmatched markers are deleted, not padded with placeholder objects.

title: Join resolved paragraph marks in one pass on Accept/Reject All
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3658

## Cause
`resolve_all` and `moves::resolve` walk the paragraphs backwards and remove each resolved mark on its own with `join_next_para`/`remove_empty_para`. Each call to `delete_range`/`remove_block` clones the next paragraph, which by then holds every later join, and shifts the rest of the container, so a run of N removed marks costs O(N²).

## Fix
Both functions now resolve every paragraph in place first and collect the marks that go. The new `join_paras` then rebuilds each container in one forward pass: removable empty paragraphs are dropped, each run is joined with the new `Paragraph::append_all` (the code behind `append`, normalizing once), and section breaks are absorbed the same way `delete_range` handles them. The case of a table after a joined mark is unreachable; it is guarded by a `debug_assert!` and keeps the paragraphs unjoined, so no content is dropped.

## Verified
- Regression tests `tests::accept_and_reject_all_join_many_paragraph_marks_in_linear_time`, `tests::accept_and_reject_all_join_marks_like_one_mark_at_a_time`, `tests::accepting_a_move_joins_its_source_paragraphs`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --lib -- accept_and_reject_all_join accepting_a_move_joins`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Accepting or rejecting a selection (`review.accept`/`review.reject` over a range) still removes marks one at a time through `join_next_para`. That path only handles the marks in the selection. The regression test for the cost is still timing-based: it compares against resolving one tracked word in each of the same number of paragraphs (about 2.5× with the fix, about 87× before), because no existing API can count the copied bytes. Of the three tests named under Verified, only `accept_and_reject_all_join_many_paragraph_marks_in_linear_time` is expected to fail on `main`. `accept_and_reject_all_join_marks_like_one_mark_at_a_time` and `accepting_a_move_joins_its_source_paragraphs` pin the…

title: Write a text-box story shared by many shapes only once on docx save
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3653

## Cause
The docx shape writer `wsp` wrote a text box's whole story into `w:txbxContent` every time it was called. `BoxBudget` deliberately puts no limit on outermost boxes, so N shapes pointing at one story (possible in a crafted `.json` document) made `document.xml` grow as shapes × story size.

The writer now keeps a set of text-box story ids it has already written in this save. The first shape showing a story writes its full text. Every later shape showing the same story writes an empty `w:txbxContent` (a single empty `w:p`), so each story's text appears in the file only once.

title: Layout: a line of only pictures takes no descent; multiple spacing adds its share
author: Morzilla
body:
A line holding an inline picture taller than its text took the **picture plus the text's descent**, whatever the line spacing. The code already flagged this as an open question: Word leaves "less than a full descent" below a line of only pictures, 0.5 to 1.9 pt in two header fixtures, and needed Word probes. These are the probes.

## Measured on Word

Microsoft 365, a 30 pt inline picture, paragraph spacing 0, in 10 and 20 pt Aptos, Arial and Times New Roman, at single, 1.15 and 1.5 line spacing (54 lines). The extra height of the picture line over the picture, in Aptos 10 pt:

| Line | single | 1.15 | 1.5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| picture alone | 0.02 | 1.95 | 6.14 |
| spaces, then the picture | −0.12 | 1.80 | 6.00 |
| a word, then the picture | 2.76 | 4.68 | 8.76 |

The same pattern holds in every font and size:

- **No visible text on the line** (only pictures or spaces): no descent below the picture.
- **Text on the line:** the text's descent below the picture (2.76 pt here).
- **Multiple spacing:** adds (m − 1) × the text's natural height to either case (0.15 × 12.2 ≈ 1.83, 0.5 × 12.2 ≈ 6.1). This is where the 0.5 to 1.9 pt in the old comment came from.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| largest difference from Word, 49 measurable lines | 11.25 pt | 0.20 pt |

A real-world effect: a signature table whose last cell line is a picture fits at the bottom of the page in Word, with 1.1 pt to spare. Here it moved to a new page because of the extra descent.

## Change

In `crates/layout/src/para.rs`, line metrics for multiple spacing now work as follows:

- **Text on the line:** the line records whether it holds text besides its pictures (spaces and tabs don't count).
- **No text:** a picture taller than the text gets no descent below it, and the baseline sits on the line's bottom.
- **Leading:** multiple spacing adds its share of the text's natural height to the picture line.

At-least and exact spacing are unchanged, since I haven't measured them.

title: Inline shared Word 2003 headers, notes and comments once
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3652

## Cause
The Word 2003 XML writer converted a header or footer part again for every `w:sectPr` that referenced it, and a footnote, endnote or comment body again at every reference to the same id. The only limit was a count of stories (`MAX_STORIES`), not of output bytes, so a few KB of docx could become hundreds of MB.

## Fix
`section` now writes a header or footer only when its (header/footer, type, part) differs from the one the previous sections left in effect, since 2003 sections inherit them as OOXML does. Inlined header and footer bytes count against a 64 MiB budget, and going over it makes the export return a `DocxError::Limit` error, not silently drop a story that later sections would inherit. A repeated note id gets an empty `w:footnote`/`w:endnote` at every reference after the first, and a repeated comment is written once.

## Verified

## Not changed
The existing `MAX_STORIES` cap still skips stories past 50,000 without an error, and I left the media limits as they were. No fuzz target was added.

title: Share one table-formula budget per Update Fields pass, charge by size
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3651

## Cause
Each table-formula evaluation started its own 100,000-visit counter, so one Update Fields pass over many `=` fields could read far more cells than the cap. Each visit also cost 1 however large the cell was, even though reading a multi-megabyte cell rebuilt and parsed its whole text, and the lookup for the output language read up to 100 more cells per field without being counted.

## Fix
A `FormulaBudget` is now created once per `update_fields_in` pass and shared by every formula in it (through the new `evaluate_field_budgeted`). Each cell read costs 1 plus 1 per KB of text. Size is measured only up to what is left in the budget, so once the budget is spent, nothing more is scanned. LEFT/RIGHT charge cell by cell as they walk the row, and the output-language lookup is charged to the same budget. Cells over 1 KB are no longer parsed for a number.

## Verified
- Regression tests `cmd::references::tests::update_fields_shares_one_formula_budget`, `cmd::table_formula::tests::a_huge_cell_is_charged_by_its_size`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --lib -- update_fields_shares_one_formula_budget a_huge_cell_is_charged_by_its_size`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The single-field `evaluate_with`/`evaluate_field_with` APIs keep their own fresh budget per call. No per-pass cache of parsed cell numbers was added.

title: Cap the headless ui_requests queue and keep one Paste Special request
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3641

## Cause
`Session::ui_requests` is only drained by the egui app. Headless MCP and CLI sessions never clear it, so every dialog-opening command added an entry that was kept for the whole session. `edit.pasteSpecial` without `as` copied its full text, html, rtf and picture payloads into each entry, up to about 144 MB per call.

Added `Session::push_ui_request`, which keeps only the newest `MAX_UI_REQUESTS` (64) entries. All engine commands now queue through it. `edit.pasteSpecial` also drops any older `pasteSpecial` request before queuing a new one, so at most one set of payloads is retained.

## Not changed
The egui front end still drains the queue each frame. I did not strip the payloads from the Paste Special request, because the dialog reads them from it. I did not add queue clearing to the MCP server or the CLI runner, and I did not add an MCP test.

title: Resolve note separator revisions in Accept/Reject All
author: Silvertree2010
body:

## Cause

## Not changed

title: Cap equation matrix size when writing OMML
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3643

## Cause
The OMML writer padded every matrix row to the length of the widest row. A ragged matrix, such as one row of 5000 cells plus 5000 empty rows, was therefore written as rows × widest-row cells, so `document.xml` grew quadratically (151 MB for 5000×5000) and could run out of memory on save, autosave or convert.

## Fix
Added shared caps `MAX_MATRIX_COLS` (64) and `MAX_MATRIX_ROWS` (1000) to `doc::math`, matching the limits the docx reader already enforces. The writer now keeps at most that many rows and clamps the column count to that many columns before padding. A regression test writes the ragged 5000×5000 matrix and checks that `document.xml` stays under 1 MB.

## Verified
- Regression test `ragged_matrix_save_stays_small`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-docx --test matrix_save_size`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The linear-format and LaTeX parsers, math_edit's add-row/column operations and `.json` loading still build matrices of any size. Only the docx writer, where the quadratic output came from, is capped. The reader keeps its own literal 1000/64 limits, which match the new constants.

title: Bound total LCS work per review.compare
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3632

## Cause
`lcs_ops` fills a table of up to 4000 x 4000 cells, and `MAX_LCS` only limits one call. `compare` calls it for the block list and again in `word_diff` for every changed paragraph pair, and nothing limits the total. Documents with many long, slightly different paragraphs therefore take time that grows without bound.

## Fix
Added a per-compare cell budget, `MAX_COMPARE_CELLS` (50M). It is passed from `compare` through `word_diff` into `lcs_ops`. A table that fits is charged to the budget. When a table no longer fits, the common start and end of the pair are still matched, and the middle is marked as deleted and inserted whole without being charged. Every pair still counts as a change, and accepting all changes still gives the revised text.

## Verified
- Regression test `cmd::tools::tests::compare_bounds_total_diff_work`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --lib compare_bounds_total_diff_work`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The quadratic-memory LCS table is still there; a linear-space diff such as Myers or Hirschberg was not added. One table is still capped by `MAX_LCS`, and the total work across tables within one compare is now capped too. The budget is per `compare` call, so a `tools.macros` that runs `compare` many times still does the work once per call. The per-call `MAX_LCS` limit and the character-level threshold are unchanged.

title: Keep a document's own styles and defaults when applying a style set
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3650

## Cause
`style_set` swapped the whole style sheet for `StyleSheet::builtin()` with the set's changes and copied back only styles with `builtin == false` and the default font. Every style the docx reader marks as built-in (BodyText, ListBullet, table styles and so on) was lost, along with the latent styles, `default_para_present` and the rest of the document defaults, including the language.

## Fix
`style_set` now lays the set's styles over the document's sheet. Each style with the same id is replaced and missing ones are added. The existing style keeps its `default`, `locked` and `builtin` flags. All other styles, the latent styles and the document defaults are left alone. No style set defines its own `default_chr` or `default_para`: each set only changes individual styles, so there are no set defaults to apply.

## Not changed
The style-set definitions themselves, which styles they change and how, are unchanged. The docx reader's rule for marking a style as built-in is also unchanged.

title: Outline: re-match collapsed headings only after edits, via a hash index
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3621

## Cause
`outline::after_command` runs after every successful command and re-matches every collapsed heading, even for commands that leave the document unchanged. When an edit shifts block indices, each collapsed heading that is no longer at its old index scans every block for the nearest heading with the same text, so one Enter costs O(collapsed headings x blocks).

## Fix
`Session::run` records the document revision before dispatch and passes whether it changed, so the re-matching pass only runs after the document actually changed. The pass now builds a map from text hash to the sorted indices of free headings once, and finds the nearest match with a range lookup around the old index. This gives the same result as before, including the earlier heading winning a tie.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::outline_many_collapsed_headings_stay_fast_after_edits`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --lib outline_many_collapsed_headings_stay_fast_after_edits`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Each pass after an edit still hashes every body block and recomputes outline levels (O(blocks)). Hashing only the paragraphs that changed would need per-paragraph dirty tracking, which is a larger change. The caret-repositioning part of `after_command` is unchanged.

title: #3938: Navigation search results show their page on hover
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #3938.

Pointing at a match in the Navigation pane's Results list now shows a "Page N" tooltip, so you can see where a hit is before jumping to it. Word does this too, though I couldn't find a Microsoft page that documents it; the only source I found is a third-party training video (https://my.mandarine.academy/en/training-resources/navigation-pane-part-2-search-options-1), which says Word's tooltip shows the page and the title of the section. This PR only adds the page, which is what the issue asks for. The section title could be a follow-up.

The page comes from the layout (`DocLayout::page_of`) and is looked up only for the result under the pointer, so a list of 500 matches doesn't recompute anything each frame. The number counts from the first page, the same way as the status bar's "Page N of M", the scrollbar tip (#2551) and Go To. It's not the number formatted by a section restart, which the Pages tab shows. Happy to switch if you'd rather match the Pages tab. A match inside a header or footer gets no tooltip, because that text repeats on every page; matches in footnotes, endnotes and text boxes show the page they sit on. The string reuses the existing "Page {page}" entry, so it's already translated.

title: Ribbon: an opt-in blur of the page scrolling up under it, and other aesthetic enhancements (#4018)
author: fluorine
body:
Closes #4018

A frosted ribbon. The page that scrolls up under the ribbon shows through it as a soft blur of its colours. This is a matter of taste, so it is **off by default**. File > Options > General > Interface > "Blur the page under the ribbon" turns it on. It is a separate setting from the animation settings. Agents use `ui.ribbonBlur`.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/58050663-f78e-409e-bc16-5ea5a33f19c3

## Why a frosted interface
- **Elegance.** Soft, tinted glass looks calm and modern. The chrome takes its colour from the work below it.
- **Less claustrophobic.** The ribbon no longer reads as a solid wall over the page. The window feels more open.
- **Depth and orientation.** The blur shows that the page continues under the ribbon, and it hints how far the user has scrolled.
- **Focus.** The blur keeps the page colours but hides the detail, so it does not pull the eye from the text.
- **Opt-in.** Some people dislike it or need solid chrome for contrast, so it is off by default.

## How it works
- Each page that renders leaves a small thumbnail (about 4 pt per cell). It is kept only while the setting is on.
- Each frame, the pages that would lie under the ribbon and the ruler (if the view continued upward) are sampled into a small strip.
- The strip is blurred with three box passes per axis (close to a Gaussian). The blur is wider across than down.
- The strip is stretched over the ribbon with linear filtering. The ribbon and ruler fills, and the hover, press and checked fills of ribbon buttons, are see-through over it.
- Ribbon menus are a little see-through and shaded (darker in a dark theme, lighter in a light one). They do not blur what lies behind them.
- The title bar fades from solid at the top to see-through at its foot, so it joins the ribbon below.
- The title bar search box becomes a faint pane of glass while the blur is on.
- File (the blue menu) slides in from the left over the editor, and the page fades in beside it. It slides out a…

title: Keep the direction of left, up and down block arrows (#3919)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3919.

Word's `leftArrow`, `upArrow` and `downArrow` block arrows were all read as the one `ShapeKind::Arrow`, which is always drawn pointing right, and saved back as `rightArrow`. So an up arrow inserted in Word showed up pointing right in WordCraft, and lost its direction on save.

Changes:
- `ShapeKind` gains `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowUp` and `ArrowDown` (`Arrow` stays the right-pointing arrow, still used for the double-headed and notched/striped arrows as before).
- DOCX read (`preset_kind`, which the VML `o:spt` mapping also goes through) and the legacy `.doc` drawing mapping (spt 66/67/68) keep the direction; DOCX write emits `leftArrow` / `upArrow` / `downArrow`.
- One `wordcraft_doc::wrap::arrow_outline` now gives the arrow's outline for every direction, used by the screen renderer, the PDF export and the text-wrap outline, so the three cannot drift apart. The right arrow's geometry is unchanged (head half the thickness long, shaft 40% thick).

Tests:
- `wrap::tests::arrow_outlines_point_the_right_way`: the tip of each arrow lies on the side it points to.
- `shape_style::tests::block_arrows_keep_their_direction`: the four DrawingML presets map to the four kinds; the VML test now expects spt 66 to be the left arrow.

title: Stretch justified lines that end in a manual line break (#3924)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3924.

In a justified paragraph, a line that ends in a manual line break (Shift+Enter) stayed at its natural width, like the paragraph's last line. Word stretches it to the right margin like a wrapped line, which is what the reporter's "how it should look" picture shows.

`break_lines` (`crates/layout/src/para.rs`) only justified lines ending in `LineEnd::Wrap`; it now justifies `LineEnd::LineBreak` lines too. The paragraph's last line, and lines ending in a page or column break, are unchanged.

Word has a compatibility option for the old behaviour, `w:doNotExpandShiftReturn` in `w:compat`. It is now read into `Settings::do_not_expand_shift_return` and written back in CT_Compat order, in the same way as `w:doNotUseHTMLParagraphAutoSpacing`. When it is set, these lines keep their natural spacing, so documents that use it still lay out as they do in Word.

Tests:
- `layout::tests::justified_line_ending_in_line_break_is_stretched`: the line before the break ends at the right margin and the last line stays short. With `do_not_expand_shift_return` the line before the break stays short. The first assertion fails without the fix.
- `do_not_expand_shift_return_is_read_and_kept` (`crates/docx/tests/fixtures.rs`): the option is read, survives a write and read, and `w:val="0"` or no element reads as off.

Docs: `docs/layout-parity.md` (compat-mode row, status line, revision history) and the `ROADMAP.md` progress log.

title: Navigation pane: Results snippets show object text and turn line, page and column breaks into spaces
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Navigation pane: Results snippets no longer draw boxes or split the row.

A Results row slices the paragraph's raw text around the match. That text holds U+FFFC for every inline object, U+000C and U+000E for page and column breaks, and '\n' for a line break: the font has no glyph for the first three (tofu boxes) and the '\n' ends the row's line. `snippet_text` now builds each part (before, match, after) from the paragraph the way plain text reads: an object shows its text (a field its result, a picture a blank, so a `^g` hit stays highlighted), and line, page and column breaks become a space.

The font scan behind #3248 (`ensure_find_fonts`) reads the same `snippet_text`, so text that now shows from a field is covered by the CJK/fallback fonts too.

I couldn't confirm from Microsoft's public documentation what Word prints for a page break in a Results excerpt, so a space is my pick; happy to switch.

Validation:
- `results_snippet_has_no_control_characters_or_line_breaks`: fails on main (snippet is still `one\ntwo\u{c}three\u{e}four`), passes here; fails again if the object index ignores placeholders before the slice
- `cargo test --workspace --lib -- results_snippet_has_no`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: Update multi-column table of contents without breaking column boundaries (#3889)
author: ovezthaking
body:
Fixes #3889

### Summary
When updating a multi-column Table of Contents (such as a 2-column TOC imported from Word with a `<w:sdt>` gallery control, or created directly in WordCraft), entry tab stops previously overflowed across column boundaries or left an extra blank paragraph at the top of the left column.

### Root Causes & Fixes
1. **Right tab stop position (`regenerate_toc`)**:
   Tab stops for right-aligned page numbers previously calculated position using the full page text width (`text_width()`). It now resolves the specific column width (`col_width`) from the section containing the TOC entries (`section_index_of(start) + usize::from(has_break)`).
2. **First column leading blank paragraph (`range_toc_to_field`)**:
   Deleting the old range left a trailing paragraph carrying the `<w:sdt>` `ControlEnd`. We preserve the trailing paragraph props and insert the `TOC` field into the preceding section break paragraph, preventing an extra blank line at the top of the first column.
3. **Localized TOC style IDs (`Sumrio1`..`Sumrio4`, `CabealhodoSumrio`)**:
   Added style helpers (`toc_style_id`, `is_toc_entry_style`, `is_toc_heading_style`) to detect and preserve localized TOC entry styles based on display names (`TOC 1`..`TOC 9`, `TOC Heading`).

### Verification
- Added synthetic regression test `updating_two_column_toc_respects_column_boundaries` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/references.rs` checking right tab stop positions, layout bounds for each column, absence of leading blank paragraph, and multiple update/save cycles.
- Verified manually in the WordCraft UI: tested both a Word-generated 2-column TOC and a document created and updated directly from the UI.
- All test suites pass: `cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --lib` (911 passed), `cargo fmt --check`, and `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-engine --lib --tests -- -D warnings`.

title: Format negative zero as 0 in spreadsheet import
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/formats/src/sheet.rs:726-727 (fn number)` (no existing issue): Spreadsheet import shows negative zero as "-0".

## Cause
`number()` formats whole values with `format!("{x:.0}")`, and Rust prints negative zero as "-0". XLSX `<v>-0</v>` and ODS `value="-0"` cells therefore imported as "-0", while a spreadsheet shows 0 in General format.

## Fix
`number()` now adds `0.0` to the value before formatting the whole-number case. That turns -0.0 into 0.0 and leaves every other value unchanged. A regression test checks that `number(-0.0)` returns "0".

## Verified
- Regression test `sheet::tests::negative_zero_formats_as_zero`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-formats --lib negative_zero_formats_as_zero`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I did not add XLSX or ODS end-to-end tests. Both formats go through `number()`, and the unit test covers it directly.

title: Comments: a reply made here is saved with its parent's anchors, so Word shows it
author: jpc7k1
body:
A reply added in WordCraft (Review › Reply, or a balloon's Reply) is saved with no anchors of its own: `comments.xml` and `commentsExtended.xml` have it, with `w15:paraIdParent` pointing at its parent, but `document.xml` has no `commentRangeStart`, `commentRangeEnd` or `commentReference` for its id. Word for Mac drops such a reply. Observed in Word for Mac 16.114 with a document drafted in WordCraft (one comment, one reply): Word's PDF export of the markup shows the comment and not the reply.

Word saves a reply with its own anchors beside its parent's: both starts, then each end with its reference (`Start 0, Start 1, End 0, Ref 0, End 1, Ref 1`). The writer now does the same for a reply that has no anchors in any story. A reply read from a file keeps its own anchors, so nothing is written twice, and a second save keeps the file as it is.

After the change, the same document re-saved by WordCraft shows the reply in Word ("Commented [TD1R2]: Checked."), labelled as a reply like Word's own.

author: matstrange
body:
The CSV reader behind Select Recipients had no cap on the width of a record: every comma became a `String`, and the field cap that did exist was applied afterwards, to a list that had already been built. A 38 MB file of commas was forty million of them — a gigabyte of memory for a list that came back empty, because every cell was blank. And because every record of a wide header is padded to the header's width, 605 KB of CSV grew to 4.7 GB.

The reader now keeps its limits while it reads, and refuses a list that is over them rather than building it and cutting it:

- at most 1,000 columns in a record,
- at most 2,000,000 cells — the records times the widest record, which is what a list costs once every record is padded to the header's width,
- at most 64 MiB of cell text.

Those are the numbers the spreadsheet path already keeps (`crates/formats/src/sheet.rs`), so a list read as a CSV and the same list read as a workbook are held to one budget.

Measured through the file route (`wordcraft-cli`), before and after:

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 40,000,000 commas (38 MB) | 1,029 MB peak, the list came back empty | 92 MB, refused |
| 1,000 columns over 100,000 records (605 KB) | 4,723 MB peak | 16 MB, refused |

A list of the usual shape parses in the same time as before (0.21 s for 100,000 records of 10 columns, the same peak memory).

**The second commit** is a review finding: `Insert › Table › Spreadsheet Table` made a table of the rows `insert.table` inserts — at most a thousand — and then wrote the parsed records into it, so a longer list lost everything above that, quietly. The list is now held to the columns and rows the table really has, and one over either is refused with a message that says which.

The record limit of a recipient list is not in this PR: [#1927](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/1927) changes that line and makes the reader refuse a list that is too long rather than cut it. The two do not touch the same lines.

title: #3995: Thai one-face fallback tests skip unless a Thai font with Latin is installed
author: benandez
body:
Fixes #3995. Test only.

## Why
Three Thai fallback tests from #2175 (#1549) fail on Linux machines where the only Thai fonts are Noto Sans Thai, Noto Serif Thai and Noto Sans Thai Looped:
- `fontdb::tests::a_thai_run_with_latin_falls_back_to_one_face`
- `tests_complex::a_missing_thai_font_draws_the_whole_run_in_one_thai_face`
- `tests_complex::a_thai_substitute_without_latin_hands_the_run_to_one_face_covering_it`

Those Noto fonts have no Latin letters or digits. So no installed face covers the test run `[D] … ฿1,250.50`, and `fallback_for_run` returns `None`, as its doc comment says it should. The tests only checked that some Thai font is installed.

## What changed
The three tests now skip unless the Thai substitute (`word::resolve("TH Sarabun New", …)`) covers the whole run, i.e. a Thai font with Latin is installed (Tahoma, Leelawadee UI, Thonburi, the TLWG fonts). The check doesn't go through `fallback_for_run`, so wherever such a font exists the tests still prove it. `thai_font_installed()` stays for the other Thai tests.

## Tests
- CachyOS, Noto Thai only: the three tests skip; every other Thai test in `wordcraft-fonts` (4) and `wordcraft-layout` (6) passes.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps pass (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).
- Not run on a machine with a Thai font that has Latin, so the non-skip path is untested here.

## Related
- #3566 (MatRanc) changes the bundled-only assertion at the end of the same `fontdb` test, for craft-fonts' Noto Sans Thai. It's a different hunk, and the two complement each other.
- #3561: the product-side gap when the pinned craft-fonts has no Thai face.

title: Layout: a long note referenced on a paragraph's last lines continues below them, as in Word (#3820)
author: jpc7k1
body:
Fixes #3820.

### What

When a line references a footnote too long for the rest of the page, the note is meant to continue on the next page. WordCraft placed that line and then stopped placing the paragraph. With the reference on the paragraph's second-to-last line, widow control then took the reference line over to the next page with the last line, and the whole note with it, leaving a large gap above the separator.

### How it was observed (black-box, synthetic documents)

Word for Mac 16.114, exported PDFs:

- The trial-brief reproduction in #3820 (long note 3 referenced on the second-to-last line of a six-line paragraph): Word keeps both the reference line and the last line on page 2 and continues the note on page 3: 4 pages. WordCraft: 5 pages, with the gap.
- Three more dummy documents with a long note referenced on the *first* line of a ten-line paragraph starting 6, 8 and 10 lines above the bottom: Word keeps placing the paragraph's lines while the note shrinks, but stops before only one line of the note would be left on the page (with the paragraph 10 lines up, it keeps two body lines after the reference and three note lines, not three and one).

### Change

- `crates/layout/src/lib.rs` (paragraph placement): once a line's note is being split, the paragraph's next lines go on the page the same way (`splitting`), so widow control no longer pulls the reference line back. A line (with a split note) fits while the notes before the last one and that one's **first two lines** (all of it if it has no more) fit below it: `NoteBox::min_piece` replaces `first_piece`.
- New test `a_long_note_referenced_on_a_paragraphs_last_lines_continues_below_them` (fails before this change).

title: Layout: keep with next splits the kept paragraph on the Mac, its last lines going over (#3850)
author: jpc7k1
body:
Fixes #3850.

### What

A paragraph A with **keep with next** fits at the bottom of a page, but the paragraph after it, B, can't start there. Word for Mac splits A and carries its last two lines (widow control) over with B. WordCraft, following the Word for Windows measurements in `keep_with_next_moves_a_paragraph_only_when_it_would_fit`, moved A whole, leaving the page short; and before a three-line B it left A whole and sent B over alone, breaking the keep.

### How it was observed (black-box, synthetic documents)

Word for Mac 16.114, exported PDFs. The eight variants in #3850 (Garamond 12, double-spaced, A about six lines, B three lines, everything pushed down 0.75 lines per variant), plus the same eight with B also kept with next (a chain):

| | Word for Mac | WordCraft before | With this change |
|---|---|---|---|
| A alone kept (8 variants) | A split, last 2 lines over with B | matched 2–3 of 8 | 8 / 8 |
| A and B both kept (8 variants) | same: A split, last 2 lines over | matched 2 of 8 | 8 / 8 |

(Compared with the ligature change in #3819 applied too, since ligatures move line breaks in these Garamond documents.)

### Change

- The room a kept paragraph needs after it counts **all three lines** of a three-line paragraph with widow control: neither of its splits (two and a widow, an orphan and two) is allowed, so it starts a page only whole. This holds on every platform.
- On the Mac only (`KEEP_NEXT_SPLITS = cfg!(target_os = "macos")`), a kept paragraph that fits but whose next paragraph can't start on the page keeps all but its last lines (two with widow control, one without) on the page, when it has enough lines to split; Keep lines together still moves it whole. Elsewhere the Word for Windows behaviour is unchanged.
- `keep_with_next_moves_a_paragraph_only_when_it_would_fit` expects the Mac's split there; new test `keep_with_next_holds_before_a_three_line_paragraph` (fails before this change).

title: DOCX: a hinted East Asian or complex-script font no longer replaces the Latin font
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #4031.

Thanks for the detailed report, it pointed straight at the spot. `rpr` in `crates/docx/src/read/props.rs` used `w:eastAsia` / `w:cs` as the run's Latin font when the `rFonts` had no `w:ascii`/`w:hAnsi` and carried `w:hint="eastAsia"` / `"cs"` (added for #93 in #111). But the hint only tells Word which font to use for ambiguous characters (punctuation, quotes); Latin letters never take the East Asian font, so "corn straw" lost the heading's Times New Roman. The fallback is gone: the fonts stay in `font_ea` / `font_cs` (the reader already stores them there), and layout already uses `font_ea` for CJK characters and `font_cs` for complex-script ones. The #93 behaviour is unchanged: a Normal style with only `w:eastAsia`/`w:cs` still inherits the docDefaults Latin font.

One existing assertion changed: the #93 fixture checked that a hinted `漢字` run resolved to `font == "SimSun"`; it now checks `font == "Calibri"` and `font_ea == "SimSun"`, since the CJK characters are drawn with `font_ea`. The `w:hint="cs"` fallback had the same problem and is covered by the new test too.

What this narrows: the hint itself isn't kept, so ambiguous characters (quotes, dashes, ellipsis) in a hinted run without `w:ascii` now follow the Latin font, as hinted runs with `w:ascii` already did. A side benefit: such a run used to be saved back with `w:ascii`/`w:hAnsi` set to the East Asian font, so the file changed on save; now it round-trips apart from the hint. Happy to switch if you'd rather keep the hint on the run and use it for the ambiguous characters.

Validation:
- `hinted_east_asian_or_cs_font_does_not_replace_the_latin_font` (heading style from the issue + the hinted run): fails on main (`("宋体", Some("宋体"))` instead of `("Times New Roman", Some("宋体"))`), passes here; fails again if the fallback is put back

title: #3994: watermark font names round-trip through the textpath's CSS style
author: SusieeTheLinuxUser
body:
Fixes #3994

## What was wrong

`crates/docx/src/write/watermark.rs` wrote the watermark's font name into the VML
`v:textpath` `style` attribute after deleting `"`, `'`, `;` and `:` from it:

- a name like `Bob's Serif` was **saved under a different name** (`Bobs Serif`) — the
  quote/apostrophe/semicolon/colon was dropped instead of being carried through;
- a **trailing backslash escaped the style's closing quote**, so a CSS reader took the
  rest of the declaration (`;font-size:1pt`) as part of the font name and the watermark
  lost its size;
- a **raw newline or other control character** made the CSS string invalid, so a reader
  could drop the `font-family` or the whole style.

## Root cause

The writer sanitized by deletion because the reader's `vml_style` splits declarations on
`;`/`:` and cannot carry those characters in a value. Deletion breaks round-trip fidelity
and leaves the two characters CSS strings cannot carry raw (`\` and `"`) unescaped.

## What changed

- `write/watermark.rs` (the only writer change): the four characters a quoted CSS string
  cannot carry raw are written as CSS escapes — `\22 ` (`"`), `\3b ` (`;`), `\3a ` (`:`),
  `\5c ` (`\`) — each with its terminating space per CSS 2.1 §4.1.3; control characters
  are dropped (no font name carries one); the apostrophe, legal inside a double-quoted
  string, is kept. The 100-character cap is unchanged (on the original name).
- `read/story.rs`: new `css_string` helper (next to `vml_style`) maps the escapes back
  (`\` + up to six hex digits + one optional space; `\x` is `x`; a lone trailing `\`
  stays literal — Word writes none). Applied at both `v:textpath` `font-family` readers
  (the watermark and the Word 2007 WordArt path), after the existing quote trim and
  before the existing 100-char cap, so Word-authored raw names read exactly as before.

## Tests added

`crates/docx/tests/it/roundtrip.rs`:

title: cu20we: fix box float paragraph origins and preserve shape line caps
author: nexotiq
body:
This fixes two rendering and format-fidelity bugs in separate commits.

- **Paragraph-relative box floats:** In headers, footers, table cells, and text boxes, adding 24 pt of paragraph space-before incorrectly moved the anchored float down by 24 pt. Use the pre-spacing paragraph origin, matching body layout, while keeping text and wrap exclusions relative to the text top. A synthetic regression covers all four contexts. Tests cover DOCX/VML round trips, missing/unknown caps, raster endpoint pixels, and PDF operators. Theme-inherited caps and joins remain outside this change.

Relevant gap, parity, progress, status, and revision records are updated without increasing readiness estimates.

Native Windows launch testing and side-by-side Word comparison remain pending; hosted CI has not yet been verified.

Prepared by @nexotiq with GPT-6/Codex assistance; both commits retain AI co-author trailers. Only Rust source, synthetic regression-test code, and relevant Markdown docs are included. No binaries, ZIPs, original documents, screenshots, raw logs, or private contact/account information are included.

title: Dialogs are modal, as in Word (#3859)
author: RatkoR
body:
Fixes #3859.

Dialogs were not modal: with one open you could still click the ribbon, File, the page or other documents, type into the document, and run shortcuts such as Ctrl/⌘+O. Now they block the window behind them, as in Word.

## Behaviour
- While a modal dialog is open, the ribbon, File, the page and other windows ignore clicks. Typing, shortcuts and keytips do nothing until it closes. Nothing is dimmed, as in Word.
- WordCraft's own Open/Save As window is modal too. When a dialog opens it (Templates and Add-ins › Attach…), the browser stays above the dialog.
- Modeless, as observed in Word for Mac 16.114.1 (typing in the document and ⌘O still work while they are open): Find and Replace (including Go To), Symbol, Mark Index Entry, Cross-reference, Insert Merge Field.
- Edit Data (chart) stays modal for now. Word for Mac edits chart data in a separate Excel window, but our dialog applies its data to whichever chart is selected when OK is pressed. Making it modeless needs it to follow the selection first: #4075.
- A press beside a modal dialog shakes it a little (three swings of up to 6 points over 0.4 s) so it's clear why nothing behind it reacts; Word beeps. With animation effects off, its border flashes twice instead. A press inside the dialog (also just inside its edge) doesn't, nor does another press while it runs. The Colors dialog keeps its existing behaviour: a press beside it closes it.
- Commands from the control channel / MCP still run while a dialog is open; dialogs such as Size and Page Number Format already follow changes made underneath them.

## How
- `Dialog::is_modal()` lists the modeless dialogs.
- `dialogs::block_behind()` draws a transparent full-screen backdrop just under the dialog window. egui 0.36's hit test ignores the modal layer, so egui's own `Modal` relies on a backdrop too. It also moves the window to the top, sets the modal layer (Tab stays inside), marks the dialog modal for AccessKit, and takes keyboard focus from the document.…

title: Comments: times in the user's own time zone, in the pane and the balloons (#2322, #2337)
author: seif9116
body:
Closes #2322.
Closes #2337.

Split out of #2291, as asked in its review. It is on main and doesn't depend on #2291.

## What changes

- **The Comments pane shows comment times in local time.** It showed the file's time as written, which WordCraft writes in UTC, so a comment made at 9:00 six hours west of Greenwich read 15:00.
- **The balloons show the time too.** Under each comment's and each reply's author, in the read-only balloons and the selected one, as Word does. They showed no time.
- **Which time.** When a file has both `w:date` and `w16cex:dateUtc` (Word writes both), the UTC one is used. A `w:date` that names its zone (`Z` or `±HH:MM`) is converted, and one without a zone, as older Word writes it, shows as written. A date with no time of day stays that date. A date that doesn't parse shows nothing.
- **The file is unchanged.** Comments keep the time they were written with, and new ones are stamped in UTC as before.

The layout is `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`, as the pane had.

## New dependency

`chrono` 0.4 (`default-features = false`, `clock` only, native targets only) reads the local zone offset for a moment, through `iana-time-zone`, so a comment from before a daylight-saving change gets that day's offset. The web build asks the browser (`Date.getTimezoneOffset` through `js-sys`, already a dependency).

## Overlap

#2291 rewrites the same balloon and pane code. Whichever lands second moves the time line into the other's layout: it is one call, `local_time::comment_time`, under the author.

## Tests

`local_time.rs`: `days_round_trip`, `utc_times_show_in_local_time` (across date lines and both signs of offset), `word_times_prefer_the_utc_one`, `hostile_times_show_nothing` (out-of-range and malformed dates, no panic), `the_local_offset_is_a_real_zone`.

title: Paragraph spacing in lines: read w:beforeLines / w:afterLines and lay them out like Word
author: pakiat
body:
## What

`w:spacing/@w:beforeLines` and `@w:afterLines` (ECMA-376 §17.3.1.33, hundredths of a line) were ignored: the reader kept only `w:before`/`w:after`, layout used those points, and the writer dropped the line values. WPS Office writes both on most paragraphs of a Thai memo (for example `w:before="181" w:beforeLines="50"`), and Word uses the line value, so every such paragraph sat ~3 pt higher than in Word. Over a page of a real Thai government memo this added up to ~10 pt per page, enough to push the last line of page 2 onto the next page.

`docs/layout-parity.md` noted that spacing in lines "uses the stored points (needs the document grid)". Measured in Word, a line here does not depend on the grid unless the grid has lines, so this can be done now.

## How Word measures it (black-box, synthetic documents, Word COM `SpaceBefore`/`LineUnitBefore` + positions)

| Case | Word |
|---|---|
| `beforeLines="100"`, no `w:docGrid` | 12 pt |
| `beforeLines="50"` | 6 pt |
| `beforeLines="100"`, `w:docGrid w:linePitch="360"` (no type) | 12 pt |
| `beforeLines="100"`, `type="lines"`, `linePitch="360"` | 18 pt |
| `beforeLines="100"`, `type="lines"` / `"linesAndChars"` / `"snapToChars"`, `linePitch="500"` | 25 pt |
| the same with `w:snapToGrid w:val="0"` on the paragraph | 25 pt (still the pitch) |
| `beforeLines="100"`, docDefaults 22 pt, or the paragraph at 22 pt | 12 pt (font size doesn't matter) |
| `before="240" beforeLines="100"` | 12 pt (lines win) |
| `before="240" beforeLines="0"` | 12 pt from the points (zero = use the points) |
| `afterLines` | same rules |

Between paragraphs the usual collapsing of space after and space before applies to the converted values.

## Changes

- `doc`: `ParaProps::space_before_lines` / `space_after_lines` (inherit, overlay; `Some(0.0)` cancels an inherited value, like the character indents of #534). `ResolvedPara::space_lines` and `set_line_unit`, mirroring `set_char_unit`: a non-zero value wins over the points; `resolve_para` use…

title: Layout: a document of many pages paid a body-length scan per page
author: MoriartyPuth
body:
## What

Laying out a document whose paragraphs each start a page grows with pages × paragraphs. A 2 MB file of 200 000 one-line paragraphs (`# Heading`, so every paragraph is its own page) took **68 s** to lay out, and halving the sizes only quartered parts of the time, which is the quadratic signature; a 1.4 MB file of 200 000 plain, flowing paragraphs took **14 s**. It is format-independent: markdown, LaTeX and DOCX imports all reach the same layout.

Repro:

```sh
python3 -c "open('many-pages.md','w').write('# Heading\n' * 200_000)"
time wordcraft-cli info many-pages.md
```

## Root cause

`crates/layout/src/lib.rs`, in `footer_table_wraps` (diff base `c524027`): the page loop asks for the wrap areas of the current page's footers, and on a `footer_wraps` cache miss it re-derived the section list with `ctx.doc.sections()`. The twin site is `header_table_areas`. `Document::sections()` (`crates/doc/src/lib.rs`) walks the whole body to pair top-level blocks with their section properties, so each cache miss costs a body-length scan — and every page takes the miss path at least once, because footers (and header tables for the twin) are needed per page. With b body blocks and p pages a layout pass pays p×b for these walks.

## Fix

Carry the list on the pass state instead of re-deriving it per page: `Ctx` gains `sections: Vec<(usize, &SectionProps)>`, built once where the `Ctx` is constructed (one walk per pass), and both sites read `ctx.sections`. The document does not change during a pass, so the list cannot go stale; a re-wrap pass rebuilds the `Ctx` and re-walks once rather than per page. Reading a section's properties copies the `&SectionProps` element out of the list, since both sites take `&mut` on other `Ctx` fields across their work. The list contents are the same as before — this only stops rebuilding it.

## Measured before/after

`wordcraft-cli info`, release build, same machine (rustc 1.99.1, macOS 15, arm64):

| case | blocks | before | after |
|---|---|-…

title: DOCX: write the default font size when the document leaves it unset
author: narain1
body:
## Problem

A document saved and reopened by WordCraft changes its default font size from 11 pt to 10 pt, with no edit in between.

```rust
let mut document = Document::new();
document.styles.default_chr.size = None;
resolve_char(..).size            // 11   (resolve.rs falls back to 11.0)
let reopened = wordcraft_docx::read(&wordcraft_docx::write(&document)?)?;
resolve_char(..).size            // 10
```

## Cause

When `default_chr.size` is `None`, the writer leaves `w:sz` out of `w:docDefaults/w:rPrDefault`. The reader fills an omitted default size with 10 pt (`read/mod.rs`), while the resolver treats the same omission as 11 pt. So the size WordCraft resolves is not the size it reads back from its own file.

## Fix

- Name the resolver's fallback `DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE` (11 pt) in `wordcraft_doc::props` and use it at the two resolver sites (`size` and `size_cs`). No value changes.
- When the default size is unset, the writer emits `DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE`.

The reader is unchanged. A file from another program that has no default size is read as 10 pt, exactly as before. Only what WordCraft writes differs, and only for a document whose default size is unset.

The written size is the resolver's last fallback, not what the Normal style resolves to, so a style that sets a size keeps it (there is a test for this).

## What I am not claiming

I did not establish which value Word uses for a file with no default size. This change does not pick one and does not touch how such files are read. It only makes WordCraft's own save and reopen keep the size it resolved. If you want the reader and the resolver to agree on 10 pt instead, that is a separate, one-line change to the fallback.

## Tests

`crates/docx/tests/it/default_size.rs` adds four tests:

- an unset default size keeps its effective size across save and reopen (fails without the writer change)
- an unset default size does not take the Normal style's size (fails without the writer change)
- an explicit default size is written…

author: tyrel
body:
Fixes #4041.

## What changed

A Word TOC with its entries in columns keeps its title in a one-column section above them: the title, then a blank paragraph that ends the section with a continuous break, then the entries. After Update Table, the engine's TOC starts at the field's paragraph below the break. title: AutoFormat: *bold* and _italic_ become real formatting as you type
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## Problem

WordCraft's AutoFormat As You Type has no `*Bold* and _italic_ with real formatting` option. Typing `*word*` or `_word_` leaves the marks in the text.

Microsoft's "AutoFormat as you type" page describes the option: text enclosed in asterisks becomes bold, text enclosed in underscores becomes italic, and in Word the formatting replaces the marks (https://web.archive.org/web/20260526195210/https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/autoformat-as-you-type-195c72fc-5e3f-43d5-a0c3-bf3606e2e58e).

The page does not describe the conditions in the second to fourth items below (spans of several words, the word-start, space and object checks, Undo and Enter, Track Changes and formatting limited to styles). Those are WordCraft's own rules.

## Change

- `AutoCorrectPrefs` has a `bold_italic` switch, set and reported as `boldItalic` on `tools.autocorrect`, and the AutoCorrect dialog's AutoFormat As You Type tab has its checkbox after Ordinals. It is off by default, so typing does not change until someone turns it on. The page does not state Word's default.
- When a word is finished by a space, punctuation or Enter, a `*…*` or `_…_` span that ends there loses its marks, and the text between them becomes bold or italic, plain and complex-script alike. The span may hold several words. The opening mark has to start a word, and the enclosed text has to hold a letter or digit and may not start or end with a space, so `2*3*`, `file_name_`, `* x*` and `*?!*` stay as typed, and so do marks around a picture, field or content control.
- AutoCorrect then goes on with the word without its marks: replacements, capitals, ordinals and links apply as for an unmarked word (`*teh* ` becomes bold `The `). The opening mark is not part of the word AutoCorrect reads, so the first word of a span of several words is corrected as it is typed (`*teh end* ` becomes bold `The end `). A marked web address becomes a link, and the text typed after it is neither bold nor italic.

title: AutoCorrect: words after a no-break space are corrected
author: dotCooCoo
body:
AutoCorrect did nothing for a word typed after a no-break space (U+00A0) or an ideographic space (U+3000). `autocorrect_word` put the start of the word one byte after the last white-space character. Those two spaces take two and three bytes in UTF-8, so the offset fell inside the character, `body.get(start..)` returned `None`, and the function returned with the word as typed: no replacement, no sentence capital, no ordinal superscript and no link.

Word's AutoCorrect replaces text and capitalizes the first letter of sentences as you type ("Use the AutoCorrect dialog to set up automatic correction and text replacement as you type", [AutoCorrect options](https://web.archive.org/web/20260908175841/https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/word/autocorrect-options)). The page does not mention the kind of space before the word; with this change, WordCraft finds the word after any white-space character.

## Change

- `crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs`: the word starts after the whole white-space character (`char_indices` with `len_utf8`). This was the only place in the file that stepped one byte past a white-space character.
- `docs/typing-parity.md`: one sentence in the AutoCorrect section naming the test, the status line and a revision history row.
- `ROADMAP.md`: a progress log line, the status line and a revision history row.

## Tests

- `tests_typing::autocorrect_finds_the_word_after_a_wide_space`: `teh` after either space becomes `the`, a word after `end.` and either space gets a sentence capital, `1st` after the no-break space and `22nd` after the ideographic space get superscript suffixes, and a web address after either space becomes a link. `references.caption` could only write Word's `Label N: title` in the `Caption` style, above or below the item. A report often needs a different line for each kind of object: a table title on the left above the table, a figure caption centred under the figure, and an equation number such as `(1)` or `(1.2)` at the margin of the formula line, with no label.

author: dotCooCoo

Those two spaces take two and three bytes in UTF-8, so the offset fell inside the character, `text.get(ts..te)` returned `None`, and the token was classified as not an address.

Word's option ignores "words that are part of a URL (any web or file address)" ([Ignore uppercase words, numbers, or Internet addresses when checking spelling](https://web.archive.org/web/20251001202354/https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/ignore-uppercase-words-numbers-or-internet-addresses-when-checking-spelling-b1bd7ae8-a712-4514-8db6-1c3a10a3407d)). - `crates/proof/src/lib.rs`: `enclosing_token` starts the token after the whole white-space character (`char_indices` with `len_utf8`). This was the only place in the crate that stepped one byte past a white-space character.

title: MCP: type_text with paragraphs is one command, not a snapshot of the document per line (#3973)
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
Addresses #3973.

## What was slow
MCP `type_text` with `paragraphs: true` was a `text.newParagraph` and a `text.insert` **per line**. Every `Session::run` that edits snapshots the whole document (for Undo and for rollback), so each command costs about the size of the document, and N lines are N commands. Measured through MCP in a release build:

| Lines | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 1,250 | 139 ms | 1.4 ms |
| 2,500 | 332 ms | 2.5 ms |
| 5,000 | 896 ms | 5.0 ms |
| 10,000 | 2,833 ms (doubling the lines cost 2.4–3.2×) | 9.5 ms (doubling costs 1.8–2.0×) |

It also left one Undo step per line.

## What the issue asked ("which step of Enter does document-wide work?")
Timed inside `Session::run` on a 10,000-paragraph document (release, µs per call):

| Command | per call | two snapshots | handler | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text.newParagraph` | 188 | 61 + 66 | 53 | 6 |
| `text.insert` of one character | 85 | 47 | 31 | 6 |
| `caret.docEnd` (read-only) | 261 | – | 261 | – |

On a 100-paragraph document the same single-character `text.insert` takes 14 µs. So the snapshots are the bulk, and a command per line cannot be linear. This PR does not change them: `text.insert` already takes a carriage return as a paragraph break and does the lines at O(1) each, so `type_text` now sends all the lines in one command. (`caret.docEnd` is also O(document): it lists every paragraph to find the last one. Small, but it could be O(depth).)

## Behaviour changes, so you can decide
- **Undo:** one step takes all the lines back (it was a step per line).
- **CRLF** is one break per line end. The per-line way inserted the `\r` as a break and then added its own, so CRLF text came out double-spaced.
- **AutoCorrect no longer runs on the breaks.** The per-line way ran Enter's AutoCorrect: it capitalised every line but the last (no Enter followed it) and fixed typos there, so what came out depended on the line's place (`one\ntwo\nthree` → `one`, `Two`, `three`). The text already went in…

title: AutoFormat: Tab and Backspace at the start of a line set the paragraph's indents
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## Problem

WordCraft's AutoFormat As You Type has no "Set left- and first-indent with tabs and backspaces" option. Tab at the start of a paragraph with text types a tab character, and Backspace at its start does not take a left indent back.

Microsoft's "AutoFormat as you type" page describes the option: Tab before the first line indents the first line, Tab before any other line indents the whole paragraph, and Backspace before the first line removes an indent (https://web.archive.org/web/20260526195210/https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/autoformat-as-you-type-195c72fc-5e3f-43d5-a0c3-bf3606e2e58e).

The page does not give the size of each step, what a second Tab does, what happens in an empty paragraph or in a list item, the order in which Backspace removes the first-line and left indents, which left indent Backspace removes, or what happens while formatting is limited to the document's styles. The rules for those in the list below are WordCraft's own.

## Change

- `AutoCorrectPrefs` has a `tab_indent` switch, set and reported as `tabIndent` on `tools.autocorrect`, and the AutoCorrect dialog's AutoFormat As You Type tab has its checkbox under "Automatically as you type". It is off by default, so Tab and Backspace do not change until someone turns it on. The page does not state Word's default.
- Tab before the first line of a paragraph with text sets a first-line indent of one default tab stop. Tab before a later line, after a line break or where the text wraps, indents the whole paragraph as Increase Indent does. So does a second Tab before a first line that is already indented or hanging.

title: RTF: style-sheet names take Unicode escapes; a malformed \' escape leaks no bytes
author: galagersharp-code
body:
Two small import-fidelity fixes in the RTF reader, found in a source review.

**1. Style-sheet names lose Unicode escapes.** The `Dest::StyleSheet` arm handled every control word itself and `return`ed, so `\u`/`\uc` never reached the shared escape path — unlike the font table (`FontTbl`), revision table, info, field and bookmark destinations, which all guard with `if !matches!(w, "u" | "uc")`. Word writes non-Latin style names as escapes: a Chinese "标题 1" stylesheet name (`\u26631?\u39064? 1`) read as "?? 1", corrupting the name shown in the UI and saved back out.

Now decodes like the other text destinations. Regression test: `stylesheet_names_take_unicode_escapes` (a name written as `\u116?\u105?\u116?\u108?\u101?` decodes to "title" and `\s2` paragraphs become Title).

**2. A malformed `\'` escape leaks its bytes as text.** `\'` followed by two non-hex bytes consumed only the escape (`None => i += 2`), so `\'gZ` produced a literal "gZ" in the document. Word drops the whole escape. Now the two bytes are consumed with it (`i += 4`). Regression test: `a_malformed_hex_escape_leaves_no_stray_text`.

`cargo test -p wordcraft-formats` (252 passing) and clippy clean.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved handling of RTF documents with Unicode-escaped style names, allowing those names to be read correctly, including when fallback character counts are specified.
  * Improved handling of malformed hexadecimal escapes: invalid escapes and up to two following hexadecimal digits are consumed, while other bytes remain available to be interpreted as document text or structure. This helps preserve surrounding content when an escape is malformed.

title: Markdown: escape lines that would start a fenced code block
author: galagersharp-code
body:
Found in a source review of the Markdown exporter.

`escape_line_start` covered headings, quotes, lists and thematic breaks but not a fence. A paragraph (or list item) with a hard line break whose next line starts with ``` or ~~~ exported unescaped — and in any Markdown renderer, or on re-import, that fence runs to the next fence or the end of the file, taking the rest of the exported document with it. Pasted code snippets make this easy to hit.

The first backtick/tilde is escaped now, like the other block starts. Regression test: `escape_line_start_escapes_fenced_code_starts`.

title: Engine: keep cell widths in step after Insert Column; validate a version restore before saving
author: galagersharp-code
body:
Two small correctness fixes, found in a source review.

**1. `table.insertColumnLeft/Right` never shrank the cells.** The command scales the grid to keep the table's width, but `insert_col` gives the new cells the pre-scale column width and the layout prefers a cell width over the grid — so the shrink never reached the layout or the saved `w:tcW`, and `tblGrid` disagreed with the cells. `sync_cell_widths` now runs after the scale, as the other width-changing paths do. Regression test: `inserting_a_column_keeps_cell_widths_in_step_with_the_grid`.

**2. `file.versions` saved before it validated.** With `{"save": "v1", "restore": <bad or refused>}`, the snapshot was already in the list when the command failed — against the run contract that a rejected command leaves things as they were. The restore is now resolved and validated (including the protection check) before the save. Regression test: `a_rejected_version_restore_saves_nothing`.

`cargo test -p wordcraft-engine` (910 passing) and clippy clean.

title: MCP: keep serving when the app isn't open yet (#4078)
author: galagersharp-code
body:
Fixes #4078.

`wordcraft-cli mcp --connect <addr>` exited at once when the app wasn't running ("can't reach the WordCraft app…"), so the client marked the server failed for its whole session and opening WordCraft afterwards didn't help.

The server now falls back to a lazy remote, the way lightcraft-cli already behaves:

- `initialize` / `tools/list` / `resources` answer normally;
- a tool call returns "WordCraft app at … is not reachable: …; will retry on each call";
- the first call that finds the app's port open connects and carries on. The control key is read on that connection (a lazy remote sends no key warning and describes itself as waiting until it has connected).

`Remote::lazy` shares the reconnect/retry/key logic with `connect` (one new `connected` flag gates the key warning, the description and the retry hint). Regression test: `a_lazy_remote_serves_once_the_app_opens` (fails with the retry hint while nothing listens; connects and answers once the fake app is up; the key travels). `docs/mcp.md` documents the behaviour.

`cargo test -p wordcraft-mcp -p wordcraft-cli` green, clippy clean.

title: Ignore quoted text when detecting recipient CSV delimiter
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/mailings.rs:526-527 (parse_csv)` (no existing issue): Recipient CSV delimiter detection counts separators inside quoted header fields.

## Cause
parse_csv chose the delimiter by counting ',', ';' and tab in the raw first line, including text inside quotes. Commas inside a quoted header could outnumber the real ';' separators, so the file was split on the wrong character.

## Fix
Delimiter counting now skips quoted text in the first line. The parsing loop is unchanged. A regression test covers a quoted header with commas and a ';' separator.

## Verified
- Regression test `cmd::mailings::tests::csv_delimiter_ignores_quoted_text`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --lib csv_delimiter_ignores_quoted_text`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The first-physical-line heuristic is unchanged, so a quoted header containing a newline is still cut at the line break. Tie-breaking between delimiters is also unchanged.

title: AutoFormat: border lines and +---+ tables track the characters they delete
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## Problem

With Track Changes on, the border-line AutoFormat (Enter after `---`, `===`, `***`, `___`, `~~~` or `###`) and the `+---+` table AutoFormat removed the typed characters outright. When the characters were already in the document before tracking was turned on, or another author typed them, Reject All could not bring them back. At the top of a story the border was not recorded as a formatting change either, because Enter's split changes the block count and the formatting comparison after the command skips containers whose block count changed.

Microsoft's "AutoFormat as you type" page describes both options (https://web.archive.org/web/20260526195210/https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/autoformat-as-you-type-195c72fc-5e3f-43d5-a0c3-bf3606e2e58e). No public page says what Word does with them while Track Changes is on, so the rules below are WordCraft's own.

## Change

- Both AutoFormats delete the characters through `delete_selection`, the tracked deletion Backspace uses: characters the same author inserted are removed, and other characters are marked deleted.
- Below a paragraph, the border on the paragraph above was already a tracked formatting change. The caret now goes after any characters marked deleted.
- At the top of a story, the border is recorded as a tracked formatting change, and the paragraph splits after any characters marked deleted, so typing continues in the new paragraph.
- The table is inserted untracked, as Insert › Table inserts one, so it stays after Reject All. The characters stay, marked deleted, in the paragraph after the table.
- A line that holds a tracked deletion no longer triggers either AutoFormat, so Enter after the deleted characters is a plain Enter.
- `docs/typing-parity.md` and the `ROADMAP.md` progress log describe the behavior.

Without Track Changes, both AutoFormats behave as before.

author: Menonro
body:
Fixes #3986.

Word shows a paragraph whose mark is hidden (`w:pPr/w:rPr/w:vanish`) on one line with the next paragraph. Observed in Word for Windows 16.0.20527 on synthetic files:

| Case | Word |
|---|---|
| `Alpha` (mark hidden), `Omega` | one line `AlphaOmega`, no space added |
| first: 0 pt before, 12 pt after, left, no indent; next: 24 pt before, 0 pt after, right, 72 pt indent | `AlphaOmega` at the first one's place (no space before, left, no indent); 0 pt after |
| list items `1.` (mark hidden), `2.`, `3.` | `1. AlphaOmega`, then `3.`: the joined item is counted, its number not drawn |
| number only on the next paragraph | no number |
| `One` (hidden), `Two` (hidden), `Three` | `OneTwoThree` |
| a 14 pt bold heading (hidden), then justified 10 pt body text | the body text starts on the heading's line and baseline; its next lines are its own (margin, justified) |
| a long first paragraph, a centred next one | lines that start in the first one keep its indents and alignment; lines that start in the next one take the next one's |
| a table after the paragraph | no join |

title: Add an Android app shell
author: tzhazuma
body:
This adds `apps/wordcraft-android`: a Gradle project that hosts the existing egui UI inside an `android-activity` window, plus the platform seams the desktop shell normally supplies. The engine, the UI and the theme are untouched.

## What the shell does

- **Entry point** — builds as `libmain.so`, loaded with `System.loadLibrary`; `android_main` is the usual `android-activity` entry.
- **File pickers** — `Services::pick_open` starts `ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT` through the Activity (six JNI calls in `src/saf.rs`); the picked document is copied into `<filesDir>/import/` and its real path comes back over the app's own control channel, so the *desktop* `app.open` command does the opening. `pick_save` answers with a scratch path in `<filesDir>/export/` and a worker publishes the finished file to the `ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT` destination.
- **Storage and fonts** — the data directory comes from `AndroidApp::internal_data_path()` and WordCraft's `ui.json`/`prefs.json` pair is loaded before the first frame and written in `on_exit`; the CJK face in `/system/fonts` is appended after the theme installs its families.
- **Touch** — 40 pt hit targets and wider sliders after the theme's style exists. The layout is not zoomed: a page layout designed for a desktop window needs a touch rework, not a scale factor.

## What is deliberately not here

No port-specific configuration: no release repository, feed or version override is part of this change.

Known gaps: the system clipboard is not wired; printing has no backend; a document opens from the app's own import copy ("save back to the original" is not wired); the launcher icons are the Android Studio template's placeholder art.

1. Is an Android target something you want in-tree, or would you rather keep it as a separate fork? If the latter, close this and we will keep maintaining it downstream.

title: web-embed: hand the browser app a file and get the document back as PDF bytes
author: fabric-io-rodrigues
body:
## Summary

A page hosting WordCraft in the browser can now **hand it a file** and **get the document back as bytes**: a PDF, or any format WordCraft saves. A new **headless wasm converter** (`wordcraft-wasm`) does the same without the editor, in a page or a Web Worker: `wordcraft-cli convert` for JavaScript.

Before this, documents reached the web app only through the file picker or a drop, and left it only as a download from the UI. A page had no way to integrate the editor.

## What changes

### 1. Engine: `io::convert_bytes` (`crates/engine/src/io.rs`)
- `convert_bytes(name, bytes, to, &ConvertOptions)`: opens a document from bytes (the format comes from the name's extension) and writes it as any of `SAVE_EXTS`.
- Built on `open_bytes_in` and `save_bytes_opts`; no new format logic.
- Inputs over 200 MB (`MAX_CONVERT_BYTES`) and unknown formats are an `Err`, never a panic.
- `can_convert_to(to)` takes an extension with or without its dot, in any case.

### 2. Browser app (`apps/wordcraft-web`)

**Files in**

| Way | How it works |
|---|---|
| `?file=<url>` (+ `&name=`) | `fetch()` at startup. Only `http`, `https` and `blob` addresses, up to 200 MB (`Content-Length` checked before reading). A failure goes to the status line and the app opens as usual. |
| `window.wordcraft.open(name, bytes)` | Takes a `Uint8Array` or an `ArrayBuffer`. |
| `postMessage` `wordcraft:open` | For the app in an `<iframe>`. |

All three put the file in the same `Inbox` a drop uses, so they behave the same way: a document opens (asking Save / Don't Save / Cancel first when there are unsaved changes) and a picture is inserted.

- `await wordcraft.exportPdf({markup?})` returns the PDF as a `Uint8Array`.

author: dotCooCoo

## Problem

The border-line AutoFormat (Enter after `---`, `===`, `***`, `___`, `~~~` or `###`) and the `+---+` table AutoFormat leave a numbered paragraph alone, but `border_line` and `table_line` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs` read only the paragraph's own `numbering`. A heading numbered through a heading-linked Multilevel List carries its number in its style, so both AutoFormats applied there:

- At the top of the document, Enter after `---` in such a heading removed the characters, switched off the heading's number and left no border: the split took the empty-list-item branch, and `apply_border_line` then cleared the border on the same paragraph. The next text went into the heading.
- Below another paragraph, the border went on the paragraph above, and the next text went into the emptied, numbered heading.
- `+--+--+` made a table and left the emptied, numbered heading after it.

Microsoft's "AutoFormat as you type" page describes both options (https://web.archive.org/web/20260526195210/https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/autoformat-as-you-type-195c72fc-5e3f-43d5-a0c3-bf3606e2e58e). It does not say what happens in a numbered paragraph; WordCraft's existing rule leaves one alone, and this change applies that rule to style numbering too.

## Change

- `border_line` and `table_line` check the paragraph's resolved numbering (`s.doc.styles.resolve_para`), as `list_autoformat` does since dff6221 (`text.rs:145-148`). Direct numbering, and `num: 0` over a numbered style, give the same result as before.
- `docs/typing-parity.md` (a row in the Lists table) and the `ROADMAP.md` progress log describe the behavior.

title: DOCX: a drop cap's letter takes the text's size back, not the file's enlarged one (#3000)
author: SusieeTheLinuxUser
body:
Fixes #3000

Word writes a drop cap as its own framed paragraph (`w:framePr w:dropCap`) holding the letter at the enlarged size the Drop Cap dialog computed (`w:sz`/`w:szCs` on the letter's run), followed by the paragraph it starts ("B" + "efore we start…"). The reader merges that framed paragraph into the one it starts and already translates the letter's *font* into `drop_cap_font`, giving the letter back the text's font — because the layout sizes a dropped letter from the text around it (`big.size` in `crates/layout/src/para.rs` is computed from the first run's size times the `lines` count).

The letter's *size* never got that treatment, so a Word-authored drop cap kept the file's enlarged size (e.g. 44 pt in a 12 pt paragraph), and the layout enlarged it **again**: `((lines-1) * line_h + size*0.7)/0.7` on 44 pt gives a ~195 pt letter for a 3-line drop cap that should be ~53 pt. On screen that is exactly issue #3000: the letter renders a multiple of its correct size, intrudes into the line above and pushes the first lines' text far right, while Word shows a letter that spans the three lines it drops through (measured from the report's screenshots: WordCraft's letter is 108×164 px where Word's is 54×81 px — 2.0× too large in both dimensions).

Two changes:

- **Read** (`crates/docx/src/read/story.rs`): the merge gives the letter run the text's `size`/`sizeCs` (inheriting when the text has none), the same way it already did for the font.
- **Write** (`crates/docx/src/write/story.rs`): the framed letter paragraph is saved with the letter at the size the layout draws it, resolved from the paragraph style like the layout resolves it. Word draws a framed drop cap at its run's own `w:sz`, so this is what keeps a Word file's drop cap intact after a WordCraft save — and fixes dialog-made drop caps, which were always saved with a body-sized letter.

The size formula lives in one shared function, `wordcraft_doc::resolve::drop_cap_size` (next to `MAX_DROP_CAP_DISTANCE`); the …

title: Paste: composite CSS colours with alpha over the page instead of dropping it
author: galagersharp-code
body:
Found while reproducing a user report of dark-theme web content pasting unreadably (secondary text on sites like linux.do and chat UIs).

`parse_color` accepted `rgba(...)`, `rgb(... / a)` and `#rrggbbaa` but discarded the alpha: `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.45)` — the secondary text colour of dark-theme sites — pasted as solid black, `#0080ff50` pasted as `#0080ff`.

The model's `Rgb` keeps opaque colours, and a paste lands on a white page, so the honest conversion is compositing over white: `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.45)` now reads as `rgb(140, 140, 140)` — what the eye saw on the site — and fully transparent text becomes white (invisible, as it was there). Opaque colours are unchanged. Legacy comma syntax (`rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.45)`), the modern slash syntax (`rgb(0 0 0 / 0.45)`, percentages included) and `#rrggbbaa` all carry the alpha now; `hsla(...)` too.

Regression tests: `colors_with_alpha_composite_over_white`, plus the composited expectations added to `colors`.

`cargo test -p wordcraft-formats` green (253), clippy clean.

title: Reject '+' sign in print page ranges
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/print.rs:42 (parse_page_range, closure `page`)` (no existing issue): Print page range accepts a '+' sign in page numbers ("+3" prints page 3).

## Cause
`parse_page_range` parsed each page number with `str::parse::<usize>()`, which accepts a leading '+'. Inputs like `+3`, `1-+3` and `+2-+4` were therefore treated as valid page ranges.

## Fix
The `page` closure now returns the existing "isn't a page or a range like 2-4" error unless the text is made up only of ASCII digits. The `bad` list in the existing regression test now includes `+3`, `1-+3` and `+2-+4`.

- Regression test `print::tests::ranges_parse_and_hostile_ones_are_errors`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-engine --lib ranges_parse_and_hostile_ones_are_errors`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`parse_date` and `Rgb::parse` have the same kind of '+' sign problem. I did not change them.

title: Equations: Left and Right step into an equation next to the caret, as in Word
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #4138.

`caret.left` / `caret.right` treated an equation's object character like any other character, so the arrows jumped over it and only a click opened it. Now, without Shift, an arrow onto an equation opens it through `equation.edit`: Right from just before it lands at its start, Left from just after it at its end.
