This doesn't touch the in-equation selection work in #3431; the shared pieces are `equation.edit`, now `pub(super)` so the caret code can call it, and one new `Session` field.

title: Import LaTeX \^{} and \~{} as plain ^ and ~
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/formats/src/latex.rs:2212-2216 (accent command handling, fallback for an empty argument)` (no existing issue): LaTeX import turns \^{} and \~{} into lone combining marks instead of ^ and ~.

## Cause
The LaTeX accent handler combined the accent mark with the first character of its argument. With an empty group such as `\^{}` or `\~{}`, it emitted only the bare combining mark (U+0302 or U+0303). That mark attached invisibly to the neighbouring letter instead of showing `^` or `~`.

## Fix
When the accent argument is empty, the handler now emits the plain character for `'`, `` ` ``, `^`, `"` and `~`. Other accent commands keep the old fallback. A regression test covers `x\^{}y \~{}z 2\^{}10 \texttt{\~{}/dir}`.

## Verified
- Regression test `latex::tests::empty_accent_group_is_plain_character`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-formats empty_accent_group`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The fallback for letter-named accents with an empty argument (`\u{}`, `\v{}`, `\c{}` and similar) still emits the combining mark. Accents with a non-empty argument are unchanged.

title: Picture memory limits for 6 audit issues: one decoder, TIFF strips, styles, Remove Background, Windows paste, render cache
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
Six audit issues about picture memory have one cause: every place that decodes a picture set its own limits, and some set none. This PR gives them one decoder, `wordcraft_geom::picture`, that reads the header and refuses a picture before anything is allocated when its decode would pass the budget. The picture edits and caches built on top are bounded too. Each issue is its own commit (#3665 has a second one from review), so every fix reads and reverts on its own. Based on main at 9d1067fc.

Fixes #3644, fixes #3645, fixes #3611, fixes #3647, fixes #3623, fixes #3665.

## Fixes

**One decoder checks the header against the budget, progressive JPEG coefficients included (#3644).** `probe` guesses the format, reads the header and works out the decode's peak: the output beside what the decoder holds while decoding, then beside its RGBA8 conversion, then beside a premultiplied copy. A progressive JPEG's decoder (zune-jpeg) keeps an `i16` for every coefficient of every component in whole MCUs, and the SOF header gives that size. A 7900 × 7900 progressive JPEG without subsampling needs 9 bytes a pixel (561 MB), past the 512 MB budget, though two RGBA buffers (499 MB) fit; ordinary 4:2:0 photos come out at the same 8 bytes a pixel as before. Render and PDF export ask the probe in their wrappers (`decode_pixmap`, `load_image`), and the crop dialog, picture edits, wrap outlines and the RTF re-encode decode through it. The geom crate gets it behind a new `image` feature, which the six crates that decode pictures turn on.

**TIFF pictures with JPEG strips are never decoded, and aren't inserted (#3645).** tiff 0.11.3 decodes a JPEG strip (compression 7) with a zune-jpeg decoder of its own and default options, up to 16384 × 16384 a strip whatever the TIFF declares. The probe reads the first image's compression from the IFD and decodes only none, CCITT Group 4, LZW, Deflate and PackBits. Such a TIFF in an opened document gets the grey box, and Insert Picture and Change Picture refu…

title: Draw no shading for an empty paragraph closing a section mid-page
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3975

## Cause
An empty paragraph that ends a section is laid out like any other paragraph, so `push_para` draws its shading as a fill. For a continuous break, `place_para` gives back only the paragraph's room, so the fill stays under the next section's first line. For a new-page break the paragraph takes the ordinary path and is shaded the same way. Word draws no shading in either case.

## Fix
`place_para` now drops the `Placed::Fill` items added while laying out an empty, object-free paragraph that carries a section break and is not at the top of a column or page. The new test covers continuous and new-page breaks, plus a control where the section-closing paragraph has text and stays shaded.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::an_empty_section_closing_paragraph_is_not_shaded`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-layout an_empty_section_closing_paragraph_is_not_shaded`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Borders of such a paragraph are unchanged. The case where the paragraph sits at the top of a page, such as a section that holds only this mark, is also unchanged.

title: Draw in-front-of-text pictures above tables laid out after them
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3863

## Cause
Body layout added a paragraph's in-front-of-text floats to the page's item list right after that paragraph's lines, so they were drawn in document order. Any table or text laid out later on the same page was drawn over a picture anchored before it. That is why the picture showed under the calendar's tables only sometimes, depending on where it was anchored.

## Fix
The page builder now records, per page, where each body paragraph's in-front items sit, counted after the behind-text items. Column-balancing snapshots and page take-back keep these records in step. Once pagination is done, those items move to the end of their page's list, in their original order, so they are drawn above the page's tables and text, as in Word.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::an_in_front_of_text_picture_stays_above_a_later_table`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-layout --lib an_in_front_of_text_picture_stays_above_a_later_table`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Floats anchored inside table cells, text boxes, headers/footers and the outline view keep their current stacking. A float in a cell is still drawn with its cell, so it can end up under a later cell of the same table. Behind-text floats and the relativeHeight ordering within a paragraph are unchanged.

title: A selected picture survives Enter and breaks (#4126)
author: RatkoR
body:
Fixes #4126.

Selecting a picture and pressing Enter deleted it: Enter replaced the selected object like selected text. Word keeps it.

## Behaviour
Observed in Word for Mac 16.114.1, with an inline picture and with Square wrapping:
- **Enter** on a selected picture or shape does nothing, however many times it is pressed. The picture stays selected.
- **Shift+Enter** puts a line break in front of the picture and keeps it selected. Each press moves an inline picture down a line; with a floating picture, the text after its anchor moves down.
- **Page break** (⌘Return, Insert › Page Break, Layout › Breaks › Page) goes in front of the picture, which moves to the next page.
- **Column break** does the same. Not observed in Word, but replacing the picture is clearly wrong.
- A break on a picture inside a Picture content control goes in front of the control, and the picture stays selected.
- A selected **text box** is unchanged: in the app, Enter puts the caret in its text.

## How

title: #4181: a click just outside a floating table skips its turned cell text
author: rabis7575
body:
Closes #4181

Turned cell text takes a click up to 2pt outside its bounds, and that check ran before the floating-table rule from #2038. So a click just outside a floating table, next to a cell whose text is turned (Text Direction on the cell, or a section whose text runs down or up the page), still put the caret in that cell. Now it goes to the text beside or after the table, as it already did next to upright cell text.

## What changes

- **A click 1–2pt outside a floating table** (above, below or beside it) across from turned cell text goes to the text beside or after the table, not into the cell.
- **A click on the table's area**, its edge included, still lands in the cell under it.
- **Which text:** cells with Text Direction (down or up) in an ordinary section, and every cell of a floating table in a section whose text runs down or up the page.
- **A page with no upright text but a floating table's cells:** a click outside the table goes to other turned text on the page; one by the table's own turned text still lands in that cell, not in the nearest upright cell. Before, the last fallback took the nearest upright line and left turned text out.
- **Unchanged:** tables in the text flow keep such a click in the cell, as before; tables in headers, footers and text boxes are hit as before.

## Engine

`DocLayout::hit` now works out the floating-table rule (`away`: a line of a floating table's cell when the point is outside the area its cells cover) before it looks at turned text, and passes it to `turned_hit`, the way `nearest_turned` already takes it. When no upright line passes the rule, `hit` tries the turned text outside floating tables, then any turned text under the point, and only then the nearest upright line. Everything that places the caret from a point goes through `hit` (`caret.set`, drag selection, Draw Table's start), so they all follow. No new commands or parameters.

## Checked by hand

title: Proofing: one engine and language table for the dictionary languages, fixing three bugs the copies hid
author: VoiceLessQ

The languages WordCraft proofs with a Hunspell dictionary (Polish, Portuguese, Italian, Croatian, Turkish, Russian, Czech, Indonesian and four Spanish varieties) were written one copy at a time. With **Regular expressions** on, Replace with now expands capture groups instead of inserting them as typed.

title: #4187: read tracked changes from .doc files
author: sarsonj
body:
Fixes #4187.

## Problem

The `.doc` (Word 97-2003) reader dropped the revision-mark sprms, so a document with tracked changes imported its deleted and its inserted text as plain text, side by side ("Alice SmithBob Jones", digits of an old and a new date interleaved).

## Change

New `crates/docbin/src/revision.rs`:

- **Marks:** reads `sprmCFRMarkIns` / `sprmCFRMarkDel` (toggles), `sprmCIbstRMark` / `sprmCIbstRMarkDel` (author index) and `sprmCDttmRMark` / `sprmCDttmRMarkDel` (DTTM) from a CHPX grpprl, with a piece's Prc applied after it ([MS-DOC] §2.6.1).
- **Revisions:** interns each distinct (kind, author, date) into `Document::revisions`, the way the DOCX reader does for `w:ins` / `w:del`, and points `CharProps::ins` / `del` at it. Capped at 65,536 entries; a raw-key cache means a tracked character doesn't allocate.
- **Dates:** a DTTM becomes `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:00Z`. A zero or impossible DTTM gives an empty date.

In `lib.rs` the walker applies the marks to text, to inline objects (pictures, drawn objects, note references, fields, taken from the anchor character) and to paragraph marks. A deleted mark joins its paragraph with the next one on Accept.

Author names come from `SttbfRMark` (FIB pair 51) through the existing STTB reader, now with a configurable length cap (256 characters for authors, 40 for bookmarks as before).

Formatting revisions (`sprmCPropRMark`, `sprmPPropRMark`) are not read yet.

## Verification

- **Unit tests:** DTTM decoding, interning and dedup, an out-of-range author index, the full-table fallback.
- **Reader tests (synthetic `.doc`):**
  - `tracked_changes_read_from_revision_marks`: inserted and deleted runs and a deleted paragraph mark, with authors and dates.
  - `tracked_changes_from_a_piece_prc_without_an_author_table`: a Prc overriding the CHPX, and no `SttbfRMark`.
- **Real-world document** (private, not attached), compared with Word's own DOCX conversion of the same file:
  - identical authors (2), dates and paragraph-mark revi…

title: Command fuzz catches caught panics; AutoSave switch works on an opened file (#3307)
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
Two small fixes, one commit each, based on main at ffa51443f.

## The command fuzz now sees panics

`hostile_params_never_panic` runs every command with junk parameters, and the never-crash rule in CLAUDE.md points to it as the proof. It threw the result away, though. `Session::run` catches a panic inside a command and returns `Err(Failed("<id> panicked: ..."))`, so a command that panicked on junk still passed. The test was blind. The Outline view fuzz in `outline_level_changes_are_undoable` had the same gap.

Both now go through `run_junk`, which fails the test on that error instead of throwing it away. No command panics there today (611 commands, 8 junk inputs each), so CI stays green; the test just starts catching the next one. Planting a panic in `edit.repeat` fails it with "edit.repeat panicked: mutation", where before it passed.

The fuzz skips `file.*`, `insert.picture` and `insert.textFromFile`, as it did before.

## AutoSave switch on an opened file (#3307)

Open a saved .docx and the AutoSave switch is greyed out; click it and you get Save As. The Discord reports in #3307 and a newer one say the same thing: a file you work on every day needs a manual save before AutoSave will cover it.

The rule underneath stays. It came from #151, where opening a file and typing one character rewrote the original about 2.5 s later, without anyone pressing Save, and that matters because a save drops what the readers don't model (content controls, charts, SmartArt). But clicking the switch is as clear a go-ahead as pressing Save. So for a file only opened in this window, the switch now shows off rather than blocked, and turning it on (by click, or `file.autosave` from a script) lets AutoSave write that file. From a script, a `value` that isn't true or false is an error, so it can't turn AutoSave on by accident. title: Layout: a no-break space is as wide as a space, not as the font's own U+00A0 glyph
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #4192.

Thanks to janvier-s for the report: the cause and the place were exactly where the issue said. The `map` closure around `shape_run`/`shape` in `crates/layout/src/para.rs` passed U+00A0 to the shaper unchanged, so fonts whose `uni00A0` glyph is wider than their space (Lucida Bright draws it twice as wide) made no-break spaces too wide. The closure now maps U+00A0 to U+0020 for shaping only, after the symbol-font mapping so a symbol font's own 0xA0 is untouched. Line breaking is computed from the paragraph text, so the no-break behaviour is unchanged. U+202F and U+2007 are left as they are, since the issue hasn't checked Word's behaviour for them.

Validation:
- `tests_nbsp::a_no_break_space_is_as_wide_as_a_space`: fails on main (ten no-break spaces measure 75.48 pt, ten spaces 41.73 pt), passes here. The font is the bundled Inter with its U+00A0 advance doubled and renamed in memory, so the test needs no installed font.
- `cargo test --workspace --lib -- tests_nbsp`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

Chart and SmartArt labels (`display.rs`) still shape the no-break space as it is; happy to do those in a follow-up.

title: The anchor mark of a selected floating object (#4195)
author: RatkoR
body:
Part of #4195 (the second of its three parts). Builds on the bold drop caret in #4208, but doesn't depend on it.

When you dragged a floating picture, nothing showed which paragraph it would anchor to, so you dropped it blindly. Word for Mac (observed by hand, Square wrapping) shows an anchor left of the paragraph a selected picture is anchored to, and while you drag, the anchor follows the paragraph it would attach to.

## Behaviour
- **Selected:** a selected floating picture, shape or text box shows an anchor mark left of the text, beside the first line of its paragraph. The icon is original, drawn in code in `icons.rs`.
- **Moving or resizing:** the mark moves to the paragraph the drop will anchor the object to, the one under the middle of its top edge. Resizing counts too, because it places the object again. Ctrl/⌘+drag shows the copy's anchor.
- **On a page the paragraph continues onto:** the mark sits beside the paragraph's top line on that page, as Word shows it, both while dragging and when selected.
- **No mark:** In Line with Text objects, objects in table cells (the mark would sit on the neighbouring cell), turned text, and Read Mode.

## How
- `cmd::objects::drop_anchor` (engine) now holds the drop's anchor choice: it keeps a corner on the page, then picks the paragraph under the top edge, else the nearest line. It was moved out of `move_object_once`, whose behaviour and errors are unchanged. The UI calls the same function, so the mark and the drop can't disagree.
- `DocLayout::line_box_left` (layout): the left edge of the text box holding a line, before indents and alignment.
- `DocLayout::para_start_on` (layout): the start of a paragraph's first line on a page, where the mark goes.
- `objects.rs` (UI): the drag works out the anchor when the pointer moves (stored on `ObjectDrag`, like the inline drop caret). `paint_anchor` draws the mark 9 pt square in the caret's contrast colour over the paper (`canvas::paper_caret_color`), so painting it every frame d…

title: feat(docx): settings_kept_unowned, to check a written settings part kept what the model doesn't hold
author: Fubeo
body:
merge keeps the children of w:settings that the model doesn't own, but a
caller can't tell afterwards whether it did: a child that refers to a
relationship goes, and a merge that can't scan the original falls back to
the generated part. settings_kept_unowned(original, written) answers that,
byte for byte, so an embedder can refuse a save that would lose settings
silently. A self-closing <w:compat/> that merge expands to hold the
compatibility mode counts as kept. SETTINGS_ORIG is exported so callers can
find the original part.


Tested: `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo test -p wordcraft-docx` (461 tests) on Linux with Rust 1.95. `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-docx --no-deps` with 1.95 stops on an existing `collapsible_match` in `read/story.rs:735`, not in this change.

Fub carries this as a patch on its vendored copy of WordCraft (v0.10.0); upstreaming it lets us drop the patch.

title: Format readers: one border-type table for .doc, one HYPERLINK parser for DOCX, RTF and .doc
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
Two pieces of reader code lived in copies that had drifted apart. The .doc reader decoded a border's type byte with two tables, one for paragraphs and one for tables, and the table one was wrong. The DOCX, RTF and .doc readers each parsed `HYPERLINK` field codes with a copy of their own, and every copy had gaps another had fixed. This PR keeps one of each. It has five commits: the border fix, then the shared parser with DOCX, then RTF, then .doc, then a review fix for backslashes in RTF link export. Based on main at fc7bdcb9.

## .doc table borders

`table.rs` kept its own table for `brcType` that disagreed with the BrcType table in [MS-DOC], which `fmt.rs` follows for paragraph borders. Dotted read as dashed, triple as wave, double wave as thick, 3-D emboss as wave, and thin-thick with a large gap as triple. Worse, a nil border (all bits set) drew as a 12-point single line. The six borders of `sprmTTableBorders80` are Brc80MayBeNil, where nil means "no border".

Table borders now go through the paragraph decoder. An all-zero border becomes an explicit "no border" instead of unset; the .doc reader gives tables no style, so that draws the same. The 12-point cap the table copy had now covers paragraph borders too, matching what the DOCX reader allows for `w:sz`.

## HYPERLINK fields

`wordcraft_doc::link::hyperlink_target` starts from the DOCX copy, the most complete. That one reads `\"` and `\\` inside quotes and skips the values of `\o` and `\t`. The shared parser takes the bookmark rules the other two had, and closes gaps all of them had somewhere:

| Field code | DOCX before | RTF before | .doc before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HYPERLINK \o "tip" "http://a.b/c"` | `http://a.b/c` | `tip` | `http://a.b/c` | `http://a.b/c` |
| `HYPERLINK \l "bm" \* MERGEFORMAT` | `MERGEFORMAT#bm` | `MERGEFORMAT#bm` | `#bm` | `#bm` |
| `HYPERLINK \m "http://a.b/c"` | `http://a.b/c` | `http://a.b/c` | no link | `http://a.b/c` |
| `HYPERLINKX "http://a.b/c"` | no link | `X` | no l…

title: security: require the data integrity check on encrypted DOCX packages
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary

`decrypt` only verified the HMAC when `EncryptionInfo` carried a `dataIntegrity` element, so an attacker who removed it could alter the ciphertext or the plaintext-length header and still get plaintext back, unauthenticated. The integrity check (MS-OFFCRYPTO 2.3.4.14) is now mandatory: `parse_info` refuses an agile `EncryptionInfo` without `dataIntegrity`. WordCraft's own `encrypt` always writes it, as does Word.

## CodeRabbit findings

- F-336 (CWE-354), `crates/docx/src/crypt.rs`

The other medium findings for wordcraft are already covered by open PRs (#3871, #3872, #3874, #3877). This PR touches only the integrity branch and does not overlap their changes to `crypt.rs` (the CFB precheck lines in `is_encrypted` / `decrypt`).

## Tests

- New `a_file_without_data_integrity_is_refused`; `hostile_encryption_info_errors_without_panicking` now expects the stripped file to fail.
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-docx` (all pass), `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-docx --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Restrict Editing: Enter and typing at the start or end of an exception line go inside it
author: dotCooCoo
body:
In a read-only or comments-only document, an exception that starts a paragraph has its start marker at the start of
the line. Home, Left, Right from the line above and Down into an empty line put the caret before that marker, which is
outside the exception, so Enter and typing there were refused. benandez reported this on #4123: with an editable region
straight after a protected short line, Enter was refused. The same happened at the end of a line that an exception
ends, where End puts the caret after the end marker.

Cause: `controls::prepare_edit` moves the caret over the markers of a block-level content control
(`Document::typing_pos`, `crates/doc/src/control.rs:675`), but not over a `PermStart` or `PermEnd`, so the edit lands
outside the exception and the protection check rolls it back.

Fix: `protect::typing_pos` moves a caret right before the start of an exception the author may edit to just inside it,
and one right after its end back inside it. `prepare_edit` calls it after `Document::typing_pos`, so typing, paste and
Enter all use it. Outside the exceptions nothing changes.

Test: `cmd::protect::tests::typing_at_the_start_or_end_of_an_exception_line_goes_inside_it` covers Enter and typing
after Home and after End on an exception line, refusals at the start of "Title" and the end of the document, and two
Enters on an empty editable line after "Title" with Built-in Heading styles on, which leave "Title" Normal. It fails on
`main` at the first Enter.

On Windows 11 (x86-64), on top of `main` at `fc7bdcb9`: `cargo xtask ci` passes its 8 steps: 4,118 tests passed
(doctests included), 0 failed, 4 ignored. The branch merges cleanly with `main` at `b4da59f0`.

title: Fields: \* DollarText and \* Hex write the result, and PAGE reads \* ArabicDash
author: dotCooCoo
body:
Builds on #4224, which builds on #4217. Until both merge, this diff also shows their commits.

WordCraft did not read the `\* DollarText` and `\* Hex` field switches, so a field or table formula with them showed its digits. `{ PAGE \* ArabicDash }` showed the plain page number.

Word's Format field results page (archived): https://web.archive.org/web/20260216055821/https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/format-field-results-baa61f5a-5636-4f11-ab4f-6c36ae43508c

What changes:
- `\* DollarText` writes the result in lowercase cardinal text, then "and" and the first two decimals (rounded) over 100, as the page describes: `{ = 9.20 + 5.35 \* DollarText \* Upper }` shows "FOURTEEN AND 55/100". A capitalization switch applies after it.
- `\* Hex` writes uppercase hexadecimal digits: 458 shows "1CA", as in the page's example. WordCraft writes uppercase for `\* hex` too; the page shows only the uppercase example.
- `{ PAGE \* ArabicDash }` shows "- 31 -". The page lists ArabicDash for page numbers only and does not say which fields that covers. WordCraft reads it on PAGE only; other fields, PAGEREF included, skip it and read the next format switch.
- The page-number fields, SEQ, PAGEREF and the NUMWORDS, NUMCHARS and REVNUM counts read the switches through `field_number` (`crates/layout/src/fields.rs`), and table formulas read them in `format_switches` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/table_formula.rs`).
- Cardinal, ordinal and dollar text keep the digits of a number past 999,999, as table formulas already do in #4224. Before, `\* CardText` showed "nine hundred ninety-nine thousand nine hundred ninety-nine" for such a number and `\* OrdText` showed "nine hundred ninety-nine thousand nine hundred ninety-ninth". A negative DollarText result, and a fractional or negative Hex result, keep their digits. The page does not cover these cases, so this is WordCraft's own rule.

title: Content controls: resolve lone table-open markers in linear time (#3826)
author: madhasoeki
body:
Fixes #3826.

## Summary

In `crates/doc/src/control.rs`, `control::orphans` identifies the `nth` index of each lone table-open marker. Previously, it repeatedly scanned backward over earlier events for every marker:

```rust
let nth = events.iter().take(k).filter(|x| matches!(x, ControlEvent::Open { block, off: None, .. } if *block == e.block())).count();
```

For documents with many unpaired table-wrapping control markers, this led to quadratic work ((\text{lone} \times \text{events})$) on edits that check for orphaned markers.

This PR resolves them in linear time ((\text{events})$):
- Precomputes the running per-block count of table opens in a single pass over `events` using a `HashMap<usize, usize>` and `open_nth: Vec<usize>`.
- Looks up the `nth` index in (1)$ (`open_nth.get(k).copied().unwrap_or(0)`), preserving the exact same `nth` values as before.

## Verification

- Added regression tests in `crates/doc/src/tests.rs`:
  - `lone_table_open_markers_linear_time`: verifies 2,000 lone table-open markers resolve in linear time and clear cleanly via `balance_controls()`.
  - `lone_table_open_markers_mixed_tables_and_paired`: verifies mixed tables with paired and unpaired controls resolve exact `nth` indices and remove only orphaned markers.
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-doc` (206 passed)
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-docx --test it content_controls` (10 passed)
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo xtask layers`
- `cargo xtask assets`
- `cargo xtask wasm`

title: Read Mode: ink and drag previews follow the Page color, which is kept between entries
author: dotCooCoo
body:
Follows up #4172 from the follow-ups in #4194 (aiongg): "ink, object drag previews and table drags in Read Mode still follow dark mode instead of the Read Mode page colour", "the Read Mode page colour resets on each entry; the reference app keeps it. Some names reach `tl!` as variables.", and benandez's note on #4172: "That works, but a helper would stop them drifting apart." (the sepia paper drawn in `canvas.rs` and in `render`).

## Change

- `canvas::dark_page` says whether the pages are drawn dark: Switch Modes, or in Read Mode the Page color's Inverse. The page rasters, the live and replayed ink (`ink.rs`), the object drag preview (`objects.rs`) and the table drag arrows (`table_mouse.rs`) use it. Before, the ink, previews and arrows followed Switch Modes in Read Mode too, so with Switch Modes on and Sepia chosen, black ink was drawn light on sepia paper.

- `view.readMode` no longer resets the Page color: it starts at None and stays as last set when Read Mode is entered again. It is still a view setting that is not saved with the document or between runs. Column width, text size and line spacing still reset on each entry. Microsoft's `View.PageColor` reference ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/vba/api/word.view.pagecolor)) and GCFGlobal's Read Mode tip ([GCFGlobal](https://edu.gcfglobal.org/en/word-tips/reduce-eye-strain-with-read-mode/1/)) do not say whether Word keeps it; this follows the note in #4194.

title: AutoFormat: a tracked heading or border line replaces another author's formatting change
author: dotCooCoo
body:
Follows up #4123 (FredApps: "Reuse the ownership-aware recording rule in fmt_revisions::change (which supersedes other-author changes) and add a two-author regression.") and #4129 (benandez: the top-of-story border record is skipped when the paragraph already carries a formatting revision).

## Change

- The heading AutoFormat (when it removes tabs the same author typed) and the border-line AutoFormat at the top of a story record their formatting change through a new `fmt_revisions::record_para_props`, which uses `Recorder::change`: the author's own earlier change keeps the formatting before it, and another author's is replaced. Before, both skipped the record when the paragraph already had a formatting change, so the new heading or border was credited to the earlier author and Reject went back past that author's formatting.
- `heading_line` checks that the resolved outline level is `None` instead of comparing it with 9. `doc` has no named constant for the body-text level; `ResolvedPara::from` already drops levels 9 and above (`crates/doc/src/resolve.rs:263`).
- `docs/typing-parity.md` and the `ROADMAP.md` progress log describe the change.

benandez also asked whether Enter is refused in an editable region right after a protected short line, and whether `border_line` has the same gap. Neither path can reach protected text: `heading_line` needs an empty paragraph after a line with no inline objects, and a region boundary is a `PermStart` or `PermEnd` object; `border_line` needs the paragraph to hold only the repeated character. A new test types Enter twice and a border line in such a region.

`mergefield_name` matched with `strip_prefix("MERGEFIELD")`. A field typed as `{ mergefield City }` was therefore no merge field at all: Check for Errors skipped it, and Preview Results and Finish & Merge left it alone. `{ MERGEFIELDX a }` went the other way and merged as a field named `X`.

Field-type names ignore case in ECMA-376 Part 1, 17.16.1 ("The field-type names DATE, Date, dAtE, and date are equivalent"), and the other keywords in mailings.rs already go through the upper-cased `keyword()`. Now the type ends at the first space or quote and is compared ignoring case, the rule the shared HYPERLINK parser in #4222 follows. The two IF checks for a nested MERGEFIELD ignore case too.

Follow-up from review (f3961d74d): those two checks looked for the word anywhere in the IF, so once case stopped mattering, a quoted value counted too. `IF { PAGE } = "mergefield" "yes" "no"` was evaluated as a rule on an empty field and showed "no". Both checks now ask what `condition()` already reads: the IF's first nested field, through `mergefield_name`. An IF on other fields keeps its result.

author: VoiceLessQ

Moving and lining up pictures, shapes and text boxes by numbers, not only by dragging. The document model, layout and the DOCX writer already handle alignment and offsets relative to the page, margin, column, paragraph and margin areas (`Float::h_rel`, `h_align`, `x` and the vertical twins). title: Text boxes: a press inside one goes to its text, not to a picture under it
author: arcanii
body:
## What it does

A press inside a text box selected any picture or shape lying under the box. So the box's text could not be reached with the mouse. A form built as a scanned picture, with text boxes laid over it to fill in, could not be edited: one such document has 285 pictures and 294 text boxes, and every click on a box's text selected the picture.

Now a press inside a text box goes to its text, whatever lies under the box.
- The box's border still grabs the box.
- A picture around the box still grabs the picture.
- An object in front of the box still wins where it covers the box.

- **The hit test:** `DocLayout::object_at_in` (`crates/layout/src/hit.rs`) now takes the topmost object under the press. When that is the inside of a text box, it returns nothing, so the press goes to the box's text through `story_at`. It already did that when nothing lay under the box.

title: Parse \genfrac in LaTeX import so binomials survive export
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/doc/src/math_latex.rs:861-865 (to_latex, FracKind::NoBar)` (no existing issue): LaTeX export of a no-bar fraction (\binom) writes \genfrac, which LaTeX import turns into garbage text.

## Cause
to_latex writes a no-bar fraction as `\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{k}`, but parse_latex had no `\genfrac` support. The command came back as the plain text `\genfrac0ptnk`, so an equation with a binomial coefficient was corrupted by a LaTeX export and import.

## Fix
parse_latex now reads `\genfrac{left}{right}{thickness}{style}{num}{den}`. A zero thickness (`0pt`, `0.0pt`, `0 pt`, `0\,pt`, `0em`) gives a NoBar fraction. An empty or non-zero thickness gives a Bar fraction. Non-empty delimiters wrap the fraction in a Delim node.

## Verified
- Regression test `math_latex::tests::latex_binom_round_trip`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p wordcraft-doc latex_binom_round_trip`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The to_latex output is unchanged and still writes `\genfrac`. Only a single-character delimiter is read. A multi-character delimiter argument is treated as no delimiter. Only plain `number unit` thicknesses are recognised; expressions such as `\dimexpr` are treated as non-zero. The style argument is ignored.

title: feat(pdf): bulleted and numbered lists are lists in tagged PDF
author: MyAIPlugins
body:
Bulleted and numbered lists were exported to tagged PDF as plain paragraphs, with the bullet or number read as part of the text. A screen reader could not announce "list, 3 items", move between items or skip the list.

A list paragraph (numbered or bulleted, showing its label, not a numbered heading) is now a list item, tagged the way Word writes lists:

- consecutive items of the same story and container (body, table cell, note) are one `L`;
- each item is an `LI` with the bullet or number in `Lbl` and the text in `LBody`;
- a deeper level is an `L` nested in the `LBody` of the item before it;
- `L` carries `ListNumbering` from the level's number format: `Disc` for bullets, `Decimal`, `LowerRoman`/`UpperRoman`, `LowerAlpha`/`UpperAlpha`, `None` for the other formats.

To tell the label from the text, `Draw::Glyphs` gets `list_label`, set only on the label's glyphs in `lines`. Screen and print rendering are unchanged.

Two cases that would otherwise break the list structure are covered too:

- **A picture inline in a list item** is a `Figure` inside the item's `LBody`. Before, an inline picture became its own `Figure` after its paragraph, which here would split the list in two around it. Pictures in other paragraphs are unchanged.
- **Turned text** (Table Layout › Text Direction) is now tagged piece by piece inside its turned frame: a list item's number or bullet is its `Lbl`, and pictures are `Figure`s with their alt text, or artifacts when marked decorative. Before, the whole turned paragraph, pictures included, was tagged as paragraph content. This also closes the case left out of #2086.

title: Mail merge: hold a CSV recipient list to the spreadsheet limits while it is read (#4053)
author: beeraw
body:
Fixes #4053.

The CSV reader behind Select Recipients built every record in full before any limit applied: each separator became a `String`, and `MAX_FIELDS` was only applied afterwards, in `header_split`, which then padded every record to the header's width. A 38 MB line of commas cost about a gigabyte, and 1,000 columns over 100,000 records cost several.

What changes:
- `parse_csv` holds a list to the spreadsheet path's budget while it reads it, and refuses the list (`CmdError::Failed`, naming the limit) instead of building it and cutting it:
  - a record wider than `max_cols`,
  - more than `sheet::MAX_CELLS` cells, counted as records times the widest record (what the list costs once padded),
  - more than `sheet::MAX_TEXT_BYTES` of cell text.
- `max_cols` is a parameter: `MAX_FIELDS` (1,000) for `mailings.recipients` (`csv`, `path`, `data`), 63 for `insert.spreadsheet`, the most columns `insert.table` makes.
- The 100,000-record cap is unchanged.
- A refused list leaves the current recipient list in place.

Tests (`crates/engine/src/cmd/mailings.rs`):
- a record exactly `MAX_FIELDS` wide is kept, one column more is refused;
- a list one record past the cell budget is refused, one at it is kept;
- more text than the budget is refused;
- `mailings.recipients` refuses an over-wide list and keeps the previous one; `insert.spreadsheet` refuses 64 columns and accepts 63.

`ROADMAP.md`: a progress log entry, a revision history row and the status line.

`cargo xtask ci` passes locally (macOS arm64). `storytold/craftrules` isn't visible from outside the organisation, so I followed the never-crash and progress-docs rules as AGENTS.md summarises them.

title: #4190: read text languages from .doc and RTF files
author: sarsonj
body:
Closes #4190.

## Summary

`.doc` and RTF files imported with no text language, so proofing fell back to the default language. A Czech document was spell-checked as English and almost every word was underlined. Both readers now read the language of each run and of each style, and the RTF reader also reads the document defaults.

## Changes

- **`crates/doc/src/lcid.rs`**, new: maps a Windows language ID to a BCP 47 tag (`0x0405` → `cs-CZ`). It covers all 454 IDs that name a language in [MS-LCID] §2.2, including the reserved ones Office uses, and was generated from the spec's table. IDs that name no language (`0x0400` user default, `0x0800`, `0x1000`, …) return `None`, so the run keeps the language it inherits. `.doc` and RTF share the table.
- **`.doc`** (`crates/docbin/src/fmt.rs`): `sprmCRgLid0_80` / `sprmCRgLid0` → `lang`, `sprmCRgLid1_80` / `sprmCRgLid1` → `lang_ea`, `sprmCLidBi` → `lang_bidi`, and `sprmCNoProof` → `no_proof`, for runs and style CHPXs alike.
- **RTF** (`crates/formats/src/rtf.rs`): `\lang`, `\langnp`, `\langfe`, `\langfenp`, `\alang` and `\noproof` on runs. `\deflang`, `\deflangfe` and `\adeflang` become the document's default character properties.
- `Fmt` (`crates/formats/src/model.rs`) carries the languages and `no_proof` into `CharProps`. Exporters are unchanged.

title: #4250: a float anchored on a later page of a long paragraph is drawn there
author: RatkoR
body:
Fixes #4250.

## Problem

A floating picture or shape anchored mid-paragraph, on a page the paragraph only continues onto, was drawn on the page where the paragraph starts. So:
- an object dropped in the middle of such a page jumped back to the paragraph's first page;
- a document from Word with a picture anchored like that showed it on the wrong page.

Observed in Word for Mac: a float is drawn on the page of its anchor's line. A `positionV relativeFrom="paragraph"` offset is measured from the paragraph's top **on that page**. Adding text on page 1 leaves the picture where it is on page 2, and the text moves around it.

## Fix

**Layout** (`crates/layout/src/lib.rs`):
- A float whose anchor line doesn't fit on the paragraph's first page is "late". Layout places it when it lays out the piece of the paragraph that holds that line, measured from that piece's top.
- The late float's wrap area is added for that page, so the text there flows around it. Earlier pages are laid out as before.
- If the anchor line only moves to the next page because the float's own wrap pushes it there (e.g. with footnotes), the float stays on the first page with its wrap, as before.
- Kept as they were:
  - the cover-page rule (#1632);
  - the #1374 wrap relay;
  - early floats (#2048);
  - equation numbers;
  - web view.
- Lateness only counts once the paragraph runs past the page's last column. A float anchored in a later column of the same page still goes with its first piece; that's noted as "not yet" in `docs/layout-parity.md`.
- Finding the anchor lines is a single pass, cached per paragraph layout, so the linear-time test for many hidden anchors still passes.

**Engine** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/objects.rs`): when an object anchored on a later page of a paragraph is dragged back onto the page where that paragraph starts, it is anchored at the paragraph's start. Without this it went back to its anchor's page. Found while testing in the app.

title: .doc import: a paragraph keeps at most 64 tab stops, and each style is resolved once (#3707)
author: beeraw
body:
Fixes #3707.

A `.doc` paragraph style could carry any number of `sprmPChgTabsPapx` / `sprmPChgTabs` sprms, and `change_tabs` never capped the list it built, so one style could hold tens of thousands of stops, each new stop scanning all the others. `stylesheet()` then applied every style's whole base chain again, so a base style shared by thousands of styles was replayed once per style.

What changes (`crates/docbin/src/fmt.rs`):
- A paragraph keeps at most 64 tab stops (`MAX_TABS`), as Word does and as the DOCX reader already does (`take(64)`). Past that, neither new stops nor `Clear` markers are added; a stop that replaces one at its own position still fits.
- `stylesheet()` resolves each style once through a new `resolve`, which keeps every style's resolved character and paragraph properties. A style whose chain is its parent's chain plus itself starts from the parent's properties and applies only its own grpprls. A chain cut by a cycle or by `MAX_STYLE_DEPTH` in a corrupt file is still applied whole, as before, so it resolves to the same properties. The recursion follows the chain, so it is at most `MAX_STYLE_DEPTH` deep.

Tests (`crates/docbin/src/tests.rs`):
- `many_tab_sprms_in_a_base_style_read_in_bounded_time`: the issue's shape built in code, a base style with 330 sprms of 64 stops each (21,120 before the cap) plus removals, and 4,095 styles based on it. Every style ends with 1 to 64 stops, under the 10 s bound the other hostile-input tests use. On main it fails: the run took 837 s. With this change it takes 0.01 s.
- `style_tab_stops_inherit_down_the_chain`: stops added and removed down a three-level chain, and two styles that name each other as their base. It passes on main and with this change, so the memoised styles resolve as before.

`ROADMAP.md`: a progress log entry, a revision history row and the status line.
